Come now, venerable sir, I will go and refute the doctrine of the ascetic Gotama on this point.” “Go, householder, and refute the doctrine of the ascetic Gotama on this point. For either I, householder, or Dīghatapassī the Nigaṇṭha, or you should refute the doctrine of the ascetic Gotama.”

60. Evaṃ vutte, dīghatapassī nigaṇṭho nigaṇṭhaṃ nāṭaputtaṃ etadavoca – “na kho metaṃ, bhante, ruccati yaṃ upāli gahapati samaṇassa gotamassa vādaṃ āropeyya. Samaṇo hi, bhante, gotamo māyāvī āvaṭṭaniṃ māyaṃ jānāti yāya aññatitthiyānaṃ sāvake āvaṭṭetī”ti. “Aṭṭhānaṃ kho etaṃ, tapassi, anavakāso yaṃ upāli gahapati samaṇassa gotamassa sāvakattaṃ upagaccheyya. Ṭhānañca kho etaṃ vijjati yaṃ samaṇo gotamo upālissa gahapatissa sāvakattaṃ upagaccheyya. Gaccha, tvaṃ, gahapati, samaṇassa gotamassa imasmiṃ kathāvatthusmiṃ vādaṃ āropehi. Ahaṃ vā hi, gahapati, samaṇassa gotamassa vādaṃ āropeyyaṃ, dīghatapassī vā nigaṇṭho, tvaṃ vā”ti. Dutiyampi kho dīghatapassī…pe… tatiyampi kho dīghatapassī nigaṇṭho nigaṇṭhaṃ nāṭaputtaṃ etadavoca – “na kho metaṃ, bhante, ruccati yaṃ upāli gahapati samaṇassa gotamassa vādaṃ [T 2.0060] āropeyya. Samaṇo hi, bhante, gotamo māyāvī āvaṭṭaniṃ māyaṃ jānāti yāya aññatitthiyānaṃ sāvake āvaṭṭetī”ti. “Aṭṭhānaṃ kho etaṃ, tapassi[V 2.0044], anavakāso yaṃ upāli gahapati samaṇassa gotamassa sāvakattaṃ [M 2.0039] upagaccheyya. Ṭhānañca kho etaṃ vijjati yaṃ samaṇo gotamo upālissa gahapatissa sāvakattaṃ upagaccheyya. Gaccha tvaṃ, gahapati, samaṇassa gotamassa imasmiṃ kathāvatthusmiṃ vādaṃ āropehi. Ahaṃ vā hi, gahapati, samaṇassa gotamassa vādaṃ āropeyyaṃ, dīghatapassī vā nigaṇṭho, tvaṃ vā”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho upāli gahapati nigaṇṭhassa nāṭaputtassa paṭissutvā uṭṭhāyāsanā nigaṇṭhaṃ nāṭaputtaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā [T 2.0061] yena pāvārikambavanaṃ yena [P 1.0376] bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho upāli gahapati bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “āgamā nu khvidha, bhante, dīghatapassī nigaṇṭho”ti?

60. When this was said, the Nigaṇṭha Dīghatapassī said to the Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta: “Venerable sir, it does not please me that the householder Upāli should refute the ascetic Gotama. For the ascetic Gotama, venerable sir, is a trickster; he knows a converting magic by which he converts the disciples of other sectarians.” “It is impossible, ascetic, there is no chance that the householder Upāli could go over to the ascetic Gotama’s discipleship. But it is possible that the ascetic Gotama could go over to the householder Upāli’s discipleship. Go, householder, and refute the ascetic Gotama on this point of discussion. For either I, householder, or the Nigaṇṭha Dīghatapassī, or you, should refute the ascetic Gotama.” A second time… and a third time the Nigaṇṭha Dīghatapassī said to the Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta: “Venerable sir, it does not please me that the householder Upāli should refute the ascetic Gotama. For the ascetic Gotama, venerable sir, is a trickster; he knows a converting magic by which he converts the disciples of other sectarians.” “It is impossible, ascetic, there is no chance that the householder Upāli could go over to the ascetic Gotama’s discipleship. But it is possible that the ascetic Gotama could go over to the householder Upāli’s discipleship. Go, householder, and refute the ascetic Gotama on this point of discussion. For either I, householder, or the Nigaṇṭha Dīghatapassī, or you, should refute the ascetic Gotama.” “So be it, venerable sir,” the householder Upāli replied to the Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta. Then he rose from his seat, paid homage to the Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta, and, circumambulating him to the right, he went to Pāvārika’s Mango Grove, where the Blessed One was. He approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, and sat down to one side. Sitting to one side, the householder Upāli asked the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, has the Nigaṇṭha Dīghatapassī come here?”

“Āgamā khvidha, gahapati, dīghatapassī nigaṇṭho”ti.

“The Nigaṇṭha Dīghatapassī has indeed come here, householder.”

“Ahu kho pana te, bhante, dīghatapassinā nigaṇṭhena saddhiṃ kocideva kathāsallāpo”ti?

“But, venerable sir, did you have any conversation with the Nigaṇṭha Dīghatapassī?”

“Ahu kho me, gahapati, dīghatapassinā nigaṇṭhena saddhiṃ kocideva kathāsallāpo”ti.

“I did have a certain conversation with the Nigaṇṭha Dīghatapassī, householder.”

“Yathā kathaṃ pana te, bhante, ahu dīghatapassinā nigaṇṭhena saddhiṃ kocideva kathāsallāpo”ti?

“But venerable sir, in what way was your conversation with the Nigaṇṭha Dīghatapassī?”

Atha kho bhagavā yāvatako ahosi dīghatapassinā nigaṇṭhena saddhiṃ kathāsallāpo taṃ sabbaṃ upālissa gahapatissa ārocesi.

Then the Blessed One related to the householder Upāli the entire conversation he had with the Nigaṇṭha Dīghatapassī.

61. Evaṃ vutte, upāli gahapati bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “sādhu sādhu, bhante tapassī! Yathā taṃ sutavatā sāvakena sammadeva satthusāsanaṃ ājānantena evamevaṃ dīghatapassinā nigaṇṭhena bhagavato byākataṃ. Kiñhi sobhati chavo manodaṇḍo imassa evaṃ oḷārikassa kāyadaṇḍassa upanidhāya? Atha kho kāyadaṇḍova mahāsāvajjataro pāpassa kammassa kiriyāya pāpassa [V 2.0045] kammassa pavattiyā, no tathā vacīdaṇḍo, no tathā manodaṇḍo”ti. “Sace kho tvaṃ, gahapati, sacce patiṭṭhāya manteyyāsi siyā no ettha kathāsallāpo”ti. “Sacce ahaṃ, bhante, patiṭṭhāya mantessāmi; hotu no ettha kathāsallāpo”ti.

61. When this was said, the householder Upāli said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, the ascetic's reply was excellent, excellent! The Nigaṇṭha Dīghatapassī has answered the Blessed One just as a learned disciple who rightly understands the Teacher’s instruction would answer. For what is the wretched mental rod in comparison to this gross bodily rod? Indeed, the bodily rod is far more blameworthy for the performance of evil kamma and for the perpetuation of evil kamma; not so the verbal rod, not so the mental rod.” “If you, householder, were to discuss this established in truth, we might have a conversation here.” “Venerable sir, I will discuss this established in truth; let us have a conversation here.”

62. “Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, gahapati, idhassa nigaṇṭho ābādhiko dukkhito [T 2.0062] bāḷhagilāno sītodakapaṭikkhitto uṇhodakapaṭisevī. So sītodakaṃ alabhamāno kālaṅkareyya. Imassa pana, gahapati, nigaṇṭho nāṭaputto katthūpapattiṃ paññapetī”ti?

62. “What do you think, householder? Suppose there is a Nigaṇṭha here who is afflicted, suffering, and gravely ill, who has rejected cold water and is accustomed to using hot water. If he does not obtain cold water, he might die. Now, householder, where does the Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta declare that he is reborn?”

“Atthi, bhante, manosattā nāma devā tattha so upapajjati”.

“Venerable sir, there are devas called ‘those attached to mind,’ and he is reborn there.”

“Taṃ kissa hetu”?

“For what reason?”

“Asu hi, bhante[M 2.0040], manopaṭibaddho kālaṅkarotī”ti.

“Because, venerable sir, he dies mentally attached.”

“Manasi karohi, gahapati gahapati gahapati manasi karohi (sī. syā. kaṃ.), gahapati manasi karohi (ka.), gahapati gahapati (pī.), manasi karitvā kho, gahapati, byākarohi. Na kho te sandhiyati purimena vā pacchimaṃ, pacchimena vā purimaṃ. Bhāsitā kho pana te, gahapati, esā vācā – ‘sacce ahaṃ, bhante, patiṭṭhāya mantessāmi, hotu no ettha kathāsallāpo’”ti. “Kiñcāpi, bhante, bhagavā evamāha, atha kho kāyadaṇḍova mahāsāvajjataro pāpassa kammassa kiriyāya pāpassa kammassa pavattiyā, no tathā vacīdaṇḍo, no tathā manodaṇḍo”ti.

“Take this to mind, householder. Having taken this to mind, householder, then answer. Your earlier statement does not cohere with your later one, nor your later with your earlier. Yet, householder, you spoke this sentence: ‘Venerable sir, I will discuss this established in truth; let us have a conversation here.’” “Although the Blessed One says this, venerable sir, still the bodily rod is far more blameworthy for the performance of evil kamma and for the perpetuation of evil kamma; not so the verbal rod, not so the mental rod.”

63. “Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, gahapati[P 1.0377], idhassa nigaṇṭho nāṭaputto cātuyāmasaṃvarasaṃvuto sabbavārivārito sabbavāriyutto sabbavāridhuto sabbavāriphuṭo. So abhikkamanto paṭikkamanto bahū khuddake pāṇe saṅghātaṃ āpādeti. Imassa pana, gahapati, nigaṇṭho nāṭaputto kaṃ vipākaṃ paññapetī”ti?

63. “What do you think, householder? Suppose there is a Nigaṇṭha here restrained by the fourfold restraint, restrained from all water, endowed with the restraint from all water, having shaken off all water, and suffused by the restraint from all water. As he walks back and forth, he causes the destruction of many small living beings. Now, householder, what result does the Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta declare for this?”

“Asañcetanikaṃ, bhante, nigaṇṭho nāṭaputto no mahāsāvajjaṃ paññapetī”ti.

“Venerable sir, the Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta does not declare what is unintentional to be greatly blameworthy.”

“Sace [V 2.0046] pana, gahapati, cetetī”ti?

“But if, householder, he intends it?”

“Mahāsāvajjaṃ, bhante, hotī”ti.

“It is greatly blameworthy, venerable sir.”

“Cetanaṃ pana, gahapati, nigaṇṭho nāṭaputto kismiṃ paññapetī”ti?

“And in what, householder, does the Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta declare intention to be?”

“Manodaṇḍasmiṃ, bhante”ti.

“In the mental rod, venerable sir.”

“Manasi karohi, gahapati[T 2.0063], manasi karitvā kho, gahapati, byākarohi. Na kho te sandhiyati purimena vā pacchimaṃ, pacchimena vā purimaṃ. Bhāsitā kho pana te, gahapati, esā vācā – ‘sacce ahaṃ, bhante, patiṭṭhāya mantessāmi; hotu no ettha kathāsallāpo’”ti. “Kiñcāpi, bhante, bhagavā evamāha, atha kho kāyadaṇḍova mahāsāvajjataro pāpassa kammassa kiriyāya pāpassa kammassa pavattiyā, no tathā vacīdaṇḍo, no tathā manodaṇḍo”ti.

“Attend closely, householder, and having attended closely, then reply. Your earlier and later statements do not cohere, nor does the later with the earlier. Yet, householder, this statement was made by you: ‘Venerable sir, I shall discuss this having taken my stand on truth; let there be a conversation between us here.’" “Although the Blessed One says this, venerable sir, still the rod of the body is more gravely blameworthy for the performance of an evil kamma and for the perpetuation of an evil kamma, not so the rod of speech, not so the rod of the mind.”

64. “Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, gahapati, ayaṃ nāḷandā iddhā ceva phītā ca bahujanā ākiṇṇamanussā”ti?

64. “What do you think, householder? Is this Nāḷandā prosperous and flourishing, with many people, teeming with inhabitants?”

“Evaṃ, bhante, ayaṃ nāḷandā iddhā ceva phītā ca bahujanā ākiṇṇamanussā”ti.

“So it is, venerable sir. This Nāḷandā is prosperous and flourishing, with many people, teeming with inhabitants.”

“Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, gahapati, idha puriso āgaccheyya ukkhittāsiko. So evaṃ vadeyya – ‘ahaṃ yāvatikā imissā nāḷandāya pāṇā te ekena khaṇena ekena muhuttena ekaṃ maṃsakhalaṃ ekaṃ maṃsapuñjaṃ karissāmī’ti. Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, gahapati, pahoti nu kho so puriso yāvatikā imissā nāḷandāya pāṇā te ekena khaṇena ekena muhuttena [M 2.0041] ekaṃ maṃsakhalaṃ ekaṃ maṃsapuñjaṃ kātu”nti?

“What do you think, householder? Suppose a man with a drawn sword were to come here and say: ‘In a single instant, in a single moment, I will make all the living beings in this Nāḷandā into one mass of flesh, one heap of flesh.’ What do you think, householder, would that man be able to make all the living beings in this Nāḷandā into one mass of flesh, one heap of flesh, in a single instant, in a single moment?”

“Dasapi, bhante, purisā, vīsampi, bhante, purisā, tiṃsampi, bhante, purisā, cattārīsampi, bhante, purisā, paññāsampi, bhante, purisā nappahonti yāvatikā imissā nāḷandāya pāṇā te ekena khaṇena ekena muhuttena ekaṃ maṃsakhalaṃ ekaṃ maṃsapuñjaṃ kātuṃ. Kiñhi sobhati eko chavo puriso”ti!

“Venerable sir, not ten men, not twenty men, not thirty men, not forty men, not fifty men would be able to make all the living beings in this Nāḷandā into one mass of flesh, one heap of flesh, in a single instant, in a single moment. What is one wretched man to accomplish?”

“Taṃ [V 2.0047] kiṃ maññasi, gahapati[T 2.0064], idha āgaccheyya samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā iddhimā cetovasippatto. So evaṃ vadeyya – ‘ahaṃ imaṃ nāḷandaṃ ekena manopadosena bhasmaṃ karissāmī’ti. Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, gahapati, pahoti nu kho so samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā iddhimā cetovasippatto imaṃ nāḷandaṃ ekena manopadosena bhasmaṃ kātu”nti[P 1.0378]?

“What do you think, householder? Suppose a recluse or brahmin, endowed with psychic power and mastery of mind, were to come here and say: ‘I will reduce this Nāḷandā to ashes with a single corruption of the mind.’ What do you think, householder, would that recluse or brahmin, endowed with psychic power and mastery of mind, be able to reduce this Nāḷandā to ashes with a single corruption of the mind?”

“Dasapi, bhante, nāḷandā, vīsampi nāḷandā, tiṃsampi nāḷandā, cattārīsampi nāḷandā, paññāsampi nāḷandā pahoti so samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā iddhimā cetovasippatto ekena manopadosena bhasmaṃ kātuṃ. Kiñhi sobhati ekā chavā nāḷandā”ti!

“Venerable sir, that recluse or brahmin, endowed with psychic power and mastery of mind, could reduce ten Nāḷandās, twenty Nāḷandās, thirty Nāḷandās, forty Nāḷandās, or fifty Nāḷandās to ashes with a single corruption of the mind. What is one paltry Nāḷandā to accomplish?”

“Manasi karohi, gahapati, manasi karitvā kho, gahapati, byākarohi. Na kho te sandhiyati purimena vā pacchimaṃ, pacchimena vā purimaṃ. Bhāsitā kho pana te, gahapati, esā vācā – ‘sacce ahaṃ, bhante, patiṭṭhāya mantessāmi; hotu no ettha kathāsallāpo’”ti.

“Attend closely, householder, and having attended closely, then reply. Your earlier and later statements do not cohere, nor does the later with the earlier. Yet, householder, this statement was made by you: ‘Venerable sir, I shall discuss this having taken my stand on truth; let there be a conversation between us here.’”

“Kiñcāpi, bhante, bhagavā evamāha, atha kho kāyadaṇḍova mahāsāvajjataro pāpassa kammassa kiriyāya pāpassa kammassa pavattiyā, no tathā vacīdaṇḍo, no tathā manodaṇḍo”ti.

“Although the Blessed One says this, venerable sir, still the rod of the body is more gravely blameworthy for the performance of an evil kamma and for the perpetuation of an evil kamma, not so the rod of speech, not so the rod of the mind.”

65. “Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, gahapati, sutaṃ te daṇḍakīraññaṃ daṇḍakāraññaṃ (sī. pī.) kāliṅgāraññaṃ majjhāraññaṃ mejjhāraññaṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) mātaṅgāraññaṃ araññaṃ araññabhūta”nti?

65. “What do you think, householder? Have you heard of the Daṇḍakī forest, the Kāliṅga forest, the Majjha forest, and the Mātaṅga forest becoming a desolate wilderness?”

“Evaṃ, bhante, sutaṃ me daṇḍakīraññaṃ kāliṅgāraññaṃ majjhāraññaṃ mātaṅgāraññaṃ araññaṃ araññabhūta”nti.

“So it is, venerable sir. I have heard of the Daṇḍakī forest, the Kāliṅga forest, the Majjha forest, and the Mātaṅga forest becoming a desolate wilderness.”

“Taṃ [T 2.0065] kiṃ maññasi, gahapati, kinti te sutaṃ kena taṃ daṇḍakīraññaṃ kāliṅgāraññaṃ majjhāraññaṃ mātaṅgāraññaṃ araññaṃ araññabhūta”nti?

“What do you think, householder? What have you heard was the cause for the Daṇḍakī forest, the Kāliṅga forest, the Majjha forest, and the Mātaṅga forest becoming a desolate wilderness?”

“Sutaṃ [V 2.0048] metaṃ, bhante, isīnaṃ manopadosena taṃ daṇḍakīraññaṃ kāliṅgāraññaṃ majjhāraññaṃ mātaṅgāraññaṃ araññaṃ araññabhūta”nti.

“I have heard this, venerable sir: it was through the seers’ corruption of mind that the Daṇḍakī forest, the Kāliṅga forest, the Majjha forest, and the Mātaṅga forest became a desolate wilderness.”

“Manasi karohi, gahapati, manasi karitvā kho, gahapati, byākarohi. Na kho te sandhiyati purimena vā pacchimaṃ, pacchimena vā purimaṃ. Bhāsitā kho pana te, gahapati, esā vācā – ‘sacce ahaṃ, bhante, patiṭṭhāya mantessāmi; hotu no ettha kathāsallāpo’”ti.

“Attend closely, householder, and having attended closely, then reply. Your earlier and later statements do not cohere, nor does the later with the earlier. Yet, householder, this statement was made by you: ‘Venerable sir, I shall discuss this having taken my stand on truth; let there be a conversation between us here.’”

66. “Purimenevāhaṃ[M 2.0042], bhante, opammena bhagavato attamano abhiraddho. Api cāhaṃ imāni bhagavato vicitrāni pañhapaṭibhānāni sotukāmo, evāhaṃ bhagavantaṃ paccanīkaṃ kātabbaṃ amaññissaṃ. Abhikkantaṃ, bhante, abhikkantaṃ, bhante! Seyyathāpi, bhante, nikkujjitaṃ vā ukkujjeyya, paṭicchannaṃ vā vivareyya, mūḷhassa vā maggaṃ ācikkheyya, andhakāre vā telapajjotaṃ dhāreyya – cakkhumanto rūpāni dakkhantīti; evamevaṃ bhagavatā anekapariyāyena dhammo pakāsito. Esāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavantaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāmi dhammañca [P 1.0379] bhikkhusaṅghañca. Upāsakaṃ maṃ bhagavā dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṃ saraṇaṃ gata”nti.

66. “Venerable sir, I was already pleased and delighted by the Blessed One’s first simile. But as I was eager to hear these diverse and brilliant answers to questions from the Blessed One, I thought it right to oppose the Blessed One. Excellent, venerable sir, excellent! It is as if one were to set upright what was overturned, to reveal what was hidden, to show the way to one who was lost, or to hold a lamp in the dark so that those with eyes could see forms. In that very same way, the Dhamma has been made clear by the Blessed One in numerous ways. I go to the Blessed One for refuge, to the Dhamma, and to the Saṅgha of bhikkhus. May the Blessed One remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life, from this day forward.”

67. “Anuviccakāraṃ kho, gahapati, karohi, anuviccakāro tumhādisānaṃ [T 2.0066] ñātamanussānaṃ sādhu hotī”ti. “Imināpāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavato bhiyyosomattāya attamano abhiraddho yaṃ maṃ bhagavā evamāha – ‘anuviccakāraṃ kho, gahapati, karohi, anuviccakāro tumhādisānaṃ ñātamanussānaṃ sādhu hotī’ti. Mañhi, bhante, aññatitthiyā sāvakaṃ labhitvā kevalakappaṃ nāḷandaṃ paṭākaṃ parihareyyuṃ – ‘upāli amhākaṃ gahapati sāvakattaṃ upagato’ti. Atha ca pana maṃ bhagavā evamāha – ‘anuviccakāraṃ kho, gahapati, karohi, anuviccakāro tumhādisānaṃ ñātamanussānaṃ sādhu hotī’ti. Esāhaṃ, bhante, dutiyampi bhagavantaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāmi dhammañca bhikkhusaṅghañca. Upāsakaṃ maṃ bhagavā dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṃ saraṇaṃ gata”nti.

67. “Householder, make an investigation. Making an investigation is good for well-known people like you.” “Venerable sir, by this, I am even more delighted and gratified toward the Blessed One, that the Blessed One said to me: ‘Householder, make an investigation. Making an investigation is good for well-known people like you.’ For, venerable sir, if the followers of other sects were to gain me as a disciple, they would carry a banner all over Nāḷanda, proclaiming: ‘Upāli the householder has come over to our discipleship!’ But the Blessed One tells me: ‘Householder, make an investigation. Making an investigation is good for well-known people like you.’ And so, venerable sir, for the second time, I go for refuge to the Blessed One, to the Dhamma, and to the Saṅgha of bhikkhus. May the Blessed One remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge from this day forth, for as long as life lasts.”

68. “Dīgharattaṃ kho te, gahapati, nigaṇṭhānaṃ opānabhūtaṃ kulaṃ yena nesaṃ upagatānaṃ piṇḍakaṃ dātabbaṃ maññeyyāsī”ti. “Imināpāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavato bhiyyosomattāya attamano [V 2.0049] abhiraddho yaṃ maṃ bhagavā evamāha – ‘dīgharattaṃ kho te, gahapati, nigaṇṭhānaṃ opānabhūtaṃ kulaṃ yena nesaṃ upagatānaṃ piṇḍakaṃ dātabbaṃ maññeyyāsī’ti. Sutaṃ metaṃ, bhante, samaṇo gotamo evamāha – ‘mayhameva dānaṃ dātabbaṃ, nāññesaṃ dānaṃ dātabbaṃ; mayhameva sāvakānaṃ dānaṃ dātabbaṃ, nāññesaṃ sāvakānaṃ dānaṃ dātabbaṃ; mayhameva dinnaṃ mahapphalaṃ, nāññesaṃ dinnaṃ mahapphalaṃ; mayhameva sāvakānaṃ [T 2.0067] dinnaṃ mahapphalaṃ, nāññesaṃ sāvakānaṃ dinnaṃ mahapphala’nti. Atha ca pana maṃ bhagavā nigaṇṭhesupi dāne samādapeti. Api ca, bhante, mayamettha kālaṃ jānissāma. Esāhaṃ, bhante, tatiyampi bhagavantaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāmi dhammañca bhikkhusaṅghañca. Upāsakaṃ maṃ bhagavā dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṃ saraṇaṃ gata”nti.

68. “Householder, for a long time your family has been like a watering place for the Nigaṇṭhas, so you should consider that almsfood should be given to them when they come.” “Venerable sir, by this, I am even more delighted and gratified toward the Blessed One, that the Blessed One said to me: ‘Householder, for a long time your family has been like a watering place for the Nigaṇṭhas, so you should consider that almsfood should be given to them when they come.’ For I have heard, venerable sir, that the recluse Gotama says: ‘Gifts should be given to me alone, not to others; gifts should be given to my disciples alone, not to the disciples of others; what is given to me alone is of great fruit, what is given to others is not of great fruit; what is given to my disciples alone is of great fruit, what is given to the disciples of others is not of great fruit.’ Yet the Blessed One encourages me to give to the Nigaṇṭhas as well. But, venerable sir, we will know the proper time for this. And so, venerable sir, for the third time, I go for refuge to the Blessed One, to the Dhamma, and to the Saṅgha of bhikkhus. May the Blessed One remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge from this day forth, for as long as life lasts.”

69. Atha [M 2.0043] kho bhagavā upālissa gahapatissa anupubbiṃ kathaṃ ānupubbīkathaṃ (sī.), ānupubbikathaṃ (pī.), anupubbikathaṃ (syā. kaṃ. ka.) kathesi, seyyathidaṃ – dānakathaṃ sīlakathaṃ saggakathaṃ, kāmānaṃ ādīnavaṃ okāraṃ saṃkilesaṃ, nekkhamme ānisaṃsaṃ pakāsesi. Yadā bhagavā aññāsi upāliṃ gahapatiṃ kallacittaṃ [P 1.0380] muducittaṃ vinīvaraṇacittaṃ udaggacittaṃ pasannacittaṃ, atha yā buddhānaṃ sāmukkaṃsikā dhammadesanā taṃ pakāsesi – dukkhaṃ, samudayaṃ, nirodhaṃ, maggaṃ. Seyyathāpi nāma suddhaṃ vatthaṃ apagatakāḷakaṃ sammadeva rajanaṃ paṭiggaṇheyya, evameva upālissa gahapatissa tasmiṃyeva āsane virajaṃ vītamalaṃ dhammacakkhuṃ udapādi – ‘yaṃ kiñci samudayadhammaṃ sabbaṃ taṃ nirodhadhamma’nti. Atha kho upāli gahapati diṭṭhadhammo pattadhammo viditadhammo pariyogāḷhadhammo tiṇṇavicikiccho vigatakathaṃkatho vesārajjappatto aparappaccayo satthusāsane bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “handa ca dāni mayaṃ, bhante, gacchāma, bahukiccā mayaṃ bahukaraṇīyā”ti. “Yassadāni tvaṃ, gahapati, kālaṃ maññasī”ti.

69. Then the Blessed One gave householder Upāli a progressive discourse, that is, a talk on generosity, on morality, on heaven; he explained the danger, degradation, and defilement of sensual pleasures, and the benefits of renunciation. When the Blessed One knew that householder Upāli's mind was ready, pliable, free from hindrances, uplifted, and confident, he revealed the teaching unique to the Buddhas: suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path. Just as a clean cloth free from stains would properly absorb dye, so too in that very seat the dust-free, stainless vision of the Dhamma arose in householder Upāli: ‘Whatever is subject to arising is all subject to cessation.’ Then householder Upāli, having seen the Dhamma, attained the Dhamma, known the Dhamma, plunged into the Dhamma, crossed over doubt, dispelled uncertainty, gained assurance, and become independent of others in the Teacher’s dispensation, said to the Blessed One: “Now, venerable sir, we wish to depart. We have much to do and many duties.” “You may go, householder, when you think it is time.”

70. Atha kho upāli gahapati bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinanditvā anumoditvā [T 2.0068] uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā yena sakaṃ nivesanaṃ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā dovārikaṃ āmantesi – “ajjatagge, samma dovārika, āvarāmi dvāraṃ nigaṇṭhānaṃ nigaṇṭhīnaṃ, anāvaṭaṃ dvāraṃ bhagavato bhikkhūnaṃ bhikkhunīnaṃ upāsakānaṃ upāsikānaṃ. Sace koci nigaṇṭho āgacchati tamenaṃ tvaṃ evaṃ vadeyyāsi – ‘tiṭṭha, bhante, mā pāvisi. Ajjatagge upāli gahapati samaṇassa gotamassa sāvakattaṃ upagato. Āvaṭaṃ dvāraṃ nigaṇṭhānaṃ nigaṇṭhīnaṃ, anāvaṭaṃ dvāraṃ bhagavato bhikkhūnaṃ bhikkhunīnaṃ upāsakānaṃ upāsikānaṃ[V 2.0050]. Sace te, bhante, piṇḍakena attho, ettheva tiṭṭha, ettheva te āharissantī’”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho dovāriko upālissa gahapatissa paccassosi.

70. Then the householder Upāli, having delighted in and approved the Blessed One’s discourse, rose from his seat, paid homage to the Blessed One, and circumambulated him clockwise. He then went to his own residence. Arriving there, he addressed the gatekeeper: “From today onward, good gatekeeper, I close the door to the Nigaṇṭhas and Nigaṇṭhīs; the door is open to the Blessed One, his monks and nuns, and his male and female lay followers. If any Nigaṇṭha comes, you should say to him: ‘Wait, venerable sir, do not enter. From today onward, the householder Upāli has become a disciple of the ascetic Gotama. The door is closed to the Nigaṇṭhas and Nigaṇṭhīs, but open to the Blessed One, his monks and nuns, and his male and female lay followers. If you, venerable sir, need alms, just wait here, and they will bring them to you.’” “Yes, venerable sir,” the gatekeeper replied to the householder Upāli.

71. Assosi kho dīghatapassī nigaṇṭho – “upāli kira gahapati samaṇassa gotamassa sāvakattaṃ upagato”ti. Atha kho dīghatapassī nigaṇṭho yena nigaṇṭho nāṭaputto tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā nigaṇṭhaṃ nāṭaputtaṃ etadavoca – “sutaṃ metaṃ, bhante, upāli kira gahapati samaṇassa gotamassa sāvakattaṃ upagato”ti. “Aṭṭhānaṃ kho etaṃ, tapassi[M 2.0044], anavakāso yaṃ upāli gahapati samaṇassa gotamassa sāvakattaṃ upagaccheyya. Ṭhānañca kho etaṃ vijjati yaṃ samaṇo gotamo upālissa gahapatissa sāvakattaṃ upagaccheyyā”ti[P 1.0381]. Dutiyampi kho dīghatapassī nigaṇṭho…pe… tatiyampi kho dīghatapassī nigaṇṭho nigaṇṭhaṃ nāṭaputtaṃ etadavoca – “sutaṃ metaṃ, bhante [T 2.0069] …pe… upālissa gahapatissa sāvakattaṃ upagaccheyyā”ti. “Handāhaṃ, bhante, gacchāmi yāva jānāmi yadi vā upāli gahapati samaṇassa gotamassa sāvakattaṃ upagato yadi vā no”ti. “Gaccha tvaṃ, tapassi, jānāhi yadi vā upāli gahapati samaṇassa gotamassa sāvakattaṃ upagato yadi vā no”ti.

71. The Nigaṇṭha Dīghatapassī heard: "The householder Upāli, it is said, has gone over to the discipleship of the ascetic Gotama." Then the Nigaṇṭha Dīghatapassī approached the Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta. Having approached, he said this to the Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta: "Venerable sir, I have heard this: the householder Upāli, it is said, has gone over to the discipleship of the ascetic Gotama." "This is impossible, Tapassi, it is not a possibility that the householder Upāli would go over to the discipleship of the ascetic Gotama. But this is a possibility: that the ascetic Gotama would go over to the discipleship of the householder Upāli." A second time... and a third time the Nigaṇṭha Dīghatapassī said this to the Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta: "Venerable sir, I have heard this... that the ascetic Gotama would go over to the discipleship of the householder Upāli." "Now, venerable sir, I shall go to find out whether the householder Upāli has gone over to the discipleship of the ascetic Gotama or not." "Go, Tapassi, and find out whether the householder Upāli has gone over to the discipleship of the ascetic Gotama or not."

72. Atha kho dīghatapassī nigaṇṭho yena upālissa gahapatissa nivesanaṃ tenupasaṅkami. Addasā kho dovāriko dīghatapassiṃ nigaṇṭhaṃ dūratova āgacchantaṃ. Disvāna dīghatapassiṃ nigaṇṭhaṃ etadavoca – “tiṭṭha, bhante, mā pāvisi. Ajjatagge upāli gahapati samaṇassa gotamassa sāvakattaṃ upagato. Āvaṭaṃ dvāraṃ nigaṇṭhānaṃ nigaṇṭhīnaṃ, anāvaṭaṃ dvāraṃ bhagavato bhikkhūnaṃ bhikkhunīnaṃ upāsakānaṃ upāsikānaṃ[T 2.0070]. Sace te, bhante, piṇḍakena attho, ettheva tiṭṭha, ettheva te āharissantī”ti. “Na me, āvuso, piṇḍakena attho”ti vatvā tato paṭinivattitvā yena nigaṇṭho nāṭaputto tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā nigaṇṭhaṃ nāṭaputtaṃ etadavoca – “saccaṃyeva kho, bhante, yaṃ upāli gahapati samaṇassa gotamassa sāvakattaṃ upagato. Etaṃ kho te ahaṃ, bhante, nālatthaṃ na kho me, bhante, ruccati yaṃ upāli gahapati samaṇassa gotamassa vādaṃ āropeyya. Samaṇo hi, bhante, gotamo māyāvī āvaṭṭaniṃ māyaṃ jānāti yāya aññatitthiyānaṃ sāvake āvaṭṭetīti. Āvaṭṭo kho te, bhante, upāli gahapati samaṇena gotamena āvaṭṭaniyā māyāyā”ti. “Aṭṭhānaṃ kho etaṃ, tapassi, anavakāso [V 2.0051] yaṃ upāli gahapati samaṇassa gotamassa sāvakattaṃ upagaccheyya. Ṭhānañca kho etaṃ vijjati yaṃ samaṇo gotamo upālissa gahapatissa sāvakattaṃ upagaccheyyā”ti. Dutiyampi kho dīghatapassī nigaṇṭho nigaṇṭhaṃ nāṭaputtaṃ etadavoca – “saccaṃyeva, bhante…pe… [T 2.0071] upālissa gahapatissa sāvakattaṃ upagaccheyyā”ti. Tatiyampi kho dīghatapassī nigaṇṭho nigaṇṭhaṃ nāṭaputtaṃ etadavoca – “saccaṃyeva kho, bhante…pe… [P 1.0382] upālissa gahapatissa sāvakattaṃ upagaccheyyā”ti. “Handa cāhaṃ[M 2.0045], tapassi, gacchāmi yāva cāhaṃ sāmaṃyeva jānāmi yadi vā upāli gahapati samaṇassa gotamassa sāvakattaṃ upagato yadi vā no”ti.

72. Then the Nigaṇṭha Dīghatapassī approached the residence of the householder Upāli. The gatekeeper saw the Nigaṇṭha Dīghatapassī coming from afar. Having seen him, the gatekeeper said this to the Nigaṇṭha Dīghatapassī: "Stop, venerable sir, do not enter. From today onward, the householder Upāli has gone over to the discipleship of the ascetic Gotama. The door is closed to male Nigaṇṭhas and female Nigaṇṭhīs; the door is open to the Blessed One’s monks and nuns, and his male and female lay disciples. If you, venerable sir, have need of alms-food, stand right here, and they will bring it to you right here." "I have no need of alms-food, friend." Having said this, he turned back from there and approached the Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta. Having approached, he said this to the Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta: "It is indeed true, venerable sir, that the householder Upāli has gone over to the discipleship of the ascetic Gotama. I was unable to persuade you in this matter, venerable sir. It did not seem right to me, venerable sir, that the householder Upāli should challenge the teaching of the ascetic Gotama. For, venerable sir, the ascetic Gotama is a magician; he knows the converting magic by which he wins over the disciples of other teachers. Indeed, venerable sir, your householder Upāli has been won over by the ascetic Gotama with his converting magic." "This is impossible, Tapassi, it is not a possibility that the householder Upāli would go over to the discipleship of the ascetic Gotama. But this is a possibility: that the ascetic Gotama would go over to the discipleship of the householder Upāli." A second time... and a third time the Nigaṇṭha Dīghatapassī said this to the Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta: "It is indeed true, venerable sir... that the ascetic Gotama would go over to the discipleship of the householder Upāli." "Now, Tapassi, I shall go and find out for myself whether the householder Upāli has gone over to the discipleship of the ascetic Gotama or not."

Atha kho nigaṇṭho nāṭaputto mahatiyā nigaṇṭhaparisāya saddhiṃ yena upālissa gahapatissa nivesanaṃ tenupasaṅkami. Addasā kho dovāriko nigaṇṭhaṃ nāṭaputtaṃ dūratova āgacchantaṃ. Disvāna nigaṇṭhaṃ nāṭaputtaṃ etadavoca – “tiṭṭha, bhante, mā pāvisi. Ajjatagge upāli gahapati samaṇassa gotamassa sāvakattaṃ upagato. Āvaṭaṃ dvāraṃ nigaṇṭhānaṃ nigaṇṭhīnaṃ, anāvaṭaṃ dvāraṃ bhagavato bhikkhūnaṃ bhikkhunīnaṃ upāsakānaṃ upāsikānaṃ. Sace te, bhante, piṇḍakena attho, ettheva tiṭṭha, ettheva te āharissantī”ti. “Tena hi, samma dovārika, yena upāli gahapati tenupasaṅkama; upasaṅkamitvā upāliṃ gahapatiṃ evaṃ vadehi – ‘nigaṇṭho, bhante, nāṭaputto mahatiyā nigaṇṭhaparisāya saddhiṃ bahidvārakoṭṭhake ṭhito; so te dassanakāmo’”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho dovāriko nigaṇṭhassa nāṭaputtassa paṭissutvā yena upāli gahapati tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā upāliṃ gahapatiṃ etadavoca – “nigaṇṭho, bhante, nāṭaputto mahatiyā nigaṇṭhaparisāya saddhiṃ [T 2.0072] bahidvārakoṭṭhake ṭhito; so te dassanakāmo”ti. “Tena hi, samma dovārika, majjhimāya dvārasālāya āsanāni paññapehī”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho dovāriko upālissa gahapatissa paṭissutvā majjhimāya dvārasālāya āsanāni paññapetvā yena upāli gahapati tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā upāliṃ gahapatiṃ etadavoca – “paññattāni kho, bhante, majjhimāya dvārasālāya āsanāni. Yassadāni kālaṃ maññasī”ti.

Then the Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta, together with a large assembly of Nigaṇṭhas, approached the residence of the householder Upāli. The gatekeeper saw the Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta coming from afar. Having seen him, the gatekeeper said this to the Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta: "Stop, venerable sir, do not enter. From today onward, the householder Upāli has gone over to the discipleship of the ascetic Gotama. The door is closed to male Nigaṇṭhas and female Nigaṇṭhīs; the door is open to the Blessed One’s monks and nuns, and his male and female lay disciples. If you, venerable sir, have need of alms-food, stand right here, and they will bring it to you right here." "In that case, friend gatekeeper, approach the householder Upāli. Having approached, say this to the householder Upāli: 'Venerable sir, the Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta is standing at the outer gatehouse with a large assembly of Nigaṇṭhas; he desires to see you.'" "Very well, venerable sir," the gatekeeper replied to the Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta. He then approached the householder Upāli. Having approached, he said this to the householder Upāli: "Venerable sir, the Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta is standing at the outer gatehouse with a large assembly of Nigaṇṭhas; he desires to see you." "In that case, friend gatekeeper, prepare seats in the hall of the middle gate." "Very well, venerable sir," the gatekeeper replied to the householder Upāli. Having prepared seats in the hall of the middle gate, he approached the householder Upāli. Having approached, he said this to the householder Upāli: "Venerable sir, the seats have been prepared in the hall of the middle gate. You may now proceed when you deem it is time."

73. Atha kho upāli gahapati yena majjhimā [P 1.0383] dvārasālā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā yaṃ tattha āsanaṃ aggañca seṭṭhañca uttamañca paṇītañca tattha sāmaṃ nisīditvā dovārikaṃ āmantesi [V 2.0052] – “tena hi, samma dovārika, yena nigaṇṭho nāṭaputto tenupasaṅkama; upasaṅkamitvā nigaṇṭhaṃ nāṭaputtaṃ evaṃ vadehi – ‘upāli, bhante, gahapati evamāha – pavisa kira, bhante, sace ākaṅkhasī’”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho dovāriko upālissa gahapatissa paṭissutvā yena nigaṇṭho nāṭaputto tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā nigaṇṭhaṃ nāṭaputtaṃ etadavoca – “upāli, bhante, gahapati evamāha – ‘pavisa kira, bhante, sace ākaṅkhasī’”ti. Atha [M 2.0046] kho nigaṇṭho nāṭaputto mahatiyā nigaṇṭhaparisāya saddhiṃ yena majjhimā dvārasālā tenupasaṅkami. Atha kho upāli gahapati – yaṃ sudaṃ pubbe yato passati nigaṇṭhaṃ nāṭaputtaṃ dūratova āgacchantaṃ disvāna tato paccuggantvā yaṃ tattha āsanaṃ aggañca seṭṭhañca uttamañca paṇītañca taṃ uttarāsaṅgena [T 2.0073] sammajjitvā pamajjitvā (sī. pī.) pariggahetvā nisīdāpeti so – dāni yaṃ tattha āsanaṃ aggañca seṭṭhañca uttamañca paṇītañca tattha sāmaṃ nisīditvā nigaṇṭhaṃ nāṭaputtaṃ etadavoca – “saṃvijjanti kho, bhante, āsanāni; sace ākaṅkhasi, nisīdā”ti. Evaṃ vutte, nigaṇṭho nāṭaputto upāliṃ gahapatiṃ etadavoca – “ummattosi tvaṃ, gahapati, dattosi tvaṃ, gahapati! ‘Gacchāmahaṃ, bhante, samaṇassa gotamassa vādaṃ āropessāmī’ti gantvā mahatāsi vādasaṅghāṭena paṭimukko āgato. Seyyathāpi, gahapati, puriso aṇḍahārako gantvā ubbhatehi aṇḍehi āgaccheyya, seyyathā vā pana gahapati puriso akkhikahārako gantvā ubbhatehi akkhīhi āgaccheyya; evameva kho tvaṃ, gahapati, ‘gacchāmahaṃ, bhante, samaṇassa gotamassa vādaṃ āropessāmī’ti gantvā mahatāsi vādasaṅghāṭena paṭimukko āgato. Āvaṭṭosi kho tvaṃ, gahapati, samaṇena gotamena āvaṭṭaniyā māyāyā”ti.

73. Then the householder Upāli approached the middle gate-hall. Having approached, he himself sat down on the seat that was the foremost, the best, the supreme, and the most excellent, and addressed the gatekeeper: “Well then, good gatekeeper, go to where the Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta is. Having approached, say this to the Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta: ‘Venerable sir, the householder Upāli says this: “Please enter, venerable sir, if you wish.”’” “Yes, venerable sir,” the gatekeeper replied to the householder Upāli. He then went to where the Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta was and said this: “Venerable sir, the householder Upāli says this: ‘Please enter, venerable sir, if you wish.’” Then the Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta, together with a great assembly of Nigaṇṭhas, approached the middle gate-hall. Now, the householder Upāli—who previously, whenever he saw the Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta coming from afar, would go out to meet him, and having wiped the seat there that was the foremost, the best, the supreme, and the most excellent with his upper robe, and having taken it up, would have him sit—now himself sat on that seat there that was the foremost, the best, the supreme, and the most excellent, and said this to the Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta: “Venerable sir, seats are available; if you wish, please sit down.” When this was said, the Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta said this to the householder Upāli: “You are mad, householder! You are foolish, householder! Having gone saying, ‘I shall go, venerable sir, and bring a charge against the ascetic Gotama’s teaching,’ you have returned enveloped by a great mass of teaching. Just as, householder, a man who goes to fetch testicles might return with his testicles removed, or as, householder, a man who goes to fetch eyes might return with his eyes plucked out; even so, householder, having gone saying, ‘I shall go, venerable sir, and bring a charge against the ascetic Gotama’s teaching,’ you have returned enveloped by a great mass of teaching. You have been converted, householder, by the ascetic Gotama with his converting magic!”

74. “Bhaddikā, bhante, āvaṭṭanī māyā; kalyāṇī, bhante, āvaṭṭanī māyā; piyā me, bhante, ñātisālohitā imāya āvaṭṭaniyā āvaṭṭeyyuṃ; piyānampi me assa ñātisālohitānaṃ dīgharattaṃ hitāya sukhāya; sabbe cepi, bhante, khattiyā imāya āvaṭṭaniyā āvaṭṭeyyuṃ; sabbesānampissa khattiyānaṃ dīgharattaṃ hitāya [P 1.0384] sukhāya; sabbe cepi, bhante, brāhmaṇā…pe… vessā…pe… suddā imāya āvaṭṭaniyā āvaṭṭeyyuṃ; sabbesānampissa suddānaṃ [T 2.0074] dīgharattaṃ hitāya sukhāya; sadevako cepi, bhante, loko samārako sabrahmako sassamaṇabrāhmaṇī pajā sadevamanussā imāya āvaṭṭaniyā āvaṭṭeyyuṃ; sadevakassapissa lokassa samārakassa sabrahmakassa sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiyā [V 2.0053] pajāya sadevamanussāya dīgharattaṃ hitāya sukhāyāti. Tena hi, bhante, upamaṃ te karissāmi. Upamāya pidhekacce viññū purisā bhāsitassa atthaṃ ājānanti.

74. “Venerable sir, this converting magic is good; venerable sir, this converting magic is excellent. May my dear kinsmen and relatives be converted by this converting magic; it would be for the long-term welfare and happiness of my dear kinsmen and relatives. If all the nobles, venerable sir, were to be converted by this converting magic, it would be for the long-term welfare and happiness of all those nobles. If all the brahmins… the merchants… the commoners, venerable sir, were to be converted by this converting magic, it would be for the long-term welfare and happiness of all those commoners. If this world with its devas, Māra, and Brahmā, this generation with its ascetics and brahmins, devas and humans, venerable sir, were to be converted by this converting magic, it would be for the long-term welfare and happiness of this world with its devas, Māra, and Brahmā, this generation with its ascetics and brahmins, devas and humans. Therefore, venerable sir, I will give you a simile. For by a simile, some intelligent persons in this world understand the meaning of what has been said.”

75. “Bhūtapubbaṃ[M 2.0047], bhante, aññatarassa brāhmaṇassa jiṇṇassa vuḍḍhassa mahallakassa daharā māṇavikā pajāpatī ahosi gabbhinī upavijaññā. Atha kho, bhante, sā māṇavikā taṃ brāhmaṇaṃ etadavoca – ‘gaccha tvaṃ, brāhmaṇa, āpaṇā makkaṭacchāpakaṃ kiṇitvā ānehi, yo me kumārakassa kīḷāpanako bhavissatī’ti. Evaṃ vutte, so brāhmaṇo taṃ māṇavikaṃ etadavoca – ‘āgamehi tāva, bhoti, yāva vijāyati. Sace tvaṃ, bhoti, kumārakaṃ vijāyissasi, tassā te ahaṃ āpaṇā makkaṭacchāpakaṃ kiṇitvā ānessāmi, yo te kumārakassa kīḷāpanako bhavissati. Sace pana tvaṃ, bhoti, kumārikaṃ vijāyissasi, tassā te ahaṃ āpaṇā makkaṭacchāpikaṃ kiṇitvā ānessāmi, yā te kumārikāya kīḷāpanikā bhavissatī’ti. Dutiyampi kho, bhante, sā māṇavikā…pe… [T 2.0075] tatiyampi kho, bhante, sā māṇavikā taṃ brāhmaṇaṃ etadavoca – ‘gaccha tvaṃ, brāhmaṇa, āpaṇā makkaṭacchāpakaṃ kiṇitvā ānehi, yo me kumārakassa kīḷāpanako bhavissatī’ti. Atha kho, bhante, so brāhmaṇo tassā māṇavikāya sāratto paṭibaddhacitto āpaṇā makkaṭacchāpakaṃ kiṇitvā ānetvā taṃ māṇavikaṃ etadavoca – ‘ayaṃ te, bhoti, āpaṇā makkaṭacchāpako [P 1.0385] kiṇitvā ānīto, yo te kumārakassa kīḷāpanako bhavissatī’ti. Evaṃ vutte, bhante, sā māṇavikā taṃ brāhmaṇaṃ etadavoca – ‘gaccha tvaṃ, brāhmaṇa, imaṃ makkaṭacchāpakaṃ ādāya yena rattapāṇi rajataputto tenupasaṅkama; upasaṅkamitvā rattapāṇiṃ rajakaputtaṃ evaṃ vadehi – icchāmahaṃ, samma rattapāṇi, imaṃ makkaṭacchāpakaṃ pītāvalepanaṃ nāma raṅgajātaṃ rajitaṃ ākoṭitapaccākoṭitaṃ ubhatobhāgavimaṭṭha’nti.

75. “Once upon a time, venerable sir, there was a certain brahmin who was decrepit, aged, and advanced in years. His young wife, a maiden, was pregnant and about to give birth. Then, venerable sir, that young woman said this to the brahmin: ‘Go, brahmin, buy a young monkey from the market and bring it here, which will be a plaything for my son.’ When this was said, that brahmin said this to the young woman: ‘Wait, madam, until you give birth. If, madam, you give birth to a boy, I will buy a young male monkey from the market and bring it for him, which will be a plaything for your son. But if, madam, you give birth to a girl, I will buy a young female monkey from the market and bring it for her, which will be a plaything for your daughter.’ A second time, venerable sir, that young woman… and a third time, venerable sir, that young woman said this to the brahmin: ‘Go, brahmin, buy a young monkey from the market and bring it here, which will be a plaything for my son.’ Then, venerable sir, that brahmin, being infatuated with and his mind bound to that young woman, bought a young monkey from the market, brought it, and said this to the young woman: ‘Here, madam, is the young monkey bought from the market and brought for you, which will be a plaything for your son.’ When this was said, venerable sir, that young woman said this to the brahmin: ‘Go, brahmin, take this young monkey and approach Rattapāṇi, the dyer’s son. Having approached, say this to Rattapāṇi, the dyer’s son: “Friend Rattapāṇi, I wish to have this young monkey dyed with a kind of dye called ‘yellow-ointment,’ beaten and re-beaten, and smoothed on both sides.”’”

“Atha kho, bhante, so brāhmaṇo tassā māṇavikāya sāratto paṭibaddhacitto taṃ makkaṭacchāpakaṃ ādāya yena rattapāṇi [T 2.0076] rajakaputto tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā rattapāṇiṃ rajakaputtaṃ etadavoca – ‘icchāmahaṃ, samma rattapāṇi, imaṃ makkaṭacchāpakaṃ pītāvalepanaṃ nāma raṅgajātaṃ rajitaṃ ākoṭitapaccākoṭitaṃ ubhatobhāgavimaṭṭha’nti. Evaṃ vutte, bhante, rattapāṇi rajakaputto taṃ brāhmaṇaṃ etadavoca – ‘ayaṃ kho te, makkaṭacchāpako raṅgakkhamo hi kho, no ākoṭanakkhamo[V 2.0054], no vimajjanakkhamo’ti. Evameva kho, bhante, bālānaṃ nigaṇṭhānaṃ vādo raṅgakkhamo [M 2.0048] hi kho bālānaṃ no paṇḍitānaṃ, no anuyogakkhamo, no vimajjanakkhamo. Atha kho, bhante, so brāhmaṇo aparena samayena navaṃ dussayugaṃ ādāya yena rattapāṇi rajakaputto tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā rattapāṇiṃ rajakaputtaṃ etadavoca – ‘icchāmahaṃ, samma rattapāṇi, imaṃ navaṃ dussayugaṃ pītāvalepanaṃ nāma raṅgajātaṃ rajitaṃ ākoṭitapaccākoṭitaṃ ubhatobhāgavimaṭṭha’nti. Evaṃ vutte, bhante, rattapāṇi rajakaputto taṃ brāhmaṇaṃ etadavoca – ‘idaṃ kho te, bhante, navaṃ dussayugaṃ raṅgakkhamañceva ākoṭanakkhamañca vimajjanakkhamañcā’ti. Evameva kho, bhante, tassa bhagavato vādo arahato sammāsambuddhassa raṅgakkhamo ceva paṇḍitānaṃ no bālānaṃ, anuyogakkhamo ca vimajjanakkhamo cā”ti.

“Then, venerable sir, that brahmin, infatuated and with his mind attached to that maiden, took that young monkey and approached Rattapāṇi the dyer’s son. Having approached, he said this to Rattapāṇi the dyer’s son: ‘Friend Rattapāṇi, I wish to have this young monkey dyed with the kind of dye called Pītāvalepana, beaten and re-beaten, and rubbed on both sides.’ When this was said, venerable sir, Rattapāṇi the dyer’s son said this to that brahmin: ‘This young monkey of yours, sir, is indeed fit for dyeing, but it is not fit for beating, nor is it fit for rubbing.’ Just so, venerable sir, the doctrine of the foolish Nigaṇṭhas is fit for the infatuation of fools, but not of the wise; it is not fit for repeated application, nor is it fit for examination. Then, venerable sir, that brahmin on another occasion took a new pair of cloths and approached Rattapāṇi the dyer’s son. Having approached, he said this to Rattapāṇi the dyer’s son: ‘Friend Rattapāṇi, I wish to have this new pair of cloths dyed with the kind of dye called Pītāvalepana, beaten and re-beaten, and rubbed on both sides.’ When this was said, venerable sir, Rattapāṇi the dyer’s son said this to that brahmin: ‘This new pair of cloths of yours, venerable sir, is fit for dyeing, fit for beating, and fit for rubbing.’ Just so, venerable sir, the doctrine of that Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, is fit for the appreciation of the wise, not of fools, and it is fit for repeated application and fit for examination.”

“Sarājikā kho, gahapati, parisā evaṃ jānāti – ‘upāli gahapati nigaṇṭhassa nāṭaputtassa sāvako’ti. Kassa taṃ, gahapati, sāvakaṃ dhāremā”ti? Evaṃ [T 2.0077] vutte, upāli gahapati uṭṭhāyāsanā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā yena bhagavā tenañjaliṃ [P 1.0386] paṇāmetvā nigaṇṭhaṃ nāṭaputtaṃ etadavoca – “tena hi, bhante, suṇohi yassāhaṃ sāvako”ti –

“Householder, the assembly including the king knows this: ‘The householder Upāli is a disciple of Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta.’ As whose disciple, householder, should we regard you?” When this was said, the householder Upāli rose from his seat, arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, extended his joined hands in reverence toward the Blessed One, and said this to Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta: “Well then, venerable sir, listen to whose disciple I am.”

76.

76.

“Dhīrassa vigatamohassa, pabhinnakhīlassa vijitavijayassa;

Anīghassa susamacittassa, vuddhasīlassa sādhupaññassa;

Vesamantarassa vessantarassa (sī. pī.) vimalassa, bhagavato tassa sāvakohamasmi.

“I am a disciple of that Blessed One, the wise, who is free from delusion, who has destroyed the heart's barrenness, the completely victorious one; who is untroubled, with a perfectly balanced mind, consummate in virtue, of excellent wisdom; who has transcended all unevenness, the stainless one.”

“Akathaṃkathissa tusitassa, vantalokāmisassa muditassa;

Katasamaṇassa manujassa, antimasārīrassa narassa;

Anopamassa virajassa, bhagavato tassa sāvakohamasmi.

“I am a disciple of that Blessed One, who is free from doubt, contented, who has disgorged worldly bait, who is joyful; the perfected recluse, the unique being, the noble man, who bears his final body; the incomparable one, free from dust.”

“Asaṃsayassa kusalassa, venayikassa sārathivarassa;

Anuttarassa ruciradhammassa, nikkaṅkhassa pabhāsakassa pabhāsakarassa (sī. syā. pī.);

Mānacchidassa vīrassa, bhagavato tassa sāvakohamasmi.

“I am a disciple of that Blessed One, who is free from doubt, the skilled one, the guide, the supreme charioteer; the unsurpassed, of splendid Dhamma, free from uncertainty, the illuminator; the cutter of conceit, the hero.”

“Nisabhassa [V 2.0055] appameyyassa, gambhīrassa monapattassa;

Khemaṅkarassa vedassa, dhammaṭṭhassa saṃvutattassa;

Saṅgātigassa muttassa, bhagavato tassa sāvakohamasmi.

“I am a disciple of that Blessed One, the bull among men, the immeasurable, the profound, who has attained sagehood; the maker of security, the knower, established in Dhamma, of restrained self; who has overcome attachment, the liberated one.”

“Nāgassa [M 2.0049] pantasenassa, khīṇasaṃyojanassa muttassa;

Paṭimantakassa paṭimantassa (ka.) dhonassa, pannadhajassa vītarāgassa;

Dantassa nippapañcassa, bhagavato tassa sāvakohamasmi.

“I am a disciple of that Blessed One, the sinless one, who resorts to seclusion, whose fetters are destroyed, the liberated one; the sagacious, the pure, with banner lowered, free from passion; the tamed, free from mental proliferation.”

“Isisattamassa akuhassa, tevijjassa brahmapattassa;

Nhātakassa nahātakassa (sī. syā. pī.) padakassa, passaddhassa viditavedassa;

Purindadassa sakkassa, bhagavato tassa sāvakohamasmi.

“I am a disciple of that Blessed One, the seventh of the seers, the undeceptive, possessor of the three true knowledges, who has attained the holy state; the one who has bathed away evil, the master of the path, the tranquil one, the foremost giver of the gift, the capable one.”

“Ariyassa bhāvitattassa, pattipattassa veyyākaraṇassa;

Satimato vipassissa, anabhinatassa no apanatassa;

Anejassa vasippattassa, bhagavato tassa sāvakohamasmi[T 2.0078].

“I am a disciple of that Blessed One, the noble one, of developed self, who has attained what is to be attained, the expounder; the mindful, the insightful, who is neither inclined nor disinclined; the imperturbable, who has attained mastery.”

“Samuggatassa sammaggatassa (sī. syā. pī.) jhāyissa, ananugatantarassa suddhassa;

Asitassa hitassa appahīnassa (sī. pī.), appabhītassa (syā.), pavivittassa aggappattassa;

Tiṇṇassa tārayantassa, bhagavato tassa sāvakohamasmi.

“I am a disciple of that Blessed One, the renowned, who has burned up defilements, with an unfettered mind, the pure; the unattached, the benefactor, the secluded, who has reached the supreme state; who has crossed over, who helps others to cross over.”

“Santassa bhūripaññassa, mahāpaññassa vītalobhassa;

Tathāgatassa sugatassa, appaṭipuggalassa asamassa;

Visāradassa nipuṇassa, bhagavato tassa sāvakohamasmi.

“I am a disciple of that Blessed One, the peaceful one, of vast wisdom, of great wisdom, free from greed; the Tathāgata, the Sugata, the peerless person, the unequalled; the confident, the subtle one.”

“Taṇhacchidassa buddhassa, vītadhūmassa anupalittassa;

Āhuneyyassa yakkhassa, uttamapuggalassa atulassa;

Mahato yasaggapattassa, bhagavato tassa sāvakohamasmī”ti.

“I am a disciple of that Blessed One, who has cut off craving, the Awakened One, who is free from smoke, unsmeared; worthy of offerings, a venerable being, the supreme person, the incomparable; the great one, who has reached the pinnacle of fame.”

77. “Kadā [V 2.0056] saññūḷhā pana te, gahapati, ime samaṇassa gotamassa vaṇṇā”ti? “Seyyathāpi, bhante, nānāpupphānaṃ mahāpuppharāsi[P 1.0387], tamenaṃ dakkho mālākāro vā mālākārantevāsī vā vicittaṃ mālaṃ gantheyya; evameva kho, bhante, so bhagavā anekavaṇṇo anekasatavaṇṇo. Ko hi, bhante, vaṇṇārahassa vaṇṇaṃ na karissatī”ti? Atha kho nigaṇṭhassa nāṭaputtassa bhagavato sakkāraṃ asahamānassa tattheva uṇhaṃ lohitaṃ mukhato uggacchīti uggañchi (sī. syā. pī.).

77. “But when, householder, were these praises of the ascetic Gotama composed by you?” “Venerable sir, it is just as a skilled garland-maker or his apprentice might string a variegated garland from a great heap of many kinds of flowers; even so, venerable sir, the Blessed One is of many qualities, of many hundreds of qualities. For who, venerable sir, would not speak the praise of one who is worthy of praise?” Then, unable to bear the reverence shown to the Blessed One, hot blood gushed from the mouth of Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta right there on the spot.

Upālisuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ chaṭṭhaṃ.

The Upāli Sutta, the sixth, is concluded.

7. Kukkuravatikasuttaṃ

7. The Discourse on the Dog-Duty Ascetic

78. Evaṃ [T 2.0079][M 2.0050][V 2.0057] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā koliyesu viharati haliddavasanaṃ nāma koliyānaṃ nigamo. Atha kho puṇṇo ca koliyaputto govatiko acelo ca seniyo kukkuravatiko yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā puṇṇo koliyaputto govatiko bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Acelo pana seniyo kukkuravatiko bhagavatā saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā kukkurova palikujjitvā palikuṇṭhitvā (syā. kaṃ.), paliguṇṭhitvā (ka.) ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho puṇṇo koliyaputto govatiko bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “ayaṃ[T 2.0080], bhante, acelo seniyo kukkuravatiko dukkarakārako chamānikkhittaṃ bhojanaṃ bhuñjati. Tassa taṃ kukkuravataṃ dīgharattaṃ samattaṃ samādinnaṃ. Tassa kā gati, ko abhisamparāyo”ti? “Alaṃ, puṇṇa, tiṭṭhatetaṃ; mā maṃ etaṃ pucchī”ti. Dutiyampi kho puṇṇo koliyaputto govatiko…pe… tatiyampi kho puṇṇo koliyaputto govatiko bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “ayaṃ, bhante, acelo seniyo kukkuravatiko dukkarakārako chamānikkhittaṃ bhojanaṃ bhuñjati. Tassa taṃ kukkuravataṃ dīgharattaṃ samattaṃ samādinnaṃ. Tassa kā gati, ko abhisamparāyo”ti?

78. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling among the Koliyans, in a Koliyan town named Haliddavasana. Then Puṇṇa, a son of the Koliyans who was a cow-duty ascetic, and Seniya, a naked dog-duty ascetic, approached the Blessed One. Having approached, Puṇṇa, the son of the Koliyans who was a cow-duty ascetic, paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Seniya the naked dog-duty ascetic, however, exchanged courteous greetings with the Blessed One. Having concluded their pleasant and memorable talk, he curled up like a dog and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, Puṇṇa, the son of the Koliyans who was a cow-duty ascetic, said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, this naked ascetic Seniya, the dog-duty ascetic, is a performer of difficult feats: he eats food that has been thrown on the ground. He has undertaken this dog-duty completely for a long time. What is his destination? What is his future state?” “Enough, Puṇṇa, let this be. Do not ask me this.” For a second time... and for a third time Puṇṇa, the son of the Koliyans who was a cow-duty ascetic, said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, this naked ascetic Seniya, the dog-duty ascetic, is a performer of difficult feats: he eats food that has been thrown on the ground. He has undertaken this dog-duty completely for a long time. What is his destination? What is his future state?”

79. “Addhā kho te ahaṃ, puṇṇa, na labhāmi. Alaṃ, puṇṇa, tiṭṭhatetaṃ; mā maṃ etaṃ pucchīti; api ca tyāhaṃ byākarissāmi. Idha, puṇṇa, ekacco kukkuravataṃ bhāveti paripuṇṇaṃ abbokiṇṇaṃ, kukkurasīlaṃ bhāveti paripuṇṇaṃ abbokiṇṇaṃ, kukkuracittaṃ bhāveti paripuṇṇaṃ abbokiṇṇaṃ[P 1.0388], kukkurākappaṃ bhāveti paripuṇṇaṃ abbokiṇṇaṃ. So kukkuravataṃ bhāvetvā paripuṇṇaṃ abbokiṇṇaṃ, kukkurasīlaṃ bhāvetvā paripuṇṇaṃ abbokiṇṇaṃ, kukkuracittaṃ bhāvetvā paripuṇṇaṃ abbokiṇṇaṃ, kukkurākappaṃ bhāvetvā paripuṇṇaṃ abbokiṇṇaṃ kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā kukkurānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjati. Sace kho panassa evaṃdiṭṭhi hoti – ‘imināhaṃ sīlena vā vatena vā tapena vā brahmacariyena vā devo vā bhavissāmi devaññataro vā’ti, sāssa sāyaṃ (ka.) hoti micchādiṭṭhi. Micchādiṭṭhissa micchādiṭṭhikassa (sī.) kho ahaṃ, puṇṇa, dvinnaṃ gatīnaṃ aññataraṃ gatiṃ vadāmi [V 2.0058] – nirayaṃ vā tiracchānayoniṃ vā. Iti kho, puṇṇa, sampajjamānaṃ [M 2.0051] kukkuravataṃ kukkurānaṃ sahabyataṃ upaneti, vipajjamānaṃ niraya”nti. Evaṃ vutte, acelo seniyo kukkuravatiko parodi, assūni pavattesi.

79. “Indeed, Puṇṇa, I do not get my wish from you when I say: ‘Enough, Puṇṇa, let this be; do not ask me this.’ But still, I will answer you. Here, Puṇṇa, a certain person develops the dog-practice completely and uninterruptedly, develops dog-conduct completely and uninterruptedly, develops a dog-mind completely and uninterruptedly, and develops dog-deportment completely and uninterruptedly. Having developed the dog-practice completely and uninterruptedly, dog-conduct completely and uninterruptedly, a dog-mind completely and uninterruptedly, and dog-deportment completely and uninterruptedly, with the breakup of the body, after death, he is reborn in the company of dogs. But if he should have such a view as this: ‘By this conduct, or this practice, or this austerity, or this holy life, I will become a god or one of the gods,’ that is wrong view for him. For one with wrong view, Puṇṇa, I declare one of two destinations: either hell or the animal realm. Thus, Puṇṇa, the dog-practice, when perfected, leads to the company of dogs; but when it fails, it leads to hell.” When this was said, Seniya the naked dog-duty ascetic wept and shed tears.

Atha kho bhagavā puṇṇaṃ koliyaputtaṃ govatikaṃ etadavoca – “etaṃ [T 2.0081] kho te ahaṃ, puṇṇa, nālatthaṃ. Alaṃ, puṇṇa, tiṭṭhatetaṃ; mā maṃ etaṃ pucchī”ti. “Nāhaṃ, bhante, etaṃ rodāmi yaṃ maṃ bhagavā evamāha; api ca me idaṃ, bhante, kukkuravataṃ dīgharattaṃ samattaṃ samādinnaṃ. Ayaṃ, bhante, puṇṇo koliyaputto govatiko. Tassa taṃ govataṃ dīgharattaṃ samattaṃ samādinnaṃ. Tassa kā gati, ko abhisamparāyo”ti? “Alaṃ, seniya, tiṭṭhatetaṃ; mā maṃ etaṃ pucchī”ti. Dutiyampi kho acelo seniyo…pe… tatiyampi kho acelo seniyo kukkuravatiko bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “ayaṃ, bhante, puṇṇo koliyaputto govatiko. Tassa taṃ govataṃ dīgharattaṃ samattaṃ samādinnaṃ. Tassa kā gati, ko abhisamparāyo”ti?

Then the Blessed One said to Puṇṇa, the son of the Koliyans who was a cow-duty ascetic: “This, Puṇṇa, is what I did not get from you when I said: ‘Enough, Puṇṇa, let this be; do not ask me this.’” Then Seniya, the naked dog-duty ascetic, said: “Venerable sir, I am not weeping because of what the Blessed One has said to me. But, venerable sir, this dog-duty has been undertaken by me completely for a long time. This Puṇṇa, venerable sir, is a son of the Koliyans and a cow-duty ascetic. His cow-duty has been undertaken completely for a long time. What is his destination? What is his future state?” “Enough, Seniya, let this be. Do not ask me this.” For a second time... and for a third time Seniya, the naked dog-duty ascetic, said this to the Blessed One: “This Puṇṇa, venerable sir, is a son of the Koliyans and a cow-duty ascetic. His cow-duty has been undertaken completely for a long time. What is his destination? What is his future state?”

80. “Addhā kho te ahaṃ, seniya, na labhāmi. Alaṃ, seniya, tiṭṭhatetaṃ; mā maṃ etaṃ pucchīti; api ca tyāhaṃ byākarissāmi. Idha, seniya, ekacco govataṃ bhāveti paripuṇṇaṃ abbokiṇṇaṃ, gosīlaṃ bhāveti paripuṇṇaṃ abbokiṇṇaṃ, gocittaṃ bhāveti paripuṇṇaṃ abbokiṇṇaṃ, gavākappaṃ gvākappaṃ (ka.) bhāveti paripuṇṇaṃ abbokiṇṇaṃ. So govataṃ bhāvetvā paripuṇṇaṃ abbokiṇṇaṃ, gosīlaṃ bhāvetvā paripuṇṇaṃ abbokiṇṇaṃ, gocittaṃ bhāvetvā paripuṇṇaṃ abbokiṇṇaṃ, gavākappaṃ bhāvetvā paripuṇṇaṃ abbokiṇṇaṃ kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā gunnaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjati. Sace kho [P 1.0389] panassa evaṃdiṭṭhi hoti – ‘imināhaṃ sīlena vā vatena vā tapena vā brahmacariyena vā devo vā bhavissāmi devaññataro vā’ti[T 2.0082], sāssa hoti micchādiṭṭhi. Micchādiṭṭhissa kho ahaṃ, seniya, dvinnaṃ gatīnaṃ aññataraṃ gatiṃ vadāmi – nirayaṃ vā tiracchānayoniṃ vā. Iti kho, seniya, sampajjamānaṃ govataṃ gunnaṃ sahabyataṃ upaneti, vipajjamānaṃ niraya”nti. Evaṃ vutte, puṇṇo koliyaputto govatiko parodi, assūni pavattesi.

80. “Indeed, Seniya, I do not get my wish from you when I say: ‘Enough, Seniya, let this be; do not ask me this.’ But still, I will answer you. Here, Seniya, a certain person develops the cow-practice completely and uninterruptedly, develops cow-conduct completely and uninterruptedly, develops a cow-mind completely and uninterruptedly, and develops cow-deportment completely and uninterruptedly. Having developed the cow-practice completely and uninterruptedly, cow-conduct completely and uninterruptedly, a cow-mind completely and uninterruptedly, and cow-deportment completely and uninterruptedly, with the breakup of the body, after death, he is reborn in the company of cattle. But if he should have such a view as this: ‘By this conduct, or this practice, or this austerity, or this holy life, I will become a god or one of the gods,’ that is wrong view for him. For one with wrong view, Seniya, I declare one of two destinations: either hell or the animal realm. Thus, Seniya, the cow-practice, when perfected, leads to the company of cattle; but when it fails, it leads to hell.” When this was said, Puṇṇa, the son of the Koliyans who was a cow-duty ascetic, wept and shed tears.

Atha kho bhagavā acelaṃ seniyaṃ kukkuravatikaṃ etadavoca – “etaṃ kho te ahaṃ, seniya[V 2.0059], nālatthaṃ. Alaṃ, seniya, tiṭṭhatetaṃ; mā maṃ [M 2.0052] etaṃ pucchī”ti. “Nāhaṃ, bhante, etaṃ rodāmi yaṃ maṃ bhagavā evamāha; api ca me idaṃ, bhante, govataṃ dīgharattaṃ samattaṃ samādinnaṃ. Evaṃ pasanno ahaṃ, bhante, bhagavati; pahoti bhagavā tathā dhammaṃ desetuṃ yathā ahaṃ cevimaṃ govataṃ pajaheyyaṃ, ayañceva acelo seniyo kukkuravatiko taṃ kukkuravataṃ pajaheyyā”ti. “Tena hi, puṇṇa, suṇāhi, sādhukaṃ manasi karohi, bhāsissāmī”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho puṇṇo koliyaputto govatiko bhagavato paccassosi. Bhagavā etadavoca –

Then the Blessed One said this to Seniya the naked ascetic, the dog-duty practitioner: “Seniya, I did not succeed with you in this matter. Enough, Seniya, let this be; do not ask me this.” Then Puṇṇa the Koliyan, the cow-duty practitioner, said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, I am not weeping because the Blessed One says this to me. And yet, venerable sir, this cow-duty of mine has been undertaken and practiced completely for a long time. I have such confidence in the Blessed One, venerable sir; the Blessed One is able to teach the Dhamma in such a way that I might abandon this cow-duty, and this naked ascetic Seniya, the dog-duty practitioner, might abandon that dog-duty.” “In that case, Puṇṇa, listen and pay close attention; I will speak.” “Yes, venerable sir,” replied Puṇṇa the Koliyan, the cow-duty practitioner, to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said this:

81. “Cattārimāni, puṇṇa, kammāni mayā sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā paveditāni. Katamāni cattāri? Atthi, puṇṇa, kammaṃ kaṇhaṃ kaṇhavipākaṃ; atthi, puṇṇa, kammaṃ sukkaṃ sukkavipākaṃ; atthi, puṇṇa, kammaṃ kaṇhasukkaṃ kaṇhasukkavipākaṃ; atthi, puṇṇa, kammaṃ akaṇhaṃ asukkaṃ akaṇhaasukkavipākaṃ, kammakkhayāya saṃvattati[T 2.0083].

81. “Puṇṇa, these four kinds of kamma have been realized by me myself through direct knowledge and proclaimed. What four? There is, Puṇṇa, kamma that is dark with a dark result; there is, Puṇṇa, kamma that is bright with a bright result; there is, Puṇṇa, kamma that is dark-and-bright with a dark-and-bright result; there is, Puṇṇa, kamma that is neither dark nor bright with a neither-dark-nor-bright result, which leads to the destruction of kamma.

“Katamañca, puṇṇa, kammaṃ kaṇhaṃ kaṇhavipākaṃ? Idha, puṇṇa, ekacco sabyābajjhaṃ sabyāpajjhaṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ.) kāyasaṅkhāraṃ abhisaṅkharoti, sabyābajjhaṃ vacīsaṅkhāraṃ abhisaṅkharoti, sabyābajjhaṃ manosaṅkhāraṃ abhisaṅkharoti. So sabyābajjhaṃ kāyasaṅkhāraṃ abhisaṅkharitvā, sabyābajjhaṃ vacīsaṅkhāraṃ abhisaṅkharitvā, sabyābajjhaṃ manosaṅkhāraṃ abhisaṅkharitvā, sabyābajjhaṃ lokaṃ upapajjati. Tamenaṃ sabyābajjhaṃ lokaṃ upapannaṃ samānaṃ sabyābajjhā phassā phusanti. So sabyābajjhehi phassehi phuṭṭho samāno sabyābajjhaṃ vedanaṃ vedeti ekantadukkhaṃ, seyyathāpi sattā nerayikā[P 1.0390]. Iti kho, puṇṇa, bhūtā bhūtassa upapatti hoti; yaṃ karoti tena upapajjati, upapannamenaṃ phassā phusanti. Evaṃpāhaṃ, puṇṇa, ‘kammadāyādā sattā’ti vadāmi. Idaṃ vuccati, puṇṇa, kammaṃ kaṇhaṃ kaṇhavipākaṃ.

“And what, Puṇṇa, is dark kamma with a dark result? Here, Puṇṇa, a certain person generates an afflictive bodily formation, generates an afflictive verbal formation, and generates an afflictive mental formation. Having generated an afflictive bodily formation, an afflictive verbal formation, and an afflictive mental formation, they are reborn into an afflictive world. When they have been reborn into an afflictive world, afflictive contacts touch them. Being touched by afflictive contacts, they experience an exclusively painful feeling, just as beings in hell do. Thus, Puṇṇa, the rebirth of a being is from what has come to be; by what one does, by that one is reborn; and when reborn, contacts touch them. In this way, Puṇṇa, I say: ‘Beings are heirs to their kamma.’ This, Puṇṇa, is called dark kamma with a dark result.

“Katamañca, puṇṇa, kammaṃ sukkaṃ sukkavipākaṃ? Idha, puṇṇa, ekacco abyābajjhaṃ kāyasaṅkhāraṃ abhisaṅkharoti, abyābajjhaṃ vacīsaṅkhāraṃ abhisaṅkharoti, abyābajjhaṃ manosaṅkhāraṃ abhisaṅkharoti. So abyābajjhaṃ kāyasaṅkhāraṃ abhisaṅkharitvā, abyābajjhaṃ vacīsaṅkhāraṃ abhisaṅkharitvā, abyābajjhaṃ manosaṅkhāraṃ abhisaṅkharitvā abyābajjhaṃ lokaṃ upapajjati. Tamenaṃ abyābajjhaṃ lokaṃ upapannaṃ [M 2.0053] samānaṃ abyābajjhā phassā phusanti. So abyābajjhehi phassehi phuṭṭho [V 2.0060] samāno abyābajjhaṃ vedanaṃ vedeti ekantasukhaṃ, seyyathāpi devā subhakiṇhā. Iti kho[T 2.0084], puṇṇa, bhūtā bhūtassa upapatti hoti; yaṃ karoti tena upapajjati, upapannamenaṃ phassā phusanti. Evaṃpāhaṃ, puṇṇa, ‘kammadāyādā sattā’ti vadāmi. Idaṃ vuccati, puṇṇa, kammaṃ sukkaṃ sukkavipākaṃ.

“And what, Puṇṇa, is bright kamma with a bright result? Here, Puṇṇa, a certain person generates a non-afflictive bodily formation, generates a non-afflictive verbal formation, and generates a non-afflictive mental formation. Having generated a non-afflictive bodily formation, a non-afflictive verbal formation, and a non-afflictive mental formation, they are reborn into a non-afflictive world. When they have been reborn into a non-afflictive world, non-afflictive contacts touch them. Being touched by non-afflictive contacts, they experience an exclusively pleasant feeling, just as the Subhakiṇhā gods do. Thus, Puṇṇa, the rebirth of a being is from what has come to be; by what one does, by that one is reborn; and when reborn, contacts touch them. In this way, Puṇṇa, I say: ‘Beings are heirs to their kamma.’ This, Puṇṇa, is called bright kamma with a bright result.

“Katamañca, puṇṇa, kammaṃ kaṇhasukkaṃ kaṇhasukkavipākaṃ? Idha, puṇṇa, ekacco sabyābajjhampi abyābajjhampi kāyasaṅkhāraṃ abhisaṅkharoti, sabyābajjhampi abyābajjhampi vacīsaṅkhāraṃ abhisaṅkharoti, sabyābajjhampi abyābajjhampi manosaṅkhāraṃ abhisaṅkharoti. So sabyābajjhampi abyābajjhampi kāyasaṅkhāraṃ abhisaṅkharitvā, sabyābajjhampi abyābajjhampi vacīsaṅkhāraṃ abhiṅkharitvā, sabyābajjhampi abyābajjhampi manosaṅkhāraṃ abhisaṅkharitvā sabyābajjhampi abyābajjhampi lokaṃ upapajjati. Tamenaṃ sabyābajjhampi abyābajjhampi lokaṃ upapannaṃ samānaṃ sabyābajjhāpi abyābajjhāpi phassā phusanti. So sabyābajjhehipi abyābajjhehipi phassehi phuṭṭho samāno sabyābajjhampi abyābajjhampi vedanaṃ vedeti vokiṇṇasukhadukkhaṃ, seyyathāpi manussā ekacce ca devā ekacce ca vinipātikā. Iti kho, puṇṇa, bhūtā bhūtassa upapatti hoti; yaṃ karoti tena upapajjati. Upapannamenaṃ phassā phusanti. Evaṃpāhaṃ, puṇṇa, ‘kammadāyādā sattā’ti vadāmi. Idaṃ vuccati, puṇṇa, kammaṃ kaṇhasukkaṃ kaṇhasukkavipākaṃ.

“And what, Puṇṇa, is dark-and-bright kamma with a dark-and-bright result? Here, Puṇṇa, a certain person generates a bodily formation that is both afflictive and non-afflictive, a verbal formation that is both afflictive and non-afflictive, and a mental formation that is both afflictive and non-afflictive. Having generated a bodily formation, a verbal formation, and a mental formation that are both afflictive and non-afflictive, they are reborn into a world that is both afflictive and non-afflictive. When they have been reborn into a world that is both afflictive and non-afflictive, both afflictive and non-afflictive contacts touch them. Being touched by both afflictive and non-afflictive contacts, they experience a feeling of mixed pleasure and pain, just as humans, some devas, and some beings in a state of downfall do. Thus, Puṇṇa, the rebirth of a being is from what has come to be; by what one does, by that one is reborn; and when reborn, contacts touch them. In this way, Puṇṇa, I say: ‘Beings are heirs to their kamma.’ This, Puṇṇa, is called dark-and-bright kamma with a dark-and-bright result.

“Katamañca[P 1.0391], puṇṇa, kammaṃ akaṇhaṃ asukkaṃ akaṇhaasukkavipākaṃ, kammakkhayāya saṃvattati? Tatra, puṇṇa, yamidaṃ [T 2.0085] kammaṃ kaṇhaṃ kaṇhavipākaṃ tassa pahānāya yā cetanā, yamidaṃ yampidaṃ (sī. pī.) kammaṃ sukkaṃ sukkavipākaṃ tassa pahānāya yā cetanā, yamidaṃ yampidaṃ (sī. pī.) kammaṃ kaṇhasukkaṃ kaṇhasukkavipākaṃ tassa pahānāya yā cetanā – idaṃ vuccati, puṇṇa, kammaṃ akaṇhaṃ asukkaṃ akaṇhaasukkavipākaṃ, kammakkhayāya saṃvattatīti. Imāni kho, puṇṇa, cattāri kammāni mayā sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā paveditānī”ti.

“And what, Puṇṇa, is the kamma that is neither dark nor bright, with a neither-dark-nor-bright result, which leads to the destruction of kamma? In this case, Puṇṇa, it is the volition for abandoning that kamma which is dark with a dark result, the volition for abandoning that kamma which is bright with a bright result, and the volition for abandoning that kamma which is dark-and-bright with a dark-and-bright result. This, Puṇṇa, is called the kamma that is neither dark nor bright, with a neither-dark-nor-bright result, which leads to the destruction of kamma. These, Puṇṇa, are the four kinds of kamma that I have realized by myself through direct knowledge and proclaimed.”

82. Evaṃ vutte, puṇṇo koliyaputto govatiko bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “abhikkantaṃ, bhante, abhikkantaṃ, bhante! Seyyathāpi, bhante…pe… upāsakaṃ maṃ bhagavā dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṃ [V 2.0061] saraṇaṃ gata”nti. Acelo [M 2.0054] pana seniyo kukkuravatiko bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “abhikkantaṃ, bhante, abhikkantaṃ, bhante! Seyyathāpi, bhante…pe… pakāsito. Esāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavantaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāmi dhammañca bhikkhusaṅghañca. Labheyyāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavato santike pabbajjaṃ, labheyyaṃ upasampada”nti. “Yo kho, seniya[T 2.0086], aññatitthiyapubbo imasmiṃ dhammavinaye ākaṅkhati pabbajjaṃ, ākaṅkhati upasampadaṃ so cattāro māse parivasati. Catunnaṃ māsānaṃ accayena āraddhacittā bhikkhū pabbājenti, upasampādenti bhikkhubhāvāya. Api ca mettha puggalavemattatā viditā”ti.

82. When this was said, Puṇṇa the Koliyan, who practiced the cow-vow, said to the Blessed One: “Excellent, venerable sir! Excellent, venerable sir! Just as, venerable sir, one might set upright what had been overturned, or disclose what had been hidden, or point out the way to one who had gone astray, or bring a lamp into the darkness so that those with eyes could see forms, in the same way has the Blessed One made the Dhamma clear in various ways. May the Blessed One remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge from this day forward for as long as life lasts.” Then Seniya the naked ascetic, who practiced the dog-vow, said to the Blessed One: “Excellent, venerable sir! Excellent, venerable sir! Just as, venerable sir, one might set upright what had been overturned … so too has the Dhamma been made clear. I, venerable sir, go for refuge to the Blessed One, to the Dhamma, and to the Bhikkhu Saṅgha. May I, venerable sir, receive the going forth in the Blessed One’s presence; may I receive the higher ordination.” “Seniya, one who previously belonged to another sect and desires the going forth and desires the higher ordination in this Dhamma and Discipline, must undergo probation for four months. At the end of four months, the bhikkhus, being satisfied, give him the going forth and the higher ordination into the state of a bhikkhu. But in this matter, individual differences are known to me.”

“Sace, bhante, aññatitthiyapubbā imasmiṃ dhammavinaye ākaṅkhantā pabbajjaṃ ākaṅkhantā upasampadaṃ te cattāro māse parivasanti catunnaṃ māsānaṃ accayena āraddhacittā bhikkhū pabbājenti upasampādenti bhikkhubhāvāya, ahaṃ cattāri vassāni parivasissāmi. Catunnaṃ vassānaṃ accayena āraddhacittā bhikkhū pabbājentu, upasampādentu bhikkhubhāvāyā”ti. Alattha kho acelo seniyo kukkuravatiko bhagavato santike pabbajjaṃ, alattha upasampadaṃ. Acirūpasampanno kho panāyasmā seniyo eko vūpakaṭṭho appamatto [P 1.0392] ātāpī pahitatto viharanto nacirasseva – yassatthāya kulaputtā sammadeva agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajanti tadanuttaraṃ – brahmacariyapariyosānaṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja vihāsi. ‘Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti abbhaññāsi. Aññataro kho panāyasmā seniyo arahataṃ ahosīti.

“Venerable sir, if those who formerly belonged to other sects, desiring the going forth and desiring the higher ordination in this Dhamma and Discipline, must undergo probation for four months, and at the end of four months, the bhikkhus, being satisfied, give them the going forth and the higher ordination into the state of a bhikkhu—then I will undergo probation for four years. At the end of four years, let the bhikkhus, being satisfied, give me the going forth and the higher ordination into the state of a bhikkhu.” The naked ascetic Seniya, who practiced the dog-vow, received the going forth in the presence of the Blessed One, and he received the higher ordination. Not long after his higher ordination, the Venerable Seniya, dwelling alone, withdrawn, diligent, ardent, and resolute, soon realized for himself—through direct knowledge—in this very life that unsurpassed culmination of the holy life for which clansmen rightly go forth from the household life into homelessness. He dwelled having attained it, and he understood: “Birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is no more for this state of being.” And the Venerable Seniya became one of the arahants.

Kukkuravatikasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ sattamaṃ.

The seventh Sutta on the Dog-Vow Practitioner is concluded.

8. Abhayarājakumārasuttaṃ

8. The Sutta to Prince Abhaya

83. Evaṃ [T 2.0087][V 2.0062] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe. Atha kho abhayo rājakumāro yena nigaṇṭho nāṭaputto tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā nigaṇṭhaṃ nāṭaputtaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho abhayaṃ rājakumāraṃ nigaṇṭho nāṭaputto etadavoca – “ehi tvaṃ, rājakumāra, samaṇassa gotamassa vādaṃ [M 2.0055] āropehi. Evaṃ te kalyāṇo kittisaddo abbhuggacchissati – ‘abhayena rājakumārena samaṇassa gotamassa evaṃ mahiddhikassa evaṃ mahānubhāvassa vādo āropito’”ti. “Yathā kathaṃ panāhaṃ, bhante, samaṇassa gotamassa evaṃ mahiddhikassa evaṃ mahānubhāvassa vādaṃ āropessāmī”ti? “Ehi tvaṃ, rājakumāra, yena samaṇo gotamo tenupasaṅkama; upasaṅkamitvā samaṇaṃ gotamaṃ evaṃ vadehi – ‘bhāseyya nu kho, bhante, tathāgato taṃ vācaṃ yā sā vācā paresaṃ appiyā amanāpā’ti? Sace te samaṇo gotamo evaṃ puṭṭho evaṃ byākaroti – ‘bhāseyya, rājakumāra, tathāgato taṃ vācaṃ yā sā vācā paresaṃ appiyā amanāpā’ti, tamenaṃ tvaṃ evaṃ vadeyyāsi – ‘atha kiñcarahi te, bhante, puthujjanena nānākaraṇaṃ? Puthujjanopi hi taṃ vācaṃ bhāseyya yā sā vācā paresaṃ appiyā amanāpā’ti. Sace [T 2.0088] pana te samaṇo gotamo evaṃ puṭṭho evaṃ byākaroti – ‘na, rājakumāra, tathāgato taṃ vācaṃ bhāseyya yā sā vācā paresaṃ [P 1.0393] appiyā amanāpā’ti, tamenaṃ tvaṃ evaṃ vadeyyāsi – ‘atha kiñcarahi te, bhante, devadatto byākato – “āpāyiko devadatto, nerayiko devadatto, kappaṭṭho devadatto, atekiccho devadatto”ti? Tāya ca pana te vācāya devadatto kupito ahosi anattamano’ti. Imaṃ kho te, rājakumāra, samaṇo gotamo ubhatokoṭikaṃ pañhaṃ puṭṭho samāno neva sakkhiti uggilituṃ na sakkhiti ogilituṃ. Seyyathāpi nāma purisassa ayosiṅghāṭakaṃ kaṇṭhe vilaggaṃ, so neva sakkuṇeyya uggilituṃ na sakkuṇeyya ogilituṃ; evameva kho te, rājakumāra, samaṇo gotamo imaṃ ubhatokoṭikaṃ pañhaṃ puṭṭho samāno neva sakkhiti uggilituṃ na sakkhiti ogilitu”nti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho abhayo rājakumāro nigaṇṭhassa nāṭaputtassa paṭissutvā uṭṭhāyāsanā nigaṇṭhaṃ nāṭaputtaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi.

83. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Rājagaha, in the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrel Sanctuary. Then Prince Abhaya approached the Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta. Having approached, he paid homage to the Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta said this to Prince Abhaya: "Come, Prince, bring an accusation against the ascetic Gotama. Thus, a good reputation will arise for you: ‘Prince Abhaya has brought an accusation against the ascetic Gotama, so mighty and so powerful!’" "But how, venerable sir, shall I bring an accusation against the ascetic Gotama, so mighty and so powerful?" "Come, Prince, approach the ascetic Gotama and say to him: ‘Venerable sir, would the Tathāgata speak words that are disagreeable and unpleasant to others?’ If the ascetic Gotama, being asked thus, answers: ‘Prince, the Tathāgata would speak words that are disagreeable and unpleasant to others,’ then you should say to him: ‘Then, venerable sir, what is the difference between you and an ordinary person? For an ordinary person also speaks words that are disagreeable and unpleasant to others.’ But if the ascetic Gotama, being asked thus, answers: ‘No, Prince, the Tathāgata would not speak words that are disagreeable and unpleasant to others,’ then you should say to him: ‘Then, venerable sir, why did you declare of Devadatta: “Devadatta is bound for the state of deprivation, Devadatta is bound for hell, Devadatta will remain for the eon, Devadatta is incorrigible”? Devadatta was angered and displeased by those words of yours.’ This, Prince, is a two-pronged question for the ascetic Gotama. When asked this, he will neither be able to spit it out nor swallow it. Just as if an iron spike were stuck in a man’s throat, he would be unable to spit it out or swallow it; so too, Prince, when the ascetic Gotama is asked this two-pronged question, he will neither be able to spit it out nor swallow it." "So be it, venerable sir," replied Prince Abhaya. Having consented to the Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta's words, he rose from his seat, paid homage to him, circumambulated him with his right side toward him, and approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side.

84. Ekamantaṃ [V 2.0063] nisinnassa kho abhayassa rājakumārassa sūriyaṃ suriyaṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) ulloketvā etadahosi – “akālo kho ajja bhagavato vādaṃ āropetuṃ[M 2.0056]. Sve dānāhaṃ sake nivesane bhagavato vādaṃ āropessāmī”ti bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “adhivāsetu me, bhante, bhagavā svātanāya attacatuttho bhatta”nti. Adhivāsesi bhagavā tuṇhībhāvena. Atha [T 2.0089] kho abhayo rājakumāro bhagavato adhivāsanaṃ viditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā pakkāmi. Atha kho bhagavā tassā rattiyā accayena pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya yena abhayassa rājakumārassa nivesanaṃ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi. Atha kho abhayo rājakumāro bhagavantaṃ paṇītena khādanīyena bhojanīyena sahatthā santappesi sampavāresi. Atha kho abhayo rājakumāro bhagavantaṃ bhuttāviṃ onītapattapāṇiṃ aññataraṃ nīcaṃ āsanaṃ gahetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi.

84. Then Prince Abhaya, who was sitting to one side, looked up at the sun and this thought occurred to him: 'Today is not the right time to bring an accusation against the Blessed One. Tomorrow I will bring an accusation against the Blessed One at my own residence.' So he said to the Blessed One: 'Venerable sir, may the Blessed One, with himself as the fourth, consent to a meal from me tomorrow.' The Blessed One consented by silence. Then Prince Abhaya, knowing the Blessed One's consent, rose from his seat, paid homage to the Blessed One, circumambulated him keeping him to the right, and departed. Then, at the passing of that night, the Blessed One, having dressed in the morning, took his bowl and robe and approached the residence of Prince Abhaya. Having approached, he sat down on the prepared seat. Then Prince Abhaya, with his own hands, satisfied and served the Blessed One with excellent hard and soft food. Then, when the Blessed One had eaten and had withdrawn his hand from the bowl, Prince Abhaya took a lower seat and sat down to one side.

85.
