Householders, there are some ascetics and brahmins who speak thus, holding such a view: ‘There is no cessation of becoming in any way.’ And indeed, householders, some other ascetics and brahmins hold a view directly opposed to them. They say: ‘There is, in every way, a cessation of becoming.’ What do you think, householders? Are not these ascetics and brahmins directly opposed to one another in their views?” “So it is, venerable sir.” “Therein, householders, a discerning person reflects thus: ‘As for those venerable ascetics and brahmins who hold the view, “There is no cessation of becoming in any way”—this I have not seen. As for those venerable ascetics and brahmins who hold the view, “There is, in every way, a cessation of becoming”—this I have not known. I, not knowing and not seeing, were I to take one side and declare, “This alone is true, anything else is false,” that would not be fitting for me. If the statement of those venerable ascetics and brahmins who hold the view, “There is no cessation of becoming in any way,” were true, it is possible that I will be reborn among the formless, perception-made deities; it is certain that my rebirth will be there. But if the statement of those venerable ascetics and brahmins who hold the view, “There is, in every way, a cessation of becoming,” were true, it is possible that I will attain final Nibbāna in this very life. The view of those venerable ascetics and brahmins who hold that “There is no cessation of becoming in any way” is close to passion, close to bondage, close to delight, close to obsession, close to clinging. But the view of those venerable ascetics and brahmins who hold that “There is, in every way, a cessation of becoming” is close to non-passion, close to non-bondage, close to non-delight, close to non-obsession, close to non-clinging.’ Having reflected thus, he practices for disenchantment with, dispassion toward, and cessation of becoming itself.

105. “Cattārome, gahapatayo, puggalā santo saṃvijjamānā lokasmiṃ. Katame cattāro? Idha, gahapatayo, ekacco puggalo attantapo hoti attaparitāpanānuyogamanuyutto. Idha, gahapatayo, ekacco puggalo parantapo hoti paraparitāpanānuyogamanuyutto. Idha, gahapatayo, ekacco puggalo attantapo ca hoti attaparitāpanānuyogamanuyutto parantapo ca paraparitāpanānuyogamanuyutto. Idha, gahapatayo, ekacco puggalo nevattantapo hoti nāttaparitāpanānuyogamanuyutto na parantapo na paraparitāpanānuyogamanuyutto; so anattantapo [P 1.0412] aparantapo diṭṭheva dhamme nicchāto nibbuto sītībhūto sukhappaṭisaṃvedī brahmabhūtena attanā viharati.

105. Householders, these four persons are found existing in the world. Which four? Here, householders, a certain person is a self-tormentor, devoted to the practice of self-torment. Here, householders, a certain person is a tormentor of others, devoted to the practice of tormenting others. Here, householders, a certain person is both a self-tormentor, devoted to the practice of self-torment, and a tormentor of others, devoted to the practice of tormenting others. Here, householders, a certain person is neither a self-tormentor, not devoted to the practice of self-torment, nor a tormentor of others, not devoted to the practice of tormenting others; he, being neither a self-tormentor nor a tormentor of others, in this very life is without thirst, quenched, cooled, experiencing happiness, abiding with a self that has become supreme.

106. “Katamo ca, gahapatayo, puggalo attantapo attaparitāpanānuyogamanuyutto[T 2.0119]? Idha, gahapatayo, ekacco puggalo acelako hoti muttācāro hatthāpalekhano…pe… vitthāro ma. ni. 2.6-7 kandarakasutte iti evarūpaṃ anekavihitaṃ kāyassa ātāpanaparitāpanānuyogamanuyutto viharati. Ayaṃ vuccati, gahapatayo, puggalo attantapo attaparitāpanānuyogamanuyutto.

106. And what, householders, is the person who is a self-tormentor, devoted to the practice of self-torment? Here, householders, a certain person is naked, of unrestrained habits, licks his hands clean… and so on, he dwells devoted to the practice of mortifying and tormenting the body in various ways. This, householders, is called the person who is a self-tormentor, devoted to the practice of self-torment.

“Katamo [M 2.0075][V 2.0082] ca, gahapatayo, puggalo parantapo paraparitāpanānuyogamanuyutto? Idha, gahapatayo, ekacco puggalo orabbhiko hoti sūkariko…pe… ye vā panaññepi keci kurūrakammantā. Ayaṃ vuccati, gahapatayo, puggalo parantapo paraparitāpanānuyogamanuyutto.

And what, householders, is the person who is a tormentor of others, devoted to the practice of tormenting others? Here, householders, a certain person is a butcher of sheep, a butcher of pigs… or anyone else engaged in any cruel occupation. This, householders, is called the person who is a tormentor of others, devoted to the practice of tormenting others.

“Katamo ca, gahapatayo, puggalo attantapo ca attaparitāpanānuyogamanuyutto parantapo ca paraparitāpanānuyogamanuyutto? Idha, gahapatayo, ekacco puggalo rājā vā hoti khattiyo muddhāvasitto…pe… tepi daṇḍatajjitā bhayatajjitā assumukhā rudamānā parikammāni karonti. Ayaṃ vuccati, gahapatayo, puggalo attantapo ca attaparitāpanānuyogamanuyutto parantapo ca paraparitāpanānuyogamanuyutto.

And what, householders, is the person who is both a self-tormentor, devoted to the practice of self-torment, and a tormentor of others, devoted to the practice of tormenting others? Here, householders, a certain person is a king, an anointed khattiya… and so on… and his workers, threatened by the rod, threatened by fear, with tearful faces, weeping, perform their tasks. This, householders, is called the person who is both a self-tormentor, devoted to the practice of self-torment, and a tormentor of others, devoted to the practice of tormenting others.

“Katamo ca, gahapatayo, puggalo nevattantapo nāttaparitāpanānuyogamanuyutto na parantapo na paraparitāpanānuyogamanuyutto; so anattantapo aparantapo diṭṭheva dhamme nicchāto nibbuto sītībhūto sukhappaṭisaṃvedī brahmabhūtena attanā viharati? Idha, gahapatayo, tathāgato loke uppajjati arahaṃ sammāsambuddho…pe… so ime pañca nīvaraṇe pahāya cetaso [T 2.0120] upakkilese paññāya dubbalīkaraṇe vivicceva kāmehi vivicca akusalehi dhammehi savitakkaṃ savicāraṃ vivekajaṃ pītisukhaṃ paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati. Vitakkavicārānaṃ vūpasamā ajjhattaṃ sampasādanaṃ cetaso ekodibhāvaṃ avitakkaṃ avicāraṃ samādhijaṃ pītisukhaṃ dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ…pe… tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ… catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati.

And what, householders, is the person who is neither a self-tormentor, not devoted to the practice of self-torment, nor a tormentor of others, not devoted to the practice of tormenting others; who, being neither a self-tormentor nor a tormentor of others, in this very life is without thirst, quenched, cooled, experiencing happiness, abiding with a self that has become supreme? Here, householders, a Tathāgata arises in the world, an Arahant, a Perfectly Enlightened One… Having abandoned these five hindrances—defilements of the mind that weaken wisdom—secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unwholesome states, he enters and abides in the first jhāna, which is accompanied by applied and sustained thought, with rapture and happiness born of seclusion. With the stilling of applied and sustained thought, he enters and abides in the second jhāna, which has internal confidence and unification of mind, is without applied and sustained thought, and is filled with rapture and happiness born of concentration… the third jhāna… he enters and abides in the fourth jhāna.

“So evaṃ samāhite citte parisuddhe pariyodāte anaṅgaṇe vigatūpakkilese mudubhūte kammaniye ṭhite āneñjappatte pubbenivāsānussatiñāṇāya cittaṃ abhininnāmeti. So anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussarati seyyathidaṃ – ekampi jātiṃ dvepi jātiyo…pe… iti sākāraṃ sauddesaṃ anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussarati. So evaṃ samāhite citte parisuddhe [P 1.0413] pariyodāte anaṅgaṇe vigatūpakkilese mudubhūte kammaniye ṭhite āneñjappatte sattānaṃ [V 2.0083] cutūpapātañāṇāya cittaṃ abhininnāmeti. So dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena satte passati cavamāne upapajjamāne hīne paṇīte suvaṇṇe dubbaṇṇe, sugate duggate…pe… yathākammūpage satte pajānāti. So evaṃ samāhite [M 2.0076] citte parisuddhe pariyodāte anaṅgaṇe vigatūpakkilese mudubhūte kammaniye ṭhite āneñjappatte āsavānaṃ khayañāṇāya cittaṃ abhininnāmeti. So ‘idaṃ dukkha’nti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti…pe… ‘ayaṃ āsavanirodhagāminī [T 2.0121] paṭipadā’ti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti. Tassa evaṃ jānato evaṃ passato kāmāsavāpi cittaṃ vimuccati, bhavāsavāpi cittaṃ vimuccati, avijjāsavāpi cittaṃ vimuccati. Vimuttasmiṃ vimuttamiti ñāṇaṃ hoti. ‘Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti pajānāti. Ayaṃ vuccati, gahapatayo, puggalo nevattantapo nāttaparitāpanānuyogamanuyutto na parantapo na paraparitāpanānuyogamanuyutto; so anattantapo aparantapo diṭṭheva dhamme nicchāto nibbuto sītībhūto sukhappaṭisaṃvedī brahmabhūtena attanā viharatī”ti.

When his mind is thus concentrated, purified, bright, unblemished, rid of defilements, malleable, workable, firm, and unshakable, he directs and inclines it to the knowledge of the recollection of past abodes. He recollects his manifold past abodes, that is, one birth, two births… and so on… Thus with their aspects and details he recollects his manifold past abodes. When his mind is thus concentrated, purified, bright, unblemished, rid of defilements, malleable, workable, firm, and unshakable, he directs and inclines it to the knowledge of the passing away and reappearance of beings. With the divine eye, which is purified and surpasses the human, he sees beings passing away and reappearing—inferior and superior, of good complexion and of bad complexion, in a good destination and in a bad destination… and so on… He understands how beings fare according to their kamma. When his mind is thus concentrated, purified, bright, unblemished, rid of defilements, malleable, workable, firm, and unshakable, he directs and inclines it to the knowledge of the destruction of the taints. He understands as it really is: ‘This is suffering’… and so on… ‘This is the path leading to the cessation of the taints.’ For him, knowing and seeing thus, his mind is liberated from the taint of sensual desire, from the taint of becoming, and from the taint of ignorance. When it is liberated, the knowledge arises: ‘It is liberated.’ He understands: ‘Birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this state of being.’ This person, householders, is called one who neither torments himself nor is devoted to the practice of self-torment, and who neither torments others nor is devoted to the practice of tormenting others. He, not tormenting himself and not tormenting others, in this very life abides without craving, quenched, cooled, experiencing happiness, with a self that has become sublime.

Evaṃ vutte, sāleyyakā brāhmaṇagahapatikā bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ – “abhikkantaṃ, bho gotama, abhikkantaṃ, bho gotama! Seyyathāpi, bho gotama, nikkujjitaṃ vā ukkujjeyya, paṭicchannaṃ vā vivareyya, mūḷhassa vā maggaṃ ācikkheyya, andhakāre vā telapajjotaṃ dhāreyya ‘cakkhumanto rūpāni dakkhantī’ti; evamevaṃ bhotā gotamena anekapariyāyena dhammo pakāsito. Ete mayaṃ bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāma dhammañca bhikkhusaṅghañca. Upāsake no bhavaṃ gotamo dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṃ saraṇaṃ gate”ti.

When this was said, the brahmin householders of Sālā said to the Blessed One: "Excellent, Master Gotama! Excellent, Master Gotama! Just as, Master Gotama, one might set upright what has been overturned, or reveal what has been hidden, or show the path to one who is lost, or hold up an oil lamp in the darkness so that those with eyes might see forms—in the very same way, the Dhamma has been made clear by the venerable Gotama in many ways. We go to the venerable Gotama for refuge, to the Dhamma, and to the Sangha of bhikkhus. May the venerable Gotama remember us as lay followers who have gone for refuge for life, from this day forward."

Apaṇṇakasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ dasamaṃ.

The Apaṇṇaka Sutta, the tenth, is concluded.

Gahapativaggo niṭṭhito paṭhamo.

The Chapter on Householders, the first, is concluded.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary of that chapter:

Kandaranāgarasekhavato [T 2.0122] ca, potaliyo puna jīvakabhacco;

Upālidamatho kukkuraabhayo, bahuvedanīyāpaṇṇakato dasamo.

Kandaraka, Aṭṭhakanāgara, and Sekha-paṭipadā; then Potaliya and again Jīvaka; Upāli, Kukkuravatika, and Abhayarājakumāra; Bahuvedanīya, and Apaṇṇaka as the tenth.

2. Bhikkhuvaggo

2. The Chapter on Monks

1. Ambalaṭṭhikarāhulovādasuttaṃ

1. The Discourse on Advice to Rāhula at Ambalaṭṭhikā

107. [M 2.0077][V 2.0084] Evaṃ [T 2.0123][P 1.0414] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe. Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā rāhulo ambalaṭṭhikāyaṃ viharati. Atha kho bhagavā sāyanhasamayaṃ paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito yena ambalaṭṭhikā yenāyasmā rāhulo tenupasaṅkami. Addasā kho āyasmā rāhulo bhagavantaṃ dūratova āgacchantaṃ. Disvāna āsanaṃ paññāpesi, udakañca pādānaṃ. Nisīdi bhagavā paññatte āsane. Nisajja pāde pakkhālesi. Āyasmāpi kho rāhulo bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi.

107. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Rājagaha, in the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrels' Feeding Ground. At that time, the Venerable Rāhula was dwelling at Ambalaṭṭhikā. Then, in the evening, the Blessed One rose from his solitary abiding and went to Ambalaṭṭhikā, to where the Venerable Rāhula was. The Venerable Rāhula saw the Blessed One coming from afar. Seeing him, he prepared a seat and water for washing the feet. The Blessed One sat down on the prepared seat. Having sat down, he washed his feet. The Venerable Rāhula, too, having paid homage to the Blessed One, sat down to one side.

108. Atha kho bhagavā parittaṃ udakāvasesaṃ udakādhāne ṭhapetvā āyasmantaṃ rāhulaṃ āmantesi – “passasi no tvaṃ, rāhula, imaṃ parittaṃ udakāvasesaṃ udakādhāne ṭhapita”nti? “Evaṃ, bhante”. “Evaṃ parittakaṃ kho, rāhula, tesaṃ sāmaññaṃ yesaṃ natthi sampajānamusāvāde lajjā”ti. Atha kho bhagavā parittaṃ udakāvasesaṃ chaḍḍetvā āyasmantaṃ rāhulaṃ āmantesi – “passasi no tvaṃ, rāhula, parittaṃ udakāvasesaṃ chaḍḍita”nti? “Evaṃ, bhante”. “Evaṃ chaḍḍitaṃ kho, rāhula, tesaṃ sāmaññaṃ yesaṃ natthi sampajānamusāvāde lajjā”ti. Atha kho bhagavā [T 2.0124] taṃ udakādhānaṃ nikkujjitvā āyasmantaṃ rāhulaṃ āmantesi – “passasi no tvaṃ, rāhula, imaṃ udakādhānaṃ nikkujjita”nti? “Evaṃ, bhante”. “Evaṃ nikkujjitaṃ kho, rāhula, tesaṃ sāmaññaṃ yesaṃ natthi sampajānamusāvāde lajjā”ti. Atha kho bhagavā taṃ udakādhānaṃ ukkujjitvā āyasmantaṃ rāhulaṃ āmantesi – “passasi no tvaṃ, rāhula, imaṃ udakādhānaṃ rittaṃ tuccha”nti? “Evaṃ, bhante”. “Evaṃ rittaṃ tucchaṃ kho, rāhula, tesaṃ sāmaññaṃ yesaṃ natthi [V 2.0085] sampajānamusāvāde lajjāti. Seyyathāpi, rāhula, rañño nāgo īsādanto urūḷhavā ubbūḷhavā (sī. pī.) abhijāto saṅgāmāvacaro saṅgāmagato purimehipi pādehi kammaṃ karoti, pacchimehipi pādehi kammaṃ karoti, purimenapi kāyena kammaṃ karoti, pacchimenapi kāyena kammaṃ karoti, sīsenapi kammaṃ karoti, kaṇṇehipi [M 2.0078] kammaṃ karoti, dantehipi kammaṃ karoti, naṅguṭṭhenapi kammaṃ [P 1.0415] karoti; rakkhateva soṇḍaṃ. Tattha hatthārohassa evaṃ hoti – ‘ayaṃ kho rañño nāgo īsādanto urūḷhavā abhijāto saṅgāmāvacaro saṅgāmagato purimehipi pādehi kammaṃ karoti, pacchimehipi pādehi kammaṃ karoti…pe… naṅguṭṭhenapi kammaṃ karoti; rakkhateva soṇḍaṃ[T 2.0125]. Apariccattaṃ kho rañño nāgassa jīvita’nti. Yato kho, rāhula, rañño nāgo īsādanto urūḷhavā abhijāto saṅgāmāvacaro saṅgāmagato purimehipi pādehi kammaṃ karoti, pacchimehipi pādehi kammaṃ karoti…pe… naṅguṭṭhenapi kammaṃ karoti, soṇḍāyapi kammaṃ karoti, tattha hatthārohassa evaṃ hoti – ‘ayaṃ kho rañño nāgo īsādanto urūḷhavā abhijāto saṅgāmāvacaro saṅgāmagato purimehipi pādehi kammaṃ karoti, pacchimehipi pādehi kammaṃ karoti, purimenapi kāyena kammaṃ karoti, pacchimenapi kāyena kammaṃ karoti, sīsenapi kammaṃ karoti, kaṇṇehipi kammaṃ karoti, dantehipi kammaṃ karoti, naṅguṭṭhenapi kammaṃ karoti, soṇḍāyapi kammaṃ karoti. Pariccattaṃ kho rañño nāgassa jīvitaṃ. Natthi dāni kiñci rañño nāgassa akaraṇīya’nti. Evameva kho, rāhula, yassa kassaci sampajānamusāvāde natthi lajjā, nāhaṃ tassa kiñci pāpaṃ akaraṇīyanti vadāmi. Tasmātiha te, rāhula, ‘hassāpi na musā bhaṇissāmī’ti – evañhi te, rāhula, sikkhitabbaṃ.

108. Then the Blessed One, having left a little remaining water in the water vessel, addressed the Venerable Rāhula: “Do you see, Rāhula, this little remaining water left in the water vessel?” “Yes, venerable sir.” “Just as little, Rāhula, is the recluseship of those who have no shame in speaking a deliberate falsehood.” Then the Blessed One, having thrown away that little remaining water, addressed the Venerable Rāhula: “Do you see, Rāhula, that little remaining water thrown away?” “Yes, venerable sir.” “Just so thrown away, Rāhula, is the recluseship of those who have no shame in speaking a deliberate falsehood.” Then the Blessed One, having overturned the water vessel, addressed the Venerable Rāhula: “Do you see, Rāhula, this water vessel overturned?” “Yes, venerable sir.” “Just so overturned, Rāhula, is the recluseship of those who have no shame in speaking a deliberate falsehood.” Then the Blessed One, having set the water vessel upright, addressed the Venerable Rāhula: “Do you see, Rāhula, this water vessel empty and void?” “Yes, venerable sir.” “Just so empty and void, Rāhula, is the recluseship of those who have no shame in speaking a deliberate falsehood. Suppose, Rāhula, there was a king's elephant with tusks like chariot poles, of great stature, of noble breed, accustomed to battle, gone into battle. It performs its work with its front legs, it performs its work with its hind legs, it performs its work with its forequarters, it performs its work with its hindquarters, it performs its work with its head, it performs its work with its ears, it performs its work with its tusks, it performs its work with its tail; but it protects its trunk. The elephant rider thinks: ‘This king's elephant... performs its work with its tail, but it protects its trunk. The king's elephant has not yet given up its life.’ But when, Rāhula, the king's elephant... performs its work with its tail, and also performs its work with its trunk, the elephant rider thinks: ‘This king's elephant... performs its work with its tail, and also performs its work with its trunk. The king's elephant has now given up its life. There is now nothing the king's elephant will not do.’ In the same way, Rāhula, for anyone who has no shame in speaking a deliberate falsehood, I say there is no evil they would not do. Therefore, Rāhula, you should train yourself thus: ‘I will not speak a falsehood, even in jest.’ This, Rāhula, is how you should train.

109. “Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, rāhula, kimatthiyo ādāso”ti? “Paccavekkhaṇattho, bhante”ti. “Evameva kho, rāhula, paccavekkhitvā paccavekkhitvā kāyena kammaṃ kattabbaṃ, paccavekkhitvā paccavekkhitvā vācāya kammaṃ kattabbaṃ, paccavekkhitvā paccavekkhitvā manasā kammaṃ kattabbaṃ. Yadeva [T 2.0126] tvaṃ, rāhula, kāyena kammaṃ kattukāmo ahosi, tadeva te kāyakammaṃ paccavekkhitabbaṃ – ‘yaṃ nu kho ahaṃ idaṃ kāyena kammaṃ kattukāmo idaṃ me kāyakammaṃ attabyābādhāyapi saṃvatteyya, parabyābādhāyapi saṃvatteyya, ubhayabyābādhāyapi saṃvatteyya – akusalaṃ idaṃ kāyakammaṃ dukkhudrayaṃ dukkhundrayaṃ, dukkhudayaṃ (ka.) dukkhavipāka’nti? Sace tvaṃ, rāhula, paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jāneyyāsi – ‘yaṃ kho ahaṃ idaṃ kāyena kammaṃ kattukāmo idaṃ me kāyakammaṃ attabyābādhāyapi [V 2.0086] saṃvatteyya, parabyābādhāyapi saṃvatteyya, ubhayabyābādhāyapi [M 2.0079] saṃvatteyya – akusalaṃ idaṃ kāyakammaṃ dukkhudrayaṃ dukkhavipāka’nti, evarūpaṃ te, rāhula, kāyena kammaṃ sasakkaṃ na karaṇīyaṃ saṃsakkaṃ na ca karaṇīyaṃ (ka.). Sace [P 1.0416] pana tvaṃ, rāhula, paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jāneyyāsi – ‘yaṃ kho ahaṃ idaṃ kāyena kammaṃ kattukāmo idaṃ me kāyakammaṃ nevattabyābādhāyapi saṃvatteyya, na parabyābādhāyapi saṃvatteyya, na ubhayabyābādhāyapi saṃvatteyya – kusalaṃ idaṃ kāyakammaṃ sukhudrayaṃ sukhavipāka’nti, evarūpaṃ te, rāhula, kāyena kammaṃ karaṇīyaṃ.

109. “What do you think, Rāhula, for what purpose is a mirror?” “For the purpose of reflection, venerable sir.” “Even so, Rāhula, having reflected again and again, a bodily action should be done; having reflected again and again, a verbal action should be done; having reflected again and again, a mental action should be done. Whenever you, Rāhula, wish to perform a bodily action, that very bodily action should be reflected upon by you: ‘Would this bodily action that I wish to perform lead to my own affliction, or to the affliction of others, or to the affliction of both? Is this bodily action unwholesome, giving rise to suffering, with a painful result?’ If, Rāhula, while reflecting, you should know thus: ‘This bodily action that I wish to perform would lead to my own affliction, or to the affliction of others, or to the affliction of both; this bodily action is unwholesome, giving rise to suffering, with a painful result,’ then, Rāhula, such a bodily action should absolutely not be done by you. But if, Rāhula, while reflecting, you should know thus: ‘This bodily action that I wish to perform would lead neither to my own affliction, nor to the affliction of others, nor to the affliction of both; this bodily action is wholesome, giving rise to happiness, with a happy result,’ then, Rāhula, such a bodily action should be done by you.”

“Karontenapi te, rāhula, kāyena kammaṃ tadeva te kāyakammaṃ paccavekkhitabbaṃ – ‘yaṃ nu kho ahaṃ idaṃ kāyena kammaṃ karomi idaṃ me kāyakammaṃ attabyābādhāyapi [T 2.0127] saṃvattati, parabyābādhāyapi saṃvattati, ubhayabyābādhāyapi saṃvattati – akusalaṃ idaṃ kāyakammaṃ dukkhudrayaṃ dukkhavipāka’nti? Sace pana tvaṃ, rāhula, paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jāneyyāsi – ‘yaṃ kho ahaṃ idaṃ kāyena kammaṃ karomi idaṃ me kāyakammaṃ attabyābādhāyapi saṃvattati, parabyābādhāyapi saṃvattati, ubhayabyābādhāyapi saṃvattati – akusalaṃ idaṃ kāyakammaṃ dukkhudrayaṃ dukkhavipāka’nti, paṭisaṃhareyyāsi tvaṃ, rāhula, evarūpaṃ kāyakammaṃ. Sace pana tvaṃ, rāhula, paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jāneyyāsi – ‘yaṃ kho ahaṃ idaṃ kāyena kammaṃ karomi idaṃ me kāyakammaṃ nevattabyābādhāyapi [T 2.0128] saṃvattati, na parabyābādhāyapi saṃvattati, na ubhayabyābādhāyapi saṃvattati – kusalaṃ idaṃ kāyakammaṃ sukhudrayaṃ sukhavipāka’nti, anupadajjeyyāsi tvaṃ, rāhula, evarūpaṃ kāyakammaṃ.

“Rāhula, even while performing a bodily action, you should reflect upon that very bodily action: ‘Does this bodily action that I am performing lead to my own affliction, to the affliction of others, or to the affliction of both? Is this bodily action unwholesome, giving rise to suffering, with a painful result?’ If, Rāhula, upon reflection, you should know thus: ‘This bodily action that I am performing leads to my own affliction, to the affliction of others, and to the affliction of both; this bodily action is unwholesome, giving rise to suffering, with a painful result,’ then, Rāhula, you should desist from such a bodily action. But if, Rāhula, upon reflection, you should know thus: ‘This bodily action that I am performing leads neither to my own affliction, nor to the affliction of others, nor to the affliction of both; this bodily action is wholesome, giving rise to happiness, with a happy result,’ then, Rāhula, you should continue with such a bodily action.”

“Katvāpi te, rāhula, kāyena kammaṃ tadeva te kāyakammaṃ paccavekkhitabbaṃ – ‘yaṃ nu kho ahaṃ idaṃ kāyena kammaṃ akāsiṃ idaṃ me kāyakammaṃ attabyābādhāyapi saṃvattati saṃvatti (pī.), parabyābādhāyapi saṃvattati, ubhayabyābādhāyapi saṃvattati – akusalaṃ idaṃ kāyakammaṃ dukkhudrayaṃ dukkhavipāka’nti? Sace kho tvaṃ, rāhula, paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jāneyyāsi – ‘yaṃ kho ahaṃ idaṃ kāyena kammaṃ akāsiṃ, idaṃ me kāyakammaṃ attabyābādhāyapi saṃvattati, parabyābādhāyapi saṃvattati, ubhayabyābādhāyapi saṃvattati – akusalaṃ idaṃ kāyakammaṃ dukkhudrayaṃ dukkhavipāka’nti, evarūpaṃ te, rāhula, kāyakammaṃ satthari vā viññūsu vā sabrahmacārīsu [M 2.0080] desetabbaṃ, vivaritabbaṃ, uttānīkātabbaṃ; desetvā vivaritvā uttānīkatvā āyatiṃ saṃvaraṃ [P 1.0417] āpajjitabbaṃ[V 2.0087]. Sace pana tvaṃ, rāhula, paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jāneyyāsi – ‘yaṃ kho ahaṃ idaṃ kāyena kammaṃ akāsiṃ idaṃ me kāyakammaṃ nevattabyābādhāyapi saṃvattati, na parabyābādhāyapi saṃvattati, na ubhayabyābādhāyapi saṃvattati – kusalaṃ idaṃ kāyakammaṃ sukhudrayaṃ sukhavipāka’nti, teneva tvaṃ, rāhula, pītipāmojjena vihareyyāsi ahorattānusikkhī kusalesu dhammesu.

“Rāhula, even after having performed a bodily action, you should reflect upon that very bodily action: ‘Did this bodily action that I have done lead to my own affliction, to the affliction of others, or to the affliction of both? Was this bodily action unwholesome, giving rise to suffering, with a painful result?’ If, Rāhula, upon reflection, you should know thus: ‘This bodily action that I have done led to my own affliction, to the affliction of others, and to the affliction of both; this bodily action is unwholesome, giving rise to suffering, with a painful result,’ then, Rāhula, such a bodily action should be declared, revealed, and made plain to the Teacher, or to the wise, or to your companions in the holy life. Having declared, revealed, and made it plain, you should undertake restraint in the future. But if, Rāhula, upon reflection, you should know thus: ‘This bodily action that I have done led neither to my own affliction, nor to the affliction of others, nor to the affliction of both; this bodily action is wholesome, giving rise to happiness, with a happy result,’ then, Rāhula, with that very joy and gladness you should dwell, training day and night in wholesome states.”

110. “Yadeva tvaṃ, rāhula, vācāya kammaṃ kattukāmo ahosi, tadeva te vacīkammaṃ paccavekkhitabbaṃ – ‘yaṃ nu kho ahaṃ idaṃ vācāya kammaṃ kattukāmo idaṃ me vacīkammaṃ attabyābādhāyapi saṃvatteyya, parabyābādhāyapi saṃvatteyya, ubhayabyābādhāyapi saṃvatteyya – akusalaṃ idaṃ vacīkammaṃ dukkhudrayaṃ dukkhavipāka’nti? Sace tvaṃ, rāhula, paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jāneyyāsi – ‘yaṃ kho ahaṃ idaṃ vācāya kammaṃ kattukāmo idaṃ me vacīkammaṃ attabyābādhāyapi saṃvatteyya, parabyābādhāyapi saṃvatteyya, ubhayabyābādhāyapi saṃvatteyya – akusalaṃ idaṃ vacīkammaṃ dukkhudrayaṃ dukkhavipāka’nti, evarūpaṃ te, rāhula, vācāya kammaṃ sasakkaṃ na karaṇīyaṃ. Sace pana tvaṃ, rāhula, paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jāneyyāsi – ‘yaṃ kho ahaṃ idaṃ vācāya kammaṃ kattukāmo idaṃ me vacīkammaṃ nevattabyābādhāyapi saṃvatteyya, na parabyābādhāyapi saṃvatteyya – kusalaṃ idaṃ vacīkammaṃ sukhudrayaṃ sukhavipāka’nti, evarūpaṃ te, rāhula, vācāya kammaṃ karaṇīyaṃ.

110. “Rāhula, whatever verbal action you wish to perform, you should reflect upon that very verbal action: ‘This verbal action that I wish to perform—would it lead to my own affliction, to the affliction of others, or to the affliction of both? Is this verbal action unwholesome, giving rise to suffering, with a painful result?’ If, upon reflection, you know, Rāhula: ‘This verbal action that I wish to perform would lead to my own affliction, to the affliction of others, or to the affliction of both; this verbal action is unwholesome, giving rise to suffering, with a painful result,’ then, Rāhula, such a verbal action should certainly not be done by you. But if, upon reflection, you know, Rāhula: ‘This verbal action that I wish to perform would not lead to my own affliction, nor to the affliction of others, nor to the affliction of both; this verbal action is wholesome, giving rise to happiness, with a happy result,’ then, Rāhula, such a verbal action should be done by you.”

“Karontenapi, rāhula, vācāya kammaṃ tadeva te vacīkammaṃ paccavekkhitabbaṃ – ‘yaṃ nu kho ahaṃ idaṃ vācāya kammaṃ karomi idaṃ me vacīkammaṃ attabyābādhāyapi saṃvattati, parabyābādhāyapi [T 2.0129] saṃvattati, ubhayabyābādhāyapi saṃvattati – akusalaṃ idaṃ vacīkammaṃ dukkhudrayaṃ dukkhavipāka’nti? Sace pana tvaṃ, rāhula, paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jāneyyāsi – ‘yaṃ kho ahaṃ idaṃ vācāya kammaṃ karomi idaṃ me vacīkammaṃ attabyābādhāyapi saṃvattati, parabyābādhāyapi saṃvattati, ubhayabyābādhāyapi saṃvattati – akusalaṃ idaṃ vacīkammaṃ dukkhudrayaṃ dukkhavipāka’nti, paṭisaṃhareyyāsi tvaṃ, rāhula, evarūpaṃ vacīkammaṃ. Sace pana tvaṃ, rāhula, paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jāneyyāsi – ‘yaṃ kho ahaṃ idaṃ vācāya kammaṃ karomi idaṃ me vacīkammaṃ [M 2.0081] nevattabyābādhāyapi saṃvattati, na parabyābādhāyapi saṃvattati, na [P 1.0418] ubhayabyābādhāyapi saṃvattati [V 2.0088] – kusalaṃ idaṃ vacīkammaṃ sukhudrayaṃ sukhavipāka’nti, anupadajjeyyāsi, tvaṃ rāhula, evarūpaṃ vacīkammaṃ.

“Rāhula, even while performing a verbal action, you should reflect upon that very verbal action: ‘Does this verbal action that I am performing lead to my own affliction, to the affliction of others, or to the affliction of both? Is this verbal action unwholesome, giving rise to suffering, with a painful result?’ If, upon reflection, you know, Rāhula: ‘This verbal action that I am performing leads to my own affliction, to the affliction of others, and to the affliction of both; this verbal action is unwholesome, giving rise to suffering, with a painful result,’ then, Rāhula, you should desist from such a verbal action. But if, upon reflection, you know, Rāhula: ‘This verbal action that I am performing does not lead to my own affliction, nor to the affliction of others, nor to the affliction of both; this verbal action is wholesome, giving rise to happiness, with a happy result,’ then, Rāhula, you should continue with such a verbal action.”

“Katvāpi te, rāhula, vācāya kammaṃ tadeva te vacīkammaṃ paccavekkhitabbaṃ – ‘yaṃ nu kho ahaṃ idaṃ vācāya kammaṃ akāsiṃ idaṃ me vacīkammaṃ attabyābādhāyapi saṃvattati saṃvatti (sī. pī.), parabyābādhāyapi saṃvattati, ubhayabyābādhāyapi saṃvattati – akusalaṃ idaṃ vacīkammaṃ dukkhudrayaṃ dukkhavipāka’nti? Sace kho tvaṃ, rāhula, paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jāneyyāsi – ‘yaṃ kho ahaṃ idaṃ vācāya kammaṃ akāsiṃ idaṃ me vacīkammaṃ attabyābādhāyapi saṃvattati, parabyābādhāyapi saṃvattati, ubhayabyābādhāyapi saṃvattati – akusalaṃ idaṃ vacīkammaṃ dukkhudrayaṃ dukkhavipāka’nti, evarūpaṃ te, rāhula, vacīkammaṃ satthari vā viññūsu vā sabrahmacārīsu desetabbaṃ, vivaritabbaṃ, uttānīkattabbaṃ[T 2.0130]; desetvā vivaritvā uttānīkatvā āyatiṃ saṃvaraṃ āpajjitabbaṃ. Sace pana tvaṃ, rāhula, paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jāneyyāsi – ‘yaṃ kho ahaṃ idaṃ vācāya kammaṃ akāsiṃ idaṃ me vacīkammaṃ nevattabyābādhāyapi saṃvattati, na parabyābādhāyapi saṃvattati, na ubhayabyābādhāyapi saṃvattati – kusalaṃ idaṃ vacīkammaṃ sukhudrayaṃ sukhavipāka’nti, teneva tvaṃ, rāhula, pītipāmojjena vihareyyāsi ahorattānusikkhī kusalesu dhammesu.

Rāhula, even after having performed a verbal action, you should reflect upon that very verbal action: ‘This verbal action that I have performed—did it lead to my own affliction, to the affliction of others, or to the affliction of both? Was this verbal action unwholesome, giving rise to suffering, and having a painful result?’ If, upon reflection, you know, Rāhula: ‘This verbal action that I have performed led to my own affliction, to the affliction of others, and to the affliction of both; this verbal action was unwholesome, giving rise to suffering, and having a painful result,’ then, Rāhula, such a verbal action should be declared to the Teacher or to the wise or to your companions in the holy life; it should be disclosed and laid open. Having declared, disclosed, and laid it open, you should undertake restraint in the future. But if, upon reflection, you know, Rāhula: ‘This verbal action that I have performed did not lead to my own affliction, nor to the affliction of others, nor to the affliction of both; this verbal action was wholesome, giving rise to happiness, and having a pleasant result,’ then, Rāhula, with that same joy and gladness you should dwell, training day and night in wholesome states.

111. “Yadeva tvaṃ, rāhula, manasā kammaṃ kattukāmo ahosi, tadeva te manokammaṃ paccavekkhitabbaṃ – ‘yaṃ nu kho ahaṃ idaṃ manasā kammaṃ kattukāmo idaṃ me manokammaṃ attabyābādhāyapi saṃvatteyya, parabyābādhāyapi saṃvatteyya, ubhayabyābādhāyapi saṃvatteyya – akusalaṃ idaṃ manokammaṃ dukkhudrayaṃ dukkhavipāka’nti? Sace tvaṃ, rāhula, paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jāneyyāsi – ‘yaṃ kho ahaṃ idaṃ manasā kammaṃ kattukāmo idaṃ me manokammaṃ attabyābādhāyapi saṃvatteyya, parabyābādhāyapi saṃvatteyya, ubhayabyābādhāyapi saṃvatteyya – akusalaṃ idaṃ manokammaṃ dukkhudrayaṃ dukkhavipāka’nti, evarūpaṃ te, rāhula, manasā kammaṃ sasakkaṃ na karaṇīyaṃ. Sace pana tvaṃ, rāhula, paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jāneyyāsi – ‘yaṃ kho ahaṃ [M 2.0082] idaṃ manasā kammaṃ kattukāmo idaṃ me manokammaṃ nevattabyābādhāyapi saṃvatteyya, na parabyābādhāyapi [V 2.0089] saṃvatteyya, na ubhayabyābādhāyapi saṃvatteyya – kusalaṃ idaṃ manokammaṃ [T 2.0131] sukhudrayaṃ [P 1.0419] sukhavipāka’nti, evarūpaṃ te, rāhula, manasā kammaṃ karaṇīyaṃ.

111. Rāhula, whatever mental action you wish to perform, you should reflect upon that very mental action: ‘This mental action that I wish to perform—would it lead to my own affliction, to the affliction of others, or to the affliction of both? Is this mental action unwholesome, giving rise to suffering, and having a painful result?’ If, upon reflection, you know, Rāhula: ‘This mental action that I wish to perform would lead to my own affliction, to the affliction of others, and to the affliction of both; this mental action is unwholesome, giving rise to suffering, and having a painful result,’ then, Rāhula, such a mental action should certainly not be done by you. But if, upon reflection, you know, Rāhula: ‘This mental action that I wish to perform would not lead to my own affliction, nor to the affliction of others, nor to the affliction of both; this mental action is wholesome, giving rise to happiness, and having a pleasant result,’ then, Rāhula, such a mental action should be done by you.

“Karontenapi te, rāhula, manasā kammaṃ tadeva te manokammaṃ paccavekkhitabbaṃ – ‘yaṃ nu kho ahaṃ idaṃ manasā kammaṃ karomi idaṃ me manokammaṃ attabyābādhāyapi saṃvattati, parabyābādhāyapi saṃvattati, ubhayabyābādhāyapi saṃvattati – akusalaṃ idaṃ manokammaṃ dukkhudrayaṃ dukkhavipāka’nti? Sace pana tvaṃ, rāhula, paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jāneyyāsi – ‘yaṃ kho ahaṃ idaṃ manasā kammaṃ karomi idaṃ me manokammaṃ attabyābādhāyapi saṃvattati, parabyābādhāyapi saṃvattati, ubhayabyābādhāyapi saṃvattati – akusalaṃ idaṃ manokammaṃ dukkhudrayaṃ dukkhavipāka’nti, paṭisaṃhareyyāsi tvaṃ, rāhula, evarūpaṃ manokammaṃ. Sace pana tvaṃ, rāhula, paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jāneyyāsi – ‘yaṃ kho ahaṃ idaṃ manasā kammaṃ karomi idaṃ me manokammaṃ nevattabyābādhāyapi saṃvattati, na parabyābādhāyapi saṃvattati, na ubhayabyābādhāyapi saṃvattati – kusalaṃ idaṃ manokammaṃ sukhudrayaṃ sukhavipāka’nti, anupadajjeyyāsi tvaṃ, rāhula, evarūpaṃ manokammaṃ.

Rāhula, while you are performing a mental action, you should reflect upon that very mental action: ‘This mental action that I am now performing—does it conduce to my own affliction, to the affliction of others, or to the affliction of both? Is this mental action unwholesome, giving rise to suffering, and having a painful result?’ If, upon reflection, you know, Rāhula: ‘This mental action that I am performing conduces to my own affliction, to the affliction of others, and to the affliction of both; this mental action is unwholesome, giving rise to suffering, and having a painful result,’ then, Rāhula, you should desist from such a mental action. But if, upon reflection, you know, Rāhula: ‘This mental action that I am performing conduces neither to my own affliction, nor to the affliction of others, nor to the affliction of both; this mental action is wholesome, giving rise to happiness, and having a pleasant result,’ then, Rāhula, you should continue with such a mental action.

“Katvāpi te, rāhula, manasā kammaṃ tadeva te manokammaṃ paccavekkhitabbaṃ – ‘yaṃ nu kho ahaṃ idaṃ manasā kammaṃ akāsiṃ idaṃ me manokammaṃ attabyābādhāyapi saṃvattati saṃvatti (sī. pī.), parabyābādhāyapi saṃvattati, ubhayabyābādhāyapi saṃvattati – akusalaṃ idaṃ manokammaṃ dukkhudrayaṃ dukkhavipāka’nti? Sace kho tvaṃ, rāhula, paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jāneyyāsi – ‘yaṃ [T 2.0132] kho ahaṃ idaṃ manasā kammaṃ akāsiṃ idaṃ me manokammaṃ attabyābādhāyapi saṃvattati, parabyābādhāyapi saṃvattati, ubhayabyābādhāyapi saṃvattati – akusalaṃ idaṃ manokammaṃ dukkhudrayaṃ dukkhavipāka’nti, evarūpaṃ pana evarūpe (sī. pī.), evarūpe pana (syā. kaṃ.) te, rāhula, manokammaṃ manokamme (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) aṭṭīyitabbaṃ harāyitabbaṃ jigucchitabbaṃ; aṭṭīyitvā harāyitvā jigucchitvā āyatiṃ saṃvaraṃ āpajjitabbaṃ. Sace pana tvaṃ, rāhula, paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jāneyyāsi – ‘yaṃ kho ahaṃ idaṃ manasā kammaṃ akāsiṃ [M 2.0083] idaṃ me manokammaṃ nevattabyābādhāyapi saṃvattati, na parabyābādhāyapi saṃvattati, na ubhayabyābādhāyapi saṃvattati – kusalaṃ idaṃ manokammaṃ sukhudrayaṃ sukhavipāka’nti, teneva tvaṃ, rāhula, pītipāmojjena vihareyyāsi ahorattānusikkhī kusalesu dhammesu.

Rāhula, even after having performed a mental action, you should reflect upon that very mental action: ‘This mental action that I have performed—did it lead to my own affliction, to the affliction of others, or to the affliction of both? Was this mental action unwholesome, giving rise to suffering, and having a painful result?’ If, upon reflection, you know, Rāhula: ‘This mental action that I have performed led to my own affliction, to the affliction of others, and to the affliction of both; this mental action was unwholesome, giving rise to suffering, and having a painful result,’ then, Rāhula, you should be distressed by, ashamed of, and disgusted with such a mental action. Having been distressed, ashamed, and disgusted, you should undertake restraint in the future. But if, upon reflection, you know, Rāhula: ‘This mental action that I have performed did not lead to my own affliction, nor to the affliction of others, nor to the affliction of both; this mental action was wholesome, giving rise to happiness, and having a pleasant result,’ then, Rāhula, with that very joy and gladness you should dwell, training day and night in wholesome states.

112. “Ye [V 2.0090][P 1.0420] hi keci, rāhula, atītamaddhānaṃ samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā kāyakammaṃ parisodhesuṃ, vacīkammaṃ parisodhesuṃ, manokammaṃ parisodhesuṃ, sabbe te evamevaṃ paccavekkhitvā paccavekkhitvā kāyakammaṃ parisodhesuṃ, paccavekkhitvā paccavekkhitvā vacīkammaṃ parisodhesuṃ, paccavekkhitvā paccavekkhitvā manokammaṃ parisodhesuṃ. Yepi hi keci, rāhula, anāgatamaddhānaṃ samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā kāyakammaṃ parisodhessanti, vacīkammaṃ parisodhessanti, manokammaṃ parisodhessanti, sabbe te evamevaṃ paccavekkhitvā paccavekkhitvā kāyakammaṃ parisodhessanti, paccavekkhitvā paccavekkhitvā vacīkammaṃ parisodhessanti[T 2.0133], paccavekkhitvā paccavekkhitvā manokammaṃ parisodhessanti. Yepi hi keci, rāhula, etarahi samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā kāyakammaṃ parisodhenti, vacīkammaṃ parisodhenti, manokammaṃ parisodhenti, sabbe te evamevaṃ paccavekkhitvā paccavekkhitvā kāyakammaṃ parisodhenti, paccavekkhitvā paccavekkhitvā vacīkammaṃ parisodhenti, paccavekkhitvā paccavekkhitvā manokammaṃ parisodhenti. Tasmātiha, rāhula, ‘paccavekkhitvā paccavekkhitvā kāyakammaṃ parisodhessāmi, paccavekkhitvā paccavekkhitvā vacīkammaṃ parisodhessāmi, paccavekkhitvā paccavekkhitvā manokammaṃ parisodhessāmī’ti – evañhi te, rāhula, sikkhitabba”nti.

112. Rāhula, whatever ascetics or brahmins in the past purified their bodily action, verbal action, and mental action, all of them did so in this very way: by reflecting again and again they purified their bodily action; by reflecting again and again they purified their verbal action; and by reflecting again and again they purified their mental action. Whatever ascetics or brahmins in the future will purify their bodily action, verbal action, and mental action, all of them will do so in this very way: by reflecting again and again they will purify their bodily action; by reflecting again and again they will purify their verbal action; and by reflecting again and again they will purify their mental action. Whatever ascetics or brahmins at present are purifying their bodily action, verbal action, and mental action, all of them are doing so in this very way: by reflecting again and again they are purifying their bodily action; by reflecting again and again they are purifying their verbal action; and by reflecting again and again they are purifying their mental action. Therefore, Rāhula, you should train thus: ‘By reflecting again and again I will purify my bodily action; by reflecting again and again I will purify my verbal action; and by reflecting again and again I will purify my mental action.’ Thus indeed, Rāhula, should you train.

Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamano āyasmā rāhulo bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandīti.

The Blessed One said this. The Venerable Rāhula, pleased, rejoiced in the Blessed One's discourse.

Ambalaṭṭhikarāhulovādasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ paṭhamaṃ.

The Ambalaṭṭhika-Rāhulovāda Sutta, the first, is concluded.

2. Mahārāhulovādasuttaṃ

2. The Great Discourse of Exhortation to Rāhula

113. Evaṃ [T 2.0134][V 2.0091] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Atha kho bhagavā pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya sāvatthiṃ piṇḍāya pāvisi. Āyasmāpi kho [M 2.0084] rāhulo pubbaṇhasamayaṃ [P 1.0421] nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya bhagavantaṃ piṭṭhito piṭṭhito anubandhi. Atha kho bhagavā apaloketvā āyasmantaṃ rāhulaṃ āmantesi – “yaṃ kiñci, rāhula, rūpaṃ – atītānāgatapaccuppannaṃ ajjhattaṃ vā bahiddhā vā oḷārikaṃ vā sukhumaṃ vā hīnaṃ vā paṇītaṃ vā yaṃ dūre santike vā – sabbaṃ rūpaṃ ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya daṭṭhabba”nti. “Rūpameva nu kho, bhagavā, rūpameva nu kho, sugatā”ti? “Rūpampi, rāhula, vedanāpi, rāhula, saññāpi, rāhula, saṅkhārāpi, rāhula, viññāṇampi, rāhulā”ti. Atha kho āyasmā rāhulo “ko najja ko nujja (syā. kaṃ.) bhagavatā sammukhā ovādena ovadito gāmaṃ piṇḍāya pavisissatī”ti tato paṭinivattitvā aññatarasmiṃ rukkhamūle nisīdi pallaṅkaṃ ābhujitvā ujuṃ kāyaṃ paṇidhāya parimukhaṃ satiṃ upaṭṭhapetvā. Addasā kho āyasmā sāriputto āyasmantaṃ rāhulaṃ aññatarasmiṃ rukkhamūle nisinnaṃ pallaṅkaṃ ābhujitvā ujuṃ kāyaṃ paṇidhāya parimukhaṃ satiṃ upaṭṭhapetvā[T 2.0135]. Disvāna āyasmantaṃ rāhulaṃ āmantesi – “ānāpānassatiṃ, rāhula, bhāvanaṃ bhāvehi. Ānāpānassati, rāhula, bhāvanā bhāvitā bahulīkatā mahapphalā hoti mahānisaṃsā”ti.

113. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. Then the Blessed One, having dressed in the morning, took his bowl and robe and entered Sāvatthī for alms. And the Venerable Rāhula also, having dressed in the morning, took his bowl and robe and followed right behind the Blessed One. Then the Blessed One, turning around, addressed the Venerable Rāhula: “Rāhula, whatever form there is—past, future, or present; internal or external; gross or subtle; inferior or superior; far or near—all form should be seen as it really is with proper wisdom: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.’” “Is it only form, Blessed One? Is it only form, Sugata?” “Form also, Rāhula; feeling also, Rāhula; perception also, Rāhula; formations also, Rāhula; and consciousness also, Rāhula.” Then the Venerable Rāhula thought: “Who today, having been exhorted face to face by the Blessed One, would enter the village for alms?” He then turned back from there and sat down at the foot of a certain tree, folding his legs crosswise, setting his body erect, and establishing mindfulness before him. The Venerable Sāriputta saw the Venerable Rāhula sitting at the foot of a certain tree, folding his legs crosswise, setting his body erect, and establishing mindfulness before him. Seeing this, he addressed the Venerable Rāhula: “Rāhula, develop the meditation of mindfulness of breathing. Mindfulness of breathing, Rāhula, when developed and cultivated, is of great fruit and great benefit.”

114. Atha kho āyasmā rāhulo sāyanhasamayaṃ paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā rāhulo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “kathaṃ bhāvitā nu kho, bhante, ānāpānassati, kathaṃ bahulīkatā mahapphalā hoti mahānisaṃsā”ti? “Yaṃ kiñci, rāhula, ajjhattaṃ paccattaṃ kakkhaḷaṃ kharigataṃ upādinnaṃ, seyyathidaṃ – kesā lomā nakhā dantā taco maṃsaṃ nhāru nahāru (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) aṭṭhi aṭṭhimiñjaṃ vakkaṃ hadayaṃ yakanaṃ kilomakaṃ pihakaṃ papphāsaṃ antaṃ antaguṇaṃ udariyaṃ karīsaṃ, yaṃ [V 2.0092] vā panaññampi kiñci ajjhattaṃ paccattaṃ kakkhaḷaṃ kharigataṃ upādinnaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati, rāhula, ajjhattikā pathavīdhātu paṭhavīdhātu (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.). Yā ceva kho pana ajjhattikā pathavīdhātu yā ca bāhirā pathavīdhātu, pathavīdhāturevesā. Taṃ ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti – evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya daṭṭhabbaṃ. Evametaṃ [P 1.0422] yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya disvā pathavīdhātuyā nibbindati, pathavīdhātuyā cittaṃ virājeti”.

114. Then, in the evening, the Venerable Rāhula arose from seclusion and approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Sitting to one side, the Venerable Rāhula said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, how is mindfulness of breathing developed, how is it cultivated, so that it is of great fruit and great benefit?” “Rāhula, whatever is internal, personal, hard, solid, and clung to—that is to say: head hairs, body hairs, nails, teeth, skin, flesh, sinews, bones, bone marrow, kidneys, heart, liver, pleura, spleen, lungs, intestines, mesentery, stomach contents, feces, or whatever else is internal, personal, hard, solid, and clung to—this, Rāhula, is called the internal earth element. Both the internal earth element and the external earth element are simply the earth element. This should be seen as it really is with proper wisdom: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.’ Seeing this as it really is with proper wisdom, one becomes disenchanted with the earth element and detaches the mind from the earth element.”

115. “Katamā [M 2.0085] ca, rāhula, āpodhātu? Āpodhātu siyā ajjhattikā, siyā bāhirā. Katamā ca, rāhula, ajjhattikā āpodhātu[T 2.0136]? Yaṃ ajjhattaṃ paccattaṃ āpo āpogataṃ upādinnaṃ, seyyathidaṃ – pittaṃ semhaṃ pubbo lohitaṃ sedo medo assu vasā kheḷo siṅghāṇikā lasikā muttaṃ, yaṃ vā panaññampi kiñci ajjhattaṃ paccattaṃ āpo āpogataṃ upādinnaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati, rāhula, ajjhattikā āpodhātu. Yā ceva kho pana ajjhattikā āpodhātu yā ca bāhirā āpodhātu āpodhāturevesā. Taṃ ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti – evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya daṭṭhabbaṃ. Evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya disvā āpodhātuyā nibbindati, āpodhātuyā cittaṃ virājeti.

115. “And what, Rāhula, is the water element? The water element may be internal or external. And what, Rāhula, is the internal water element? Whatever is internal, personal, liquid, fluid, and clung to—that is to say: bile, phlegm, pus, blood, sweat, fat, tears, grease, saliva, snot, synovial fluid, and urine; or whatever else is internal, personal, liquid, fluid, and clung to—this, Rāhula, is called the internal water element. Now, both the internal water element and the external water element are simply the water element. This should be seen as it really is with right wisdom: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.’ Seeing it thus as it really is with right wisdom, one becomes disenchanted with the water element and detaches the mind from the water element.”

116. “Katamā ca, rāhula, tejodhātu? Tejodhātu siyā ajjhattikā, siyā bāhirā. Katamā ca, rāhula, ajjhattikā tejodhātu? Yaṃ ajjhattaṃ paccattaṃ tejo tejogataṃ upādinnaṃ, seyyathidaṃ – yena ca santappati yena ca jīrīyati yena ca pariḍayhati yena ca asitapītakhāyitasāyitaṃ sammā pariṇāmaṃ gacchati, yaṃ vā panaññampi kiñci ajjhattaṃ paccattaṃ tejo tejogataṃ upādinnaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati, rāhula, ajjhattikā tejodhātu. Yā ceva kho pana ajjhattikā tejodhātu yā ca bāhirā tejodhātu tejodhāturevesā. Taṃ ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti – evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya daṭṭhabbaṃ. Evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya disvā tejodhātuyā nibbindati, tejodhātuyā cittaṃ virājeti.

116. “And what, Rāhula, is the fire element? The fire element may be internal or external. And what, Rāhula, is the internal fire element? Whatever is internal, personal, heat, fiery, and clung to—that is to say: that by which one is warmed, ages, and is burnt up; and that by which what is eaten, drunk, chewed, and tasted is properly digested; or whatever else is internal, personal, heat, fiery, and clung to—this, Rāhula, is called the internal fire element. Now, both the internal fire element and the external fire element are simply the fire element. This should be seen as it really is with right wisdom: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.’ Seeing it thus as it really is with right wisdom, one becomes disenchanted with the fire element and detaches the mind from the fire element.”

117. “Katamā [T 2.0137] ca, rāhula, vāyodhātu? Vāyodhātu siyā ajjhattikā, siyā bāhirā. Katamā ca, rāhula, ajjhattikā vāyodhātu? Yaṃ ajjhattaṃ paccattaṃ vāyo vāyogataṃ upādinnaṃ, seyyathidaṃ – uddhaṅgamā vātā, adhogamā vātā, kucchisayā vātā, koṭṭhāsayā koṭṭhasayā (sī. pī.) vātā[V 2.0093], aṅgamaṅgānusārino vātā, assāso passāso, iti yaṃ vā panaññampi kiñci ajjhattaṃ paccattaṃ vāyo vāyogataṃ upādinnaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati, rāhula, ajjhattikā vāyodhātu. Yā ceva kho pana ajjhattikā vāyodhātu yā ca bāhirā vāyodhātu vāyodhāturevesā. Taṃ ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi[M 2.0086], na meso attā’ti – evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya [P 1.0423] daṭṭhabbaṃ. Evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya disvā vāyodhātuyā nibbindati, vāyodhātuyā cittaṃ virājeti.

117. “And what, Rāhula, is the wind element? The wind element may be internal or external. And what, Rāhula, is the internal wind element? Whatever is internal, personal, wind, windy, and clung to—that is to say: upward-going winds, downward-going winds, winds in the belly, winds in the bowels, winds that course through the limbs, the in-breath and the out-breath; or whatever else is internal, personal, wind, windy, and clung to—this, Rāhula, is called the internal wind element. Now, both the internal wind element and the external wind element are simply the wind element. This should be seen as it really is with right wisdom: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.’ Seeing it thus as it really is with right wisdom, one becomes disenchanted with the wind element and detaches the mind from the wind element.”

118. “Katamā ca, rāhula, ākāsadhātu? Ākāsadhātu siyā ajjhattikā, siyā bāhirā. Katamā ca, rāhula, ajjhattikā ākāsadhātu? Yaṃ ajjhattaṃ paccattaṃ ākāsaṃ ākāsagataṃ upādinnaṃ, seyyathidaṃ – kaṇṇacchiddaṃ nāsacchiddaṃ mukhadvāraṃ, yena ca asitapītakhāyitasāyitaṃ ajjhoharati, yattha ca asitapītakhāyitasāyitaṃ santiṭṭhati, yena ca asitapītakhāyitasāyitaṃ adhobhāgaṃ adhobhāgā (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) nikkhamati, yaṃ vā panaññampi kiñci ajjhattaṃ paccattaṃ ākāsaṃ ākāsagataṃ, aghaṃ aghagataṃ, vivaraṃ vivaragataṃ, asamphuṭṭhaṃ, maṃsalohitehi upādinnaṃ [T 2.0138] ākāsagataṃ upādinnaṃ (sī. pī.) – ayaṃ vuccati, rāhula, ajjhattikā ākāsadhātu. Yā ceva kho pana ajjhattikā ākāsadhātu yā ca bāhirā ākāsadhātu ākāsadhāturevesā. Taṃ ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti – evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya daṭṭhabbaṃ. Evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya disvā ākāsadhātuyā cittaṃ nibbindati, ākāsadhātuyā cittaṃ virājeti.

118. “And what, Rāhula, is the space element? The space element may be internal or external. And what, Rāhula, is the internal space element? Whatever is internal, personal, space, spatial, and clung to—that is to say: the ear-hole, the nostril, the opening of the mouth; and that by which one swallows what is eaten, drunk, chewed, and tasted; and where what is eaten, drunk, chewed, and tasted remains; and that by which what is eaten, drunk, chewed, and tasted is expelled from the lower part; or whatever else is internal, personal, space, spatial, void, vacuity, an aperture, a cavity, and, being untouched by flesh and blood, is clung to—this, Rāhula, is called the internal space element. Now, both the internal space element and the external space element are simply the space element. This should be seen as it really is with right wisdom: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.’ Seeing it thus as it really is with right wisdom, one becomes disenchanted with the space element and detaches the mind from the space element.”

119. “Pathavīsamaṃ, rāhula, bhāvanaṃ bhāvehi. Pathavīsamañhi te, rāhula, bhāvanaṃ bhāvayato uppannā manāpāmanāpā phassā cittaṃ na pariyādāya ṭhassanti. Seyyathāpi, rāhula, pathaviyā sucimpi nikkhipanti, asucimpi nikkhipanti, gūthagatampi nikkhipanti, muttagatampi nikkhipanti, kheḷagatampi nikkhipanti, pubbagatampi nikkhipanti, lohitagatampi nikkhipanti, na ca tena pathavī aṭṭīyati vā harāyati vā jigucchati vā; evameva kho tvaṃ, rāhula, pathavīsamaṃ bhāvanaṃ bhāvehi. Pathavīsamañhi te, rāhula, bhāvanaṃ bhāvayato uppannā manāpāmanāpā phassā cittaṃ na pariyādāya ṭhassanti.

119. “Develop the meditation, Rāhula, to be like the earth. For when you are developing the meditation to be like the earth, arisen pleasant and unpleasant contacts will not take possession of your mind and remain. Just as, Rāhula, people throw clean things on the earth, and they also throw unclean things, they throw feces, they throw urine, they throw spittle, they throw pus, and they throw blood, yet the earth is not troubled, humiliated, or disgusted by that; in the same way, Rāhula, develop the meditation to be like the earth. For when you are developing the meditation to be like the earth, arisen pleasant and unpleasant contacts will not take possession of your mind and remain.”

“Āposamaṃ, rāhula, bhāvanaṃ bhāvehi. Āposamañhi te, rāhula, bhāvanaṃ bhāvayato uppannā manāpāmanāpā phassā cittaṃ na pariyādāya ṭhassanti. Seyyathāpi, rāhula, āpasmiṃ sucimpi [V 2.0094] dhovanti, asucimpi dhovanti, gūthagatampi dhovanti, muttagatampi dhovanti, kheḷagatampi dhovanti, pubbagatampi dhovanti, lohitagatampi dhovanti, na ca [T 2.0139] tena āpo aṭṭīyati [M 2.0087] vā harāyati vā jigucchati vā; evameva kho [P 1.0424] tvaṃ, rāhula, āposamaṃ bhāvanaṃ bhāvehi. Āposamañhi te, rāhula, bhāvanaṃ bhāvayato uppannā manāpāmanāpā phassā cittaṃ na pariyādāya ṭhassanti.

“Develop the meditation, Rāhula, to be like water. For when you are developing the meditation to be like water, arisen pleasant and unpleasant contacts will not take possession of your mind and remain. Just as, Rāhula, people wash clean things in water, and they also wash unclean things, they wash feces, they wash urine, they wash spittle, they wash pus, and they wash blood, yet the water is not troubled, humiliated, or disgusted by that; in the same way, Rāhula, develop the meditation to be like water. For when you are developing the meditation to be like water, arisen pleasant and unpleasant contacts will not take possession of your mind and remain.”

“Tejosamaṃ, rāhula, bhāvanaṃ bhāvehi. Tejosamañhi te, rāhula, bhāvanaṃ bhāvayato uppannā manāpāmanāpā phassā cittaṃ na pariyādāya ṭhassanti. Seyyathāpi, rāhula, tejo sucimpi dahati, asucimpi dahati, gūthagatampi dahati, muttagatampi dahati, kheḷagatampi dahati, pubbagatampi dahati, lohitagatampi dahati, na ca tena tejo aṭṭīyati vā harāyati vā jigucchati vā; evameva kho tvaṃ, rāhula, tejosamaṃ bhāvanaṃ bhāvehi. Tejosamañhi te, rāhula, bhāvanaṃ bhāvayato uppannā manāpāmanāpā phassā cittaṃ na pariyādāya ṭhassanti.

“Rāhula, develop the development that is like fire. For, Rāhula, when you are developing the development that is like fire, arisen pleasant and unpleasant contacts will not take possession of your mind and remain. Just as, Rāhula, fire burns clean things and also burns unclean things; it burns feces, urine, spittle, pus, and blood, yet the fire is not troubled, ashamed, or disgusted by that. In the same way, Rāhula, develop the development that is like fire. For, Rāhula, when you are developing the development that is like fire, arisen pleasant and unpleasant contacts will not take possession of your mind and remain.”

“Vāyosamaṃ, rāhula, bhāvanaṃ bhāvehi. Vāyosamañhi te, rāhula, bhāvanaṃ bhāvayato uppannā manāpāmanāpā phassā cittaṃ na pariyādāya ṭhassanti. Seyyathāpi, rāhula, vāyo sucimpi upavāyati, asucimpi upavāyati, gūthagatampi upavāyati, muttagatampi upavāyati, kheḷagatampi upavāyati, pubbagatampi upavāyati, lohitagatampi upavāyati, na ca tena vāyo aṭṭīyati vā harāyati vā jigucchati vā; evameva kho tvaṃ, rāhula, vāyosamaṃ bhāvanaṃ bhāvehi. Vāyosamañhi te, rāhula, bhāvanaṃ bhāvayato uppannā manāpāmanāpā phassā cittaṃ na pariyādāya [T 2.0140] ṭhassanti.

“Rāhula, develop the development that is like the wind. For, Rāhula, when you are developing the development that is like the wind, arisen pleasant and unpleasant contacts will not take possession of your mind and remain. Just as, Rāhula, the wind blows on clean things and also blows on unclean things; it blows on feces, urine, spittle, pus, and blood, yet the wind is not troubled, ashamed, or disgusted by that. In the same way, Rāhula, develop the development that is like the wind. For, Rāhula, when you are developing the development that is like the wind, arisen pleasant and unpleasant contacts will not take possession of your mind and remain.”

“Ākāsasamaṃ, rāhula, bhāvanaṃ bhāvehi. Ākāsasamañhi te, rāhula, bhāvanaṃ bhāvayato uppannā manāpāmanāpā phassā cittaṃ na pariyādāya ṭhassanti. Seyyathāpi, rāhula, ākāso na katthaci patiṭṭhito; evameva kho tvaṃ, rāhula, ākāsasamaṃ bhāvanaṃ bhāvehi. Ākāsasamañhi te, rāhula, bhāvanaṃ bhāvayato uppannā manāpāmanāpā phassā cittaṃ na pariyādāya ṭhassanti.

“Rāhula, develop the development that is like space. For, Rāhula, when you are developing the development that is like space, arisen pleasant and unpleasant contacts will not take possession of your mind and remain. Just as, Rāhula, space is not established anywhere, in the same way, Rāhula, develop the development that is like space. For, Rāhula, when you are developing the development that is like space, arisen pleasant and unpleasant contacts will not take possession of your mind and remain.”

120. “Mettaṃ, rāhula, bhāvanaṃ bhāvehi. Mettañhi te, rāhula, bhāvanaṃ bhāvayato yo byāpādo [V 2.0095] so pahīyissati. Karuṇaṃ, rāhula, bhāvanaṃ bhāvehi. Karuṇañhi te, rāhula, bhāvanaṃ bhāvayato yā vihesā sā pahīyissati. Muditaṃ, rāhula, bhāvanaṃ bhāvehi. Muditañhi te, rāhula, bhāvanaṃ bhāvayato yā arati sā pahīyissati. Upekkhaṃ[M 2.0088], rāhula, bhāvanaṃ bhāvehi. Upekkhañhi te, rāhula, bhāvanaṃ bhāvayato yo paṭigho so pahīyissati. Asubhaṃ, rāhula, bhāvanaṃ bhāvehi. Asubhañhi te, rāhula, bhāvanaṃ bhāvayato yo rāgo so pahīyissati. Aniccasaññaṃ, rāhula, bhāvanaṃ bhāvehi. Aniccasaññañhi [P 1.0425] te, rāhula, bhāvanaṃ bhāvayato yo asmimāno so pahīyissati.

120. “Rāhula, develop the development of loving-kindness. For, Rāhula, when you are developing the development of loving-kindness, whatever ill will there is will be abandoned. Rāhula, develop the development of compassion. For, Rāhula, when you are developing the development of compassion, whatever cruelty there is will be abandoned. Rāhula, develop the development of sympathetic joy. For, Rāhula, when you are developing the development of sympathetic joy, whatever discontent there is will be abandoned. Rāhula, develop the development of equanimity. For, Rāhula, when you are developing the development of equanimity, whatever aversion there is will be abandoned. Rāhula, develop the development of foulness. For, Rāhula, when you are developing the development of foulness, whatever lust there is will be abandoned. Rāhula, develop the development of the perception of impermanence. For, Rāhula, when you are developing the development of the perception of impermanence, whatever conceit ‘I am’ there is will be abandoned.”

121. “Ānāpānassatiṃ, rāhula, bhāvanaṃ bhāvehi. Ānāpānassati hi te, rāhula, bhāvitā bahulīkatā mahapphalā hoti mahānisaṃsā. Kathaṃ bhāvitā ca, rāhula, ānāpānassati, kathaṃ bahulīkatā mahapphalā hoti mahānisaṃsā[T 2.0141]? Idha, rāhula, bhikkhu araññagato vā rukkhamūlagato vā suññāgāragato vā nisīdati pallaṅkaṃ ābhujitvā ujuṃ kāyaṃ paṇidhāya parimukhaṃ satiṃ upaṭṭhapetvā. So satova assasati satova sato (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) passasati.

121. “Rāhula, develop the development of mindfulness of breathing. For, Rāhula, mindfulness of breathing, when developed and made much of, is of great fruit and great benefit. And how, Rāhula, is mindfulness of breathing developed and made much of so that it is of great fruit and great benefit? Here, Rāhula, a bhikkhu—having gone to the forest, or to the root of a tree, or to a secluded place—sits down, having folded his legs crosswise, held his body erect, and established mindfulness before him. Mindful he breathes out, mindful he breathes in.”

“Dīghaṃ vā assasanto ‘dīghaṃ assasāmī’ti pajānāti, dīghaṃ vā passasanto ‘dīghaṃ passasāmī’ti pajānāti; rassaṃ vā assasanto ‘rassaṃ assasāmī’ti pajānāti, rassaṃ vā passasanto ‘rassaṃ passasāmī’ti pajānāti. ‘Sabbakāyappaṭisaṃvedī assasissāmī’ti sikkhati; ‘sabbakāyappaṭisaṃvedī passasissāmī’ti sikkhati; ‘passambhayaṃ kāyasaṅkhāraṃ assasissāmī’ti sikkhati; ‘passambhayaṃ kāyasaṅkhāraṃ passasissāmī’ti sikkhati.

“Breathing out long, he knows distinctly: ‘I am breathing out long’; or breathing in long, he knows distinctly: ‘I am breathing in long.’ Or breathing out short, he knows distinctly: ‘I am breathing out short’; or breathing in short, he knows distinctly: ‘I am breathing in short.’ He trains thus: ‘I will breathe out experiencing the whole body’; he trains thus: ‘I will breathe in experiencing the whole body.’ He trains thus: ‘I will breathe out calming the bodily formation’; he trains thus: ‘I will breathe in calming the bodily formation.’”

“‘Pītippaṭisaṃvedī assasissāmī’ti sikkhati; ‘pītippaṭisaṃvedī passasissāmī’ti sikkhati; ‘sukhappaṭisaṃvedī assasissāmī’ti sikkhati; ‘sukhappaṭisaṃvedī passasissāmī’ti sikkhati; ‘cittasaṅkhārappaṭisaṃvedī assasissāmī’ti sikkhati; ‘cittasaṅkhārappaṭisaṃvedī passasissāmī’ti sikkhati; ‘passambhayaṃ cittasaṅkhāraṃ assasissāmī’ti sikkhati; ‘passambhayaṃ cittasaṅkhāraṃ passasissāmī’ti sikkhati.

“He trains thus: ‘I will breathe out experiencing rapture’; he trains thus: ‘I will breathe in experiencing rapture.’ He trains thus: ‘I will breathe out experiencing happiness’; he trains thus: ‘I will breathe in experiencing happiness.’ He trains thus: ‘I will breathe out experiencing the mental formation’; he trains thus: ‘I will breathe in experiencing the mental formation.’ He trains thus: ‘I will breathe out calming the mental formation’; he trains thus: ‘I will breathe in calming the mental formation.’”

“‘Cittappaṭisaṃvedī assasissāmī’ti sikkhati; ‘cittappaṭisaṃvedī passasissāmī’ti sikkhati[V 2.0096]; ‘abhippamodayaṃ cittaṃ assasissāmī’ti sikkhati; ‘abhippamodayaṃ cittaṃ passasissāmī’ti sikkhati; ‘samādahaṃ cittaṃ assasissāmī’ti sikkhati; ‘samādahaṃ cittaṃ passasissāmī’ti sikkhati; ‘vimocayaṃ cittaṃ assasissāmī’ti sikkhati; ‘vimocayaṃ cittaṃ passasissāmī’ti sikkhati.

“He trains thus: ‘I will breathe out experiencing the mind’; he trains thus: ‘I will breathe in experiencing the mind.’ He trains thus: ‘I will breathe out gladdening the mind’; he trains thus: ‘I will breathe in gladdening the mind.’ He trains thus: ‘I will breathe out concentrating the mind’; he trains thus: ‘I will breathe in concentrating the mind.’ He trains thus: ‘I will breathe out liberating the mind’; he trains thus: ‘I will breathe in liberating the mind.’”

“‘Aniccānupassī [M 2.0089] assasissāmī’ti [T 2.0142] sikkhati; ‘aniccānupassī passasissāmī’ti sikkhati; ‘virāgānupassī assasissāmī’ti sikkhati; ‘virāgānupassī passasissāmī’ti sikkhati; ‘nirodhānupassī assasissāmī’ti sikkhati; ‘nirodhānupassī passasissāmī’ti sikkhati; ‘paṭinissaggānupassī assasissāmī’ti sikkhati; ‘paṭinissaggānupassī passasissāmī’ti sikkhati.

“He trains thus: ‘I will breathe out contemplating impermanence’; he trains thus: ‘I will breathe in contemplating impermanence.’ He trains thus: ‘I will breathe out contemplating fading away’; he trains thus: ‘I will breathe in contemplating fading away.’ He trains thus: ‘I will breathe out contemplating cessation’; he trains thus: ‘I will breathe in contemplating cessation.’ He trains thus: ‘I will breathe out contemplating relinquishment’; he trains thus: ‘I will breathe in contemplating relinquishment.’”

“Evaṃ bhāvitā kho, rāhula, ānāpānassati, evaṃ bahulīkatā mahapphalā hoti mahānisaṃsā. Evaṃ bhāvitāya, rāhula, ānāpānassatiyā, evaṃ [P 1.0426] bahulīkatāya yepi te carimakā assāsā tepi viditāva nirujjhanti no aviditā”ti.

Rāhula, when mindfulness of breathing is thus developed and cultivated, it is of great fruit and great benefit. Rāhula, when mindfulness of breathing is thus developed and cultivated, even the final in-breaths and out-breaths cease with knowledge, not without knowledge.

Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamano āyasmā rāhulo bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandīti.

The Blessed One said this. The Venerable Rāhula, pleased, rejoiced in the Blessed One’s words.

Mahārāhulovādasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ dutiyaṃ.

The Greater Discourse of Advice to Rāhula, the second, is finished.

3. Cūḷamālukyasuttaṃ

3. The Shorter Discourse to Mālukyaputta

122. Evaṃ [T 2.0143][V 2.0097] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Atha kho āyasmato mālukyaputtassa māluṅkyaputtassa (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) rahogatassa paṭisallīnassa evaṃ cetaso parivitakko udapādi – “yānimāni diṭṭhigatāni bhagavatā abyākatāni ṭhapitāni paṭikkhittāni – ‘sassato loko’tipi, ‘asassato loko’tipi, ‘antavā loko’tipi, ‘anantavā loko’tipi, ‘taṃ jīvaṃ taṃ sarīra’ntipi, ‘aññaṃ jīvaṃ aññaṃ sarīra’ntipi, ‘hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’tipi, ‘na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’tipi, ‘hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’tipi, ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’tipi – tāni me bhagavā na byākaroti. Yāni me bhagavā na byākaroti taṃ me na ruccati, taṃ me nakkhamati. Sohaṃ bhagavantaṃ upasaṅkamitvā etamatthaṃ pucchissāmi. Sace me bhagavā byākarissati – ‘sassato loko’ti vā ‘asassato loko’ti vā…pe… ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti vā – evāhaṃ bhagavati brahmacariyaṃ [M 2.0090] carissāmi; no ce me bhagavā byākarissati – ‘sassato loko’ti vā ‘asassato loko’ti vā…pe… ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato [T 2.0144] paraṃ maraṇā’ti vā – evāhaṃ sikkhaṃ paccakkhāya hīnāyāvattissāmī”ti.

122. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. Then, while the Venerable Mālukyaputta was alone in seclusion, the following reflection arose in his mind: “These speculative views that have been left undeclared by the Blessed One, set aside, and rejected—‘The world is eternal,’ or ‘The world is not eternal,’ ‘The world is finite,’ or ‘The world is infinite,’ ‘The soul is the same as the body,’ or ‘The soul is one thing and the body another,’ ‘The Tathāgata exists after death,’ or ‘The Tathāgata does not exist after death,’ ‘The Tathāgata both exists and does not exist after death,’ or ‘The Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death’—the Blessed One does not declare these to me. That the Blessed One does not declare these to me does not please me, and I do not approve of it. I will approach the Blessed One and ask him about this matter. If the Blessed One declares to me, ‘The world is eternal,’ or ‘The world is not eternal,’… or ‘The Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death,’ then I will live the holy life under the Blessed One. But if the Blessed One does not declare to me, ‘The world is eternal,’ or ‘The world is not eternal,’… or ‘The Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death,’ then I will renounce the training and return to the lower life.”

123. Atha [P 1.0427] kho āyasmā mālukyaputto sāyanhasamayaṃ paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā mālukyaputto bhagavantaṃ etadavoca –

123. Then the Venerable Mālukyaputta, arising from seclusion in the evening, approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the Venerable Mālukyaputta said this to the Blessed One:

124. “Idha mayhaṃ, bhante, rahogatassa paṭisallīnassa evaṃ cetaso parivitakko udapādi – yānimāni diṭṭhigatāni bhagavatā abyākatāni ṭhapitāni paṭikkhittāni – ‘sassato loko’tipi, ‘asassato loko’tipi…pe… ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’tipi – tāni me bhagavā na byākaroti. Yāni me bhagavā na byākaroti taṃ me [V 2.0098] na ruccati, taṃ me nakkhamati. Sohaṃ bhagavantaṃ upasaṅkamitvā etamatthaṃ pucchissāmi. Sace me bhagavā byākarissati – ‘sassato loko’ti vā, ‘asassato loko’ti vā…pe… [T 2.0145] ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti vā – evāhaṃ bhagavati, brahmacariyaṃ carissāmi. No ce me bhagavā byākarissati – ‘sassato loko’ti vā, ‘asassato loko’ti vā…pe… ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti vā – evāhaṃ sikkhaṃ paccakkhāya hīnāyāvattissāmīti. Sace bhagavā jānāti – ‘sassato loko’ti, ‘sassato loko’ti me bhagavā byākarotu; sace bhagavā jānāti – ‘asassato loko’ti, ‘asassato loko’ti me bhagavā byākarotu. No ce bhagavā jānāti – ‘sassato loko’ti vā, ‘asassato loko’ti vā, ajānato kho pana apassato etadeva ujukaṃ hoti yadidaṃ – ‘na jānāmi, na passāmī’ti. Sace bhagavā jānāti – ‘antavā loko’ti, ‘anantavā loko’ti me bhagavā byākarotu; sace bhagavā jānāti – ‘anantavā loko’ti, ‘anantavā loko’ti me bhagavā byākarotu. No ce bhagavā jānāti – ‘antavā loko’ti vā, ‘anantavā loko’ti vā, ajānato kho pana apassato etadeva [M 2.0091] ujukaṃ hoti yadidaṃ – ‘na jānāmi, na passāmī’ti. Sace bhagavā jānāti – ‘taṃ jīvaṃ taṃ sarīra’nti, ‘taṃ jīvaṃ taṃ sarīra’nti me bhagavā byākarotu; sace bhagavā jānāti – ‘aññaṃ jīvaṃ aññaṃ sarīra’nti, ‘aññaṃ jīvaṃ aññaṃ sarīra’nti me bhagavā byākarotu. No ce bhagavā jānāti – ‘taṃ jīvaṃ taṃ sarīra’nti vā, ‘aññaṃ jīvaṃ aññaṃ sarīra’nti vā, ajānato kho pana apassato etadeva ujukaṃ hoti yadidaṃ – ‘na [T 2.0146] jānāmi, na passāmī’ti. Sace bhagavā jānāti – ‘hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti, ‘hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti me bhagavā [P 1.0428] byākarotu; sace bhagavā jānāti – ‘na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti, ‘na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti me bhagavā byākarotu. No ce bhagavā jānāti – ‘hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti vā, ‘na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti vā, ajānato kho pana apassato etadeva ujukaṃ hoti yadidaṃ – ‘na jānāmi na passāmī’ti. Sace bhagavā jānāti – ‘hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti, ‘hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti me bhagavā byākarotu; sace bhagavā jānāti – ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti, ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti me bhagavā byākarotu. No ce bhagavā jānāti – ‘hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti vā, ‘neva hoti na [V 2.0099] na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti vā, ajānato kho pana apassato etadeva ujukaṃ hoti yadidaṃ – ‘na jānāmi, na passāmī’”ti.

124. “Venerable sir, while I was alone in seclusion, this reflection arose in my mind: ‘These speculative views that have been left undeclared by the Blessed One, set aside, and rejected—namely, “The world is eternal,” or “The world is not eternal,” … or “The Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death”—the Blessed One does not declare these to me. That the Blessed One does not declare these to me—this does not please me, this does not satisfy me. I will approach the Blessed One and ask him about this matter. If the Blessed One declares to me, “The world is eternal,” or “The world is not eternal,” … or “The Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death,” then I will live the holy life under the Blessed One. But if the Blessed One does not declare to me, “The world is eternal,” or “The world is not eternal,” … or “The Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death,” then I will renounce the training and return to the lower life.’ If the Blessed One knows, ‘The world is eternal,’ then let the Blessed One declare to me, ‘The world is eternal.’ If the Blessed One knows, ‘The world is not eternal,’ then let the Blessed One declare to me, ‘The world is not eternal.’ But if the Blessed One does not know whether ‘The world is eternal’ or ‘The world is not eternal,’ then for one who does not know and does not see, the straightforward thing is to say, ‘I do not know, I do not see.’ If the Blessed One knows, ‘The world is finite,’ then let the Blessed One declare to me, ‘The world is finite.’ If the Blessed One knows, ‘The world is infinite,’ then let the Blessed One declare to me, ‘The world is infinite.’ But if the Blessed One does not know whether ‘The world is finite’ or ‘The world is infinite,’ then for one who does not know and does not see, the straightforward thing is to say, ‘I do not know, I do not see.’ If the Blessed One knows, ‘The life-principle is the same as the body,’ then let the Blessed One declare to me, ‘The life-principle is the same as the body.’ If the Blessed One knows, ‘The life-principle is one thing and the body another,’ then let the Blessed One declare to me, ‘The life-principle is one thing and the body another.’ But if the Blessed One does not know whether ‘The life-principle is the same as the body’ or ‘The life-principle is one thing and the body another,’ then for one who does not know and does not see, the straightforward thing is to say, ‘I do not know, I do not see.’ If the Blessed One knows, ‘The Tathāgata exists after death,’ then let the Blessed One declare to me, ‘The Tathāgata exists after death.’ If the Blessed One knows, ‘The Tathāgata does not exist after death,’ then let the Blessed One declare to me, ‘The Tathāgata does not exist after death.’ But if the Blessed One does not know whether ‘The Tathāgata exists after death’ or ‘The Tathāgata does not exist after death,’ then for one who does not know and does not see, the straightforward thing is to say, ‘I do not know, I do not see.’ If the Blessed One knows, ‘The Tathāgata both exists and does not exist after death,’ then let the Blessed One declare to me, ‘The Tathāgata both exists and does not exist after death.’ If the Blessed One knows, ‘The Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death,’ then let the Blessed One declare to me, ‘The Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death.’ But if the Blessed One does not know whether ‘The Tathāgata both exists and does not exist after death’ or ‘The Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death,’ then for one who does not know and does not see, the straightforward thing is to say, ‘I do not know, I do not see.’”

125. “Kiṃ nu kiṃ nu kho (syā. kaṃ. ka.) tāhaṃ, mālukyaputta, evaṃ avacaṃ – ‘ehi tvaṃ, mālukyaputta, mayi brahmacariyaṃ cara, ahaṃ te byākarissāmi – ‘sassato loko’ti vā, ‘asassato loko’ti vā, ‘antavā loko’ti vā, ‘anantavā loko’ti vā, ‘taṃ jīvaṃ taṃ sarīra’nti vā, ‘aññaṃ jīvaṃ aññaṃ sarīra’nti vā, ‘hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti vā, ‘na hoti [T 2.0147] tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti vā, ‘hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti vā, ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti vā”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”. “Tvaṃ vā pana maṃ evaṃ avaca – ahaṃ, bhante, bhagavati brahmacariyaṃ carissāmi[M 2.0092], bhagavā me byākarissati – ‘sassato loko’ti vā, ‘asassato loko’ti vā, ‘antavā loko’ti vā, ‘anantavā loko’ti vā, ‘taṃ jīvaṃ taṃ sarīra’nti vā, ‘aññaṃ jīvaṃ aññaṃ sarīra’nti vā, ‘hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti vā, ‘na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti vā, ‘hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti vā, ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti vā”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”. “Iti kira, mālukyaputta, nevāhaṃ taṃ vadāmi – ehi tvaṃ, mālukyaputta, mayi brahmacariyaṃ cara, ahaṃ te byākarissāmi – ‘sassato loko’ti vā, ‘asassato loko’ti vā…pe… ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇāti vā’ti; napi kira maṃ tvaṃ vadesi – ahaṃ, bhante, bhagavati brahmacariyaṃ carissāmi, bhagavā me byākarissati – ‘sassato loko’ti vā ‘asassato loko’ti vā…pe… ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti vā”ti. Evaṃ sante, moghapurisa, ko santo kaṃ paccācikkhasi?

125. “Did I ever say to you, Mālukyaputta, ‘Come, Mālukyaputta, practice the holy life under me, and I will declare to you: “the world is eternal,” or “the world is not eternal,” or “the world is finite,” or “the world is infinite,” or “the life-principle is the same as the body,” or “the life-principle is one thing and the body is another,” or “a Tathāgata exists after death,” or “a Tathāgata does not exist after death,” or “a Tathāgata both exists and does not exist after death,” or “a Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death”’?” “No, venerable sir.” “Or did you, for your part, say to me: ‘Venerable sir, I will practice the holy life under the Blessed One, and the Blessed One will declare to me: “the world is eternal,” or “the world is not eternal,” or “the world is finite,” or “the world is infinite,” or “the life-principle is the same as the body,” or “the life-principle is one thing and the body is another,” or “a Tathāgata exists after death,” or “a Tathāgata does not exist after death,” or “a Tathāgata both exists and does not exist after death,” or “a Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death”’?” “No, venerable sir.” “So then, Mālukyaputta, I did not say to you, ‘Come, Mālukyaputta, practice the holy life under me, and I will declare to you… “a Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death”’; and nor did you say to me, ‘Venerable sir, I will practice the holy life under the Blessed One, and the Blessed One will declare to me… “a Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death”.’ That being so, foolish man, who are you and whom are you repudiating?”

126. “Yo kho, mālukyaputta, evaṃ vadeyya – ‘na tāvāhaṃ bhagavati brahmacariyaṃ carissāmi yāva me bhagavā na byākarissati – “sassato loko”ti vā, “asassato loko”ti vā…pe… [T 2.0148] “neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā”ti vāti, abyākatameva [P 1.0429] taṃ, mālukyaputta, tathāgatena assa, atha so puggalo kālaṃ kareyya. Seyyathāpi, mālukyaputta, puriso sallena viddho assa savisena gāḷhapalepanena. Tassa mittāmaccā ñātisālohitā bhisakkaṃ sallakattaṃ upaṭṭhapeyyuṃ.
