Having heard it from the Blessed One, the monks will remember it.” “Anuruddhas, the Tathāgata does not make declarations about disciples who have passed on and died regarding their rebirths—‘So-and-so has been reborn there; so-and-so has been reborn there’—for the sake of deceiving people, nor for the sake of flattering people, nor for the benefit of gain, honor, and renown, nor with the thought, ‘Thus let people know me.’ But, Anuruddhas, there are clansmen who have faith, who are of great joy and abundant gladness. Having heard that, they direct their minds toward that attainment. For them, Anuruddhas, that leads to their welfare and happiness for a long time.”

169. “Idhānuruddhā, bhikkhu suṇāti – ‘itthannāmo bhikkhu kālaṅkato kālakato (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.); so bhagavatā byākato – aññāya saṇṭhahī’ti. So kho panassa āyasmā sāmaṃ diṭṭho vā hoti anussavassuto vā – ‘evaṃsīlo so āyasmā ahosi itipi, evaṃdhammo so āyasmā ahosi itipi, evaṃpañño so āyasmā ahosi itipi, evaṃvihārī so āyasmā ahosi itipi, evaṃvimutto so āyasmā ahosi itipī’ti. So tassa saddhañca sīlañca sutañca cāgañca paññañca anussaranto tadatthāya cittaṃ upasaṃharati. Evampi kho, anuruddhā, bhikkhuno phāsuvihāro hoti.

169. Here, Anuruddhas, a monk hears: ‘The monk named so-and-so has passed away; he has been declared by the Blessed One: “He has become established in final knowledge.”’ Now, that venerable one may have been seen by him in person or heard of by report: ‘That venerable one was of such virtue, thus was his nature, thus was his wisdom, thus was his abiding, and thus was his liberation.’ Recollecting that one’s faith, virtue, learning, generosity, and wisdom, he directs his mind toward that same attainment. In this way too, Anuruddhas, a monk has a comfortable abiding.

“Idhānuruddhā[V 2.0138], bhikkhu suṇāti – ‘itthannāmo bhikkhu kālaṅkato; so bhagavatā byākato – pañcannaṃ orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā opapātiko tattha parinibbāyī anāvattidhammo tasmā lokā’ti. So [T 2.0208] kho panassa āyasmā sāmaṃ diṭṭho vā hoti anussavassuto vā [M 2.0129] – ‘evaṃsīlo so āyasmā ahosi itipi, evaṃdhammo…pe… evaṃpañño… evaṃvihārī… evaṃvimutto so āyasmā ahosi itipī’ti. So tassa saddhañca sīlañca sutañca cāgañca paññañca anussaranto tadatthāya cittaṃ upasaṃharati. Evampi kho, anuruddhā, bhikkhuno phāsuvihāro hoti.

Here, Anuruddhas, a monk hears: ‘The monk named so-and-so has passed away; he has been declared by the Blessed One: “With the complete destruction of the five lower fetters, he has been spontaneously reborn, will attain final Nibbāna there, and is of a nature not to return from that world.”’ Now, that venerable one may have been seen by him in person or heard of by report: ‘That venerable one was of such virtue, thus was his nature, thus was his wisdom, thus was his abiding, and thus was his liberation.’ Recollecting that one’s faith, virtue, learning, generosity, and wisdom, he directs his mind toward that same attainment. In this way too, Anuruddhas, a monk has a comfortable abiding.

“Idhānuruddhā, bhikkhu suṇāti – ‘itthannāmo bhikkhu kālaṅkato; so bhagavatā byākato – tiṇṇaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā rāgadosamohānaṃ tanuttā sakadāgāmī sakideva imaṃ lokaṃ āgantvā dukkhassantaṃ karissatī’ti. So kho panassa āyasmā sāmaṃ diṭṭho vā hoti anussavassuto vā – ‘evaṃsīlo so āyasmā ahosi itipi, evaṃdhammo…pe… evaṃpañño… evaṃvihārī… evaṃvimutto so āyasmā ahosi itipī’ti. So tassa saddhañca sīlañca sutañca cāgañca paññañca anussaranto tadatthāya cittaṃ [P 1.0466] upasaṃharati. Evampi kho, anuruddhā, bhikkhuno phāsuvihāro hoti.

Here, Anuruddhas, a bhikkhu hears: ‘A bhikkhu of such-and-such a name has passed away; he has been declared by the Blessed One: “With the destruction of the three fetters and the attenuation of greed, hatred, and delusion, he is a once-returner who, having come to this world only once, will make an end of suffering.”’ Now, that venerable one may have been seen by him in person or heard of by report: ‘That venerable one was of such virtue, of such a nature... of such wisdom... of such an abiding... of such liberation.’ Remembering that one's faith, virtue, learning, generosity, and wisdom, he directs his mind toward that attainment. In this way also, Anuruddhas, a bhikkhu has a comfortable abiding.

“Idhānuruddhā, bhikkhu suṇāti – ‘itthannāmo bhikkhu kālaṅkato; so bhagavatā byākato – tiṇṇaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā sotāpanno avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyaṇo’ti. So kho panassa āyasmā sāmaṃ diṭṭho vā hoti anussavassuto vā – ‘evaṃsīlo so āyasmā ahosi itipi, evaṃdhammo…pe… evaṃpañño… evaṃvihārī… evaṃvimutto so āyasmā ahosi [T 2.0209] itipī’ti. So tassa saddhañca sīlañca sutañca cāgañca paññañca anussaranto tadatthāya cittaṃ upasaṃharati. Evampi kho, anuruddhā, bhikkhuno phāsuvihāro hoti.

Here, Anuruddhas, a bhikkhu hears: ‘A bhikkhu of such-and-such a name has passed away; he has been declared by the Blessed One: “With the destruction of the three fetters, he is a stream-enterer, not subject to states of woe, certain, and bound for enlightenment.”’ Now, that venerable one may have been seen by him in person or heard of by report: ‘That venerable one was of such virtue, of such a nature... of such wisdom... of such an abiding... of such liberation.’ Remembering that one's faith, virtue, learning, generosity, and wisdom, he directs his mind toward that attainment. In this way also, Anuruddhas, a bhikkhu has a comfortable abiding.

170. “Idhānuruddhā, bhikkhunī suṇāti – ‘itthannāmā bhikkhunī kālaṅkatā; sā bhagavatā byākatā – aññāya saṇṭhahī’ti. Sā kho panassā bhaginī sāmaṃ diṭṭhā vā hoti anussavassutā vā – ‘evaṃsīlā sā bhaginī ahosi itipi, evaṃdhammā sā bhaginī ahosi itipi[V 2.0139], evaṃpaññā sā bhaginī ahosi itipi, evaṃvihārinī sā bhaginī ahosi itipi, evaṃvimuttā sā bhaginī ahosi itipī’ti. Sā tassā saddhañca sīlañca sutañca cāgañca paññañca anussarantī tadatthāya cittaṃ upasaṃharati. Evampi kho, anuruddhā, bhikkhuniyā phāsuvihāro hoti.

170. Here, Anuruddhas, a bhikkhunī hears: ‘A bhikkhunī of such-and-such a name has passed away; she has been declared by the Blessed One: “She is established in final knowledge.”’ Now, that sister may have been seen by her in person or heard of by report: ‘That sister was of such virtue, of such a nature, of such wisdom, of such an abiding, and of such liberation.’ Remembering that sister's faith, virtue, learning, generosity, and wisdom, she directs her mind toward that attainment. In this way also, Anuruddhas, a bhikkhunī has a comfortable abiding.

“Idhānuruddhā[M 2.0130], bhikkhunī suṇāti – ‘itthannāmā bhikkhunī kālaṅkatā; sā bhagavatā byākatā – pañcannaṃ orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā opapātikā tattha parinibbāyinī anāvattidhammā tasmā lokā’ti. Sā kho panassā bhaginī sāmaṃ diṭṭhā vā hoti anussavassutā vā – ‘evaṃsīlā sā bhaginī ahosi itipi, evaṃdhammā…pe… evaṃpaññā… evaṃvihārinī… evaṃvimuttā sā bhaginī ahosi itipī’ti. Sā tassā saddhañca sīlañca sutañca cāgañca paññañca anussarantī tadatthāya cittaṃ upasaṃharati. Evampi [T 2.0210] kho, anuruddhā, bhikkhuniyā phāsuvihāro hoti.

Here, Anuruddhas, a bhikkhunī hears: ‘A bhikkhunī of such-and-such a name has passed away; she has been declared by the Blessed One: “With the destruction of the five lower fetters, she has arisen spontaneously, will attain final Nibbāna there, and is of a nature not to return from that world.”’ Now, that sister may have been seen by her in person or heard of by report: ‘That sister was of such virtue, of such a nature... of such wisdom... of such an abiding... of such liberation.’ Remembering that sister's faith, virtue, learning, generosity, and wisdom, she directs her mind toward that attainment. In this way also, Anuruddhas, a bhikkhunī has a comfortable abiding.

“Idhānuruddhā, bhikkhunī suṇāti – ‘itthannāmā bhikkhunī kālaṅkatā; sā bhagavatā byākatā – tiṇṇaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā rāgadosamohānaṃ tanuttā sakadāgāminī sakideva imaṃ lokaṃ āgantvā dukkhassantaṃ karissatī’ti. Sā kho panassā bhaginī sāmaṃ diṭṭhā vā hoti anussavassutā vā – ‘evaṃsīlā sā bhaginī ahosi itipi, evaṃdhammā…pe… evaṃpaññā… evaṃvihārinī… evaṃvimuttā sā bhaginī ahosi itipī’ti. Sā tassā saddhañca sīlañca sutañca cāgañca paññañca anussarantī tadatthāya cittaṃ upasaṃharati. Evampi kho, anuruddhā, bhikkhuniyā phāsuvihāro hoti.

Here, Anuruddhas, a bhikkhunī hears: ‘A bhikkhunī of such-and-such a name has passed away; she has been declared by the Blessed One: “With the destruction of the three fetters and the attenuation of greed, hatred, and delusion, she is a once-returner who, having come to this world only once, will make an end of suffering.”’ Now, that sister may have been seen by her in person or heard of by report: ‘That sister was of such virtue, of such a nature... of such wisdom... of such an abiding... of such liberation.’ Remembering that sister's faith, virtue, learning, generosity, and wisdom, she directs her mind toward that attainment. In this way also, Anuruddhas, a bhikkhunī has a comfortable abiding.

“Idhānuruddhā, bhikkhunī suṇāti – ‘itthannāmā bhikkhunī kālaṅkatā; sā bhagavatā byākatā – tiṇṇaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā sotāpannā avinipātadhammā niyatā sambodhiparāyaṇā’ti[P 1.0467]. Sā kho panassā bhaginī sāmaṃ diṭṭhā vā hoti anussavassutā vā – ‘evaṃsīlā sā bhaginī ahosi itipi, evaṃdhammā… evaṃpaññā… evaṃvihārinī… evaṃvimuttā sā bhaginī ahosi itipī’ti. Sā tassā saddhañca sīlañca sutañca cāgañca paññañca anussarantī [V 2.0140] tadatthāya cittaṃ upasaṃharati. Evampi kho, anuruddhā, bhikkhuniyā phāsuvihāro hoti.

Here, Anuruddhas, a bhikkhunī hears: ‘A bhikkhunī of such-and-such a name has passed away; she has been declared by the Blessed One: “With the destruction of the three fetters, she is a stream-enterer, not subject to states of woe, certain, and bound for enlightenment.”’ Now, that sister may have been seen by her in person or heard of by report: ‘That sister was of such virtue, of such a nature... of such wisdom... of such an abiding... of such liberation.’ Remembering that sister's faith, virtue, learning, generosity, and wisdom, she directs her mind toward that attainment. In this way also, Anuruddhas, a bhikkhunī has a comfortable abiding.

171. “Idhānuruddhā, upāsako suṇāti – ‘itthannāmo upāsako kālaṅkato; so bhagavatā byākato – pañcannaṃ orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā opapātiko tattha parinibbāyī anāvattidhammo tasmā [T 2.0211] lokā’ti. So kho panassa āyasmā sāmaṃ diṭṭho vā hoti anussavassuto vā – ‘evaṃsīlo so āyasmā ahosi itipi, evaṃdhammo [M 2.0131] so āyasmā ahosi itipi, evaṃpañño so āyasmā ahosi itipi, evaṃvihārī so āyasmā ahosi itipi, evaṃvimutto so āyasmā ahosi itipī’ti. So tassa saddhañca sutañca cāgañca paññañca anussaranto tadatthāya cittaṃ upasaṃharati. Evampi kho, anuruddhā, upāsakassa phāsuvihāro hoti.

171. Here, Anuruddhas, a male lay follower hears: ‘A male lay follower of such-and-such a name has passed away; he has been declared by the Blessed One: “With the destruction of the five lower fetters, he has arisen spontaneously, will attain final Nibbāna there, and is of a nature not to return from that world.”’ Now, that venerable one may have been seen by him in person or heard of by report: ‘That venerable one was of such virtue, of such a nature, of such wisdom, of such an abiding, and of such liberation.’ Remembering that one's faith, virtue, learning, generosity, and wisdom, he directs his mind toward that attainment. In this way also, Anuruddhas, a male lay follower has a comfortable abiding.

“Idhānuruddhā, upāsako suṇāti – ‘itthannāmo upāsako kālaṅkato; so bhagavatā byākato – tiṇṇaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā rāgadosamohānaṃ tanuttā sakadāgāmī sakideva imaṃ lokaṃ āgantvā dukkhassantaṃ karissatī’ti. So kho panassa āyasmā sāmaṃ diṭṭho vā hoti anussavassuto vā – ‘evaṃsīlo so āyasmā ahosi itipi, evaṃdhammo… evaṃpañño… evaṃvihārī… evaṃvimutto so āyasmā ahosi itipī’ti. So tassa saddhañca sīlañca sutañca cāgañca paññañca anussaranto tadatthāya cittaṃ upasaṃharati. Evampi kho, anuruddhā, upāsakassa phāsuvihāro hoti.

Here, Anuruddhas, a lay follower hears: 'A lay follower of such-and-such a name has passed away. He has been declared by the Blessed One: “With the destruction of the three fetters and the attenuation of greed, hatred, and delusion, he is a once-returner who, having come to this world only once, will make an end of suffering.”' And that venerable one may have been seen by him personally or heard of by report, thus: 'That venerable one was of such virtue... of such a nature... of such wisdom... of such an abiding... was liberated in such a way.' Remembering that one’s faith, virtue, learning, generosity, and wisdom, he directs his mind toward that state. In this way also, Anuruddhas, a lay follower has a comfortable abiding.

“Idhānuruddhā, upāsako suṇāti – ‘itthannāmo upāsako kālaṅkato; so bhagavatā byākato – tiṇṇaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā sotāpanno avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyaṇo’ti. So kho panassa āyasmā sāmaṃ diṭṭho vā hoti anussavassuto vā – ‘evaṃsīlo so āyasmā ahosi itipi, evaṃdhammo…pe… [T 2.0212] evaṃpañño… evaṃvihārī… evaṃvimutto so āyasmā ahosi itipī’ti. So tassa saddhañca sīlañca sutañca cāgañca paññañca anussaranto tadatthāya cittaṃ upasaṃharati. Evampi kho, anuruddhā upāsakassa phāsuvihāro hoti.

Here, Anuruddhas, a lay follower hears: 'A lay follower of such-and-such a name has passed away. He has been declared by the Blessed One: “With the destruction of the three fetters, he has become a stream-enterer, is not of a nature to fall into the lower realms, is certain, and is bound for supreme enlightenment.”' And that venerable one may have been seen by him personally or heard of by report, thus: 'That venerable one was of such virtue... of such a nature... of such wisdom... of such an abiding... was liberated in such a way.' Remembering that one’s faith, virtue, learning, generosity, and wisdom, he directs his mind toward that state. In this way also, Anuruddhas, a lay follower has a comfortable abiding.

172. “Idhānuruddhā[V 2.0141], upāsikā suṇāti – ‘itthannāmā upāsikā kālaṅkatā; sā bhagavatā byākatā – pañcannaṃ orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā opapātikā tattha parinibbāyinī anāvattidhammā tasmā lokā’ti. Sā kho panassā bhaginī sāmaṃ diṭṭhā vā hoti anussavassutā vā – ‘evaṃsīlā sā bhaginī ahosi itipi, evaṃdhammā… evaṃpaññā… evaṃvihārinī… evaṃvimuttā [P 1.0468] sā bhaginī ahosi itipī’ti. Sā tassā saddhañca sīlañca sutañca cāgañca paññañca anussarantī tadatthāya cittaṃ [M 2.0132] upasaṃharati. Evampi kho, anuruddhā, upāsikāya phāsuvihāro hoti.

172. Here, Anuruddhas, a female lay follower hears: ‘A female lay follower of such-and-such a name has passed away. She has been declared by the Blessed One: “With the destruction of the five lower fetters, she is of spontaneous birth, will attain Parinibbāna there, and is of a nature not to return from that world.”’ And that sister may have been seen by her personally or heard of by report, thus: ‘That sister was of such virtue... of such a nature... of such wisdom... of such an abiding... was liberated in such a way.’ She, remembering that one’s faith, virtue, learning, generosity, and wisdom, directs her mind toward that state. In this way also, Anuruddhas, a female lay follower has a comfortable abiding.

“Idhānuruddhā, upāsikā suṇāti – ‘itthannāmā upāsikā kālaṅkatā; sā bhagavatā byākatā – tiṇṇaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā rāgadosamohānaṃ tanuttā sakadāgāminī sakideva imaṃ lokaṃ āgantvā dukkhassantaṃ karissatī’ti. Sā kho panassā bhaginī sāmaṃ diṭṭhā vā hoti anussavassutā vā – ‘evaṃsīlā sā bhaginī ahosi itipi, evaṃdhammā… evaṃpaññā… evaṃvihārinī… evaṃvimuttā sā bhaginī ahosi itipī’ti. Sā tassā saddhañca sīlañca sutañca cāgañca paññañca anussarantī tadatthāya [T 2.0213] cittaṃ upasaṃharati. Evampi kho, anuruddhā, upāsikāya phāsuvihāro hoti.

Here, Anuruddhas, a female lay follower hears: ‘A female lay follower of such-and-such a name has passed away. She has been declared by the Blessed One: “With the destruction of the three fetters and the attenuation of greed, hatred, and delusion, she is a once-returner who, having come to this world only once, will make an end of suffering.”’ And that sister may have been seen by her personally or heard of by report, thus: ‘That sister was of such virtue... of such a nature... of such wisdom... of such an abiding... was liberated in such a way.’ She, remembering that one’s faith, virtue, learning, generosity, and wisdom, directs her mind toward that state. In this way also, Anuruddhas, a female lay follower has a comfortable abiding.

“Idhānuruddhā, upāsikā suṇāti – ‘itthannāmā upāsikā kālaṅkatā; sā bhagavatā byākatā – tiṇṇaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā sotāpannā avinipātadhammā niyatā sambodhiparāyaṇā’ti. Sā kho panassā bhaginī sāmaṃ diṭṭhā vā hoti anussavassutā vā – ‘evaṃsīlā sā bhaginī ahosi itipi, evaṃdhammā sā bhaginī ahosi itipi, evaṃpaññā sā bhaginī ahosi itipi, evaṃvihārinī sā bhaginī ahosi itipi, evaṃvimuttā sā bhaginī ahosi itipī’ti. Sā tassā saddhañca sīlañca sutañca cāgañca paññañca anussarantī tadatthāya cittaṃ upasaṃharati. Evampi kho, anuruddhā, upāsikāya phāsuvihāro hoti.

Here, Anuruddhas, a female lay follower hears: 'A female lay follower of such-and-such a name has passed away. She has been declared by the Blessed One: “With the destruction of the three fetters, she has become a stream-enterer, is not of a nature to fall into the lower realms, is certain, and is bound for supreme enlightenment.”' And that sister may have been seen by her personally or heard of by report, thus: 'That sister was of such virtue... of such a nature... of such wisdom... of such an abiding... was liberated in such a way.' She, remembering that one’s faith, virtue, learning, generosity, and wisdom, directs her mind toward that state. In this way also, Anuruddhas, a female lay follower has a comfortable abiding.

“Iti [V 2.0142] kho, anuruddhā, tathāgato na janakuhanatthaṃ na janalapanatthaṃ na lābhasakkārasilokānisaṃsatthaṃ na ‘iti maṃ jano jānātū’ti sāvake abbhatīte kālaṅkate upapattīsu byākaroti – ‘asu amutra upapanno, asu amutra upapanno’ti. Santi ca kho, anuruddhā, kulaputtā saddhā uḷāravedā uḷārapāmojjā. Te taṃ sutvā tadatthāya cittaṃ upasaṃharanti. Tesaṃ taṃ, anuruddhā, hoti dīgharattaṃ hitāya sukhāyā”ti.

Thus, Anuruddhas, the Tathāgata does not declare the rebirths of disciples who have passed on and died—saying, 'So-and-so has been reborn there, so-and-so has been reborn there'—not for the sake of deceiving people, not for the sake of flattering people, not for the sake of gain, honor, and praise, and not with the thought, 'Let people know me thus.' But, Anuruddhas, there are clansmen with faith, who have great delight and great gladness. Hearing that, they direct their minds toward that state. For them, Anuruddhas, that will be for their long-term welfare and happiness.

Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamano āyasmā anuruddho bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandīti.

The Blessed One said this. The Venerable Anuruddha, pleased, rejoiced in the words of the Blessed One.

Naḷakapānasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ aṭṭhamaṃ.

The Naḷakapāna Sutta, the eighth, is concluded.

9. Goliyānisuttaṃ

9. The Goliyāni Sutta

173. Evaṃ [T 2.0214][M 2.0133][V 2.0143][P 1.0469] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe. Tena kho pana samayena goliyāni gulissāni (sī. pī.), golissāni (syā. kaṃ.) nāma bhikkhu āraññiko āraññako (sabbattha) padasamācāro padarasamācāro (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) saṅghamajjhe osaṭo hoti kenacideva karaṇīyena. Tatra kho āyasmā sāriputto goliyāniṃ bhikkhuṃ ārabbha bhikkhū āmantesi –

173. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Rājagaha, in the Veḷuvana, the Squirrels' Feeding Ground. Now at that time, a bhikkhu named Goliyāni, a forest-dweller of coarse conduct, had come into the midst of the Saṅgha on account of some business. There, the Venerable Sāriputta, on account of the bhikkhu Goliyāni, addressed the bhikkhus:

“Āraññikenāvuso, bhikkhunā saṅghagatena saṅghe viharantena sabrahmacārīsu sagāravena bhavitabbaṃ sappatissena. Sace, āvuso, āraññiko bhikkhu saṅghagato saṅghe viharanto sabrahmacārīsu agāravo hoti appatisso, tassa bhavanti vattāro. ‘Kiṃ panimassāyasmato āraññikassa ekassāraññe serivihārena, yo ayamāyasmā sabrahmacārīsu agāravo hoti appatisso’ti – tassa appatissotissa (sī. pī.) bhavanti vattāro. Tasmā āraññikena bhikkhunā saṅghagatena saṅghe viharantena sabrahmacārīsu sagāravena bhavitabbaṃ sappatissena.

“Friends, a forest-dwelling bhikkhu who has come to the Saṅgha and is dwelling in the Saṅgha should be respectful and deferential towards his companions in the holy life. If, friends, a forest-dwelling bhikkhu who has come to the Saṅgha and is dwelling in the Saṅgha is disrespectful and not deferential towards his companions in the holy life, there will be those who speak against him, saying: ‘What is the use of this venerable one’s dwelling as he pleases alone in the forest, since this venerable one is disrespectful and not deferential towards his companions in the holy life?’ Thus, there will be those who speak against him. Therefore, a forest-dwelling bhikkhu who has come to the Saṅgha and is dwelling in the Saṅgha should be respectful and deferential towards his companions in the holy life.”

“Āraññikenāvuso, bhikkhunā saṅghagatena saṅghe viharantena āsanakusalena bhavitabbaṃ – ‘iti there ca bhikkhū nānupakhajja nisīdissāmi nave ca bhikkhū na āsanena paṭibāhissāmī’ti. Sace, āvuso, āraññiko [T 2.0215] bhikkhu saṅghagato saṅghe viharanto na āsanakusalo hoti, tassa bhavanti vattāro. ‘Kiṃ panimassāyasmato āraññikassa ekassāraññe serivihārena, yo ayamāyasmā āsanakusalo na hotī’ti yo ayamāyasmā ābhisamācārikampi dhammaṃ na jānātīti (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) – tassa bhavanti vattāro. Tasmā āraññikena bhikkhunā saṅghagatena saṅghe viharantena āsanakusalena bhavitabbaṃ.

“Friends, a forest-dwelling bhikkhu who has come to the Saṅgha and is dwelling in the Saṅgha should be skilled in regard to seating, thinking: ‘I will sit without crowding the elder bhikkhus, and I will not obstruct the junior bhikkhus from a seat.’ If, friends, a forest-dwelling bhikkhu who has come to the Saṅgha and is dwelling in the Saṅgha is not skilled in regard to seating, there will be those who speak against him, saying: ‘What is the use of this venerable one’s dwelling as he pleases alone in the forest, since this venerable one is not skilled in regard to seating?’ Thus, there will be those who speak against him. Therefore, a forest-dwelling bhikkhu who has come to the Saṅgha and is dwelling in the Saṅgha should be skilled in regard to seating.

“Āraññikenāvuso, bhikkhunā saṅghagatena saṅghe viharantena ābhisamācārikopi dhammo jānitabbo. Sace, āvuso, āraññiko bhikkhu saṅghagato saṅghe viharanto ābhisamācārikampi dhammaṃ na jānāti, tassa bhavanti vattāro. ‘Kiṃ panimassāyasmato āraññikassa ekassāraññe serivihārena yo ayamāyasmā ābhisamācārikampi dhammaṃ [M 2.0134] na jānātī’ti [V 2.0144] – tassa bhavanti vattāro. Tasmā āraññikena bhikkhunā saṅghagatena saṅghe viharantena ābhisamācārikopi dhammo jānitabbo ayaṃ ābhisamācārikatatiyavāro sī. syā. kaṃ. pī. potthakesu na dissati.

“Friends, a forest-dwelling bhikkhu who has come to the Saṅgha and is dwelling in the Saṅgha should also know the teaching concerning proper conduct. If, friends, a forest-dwelling bhikkhu who has come to the Saṅgha and is dwelling in the Saṅgha does not know the teaching concerning proper conduct, there will be those who speak against him, saying: ‘What is the use of this venerable one’s dwelling as he pleases alone in the forest, since this venerable one does not know the teaching concerning proper conduct?’ Thus, there will be those who speak against him. Therefore, a forest-dwelling bhikkhu who has come to the Saṅgha and is dwelling in the Saṅgha should also know the teaching concerning proper conduct.

“Āraññikenāvuso, bhikkhunā saṅghagatena saṅghe viharantena nātikālena gāmo pavisitabbo nātidivā na divā (syā. kaṃ. pī. ka.) paṭikkamitabbaṃ. Sace, āvuso, āraññiko bhikkhu saṅghagato saṅghe viharanto atikālena gāmaṃ pavisati atidivā paṭikkamati, tassa bhavanti vattāro. ‘Kiṃ panimassāyasmato āraññikassa ekassāraññe serivihārena yo ayamāyasmā atikālena gāmaṃ pavisati atidivā paṭikkamatī’ti – tassa bhavanti vattāro. Tasmā āraññikena bhikkhunā saṅghagatena saṅghe viharantena nātikālena gāmo pavisitabbo, nātidivā paṭikkamitabbaṃ.

“Friends, a forest-dwelling bhikkhu who has come to the Saṅgha and is dwelling in the Saṅgha should not enter a village too early, nor should he depart too late in the day. If, friends, a forest-dwelling bhikkhu who has come to the Saṅgha and is dwelling in the Saṅgha enters a village too early and departs too late in the day, there will be those who speak against him, saying: ‘What is the use of this venerable one’s dwelling as he pleases alone in the forest, since this venerable one enters a village too early and departs too late in the day?’ Thus, there will be those who speak against him. Therefore, a forest-dwelling bhikkhu who has come to the Saṅgha and is dwelling in the Saṅgha should not enter a village too early, nor should he depart too late in the day.

“Āraññikenāvuso, bhikkhunā saṅghagatena saṅghe viharantena na [T 2.0216] purebhattaṃ [P 1.0470] pacchābhattaṃ kulesu cārittaṃ āpajjitabbaṃ. Sace, āvuso, āraññiko bhikkhu saṅghagato saṅghe viharanto purebhattaṃ pacchābhattaṃ kulesu cārittaṃ āpajjati, tassa bhavanti vattāro. ‘Ayaṃ nūnimassāyasmato āraññikassa ekassāraññe serivihārena viharato vikālacariyā bahulīkatā, tamenaṃ saṅghagatampi samudācaratī’ti – tassa bhavanti vattāro. Tasmā āraññikena bhikkhunā saṅghagatena saṅghe viharantena na purebhattaṃ pacchābhattaṃ kulesu cārittaṃ āpajjitabbaṃ.

“Friends, a forest-dwelling bhikkhu who has come to the Saṅgha and is dwelling in the Saṅgha should not engage in roaming among families before the meal or after the meal. If, friends, a forest-dwelling bhikkhu who has come to the Saṅgha and is dwelling in the Saṅgha engages in roaming among families before the meal or after the meal, there will be those who speak against him, saying: ‘Surely, for this venerable one who dwells as he pleases alone in the forest, this wandering at the wrong time has been frequently practiced; it manifests in him even when he has come to the Saṅgha.’ Thus, there will be those who speak against him. Therefore, a forest-dwelling bhikkhu who has come to the Saṅgha and is dwelling in the Saṅgha should not engage in roaming among families before the meal or after the meal.

“Āraññikenāvuso, bhikkhunā saṅghagatena saṅghe viharantena anuddhatena bhavitabbaṃ acapalena. Sace, āvuso, āraññiko bhikkhu saṅghagato saṅghe viharanto uddhato hoti capalo, tassa bhavanti vattāro. ‘Idaṃ nūnimassāyasmato āraññikassa ekassāraññe serivihārena viharato uddhaccaṃ cāpalyaṃ bahulīkataṃ, tamenaṃ saṅghagatampi samudācaratī’ti – tassa bhavanti vattāro. Tasmā āraññikena bhikkhunā saṅghagatena saṅghe viharantena anuddhatena bhavitabbaṃ acapalena.

“Friends, a forest-dwelling bhikkhu who has come to the Saṅgha and is dwelling in the Saṅgha should be not restless and not fickle. If, friends, a forest-dwelling bhikkhu who has come to the Saṅgha and is dwelling in the Saṅgha is restless and fickle, there will be those who speak against him, saying: ‘Surely, for this venerable one who dwells as he pleases alone in the forest, this restlessness and fickleness have been frequently practiced; it manifests in him even when he has come to the Saṅgha.’ Thus, there will be those who speak against him. Therefore, a forest-dwelling bhikkhu who has come to the Saṅgha and is dwelling in the Saṅgha should be not restless and not fickle.

“Āraññikenāvuso[M 2.0135], bhikkhunā saṅghagatena saṅghe viharantena amukharena bhavitabbaṃ avikiṇṇavācena. Sace, āvuso, āraññiko bhikkhu saṅghagato saṅghe viharanto mukharo hoti [V 2.0145] vikiṇṇavāco, tassa bhavanti vattāro. ‘Kiṃ panimassāyasmato āraññikassa ekassāraññe serivihārena yo ayamāyasmā mukharo vikiṇṇavāco’ti – tassa bhavanti [T 2.0217] vattāro. Tasmā āraññikena bhikkhunā saṅghagatena saṅghe viharantena amukharena bhavitabbaṃ avikiṇṇavācena.

“Friends, a forest-dwelling bhikkhu who has come to the Saṅgha and is dwelling in the Saṅgha should not be sharp-tongued and should not be of scattered speech. If, friends, a forest-dwelling bhikkhu who has come to the Saṅgha and is dwelling in the Saṅgha is sharp-tongued and of scattered speech, there will be those who speak against him, saying: ‘What is the use of this venerable one’s dwelling as he pleases alone in the forest, since this venerable one is sharp-tongued and of scattered speech?’ Thus, there will be those who speak against him. Therefore, a forest-dwelling bhikkhu who has come to the Saṅgha and is dwelling in the Saṅgha should not be sharp-tongued and should not be of scattered speech.”

“Āraññikenāvuso, bhikkhunā saṅghagatena saṅghe viharantena suvacena subbacena (sī. ka.) bhavitabbaṃ kalyāṇamittena. Sace, āvuso, āraññiko bhikkhu saṅghagato saṅghe viharanto dubbaco hoti pāpamitto, tassa bhavanti vattāro. ‘Kiṃ panimassāyasmato āraññikassa ekassāraññe serivihārena yo ayamāyasmā dubbaco pāpamitto’ti – tassa bhavanti vattāro. Tasmā āraññikena bhikkhunā saṅghagatena saṅghe viharantena suvacena bhavitabbaṃ kalyāṇamittena.

“Friends, a forest-dwelling bhikkhu who has come to the Saṅgha and is dwelling in the Saṅgha should be easy to admonish and have good friends. If, friends, a forest-dwelling bhikkhu who has come to the Saṅgha and is dwelling in the Saṅgha is difficult to admonish and has bad friends, there will be those who speak against him, saying: ‘What is the use of this venerable one’s dwelling as he pleases alone in the forest, since this venerable one is difficult to admonish and has bad friends?’ Thus, there will be those who speak against him. Therefore, a forest-dwelling bhikkhu who has come to the Saṅgha and is dwelling in the Saṅgha should be easy to admonish and have good friends.”

“Āraññikenāvuso, bhikkhunā indriyesu guttadvārena bhavitabbaṃ. Sace, āvuso, āraññiko bhikkhu indriyesu aguttadvāro hoti, tassa bhavanti vattāro. ‘Kiṃ panimassāyasmato āraññikassa ekassāraññe serivihārena yo ayamāyasmā [P 1.0471] indriyesu aguttadvāro’ti – tassa bhavanti vattāro. Tasmā āraññikena bhikkhunā indriyesu guttadvārena bhavitabbaṃ.

“Friends, a forest-dwelling bhikkhu should have the doors of his sense faculties guarded. If, friends, a forest-dwelling bhikkhu does not have the doors of his sense faculties guarded, there will be those who speak against him, saying: ‘What is the use of this venerable one’s dwelling as he pleases alone in the forest, since this venerable one does not have the doors of his sense faculties guarded?’ Thus, there will be those who speak against him. Therefore, a forest-dwelling bhikkhu should have the doors of his sense faculties guarded.”

“Āraññikenāvuso, bhikkhunā bhojane mattaññunā bhavitabbaṃ. Sace, āvuso, āraññiko bhojane amattaññū hoti, tassa bhavanti vattāro. ‘Kiṃ panimassāyasmato āraññikassa ekassāraññe serivihārena yo ayamāyasmā bhojane amattaññū’ti – tassa bhavanti vattāro. Tasmā āraññikena bhikkhunā bhojane mattaññunā [T 2.0218] bhavitabbaṃ.

“Friends, a forest-dwelling bhikkhu should be moderate in eating. If, friends, a forest-dwelling bhikkhu is not moderate in eating, there will be those who speak against him, saying: ‘What is the use of this venerable one’s dwelling as he pleases alone in the forest, since this venerable one is not moderate in eating?’ Thus, there will be those who speak against him. Therefore, a forest-dwelling bhikkhu should be moderate in eating.”

“Āraññikenāvuso, bhikkhunā jāgariyaṃ anuyuttena bhavitabbaṃ. Sace, āvuso, āraññiko bhikkhu jāgariyaṃ ananuyutto hoti, tassa [M 2.0136] bhavanti vattāro. ‘Kiṃ panimassāyasmato āraññikassa ekassāraññe serivihārena yo ayamāyasmā jāgariyaṃ ananuyutto’ti – tassa bhavanti vattāro. Tasmā āraññikena bhikkhunā jāgariyaṃ anuyuttena bhavitabbaṃ.

Friends, a forest-dwelling bhikkhu should be devoted to wakefulness. If, friends, a forest-dwelling bhikkhu is not devoted to wakefulness, there will be those who speak reproachfully of him: ‘What benefit is there from this venerable one’s solitary life in the forest as he pleases, since this venerable one is not devoted to wakefulness?’ There will be those who speak reproachfully of him. Therefore, a forest-dwelling bhikkhu should be devoted to wakefulness.

“Āraññikenāvuso[V 2.0146], bhikkhunā āraddhavīriyena bhavitabbaṃ. Sace, āvuso, āraññiko bhikkhu kusīto hoti, tassa bhavanti vattāro. ‘Kiṃ panimassāyasmato āraññikassa ekassāraññe serivihārena yo ayamāyasmā kusīto’ti – tassa bhavanti vattāro. Tasmā āraññikena bhikkhunā āraddhavīriyena bhavitabbaṃ.

Friends, a forest-dwelling bhikkhu should have his energy aroused. If, friends, a forest-dwelling bhikkhu is lazy, there will be those who speak reproachfully of him: ‘What benefit is there from this venerable one’s solitary life in the forest as he pleases, since this venerable one is lazy?’ There will be those who speak reproachfully of him. Therefore, a forest-dwelling bhikkhu should have his energy aroused.

“Āraññikenāvuso, bhikkhunā upaṭṭhitassatinā bhavitabbaṃ. Sace, āvuso, āraññiko bhikkhu muṭṭhassatī hoti, tassa bhavanti vattāro. ‘Kiṃ panimassāyasmato āraññikassa ekassāraññe serivihārena yo ayamāyasmā muṭṭhassatī’ti – tassa bhavanti vattāro. Tasmā āraññikena bhikkhunā upaṭṭhitassatinā bhavitabbaṃ.

Friends, a forest-dwelling bhikkhu should have mindfulness established. If, friends, a forest-dwelling bhikkhu is of lapsed mindfulness, there will be those who speak reproachfully of him: ‘What benefit is there from this venerable one’s solitary life in the forest as he pleases, since this venerable one is of lapsed mindfulness?’ There will be those who speak reproachfully of him. Therefore, a forest-dwelling bhikkhu should have mindfulness established.

“Āraññikenāvuso, bhikkhunā samāhitena bhavitabbaṃ. Sace, āvuso, āraññiko bhikkhu asamāhito hoti, tassa bhavanti vattāro. ‘Kiṃ panimassāyasmato āraññikassa ekassāraññe serivihārena [T 2.0219] yo ayamāyasmā asamāhito’ti – tassa bhavanti vattāro. Tasmā āraññikena bhikkhunā samāhitena bhavitabbaṃ.

Friends, a forest-dwelling bhikkhu should be concentrated. If, friends, a forest-dwelling bhikkhu is unconcentrated, there will be those who speak reproachfully of him: ‘What benefit is there from this venerable one’s solitary life in the forest as he pleases, since this venerable one is unconcentrated?’ There will be those who speak reproachfully of him. Therefore, a forest-dwelling bhikkhu should be concentrated.

“Āraññikenāvuso, bhikkhunā paññavatā bhavitabbaṃ. Sace, āvuso, āraññiko bhikkhu duppañño hoti, tassa bhavanti vattāro[P 1.0472]. ‘Kiṃ panimassāyasmato āraññikassa ekassāraññe serivihārena yo ayamāyasmā duppañño’ti – tassa bhavanti vattāro. Tasmā āraññikena bhikkhunā paññavatā bhavitabbaṃ.

Friends, a forest-dwelling bhikkhu should be possessed of wisdom. If, friends, a forest-dwelling bhikkhu is of little wisdom, there will be those who speak reproachfully of him: ‘What benefit is there from this venerable one’s solitary life in the forest as he pleases, since this venerable one is of little wisdom?’ There will be those who speak reproachfully of him. Therefore, a forest-dwelling bhikkhu should be possessed of wisdom.

“Āraññikenāvuso, bhikkhunā abhidhamme abhivinaye yogo karaṇīyo. Santāvuso, āraññikaṃ bhikkhuṃ abhidhamme abhivinaye pañhaṃ pucchitāro. Sace, āvuso, āraññiko bhikkhu abhidhamme abhivinaye pañhaṃ puṭṭho na sampāyati, tassa bhavanti vattāro. ‘Kiṃ panimassāyasmato āraññikassa ekassāraññe serivihārena yo ayamāyasmā abhidhamme abhivinaye pañhaṃ puṭṭho na sampāyatī’ti – tassa bhavanti vattāro. Tasmā [M 2.0137] āraññikena bhikkhunā abhidhamme abhivinaye yogo karaṇīyo.

Friends, a forest-dwelling bhikkhu should apply himself to the Abhidhamma and the Abhivinaya. For, friends, there are those who question a forest-dwelling bhikkhu on the Abhidhamma and the Abhivinaya. If, friends, a forest-dwelling bhikkhu, when questioned on the Abhidhamma and the Abhivinaya, cannot answer satisfactorily, there will be those who speak reproachfully of him: ‘What benefit is there from this venerable one’s solitary life in the forest as he pleases, since, when questioned on the Abhidhamma and the Abhivinaya, he cannot answer satisfactorily?’ There will be those who speak reproachfully of him. Therefore, a forest-dwelling bhikkhu should apply himself to the Abhidhamma and the Abhivinaya.

“Āraññikenāvuso[V 2.0147], bhikkhunā ye te santā vimokkhā atikkamma rūpe āruppā tattha yogo karaṇīyo. Santāvuso, āraññikaṃ bhikkhuṃ ye te santā vimokkhā atikkamma rūpe āruppā tattha pañhaṃ pucchitāro. Sace, āvuso, āraññiko bhikkhu ye te santā vimokkhā atikkamma rūpe āruppā tattha pañhaṃ puṭṭho na sampāyati, tassa bhavanti vattāro. ‘Kiṃ panimassāyasmato āraññikassa ekassāraññe serivihārena yo ayamāyasmā ye te santā vimokkhā atikkamma rūpe āruppā tattha pañhaṃ puṭṭho na sampāyatī’ti – tassa [T 2.0220] bhavanti vattāro. Tasmā āraññikena bhikkhunā ye te santā vimokkhā atikkamma rūpe āruppā tattha yogo karaṇīyo.

Friends, a forest-dwelling bhikkhu should apply himself to those peaceful liberations that are the formless attainments transcending form. For, friends, there are those who question a forest-dwelling bhikkhu about those peaceful liberations that are the formless attainments transcending form. If, friends, a forest-dwelling bhikkhu, when questioned about those peaceful liberations that are the formless attainments transcending form, cannot answer satisfactorily, there will be those who speak reproachfully of him: ‘What benefit is there from this venerable one’s solitary life in the forest as he pleases, since, when questioned about those peaceful liberations that are the formless attainments transcending form, he cannot answer satisfactorily?’ There will be those who speak reproachfully of him. Therefore, a forest-dwelling bhikkhu should apply himself to those peaceful liberations that are the formless attainments transcending form.

“Āraññikenāvuso, bhikkhunā uttari manussadhamme yogo karaṇīyo. Santāvuso, āraññikaṃ bhikkhuṃ uttari manussadhamme pañhaṃ pucchitāro. Sace, āvuso, āraññiko bhikkhu uttari manussadhamme pañhaṃ puṭṭho na sampāyati, tassa bhavanti vattāro. ‘Kiṃ panimassāyasmato āraññikassa ekassāraññe serivihārena yo ayamāyasmā yassatthāya pabbajito tamatthaṃ na jānātī’ti – tassa bhavanti vattāro. Tasmā āraññikena bhikkhunā uttari manussadhamme yogo karaṇīyo”ti.

Friends, a forest-dwelling bhikkhu should apply himself to the supramundane states. For, friends, there are those who question a forest-dwelling bhikkhu about the supramundane states. If, friends, a forest-dwelling bhikkhu, when questioned about the supramundane states, cannot answer satisfactorily, there will be those who speak reproachfully of him: ‘What benefit is there from this venerable one’s solitary life in the forest as he pleases, since he does not know the very purpose for which he went forth?’ There will be those who speak reproachfully of him. Therefore, a forest-dwelling bhikkhu should apply himself to the supramundane states.

Evaṃ vutte, āyasmā mahāmoggallāno mahāmoggalāno (ka.) āyasmantaṃ sāriputtaṃ etadavoca – “āraññikeneva nu kho, āvuso sāriputta, bhikkhunā ime dhammā samādāya vattitabbā udāhu gāmantavihārināpī”ti[P 1.0473]? “Āraññikenāpi kho, āvuso moggallāna, bhikkhunā ime dhammā samādāya vattitabbā pageva gāmantavihārinā”ti.

When this was said, the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna said this to the Venerable Sāriputta: “Friend Sāriputta, should these principles be undertaken and practiced only by a forest-dwelling bhikkhu, or also by one who dwells near a village?” “Friend Moggallāna, these principles should be undertaken and practiced by a forest-dwelling bhikkhu, and all the more so by one who dwells near a village.”

Goliyānisuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ navamaṃ.

The Goliyāni Sutta, the ninth, is finished.

10. Kīṭāgirisuttaṃ

10. The Kīṭāgiri Sutta

174. Evaṃ [T 2.0221][M 2.0138][V 2.0148] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā kāsīsu cārikaṃ carati mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ. Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – “ahaṃ kho, bhikkhave, aññatreva rattibhojanā rattibhojanaṃ (ka.) bhuñjāmi. Aññatra kho panāhaṃ, bhikkhave, rattibhojanā bhuñjamāno appābādhatañca sañjānāmi appātaṅkatañca lahuṭṭhānañca balañca phāsuvihārañca. Etha, tumhepi, bhikkhave, aññatreva rattibhojanā bhuñjatha. Aññatra kho pana, bhikkhave, tumhepi rattibhojanā bhuñjamānā appābādhatañca sañjānissatha appātaṅkatañca lahuṭṭhānañca balañca phāsuvihārañcā”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Atha kho bhagavā kāsīsu anupubbena cārikaṃ caramāno yena kīṭāgiri nāma kāsīnaṃ nigamo tadavasari. Tatra sudaṃ bhagavā kīṭāgirismiṃ viharati kāsīnaṃ nigame.

174. Thus have I heard. At one time, the Blessed One was journeying on tour in the Kāsī country with a large Saṅgha of bhikkhus. There, the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus, I eat, abstaining from eating at night. Bhikkhus, by eating while abstaining from eating at night, I am aware of good health, freedom from affliction, lightness, strength, and dwelling in comfort. Come, you too, bhikkhus, should eat, abstaining from eating at night. Bhikkhus, by eating while abstaining from eating at night, you too will be aware of good health, freedom from affliction, lightness, strength, and dwelling in comfort.” “So be it, venerable sir,” those bhikkhus replied to the Blessed One. Then the Blessed One, journeying on tour by stages through the Kāsī country, arrived at Kīṭāgiri, a market town of the Kāsīs. There the Blessed One dwelt at Kīṭāgiri, in the market town of the Kāsīs.

175. Tena kho pana samayena assajipunabbasukā nāma bhikkhū kīṭāgirismiṃ āvāsikā honti. Atha kho sambahulā bhikkhū yena assajipunabbasukā bhikkhū tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā assajipunabbasuke bhikkhū etadavocuṃ – “bhagavā kho, āvuso, aññatreva rattibhojanā bhuñjati bhikkhusaṅgho ca. Aññatra kho panāvuso, rattibhojanā bhuñjamānā appābādhatañca sañjānanti appātaṅkatañca [T 2.0222] lahuṭṭhānañca balañca phāsuvihārañca. Etha, tumhepi, āvuso, aññatreva rattibhojanā bhuñjatha. Aññatra kho panāvuso, tumhepi rattibhojanā bhuñjamānā appābādhatañca sañjānissatha appātaṅkatañca lahuṭṭhānañca balañca phāsuvihārañcā”ti[P 1.0474]. Evaṃ vutte, assajipunabbasukā bhikkhū te bhikkhū etadavocuṃ – “mayaṃ kho, āvuso, sāyañceva bhuñjāma pāto ca divā ca vikāle. Te mayaṃ sāyañceva bhuñjamānā pāto ca divā ca vikāle appābādhatañca sañjānāma appātaṅkatañca lahuṭṭhānañca balañca phāsuvihārañca. Te mayaṃ kiṃ sandiṭṭhikaṃ hitvā kālikaṃ anudhāvissāma? Sāyañceva mayaṃ bhuñjissāma pāto ca divā ca vikāle”ti.

175. Now at that time, bhikkhus named Assaji and Punabbasu were resident at Kīṭāgiri. Then many bhikkhus approached the bhikkhus Assaji and Punabbasu and said this to them: “Friends, the Blessed One eats, abstaining from eating at night, and so does the Saṅgha of bhikkhus. Friends, by eating while abstaining from eating at night, they are aware of good health, freedom from affliction, lightness, strength, and dwelling in comfort. Come, you too, friends, should eat, abstaining from eating at night. Friends, by eating while abstaining from eating at night, you too will be aware of good health, freedom from affliction, lightness, strength, and dwelling in comfort.” When this was said, the bhikkhus Assaji and Punabbasu said this to those bhikkhus: “Friends, we eat in the evening, in the morning, and during the day at the wrong time. By eating in the evening, in the morning, and during the day at the wrong time, we are aware of good health, freedom from affliction, lightness, strength, and dwelling in comfort. Why should we, having abandoned a benefit visible in the present, run after one that is of a future time? We will eat in the evening, in the morning, and during the day at the wrong time.”

Yato [V 2.0149] kho te bhikkhū nāsakkhiṃsu assajipunabbasuke bhikkhū saññāpetuṃ, atha yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā [M 2.0139] ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Ekamantaṃ nisinnā kho te bhikkhū bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ – “idha mayaṃ, bhante, yena assajipunabbasukā bhikkhū tenupasaṅkamimha; upasaṅkamitvā assajipunabbasuke bhikkhū etadavocumha – ‘bhagavā kho, āvuso, aññatreva rattibhojanā bhuñjati bhikkhusaṅgho ca; aññatra kho panāvuso, rattibhojanā bhuñjamānā appābādhatañca sañjānanti appātaṅkatañca lahuṭṭhānañca balañca phāsuvihārañca. Etha, tumhepi, āvuso[T 2.0223], aññatreva rattibhojanā bhuñjatha. Aññatra kho panāvuso, tumhepi rattibhojanā bhuñjamānā appābādhatañca sañjānissatha appātaṅkatañca lahuṭṭhānañca balañca phāsuvihārañcā’ti. Evaṃ vutte, bhante, assajipunabbasukā bhikkhū amhe etadavocuṃ – ‘mayaṃ kho, āvuso, sāyañceva bhuñjāma pāto ca divā ca vikāle. Te mayaṃ sāyañceva bhuñjamānā pāto ca divā ca vikāle appābādhatañca sañjānāma appātaṅkatañca lahuṭṭhānañca balañca phāsuvihārañca. Te mayaṃ kiṃ sandiṭṭhikaṃ hitvā kālikaṃ anudhāvissāma? Sāyañceva mayaṃ bhuñjissāma pāto ca divā ca vikāle’ti. Yato kho mayaṃ, bhante, nāsakkhimha assajipunabbasuke bhikkhū saññāpetuṃ, atha mayaṃ etamatthaṃ bhagavato ārocemā”ti.

Since those bhikkhus were unable to persuade the bhikkhus Assaji and Punabbasu, they approached the Blessed One. Having approached and paid homage to the Blessed One, they sat down to one side. Seated to one side, those bhikkhus said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, we approached the bhikkhus Assaji and Punabbasu and said this to them: ‘Friends, the Blessed One eats, abstaining from eating at night, and so does the Saṅgha of bhikkhus. Friends, by eating while abstaining from eating at night, they are aware of good health, freedom from affliction, lightness, strength, and dwelling in comfort. Come, you too, friends, should eat, abstaining from eating at night. Friends, by eating while abstaining from eating at night, you too will be aware of good health, freedom from affliction, lightness, strength, and dwelling in comfort.’ When this was said, venerable sir, the bhikkhus Assaji and Punabbasu said this to us: ‘Friends, we eat in the evening, in the morning, and during the day at the wrong time. By eating in the evening, in the morning, and during the day at the wrong time, we are aware of good health, freedom from affliction, lightness, strength, and dwelling in comfort. Why should we, having abandoned a benefit visible in the present, run after one that is of a future time? We will eat in the evening, in the morning, and during the day at the wrong time.’ Since, venerable sir, we were unable to persuade the bhikkhus Assaji and Punabbasu, we now report this matter to the Blessed One.”

176. Atha kho bhagavā aññataraṃ bhikkhuṃ āmantesi – “ehi tvaṃ, bhikkhu, mama vacanena assajipunabbasuke bhikkhū āmantehi – ‘satthā āyasmante āmantetī’”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho so bhikkhu bhagavato paṭissutvā yena assajipunabbasukā bhikkhū tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā assajipunabbasuke bhikkhū etadavoca – “satthā āyasmante āmantetī”ti. “Evamāvuso”ti kho assajipunabbasukā bhikkhū tassa bhikkhuno paṭissutvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Ekamantaṃ nisinne kho assajipunabbasuke bhikkhū bhagavā etadavoca – “saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, sambahulā bhikkhū tumhe upasaṅkamitvā [T 2.0224] etadavocuṃ – ‘bhagavā kho, āvuso, aññatreva rattibhojanā bhuñjati bhikkhusaṅgho ca. Aññatra kho panāvuso, rattibhojanā bhuñjamānā appābādhatañca sañjānanti appātaṅkatañca lahuṭṭhānañca balañca phāsuvihārañca. Etha, tumhepi, āvuso, aññatreva rattibhojanā bhuñjatha. Aññatra kho panāvuso, tumhepi rattibhojanā [V 2.0150] bhuñjamānā [P 1.0475] appābādhatañca sañjānissatha appātaṅkatañca lahuṭṭhānañca balañca phāsuvihārañcā’ti. Evaṃ vutte [M 2.0140] kira kiṃ nu (ka.), bhikkhave, tumhe te bhikkhū evaṃ avacuttha – ‘mayaṃ kho panāvuso, sāyañceva bhuñjāma pāto ca divā ca vikāle. Te mayaṃ sāyañceva bhuñjamānā pāto ca divā ca vikāle appābādhatañca sañjānāma appātaṅkatañca lahuṭṭhānañca balañca phāsuvihārañca. Te mayaṃ kiṃ sandiṭṭhikaṃ hitvā kālikaṃ anudhāvissāma? Sāyañceva mayaṃ bhuñjissāma pāto ca divā ca vikāle’”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”.

176. Then the Blessed One addressed a certain monk: 'Come, monk, with my words call the monks Assaji and Punabbasu, saying: “The Teacher calls the venerable ones.”' 'Yes, venerable sir,' that monk replied to the Blessed One. Having replied, he went to where the monks Assaji and Punabbasu were; having approached, he said this to the monks Assaji and Punabbasu: 'The Teacher calls the venerable ones.' 'Yes, friend,' the monks Assaji and Punabbasu replied to that monk. Then they went to where the Blessed One was; having approached, they paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. To the monks Assaji and Punabbasu sitting to one side, the Blessed One said this: 'Is it true, monks, that many monks approached you and said this: “Friends, the Blessed One abstains from the night meal, and so does the Sangha of monks. Friends, by abstaining from the night meal, they experience freedom from illness, freedom from affliction, lightness of body, strength, and comfortable abiding. Come, friends, you too should abstain from the night meal. Friends, by abstaining from the night meal, you too will experience freedom from illness, freedom from affliction, lightness of body, strength, and comfortable abiding.” When this was said, it is said, monks, did you say this to those monks: “But we, friends, eat in the evening, in the morning, and during the day at the wrong time. We who eat in the evening, in the morning, and during the day at the wrong time experience freedom from illness, freedom from affliction, lightness of body, strength, and comfortable abiding. Why should we, having abandoned what is directly visible, pursue what is of a future time? We will eat in the evening, in the morning, and during the day at the wrong time.”?' 'Yes, venerable sir.'

177. “Kiṃ nu me tumhe, bhikkhave, evaṃ dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānātha yaṃ kiñcāyaṃ purisapuggalo paṭisaṃvedeti sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā tassa akusalā dhammā parihāyanti kusalā dhammā abhivaḍḍhantī”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”. “Nanu me tumhe, bhikkhave, evaṃ dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānātha idhekaccassa yaṃ evarūpaṃ sukhaṃ vedanaṃ vedayato akusalā dhammā abhivaḍḍhanti kusalā dhammā parihāyanti, idha panekaccassa evarūpaṃ sukhaṃ vedanaṃ vedayato akusalā dhammā parihāyanti[T 2.0225], kusalā dhammā abhivaḍḍhanti, idhekaccassa evarūpaṃ dukkhaṃ vedanaṃ vedayato akusalā dhammā abhivaḍḍhanti kusalā dhammā parihāyanti, idha panekaccassa evarūpaṃ dukkhaṃ vedanaṃ vedayato akusalā dhammā parihāyanti kusalā dhammā abhivaḍḍhanti, idhekaccassa evarūpaṃ adukkhamasukhaṃ vedanaṃ vedayato akusalā dhammā abhivaḍḍhanti kusalā dhammā parihāyanti, idha panekaccassa evarūpaṃ adukkhamasukhaṃ vedanaṃ vedayato akusalā dhammā parihāyanti kusalā dhammā abhivaḍḍhantī”ti? “Evaṃ, bhante”.

177. “Monks, do you understand the Dhamma taught by me in this way: ‘Whatever pleasant feeling, painful feeling, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling this individual person experiences, for him unwholesome states decline and wholesome states increase’?” “No, venerable sir.” “Monks, do you not understand the Dhamma taught by me in this way: ‘Here, for a certain person experiencing such a pleasant feeling, unwholesome states increase and wholesome states decline; but here, for another person experiencing such a pleasant feeling, unwholesome states decline and wholesome states increase. Here, for a certain person experiencing such a painful feeling, unwholesome states increase and wholesome states decline; but here, for another person experiencing such a painful feeling, unwholesome states decline and wholesome states increase. Here, for a certain person experiencing such a neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, unwholesome states increase and wholesome states decline; but here, for another person experiencing such a neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, unwholesome states decline and wholesome states increase’?” “Yes, venerable sir.”

178. “Sādhu, bhikkhave! Mayā cetaṃ, bhikkhave, aññātaṃ abhavissa adiṭṭhaṃ aviditaṃ asacchikataṃ aphassitaṃ paññāya – ‘idhekaccassa evarūpaṃ sukhaṃ vedanaṃ vedayato akusalā dhammā abhivaḍḍhanti kusalā dhammā parihāyantī’ti, evāhaṃ ajānanto ‘evarūpaṃ sukhaṃ vedanaṃ pajahathā’ti vadeyyaṃ; api nu me etaṃ, bhikkhave, patirūpaṃ abhavissā”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”. “Yasmā ca kho etaṃ, bhikkhave, mayā ñātaṃ diṭṭhaṃ viditaṃ sacchikataṃ phassitaṃ paññāya – ‘idhekaccassa evarūpaṃ sukhaṃ vedanaṃ vedayato akusalā dhammā [P 1.0476] abhivaḍḍhanti kusalā dhammā parihāyantī’ti, tasmāhaṃ ‘evarūpaṃ sukhaṃ vedanaṃ pajahathā’ti vadāmi. Mayā cetaṃ, bhikkhave, aññātaṃ abhavissa adiṭṭhaṃ aviditaṃ asacchikataṃ [M 2.0141] aphassitaṃ paññāya – ‘idhekaccassa evarūpaṃ [V 2.0151] sukhaṃ vedanaṃ vedayato akusalā [T 2.0226] dhammā parihāyanti kusalā dhammā abhivaḍḍhantī’ti, evāhaṃ ajānanto ‘evarūpaṃ sukhaṃ vedanaṃ upasampajja viharathā’ti vadeyyaṃ; api nu me etaṃ, bhikkhave, patirūpaṃ abhavissā”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”. “Yasmā ca kho etaṃ, bhikkhave, mayā ñātaṃ diṭṭhaṃ viditaṃ sacchikataṃ phassitaṃ paññāya – ‘idhekaccassa evarūpaṃ sukhaṃ vedanaṃ vedayato akusalā dhammā parihāyanti, kusalā dhammā abhivaḍḍhantī’ti, tasmāhaṃ ‘evarūpaṃ sukhaṃ vedanaṃ upasampajja viharathā’ti vadāmi.

178. “Good, monks! Monks, if this principle—that for a certain person here, experiencing such a pleasant feeling, unwholesome states increase and wholesome states decline—had been unknown by me, unseen, not evident, unrealized, and not contacted by wisdom, then I, not knowing this, would say, ‘Abandon such a pleasant feeling.’ Would this have been appropriate for me?” “No, venerable sir.” “But because, monks, this principle—that for a certain person here, experiencing such a pleasant feeling, unwholesome states increase and wholesome states decline—has been known by me, seen, made evident, realized, and contacted by wisdom, therefore I say, ‘Abandon such a pleasant feeling.’ Monks, if this principle—that for a certain person here, experiencing such a pleasant feeling, unwholesome states decline and wholesome states increase—had been unknown by me, unseen, not evident, unrealized, and not contacted by wisdom, then I, not knowing this, would say, ‘Dwell having attained such a pleasant feeling.’ Would this have been appropriate for me?” “No, venerable sir.” “But because, monks, this principle—that for a certain person here, experiencing such a pleasant feeling, unwholesome states decline and wholesome states increase—has been known by me, seen, made evident, realized, and contacted by wisdom, therefore I say, ‘Dwell having attained such a pleasant feeling.’”

179. “Mayā cetaṃ, bhikkhave, aññātaṃ abhavissa adiṭṭhaṃ aviditaṃ asacchikataṃ aphassitaṃ paññāya – ‘idhekaccassa evarūpaṃ dukkhaṃ vedanaṃ vedayato akusalā dhammā abhivaḍḍhanti kusalā dhammā parihāyantī’ti, evāhaṃ ajānanto ‘evarūpaṃ dukkhaṃ vedanaṃ pajahathā’ti vadeyyaṃ; api nu me etaṃ, bhikkhave, patirūpaṃ abhavissā”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”. “Yasmā ca kho etaṃ, bhikkhave, mayā ñātaṃ diṭṭhaṃ viditaṃ sacchikataṃ phassitaṃ paññāya – ‘idhekaccassa evarūpaṃ dukkhaṃ vedanaṃ vedayato akusalā dhammā abhivaḍḍhanti kusalā dhammā parihāyantī’ti, tasmāhaṃ ‘evarūpaṃ dukkhaṃ vedanaṃ pajahathā’ti vadāmi. Mayā cetaṃ, bhikkhave, aññātaṃ abhavissa adiṭṭhaṃ aviditaṃ asacchikataṃ aphassitaṃ paññāya – ‘idhekaccassa evarūpaṃ dukkhaṃ vedanaṃ vedayato akusalā dhammā parihāyanti kusalā dhammā abhivaḍḍhantī’ti, evāhaṃ ajānanto ‘evarūpaṃ dukkhaṃ vedanaṃ upasampajja viharathā’ti vadeyyaṃ; api nu me etaṃ, bhikkhave, patirūpaṃ abhavissā”ti[T 2.0227]? “No hetaṃ, bhante”. “Yasmā ca kho etaṃ, bhikkhave, mayā ñātaṃ diṭṭhaṃ viditaṃ sacchikataṃ phassitaṃ paññāya – ‘idhekaccassa evarūpaṃ dukkhaṃ vedanaṃ vedayato akusalā dhammā parihāyanti kusalā dhammā abhivaḍḍhantī’ti, tasmāhaṃ ‘evarūpaṃ dukkhaṃ vedanaṃ upasampajja viharathā’ti vadāmi.

179. Bhikkhus, if this principle were unknown by me, unseen, not understood, unrealized, and untouched with wisdom—that ‘for a certain person here, experiencing such a painful feeling, unwholesome states increase and wholesome states decline’—then, not knowing this, would I say, ‘Abandon such a painful feeling’? Bhikkhus, would that be proper for me?” “Indeed not, venerable sir.” “And because, bhikkhus, this principle is known by me, seen, understood, realized, and touched with wisdom—that ‘for a certain person here, experiencing such a painful feeling, unwholesome states increase and wholesome states decline’—therefore I say, ‘Abandon such a painful feeling.’ Bhikkhus, if this principle were unknown by me, unseen, not understood, unrealized, and untouched with wisdom—that ‘for a certain person here, experiencing such a painful feeling, unwholesome states decline and wholesome states increase’—then, not knowing this, would I say, ‘Dwell having attained such a painful feeling’? Bhikkhus, would that be proper for me?” “Indeed not, venerable sir.” “And because, bhikkhus, this principle is known by me, seen, understood, realized, and touched with wisdom—that ‘for a certain person here, experiencing such a painful feeling, unwholesome states decline and wholesome states increase’—therefore I say, ‘Dwell having attained such a painful feeling.’”

180. “Mayā cetaṃ, bhikkhave, aññātaṃ abhavissa adiṭṭhaṃ aviditaṃ asacchikataṃ aphassitaṃ paññāya – ‘idhekaccassa evarūpaṃ adukkhamasukhaṃ vedanaṃ vedayato akusalā dhammā abhivaḍḍhanti kusalā dhammā parihāyantī’ti, evāhaṃ ajānanto ‘evarūpaṃ adukkhamasukhaṃ vedanaṃ pajahathā’ti vadeyyaṃ; api nu me etaṃ, bhikkhave, patirūpaṃ abhavissā”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”. “Yasmā ca kho etaṃ, bhikkhave, mayā ñātaṃ diṭṭhaṃ viditaṃ sacchikataṃ phassitaṃ paññāya [M 2.0142] – ‘idhekaccassa evarūpaṃ adukkhamasukhaṃ vedanaṃ vedayato akusalā dhammā abhivaḍḍhanti kusalā dhammā parihāyantī’ti, tasmāhaṃ ‘evarūpaṃ adukkhamasukhaṃ vedanaṃ pajahathā’ti vadāmi”. Mayā cetaṃ, bhikkhave, aññātaṃ abhavissa adiṭṭhaṃ aviditaṃ asacchikataṃ aphassitaṃ paññāya [V 2.0152] – ‘idhekaccassa evarūpaṃ adukkhamasukhaṃ vedanaṃ vedayato akusalā dhammā parihāyanti kusalā dhammā abhivaḍḍhantī’ti, evāhaṃ ajānanto ‘evarūpaṃ adukkhamasukhaṃ vedanaṃ upasampajja viharathā’ti vadeyyaṃ; api nu me etaṃ, bhikkhave, patirūpaṃ abhavissā”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”. “Yasmā ca kho etaṃ, bhikkhave, mayā ñātaṃ diṭṭhaṃ [T 2.0228] viditaṃ sacchikataṃ phassitaṃ paññāya – ‘idhekaccassa evarūpaṃ adukkhamasukhaṃ vedanaṃ vedayato akusalā dhammā parihāyanti kusalā dhammā abhivaḍḍhantī’ti, tasmāhaṃ ‘evarūpaṃ [P 1.0477] adukkhamasukhaṃ vedanaṃ upasampajja viharathā’ti vadāmi.

180. Bhikkhus, if this principle were unknown by me, unseen, not understood, unrealized, and untouched with wisdom—that ‘for a certain person here, experiencing such a neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, unwholesome states increase and wholesome states decline’—then, not knowing this, would I say, ‘Abandon such a neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling’? Bhikkhus, would that be proper for me?” “Indeed not, venerable sir.” “And because, bhikkhus, this principle is known by me, seen, understood, realized, and touched with wisdom—that ‘for a certain person here, experiencing such a neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, unwholesome states increase and wholesome states decline’—therefore I say, ‘Abandon such a neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling.’ Bhikkhus, if this principle were unknown by me, unseen, not understood, unrealized, and untouched with wisdom—that ‘for a certain person here, experiencing such a neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, unwholesome states decline and wholesome states increase’—then, not knowing this, would I say, ‘Dwell having attained such a neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling’? Bhikkhus, would that be proper for me?” “Indeed not, venerable sir.” “And because, bhikkhus, this principle is known by me, seen, understood, realized, and touched with wisdom—that ‘for a certain person here, experiencing such a neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, unwholesome states decline and wholesome states increase’—therefore I say, ‘Dwell having attained such a neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling.’”

181. “Nāhaṃ, bhikkhave, sabbesaṃyeva bhikkhūnaṃ ‘appamādena karaṇīya’nti vadāmi; na panāhaṃ, bhikkhave, sabbesaṃyeva bhikkhūnaṃ ‘na appamādena karaṇīya’nti vadāmi. Ye te, bhikkhave, bhikkhū arahanto khīṇāsavā vusitavanto katakaraṇīyā ohitabhārā anuppattasadatthā parikkhīṇabhavasaṃyojanā sammadaññā vimuttā, tathārūpānāhaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṃ ‘na appamādena karaṇīya’nti vadāmi. Taṃ kissa hetu? Kataṃ tesaṃ appamādena. Abhabbā te pamajjituṃ. Ye ca kho te, bhikkhave, bhikkhū sekkhā appattamānasā anuttaraṃ yogakkhemaṃ patthayamānā viharanti, tathārūpānāhaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṃ ‘appamādena karaṇīya’nti vadāmi. Taṃ kissa hetu? Appeva nāmime āyasmanto anulomikāni senāsanāni paṭisevamānā kalyāṇamitte bhajamānā indriyāni samannānayamānā – yassatthāya kulaputtā sammadeva agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajanti tadanuttaraṃ – brahmacariyapariyosānaṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja vihareyyunti! Imaṃ kho ahaṃ, bhikkhave, imesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ appamādaphalaṃ sampassamāno ‘appamādena karaṇīya’nti vadāmi.

181. Bhikkhus, I do not say for all bhikkhus that ‘it is to be done with heedfulness’; nor, bhikkhus, do I say for all bhikkhus that ‘it is not to be done with heedfulness.’ Those bhikkhus, bhikkhus, who are arahants, whose taints are destroyed, who have lived the holy life, done what was to be done, laid down the burden, attained their own goal, whose fetters of existence are utterly destroyed, and who are liberated through perfect direct knowledge—for such bhikkhus, I say, ‘it is not to be done with heedfulness.’ For what reason? It has been done by them with heedfulness. They are incapable of being heedless. But those bhikkhus, bhikkhus, who are trainees, who have not attained their mind’s goal, and who dwell aspiring for the unsurpassed security from bondage—for such bhikkhus, I say, ‘it is to be done with heedfulness.’ For what reason? It may be that these venerable ones, by frequenting suitable lodgings, associating with good friends, and rightly directing their faculties, might, in this very life, realize for themselves through direct knowledge that unsurpassed culmination of the holy life for the sake of which clansmen rightly go forth from the household life into homelessness, and having realized it, may dwell having attained it. Seeing this fruit of heedfulness for these bhikkhus, I say, ‘it is to be done with heedfulness.’”

182. “Sattime[T 2.0229], bhikkhave, puggalā santo saṃvijjamānā lokasmiṃ. Katame satta? Ubhatobhāgavimutto, paññāvimutto, kāyasakkhi, diṭṭhippatto, saddhāvimutto, dhammānusārī, saddhānusārī.

182. Bhikkhus, these seven persons are found existing in the world. Which seven? The one liberated in both ways, the one liberated by wisdom, the body-witness, the one who has attained to view, the one liberated by faith, the Dhamma-follower, and the faith-follower.

“Katamo [M 2.0143] ca, bhikkhave, puggalo ubhatobhāgavimutto? Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo ye te santā vimokkhā atikkamma rūpe āruppā te kāyena phusitvā phassitvā (sī. pī.) viharati paññāya cassa disvā [V 2.0153] āsavā parikkhīṇā honti. Ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, puggalo ubhatobhāgavimutto imassa kho ahaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno ‘na appamādena karaṇīya’nti vadāmi. Taṃ kissa hetu? Kataṃ tassa appamādena. Abhabbo so pamajjituṃ.

And what, bhikkhus, is the person liberated in both ways? Here, bhikkhus, a certain person dwells having contacted with the mental body those peaceful liberations that are the formless attainments, having transcended forms; and having seen with wisdom, his taints are destroyed. This, bhikkhus, is called the person liberated in both ways. For this bhikkhu, bhikkhus, I do not say, 'There is something to be done with heedfulness.' For what reason? What was to be done with heedfulness has been done by him. He is incapable of being heedless.

“Katamo ca, bhikkhave, puggalo paññāvimutto? Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo ye te santā vimokkhā atikkamma rūpe āruppā te na kāyena phusitvā viharati, paññāya cassa disvā āsavā parikkhīṇā honti. Ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, puggalo [P 1.0478] paññāvimutto. Imassapi kho ahaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno ‘na appamādena karaṇīya’nti vadāmi. Taṃ kissa hetu? Kataṃ tassa appamādena. Abhabbo so pamajjituṃ.

And what, bhikkhus, is the person liberated by wisdom? Here, bhikkhus, a certain person does not dwell having contacted with the mental body those peaceful liberations that are the formless attainments, having transcended forms; but having seen with wisdom, his taints are destroyed. This, bhikkhus, is called the person liberated by wisdom. For this bhikkhu also, bhikkhus, I do not say, 'There is something to be done with heedfulness.' For what reason? What was to be done with heedfulness has been done by him. He is incapable of being heedless.

“Katamo ca, bhikkhave, puggalo kāyasakkhi? Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo ye te santā vimokkhā atikkamma rūpe āruppā [T 2.0230] te kāyena phusitvā viharati, paññāya cassa disvā ekacce āsavā parikkhīṇā honti. Ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, puggalo kāyasakkhi. Imassa kho ahaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno ‘appamādena karaṇīya’nti vadāmi. Taṃ kissa hetu? Appeva nāma ayamāyasmā anulomikāni senāsanāni paṭisevamāno kalyāṇamitte bhajamāno indriyāni samannānayamāno – yassatthāya kulaputtā sammadeva agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajanti tadanuttaraṃ – brahmacariyapariyosānaṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja vihareyyāti! Imaṃ kho ahaṃ, bhikkhave, imassa bhikkhuno appamādaphalaṃ sampassamāno ‘appamādena karaṇīya’nti vadāmi.

And what, bhikkhus, is the body-witness? Here, bhikkhus, a certain person dwells having contacted with the mental body those peaceful liberations that are the formless attainments, having transcended forms; and having seen with wisdom, some of his taints are destroyed. This, bhikkhus, is called the body-witness. For this bhikkhu, bhikkhus, I say, 'There is something to be done with heedfulness.' For what reason? It is possible that this venerable one, by frequenting suitable lodgings, associating with good friends, and balancing his faculties, might realize for himself with direct knowledge in this very life that unsurpassed culmination of the holy life for the sake of which clansmen rightly go forth from the household life into homelessness, and having attained it, dwell therein. Seeing this fruit of heedfulness for this bhikkhu, bhikkhus, I say, 'There is something to be done with heedfulness.'

“Katamo ca, bhikkhave, puggalo diṭṭhippatto? Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo ye te santā vimokkhā atikkamma rūpe āruppā te na kāyena phusitvā viharati, paññāya cassa disvā ekacce āsavā parikkhīṇā honti, tathāgatappaveditā cassa dhammā paññāya vodiṭṭhā honti vocaritā. Ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, puggalo diṭṭhippatto. Imassapi kho ahaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno ‘appamādena karaṇīya’nti vadāmi. Taṃ kissa [M 2.0144] hetu? Appeva nāma ayamāyasmā anulomikāni senāsanāni paṭisevamāno kalyāṇamitte bhajamāno indriyāni samannānayamāno – yassatthāya kulaputtā sammadeva agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajanti tadanuttaraṃ – brahmacariyapariyosānaṃ [T 2.0231][V 2.0154] diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja vihareyyāti! Imaṃ kho ahaṃ, bhikkhave, imassa bhikkhuno appamādaphalaṃ sampassamāno ‘appamādena karaṇīya’nti vadāmi.

And what, bhikkhus, is the view-attainer? Here, bhikkhus, a certain person does not dwell having contacted with the mental body those peaceful liberations that are the formless attainments, having transcended forms; but having seen with wisdom, some of his taints are destroyed, and the teachings proclaimed by the Tathāgata are well seen and well examined by him with wisdom. This, bhikkhus, is called the view-attainer. For this bhikkhu also, bhikkhus, I say, 'There is something to be done with heedfulness.' For what reason? It is possible that this venerable one, by frequenting suitable lodgings, associating with good friends, and balancing his faculties, might realize for himself with direct knowledge in this very life that unsurpassed culmination of the holy life for the sake of which clansmen rightly go forth from the household life into homelessness, and having attained it, dwell therein. Seeing this fruit of heedfulness for this bhikkhu, bhikkhus, I say, 'There is something to be done with heedfulness.'

“Katamo ca, bhikkhave, puggalo saddhāvimutto. Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo ye te santā vimokkhā atikkamma rūpe āruppā te na kāyena phusitvā viharati, paññāya cassa disvā ekacce āsavā parikkhīṇā honti, tathāgate cassa saddhā niviṭṭhā hoti mūlajātā patiṭṭhitā. Ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, puggalo saddhāvimutto. Imassapi kho ahaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno ‘appamādena karaṇīya’nti vadāmi. Taṃ kissa hetu? Appeva nāma ayamāyasmā anulomikāni senāsanāni [P 1.0479] paṭisevamāno kalyāṇamitte bhajamāno indriyāni samannānayamāno – yassatthāya kulaputtā sammadeva agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajanti tadanuttaraṃ – brahmacariyapariyosānaṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja vihareyyāti! Imaṃ kho ahaṃ, bhikkhave, imassa bhikkhuno appamādaphalaṃ sampassamāno ‘appamādena karaṇīya’nti vadāmi.

And what, bhikkhus, is the person liberated by faith? Here, bhikkhus, a certain person does not dwell having contacted with the mental body those peaceful liberations that are the formless attainments, having transcended forms; but having seen with wisdom, some of his taints are destroyed, and his faith in the Tathāgata is settled, rooted, and established. This, bhikkhus, is called the person liberated by faith. For this bhikkhu also, bhikkhus, I say, 'There is something to be done with heedfulness.' For what reason? It is possible that this venerable one, by frequenting suitable lodgings, associating with good friends, and balancing his faculties, might realize for himself with direct knowledge in this very life that unsurpassed culmination of the holy life for the sake of which clansmen rightly go forth from the household life into homelessness, and having attained it, dwell therein. Seeing this fruit of heedfulness for this bhikkhu, bhikkhus, I say, 'There is something to be done with heedfulness.'

“Katamo ca, bhikkhave, puggalo dhammānusārī? Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo ye te santā vimokkhā atikkamma rūpe āruppā te na kāyena phusitvā viharati, paññāya cassa disvā ekacce āsavā parikkhīṇā disvā āsavā aparikkhīṇā (sī. pī.) honti, tathāgatappaveditā cassa [T 2.0232] dhammā paññāya mattaso nijjhānaṃ khamanti, api cassa ime dhammā honti, seyyathidaṃ – saddhindriyaṃ, vīriyindriyaṃ, satindriyaṃ, samādhindriyaṃ, paññindriyaṃ. Ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, puggalo dhammānusārī. Imassapi kho ahaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno ‘appamādena karaṇīya’nti vadāmi. Taṃ kissa hetu? Appeva nāma ayamāyasmā anulomikāni senāsanāni paṭisevamāno kalyāṇamitte bhajamāno indriyāni samannānayamāno – yassatthāya kulaputtā sammadeva agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajanti tadanuttaraṃ – brahmacariyapariyosānaṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja vihareyyāti[M 2.0145]! Imaṃ kho ahaṃ, bhikkhave, imassa bhikkhuno appamādaphalaṃ sampassamāno ‘appamādena karaṇīya’nti vadāmi.

And what, bhikkhus, is the Dhamma-follower? Here, bhikkhus, a certain person does not dwell having contacted with the mental body those peaceful liberations that are the formless attainments, having transcended forms; but having seen with wisdom, some of his taints are destroyed. Moreover, the teachings proclaimed by the Tathāgata are acceptable to him for reflection to a moderate degree with wisdom. And he has these qualities, namely: the faculty of faith, the faculty of energy, the faculty of mindfulness, the faculty of concentration, and the faculty of wisdom. This, bhikkhus, is called the Dhamma-follower. For this bhikkhu also, bhikkhus, I say, 'There is something to be done with heedfulness.' For what reason? It is possible that this venerable one, by frequenting suitable lodgings, associating with good friends, and balancing his faculties, might realize for himself with direct knowledge in this very life that unsurpassed culmination of the holy life for the sake of which clansmen rightly go forth from the household life into homelessness, and having attained it, dwell therein. Seeing this fruit of heedfulness for this bhikkhu, bhikkhus, I say, 'There is something to be done with heedfulness.'

“Katamo [V 2.0155] ca, bhikkhave, puggalo saddhānusārī? Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo ye te santā vimokkhā atikkamma rūpe āruppā te na kāyena phusitvā viharati, paññāya cassa disvā ekacce āsavā parikkhīṇā disvā āsavā aparikkhīṇā (sī. pī.) honti, tathāgate cassa saddhāmattaṃ hoti pemamattaṃ, api cassa ime dhammā honti, seyyathidaṃ – saddhindriyaṃ, vīriyindriyaṃ, satindriyaṃ, samādhindriyaṃ, paññindriyaṃ. Ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, puggalo saddhānusārī. Imassapi kho ahaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno ‘appamādena karaṇīya’nti vadāmi. Taṃ kissa hetu? Appeva nāma ayamāyasmā anulomikāni senāsanāni paṭisevamāno [T 2.0233] kalyāṇamitte bhajamāno indriyāni samannānayamāno – yassatthāya kulaputtā sammadeva agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajanti tadanuttaraṃ – brahmacariyapariyosānaṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja vihareyyāti! Imaṃ kho ahaṃ, bhikkhave, imassa bhikkhuno appamādaphalaṃ sampassamāno ‘appamādena karaṇīya’nti vadāmi.

And what, bhikkhus, is a person who is a faith-follower? Here, bhikkhus, a certain person does not dwell having contacted with the body those peaceful liberations that, transcending forms, are formless; but having seen with wisdom, some of his taints are destroyed, and he has merely faith, merely love for the Tathāgata. Moreover, he has these qualities: the faculty of faith, the faculty of energy, the faculty of mindfulness, the faculty of concentration, and the faculty of wisdom. This, bhikkhus, is called a person who is a faith-follower. For this bhikkhu, too, I say there is a task to be done with heedfulness. For what reason? It may be that this venerable one, by frequenting suitable lodgings, associating with good friends, and balancing his faculties, may realize for himself through direct knowledge in this very life that unsurpassed culmination of the holy life for which clansmen rightly go forth from the household life into homelessness, and having realized it, may enter upon it and dwell therein. Seeing this fruit of heedfulness for this bhikkhu, I say there is a task to be done with heedfulness.

183. “Nāhaṃ, bhikkhave, ādikeneva aññārādhanaṃ vadāmi; api ca, bhikkhave, anupubbasikkhā anupubbakiriyā anupubbapaṭipadā [P 1.0480] aññārādhanā hoti. Kathañca, bhikkhave, anupubbasikkhā anupubbakiriyā anupubbapaṭipadā aññārādhanā hoti? Idha, bhikkhave, saddhājāto upasaṅkamati, upasaṅkamanto payirupāsati, payirupāsanto sotaṃ odahati, ohitasoto dhammaṃ suṇāti, sutvā dhammaṃ dhāreti, dhatānaṃ dhātānaṃ (ka.) dhammānaṃ atthaṃ upaparikkhati, atthaṃ upaparikkhato dhammā nijjhānaṃ khamanti, dhammanijjhānakkhantiyā sati chando jāyati, chandajāto ussahati, ussāhetvā tuleti, tulayitvā padahati, pahitatto samāno kāyena ceva paramasaccaṃ sacchikaroti, paññāya ca naṃ ativijjha passati. Sāpi nāma, bhikkhave, saddhā nāhosi; tampi nāma, bhikkhave, upasaṅkamanaṃ nāhosi; sāpi nāma, bhikkhave, payirupāsanā nāhosi; tampi nāma, bhikkhave, sotāvadhānaṃ nāhosi[M 2.0146]; tampi nāma, bhikkhave, dhammassavanaṃ nāhosi; sāpi nāma, bhikkhave, dhammadhāraṇā nāhosi; sāpi nāma, bhikkhave, atthūpaparikkhā nāhosi; sāpi nāma, bhikkhave, dhammanijjhānakkhanti [T 2.0234] nāhosi; sopi nāma, bhikkhave, chando nāhosi; sopi nāma, bhikkhave, ussāho nāhosi; sāpi nāma, bhikkhave, tulanā nāhosi; tampi nāma, bhikkhave, padhānaṃ nāhosi. Vippaṭipannāttha, bhikkhave, micchāpaṭipannāttha, bhikkhave. Kīva dūrevime, bhikkhave, moghapurisā apakkantā imamhā dhammavinayā.

183. Bhikkhus, I do not say that the attainment of final knowledge occurs right at the beginning. Rather, bhikkhus, the attainment of final knowledge occurs through gradual training, gradual action, and gradual practice. And how, bhikkhus, does the attainment of final knowledge occur through gradual training, gradual action, and gradual practice? Here, bhikkhus, when faith has arisen, one approaches. Approaching, one pays respect. Paying respect, one lends an ear. With ear lent, one hears the Dhamma. Having heard, one retains the Dhamma. One investigates the meaning of the teachings that have been retained. For one who investigates the meaning, the teachings are approved of after reflection. With the approval of the teachings after reflection, zeal is born. When zeal has arisen, one strives. Having striven, one weighs. Having weighed, one exerts. Being one whose self is directed, one both realizes the supreme truth with the body and sees it by penetrating it with wisdom. But, bhikkhus, that faith would not have been; that approaching would not have been; that paying respect would not have been; that lending of the ear would not have been; that hearing of the Dhamma would not have been; that retaining of the Dhamma would not have been; that investigation of the meaning would not have been; that approval of the teachings after reflection would not have been; that zeal would not have been; that striving would not have been; that weighing would not have been; that exertion would not have been. You have practiced perversely, bhikkhus; you have practiced wrongly, bhikkhus. How far have these worthless men strayed from this Dhamma and Discipline!

184. “Atthi[V 2.0156], bhikkhave, catuppadaṃ veyyākaraṇaṃ yassuddiṭṭhassa viññū puriso nacirasseva paññāyatthaṃ ājāneyya. Uddisissāmi vo uddiṭṭhassāpi (ka.), bhikkhave, ājānissatha me ta”nti? “Ke ca mayaṃ, bhante, ke ca dhammassa aññātāro”ti? Yopi so, bhikkhave, satthā āmisagaru āmisadāyādo āmisehi saṃsaṭṭho viharati tassa pāyaṃ evarūpī paṇopaṇaviyā na upeti – ‘evañca no assa atha naṃ kareyyāma, na ca no evamassa na naṃ kareyyāmā’ti, kiṃ pana, bhikkhave, yaṃ tathāgato sabbaso āmisehi visaṃsaṭṭho viharati. Saddhassa, bhikkhave, sāvakassa satthusāsane pariyogāhiya pariyogāya (sī. pī. ka.), pariyogayha (syā. kaṃ.) vattato ayamanudhammo hoti – ‘satthā bhagavā, sāvakohamasmi; jānāti bhagavā, nāhaṃ jānāmī’ti. Saddhassa, bhikkhave, sāvakassa satthusāsane pariyogāhiya vattato ruḷhanīyaṃ rumhaniyaṃ (sī. pī.) satthusāsanaṃ hoti ojavantaṃ. Saddhassa, bhikkhave, sāvakassa satthusāsane pariyogāhiya [P 1.0481] vattato ayamanudhammo hoti – ‘kāmaṃ taco ca nhāru ca aṭṭhi ca avasissatu, sarīre upasussatu upasussatu sarīre (sī.), sarīre avasussatu (ka.) maṃsalohitaṃ, yaṃ [T 2.0235] taṃ purisathāmena purisavīriyena purisaparakkamena pattabbaṃ na taṃ apāpuṇitvā vīriyassa saṇṭhānaṃ santhānaṃ (sī. syā. pī.) bhavissatī’ti. Saddhassa, bhikkhave, sāvakassa satthusāsane pariyogāhiya vattato dvinnaṃ phalānaṃ aññataraṃ phalaṃ pāṭikaṅkhaṃ – diṭṭheva dhamme aññā, sati vā upādisese anāgāmitā”ti.

184. Bhikkhus, there is a four-part exposition, the meaning of which an intelligent person, when it is pointed out, would understand with wisdom before long. I will point it out to you, bhikkhus. Will you understand it from me?” “But who are we, venerable sir, and who are the knowers of the Dhamma?” “Bhikkhus, even for a teacher who is intent on material gain, a successor to material gain, who dwells entangled with material things, this kind of bargaining does not occur: ‘If it were thus for us, we would do it; and if it were not thus for us, we would not do it.’ How much less so, bhikkhus, for the Tathāgata, who dwells completely unentangled with material things. For a faithful disciple, bhikkhus, who lives committed to the Teacher’s instruction, this is the practice in accordance with the Dhamma: ‘The Blessed One is the Teacher, I am a disciple; the Blessed One knows, I do not know.’ For a faithful disciple, bhikkhus, who lives committed to the Teacher’s instruction, the Teacher’s instruction becomes fruitful and nourishing.
