For a faithful disciple, bhikkhus, who lives committed to the Teacher’s instruction, this is the practice in accordance with the Dhamma: ‘Willingly, let only skin, sinews, and bones remain, and let the flesh and blood in my body dry up; but there will be no stopping of energy until I have attained what can be attained by human strength, human energy, and human striving.’ For a faithful disciple, bhikkhus, who lives committed to the Teacher’s instruction, one of two fruits is to be expected: either final knowledge in this very life or, if there is a remnant of clinging, the state of a non-returner.”

Idamavoca [M 2.0147] bhagavā. Attamanā te bhikkhū bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandunti.

The Blessed One said this. Delighted, those bhikkhus rejoiced in the Blessed One’s words.

Kīṭāgirisuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ dasamaṃ.

The Kīṭāgiri Sutta, the tenth, is finished.

Bhikkhuvaggo niṭṭhito dutiyo.

The Chapter on Bhikkhus, the second, is finished.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary verse for this chapter:

Kuñjara-rāhula-sassataloko, mālukyaputto ca bhaddāli-nāmo;

Khudda-dijātha-sahampatiyācaṃ, nāḷaka-raññikiṭāgirināmo.

“The Elephant, Rāhula, the Eternal World, Mālukyaputta and the one named Bhaddāli; The Small Bird, then Sahampati’s Request, Nāḷaka, the King, and the one named Kīṭāgiri.”

3. Paribbājakavaggo

3. The Chapter on Wanderers

1. Tevijjavacchasuttaṃ

1. The Discourse to Vacchagotta on the Threefold Knowledge

185. Evaṃ [T 2.0236][M 2.0148][V 2.0157] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā vesāliyaṃ viharati mahāvane kūṭāgārasālāyaṃ. Tena kho pana samayena vacchagotto paribbājako ekapuṇḍarīke paribbājakārāme paṭivasati. Atha kho bhagavā pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya vesāliṃ piṇḍāya pāvisi. Atha kho bhagavato etadahosi – “atippago kho tāva vesāliyaṃ piṇḍāya carituṃ; yaṃnūnāhaṃ yena ekapuṇḍarīko paribbājakārāmo yena vacchagotto paribbājako tenupasaṅkameyya”nti. Atha kho bhagavā yena ekapuṇḍarīko paribbājakārāmo yena vacchagotto paribbājako tenupasaṅkami. Addasā kho vacchagotto paribbājako bhagavantaṃ dūratova āgacchantaṃ. Disvāna bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “etu kho, bhante, bhagavā. Svāgataṃ sāgataṃ (sī. pī.), bhante, bhagavato. Cirassaṃ kho, bhante, bhagavā imaṃ pariyāyamakāsi yadidaṃ idhāgamanāya. Nisīdatu, bhante, bhagavā idamāsanaṃ paññatta”nti. Nisīdi bhagavā paññatte āsane. Vacchagottopi kho paribbājako aññataraṃ [P 1.0482] nīcaṃ āsanaṃ gahetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ [T 2.0237] nisinno kho vacchagotto paribbājako bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “sutaṃ metaṃ, bhante – ‘samaṇo gotamo sabbaññū sabbadassāvī, aparise+saṃ ñāṇadassanaṃ paṭijānāti, carato ca me tiṭṭhato ca suttassa ca jāgarassa ca satataṃ samitaṃ ñāṇadassanaṃ paccupaṭṭhita’nti. Ye te, bhante, evamāhaṃsu – ‘samaṇo gotamo sabbaññū sabbadassāvī, aparisesaṃ ñāṇadassanaṃ paṭijānāti, carato ca me tiṭṭhato ca suttassa ca jāgarassa ca satataṃ samitaṃ ñāṇadassanaṃ paccupaṭṭhita’nti, kacci te, bhante, bhagavato vuttavādino, na ca bhagavantaṃ abhūtena abbhācikkhanti, dhammassa cānudhammaṃ byākaronti, na ca koci sahadhammiko vādānuvādo gārayhaṃ [V 2.0158] ṭhānaṃ āgacchatī”ti? “Ye te, vaccha, evamāhaṃsu – ‘samaṇo gotamo sabbaññū sabbadassāvī, aparisesaṃ ñāṇadassanaṃ paṭijānāti, carato ca me tiṭṭhato ca suttassa ca jāgarassa ca satataṃ samitaṃ ñāṇadassanaṃ paccupaṭṭhita’nti, na me te vuttavādino, abbhācikkhanti ca pana maṃ asatā abhūtenā”ti.

185. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Vesālī, in the Great Wood, in the Hall with the Peaked Roof. Now at that time, the wanderer Vacchagotta was residing in the Single White Mango Tree Wanderers’ Park. Then the Blessed One, having dressed in the morning, took his bowl and robe and entered Vesālī for alms. Then it occurred to the Blessed One: 'It is still too early to wander for alms in Vesālī. What if I were to go to the Single White Mango Tree Wanderers’ Park, to where the wanderer Vacchagotta is?' Then the Blessed One went to the Single White Mango Tree Wanderers’ Park. The wanderer Vacchagotta saw the Blessed One coming from afar. Seeing him, he said to the Blessed One: 'Come, venerable sir, the Blessed One is welcome. It has been a long time, venerable sir, since the Blessed One took the occasion to come here. Let the Blessed One be seated; this seat is prepared.' The Blessed One sat down on the prepared seat. The wanderer Vacchagotta also took a lower seat and sat to one side. Sitting to one side, the wanderer Vacchagotta said to the Blessed One: 'Venerable sir, I have heard this: “The ascetic Gotama is all-knowing, all-seeing; he claims complete knowledge and vision without remainder, such that whether he is walking, standing, sleeping, or awake, knowledge and vision are constantly and uninterruptedly present to him.” Venerable sir, as for those who say this, are they speaking in accordance with the Blessed One’s words, not misrepresenting the Blessed One with what is untrue, explaining in accordance with the Dhamma, so that no fellow Dhamma-farer would have grounds for criticism?' 'Vaccha, those who say: “The ascetic Gotama is all-knowing, all-seeing; he claims complete knowledge and vision without remainder, such that whether he is walking, standing, sleeping, or awake, knowledge and vision are constantly and uninterruptedly present to him”—they do not speak in accordance with my words; rather, they misrepresent me with what is false and untrue.'

186. “Kathaṃ [M 2.0149] byākaramānā pana mayaṃ, bhante, vuttavādino ceva bhagavato assāma, na ca bhagavantaṃ abhūtena abbhācikkheyyāma, dhammassa cānudhammaṃ byākareyyāma, na ca koci sahadhammiko vādānuvādo gārayhaṃ ṭhānaṃ āgaccheyyā”ti?

186. But how then, venerable sir, should we speak so that we would be speaking in accordance with the Blessed One's words, not misrepresenting the Blessed One with what is untrue, explaining in accordance with the Dhamma, so that no fellow Dhamma-farer would have grounds for criticism?

“‘Tevijjo samaṇo gotamo’ti kho, vaccha, byākaramāno vuttavādī ceva me assa, na ca maṃ [T 2.0238] abhūtena abbhācikkheyya, dhammassa cānudhammaṃ byākareyya, na ca koci sahadhammiko vādānuvādo gārayhaṃ ṭhānaṃ āgaccheyya. Ahañhi, vaccha, yāvadeva ākaṅkhāmi anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussarāmi, seyyathidaṃ – ekampi jātiṃ dvepi jātiyo…pe… iti sākāraṃ sauddesaṃ anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussarāmi. Ahañhi, vaccha, yāvadeva ākaṅkhāmi dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena satte passāmi cavamāne upapajjamāne hīne paṇīte suvaṇṇe dubbaṇṇe sugate duggate…pe… yathākammūpage satte pajānāmi. Ahañhi, vaccha, āsavānaṃ khayā anāsavaṃ cetovimuttiṃ paññāvimuttiṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharāmi.

'The ascetic Gotama possesses the threefold knowledge.' By declaring this, Vaccha, one would be speaking in accordance with my words, not misrepresenting me with what is untrue, explaining in accordance with the Dhamma, so that no fellow Dhamma-farer would have grounds for criticism. For I, Vaccha, as far as I wish, recollect my manifold past lives—that is, one birth, two births... and so on—with their aspects and details, I recollect my manifold past lives. For I, Vaccha, as far as I wish, with the divine eye, purified and surpassing the human, see beings passing away and being reborn—inferior and superior, beautiful and ugly, fortunate and unfortunate... and I understand beings faring on according to their kamma. For I, Vaccha, through the destruction of the taints, in this very life have realized for myself with direct knowledge the taintless liberation of mind, liberation by wisdom, and I dwell having attained it.

“‘Tevijjo samaṇo gotamo’ti [P 1.0483] kho, vaccha, byākaramāno vuttavādī ceva me assa, na ca maṃ abhūtena abbhācikkheyya, dhammassa cānudhammaṃ byākareyya, na ca koci sahadhammiko vādānuvādo gārayhaṃ ṭhānaṃ āgaccheyyā”ti.

'The ascetic Gotama possesses the threefold knowledge.' By declaring this, Vaccha, one would be speaking in accordance with my words, not misrepresenting me with what is untrue, explaining in accordance with the Dhamma, so that no fellow Dhamma-farer would have grounds for criticism.

Evaṃ vutte, vacchagotto paribbājako bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “atthi nu kho, bho gotama, koci gihī gihisaṃyojanaṃ appahāya kāyassa bhedā dukkhassantakaro”ti? “Natthi kho, vaccha, koci gihī gihisaṃyojanaṃ appahāya kāyassa bhedā dukkhassantakaro”ti.

When this was said, the wanderer Vacchagotta said to the Blessed One: 'Is there, Master Gotama, any householder who, without abandoning the householder's fetters, makes an end of suffering at the body's breakup?' 'There is not, Vaccha, any householder who, without abandoning the householder's fetters, makes an end of suffering at the body's breakup.'

“Atthi [V 2.0159] pana, bho gotama, koci gihī gihisaṃyojanaṃ appahāya kāyassa bhedā saggūpago”ti? “Na kho, vaccha, ekaṃyeva sataṃ na dve satāni na [T 2.0239] tīṇi satāni na cattāri satāni na pañca satāni, atha kho bhiyyova ye gihī gihisaṃyojanaṃ appahāya kāyassa bhedā saggūpagā”ti “atthi kho vaccha koci gihī gihisaṃyojanaṃ appahāya kāyassa bhedā saggūpagoti”. (ka.).

'But is there, Master Gotama, any householder who, without abandoning the householder's fetters, is reborn in heaven at the body's breakup?' 'Not just one hundred, Vaccha, not two hundred, not three hundred, not four hundred, not five hundred, but far more are the householders who, without abandoning the householder's fetters, are reborn in heaven at the body's breakup.'

“Atthi [M 2.0150] nu kho, bho gotama, koci ājīvako ājīviko (ka.) kāyassa bhedā dukkhassantakaro”ti? “Natthi kho, vaccha, koci ājīvako kāyassa bhedā dukkhassantakaro”ti.

'Is there, Master Gotama, any Ājīvaka who makes an end of suffering at the body's breakup?' 'No, Vaccha, there is no Ājīvaka who makes an end of suffering at the body's breakup.'

“Atthi pana, bho gotama, koci ājīvako kāyassa bhedā saggūpago”ti? “Ito kho so, vaccha, ekanavuto kappo ito ko vaccha ekanavute kappe (ka.) yamahaṃ anussarāmi, nābhijānāmi kañci ājīvakaṃ saggūpagaṃ aññatra ekena; sopāsi kammavādī kiriyavādī”ti. “Evaṃ sante, bho gotama, suññaṃ aduṃ titthāyatanaṃ antamaso saggūpagenapī”ti? “Evaṃ, vaccha, suññaṃ aduṃ titthāyatanaṃ antamaso saggūpagenapī”ti.

“Master Gotama, is there any Ājīvaka who, upon the breakup of the body, has gone to a heavenly realm?” “Vaccha, in the ninety-one eons that I recollect from this present one, I do not know of any Ājīvaka who has gone to a heavenly realm, except for one. And he, too, was one who affirmed kamma and action.” “That being so, Master Gotama, is this sectarian doctrine void even of one who has gone to a heavenly realm?” “Even so, Vaccha, this sectarian doctrine is void even of one who has gone to a heavenly realm.”

Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamano vacchagotto paribbājako bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandīti.

The Blessed One said this. Pleased, the wanderer Vacchagotta delighted in the Blessed One's words.

Tevijjavacchasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ paṭhamaṃ.

The first Tevijjavacchagotta Sutta is concluded.

2. Aggivacchasuttaṃ

2. The Aggivacchagotta Sutta

187. Evaṃ [T 2.0240][V 2.0160] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Atha kho vacchagotto paribbājako yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā [P 1.0484] bhagavatā saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho vacchagotto paribbājako bhagavantaṃ etadavoca –

187. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling in Sāvatthī, at Jeta's Grove, in Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery. Then the wanderer Vacchagotta approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he exchanged greetings with the Blessed One. Having concluded a friendly and memorable conversation, he sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the wanderer Vacchagotta said this to the Blessed One:

“Kiṃ nu kho, bho gotama, ‘sassato loko, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’nti – evaṃdiṭṭhi evaṃdiṭṭhī (sī. syā. kaṃ. ka.) bhavaṃ gotamo”ti? “Na kho ahaṃ, vaccha, evaṃdiṭṭhi – ‘sassato loko, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’”nti.

“Master Gotama, do you hold the view: ‘The world is eternal; only this is true, anything else is futile’?” “No, Vaccha, I do not hold the view: ‘The world is eternal; only this is true, anything else is futile’.”

“Kiṃ pana, bho gotama, ‘asassato loko, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’nti – evaṃdiṭṭhi bhavaṃ gotamo”ti? “Na kho ahaṃ, vaccha, evaṃdiṭṭhi – ‘asassato loko, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’”nti.

“Then, Master Gotama, do you hold the view: ‘The world is not eternal; only this is true, anything else is futile’?” “No, Vaccha, I do not hold the view: ‘The world is not eternal; only this is true, anything else is futile’.”

“Kiṃ [M 2.0151] nu kho, bho gotama, ‘antavā loko, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’nti – evaṃdiṭṭhi bhavaṃ gotamo”ti? “Na kho ahaṃ, vaccha, evaṃdiṭṭhi – ‘antavā loko, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’”nti.

“Master Gotama, do you hold the view: ‘The world is finite; only this is true, anything else is futile’?” “No, Vaccha, I do not hold the view: ‘The world is finite; only this is true, anything else is futile’.”

“Kiṃ pana, bho gotama, ‘anantavā loko, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’nti – evaṃdiṭṭhi bhavaṃ gotamo”ti? “Na kho ahaṃ, vaccha, evaṃdiṭṭhi – ‘anantavā loko, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’”nti.

“Then, Master Gotama, do you hold the view: ‘The world is infinite; only this is true, anything else is futile’?” “No, Vaccha, I do not hold the view: ‘The world is infinite; only this is true, anything else is futile’.”

“Kiṃ nu kho, bho gotama, ‘taṃ jīvaṃ taṃ sarīraṃ, idameva [T 2.0241] saccaṃ moghamañña’nti – evaṃdiṭṭhi [V 2.0161] bhavaṃ gotamo”ti? “Na kho ahaṃ, vaccha, evaṃdiṭṭhi – ‘taṃ jīvaṃ taṃ sarīraṃ, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’”nti.

“Master Gotama, do you hold the view: ‘The life principle is the same as the body; only this is true, anything else is futile’?” “No, Vaccha, I do not hold the view: ‘The life principle is the same as the body; only this is true, anything else is futile’.”

“Kiṃ pana, bho gotama, ‘aññaṃ jīvaṃ aññaṃ sarīraṃ, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’nti – evaṃdiṭṭhi bhavaṃ gotamo”ti? “Na kho ahaṃ, vaccha, evaṃdiṭṭhi – ‘aññaṃ jīvaṃ aññaṃ sarīraṃ, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’”nti.

“Then, Master Gotama, do you hold the view: ‘The life principle is one thing and the body is another; only this is true, anything else is futile’?” “No, Vaccha, I do not hold the view: ‘The life principle is one thing and the body is another; only this is true, anything else is futile’.”

“Kiṃ nu kho, bho gotama, ‘hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’nti – evaṃdiṭṭhi bhavaṃ gotamo”ti? “Na kho ahaṃ, vaccha, evaṃdiṭṭhi – ‘hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’”nti.

“Master Gotama, do you hold the view: ‘A being exists after death; only this is true, anything else is futile’?” “No, Vaccha, I do not hold the view: ‘A being exists after death; only this is true, anything else is futile’.”

“Kiṃ pana, bho gotama, ‘na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’nti – evaṃdiṭṭhi bhavaṃ gotamo”ti? “Na kho ahaṃ, vaccha, evaṃdiṭṭhi – ‘na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’”nti.

“Then, Master Gotama, do you hold the view: ‘A being does not exist after death; only this is true, anything else is futile’?” “No, Vaccha, I do not hold the view: ‘A being does not exist after death; only this is true, anything else is futile’.”

“Kiṃ nu kho, bho gotama, ‘hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’nti – evaṃdiṭṭhi bhavaṃ gotamo”ti[P 1.0485]? “Na kho ahaṃ, vaccha, evaṃdiṭṭhi – ‘hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’”nti.

“Master Gotama, do you hold the view: ‘A being both exists and does not exist after death; only this is true, anything else is futile’?” “No, Vaccha, I do not hold the view: ‘A being both exists and does not exist after death; only this is true, anything else is futile’.”

“Kiṃ pana, bho gotama, ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’nti – evaṃdiṭṭhi bhavaṃ gotamo”ti? “Na kho ahaṃ, vaccha, evaṃdiṭṭhi – ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’”nti.

“Then, Master Gotama, do you hold the view: ‘A being neither exists nor does not exist after death; only this is true, anything else is futile’?” “No, Vaccha, I do not hold the view: ‘A being neither exists nor does not exist after death; only this is true, anything else is futile’.”

188. “‘Kiṃ [T 2.0242] nu kho, bho gotama, sassato loko, idameva saccaṃ moghamaññanti – evaṃdiṭṭhi bhavaṃ gotamo’ti iti puṭṭho samāno ‘na [M 2.0152] kho ahaṃ, vaccha, evaṃdiṭṭhi – sassato loko, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’nti vadesi moghamaññantīti vadesi (sī.), moghamaññanti iti vadesi (?). ‘Kiṃ pana, bho gotama, asassato loko, idameva saccaṃ moghamaññanti – evaṃdiṭṭhi bhavaṃ gotamo’ti iti puṭṭho samāno ‘na kho ahaṃ, vaccha[V 2.0162], evaṃdiṭṭhi – asassato loko, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’nti vadesi. ‘Kiṃ nu kho, bho gotama, antavā loko, idameva saccaṃ moghamaññanti – evaṃdiṭṭhi bhavaṃ gotamo’ti iti puṭṭho samāno ‘na kho ahaṃ, vaccha, evaṃdiṭṭhi – antavā loko, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’nti vadesi. ‘Kiṃ pana, bho gotama, anantavā loko, idameva saccaṃ moghamaññanti – evaṃdiṭṭhi bhavaṃ gotamo’ti iti puṭṭho samāno ‘na kho ahaṃ, vaccha, evaṃdiṭṭhi – anantavā loko, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’nti vadesi. ‘Kiṃ nu kho, bho gotama, taṃ jīvaṃ taṃ sarīraṃ, idameva saccaṃ moghamaññanti – evaṃdiṭṭhi bhavaṃ gotamo’ti iti puṭṭho samāno ‘na kho ahaṃ, vaccha, evaṃdiṭṭhi – taṃ jīvaṃ taṃ sarīraṃ, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’nti vadesi. ‘Kiṃ pana, bho gotama, aññaṃ jīvaṃ aññaṃ sarīraṃ, idameva saccaṃ moghamaññanti – evaṃdiṭṭhi bhavaṃ gotamo’ti iti puṭṭho samāno ‘na kho ahaṃ, vaccha, evaṃdiṭṭhi – aññaṃ jīvaṃ aññaṃ sarīraṃ, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’nti vadesi. ‘Kiṃ nu kho, bho gotama, hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā, idameva saccaṃ moghamaññanti – evaṃdiṭṭhi bhavaṃ gotamo’ti iti puṭṭho samāno ‘na kho ahaṃ, vaccha, evaṃdiṭṭhi – hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’nti vadesi.

188. “When asked, ‘Venerable Gotama, do you hold the view: “The world is eternal; this alone is the truth, and anything else is worthless”?’ you reply, ‘Indeed, Vaccha, I do not hold the view: “The world is eternal; this alone is the truth, and anything else is worthless”.’ When asked, ‘Then, Venerable Gotama, do you hold the view: “The world is not eternal; this alone is the truth, and anything else is worthless”?’ you reply, ‘Indeed, Vaccha, I do not hold the view: “The world is not eternal; this alone is the truth, and anything else is worthless”.’ When asked, ‘Venerable Gotama, do you hold the view: “The world is finite; this alone is the truth, and anything else is worthless”?’ you reply, ‘Indeed, Vaccha, I do not hold the view: “The world is finite; this alone is the truth, and anything else is worthless”.’ When asked, ‘Then, Venerable Gotama, do you hold the view: “The world is infinite; this alone is the truth, and anything else is worthless”?’ you reply, ‘Indeed, Vaccha, I do not hold the view: “The world is infinite; this alone is the truth, and anything else is worthless”.’ When asked, ‘Venerable Gotama, do you hold the view: “The life-principle is the same as the body; this alone is the truth, and anything else is worthless”?’ you reply, ‘Indeed, Vaccha, I do not hold the view: “The life-principle is the same as the body; this alone is the truth, and anything else is worthless”.’ When asked, ‘Then, Venerable Gotama, do you hold the view: “The life-principle is one thing and the body another; this alone is the truth, and anything else is worthless”?’ you reply, ‘Indeed, Vaccha, I do not hold the view: “The life-principle is one thing and the body another; this alone is the truth, and anything else is worthless”.’ When asked, ‘Venerable Gotama, do you hold the view: “The Tathāgata exists after death; this alone is the truth, and anything else is worthless”?’ you reply, ‘Indeed, Vaccha, I do not hold the view: “The Tathāgata exists after death; this alone is the truth, and anything else is worthless”.’

“‘Kiṃ pana, bho gotama, na hoti tathāgato paraṃ [T 2.0243] maraṇā, idameva saccaṃ moghamaññanti – evaṃdiṭṭhi bhavaṃ gotamo’ti iti puṭṭho samāno ‘na kho ahaṃ, vaccha, evaṃdiṭṭhi – na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’nti vadesi. ‘Kiṃ nu kho, bho gotama, hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā, idameva saccaṃ moghamaññanti – evaṃdiṭṭhi bhavaṃ gotamo’ti iti puṭṭho samāno ‘na kho ahaṃ, vaccha, evaṃdiṭṭhi – hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’nti vadesi. ‘Kiṃ pana, bho gotama, neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā, idameva saccaṃ moghamaññanti – evaṃdiṭṭhi bhavaṃ gotamo’ti iti puṭṭho samāno ‘na kho [M 2.0153] ahaṃ, vaccha, evaṃdiṭṭhi – neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’nti vadesi.

“When asked, ‘Then, Venerable Gotama, do you hold the view: “The Tathāgata does not exist after death; this alone is the truth, and anything else is worthless”?’ you reply, ‘Indeed, Vaccha, I do not hold the view: “The Tathāgata does not exist after death; this alone is the truth, and anything else is worthless”.’ When asked, ‘Venerable Gotama, do you hold the view: “The Tathāgata both exists and does not exist after death; this alone is the truth, and anything else is worthless”?’ you reply, ‘Indeed, Vaccha, I do not hold the view: “The Tathāgata both exists and does not exist after death; this alone is the truth, and anything else is worthless”.’ When asked, ‘Then, Venerable Gotama, do you hold the view: “The Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death; this alone is the truth, and anything else is worthless”?’ you reply, ‘Indeed, Vaccha, I do not hold the view: “The Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death; this alone is the truth, and anything else is worthless”.’

“Kiṃ pana bho gotamo ādīnavaṃ sampassamāno evaṃ imāni sabbaso diṭṭhigatāni anupagato”ti?

“Venerable Gotama, seeing what drawback do you thus not resort to any of these speculative views at all?”

189. “‘Sassato loko’ti kho, vaccha, diṭṭhigatametaṃ diṭṭhigahanaṃ diṭṭhikantāro diṭṭhikantāraṃ (sī. pī.) diṭṭhivisūkaṃ diṭṭhivipphanditaṃ diṭṭhisaṃyojanaṃ sadukkhaṃ savighātaṃ saupāyāsaṃ sapariḷāhaṃ, na nibbidāya na [V 2.0163] virāgāya na nirodhāya na upasamāya na abhiññāya na sambodhāya na nibbānāya saṃvattati[T 2.0244]. ‘Asassato loko’ti kho, vaccha…pe… ‘antavā loko’ti kho, vaccha…pe… ‘anantavā loko’ti kho, vaccha…pe… ‘taṃ jīvaṃ taṃ sarīra’nti kho, vaccha…pe… ‘aññaṃ jīvaṃ aññaṃ sarīra’nti kho, vaccha…pe… ‘hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti kho, vaccha [P 1.0486] …pe… ‘na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti kho, vaccha…pe… ‘hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti kho, vaccha…pe… ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti kho, vaccha, diṭṭhigatametaṃ diṭṭhigahanaṃ diṭṭhikantāro diṭṭhivisūkaṃ diṭṭhivipphanditaṃ diṭṭhisaṃyojanaṃ sadukkhaṃ savighātaṃ saupāyāsaṃ sapariḷāhaṃ, na nibbidāya na virāgāya na nirodhāya na upasamāya na abhiññāya na sambodhāya na nibbānāya saṃvattati. Imaṃ kho ahaṃ, vaccha, ādīnavaṃ sampassamāno evaṃ imāni sabbaso diṭṭhigatāni anupagato”ti.

189. “Vaccha, the speculative view, ‘The world is eternal,’ is a thicket of views, a wilderness of views, a contortion of views, a vacillation of views, a fetter of views. It is accompanied by suffering, vexation, despair, and fever. It does not lead to disenchantment, to dispassion, to cessation, to peace, to direct knowledge, to enlightenment, to Nibbāna. The speculative view, ‘The world is not eternal,’ Vaccha… The speculative view, ‘The world is finite,’ Vaccha… The speculative view, ‘The world is infinite,’ Vaccha… The speculative view, ‘The life-principle is the same as the body,’ Vaccha… The speculative view, ‘The life-principle is one thing and the body another,’ Vaccha… The speculative view, ‘The Tathāgata exists after death,’ Vaccha… The speculative view, ‘The Tathāgata does not exist after death,’ Vaccha… The speculative view, ‘The Tathāgata both exists and does not exist after death,’ Vaccha… The speculative view, ‘The Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death,’ Vaccha, is a thicket of views, a wilderness of views, a contortion of views, a vacillation of views, a fetter of views. It is accompanied by suffering, vexation, despair, and fever. It does not lead to disenchantment, to dispassion, to cessation, to peace, to direct knowledge, to enlightenment, to Nibbāna. Seeing this drawback, Vaccha, I thus do not resort to any of these speculative views at all.”

“Atthi pana bhoto gotamassa kiñci diṭṭhigata”nti? “Diṭṭhigatanti kho, vaccha, apanītametaṃ tathāgatassa. Diṭṭhañhetaṃ, vaccha, tathāgatena – ‘iti rūpaṃ, iti rūpassa samudayo, iti rūpassa atthaṅgamo; iti vedanā, iti vedanāya samudayo, iti vedanāya atthaṅgamo; iti saññā, iti saññāya samudayo, iti saññāya atthaṅgamo; iti saṅkhārā, iti saṅkhārānaṃ samudayo, iti saṅkhārānaṃ atthaṅgamo; iti viññāṇaṃ, iti viññāṇassa samudayo, iti viññāṇassa atthaṅgamo’ti. Tasmā tathāgato sabbamaññitānaṃ sabbamathitānaṃ sabbaahaṃkāramamaṃkāramānānusayānaṃ khayā virāgā [T 2.0245] nirodhā cāgā paṭinissaggā anupādā vimuttoti vadāmī”ti.

“Does the Venerable Gotama have any speculative view?” “Vaccha, as for ‘a speculative view,’ that is something the Tathāgata has put away. This, Vaccha, has been seen by the Tathāgata: ‘Such is form, such is the arising of form, such is the cessation of form; such is feeling, such is the arising of feeling, such is the cessation of feeling; such is perception, such is the arising of perception, such is the cessation of perception; such are formations, such is the arising of formations, such is the cessation of formations; such is consciousness, such is the arising of consciousness, such is the cessation of consciousness.’ Therefore, I say that through the destruction, fading away, cessation, giving up, and relinquishment of all conceivings, all agitations, and all I-making, mine-making, and underlying tendencies to conceit, the Tathāgata is liberated without clinging.”

190. “Evaṃ [M 2.0154] vimuttacitto pana, bho gotama, bhikkhu kuhiṃ upapajjatī”ti? “Upapajjatīti kho, vaccha, na upeti”. “Tena hi, bho gotama, na upapajjatī”ti? “Na upapajjatīti kho, vaccha, na upeti”. “Tena hi, bho gotama, upapajjati ca na ca upapajjatī”ti? “Upapajjati ca na ca upapajjatīti kho, vaccha, na upeti”. “Tena hi, bho gotama, neva upapajjati na na upapajjatī”ti? “Neva upapajjati na na upapajjatīti kho, vaccha, na upeti”.

190. “Master Gotama, where is a bhikkhu whose mind is thus liberated reborn?” “‘Is reborn,’ Vaccha, does not apply.” “Then, Master Gotama, is he not reborn?” “‘Is not reborn,’ Vaccha, does not apply.” “Then, Master Gotama, is he both reborn and not reborn?” “‘Is both reborn and not reborn,’ Vaccha, does not apply.” “Then, Master Gotama, is he neither reborn nor not reborn?” “‘Is neither reborn nor not reborn,’ Vaccha, does not apply.”

“‘Evaṃ [V 2.0164] vimuttacitto pana, bho gotama, bhikkhu kuhiṃ upapajjatī’ti iti puṭṭho samāno ‘upapajjatīti kho, vaccha, na upetī’ti vadesi. ‘Tena hi, bho gotama, na upapajjatī’ti iti puṭṭho samāno ‘na upapajjatīti kho, vaccha, na upetī’ti vadesi. ‘Tena hi, bho gotama, upapajjati ca na ca upapajjatī’ti iti puṭṭho samāno ‘upapajjati ca na ca upapajjatīti kho, vaccha, na upetī’ti vadesi. ‘Tena hi, bho gotama, neva upapajjati na na upapajjatī’ti iti puṭṭho samāno ‘neva upapajjati na na [P 1.0487] upapajjatīti kho, vaccha, na upetī’ti vadesi. Etthāhaṃ, bho gotama, aññāṇamāpādiṃ, ettha sammohamāpādiṃ. Yāpi me esā bhoto gotamassa purimena kathāsallāpena ahu pasādamattā [T 2.0246] sāpi me etarahi antarahitā”ti. “Alañhi te, vaccha, aññāṇāya, alaṃ sammohāya. Gambhīro hāyaṃ, vaccha, dhammo duddaso duranubodho santo paṇīto atakkāvacaro nipuṇo paṇḍitavedanīyo. So tayā dujjāno aññadiṭṭhikena aññakhantikena aññarucikena aññatrayogena aññatrāyogena (dī. ni. 1.420) aññatrācariyakena” aññatthācariyakena (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.).

“‘Master Gotama, when a bhikkhu’s mind is thus liberated, where is he reborn?’ When asked this, you say, ‘Vaccha, “is reborn” does not apply.’ Asked, ‘Then, Master Gotama, is he not reborn?’ you say, ‘Vaccha, “is not reborn” does not apply.’ Asked, ‘Then, Master Gotama, is he both reborn and not reborn?’ you say, ‘Vaccha, “is both reborn and not reborn” does not apply.’ Asked, ‘Then, Master Gotama, is he neither reborn nor not reborn?’ you say, ‘Vaccha, “is neither reborn nor not reborn” does not apply.’ At this, Master Gotama, I have fallen into ignorance; at this, I have fallen into confusion. And the measure of confidence I had from the venerable Gotama's previous conversation has now vanished.” “It is fitting, Vaccha, that you are ignorant; it is fitting that you are confused. For this Dhamma, Vaccha, is profound, hard to see, hard to understand, peaceful, sublime, beyond the scope of logic, subtle, to be experienced by the wise. It is hard for you to understand, as you have a different view, a different inclination, a different preference, a different practice, and a different teacher.”

191. “Tena hi, vaccha, taññevettha paṭipucchissāmi; yathā te khameyya tathā naṃ byākareyyāsi. Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, vaccha, sace te purato aggi jaleyya, jāneyyāsi tvaṃ – ‘ayaṃ me purato aggi jalatī’”ti? “Sace me, bho gotama, purato aggi jaleyya, jāneyyāhaṃ – ‘ayaṃ me purato aggi jalatī’”ti.

191. “In that case, Vaccha, I will question you in return on this very point. Answer as seems fitting to you. What do you think, Vaccha? If a fire were burning in front of you, would you know, ‘This fire is burning in front of me’?” “If a fire were burning in front of me, Master Gotama, I would know, ‘This fire is burning in front of me.’”

“Sace pana taṃ, vaccha, evaṃ puccheyya – ‘yo te ayaṃ purato aggi jalati ayaṃ aggi kiṃ paṭicca jalatī’ti, evaṃ puṭṭho tvaṃ, vaccha, kinti byākareyyāsī”ti? “Sace maṃ, bho gotama, evaṃ puccheyya – ‘yo te ayaṃ purato aggi jalati ayaṃ aggi kiṃ paṭicca jalatī’ti, evaṃ puṭṭho ahaṃ, bho gotama, evaṃ byākareyyaṃ [M 2.0155] – ‘yo me ayaṃ purato aggi jalati ayaṃ aggi tiṇakaṭṭhupādānaṃ paṭicca jalatī’”ti.

“But if, Vaccha, one were to ask you, ‘This fire burning in front of you—dependent on what does it burn?’—being asked thus, Vaccha, how would you answer?” “If, Master Gotama, I were asked, ‘This fire burning in front of you—dependent on what does it burn?’—being asked thus, I would answer, ‘This fire burning in front of me burns in dependence on fuel of grass and wood.’”

“Sace te, vaccha, purato so aggi nibbāyeyya, jāneyyāsi tvaṃ – ‘ayaṃ me purato aggi nibbuto’”ti? “Sace me, bho gotama, purato so aggi nibbāyeyya, jāneyyāhaṃ – ‘ayaṃ me purato aggi nibbuto’”ti.

“If, Vaccha, that fire in front of you were to be extinguished, would you know, ‘This fire in front of me is extinguished’?” “If, Master Gotama, that fire in front of me were to be extinguished, I would know, ‘This fire in front of me is extinguished.’”

“Sace [V 2.0165] pana taṃ, vaccha, evaṃ puccheyya – ‘yo te ayaṃ purato aggi nibbuto so aggi ito katamaṃ [T 2.0247] disaṃ gato – puratthimaṃ vā dakkhiṇaṃ vā pacchimaṃ vā uttaraṃ vā’ti, evaṃ puṭṭho tvaṃ, vaccha, kinti byākareyyāsī”ti? “Na upeti, bho gotama, yañhi so, bho gotama, aggi tiṇakaṭṭhupādānaṃ paṭicca ajali jalati (syā. kaṃ. ka.) tassa ca pariyādānā aññassa ca anupahārā anāhāro nibbuto tveva saṅkhyaṃ gacchatī”ti.

“But if, Vaccha, one were to ask you, ‘This fire in front of you that has been extinguished—to which direction has it gone from here: east, south, west, or north?’—being asked thus, Vaccha, how would you answer?” “That does not apply, Master Gotama. For that fire, Master Gotama, burned in dependence on the fuel of grass and wood. With the exhaustion of that fuel and the non-provision of other fuel, being without sustenance, it is reckoned as ‘extinguished.’”

192. “Evameva kho, vaccha, yena rūpena tathāgataṃ paññāpayamāno paññāpeyya taṃ rūpaṃ tathāgatassa pahīnaṃ ucchinnamūlaṃ tālāvatthukataṃ anabhāvaṃkataṃ āyatiṃ anuppādadhammaṃ. Rūpasaṅkhayavimutto rūpasaṅkhāvimutto (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) evaṃ vedanāsaṅkhayādīsupi kho, vaccha, tathāgato gambhīro appameyyo duppariyogāḷho – seyyathāpi mahāsamuddo. Upapajjatīti na upeti, na upapajjatīti na upeti, upapajjati [P 1.0488] ca na ca upapajjatīti na upeti, neva upapajjati na na upapajjatīti na upeti.

192. “In just the same way, Vaccha, the form by which one designating the Tathāgata might designate him, that form has been abandoned by the Tathāgata, cut off at the root, made like a palm-tree stump, brought to non-existence, and is subject to non-arising in the future. The Tathāgata, Vaccha, is liberated from the reckoning of form; he is profound, immeasurable, unfathomable, like the great ocean. ‘Is reborn’ does not apply; ‘is not reborn’ does not apply; ‘is both reborn and not reborn’ does not apply; ‘is neither reborn nor not reborn’ does not apply.

“Yāya vedanāya tathāgataṃ paññāpayamāno paññāpeyya sā vedanā tathāgatassa pahīnā ucchinnamūlā tālāvatthukatā anabhāvaṃkatā āyatiṃ anuppādadhammā. Vedanāsaṅkhayavimutto kho, vaccha, tathāgato gambhīro appameyyo duppariyogāḷho – seyyathāpi mahāsamuddo. Upapajjatīti na upeti, na upapajjatīti na upeti, upapajjati ca na ca upapajjatīti na upeti, neva upapajjati na na upapajjatīti na upeti.

“The feeling by which one designating the Tathāgata might designate him, that feeling has been abandoned by the Tathāgata, cut off at the root, made like a palm-tree stump, brought to non-existence, and is subject to non-arising in the future. The Tathāgata, Vaccha, is liberated from the reckoning of feeling; he is profound, immeasurable, unfathomable, like the great ocean. ‘Is reborn’ does not apply; ‘is not reborn’ does not apply; ‘is both reborn and not reborn’ does not apply; ‘is neither reborn nor not reborn’ does not apply.

“Yāya saññāya tathāgataṃ paññāpayamāno paññāpeyya sā saññā tathāgatassa pahīnā [T 2.0248] ucchinnamūlā tālāvatthukatā anabhāvaṃkatā āyatiṃ anuppādadhammā. Saññāsaṅkhayavimutto kho, vaccha, tathāgato gambhīro appameyyo duppariyogāḷho – seyyathāpi mahāsamuddo. Upapajjatīti [M 2.0156] na upeti, na upapajjatīti na upeti, upapajjati ca na ca upapajjatīti na upeti, neva upapajjati na na upapajjatīti na upeti.

“The perception by which one designating the Tathāgata might designate him, that perception has been abandoned by the Tathāgata, cut off at the root, made like a palm-tree stump, brought to non-existence, and is subject to non-arising in the future. The Tathāgata, Vaccha, is liberated from the reckoning of perception; he is profound, immeasurable, unfathomable, like the great ocean. ‘Is reborn’ does not apply; ‘is not reborn’ does not apply; ‘is both reborn and not reborn’ does not apply; ‘is neither reborn nor not reborn’ does not apply.

“Yehi saṅkhārehi tathāgataṃ paññāpayamāno paññāpeyya te saṅkhārā tathāgatassa pahīnā ucchinnamūlā tālāvatthukatā anabhāvaṃkatā āyatiṃ anuppādadhammā. Saṅkhārasaṅkhayavimutto kho, vaccha, tathāgato gambhīro appameyyo duppariyogāḷho – seyyathāpi mahāsamuddo. Upapajjatīti na upeti[V 2.0166], na upapajjatīti na upeti, upapajjati ca na ca upapajjatīti na upeti, neva upapajjati na na upapajjatīti na upeti.

Vaccha, those formations by which one designating the Tathāgata might designate him, those formations have been abandoned by the Tathāgata, their roots cut off, made like a palm-tree stump, brought to non-existence, and are of a nature not to arise again in the future. Vaccha, the Tathāgata, liberated through the exhaustion of formations, is deep, immeasurable, difficult to fathom, like the great ocean. 'He is reborn' does not apply; 'he is not reborn' does not apply; 'he is both reborn and not reborn' does not apply; 'he is neither reborn nor not reborn' does not apply.

“Yena viññāṇena tathāgataṃ paññāpayamāno paññāpeyya taṃ viññāṇaṃ tathāgatassa pahīnaṃ ucchinnamūlaṃ tālāvatthukataṃ anabhāvaṃkataṃ āyatiṃ anuppādadhammaṃ. Viññāṇasaṅkhayavimutto kho, vaccha, tathāgato gambhīro appameyyo duppariyogāḷho – seyyathāpi mahāsamuddo. Upapajjatīti na upeti, na upapajjatīti na upeti, upapajjati ca na ca upapajjatīti na upeti, neva upapajjati na na upapajjatīti na upeti”.

Vaccha, that consciousness by which one designating the Tathāgata might designate him, that consciousness has been abandoned by the Tathāgata, its root cut off, made like a palm-tree stump, brought to non-existence, and is of a nature not to arise again in the future. Vaccha, the Tathāgata, liberated through the exhaustion of consciousness, is deep, immeasurable, difficult to fathom, like the great ocean. 'He is reborn' does not apply; 'he is not reborn' does not apply; 'he is both reborn and not reborn' does not apply; 'he is neither reborn nor not reborn' does not apply.

Evaṃ vutte, vacchagotto paribbājako bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “seyyathāpi, bho gotama, gāmassa vā nigamassa vā avidūre [T 2.0249] mahāsālarukkho. Tassa aniccatā sākhāpalāsā palujjeyyuṃ sākhāpalāsaṃ palujjeyya, tacapapaṭikā palujjeyyuṃ, pheggū palujjeyyuṃ pheggu palujjeyya (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.); so aparena samayena apagatasākhāpalāso apagatatacapapaṭiko apagataphegguko suddho assa, sāre patiṭṭhito; evameva bhoto gotamassa pāvacanaṃ apagatasākhāpalāsaṃ apagatatacapapaṭikaṃ apagatapheggukaṃ suddhaṃ, sāre patiṭṭhitaṃ. Abhikkantaṃ, bho gotama…pe… [P 1.0489] upāsakaṃ maṃ bhavaṃ gotamo dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṃ saraṇaṃ gata”nti.

When this was said, the wanderer Vacchagotta said to the Blessed One: 'Venerable Gotama, it is as if, not far from a village or a town, there were a great sāl tree. Due to its impermanence, its branches and leaves would fall away, its bark and outer bark would fall away, and its sapwood would fall away. In time, devoid of branches and leaves, devoid of bark and outer bark, devoid of sapwood, it would be established in the pure heartwood. In the very same way, the teaching of the Venerable Gotama is devoid of branches and leaves, devoid of bark and outer bark, devoid of sapwood, and is established in the pure heartwood. It is excellent, Venerable Gotama… May the Venerable Gotama remember me as a lay disciple who has gone for refuge for life, from this day forward.'

Aggivacchasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ dutiyaṃ.

The Aggivaccha Sutta, the second, is concluded.

3. Mahāvacchasuttaṃ

3. The Mahāvaccha Sutta

193. Evaṃ [T 2.0250][V 2.0167] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe. Atha kho vacchagotto paribbājako yena bhagavā [M 2.0157] tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho vacchagotto paribbājako bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “dīgharattāhaṃ bhotā gotamena sahakathī. Sādhu me bhavaṃ gotamo saṃkhittena kusalākusalaṃ desetū”ti. “Saṃkhittenapi kho te ahaṃ, vaccha, kusalākusalaṃ deseyyaṃ, vitthārenapi kho te ahaṃ, vaccha, kusalākusalaṃ deseyyaṃ; api ca te ahaṃ, vaccha, saṃkhittena kusalākusalaṃ desessāmi. Taṃ suṇāhi, sādhukaṃ manasi karohi, bhāsissāmī”ti. “Evaṃ, bho”ti kho vacchagotto paribbājako bhagavato paccassosi. Bhagavā etadavoca –

193. Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrels' Feeding Place. Then the wanderer Vacchagotta approached the Blessed One and exchanged greetings with him. When they had concluded their greetings and cordial talk, he sat down to one side. Sitting to one side, the wanderer Vacchagotta said to the Blessed One: 'Venerable Gotama, for a long time I have been one who converses with you. It would be good if the Venerable Gotama would teach me briefly about the wholesome and the unwholesome.' 'Vaccha, I could teach you about the wholesome and the unwholesome briefly, and I could also teach you about the wholesome and the unwholesome in detail. However, Vaccha, I will teach you about the wholesome and the unwholesome briefly. Listen to that and apply your mind well; I will speak.' 'Yes, Venerable Sir,' the wanderer Vacchagotta replied to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said this:

194. “Lobho kho, vaccha, akusalaṃ, alobho kusalaṃ; doso kho, vaccha, akusalaṃ, adoso kusalaṃ; moho kho, vaccha, akusalaṃ, amoho kusalaṃ. Iti kho, vaccha, ime tayo dhammā akusalā, tayo dhammā kusalā.

194. Greed, Vaccha, is unwholesome; non-greed is wholesome. Aversion, Vaccha, is unwholesome; non-aversion is wholesome. Delusion, Vaccha, is unwholesome; non-delusion is wholesome. Thus, Vaccha, these three things are unwholesome, and these three things are wholesome.

“Pāṇātipāto kho, vaccha, akusalaṃ, pāṇātipātā veramaṇī kusalaṃ; adinnādānaṃ kho, vaccha, akusalaṃ, adinnādānā veramaṇī kusalaṃ; kāmesumicchācāro kho, vaccha, akusalaṃ, kāmesumicchācārā veramaṇī kusalaṃ; musāvādo [T 2.0251] kho, vaccha, akusalaṃ, musāvādā veramaṇī kusalaṃ; pisuṇā vācā kho, vaccha, akusalaṃ[P 1.0490], pisuṇāya vācāya veramaṇī kusalaṃ; pharusā vācā kho, vaccha, akusalaṃ, pharusāya vācāya veramaṇī kusalaṃ; samphappalāpo kho, vaccha, akusalaṃ, samphappalāpā veramaṇī kusalaṃ; abhijjhā kho, vaccha, akusalaṃ, anabhijjhā kusalaṃ; byāpādo kho, vaccha, akusalaṃ, abyāpādo kusalaṃ; micchādiṭṭhi kho, vaccha, akusalaṃ sammādiṭṭhi kusalaṃ. Iti kho, vaccha, ime dasa dhammā akusalā, dasa dhammā kusalā.

The taking of life, Vaccha, is unwholesome; abstinence from taking life is wholesome. Taking what is not given, Vaccha, is unwholesome; abstinence from taking what is not given is wholesome. Misconduct in sensual pleasures, Vaccha, is unwholesome; abstinence from misconduct in sensual pleasures is wholesome. False speech, Vaccha, is unwholesome; abstinence from false speech is wholesome. Divisive speech, Vaccha, is unwholesome; abstinence from divisive speech is wholesome. Harsh speech, Vaccha, is unwholesome; abstinence from harsh speech is wholesome. Frivolous speech, Vaccha, is unwholesome; abstinence from frivolous speech is wholesome. Covetousness, Vaccha, is unwholesome; non-covetousness is wholesome. Ill will, Vaccha, is unwholesome; non-ill will is wholesome. Wrong view, Vaccha, is unwholesome; right view is wholesome. Thus, Vaccha, these ten things are unwholesome, and these ten things are wholesome.

“Yato [V 2.0168] kho, vaccha, bhikkhuno taṇhā pahīnā hoti ucchinnamūlā tālāvatthukatā anabhāvaṃkatā āyatiṃ anuppādadhammā, so hoti bhikkhu arahaṃ khīṇāsavo vusitavā katakaraṇīyo ohitabhāro anuppattasadattho parikkhīṇabhavasaṃyojano sammadaññā vimutto”ti.

Vaccha, when a bhikkhu's craving has been abandoned, its root cut off, made like a palm-tree stump, brought to non-existence, and is of a nature not to arise again in the future, that bhikkhu is an Arahant, one whose taints are destroyed, who has lived the holy life, done what had to be done, laid down the burden, attained his own goal, for whom the fetter of existence is destroyed, and who is liberated through right understanding.

195. “Tiṭṭhatu bhavaṃ gotamo. Atthi pana te bhoto gotamassa ekabhikkhupi sāvako yo āsavānaṃ khayā sāvako āsavānaṃ khayā (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) evamuparipi anāsavaṃ cetovimuttiṃ paññāvimuttiṃ [M 2.0158] diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharatī”ti? “Na kho, vaccha, ekaṃyeva sataṃ na dve satāni na tīṇi satāni na cattāri satāni na pañca satāni, atha kho bhiyyova ye bhikkhū mama sāvakā āsavānaṃ khayā anāsavaṃ cetovimuttiṃ paññāvimuttiṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharantī”ti.

195. 'Let that be, Venerable Gotama. But is there even one bhikkhu disciple of the Venerable Gotama who, through the destruction of the taints, dwells having realized for himself with direct knowledge, in this very life, the taintless liberation of mind, liberation by wisdom?' 'It is not just one hundred, Vaccha, not two hundred, not three hundred, not four hundred, not five hundred, but indeed many more are the bhikkhus, my disciples, who, through the destruction of the taints, dwell having realized for themselves with direct knowledge, in this very life, the taintless liberation of mind, liberation by wisdom.'

“Tiṭṭhatu bhavaṃ gotamo, tiṭṭhantu bhikkhū. Atthi pana bhoto gotamassa ekā bhikkhunīpi sāvikā yā āsavānaṃ khayā anāsavaṃ cetovimuttiṃ paññāvimuttiṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja [T 2.0252] viharatī”ti? “Na kho, vaccha, ekaṃyeva sataṃ na dve satāni na tīṇi satāni na cattāri satāni na pañca satāni, atha kho bhiyyova yā bhikkhuniyo mama sāvikā āsavānaṃ khayā anāsavaṃ cetovimuttiṃ paññāvimuttiṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharantī”ti.

“Let the Venerable Gotama be, let the monks be. But is there even one nun, a disciple of the Venerable Gotama, who, through the destruction of the taints, dwells having realized for herself with direct knowledge in this very life the taintless liberation of mind, liberation by wisdom?” “Vaccha, it is not just one hundred, not two hundred, not three hundred, not four hundred, not five hundred, but far more numerous are the nuns who are my disciples and who, through the destruction of the taints, dwell having realized for themselves with direct knowledge in this very life the taintless liberation of mind, liberation by wisdom.”

“Tiṭṭhatu bhavaṃ gotamo, tiṭṭhantu bhikkhū, tiṭṭhantu bhikkhuniyo. Atthi pana bhoto gotamassa ekupāsakopi sāvako gihī odātavasano brahmacārī yo pañcannaṃ orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā opapātiko tattha parinibbāyī anāvattidhammo tasmā lokā”ti? “Na kho, vaccha, ekaṃyeva sataṃ na dve satāni na tīṇi satāni na cattāri satāni na pañca satāni, atha kho bhiyyova ye upāsakā mama sāvakā gihī odātavasanā brahmacārino pañcannaṃ orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā [P 1.0491] opapātikā tattha parinibbāyino anāvattidhammā tasmā lokā”ti.

“Let the Venerable Gotama be, let the monks be, let the nuns be. But is there even one male lay follower, a disciple of the Venerable Gotama—a householder clad in white who lives the holy life—who, with the complete destruction of the five lower fetters, is of spontaneous birth, will attain final Nibbāna there, and is of the nature of not returning from that world?” “Vaccha, it is not just one hundred, not two hundred, not three hundred, not four hundred, not five hundred, but far more numerous are the male lay followers who are my disciples—householders clad in white who live the holy life—who, with the complete destruction of the five lower fetters, are of spontaneous birth, will attain final Nibbāna there, and are of the nature of not returning from that world.”

“Tiṭṭhatu [V 2.0169] bhavaṃ gotamo, tiṭṭhantu bhikkhū, tiṭṭhantu bhikkhuniyo, tiṭṭhantu upāsakā gihī odātavasanā brahmacārino. Atthi pana bhoto gotamassa ekupāsakopi sāvako gihī odātavasano kāmabhogī sāsanakaro ovādappaṭikaro yo tiṇṇavicikiccho vigatakathaṃkatho vesārajjappatto aparappaccayo satthusāsane viharatī”ti? “Na kho, vaccha, ekaṃyeva sataṃ na dve satāni na tīṇi satāni na cattāri satāni na pañca satāni[T 2.0253], atha kho bhiyyova ye upāsakā mama sāvakā gihī odātavasanā kāmabhogino sāsanakarā ovādappaṭikarā tiṇṇavicikicchā vigatakathaṃkathā vesārajjappattā aparappaccayā satthusāsane viharantī”ti.

“Let the Venerable Gotama be, let the monks be, let the nuns be, let the male lay followers who are householders clad in white and live the holy life be. But is there even one male lay follower, a disciple of the Venerable Gotama—a householder clad in white who enjoys sensual pleasures, who follows the instruction, acts according to the admonition, has overcome doubt, is free from questioning, has attained intrepidity, and dwells not dependent on another in the Teacher's dispensation?” “Vaccha, it is not just one hundred, not two hundred, not three hundred, not four hundred, not five hundred, but far more numerous are the male lay followers who are my disciples—householders clad in white who enjoy sensual pleasures, who follow the instruction, act according to the admonition, have overcome doubt, are free from questioning, have attained intrepidity, and dwell not dependent on another in the Teacher's dispensation.”

“Tiṭṭhatu [M 2.0159] bhavaṃ gotamo, tiṭṭhantu bhikkhū, tiṭṭhantu bhikkhuniyo, tiṭṭhantu upāsakā gihī odātavasanā brahmacārino, tiṭṭhantu upāsakā gihī odātavasanā kāmabhogino. Atthi pana bhoto gotamassa ekupāsikāpi sāvikā gihinī odātavasanā brahmacārinī yā pañcannaṃ orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā opapātikā tattha parinibbāyinī anāvattidhammā tasmā lokā”ti? “Na kho, vaccha, ekaṃyeva sataṃ na dve satāni na tīṇi satāni na cattāri satāni na pañca satāni, atha kho bhiyyova yā upāsikā mama sāvikā gihiniyo odātavasanā brahmacāriniyo pañcannaṃ orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā opapātikā tattha parinibbāyiniyo anāvattidhammā tasmā lokā”ti.

“Let the Venerable Gotama be, let the monks be, let the nuns be, let the male lay followers who are householders clad in white and live the holy life be, let the male lay followers who are householders clad in white and enjoy sensual pleasures be. But is there even one female lay disciple, a disciple of the Venerable Gotama—a householder clad in white who lives the holy life—who, with the complete destruction of the five lower fetters, is of spontaneous birth, will attain final Nibbāna there, and is of the nature of not returning from that world?” “Vaccha, it is not just one hundred, not two hundred, not three hundred, not four hundred, not five hundred, but far more numerous are the female lay disciples who are my disciples—householders clad in white who live the holy life—who, with the complete destruction of the five lower fetters, are of spontaneous birth, will attain final Nibbāna there, and are of the nature of not returning from that world.”

“Tiṭṭhatu bhavaṃ gotamo, tiṭṭhantu bhikkhū, tiṭṭhantu bhikkhuniyo, tiṭṭhantu upāsakā gihī odātavasanā brahmacārino, tiṭṭhantu upāsakā gihī odātavasanā kāmabhogino, tiṭṭhantu upāsikā gihiniyo odātavasanā brahmacāriniyo. Atthi pana bhoto gotamassa ekupāsikāpi sāvikā gihinī odātavasanā kāmabhoginī sāsanakarā ovādappaṭikarā yā tiṇṇavicikicchā vigatakathaṃkathā vesārajjappattā aparappaccayā satthusāsane viharatī”ti? “Na kho, vaccha, ekaṃyeva sataṃ na dve [T 2.0254] satāni na tīṇi satāni na cattāri satāni na pañca satāni, atha kho bhiyyova yā upāsikā mama sāvikā gihiniyo odātavasanā kāmabhoginiyo sāsanakarā ovādappaṭikarā tiṇṇavicchikicchā vigatakathaṃkathā vesārajjappattā aparappaccayā satthusāsane viharantī”ti.

“Let the Venerable Gotama be, let the monks be, let the nuns be, let the male lay followers who are householders clad in white and live the holy life be, let the male lay followers who are householders clad in white and enjoy sensual pleasures be, let the female lay followers who are householders clad in white and live the holy life be. But is there even one female lay disciple, a disciple of the Venerable Gotama—a householder clad in white who enjoys sensual pleasures, who follows the instruction, acts according to the admonition, has overcome doubt, is free from questioning, has attained intrepidity, and dwells not dependent on another in the Teacher's dispensation?” “Vaccha, it is not just one hundred, not two hundred, not three hundred, not four hundred, not five hundred, but far more numerous are the female lay disciples who are my disciples—householders clad in white who enjoy sensual pleasures, who follow the instruction, act according to the admonition, have overcome doubt, are free from questioning, have attained intrepidity, and dwell not dependent on another in the Teacher's dispensation.”

196. “Sace [V 2.0170] hi, bho gotama, imaṃ dhammaṃ bhavaṃyeva gotamo ārādhako abhavissa, no ca kho bhikkhū ārādhakā abhavissaṃsu[P 1.0492]; evamidaṃ brahmacariyaṃ aparipūraṃ abhavissa tenaṅgena. Yasmā ca kho, bho gotama, imaṃ dhammaṃ bhavañceva gotamo ārādhako bhikkhū ca ārādhakā; evamidaṃ brahmacariyaṃ paripūraṃ tenaṅgena.

196. “For if, Venerable Gotama, only the Venerable Gotama were the accomplisher of this Dhamma, and the monks were not the accomplishers, then in that aspect this holy life would be incomplete. And because, Venerable Gotama, both the Venerable Gotama is the accomplisher of this Dhamma and the monks are the accomplishers, in that aspect this holy life is complete.”

“Sace hi, bho gotama, imaṃ dhammaṃ bhavañceva gotamo ārādhako abhavissa, bhikkhū ca ārādhakā abhavissaṃsu, no ca kho bhikkhuniyo ārādhikā abhavissaṃsu; evamidaṃ brahmacariyaṃ aparipūraṃ abhavissa tenaṅgena. Yasmā ca kho, bho gotama, imaṃ dhammaṃ bhavañceva gotamo ārādhako, bhikkhū [M 2.0160] ca ārādhakā, bhikkhuniyo ca ārādhikā; evamidaṃ brahmacariyaṃ paripūraṃ tenaṅgena.

“For if, Venerable Gotama, the Venerable Gotama were the accomplisher of this Dhamma, and the monks were the accomplishers, but the nuns were not the accomplishers, then in that aspect this holy life would be incomplete. And because, Venerable Gotama, the Venerable Gotama is the accomplisher of this Dhamma, and the monks are the accomplishers, and the nuns are the accomplishers, in that aspect this holy life is complete.”

“Sace hi, bho gotama, imaṃ dhammaṃ bhavañceva gotamo ārādhako abhavissa, bhikkhū ca ārādhakā abhavissaṃsu, bhikkhuniyo ca ārādhikā abhavissaṃsu, no ca kho upāsakā gihī odātavasanā brahmacārino ārādhakā abhavissaṃsu; evamidaṃ brahmacariyaṃ aparipūraṃ abhavissa tenaṅgena. Yasmā ca kho, bho gotama, imaṃ dhammaṃ bhavañceva gotamo ārādhako, bhikkhū ca ārādhakā, bhikkhuniyo ca ārādhikā, upāsakā ca gihī [T 2.0255] odātavasanā brahmacārino ārādhakā; evamidaṃ brahmacariyaṃ paripūraṃ tenaṅgena.

“If, Master Gotama, you had accomplished this Dhamma, and the monks had accomplished it, and the nuns had accomplished it, but the male lay disciples—householders clad in white who lead the holy life—had not accomplished it, then this holy life would have been incomplete in that respect. But since, Master Gotama, you have accomplished this Dhamma, and the monks have accomplished it, and the nuns have accomplished it, and the male lay disciples—householders clad in white who lead the holy life—have also accomplished it, this holy life is complete in that respect.”

“Sace hi, bho gotama, imaṃ dhammaṃ bhavañceva gotamo ārādhako abhavissa, bhikkhū ca ārādhakā abhavissaṃsu, bhikkhuniyo ca ārādhikā abhavissaṃsu, upāsakā ca gihī odātavasanā brahmacārino ārādhakā abhavissaṃsu, no ca kho upāsakā gihī odātavasanā kāmabhogino ārādhakā abhavissaṃsu; evamidaṃ brahmacariyaṃ aparipūraṃ abhavissa tenaṅgena. Yasmā ca kho, bho gotama, imaṃ dhammaṃ bhavañceva gotamo ārādhako, bhikkhū ca ārādhakā, bhikkhuniyo ca ārādhikā, upāsakā ca gihī odātavasanā brahmacārino ārādhakā, upāsakā ca gihī odātavasanā kāmabhogino ārādhakā; evamidaṃ brahmacariyaṃ paripūraṃ tenaṅgena.

“If, Master Gotama, you had accomplished this Dhamma, and the monks had accomplished it, and the nuns had accomplished it, and the male lay disciples—householders clad in white who lead the holy life—had accomplished it, but the male lay disciples—householders clad in white who enjoy sensual pleasures—had not accomplished it, then this holy life would have been incomplete in that respect. But since, Master Gotama, you have accomplished this Dhamma, and the monks have accomplished it, and the nuns have accomplished it, and the male lay disciples—householders clad in white who lead the holy life—have accomplished it, and the male lay disciples—householders clad in white who enjoy sensual pleasures—have also accomplished it, this holy life is complete in that respect.”

“Sace [V 2.0171] hi, bho gotama, imaṃ dhammaṃ bhavañceva gotamo ārādhako abhavissa, bhikkhū ca ārādhakā abhavissaṃsu, bhikkhuniyo ca ārādhikā abhavissaṃsu, upāsakā ca gihī odātavasanā brahmacārino ārādhakā abhavissaṃsu, upāsakā ca gihī odātavasanā kāmabhogino ārādhakā abhavissaṃsu, no ca kho upāsikā gihiniyo odātavasanā brahmacāriniyo [P 1.0493] ārādhikā abhavissaṃsu; evamidaṃ brahmacariyaṃ aparipūraṃ abhavissa tenaṅgena. Yasmā ca kho, bho gotama, imaṃ dhammaṃ bhavañceva gotamo ārādhako, bhikkhū ca ārādhakā, bhikkhuniyo ca ārādhikā, upāsakā ca gihī odātavasanā brahmacārino ārādhakā, upāsakā ca gihī odātavasanā kāmabhogino ārādhakā[T 2.0256], upāsikā ca gihiniyo odātavasanā [M 2.0161] brahmacāriniyo ārādhikā; evamidaṃ brahmacariyaṃ paripūraṃ tenaṅgena.

“If, Master Gotama, you had accomplished this Dhamma, and the monks had accomplished it, and the nuns had accomplished it, and the male lay disciples—householders clad in white who lead the holy life—had accomplished it, and the male lay disciples—householders clad in white who enjoy sensual pleasures—had accomplished it, but the female lay disciples—householders clad in white who lead the holy life—had not accomplished it, then this holy life would have been incomplete in that respect. But since, Master Gotama, you have accomplished this Dhamma, and the monks have accomplished it, and the nuns have accomplished it, and the male lay disciples—householders clad in white who lead the holy life—have accomplished it, and the male lay disciples—householders clad in white who enjoy sensual pleasures—have accomplished it, and the female lay disciples—householders clad in white who lead the holy life—have also accomplished it, this holy life is complete in that respect.”

“Sace hi, bho gotama, imaṃ dhammaṃ bhavañceva gotamo ārādhako abhavissa, bhikkhū ca ārādhakā abhavissaṃsu, bhikkhuniyo ca ārādhikā abhavissaṃsu, upāsakā ca gihī odātavasanā brahmacārino ārādhakā abhavissaṃsu, upāsakā ca gihī odātavasanā kāmabhogino ārādhakā abhavissaṃsu, upāsikā ca gihiniyo odātavasanā brahmacāriniyo ārādhikā abhavissaṃsu, no ca kho upāsikā gihiniyo odātavasanā kāmabhoginiyo ārādhikā abhavissaṃsu; evamidaṃ brahmacariyaṃ aparipūraṃ abhavissa tenaṅgena. Yasmā ca kho, bho gotama, imaṃ dhammaṃ bhavañceva gotamo ārādhako, bhikkhū ca ārādhakā, bhikkhuniyo ca ārādhikā, upāsakā ca gihī odātavasanā brahmacārino ārādhakā, upāsakā ca gihī odātavasanā kāmabhogino ārādhakā, upāsikā ca gihiniyo odātavasanā brahmacāriniyo ārādhikā, upāsikā ca gihiniyo odātavasanā kāmabhoginiyo ārādhikā; evamidaṃ brahmacariyaṃ paripūraṃ tenaṅgena.

“If, Master Gotama, you had accomplished this Dhamma, and the monks had accomplished it, and the nuns had accomplished it, and the male lay disciples—householders clad in white who lead the holy life—had accomplished it, and the male lay disciples—householders clad in white who enjoy sensual pleasures—had accomplished it, and the female lay disciples—householders clad in white who lead the holy life—had accomplished it, but the female lay disciples—householders clad in white who enjoy sensual pleasures—had not accomplished it, then this holy life would have been incomplete in that respect. But since, Master Gotama, you have accomplished this Dhamma, and the monks have accomplished it, and the nuns have accomplished it, and the male lay disciples—householders clad in white who lead the holy life—have accomplished it, and the male lay disciples—householders clad in white who enjoy sensual pleasures—have accomplished it, and the female lay disciples—householders clad in white who lead the holy life—have accomplished it, and the female lay disciples—householders clad in white who enjoy sensual pleasures—have also accomplished it, this holy life is complete in that respect.”

197. “Seyyathāpi, bho gotama, gaṅgā nadī samuddaninnā samuddapoṇā samuddapabbhārā samuddaṃ āhacca tiṭṭhati, evamevāyaṃ bhoto gotamassa parisā sagahaṭṭhapabbajitā nibbānaninnā nibbānapoṇā nibbānapabbhārā nibbānaṃ āhacca tiṭṭhati. Abhikkantaṃ, bho gotama…pe… [T 2.0257] esāhaṃ bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāmi dhammañca bhikkhusaṅghañca. Labheyyāhaṃ bhoto gotamassa santike pabbajjaṃ, labheyyaṃ upasampada”nti[P 1.0494]. “Yo kho, vaccha, aññatitthiyapubbo imasmiṃ dhammavinaye ākaṅkhati [V 2.0172] pabbajjaṃ, ākaṅkhati upasampadaṃ, so cattāro māse parivasati. Catunnaṃ māsānaṃ accayena āraddhacittā bhikkhū pabbājenti upasampādenti bhikkhubhāvāya; api ca mettha puggalavemattatā viditā”ti. “Sace, bhante, aññatitthiyapubbā imasmiṃ dhammavinaye ākaṅkhantā pabbajjaṃ, ākaṅkhantā upasampadaṃ cattāro māse parivasanti, catunnaṃ māsānaṃ accayena āraddhacittā bhikkhū pabbājenti upasampādenti bhikkhubhāvāya; ahaṃ cattāri vassāni parivasissāmi. Catunnaṃ vassānaṃ accayena āraddhacittā bhikkhū pabbājentu upasampādentu bhikkhubhāvāyā”ti. Alattha kho vacchagotto paribbājako bhagavato santike pabbajjaṃ alattha upasampadaṃ.

197. “Just as, Master Gotama, the river Ganges slopes, inclines, and tends towards the ocean, and comes to rest in the ocean; even so, this assembly of yours—both householders and renunciants—slopes, inclines, and tends towards Nibbāna, and comes to rest in Nibbāna. Excellent, Master Gotama! … I go for refuge to Master Gotama, to the Dhamma, and to the Saṅgha of bhikkhus. May I receive the going forth in the presence of Master Gotama, may I receive the higher ordination.” “Vaccha, whoever was formerly of another sect and wishes for the going forth and the higher ordination in this Dhamma and Discipline undergoes probation for four months. After the passing of four months, the bhikkhus, being satisfied, give the going forth and the higher ordination for the state of a bhikkhu. However, I recognize individual differences in this matter.” “If, venerable sir, those who were formerly of other sects and wish for the going forth and the higher ordination in this Dhamma and Discipline undergo probation for four months, and after the passing of four months, the bhikkhus, being satisfied, give them the going forth and the higher ordination for the state of a bhikkhu, then I will undergo probation for four years. After the passing of four years, may the bhikkhus, being satisfied, give me the going forth and the higher ordination for the state of a bhikkhu.” Then the wanderer Vacchagotta received the going forth and the higher ordination in the presence of the Blessed One.

Acirūpasampanno [M 2.0162] kho panāyasmā vacchagotto addhamāsūpasampanno yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā vacchagotto bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “yāvatakaṃ, bhante, sekhena ñāṇena sekhāya [T 2.0258] vijjāya pattabbaṃ, anuppattaṃ taṃ mayā; uttari ca me uttariṃ me (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) bhagavā dhammaṃ desetū”ti. “Tena hi tvaṃ, vaccha, dve dhamme uttari bhāvehi – samathañca vipassanañca. Ime kho te, vaccha, dve dhammā uttari bhāvitā – samatho ca vipassanā ca – anekadhātupaṭivedhāya saṃvattissanti.

Then the Venerable Vacchagotta, who had been fully ordained not long ago, for half a month, approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the Venerable Vacchagotta said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, whatever is to be attained by the knowledge and wisdom of a trainee, all that has been attained by me. May the Blessed One teach me the Dhamma further.” “In that case, Vaccha, you should further develop two things: tranquility and insight. These two things, Vaccha, when further developed—tranquility and insight—will lead to the penetration of the manifold elements.”

198. “So tvaṃ, vaccha, yāvadeva yāvade (pī.) ākaṅkhissasi – ‘anekavihitaṃ iddhividhaṃ paccanubhaveyyaṃ – ekopi hutvā bahudhā assaṃ, bahudhāpi hutvā eko assaṃ; āvibhāvaṃ, tirobhāvaṃ; tirokuṭṭaṃ tiropākāraṃ tiropabbataṃ asajjamāno gaccheyyaṃ, seyyathāpi ākāse; pathaviyāpi ummujjanimujjaṃ kareyyaṃ, seyyathāpi udake; udakepi abhijjamāne gaccheyyaṃ, seyyathāpi pathaviyaṃ; ākāsepi pallaṅkena kameyyaṃ, seyyathāpi pakkhī sakuṇo; imepi candimasūriye evaṃmahiddhike evaṃmahānubhāve pāṇinā parimaseyyaṃ, parimajjeyyaṃ; yāvabrahmalokāpi kāyena vasaṃ vatteyya’nti, tatra tatreva sakkhibhabbataṃ pāpuṇissasi, sati satiāyatane.

198. “Then you, Vaccha, should you wish: ‘May I experience the various kinds of psychic power: being one, may I become many; being many, may I become one; may I appear and disappear; may I go unhindered through a wall, a rampart, and a mountain as if through space; may I dive into and emerge from the earth as if it were water; may I walk on water without it breaking as if on earth; may I travel cross-legged through the sky like a winged bird; with my hand, may I touch and stroke these sun and moon, so mighty and powerful; may I exercise mastery with the body even as far as the Brahma-world’—in each and every case you will attain the ability to witness it, when the basis for mindfulness is present.

“So tvaṃ, vaccha, yāvadeva ākaṅkhissasi – ‘dibbāya sotadhātuyā [P 1.0495] visuddhāya atikkantamānusikāya [V 2.0173] ubho sadde suṇeyyaṃ – dibbe ca mānuse ca, ye dūre santike cā’ti, tatra tatreva sakkhibhabbataṃ pāpuṇissasi, sati satiāyatane.

“Then you, Vaccha, should you wish: ‘With the divine ear element, purified and surpassing the human, may I hear both kinds of sounds, divine and human, those that are far and near’—in each and every case you will attain the ability to witness it, when the basis for mindfulness is present.

“So tvaṃ, vaccha, yāvadeva ākaṅkhissasi – ‘parasattānaṃ parapuggalānaṃ cetasā ceto paricca pajāneyyaṃ – sarāgaṃ vā cittaṃ sarāgaṃ [T 2.0259] cittanti pajāneyyaṃ, vītarāgaṃ vā cittaṃ vītarāgaṃ cittanti pajāneyyaṃ; sadosaṃ vā cittaṃ sadosaṃ cittanti pajāneyyaṃ, vītadosaṃ vā cittaṃ vītadosaṃ cittanti pajāneyyaṃ; samohaṃ vā cittaṃ samohaṃ cittanti pajāneyyaṃ, vītamohaṃ vā cittaṃ vītamohaṃ cittanti pajāneyyaṃ; saṃkhittaṃ vā cittaṃ saṃkhittaṃ cittanti pajāneyyaṃ, vikkhittaṃ vā cittaṃ vikkhittaṃ cittanti pajāneyyaṃ; mahaggataṃ vā cittaṃ mahaggataṃ [M 2.0163] cittanti pajāneyyaṃ, amahaggataṃ vā cittaṃ amahaggataṃ cittanti pajāneyyaṃ; sauttaraṃ vā cittaṃ sauttaraṃ cittanti pajāneyyaṃ, anuttaraṃ vā cittaṃ anuttaraṃ cittanti pajāneyyaṃ; samāhitaṃ vā cittaṃ samāhitaṃ cittanti pajāneyyaṃ, asamāhitaṃ vā cittaṃ asamāhitaṃ cittanti pajāneyyaṃ; vimuttaṃ vā cittaṃ vimuttaṃ cittanti pajāneyyaṃ, avimuttaṃ vā cittaṃ avimuttaṃ cittanti pajāneyya’nti, tatra tatreva sakkhibhabbataṃ pāpuṇissasi, sati satiāyatane.

“Then you, Vaccha, should you wish: ‘Having encompassed them with my own mind, may I know distinctly the minds of other beings, other individuals: a mind with lust as a mind with lust, a mind without lust as a mind without lust; a mind with hate as a mind with hate, a mind without hate as a mind without hate; a mind with delusion as a mind with delusion, a mind without delusion as a mind without delusion; a contracted mind as a contracted mind, a scattered mind as a scattered mind; a sublime mind as a sublime mind, a non-sublime mind as a non-sublime mind; a surpassable mind as a surpassable mind, an unsurpassable mind as an unsurpassable mind; a concentrated mind as a concentrated mind, an unconcentrated mind as an unconcentrated mind; a liberated mind as a liberated mind, an unliberated mind as an unliberated mind’—in each and every case you will attain the ability to witness it, when the basis for mindfulness is present.

“So tvaṃ, vaccha, yāvadeva ākaṅkhissasi – ‘anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussareyyaṃ, seyyathidaṃ – ekampi jātiṃ dvepi jātiyo tissopi jātiyo catassopi jātiyo pañcapi jātiyo dasapi jātiyo vīsampi jātiyo tiṃsampi jātiyo cattālīsampi jātiyo paññāsampi jātiyo jātisatampi jātisahassampi jātisatasahassampi; anekepi saṃvaṭṭakappe anekepi vivaṭṭakappe anekepi saṃvaṭṭavivaṭṭakappe – amutrāsiṃ [T 2.0260] evaṃnāmo evaṃgotto evaṃvaṇṇo evamāhāro evaṃsukhadukkhappaṭisaṃvedī evamāyupariyanto, so tato cuto amutra udapādiṃ; tatrāpāsiṃ evaṃnāmo evaṃgotto evaṃvaṇṇo evamāhāro evaṃsukhadukkhappaṭisaṃvedī evamāyupariyanto, so tato cuto idhūpapannoti; iti sākāraṃ sauddesaṃ anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussareyya’nti, tatra tatreva sakkhibhabbataṃ pāpuṇissasi, sati satiāyatane.

“Then you, Vaccha, should you wish: ‘May I recollect my manifold former existences, that is to say: one birth, two births, three births, four births, five births, ten births, twenty births, thirty births, forty births, fifty births, a hundred births, a thousand births, a hundred thousand births; many aeons of contraction, many aeons of expansion, many aeons of contraction and expansion: “In that existence I had such a name, belonged to such a clan, had such an appearance, was nourished by such food, experienced such pleasure and pain, and had such a life-span. Passing away from there, I reappeared elsewhere. There, too, I had such a name, belonged to such a clan, had such an appearance, was nourished by such food, experienced such pleasure and pain, and had such a life-span. Passing away from there, I have been reborn here.” Thus may I recollect my manifold former existences with their aspects and details’—in each and every case you will attain the ability to witness it, when the basis for mindfulness is present.

“So [P 1.0496] tvaṃ, vaccha, yāvadeva ākaṅkhissasi – ‘dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena satte passeyyaṃ cavamāne upapajjamāne hīne paṇīte suvaṇṇe dubbaṇṇe sugate [V 2.0174] duggate yathākammūpage satte pajāneyyaṃ – ime vata bhonto sattā kāyaduccaritena samannāgatā vacīduccaritena samannāgatā manoduccaritena samannāgatā ariyānaṃ upavādakā micchādiṭṭhikā micchādiṭṭhikammasamādānā, te kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapannā; ime vā pana bhonto sattā kāyasucaritena samannāgatā vacīsucaritena samannāgatā manosucaritena samannāgatā ariyānaṃ anupavādakā sammādiṭṭhikā sammādiṭṭhikammasamādānā, te kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapannāti; iti dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena satte [M 2.0164] passeyyaṃ cavamāne upapajjamāne hīne paṇīte suvaṇṇe dubbaṇṇe sugate duggate [T 2.0261] yathākammūpage satte pajāneyya’nti, tatra tatreva sakkhibhabbataṃ pāpuṇissasi, sati satiāyatane.

“Then you, Vaccha, should you wish: ‘With the divine eye, purified and surpassing the human, may I see beings passing away and being reborn—inferior and superior, of good appearance and bad appearance, in good destinations and in bad destinations; may I know distinctly how beings fare according to their kamma: “Indeed, these good beings, endowed with misconduct of body, speech, and mind, who were revilers of the noble ones, held wrong view, and were undertakers of actions based on wrong view—they, with the breakup of the body, after death, have been reborn in the plane of deprivation, a bad destination, a state of ruin, in hell. Or indeed, these good beings, endowed with good conduct of body, speech, and mind, who were not revilers of the noble ones, held right view, and were undertakers of actions based on right view—they, with the breakup of the body, after death, have been reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world.” Thus, with the divine eye, purified and surpassing the human, may I see beings passing away and being reborn—inferior and superior, of good appearance and bad appearance, in good destinations and in bad destinations; may I know distinctly how beings fare according to their kamma’—in each and every case you will attain the ability to witness it, when the basis for mindfulness is present.

“So tvaṃ, vaccha, yāvadeva ākaṅkhissasi – ‘āsavānaṃ khayā anāsavaṃ cetovimuttiṃ paññāvimuttiṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja vihareyya’nti, tatra tatreva sakkhibhabbataṃ pāpuṇissasi, sati satiāyatane”ti.

So, Vaccha, inasmuch as you shall wish: ‘Through the destruction of the taints, may I, in this very life, realize for myself with direct knowledge the taintless liberation of mind, the liberation by wisdom, and having attained it, may I dwell therein’—in that very matter you will attain the capability of realization, when there is a basis for mindfulness.”

199. Atha kho āyasmā vacchagotto bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinanditvā anumoditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā pakkāmi. Atha kho āyasmā vacchagotto eko vūpakaṭṭho appamatto ātāpī pahitatto viharanto nacirasseva – yassatthāya kulaputtā sammadeva agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajanti tadanuttaraṃ – brahmacariyapariyosānaṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja vihāsi. ‘Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti abbhaññāsi. Aññataro kho panāyasmā vacchagotto arahataṃ ahosi.

199. Then the Venerable Vacchagotta, having delighted in and rejoiced at the Blessed One’s words, rose from his seat, paid homage to the Blessed One, circumambulated him respectfully, and departed. Then, dwelling alone, secluded, diligent, ardent, and resolute, the Venerable Vacchagotta, before long, realized for himself with direct knowledge, in this very life, that unsurpassed culmination of the holy life for the sake of which clansmen rightly go forth from the household life into homelessness, and having attained it, he dwelled therein. He knew directly: ‘Birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this state of being.’ And the Venerable Vacchagotta became one of the Arahants.

200. Tena kho pana samayena sambahulā bhikkhū bhagavantaṃ dassanāya gacchanti. Addasā kho āyasmā vacchagotto te bhikkhū dūratova āgacchante. Disvāna yena te bhikkhū tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā te bhikkhū etadavoca [P 1.0497] – “handa! Kahaṃ pana tumhe āyasmanto gacchathā”ti? “Bhagavantaṃ kho mayaṃ, āvuso, dassanāya gacchāmā”ti[T 2.0262]. “Tenahāyasmanto mama vacanena bhagavato pāde sirasā vandatha, evañca vadetha – ‘vacchagotto, bhante, bhikkhu bhagavato pāde sirasā vandati, evañca vadeti – pariciṇṇo me bhagavā, pariciṇṇo me sugato’”ti. “Evamāvuso”ti [V 2.0175] kho te bhikkhū āyasmato vacchagottassa paccassosuṃ. Atha kho te bhikkhū yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Ekamantaṃ nisinnā kho te bhikkhū bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ – “āyasmā, bhante, vacchagotto bhagavato pāde sirasā vandati, evañca vadeti – ‘pariciṇṇo me bhagavā, pariciṇṇo me sugato’”ti. “Pubbeva me, bhikkhave, vacchagotto bhikkhu cetasā ceto paricca vidito – ‘tevijjo vacchagotto [M 2.0165] bhikkhu mahiddhiko mahānubhāvo’ti. Devatāpi me etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ – ‘tevijjo, bhante, vacchagotto bhikkhu mahiddhiko mahānubhāvo’”ti.

200. Now at that time, many bhikkhus were going to see the Blessed One. The Venerable Vacchagotta saw those bhikkhus coming from afar. Having seen them, he went to where those bhikkhus were, and having approached them, he said this: “Come now, venerable sirs, where are you going?” “Friend, we are going to see the Blessed One.” “In that case, venerable sirs, in my name, bow with your heads at the feet of the Blessed One and say this: ‘Venerable sir, the bhikkhu Vacchagotta bows with his head at the feet of the Blessed One and says this: “The Blessed One has been fully served by me; the Well-Farer has been fully served by me.”’” “Yes, friend,” those bhikkhus replied to the Venerable Vacchagotta. Then those bhikkhus went to where the Blessed One was. Having approached, they paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Sitting to one side, those bhikkhus said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, the Venerable Vacchagotta bows with his head at the feet of the Blessed One and says this: ‘The Blessed One has been fully served by me; the Well-Farer has been fully served by me.’” “Bhikkhus, I had already known the mind of the bhikkhu Vacchagotta, having encompassed it with my own mind: ‘The bhikkhu Vacchagotta possesses the three knowledges, is of great psychic power, and of great might.’ Deities also informed me of this matter, saying: ‘Venerable sir, the bhikkhu Vacchagotta possesses the three knowledges, is of great psychic power, and of great might.’”

Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamanā te bhikkhū bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandunti.

The Blessed One said this. Pleased, those bhikkhus delighted in the Blessed One’s words.

Mahāvacchasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ tatiyaṃ.

The third, the Great Vacchagotta Sutta, is concluded.

4. Dīghanakhasuttaṃ

4. The Dīghanakha Sutta

201. Evaṃ [T 2.0263][V 2.0176] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā rājagahe viharati gijjhakūṭe pabbate sūkarakhatāyaṃ. Atha kho dīghanakho paribbājako yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhito kho dīghanakho paribbājako bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “ahañhi, bho gotama, evaṃvādī evaṃdiṭṭhi – ‘sabbaṃ me nakkhamatī’”ti. “Yāpi kho te esā, aggivessana, diṭṭhi – ‘sabbaṃ me nakkhamatī’ti, esāpi te diṭṭhi nakkhamatī”ti? “Esā ce esāpi (ka.) me, bho gotama, diṭṭhi khameyya, taṃpassa tādisameva, taṃpassa [P 1.0498] tādisamevā”ti. “Ato kho te, aggivessana, bahū hi bahutarā lokasmiṃ ye evamāhaṃsu – ‘taṃpassa tādisameva, taṃpassa tādisamevā’ti. Te tañceva diṭṭhiṃ nappajahanti aññañca diṭṭhiṃ upādiyanti. Ato kho te, aggivessana, tanū hi tanutarā lokasmiṃ ye evamāhaṃsu – ‘taṃpassa tādisameva, taṃpassa tādisamevā’ti. Te tañceva diṭṭhiṃ pajahanti aññañca diṭṭhiṃ na upādiyanti. Santaggivessana, eke samaṇabrāhmaṇā evaṃvādino evaṃdiṭṭhino – ‘sabbaṃ me khamatī’ti; santaggivessana, eke samaṇabrāhmaṇā evaṃvādino evaṃdiṭṭhino – ‘sabbaṃ me nakkhamatī’ti; santaggivessana[T 2.0264], eke samaṇabrāhmaṇā evaṃvādino evaṃdiṭṭhino – ‘ekaccaṃ me khamati, ekaccaṃ me nakkhamatī’ti. Tatraggivessana, ye te samaṇabrāhmaṇā evaṃvādino evaṃdiṭṭhino – ‘sabbaṃ me khamatī’ti tesamayaṃ diṭṭhi sārāgāya santike, saññogāya santike, abhinandanāya santike ajjhosānāya santike [M 2.0166] upādānāya santike; tatraggivessana ye te samaṇabrāhmaṇā evaṃvādino evaṃdiṭṭhino – ‘sabbaṃ me nakkhamatī’ti tesamayaṃ diṭṭhi asārāgāya santike, asaññogāya santike, anabhinandanāya santike, anajjhosānāya santike, anupādānāya santike”ti.

201. Thus have I heard—at one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Rājagaha, on Vulture Peak, in the Sūkarakhatā cave. Then the wanderer Dīghanakha approached the Blessed One; having approached, he exchanged greetings with the Blessed One. When the courteous and friendly talk was concluded, he stood to one side. Standing to one side, the wanderer Dīghanakha said this to the Blessed One: “I, Venerable Gotama, hold such a view and such a doctrine—‘All is not acceptable to me.’” “Aggivessana, even this view of yours—‘All is not acceptable to me’—is that view not acceptable to you?” “If, Venerable Gotama, this view were acceptable to me, that would be just the same, that would be just the same.” “Aggivessana, there are many, indeed, a great many, in the world who say thus—‘That would be just the same, that would be just the same.’ They do not abandon that very view and they take up another view. Aggivessana, there are few, indeed, very few, in the world who say thus—‘That would be just the same, that would be just the same.’ They abandon that very view and do not take up another view. Aggivessana, there are some ascetics and brahmins who hold such a view and such a doctrine—‘All is acceptable to me.’ Aggivessana, there are some ascetics and brahmins who hold such a view and such a doctrine—‘All is not acceptable to me.’ Aggivessana, there are some ascetics and brahmins who hold such a view and such a doctrine—‘Some is acceptable to me, some is not acceptable to me.’ Therein, Aggivessana, among those ascetics and brahmins who hold such a view and such a doctrine—‘All is acceptable to me’—their view is near to passion, near to bondage, near to delight, near to attachment, near to grasping. Therein, Aggivessana, among those ascetics and brahmins who hold such a view and such a doctrine—‘All is not acceptable to me’—their view is near to dispassion, near to non-bondage, near to non-delight, near to non-attachment, near to non-grasping.”

202. Evaṃ vutte, dīghanakho paribbājako bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “ukkaṃseti ukkaṃsati (sī. pī. ka.) me bhavaṃ gotamo diṭṭhigataṃ, samukkaṃseti sampahaṃsati (ka.) me bhavaṃ gotamo diṭṭhigata”nti. “Tatraggivessana, ye te samaṇabrāhmaṇā evaṃvādino evaṃdiṭṭhino – ‘ekaccaṃ me khamati, ekaccaṃ me nakkhamatī’ti. Yā [V 2.0177] hi tesaṃ khamati sāyaṃ diṭṭhi sārāgāya santike, saññogāya santike, abhinandanāya santike, ajjhosānāya santike, upādānāya santike; yā hi tesaṃ nakkhamati sāyaṃ diṭṭhi asārāgāya santike, asaññogāya santike, anabhinandanāya santike, anajjhosānāya santike, anupādānāya santike.
