“Ime ca, thapati, kusalā saṅkappā kiṃsamuṭṭhānā? Samuṭṭhānampi nesaṃ vuttaṃ. ‘Saññāsamuṭṭhānā’tissa vacanīyaṃ. Katamā saññā? Saññāpi hi bahū anekavidhā [M 2.0220] nānappakārakā. Nekkhammasaññā, abyāpādasaññā, avihiṃsāsaññā – itosamuṭṭhānā kusalā saṅkappā.

“And these wholesome thoughts, master builder, from what do they arise? Their origin has also been stated. It should be said, ‘They arise from perception.’ What perception? For perception is indeed manifold, of many kinds, of various sorts. The perception of renunciation, the perception of non-ill will, the perception of non-cruelty—from these arise wholesome thoughts.”

“Ime ca, thapati, kusalā saṅkappā kuhiṃ aparisesā nirujjhanti? Nirodhopi nesaṃ vutto. Idha, thapati, bhikkhu vitakkavicārānaṃ vūpasamā…pe… dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati; etthete kusalā saṅkappā aparisesā nirujjhanti.

“And these wholesome thoughts, master builder, where do they cease without remainder? Their cessation has also been stated. Here, master builder, a bhikkhu, with the stilling of applied and sustained thought… enters and abides in the second jhāna; it is here that these wholesome thoughts cease without remainder.”

“Kathaṃ [V 2.0230] paṭipanno ca, thapati, kusalānaṃ saṅkappānaṃ nirodhāya paṭipanno hoti? Idha, thapati, bhikkhu anuppannānaṃ pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ anuppādāya chandaṃ janeti vāyamati vīriyaṃ ārabhati cittaṃ paggaṇhāti padahati; uppannānaṃ pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānāya…pe… anuppannānaṃ kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ uppādāya…pe… uppannānaṃ kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ ṭhitiyā asammosāya bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya bhāvanāya pāripūriyā chandaṃ janeti vāyamati vīriyaṃ ārabhati [T 2.0351] cittaṃ paggaṇhāti padahati. Evaṃ paṭipanno kho, thapati, kusalānaṃ saṅkappānaṃ nirodhāya paṭipanno hoti.

“And how, master builder, does one practice for the cessation of wholesome thoughts? Here, master builder, a bhikkhu generates desire, makes an effort, arouses energy, exerts his mind, and strives for the non-arising of unarisen evil, unwholesome states; for the abandoning of arisen evil, unwholesome states... for the arising of unarisen wholesome states... for the maintenance, non-degeneration, increase, abundance, development, and perfection of arisen wholesome states, he generates desire, makes an effort, arouses energy, exerts his mind, and strives. Practicing in this way, master builder, one practices for the cessation of wholesome thoughts.”

268. “Katamehi cāhaṃ, thapati, dasahi dhammehi samannāgataṃ purisapuggalaṃ paññapemi [P 2.0029] sampannakusalaṃ paramakusalaṃ uttamapattipattaṃ samaṇaṃ ayojjhaṃ? Idha, thapati, bhikkhu asekhāya sammādiṭṭhiyā samannāgato hoti, asekhena sammāsaṅkappena samannāgato hoti, asekhāya sammāvācāya samannāgato hoti, asekhena sammākammantena samannāgato hoti, asekhena sammāājīvena samannāgato hoti, asekhena sammāvāyāmena samannāgato hoti, asekhāya sammāsatiyā samannāgato hoti, asekhena sammāsamādhinā samannāgato hoti, asekhena sammāñāṇena samannāgato hoti, asekhāya sammāvimuttiyā samannāgato hoti – imehi kho ahaṃ, thapati, dasahi dhammehi samannāgataṃ purisapuggalaṃ paññapemi sampannakusalaṃ paramakusalaṃ uttamapattipattaṃ samaṇaṃ ayojjha”nti.

268. “And by what ten qualities, master builder, do I designate a person as one accomplished in the wholesome, supreme in the wholesome, who has attained the highest attainment, an invincible contemplative? Here, master builder, a bhikkhu is endowed with the right view of one beyond training, endowed with the right intention of one beyond training, endowed with the right speech of one beyond training, endowed with the right action of one beyond training, endowed with the right livelihood of one beyond training, endowed with the right effort of one beyond training, endowed with the right mindfulness of one beyond training, endowed with the right concentration of one beyond training, endowed with the right knowledge of one beyond training, and endowed with the right liberation of one beyond training. It is by these ten qualities, master builder, that I designate a person as one accomplished in the wholesome, supreme in the wholesome, who has attained the highest attainment, an invincible contemplative.”

Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamano pañcakaṅgo thapati bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandīti.

Thus spoke the Blessed One. The master builder Pañcakaṅga, delighted, greatly rejoiced in the Blessed One's words.

Samaṇamuṇḍikasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ aṭṭhamaṃ.

The Samaṇamuṇḍika Sutta, the eighth, is concluded.

9. Cūḷasakuludāyisuttaṃ

9. The Shorter Discourse to Sakuludāyin

269. Evaṃ [T 2.0352][M 2.0221][V 2.0231] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe. Tena kho pana samayena sakuludāyī paribbājako moranivāpe paribbājakārāme paṭivasati mahatiyā paribbājakaparisāya saddhiṃ. Atha kho bhagavā pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya rājagahaṃ piṇḍāya pāvisi. Atha kho bhagavato etadahosi – “atippago kho tāva rājagahe piṇḍāya carituṃ. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ yena moranivāpo paribbājakārāmo yena sakuludāyī paribbājako tenupasaṅkameyya”nti. Atha kho bhagavā yena moranivāpo paribbājakārāmo tenupasaṅkami.

269. Thus have I heard. At one time, the Blessed One was dwelling at Rājagaha, in the Veḷuvana, the Kalandakanivāpa. Now at that time, the wanderer Sakuludāyī was staying at the Moranivāpa, the wanderers' park, together with a large assembly of wanderers. Then the Blessed One, having dressed in the morning, took his bowl and robe and entered Rājagaha for alms-food. Then it occurred to the Blessed One: “It is still too early to walk for alms-food in Rājagaha. What if I were to approach the Moranivāpa, the wanderers' park, where the wanderer Sakuludāyī is?” Then the Blessed One approached the Moranivāpa, the wanderers' park.

Tena kho pana samayena sakuludāyī paribbājako mahatiyā paribbājakaparisāya saddhiṃ nisinno hoti unnādiniyā uccāsaddamahāsaddāya [P 2.0030] anekavihitaṃ tiracchānakathaṃ kathentiyā, seyyathidaṃ – rājakathaṃ corakathaṃ mahāmattakathaṃ senākathaṃ bhayakathaṃ yuddhakathaṃ annakathaṃ pānakathaṃ vatthakathaṃ sayanakathaṃ mālākathaṃ gandhakathaṃ ñātikathaṃ yānakathaṃ gāmakathaṃ nigamakathaṃ nagarakathaṃ janapadakathaṃ itthikathaṃ sūrakathaṃ visikhākathaṃ kumbhaṭṭhānakathaṃ pubbapetakathaṃ nānattakathaṃ lokakkhāyikaṃ samuddakkhāyikaṃ itibhavābhavakathaṃ iti vā. Addasā kho sakuludāyī paribbājako bhagavantaṃ dūratova āgacchantaṃ. Disvāna sakaṃ parisaṃ saṇṭhāpesi – “appasaddā bhonto hontu, mā bhonto saddamakattha. Ayaṃ samaṇo gotamo āgacchati; appasaddakāmo kho pana so āyasmā appasaddassa vaṇṇavādī. Appeva nāma appasaddaṃ parisaṃ viditvā upasaṅkamitabbaṃ maññeyyā”ti. Atha kho te paribbājakā tuṇhī ahesuṃ[T 2.0353].

Now at that time, the wanderer Sakuludāyī was sitting together with a large assembly of wanderers, making a loud, great, and echoing sound, engaged in various kinds of base talk, that is to say: talk of kings, talk of thieves, talk of great ministers, talk of armies, talk of dangers, talk of battles, talk of food, talk of drink, talk of clothing, talk of beds, talk of garlands, talk of perfumes, talk of relatives, talk of vehicles, talk of villages, talk of market towns, talk of cities, talk of countries, talk of women, talk of heroes, street-corner talk, talk at the well, talk of the departed, miscellaneous talk, speculations about the world, speculations about the ocean, and talk of prosperity and decline. The wanderer Sakuludāyī saw the Blessed One coming from afar. Having seen him, he quieted his own assembly, saying: “Sirs, be quiet. Sirs, do not make a sound. This contemplative Gotama is coming. That venerable one is a lover of quiet and speaks in praise of quiet. Perhaps, upon seeing a quiet assembly, he might think it worthwhile to approach.” Then those wanderers became silent.

270. Atha kho bhagavā yena sakuludāyī paribbājako tenupasaṅkami. Atha kho sakuludāyī paribbājako bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “etu kho, bhante, bhagavā. Svāgataṃ, bhante, bhagavato. Cirassaṃ kho, bhante, bhagavā imaṃ pariyāyamakāsi yadidaṃ idhāgamanāya. Nisīdatu, bhante, bhagavā; idamāsanaṃ paññatta”nti. Nisīdi bhagavā paññatte āsane. Sakuludāyīpi kho [V 2.0232] paribbājako aññataraṃ nīcaṃ āsanaṃ gahetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho sakuludāyiṃ paribbājakaṃ bhagavā etadavoca – “kāya nuttha, udāyi, etarahi [M 2.0222] kathāya sannisinnā, kā ca pana vo antarākathā vippakatā”ti? “Tiṭṭhatesā, bhante, kathā yāya mayaṃ etarahi kathāya sannisinnā. Nesā, bhante, kathā bhagavato dullabhā bhavissati pacchāpi savanāya. Yadāhaṃ, bhante, imaṃ parisaṃ anupasaṅkanto homi athāyaṃ parisā anekavihitaṃ tiracchānakathaṃ kathentī nisinnā hoti; yadā ca kho ahaṃ, bhante, imaṃ parisaṃ upasaṅkanto homi athāyaṃ parisā mamaññeva mukhaṃ ullokentī nisinnā hoti – ‘yaṃ no samaṇo udāyī dhammaṃ bhāsissati taṃ taṃ no (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) sossāmā’ti; yadā pana[P 2.0031], bhante, bhagavā imaṃ parisaṃ upasaṅkanto hoti athāhañceva ayañca parisā bhagavato mukhaṃ ullokentā olokentī (syā. kaṃ. ka.) nisinnā homa – ‘yaṃ no bhagavā dhammaṃ bhāsissati taṃ sossāmā’”ti.

270. Then the Blessed One approached the wanderer Sakuludāyī. Then the wanderer Sakuludāyī said to the Blessed One: 'Come, venerable sir, Blessed One. Welcome, venerable sir, to the Blessed One. It has been a long time, venerable sir, since the Blessed One made this occasion to come here. Let the Blessed One be seated, venerable sir; this seat is prepared.' The Blessed One sat down on the prepared seat. The wanderer Sakuludāyī also took a certain low seat and sat to one side. To the wanderer Sakuludāyī, so seated to one side, the Blessed One said this: 'Udāyī, for what talk are you now assembled, and what was your conversation that was interrupted?' 'Let that talk stand, venerable sir, for which we are now assembled. That talk, venerable sir, will not be difficult for the Blessed One to hear later. When I, venerable sir, do not approach this assembly, then this assembly sits engaged in various kinds of base talk. But when I, venerable sir, approach this assembly, then this assembly sits looking up to my face, thinking, “Whatever Dhamma the ascetic Udāyī will speak, that we shall hear.” And when, venerable sir, the Blessed One approaches this assembly, then both I and this assembly sit looking up to the Blessed One's face, thinking, “Whatever Dhamma the Blessed One will speak, that we shall hear.”'

271. “Tenahudāyi, taṃyevettha paṭibhātu yathā maṃ paṭibhāseyyā”si. “Purimāni[T 2.0354], bhante, divasāni purimatarāni sabbaññū sabbadassāvī aparisesaṃ ñāṇadassanaṃ paṭijānamāno ‘carato ca me tiṭṭhato ca suttassa ca jāgarassa ca satataṃ samitaṃ ñāṇadassanaṃ paccupaṭṭhita’nti. So mayā paccupaṭṭhita”nti mayā (?) pubbantaṃ ārabbha pañhaṃ puṭṭho samāno aññenaññaṃ paṭicari, bahiddhā kathaṃ apanāmesi, kopañca dosañca appaccayañca pātvākāsi. Tassa mayhaṃ, bhante, bhagavantaṃyeva ārabbha sati udapādi – ‘aho nūna bhagavā, aho nūna sugato! Yo imesaṃ dhammānaṃ sukusalo’”ti. “Ko pana so, udāyi, sabbaññū sabbadassāvī aparisesaṃ ñāṇadassanaṃ paṭijānamāno ‘carato ca me tiṭṭhato ca suttassa ca jāgarassa ca satataṃ samitaṃ ñāṇadassanaṃ paccupaṭṭhita’nti, yo tayā pubbantaṃ ārabbha pañhaṃ puṭṭho samāno aññenaññaṃ paṭicari, bahiddhā kathaṃ apanāmesi kopañca dosañca appaccayañca pātvākāsī”ti? ‘Nigaṇṭho, bhante, nāṭaputto’ti.

271. “Then, Udāyī, let that very matter occur to you here, so that you may explain it to me.” “Some days ago, venerable sir, and even earlier, one who claimed to be all-knowing and all-seeing, professing complete knowledge and vision, said: ‘Whether I am walking or standing, sleeping or awake, knowledge and vision are constantly and uninterruptedly present to me.’ When asked a question by me concerning the past, he evaded the issue with another, diverted the talk to an external matter, and displayed anger, ill will, and displeasure. Then, venerable sir, mindfulness arose in me concerning the Blessed One: ‘Ah, indeed the Blessed One! Ah, indeed the Sugata, who is so skilled in these matters!’” “But who, Udāyī, was that one claiming to be all-knowing and all-seeing, professing complete knowledge and vision, saying: ‘Whether I am walking or standing, sleeping or awake, knowledge and vision are constantly and uninterruptedly present to me,’ who, when asked a question by you concerning the past, evaded the issue with another, diverted the talk to an external matter, and displayed anger, ill will, and displeasure?” “It was Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta, venerable sir.”

“Yo kho, udāyi, anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussareyya, seyyathidaṃ – ekampi jātiṃ dvepi jātiyo…pe… iti sākāraṃ sauddesaṃ anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussareyya, so vā maṃ pubbantaṃ ārabbha pañhaṃ puccheyya, taṃ vāhaṃ pubbantaṃ ārabbha pañhaṃ puccheyyaṃ; so vā me pubbantaṃ ārabbha pañhassa [M 2.0223] veyyākaraṇena cittaṃ ārādheyya, tassa vāhaṃ pubbantaṃ ārabbha pañhassa veyyākaraṇena cittaṃ [T 2.0355] ārādheyyaṃ.

“Udāyī, whoever were to recollect their manifold past lives—that is, one birth, two births… and so on… recollecting their manifold past lives with their aspects and details—they might ask me a question concerning the past, or I might ask them a question concerning the past. They might satisfy my mind with an explanation to a question concerning the past, or I might satisfy their mind with an explanation to a question concerning the past.

“Yo [V 2.0233] so (sī. pī.) kho, udāyi, dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena satte passeyya cavamāne upapajjamāne hīne paṇīte suvaṇṇe dubbaṇṇe sugate duggate yathākammūpage satte pajāneyya, so vā maṃ aparantaṃ ārabbha pañhaṃ [P 2.0032] puccheyya, taṃ vāhaṃ aparantaṃ ārabbha pañhaṃ puccheyyaṃ; so vā me aparantaṃ ārabbha pañhassa veyyākaraṇena cittaṃ ārādheyya, tassa vāhaṃ aparantaṃ ārabbha pañhassa veyyākaraṇena cittaṃ ārādheyyaṃ.

“Udāyī, whoever with the divine eye, which is purified and surpasses the human, were to see beings passing away and being reborn—inferior and superior, of good color and bad color, in a good destination and a bad destination—and were to understand beings as they fare according to their kamma, they might ask me a question concerning the future, or I might ask them a question concerning the future. They might satisfy my mind with an explanation to a question concerning the future, or I might satisfy their mind with an explanation to a question concerning the future.

“Api ca, udāyi, tiṭṭhatu pubbanto, tiṭṭhatu aparanto. Dhammaṃ te desessāmi – imasmiṃ sati idaṃ hoti, imassuppādā idaṃ uppajjati; imasmiṃ asati idaṃ na hoti, imassa nirodhā idaṃ nirujjhatī”ti.

“Furthermore, Udāyī, let the past be, and let the future be. I will teach you the Dhamma: When this is, that is. From the arising of this, that arises. When this is not, that is not. From the cessation of this, that ceases.”

“Ahañhi, bhante, yāvatakampi me iminā attabhāvena paccanubhūtaṃ tampi nappahomi sākāraṃ sauddesaṃ anussarituṃ, kuto panāhaṃ anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussarissāmi, seyyathidaṃ – ekampi jātiṃ dvepi jātiyo…pe… iti sākāraṃ sauddesaṃ anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussarissāmi, seyyathāpi bhagavā? Ahañhi, bhante, etarahi paṃsupisācakampi na passāmi, kuto panāhaṃ dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena satte passissāmi cavamāne upapajjamāne hīne paṇīte suvaṇṇe dubbaṇṇe sugate duggate yathākammūpage satte pajānissāmi, seyyathāpi bhagavā? Yaṃ pana maṃ, bhante, bhagavā evamāha – ‘api ca, udāyi, tiṭṭhatu pubbanto, tiṭṭhatu [T 2.0356] aparanto; dhammaṃ te desessāmi – imasmiṃ sati idaṃ hoti, imassuppādā idaṃ uppajjati; imasmiṃ asati idaṃ na hoti, imassa nirodhā idaṃ nirujjhatī’ti tañca pana me bhiyyosomattāya na pakkhāyati. Appeva nāmāhaṃ, bhante, sake ācariyake bhagavato cittaṃ ārādheyyaṃ pañhassa veyyākaraṇenā”ti.

Venerable sir, I am not able to recollect with their aspects and details even what I have experienced in this very life; how then could I recollect my manifold past lives—that is, one birth, two births... and so on... recollecting my manifold past lives with their aspects and details, as the Blessed One does? Venerable sir, at present I do not even see a dust-demon; how then could I, with the divine eye, which is purified and surpasses the human, see beings passing away and being reborn—inferior and superior, of good color and bad color, in a good destination and a bad destination—and understand beings as they fare according to their kamma, as the Blessed One does? And as for what the Blessed One said to me: 'Furthermore, Udāyī, let the past be, and let the future be. I will teach you the Dhamma: When this is, that is. From the arising of this, that arises. When this is not, that is not. From the cessation of this, that ceases'—even that is not especially clear to me. Perhaps, venerable sir, I might satisfy the Blessed One’s mind by answering a question in accordance with my own teacher’s doctrine.

272. “Kinti pana te, udāyi, sake ācariyake hotī”ti? “Amhākaṃ, bhante, sake ācariyake evaṃ hoti – ‘ayaṃ paramo vaṇṇo, ayaṃ paramo vaṇṇo’”ti.

272. “But what, Udāyī, is it in your own teacher's doctrine?” “Venerable sir, in our own teacher's doctrine, it is thus: ‘This is the supreme appearance, this is the supreme appearance.’”

“Yaṃ [M 2.0224] pana te etaṃ, udāyi, sake ācariyake evaṃ hoti – ‘ayaṃ paramo vaṇṇo, ayaṃ [V 2.0234] paramo vaṇṇo’ti, katamo so paramo vaṇṇo”ti? “Yasmā, bhante, vaṇṇā añño vaṇṇo uttaritaro vā paṇītataro vā natthi so paramo vaṇṇo”ti.

“Regarding that which in your own teacher's doctrine is thus, Udāyī: ‘This is the supreme appearance, this is the supreme appearance’—which is that supreme appearance?” “Venerable sir, that appearance from which there is no other appearance more excellent or more sublime, that is the supreme appearance.”

“Katamo pana so paramo vaṇṇo yasmā vaṇṇā añño vaṇṇo uttaritaro vā paṇītataro vā natthī”ti? “Yasmā[P 2.0033], bhante, vaṇṇā añño vaṇṇo uttaritaro vā paṇītataro vā natthi so paramo vaṇṇo”ti.

“Which, then, is that supreme appearance from which there is no other appearance more excellent or more sublime?” “Venerable sir, that appearance from which there is no other appearance more excellent or more sublime, that is the supreme appearance.”

“Dīghāpi kho te esā, udāyi, phareyya – ‘yasmā, bhante, vaṇṇā añño vaṇṇo uttaritaro vā paṇītataro vā natthi so paramo vaṇṇo’ti vadesi, tañca vaṇṇaṃ na paññapesi. Seyyathāpi, udāyi, puriso evaṃ vadeyya – ‘ahaṃ yā imasmiṃ janapade janapadakalyāṇī taṃ icchāmi, taṃ kāmemī’ti. Tamenaṃ evaṃ vadeyyuṃ – ‘ambho [T 2.0357] purisa, yaṃ tvaṃ janapadakalyāṇiṃ icchasi kāmesi, jānāsi taṃ janapadakalyāṇiṃ – khattiyī vā brāhmaṇī vā vessī vā suddī vā”ti? Iti puṭṭho ‘no’ti vadeyya. Tamenaṃ evaṃ vadeyyuṃ – ‘ambho purisa, yaṃ tvaṃ janapadakalyāṇiṃ icchasi kāmesi, jānāsi taṃ janapadakalyāṇiṃ – evaṃnāmā evaṃgottāti vāti…pe… dīghā vā rassā vā majjhimā vā kāḷī vā sāmā vā maṅguracchavī vāti… amukasmiṃ gāme vā nigame vā nagare vā’ti? Iti puṭṭho ‘no’ti vadeyya. Tamenaṃ evaṃ vadeyyuṃ – ‘ambho purisa, yaṃ tvaṃ na jānāsi na passasi, taṃ tvaṃ icchasi kāmesī’”ti? Iti puṭṭho ‘āmā’ti vadeyya.

“This speech of yours could become long, Udāyī, when you say, ‘Venerable sir, that appearance from which there is no other appearance more excellent or more sublime, that is the supreme appearance,’ and yet you do not make that appearance known. Suppose, Udāyī, a man were to say, ‘I desire, I long for the most beautiful woman in this land.’ They might say to him, ‘Good man, this most beautiful woman in the land whom you desire and long for, do you know if she is of the warrior caste, the brahmin caste, the merchant caste, or the worker caste?’ Being asked thus, he would say, ‘No.’ They might say to him, ‘Good man, this most beautiful woman in the land whom you desire and long for, do you know her name and clan? … whether she is tall, short, or of medium height; whether she is dark, golden-complexioned, or of a dull complexion? … in which village, town, or city she lives?’ Being asked thus, he would say, ‘No.’ They might say to him, ‘Good man, her whom you do not know and do not see, do you desire and long for her?’ Being asked thus, he would say, ‘Yes.’”

“Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, udāyi – nanu evaṃ sante, tassa purisassa appāṭihīrakataṃ bhāsitaṃ sampajjatī”ti? “Addhā kho, bhante, evaṃ sante tassa purisassa appāṭihīrakataṃ bhāsitaṃ sampajjatī”ti.

“What do you think, Udāyī? This being so, does not that man's speech turn out to be groundless?” “Certainly, venerable sir, this being so, that man's speech turns out to be groundless.”

“Evameva kho tvaṃ, udāyi, ‘yasmā, bhante, vaṇṇā añño vaṇṇo uttaritaro vā paṇītataro vā natthi so paramo vaṇṇo’ti vadesi, tañca vaṇṇaṃ na paññapesī”ti.

“In the very same way, Udāyī, you say, ‘Venerable sir, that appearance from which there is no other appearance more excellent or more sublime, that is the supreme appearance,’ and yet you do not make that appearance known.”

“Seyyathāpi, bhante, maṇi veḷuriyo subho jātimā aṭṭhaṃso suparikammakato paṇḍukambale [V 2.0235] nikkhitto bhāsate ca tapate ca virocati ca, evaṃ vaṇṇo attā hoti arogo paraṃ maraṇā”ti.

“Venerable sir, just as a beryl gem—lustrous, of fine quality, eight-faceted, well-polished—when placed on a pale woolen blanket, shines, glows, and is radiant, so too the self has such an appearance, being without disease after death.”

273. “Taṃ [M 2.0225] kiṃ maññasi, udāyi, yo vā maṇi veḷuriyo subho [T 2.0358] jātimā aṭṭhaṃso suparikammakato paṇḍukambale nikkhitto bhāsate [P 2.0034] ca tapate ca virocati ca, yo vā rattandhakāratimisāya kimi khajjopanako – imesaṃ ubhinnaṃ vaṇṇānaṃ katamo vaṇṇo abhikkantataro ca paṇītataro cā”ti? “Yvāyaṃ, bhante, rattandhakāratimisāya kimi khajjopanako – ayaṃ imesaṃ ubhinnaṃ vaṇṇānaṃ abhikkantataro ca paṇītataro cā”ti.

273. “What do you think, Udāyī? Between the beryl gem—lustrous, of fine quality, eight-faceted, well-polished, placed on a pale woolen blanket, which shines, glows, and is radiant—and the glowworm in the pitch-black darkness of night: of these two appearances, which is more beautiful and more sublime?” “Venerable sir, between these two appearances, the glowworm in the pitch-black darkness of night is the more beautiful and more sublime.”

“Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, udāyi, yo vā rattandhakāratimisāya kimi khajjopanako, yo vā rattandhakāratimisāya telappadīpo – imesaṃ ubhinnaṃ vaṇṇānaṃ katamo vaṇṇo abhikkantataro ca paṇītataro cā”ti? “Yvāyaṃ, bhante, rattandhakāratimisāya telappadīpo – ayaṃ imesaṃ ubhinnaṃ vaṇṇānaṃ abhikkantataro ca paṇītataro cā”ti.

“What do you think, Udāyī? Between the glowworm in the pitch-black darkness of night and the oil lamp in the pitch-black darkness of night: of these two appearances, which is more beautiful and more sublime?” “Venerable sir, between these two appearances, the oil lamp in the pitch-black darkness of night is the more beautiful and more sublime.”

“Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, udāyi, yo vā rattandhakāratimisāya telappadīpo, yo vā rattandhakāratimisāya mahāaggikkhandho – imesaṃ ubhinnaṃ vaṇṇānaṃ katamo vaṇṇo abhikkantataro ca paṇītataro cā”ti? “Yvāyaṃ, bhante, rattandhakāratimisāya mahāaggikkhandho – ayaṃ imesaṃ ubhinnaṃ vaṇṇānaṃ abhikkantataro ca paṇītataro cā”ti.

“What do you think, Udāyī? Between the oil lamp in the pitch-black darkness of night and a great mass of fire in the pitch-black darkness of night: of these two appearances, which is more beautiful and more sublime?” “Venerable sir, between these two appearances, the great mass of fire in the pitch-black darkness of night is the more beautiful and more sublime.”

“Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, udāyi, yo vā rattandhakāratimisāya mahāaggikkhandho, yā vā rattiyā paccūsasamayaṃ viddhe vigatavalāhake deve osadhitārakā – imesaṃ ubhinnaṃ vaṇṇānaṃ katamo vaṇṇo abhikkantataro [T 2.0359] ca paṇītataro cā”ti? “Yvāyaṃ, bhante, rattiyā paccūsasamayaṃ viddhe vigatavalāhake deve osadhitārakā – ayaṃ imesaṃ ubhinnaṃ vaṇṇānaṃ abhikkantataro ca paṇītataro cā”ti.

“What do you think, Udāyi? Between a great mass of fire in the pitch-black darkness of night and the morning star at dawn in a clear, cloudless sky—of these two splendors, which is more beautiful and more sublime?” “Venerable sir, between these two splendors, the morning star at dawn in a clear, cloudless sky is the more beautiful and more sublime.”

“Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, udāyi, yā vā rattiyā paccūsasamayaṃ viddhe vigatavalāhake deve osadhitārakā, yo vā tadahuposathe pannarase viddhe vigatavalāhake deve abhido abhide (ka. sī.), abhidosaṃ (ka.) abhidoti abhisaddena samānatthanipātapadaṃ (chakkaṅguttaraṭīkā mahāvagga aṭṭhamasuttavaṇṇanā) aḍḍharattasamayaṃ cando [V 2.0236] – imesaṃ ubhinnaṃ vaṇṇānaṃ katamo vaṇṇo abhikkantataro ca paṇītataro cā”ti? “Yvāyaṃ, bhante, tadahuposathe pannarase viddhe vigatavalāhake deve abhido [M 2.0226] aḍḍharattasamayaṃ cando – ayaṃ imesaṃ ubhinnaṃ vaṇṇānaṃ abhikkantataro ca paṇītataro cā”ti.

“What do you think, Udāyi? Between the morning star at dawn in a clear, cloudless sky, and the moon at midnight on the fifteenth day of the Uposatha in a clear, cloudless sky—of these two splendors, which is more beautiful and more sublime?” “Venerable sir, between these two splendors, the moon at midnight on the fifteenth day of the Uposatha in a clear, cloudless sky is the more beautiful and more sublime.”

“Taṃ [P 2.0035] kiṃ maññasi, udāyi, yo vā tadahuposathe pannarase viddhe vigatavalāhake deve abhido aḍḍharattasamayaṃ cando, yo vā vassānaṃ pacchime māse saradasamaye viddhe vigatavalāhake deve abhido majjhanhikasamayaṃ sūriyo – imesaṃ ubhinnaṃ vaṇṇānaṃ katamo vaṇṇo abhikkantataro ca paṇītataro cā”ti? “Yvāyaṃ, bhante, vassānaṃ pacchime māse saradasamaye viddhe vigatavalāhake deve abhido majjhanhikasamayaṃ sūriyo – ayaṃ imesaṃ ubhinnaṃ vaṇṇānaṃ abhikkantataro ca paṇītataro cā”ti.

“What do you think, Udāyi? Between the moon at midnight on the fifteenth day of the Uposatha in a clear, cloudless sky, and the sun at midday in the last month of the rains, during the autumn season, in a clear, cloudless sky—of these two splendors, which is more beautiful and more sublime?” “Venerable sir, of these two splendors, the sun at midday in the last month of the rains, during the autumn season, in a clear, cloudless sky is the more beautiful and more sublime.”

“Ato kho te, udāyi, bahū hi bahutarā devā ye imesaṃ candimasūriyānaṃ ābhā nānubhonti, tyāhaṃ [T 2.0360] pajānāmi. Atha ca panāhaṃ na vadāmi – ‘yasmā vaṇṇā añño vaṇṇo uttaritaro vā paṇītataro vā natthī’ti. Atha ca pana tvaṃ, udāyi, ‘yvāyaṃ vaṇṇo kiminā khajjopanakena nihīnataro hīnataro (sī. pī.) ca patikiṭṭhataro ca so paramo vaṇṇo’ti vadesi, tañca vaṇṇaṃ na paññapesī”ti. “Acchidaṃ acchira (ka.), acchida (?) bhagavā kathaṃ, acchidaṃ sugato katha”nti!

“Furthermore, Udāyi, there are indeed many, many more devas who do not experience the radiance of this moon and sun; I know them. And yet, I do not say: ‘There is no other splendor more surpassing or more sublime than that.’ But you, Udāyi, say: ‘This splendor, which is more base and more contemptible than a firefly, is the supreme splendor,’ and yet you do not make that splendor known.” “How wonderful is the Blessed One's discourse! How wonderful is the Well-Farer's discourse!”

“Kiṃ pana tvaṃ, udāyi, evaṃ vadesi – ‘acchidaṃ bhagavā kathaṃ, acchidaṃ sugato kathaṃ’”ti? “Amhākaṃ, bhante, sake ācariyake evaṃ hoti – ‘ayaṃ paramo vaṇṇo, ayaṃ paramo vaṇṇo’ti. Te mayaṃ, bhante, bhagavatā sake ācariyake samanuyuñjiyamānā samanuggāhiyamānā samanubhāsiyamānā rittā tucchā aparaddhā”ti.

“But why, Udāyi, do you say: ‘How wonderful is the Blessed One's discourse! How wonderful is the Well-Farer's discourse!’?” “Venerable sir, in our own teacher's doctrine, it is held thus: ‘This is the supreme splendor, this is the supreme splendor.’ But we, venerable sir, when questioned, cross-examined, and admonished by the Blessed One concerning our own teacher's doctrine, are found to be empty, void, and at fault.”

274. “Kiṃ panudāyi, atthi ekantasukho loko, atthi ākāravatī paṭipadā ekantasukhassa lokassa sacchikiriyāyā”ti? “Amhākaṃ, bhante, sake ācariyake evaṃ hoti – ‘atthi ekantasukho loko, atthi ākāravatī paṭipadā ekantasukhassa lokassa sacchikiriyāyā’”ti.

274. “But what of this, Udāyi, is there a world of exclusive happiness? Is there a practice with a valid method for the realization of a world of exclusive happiness?” “Venerable sir, in our own teacher's doctrine, it is held thus: ‘There is a world of exclusive happiness, and there is a practice with a valid method for the realization of a world of exclusive happiness.’”

“Katamā [V 2.0237] pana sā, udāyi, ākāravatī paṭipadā ekantasukhassa lokassa sacchikiriyāyā”ti? “Idha, bhante, ekacco pāṇātipātaṃ pahāya pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti, adinnādānaṃ pahāya adinnādānā paṭivirato [M 2.0227] hoti, kāmesumicchācāraṃ pahāya kāmesumicchācārā paṭivirato [P 2.0036] hoti, musāvādaṃ pahāya musāvādā paṭivirato hoti, aññataraṃ vā pana tapoguṇaṃ samādāya vattati. Ayaṃ kho sā, bhante, ākāravatī [T 2.0361] paṭipadā ekantasukhassa lokassa sacchikiriyāyā”ti.

“And what, Udāyi, is that practice with a valid method for the realization of a world of exclusive happiness?” “Here, venerable sir, a certain person, having abandoned the destruction of life, abstains from the destruction of life; having abandoned taking what is not given, abstains from taking what is not given; having abandoned sexual misconduct, abstains from sexual misconduct; having abandoned false speech, abstains from false speech; or else, having undertaken some form of austerity, one lives in accordance with it. This, venerable sir, is that practice with a valid method for the realization of a world of exclusive happiness.”

“Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, udāyi, yasmiṃ samaye pāṇātipātaṃ pahāya pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti, ekantasukhī vā tasmiṃ samaye attā hoti sukhadukkhī vā”ti? “Sukhadukkhī, bhante”.

“What do you think, Udāyi? At the time when one, having abandoned the destruction of life, abstains from the destruction of life, is the self at that time exclusively happy, or experiencing both happiness and suffering?” “Experiencing both happiness and suffering, venerable sir.”

“Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, udāyi, yasmiṃ samaye adinnādānaṃ pahāya adinnādānā paṭivirato hoti, ekantasukhī vā tasmiṃ samaye attā hoti sukhadukkhī vā”ti? “Sukhadukkhī, bhante”.

“What do you think, Udāyi? At the time when one, having abandoned taking what is not given, abstains from taking what is not given, is the self at that time exclusively happy, or experiencing both happiness and suffering?” “Experiencing both happiness and suffering, venerable sir.”

“Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, udāyi, yasmiṃ samaye kāmesumicchācāraṃ pahāya kāmesumicchācārā paṭivirato hoti, ekantasukhī vā tasmiṃ samaye attā hoti sukhadukkhī vā”ti? “Sukhadukkhī, bhante”.

“What do you think, Udāyi? At the time when one, having abandoned sexual misconduct, abstains from sexual misconduct, is the self at that time exclusively happy, or experiencing both happiness and suffering?” “Experiencing both happiness and suffering, venerable sir.”

“Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, udāyi, yasmiṃ samaye musāvādaṃ pahāya musāvādā paṭivirato hoti, ekantasukhī vā tasmiṃ samaye attā hoti sukhadukkhī vā”ti? “Sukhadukkhī, bhante”.

“What do you think, Udāyi? At the time when one, having abandoned false speech, abstains from false speech, is the self at that time exclusively happy, or experiencing both happiness and suffering?” “Experiencing both happiness and suffering, venerable sir.”

“Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, udāyi, yasmiṃ samaye aññataraṃ tapoguṇaṃ samādāya vattati, ekantasukhī vā tasmiṃ samaye attā hoti sukhadukkhī vā”ti? “Sukhadukkhī, bhante”.

“What do you think, Udāyi? At the time when one, having undertaken some form of austerity, lives in accordance with it, is the self at that time exclusively happy, or experiencing both happiness and suffering?” “Experiencing both happiness and suffering, venerable sir.”

“Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, udāyi, api nu kho vokiṇṇasukhadukkhaṃ paṭipadaṃ āgamma ekantasukhassa [V 2.0238] lokassa sacchikiriyā hotī”ti sacchikiriyāyāti (ka.)? “Acchidaṃ bhagavā kathaṃ, acchidaṃ sugato katha”nti!

“What do you think, Udāyi? Is it possible, by relying on a practice mixed with happiness and suffering, that there can be the realization of a world of exclusive happiness?” “How wonderful is the Blessed One's discourse! How wonderful is the Well-Farer's discourse!”

“Kiṃ pana tvaṃ, udāyi, vadesi – ‘acchidaṃ bhagavā kathaṃ, acchidaṃ sugato kathaṃ’”ti? “Amhākaṃ, bhante, sake ācariyake evaṃ hoti – ‘atthi ekantasukho loko, atthi ākāravatī paṭipadā ekantasukhassa lokassa [T 2.0362] sacchikiriyāyā’ti. Te mayaṃ, bhante, bhagavatā sake ācariyake samanuyuñjiyamānā samanuggāhiyamānā samanubhāsiyamānā rittā tucchā aparaddhā”ti aparaddhā (sī.), aparaddhāpi (syā. kaṃ. pī.).

“But why, Udāyi, do you say: ‘How wonderful is the Blessed One's discourse! How wonderful is the Well-farer's discourse!’?” “Venerable sir, in our own teacher's doctrine, it is held thus: ‘There is a world of exclusive happiness, and there is a practice with a method for the realization of a world of exclusive happiness.’ But we, venerable sir, when questioned, cross-examined, and interrogated by the Blessed One concerning our own teacher's doctrine, are found to be empty, void, and at fault.”

275. “Kiṃ [M 2.0228] pana, bhante, atthi ekantasukho loko, atthi ākāravatī paṭipadā ekantasukhassa lokassa sacchikiriyāyā”ti? “Atthi [P 2.0037] kho, udāyi, ekantasukho loko, atthi ākāravatī paṭipadā ekantasukhassa lokassa sacchikiriyāyā”ti.

275. “But, venerable sir, is there a world of exclusive happiness? Is there a practice with a method for the realization of a world of exclusive happiness?” “There is, Udāyi, a world of exclusive happiness, and there is a practice with a method for the realization of a world of exclusive happiness.”

“Katamā pana sā, bhante, ākāravatī paṭipadā ekantasukhassa lokassa sacchikiriyāyā”ti? “Idhudāyi, bhikkhu vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati; vitakkavicārānaṃ vūpasamā… dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati; pītiyā ca virāgā… tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati – ayaṃ kho sā, udāyi, ākāravatī paṭipadā ekantasukhassa lokassa sacchikiriyāyā”ti.

“And what, venerable sir, is that practice with a method for the realization of a world of exclusive happiness?” “Here, Udāyi, a monk, quite secluded from sensual pleasures… enters and dwells in the first jhāna… With the stilling of directed thought and evaluation… he enters and dwells in the second jhāna… With the fading away of rapture… he enters and dwells in the third jhāna. This, Udāyi, is that practice with a method for the realization of a world of exclusive happiness.”

“Na kiṃ nu (syā. kaṃ. ka.) kho sā, bhante, ākāravatī paṭipadā ekantasukhassa lokassa sacchikiriyāya, sacchikato hissa, bhante, ettāvatā ekantasukho loko hotī”ti. “Na khvāssa, udāyi, ettāvatā ekantasukho loko sacchikato hoti; ākāravatītveva sā paṭipadā ekantasukhassa lokassa sacchikiriyāyā”ti.

“Venerable sir, that is not the practice with a method for the realization of a world of exclusive happiness. For, venerable sir, by this much a world of exclusive happiness is realized for him.” “Indeed, Udāyi, a world of exclusive happiness is not realized for him by just this much; that practice with a method is for the realization of a world of exclusive happiness.”

Evaṃ [V 2.0239] vutte, sakuludāyissa paribbājakassa parisā unnādinī uccāsaddamahāsaddā ahosi – “ettha mayaṃ anassāma sācariyakā, ettha mayaṃ anassāma panassāma (sī.) sācariyakā! Na mayaṃ ito bhiyyo uttaritaraṃ pajānāmā”ti.

When this was said, the assembly of the wanderer Sakuludāyī became noisy, with loud and great sounds, saying: “In this, we are lost, together with our teacher! In this, we are lost, together with our teacher! We do not know anything higher or more sublime than this.”

Atha kho sakuludāyī paribbājako te paribbājake appasadde [T 2.0363] katvā bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “kittāvatā panāssa, bhante, ekantasukho loko sacchikato hotī”ti? “Idhudāyi, bhikkhu sukhassa ca pahānā…pe… catutthaṃ jhānaṃ… upasampajja viharati. Yā tā devatā ekantasukhaṃ lokaṃ upapannā tāhi devatāhi saddhiṃ santiṭṭhati sallapati sākacchaṃ samāpajjati. Ettāvatā khvāssa, udāyi, ekantasukho loko sacchikato hotī”ti.

Then the wanderer Sakuludāyī, having quieted those wanderers, said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, by what measure is the world of exclusive happiness realized for him?” “Here, Udāyi, a monk, with the abandoning of pleasure… enters and abides in the fourth jhāna. He associates with, converses with, and engages in discussion with those deities who have been reborn in a world of exclusive happiness. Indeed, Udāyi, by this measure the world of exclusive happiness is realized for him.”

276. “Etassa nūna, bhante, ekantasukhassa lokassa sacchikiriyāhetu bhikkhū bhagavati brahmacariyaṃ carantī”ti? “Na kho, udāyi, ekantasukhassa lokassa sacchikiriyāhetu bhikkhū mayi brahmacariyaṃ caranti. Atthi kho, udāyi[M 2.0229], aññeva dhammā uttaritarā ca paṇītatarā ca yesaṃ sacchikiriyāhetu bhikkhū mayi brahmacariyaṃ carantī”ti.

276. “Surely, venerable sir, it is for the sake of realizing this world of exclusive happiness that monks practice the holy life under the Blessed One?” “Not so, Udāyi, it is not for the sake of realizing the world of exclusive happiness that monks practice the holy life under me. Indeed, Udāyi, there are other states, higher and more sublime, for the sake of realizing which monks practice the holy life under me.”

“Katame [P 2.0038] pana te, bhante, dhammā uttaritarā ca paṇītatarā ca yesaṃ sacchikiriyāhetu bhikkhū bhagavati brahmacariyaṃ carantī”ti? “Idhudāyi, tathāgato loke uppajjati arahaṃ sammāsambuddho vijjācaraṇasampanno sugato lokavidū anuttaro purisadammasārathi satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavā…pe… so ime pañca nīvaraṇe pahāya cetaso upakkilese paññāya dubbalīkaraṇe vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati. Ayampi kho, udāyi, dhammo uttaritaro ca paṇītataro ca yassa sacchikiriyāhetu bhikkhū mayi brahmacariyaṃ caranti”.

“But what, venerable sir, are those states, higher and more sublime, for the sake of realizing which monks practice the holy life under the Blessed One?” “Here, Udāyi, a Tathāgata arises in the world, an Arahant, a Perfectly Enlightened One, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, a Fortunate One, Knower of the world, an unsurpassed trainer of persons to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, the Buddha, the Blessed One… He, having abandoned these five hindrances, which are defilements of the mind and weakeners of wisdom, secluded from sensual pleasures… enters and abides in the first jhāna. This too, Udāyi, is a state higher and more sublime, for the sake of realizing which monks practice the holy life under me.”

“Puna caparaṃ, udāyi, bhikkhu vitakkavicārānaṃ [T 2.0364] vūpasamā…pe… dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ… tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ… catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati. Ayampi kho, udāyi, dhammo uttaritaro ca paṇītataro ca yassa sacchikiriyāhetu bhikkhū mayi brahmacariyaṃ caranti.

“Furthermore, Udāyi, a monk, with the stilling of directed thought and evaluation… enters and abides in the second jhāna… the third jhāna… the fourth jhāna. This too, Udāyi, is a state higher and more sublime, for the sake of realizing which monks practice the holy life under me.”

“So [V 2.0240] evaṃ samāhite citte parisuddhe pariyodāte anaṅgaṇe vigatūpakkilese mudubhūte kammaniye ṭhite āneñjappatte pubbenivāsānussatiñāṇāya cittaṃ abhininnāmeti. So anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussarati, seyyathidaṃ – ekampi jātiṃ dvepi jātiyo…pe… iti sākāraṃ sauddesaṃ anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussarati. Ayampi kho, udāyi, dhammo uttaritaro ca paṇītataro ca yassa sacchikiriyāhetu bhikkhū mayi brahmacariyaṃ caranti.

“With his mind thus concentrated, purified, bright, unblemished, rid of defilements, pliable, workable, established, and having attained imperturbability, he directs his mind to the knowledge of the recollection of past lives. He recollects his manifold past lives, that is: one birth, two births… Thus, with their aspects and details, he recollects his manifold past lives. This too, Udāyi, is a state higher and more sublime, for the sake of realizing which monks practice the holy life under me.”

“So evaṃ samāhite citte parisuddhe pariyodāte anaṅgaṇe vigatūpakkilese mudubhūte kammaniye ṭhite āneñjappatte sattānaṃ cutūpapātañāṇāya cittaṃ abhininnāmeti. So dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena satte passati cavamāne upapajjamāne hīne paṇīte suvaṇṇe dubbaṇṇe sugate duggate…pe… yathākammūpage satte pajānāti. Ayampi kho, udāyi, dhammo uttaritaro ca paṇītataro ca yassa sacchikiriyāhetu bhikkhū mayi brahmacariyaṃ caranti.

“With his mind thus concentrated, purified, bright, unblemished, rid of defilements, pliable, workable, established, and having attained imperturbability, he directs his mind to the knowledge of the passing away and reappearance of beings. With the divine eye, which is purified and surpasses the human, he sees beings passing away and reappearing—inferior and superior, beautiful and ugly, fortunate and unfortunate… he understands beings as faring according to their kamma. This too, Udāyi, is a state higher and more sublime, for the sake of realizing which monks practice the holy life under me.”

“So evaṃ samāhite citte parisuddhe pariyodāte anaṅgaṇe vigatūpakkilese mudubhūte kammaniye ṭhite āneñjappatte āsavānaṃ khayañāṇāya [M 2.0230] cittaṃ abhininnāmeti[T 2.0365]. So ‘idaṃ dukkha’nti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, ‘ayaṃ dukkhasamudayo’ti…pe… ‘ayaṃ dukkhanirodho’ti… ‘ayaṃ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti… ‘ime āsavā’ti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, ‘ayaṃ āsavasamudayo’ti… [P 2.0039] ‘ayaṃ āsavanirodho’ti… ‘ayaṃ āsavanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti. Tassa evaṃ jānato evaṃ passato kāmāsavāpi cittaṃ vimuccati, bhavāsavāpi cittaṃ vimuccati, avijjāsavāpi cittaṃ vimuccati. Vimuttasmiṃ vimuttamiti ñāṇaṃ hoti. ‘Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti pajānāti. Ayampi kho, udāyi, dhammo uttaritaro ca paṇītataro ca yassa sacchikiriyāhetu bhikkhū mayi brahmacariyaṃ caranti. Ime kho, udāyi, dhammā uttaritarā ca paṇītatarā ca yesaṃ sacchikiriyāhetu bhikkhū mayi brahmacariyaṃ carantī”ti.

“With his mind thus concentrated, purified, bright, unblemished, rid of defilements, pliable, workable, established, and having attained imperturbability, he directs his mind to the knowledge of the destruction of the taints. He understands as it really is: ‘This is suffering.’ He understands as it really is: ‘This is the origin of suffering.’ He understands as it really is: ‘This is the cessation of suffering.’ He understands as it really is: ‘This is the path leading to the cessation of suffering.’ He understands as it really is: ‘These are the taints.’ He understands as it really is: ‘This is the origin of the taints.’ He understands as it really is: ‘This is the cessation of the taints.’ He understands as it really is: ‘This is the path leading to the cessation of the taints.’ For him, knowing thus and seeing thus, his mind is liberated from the taint of sensual desire, his mind is liberated from the taint of existence, and his mind is liberated from the taint of ignorance. When it is liberated, the knowledge arises: ‘It is liberated.’ He understands: ‘Birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this state of being.’ This too, Udāyi, is a state higher and more sublime, for the sake of realizing which bhikkhus practice the holy life under me. These, Udāyi, are the states, higher and more sublime, for the sake of realizing which bhikkhus practice the holy life under me.”

277. Evaṃ vutte, sakuludāyī paribbājako bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “abhikkantaṃ, bhante[V 2.0241], abhikkantaṃ, bhante! Seyyathāpi, bhante, nikkujjitaṃ vā ukkujjeyya, paṭicchannaṃ vā vivareyya, mūḷhassa vā maggaṃ ācikkheyya, andhakāre vā telapajjotaṃ dhāreyya – ‘cakkhumanto rūpāni dakkhantī’ti; evamevaṃ bhagavatā anekapariyāyena dhammo pakāsito. Esāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavantaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāmi dhammañca bhikkhusaṅghañca. Labheyyāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavato santike pabbajjaṃ, labheyyaṃ upasampada”nti.

277. When this was said, the wanderer Sakuludāyī said this to the Blessed One: “Excellent, venerable sir! Excellent, venerable sir! Just as, venerable sir, one might set upright what had been overturned, or reveal what was hidden, or show the way to one who was lost, or hold up an oil lamp in the darkness, so that ‘those with eyes will see forms’; even so has the Dhamma been made clear by the Blessed One in many ways. I, venerable sir, go to the Blessed One for refuge, to the Dhamma, and to the Saṅgha of bhikkhus. May I, venerable sir, receive the going forth in the presence of the Blessed One; may I receive the higher ordination.”

Evaṃ [T 2.0366] vutte, sakuludāyissa paribbājakassa parisā sakuludāyiṃ paribbājakaṃ etadavocuṃ – “mā bhavaṃ, udāyi, samaṇe gotame brahmacariyaṃ cari; mā bhavaṃ, udāyi, ācariyo hutvā antevāsīvāsaṃ vasi. Seyyathāpi nāma udakamaṇiko maṇiko (sī. pī. ka.) hutvā udañcaniko uddekaniko (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) assa, evaṃ sampadamidaṃ evaṃ sampadametaṃ (sī. pī.) bhoto udāyissa bhavissati. Mā bhavaṃ, udāyi, samaṇe gotame brahmacariyaṃ cari; mā bhavaṃ, udāyi, ācariyo hutvā antevāsīvāsaṃ vasī”ti. Iti hidaṃ sakuludāyissa paribbājakassa parisā sakuludāyiṃ paribbājakaṃ antarāyamakāsi bhagavati brahmacariyeti.

When this was said, the assembly of the wanderer Sakuludāyī said this to the wanderer Sakuludāyī: “Do not, Master Udāyi, lead the holy life under the ascetic Gotama. Do not, Master Udāyi, having been a teacher, live the life of a pupil. Just as a large water jar might become a small water scoop, so would this befall Master Udāyī. Do not, Master Udāyi, lead the holy life under the ascetic Gotama. Do not, Master Udāyi, having been a teacher, live the life of a pupil.” Thus the assembly of the wanderer Sakuludāyī created an obstacle for the wanderer Sakuludāyī regarding the holy life with the Blessed One.

Cūḷasakuludāyisuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ navamaṃ.

The Ninth, the Cūḷasakuludāyisutta, is concluded.

10. Vekhanasasuttaṃ

10. The Vekhanasa Sutta

278. Evaṃ [T 2.0367][M 2.0231][V 2.0242][P 2.0040] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Atha kho vekhanaso vekhanasso (sī. pī.) paribbājako yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhito kho vekhanaso paribbājako bhagavato santike udānaṃ udānesi – “ayaṃ paramo vaṇṇo, ayaṃ paramo vaṇṇo”ti.

278. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery. Then the wanderer Vekhanasa approached the Blessed One; having approached, he exchanged greetings with the Blessed One. Having concluded this courteous and memorable talk, he stood to one side. Standing to one side, the wanderer Vekhanasa uttered this inspired utterance in the presence of the Blessed One: “This is the supreme appearance! This is the supreme appearance!”

“Kiṃ pana tvaṃ, kaccāna, evaṃ vadesi – ‘ayaṃ paramo vaṇṇo, ayaṃ paramo vaṇṇo’ti? Katamo, kaccāna, so paramo vaṇṇo”ti?

“But why, Kaccāna, do you say, ‘This is the supreme appearance! This is the supreme appearance!’? What, Kaccāna, is that supreme appearance?”

“Yasmā, bho gotama, vaṇṇā añño vaṇṇo uttaritaro vā paṇītataro vā natthi so paramo vaṇṇo”ti.

“Venerable Gotama, that appearance than which there is no other appearance more excellent or more sublime, that is the supreme appearance.”

“Katamo pana so, kaccāna, vaṇṇo yasmā vaṇṇā añño vaṇṇo uttaritaro vā paṇītataro vā natthī”ti?

“But what, Kaccāna, is that appearance than which there is no other appearance more excellent or more sublime?”

“Yasmā, bho gotama, vaṇṇā añño vaṇṇo uttaritaro vā paṇītataro vā natthi so paramo vaṇṇo”ti.

“Venerable Gotama, that appearance than which there is no other appearance more excellent or more sublime, that is the supreme appearance.”

“Dīghāpi kho te esā, kaccāna, phareyya – ‘yasmā, bho gotama, vaṇṇā añño vaṇṇo uttaritaro vā paṇītataro vā natthi so paramo vaṇṇo’ti vadesi, tañca vaṇṇaṃ na paññapesi. Seyyathāpi, kaccāna, puriso evaṃ vadeyya – ‘ahaṃ yā imasmiṃ janapade [T 2.0368] janapadakalyāṇī, taṃ icchāmi taṃ kāmemī’ti. Tamenaṃ evaṃ vadeyyuṃ – ‘ambho purisa, yaṃ tvaṃ janapadakalyāṇiṃ icchasi kāmesi, jānāsi taṃ janapadakalyāṇiṃ – khattiyī vā brāhmaṇī vā vessī [V 2.0243] vā suddī vā’ti? Iti puṭṭho ‘no’ti vadeyya. Tamenaṃ evaṃ vadeyyuṃ – ‘ambho purisa, yaṃ tvaṃ janapadakalyāṇiṃ icchasi kāmesi, jānāsi taṃ janapadakalyāṇiṃ ‘evaṃnāmā evaṃgottāti vāti…pe… dīghā vā rassā vā majjhimā vā kāḷī vā sāmā vā maṅguracchavī vāti… amukasmiṃ gāme vā nigame vā nagare vā’ti? Iti puṭṭho ‘no’ti vadeyya. Tamenaṃ evaṃ vadeyyuṃ – ‘ambho purisa, yaṃ tvaṃ na jānāsi na passasi, taṃ tvaṃ icchasi kāmesī’”ti? Iti puṭṭho ‘āmā’ti vadeyya.

“Kaccāna, this would be a long drawn-out affair for you, that you say, ‘Venerable Gotama, that appearance than which there is no other appearance more excellent or more sublime, that is the supreme appearance,’ and yet you do not make that appearance known. Suppose, Kaccāna, a man were to say, ‘I desire and long for the most beautiful woman in this country.’ They might say to him, ‘Good man, this most beautiful woman in the country whom you desire and long for, do you know if she is a noblewoman, a brahmin, a merchant, or a commoner?’ Being asked thus, he would say, ‘No.’ They might say to him, ‘Good man, this most beautiful woman in the country whom you desire and long for, do you know her by such a name or such a clan? … whether she is tall, short, or of medium height; dark, golden-hued, or of a mottled complexion? … in such-and-such a village, town, or city?’ Being asked thus, he would say, ‘No.’ They might say to him, ‘Good man, do you desire and long for one whom you neither know nor see?’ Being asked thus, he would say, ‘Yes.’”

“Taṃ kiṃ [P 2.0041] maññasi, kaccāna, nanu evaṃ sante tassa purisassa appāṭihīrakataṃ bhāsitaṃ sampajjatī”ti? “Addhā kho, bho gotama, evaṃ sante tassa purisassa appāṭihīrakataṃ [M 2.0232] bhāsitaṃ sampajjatī”ti. “Evameva kho tvaṃ, kaccāna, ‘yasmā, bho gotama, vaṇṇā añño vaṇṇo uttaritaro vā paṇītataro vā natthi so paramo vaṇṇo’ti vadesi; tañca vaṇṇaṃ na paññapesī”ti. “Seyyathāpi, bho gotama, maṇi veḷuriyo subho jātimā aṭṭhaṃso suparikammakato paṇḍukambale nikkhitto bhāsate ca tapate ca virocati ca, evaṃ vaṇṇo attā hoti arogo paraṃ maraṇā”ti.

“What do you think, Kaccāna? In that case, does that man’s statement not become groundless?” “Certainly, Venerable Gotama, in that case that man’s statement becomes groundless.” “In the same way, Kaccāna, you say, ‘Venerable Gotama, that appearance than which there is no other appearance more excellent or more sublime, that is the supreme appearance,’ and yet you do not make that appearance known.” “Venerable Gotama, just as a beryl gem—beautiful, of fine quality, eight-faceted, well-worked, placed on a bright red woolen cloth—shines, glows, and radiates; of such an appearance is the self, healthy after death.”

279. “Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, kaccāna, yo vā maṇi veḷuriyo subho [T 2.0369] jātimā aṭṭhaṃso suparikammakato paṇḍukambale nikkhitto bhāsate ca tapate ca virocati ca, yo vā rattandhakāratimisāya kimi khajjopanako imesaṃ ubhinnaṃ vaṇṇānaṃ katamo vaṇṇo abhikkantataro ca paṇītataro cā”ti? “Yvāyaṃ, bho gotama, rattandhakāratimisāya kimi khajjopanako, ayaṃ imesaṃ ubhinnaṃ vaṇṇānaṃ abhikkantataro ca paṇītataro cā”ti.

279. “What do you think, Kaccāna? Between the beryl gem—beautiful, of fine quality, eight-faceted, well-worked, placed on a bright red woolen cloth, which shines, glows, and radiates—and the firefly in the pitch-dark night, which of these two appearances is more excellent and more sublime?” “Venerable Gotama, of these two appearances, that of the firefly in the pitch-dark night is more excellent and more sublime.”

“Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, kaccāna, yo vā rattandhakāratimisāya kimi khajjopanako, yo vā rattandhakāratimisāya telappadīpo, imesaṃ ubhinnaṃ vaṇṇānaṃ katamo vaṇṇo abhikkantataro ca paṇītataro cā”ti? “Yvāyaṃ, bho gotama, rattandhakāratimisāya telappadīpo, ayaṃ imesaṃ ubhinnaṃ vaṇṇānaṃ abhikkantataro ca paṇītataro cā”ti.

“What do you think, Kaccāna? Between the firefly in the pitch-dark night and an oil lamp in the pitch-dark night, which of these two appearances is more excellent and more sublime?” “Venerable Gotama, of these two appearances, that of the oil lamp in the pitch-dark night is more excellent and more sublime.”

“Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, kaccāna, yo vā rattandhakāratimisāya telappadīpo, yo vā rattandhakāratimisāya [V 2.0244] mahāaggikkhandho, imesaṃ ubhinnaṃ vaṇṇānaṃ katamo vaṇṇo abhikkantataro ca paṇītataro cā”ti? “Yvāyaṃ, bho gotama, rattandhakāratimisāya mahāaggikkhandho, ayaṃ imesaṃ ubhinnaṃ vaṇṇānaṃ abhikkantataro ca paṇītataro cā”ti.

“What do you think, Kaccāna? Between an oil lamp in the pitch-dark night and a great mass of fire in the pitch-dark night, which of these two appearances is more excellent and more sublime?” “Venerable Gotama, of these two appearances, that of the great mass of fire in the pitch-dark night is more excellent and more sublime.”

“Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, kaccāna, yo vā rattandhakāratimisāya mahāaggikkhandho, yā vā rattiyā paccūsasamayaṃ viddhe [P 2.0042] vigatavalāhake deve osadhitārakā, imesaṃ ubhinnaṃ vaṇṇānaṃ katamo vaṇṇo abhikkantataro ca paṇītataro cā”ti? “Yvāyaṃ, bho gotama, rattiyā paccūsasamayaṃ [T 2.0370] viddhe vigatavalāhake deve osadhitārakā, ayaṃ imesaṃ ubhinnaṃ vaṇṇānaṃ abhikkantataro ca paṇītataro cā”ti. “Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, kaccāna, yā vā rattiyā paccūsasamayaṃ viddhe vigatavalāhake deve osadhitārakā, yo vā tadahuposathe pannarase viddhe vigatavalāhake [M 2.0233] deve abhido aḍḍharattasamayaṃ cando, imesaṃ ubhinnaṃ vaṇṇānaṃ katamo vaṇṇo abhikkantataro ca paṇītataro cā”ti? “Yvāyaṃ, bho gotama, tadahuposathe pannarase viddhe vigatavalāhake deve abhido aḍḍharattasamayaṃ cando, ayaṃ imesaṃ ubhinnaṃ vaṇṇānaṃ abhikkantataro ca paṇītataro cā”ti. “Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, kaccāna, yo vā tadahuposathe pannarase viddhe vigatavalāhake deve abhido aḍḍharattasamayaṃ cando, yo vā vassānaṃ pacchime māse saradasamaye viddhe vigatavalāhake deve abhido majjhanhikasamayaṃ sūriyo, imesaṃ ubhinnaṃ vaṇṇānaṃ katamo vaṇṇo abhikkantataro ca paṇītataro cā”ti? “Yvāyaṃ, bho gotama, vassānaṃ pacchime māse saradasamaye viddhe vigatavalāhake deve abhido majjhanhikasamayaṃ sūriyo – ayaṃ imesaṃ ubhinnaṃ vaṇṇānaṃ abhikkantataro ca paṇītataro cā”ti. “Ato kho te, kaccāna, bahū hi bahutarā devā ye imesaṃ candimasūriyānaṃ ābhā nānubhonti, tyāhaṃ pajānāmi. Atha ca panāhaṃ na vadāmi – ‘yasmā vaṇṇā añño vaṇṇo uttaritaro ca paṇītataro [T 2.0371] ca natthī’ti. Atha ca pana tvaṃ, kaccāna, ‘yvāyaṃ vaṇṇo kiminā khajjopanakena nihīnataro ca patikiṭṭhataro ca so paramo vaṇṇo’ti vadesi; tañca vaṇṇaṃ na paññapesi”.

“What do you think, Kaccāna? Between a great mass of fire in the pitch-dark night and the morning star at dawn in a high, cloudless sky, which of these two appearances is more excellent and more sublime?” “Venerable Gotama, of these two appearances, that of the morning star at dawn in a high, cloudless sky is more excellent and more sublime.” “What do you think, Kaccāna? Between the morning star at dawn in a high, cloudless sky and the unblemished moon at midnight on the fifteenth Uposatha day in a high, cloudless sky, which of these two appearances is more excellent and more sublime?” “Venerable Gotama, of these two appearances, that of the unblemished moon at midnight on the fifteenth Uposatha day in a high, cloudless sky is more excellent and more sublime.” “What do you think, Kaccāna? Between the unblemished moon at midnight on the fifteenth Uposatha day in a high, cloudless sky and the unblemished sun at midday in the last month of the rains, in the autumn season, in a high, cloudless sky, which of these two appearances is more excellent and more sublime?” “Venerable Gotama, of these two appearances, that of the unblemished sun at midday in the last month of the rains, in the autumn season, in a high, cloudless sky is more excellent and more sublime.” “Furthermore, Kaccāna, there are many, many more devas who do not experience the radiance of this moon and sun, and I know them. And yet, I do not say: ‘There is no other appearance more excellent and more sublime than that.’ But you, Kaccāna, say: ‘This appearance, which is more inferior and more contemptible than a firefly, is the supreme appearance,’ and yet you do not make that appearance known.”

280. “Pañca kho ime, kaccāna, kāmaguṇā. Katame pañca? Cakkhuviññeyyā rūpā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṃhitā rajanīyā, sotaviññeyyā saddā…pe… ghānaviññeyyā gandhā… jivhāviññeyyā rasā… kāyaviññeyyā phoṭṭhabbā iṭṭhā [P 2.0043] kantā manāpā [V 2.0245] piyarūpā kāmūpasaṃhitā rajanīyā – ime kho, kaccāna, pañca kāmaguṇā. Yaṃ kho, kaccāna, ime pañca kāmaguṇe paṭicca uppajjati sukhaṃ somanassaṃ idaṃ vuccati kāmasukhaṃ. Iti kāmehi kāmasukhaṃ, kāmasukhā kāmaggasukhaṃ tattha aggamakkhāyatī”ti.

280. “There are, Kaccāna, these five strands of sensual pleasure. What five? Forms cognizable by the eye that are desirable, pleasing, charming, endearing, connected with sensual desire, and passion-arousing. Sounds cognizable by the ear… smells cognizable by the nose… tastes cognizable by the tongue… tactile objects cognizable by the body that are desirable, pleasing, charming, endearing, connected with sensual desire, and passion-arousing. These, Kaccāna, are the five strands of sensual pleasure. Now, Kaccāna, whatever happiness and joy arises in dependence on these five strands of sensual pleasure, this is called sensual happiness. Thus it is said: ‘From sensual pleasures, there is sensual happiness; from sensual happiness, there is the supreme desirable happiness, and that is declared as the highest.’”

Evaṃ vutte, vekhanaso paribbājako bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “acchariyaṃ, bho gotama, abbhutaṃ, bho gotama! Yāva subhāsitaṃ cidaṃ bhotā gotamena – ‘kāmehi kāmasukhaṃ, kāmasukhā kāmaggasukhaṃ tattha aggamakkhāyatī’ti. (‘Kāmehi, bho gotama, kāmasukhaṃ, kāmasukhā kāmaggasukhaṃ, tattha aggamakkhāyatī’ti) ( ) sī. syā. kaṃ. pī. potthakesu natthi – “dujjānaṃ kho etaṃ, kaccāna, tayā [M 2.0234] aññadiṭṭhikena aññakhantikena aññarucikena aññatrayogena aññatrācariyakena – kāmā kāmaṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) vā kāmasukhaṃ vā kāmaggasukhaṃ vā. Ye kho te, kaccāna, bhikkhū arahanto khīṇāsavā vusitavanto katakaraṇīyā ohitabhārā anuppattasadatthā parikkhīṇabhavasaṃyojanā sammadaññā vimuttā te kho [T 2.0372] etaṃ jāneyyuṃ – kāmā vā kāmasukhaṃ vā kāmaggasukhaṃ vā”ti.

When this was said, the wanderer Vekhanasa said this to the Blessed One: “It is wonderful, Venerable Gotama! It is amazing, Venerable Gotama! How well this has been spoken by the venerable Gotama: ‘From sensual pleasures, there is sensual happiness; from sensual happiness, there is the supreme desirable happiness, and that is declared as the highest.’ Venerable Gotama, I also say: ‘From sensual pleasures, there is sensual happiness; from sensual happiness, there is the supreme desirable happiness, and that is declared as the highest.’” The Blessed One then said: “Kaccāna, it is difficult for one such as you to know—who has a different view, a different preference, a different inclination, a different practice, and a different teacher—what sensual pleasures are, what sensual happiness is, or what the supreme desirable happiness is. But, Kaccāna, those bhikkhus who are Arahants, whose taints are destroyed, who have lived the holy life, done what was to be done, laid down the burden, attained their own true goal, whose fetters of existence are utterly destroyed, and who are liberated through right knowledge—they indeed would know what sensual pleasures are, what sensual happiness is, and what the supreme desirable happiness is.”

281. Evaṃ vutte, vekhanaso paribbājako kupito anattamano bhagavantaṃyeva khuṃsento bhagavantaṃyeva vambhento bhagavantaṃyeva vadamāno “samaṇo samaṇo ca (sī. pī.) gotamo pāpito bhavissatī”ti bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “evameva panidhekacce panidheke (sī. pī.), panimeke (uparisubhasutte) samaṇabrāhmaṇā ajānantā pubbantaṃ, apassantā aparantaṃ atha ca pana ‘khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyāti – pajānāmā’ti – paṭijānanti itthattāyāti paṭijānanti (pī.). Tesamidaṃ bhāsitaṃ hassakaṃyeva sampajjati, nāmakaṃyeva sampajjati, rittakaṃyeva sampajjati, tucchakaṃyeva sampajjatī”ti. “Ye kho te, kaccāna, samaṇabrāhmaṇā ajānantā pubbantaṃ[P 2.0044], apassantā aparantaṃ, ‘khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyāti – pajānāmā’ti – paṭijānanti; tesaṃ soyeva tesaṃ tesāyaṃ (sī.), tesaṃyeva so (?) sahadhammiko niggaho hoti. Api ca, kaccāna, tiṭṭhatu pubbanto, tiṭṭhatu aparanto. Etu viññū puriso asaṭho amāyāvī ujujātiko, ahamanusāsāmi ahaṃ dhammaṃ desemi. Yathānusiṭṭhaṃ tathā paṭipajjamāno yathānusiṭṭhaṃ paṭipajjamāno (?) nacirasseva sāmaññeva ñassati sāmaṃ dakkhiti – evaṃ kira sammā evaṃ kirāyasmā (syā. ka.) bandhanā vippamokkho hoti, yadidaṃ avijjā bandhanā. Seyyathāpi, kaccāna, daharo kumāro mando uttānaseyyako kaṇṭhapañcamehi bandhanehi baddho assa suttabandhanehi; tassa vuddhimanvāya indriyānaṃ paripākamanvāya [T 2.0373] tāni bandhanāni mucceyyuṃ; so mokkhomhīti kho jāneyya no ca bandhanaṃ[V 2.0246]. Evameva kho, kaccāna, etu viññū puriso asaṭho amāyāvī ujujātiko, ahamanusāsāmi, ahaṃ dhammaṃ desemi; yathānusiṭṭhaṃ tathā paṭipajjamāno nacirasseva sāmaññe ñassati[M 2.0235], sāmaṃ dakkhiti – ‘evaṃ kira sammā bandhanā vippamokkho hoti, yadidaṃ avijjā bandhanā’”ti.

281. When this was said, the wanderer Vekhanasa, having become angry and displeased, wishing to revile the Blessed One, wishing to disparage the Blessed One, and wishing to censure the Blessed One, thinking, 'I will make the ascetic Gotama out to be ignorant,' said this to the Blessed One: 'Just so, in this world, some ascetics and brahmins, not knowing the past, not seeing the future, nevertheless claim: “Birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this state of being—we know this.” For them, this statement becomes merely laughable, becomes merely a name, becomes merely empty, becomes merely void.' 'Indeed, Kaccāna, as for those ascetics and brahmins who, not knowing the past, not seeing the future, claim: “Birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this state of being—we know this”—for them, that itself is a rightful refutation. Furthermore, Kaccāna, let the past be, let the future be. Let an intelligent person come—one who is not fraudulent, not deceitful, of straightforward nature. I will instruct him, I will teach him the Dhamma. Practicing in accordance with the instruction, before long he will know for himself, he will see for himself: “Thus, it seems, is the right release from bondage, that is, from the bondage of ignorance.” Suppose, Kaccāna, a young, tender infant boy, lying on his back, were bound with five bonds including one at the neck, that is, with string bonds. As he grows and his faculties mature, those bonds would be released. He would know, “I am free,” but he would not know the bondage. Just so, Kaccāna, let an intelligent person come—one who is not fraudulent, not deceitful, of straightforward nature. I will instruct him, I will teach him the Dhamma. Practicing in accordance with the instruction, before long he will know for himself, he will see for himself: “Thus, it seems, is the right release from bondage, that is, from the bondage of ignorance.”'

Evaṃ vutte, vekhanaso paribbājako bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “abhikkantaṃ, bho gotama…pe… upāsakaṃ maṃ bhavaṃ gotamo dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṃ saraṇaṃ gata”nti.

When this was said, the wanderer Vekhanasa said this to the Blessed One: 'Excellent, Venerable Gotama! ... May the venerable Gotama remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge from this day forth for as long as life lasts.'

Vekhanasasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ dasamaṃ.

The Vekhanasa Sutta, the tenth, is concluded.

Paribbājakavaggo niṭṭhito tatiyo.

The Third Chapter on Wanderers is concluded.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary for that is:

Puṇḍarī-aggisaha-kathināmo, dīghanakho puna bhāradvājagotto;

Sandakaudāyimuṇḍikaputto, maṇiko tathākaccāno varavaggo.

Puṇḍarīka, Aggivacchagotta together with the one named Kaṭhina; then Dīghanakha, the one of the Bhāradvāja clan; Sandaka, Udāyi, the one of Muṇḍika's son; Maṇika, and likewise Kaccāna. This is the excellent chapter.

4. Rājavaggo

4. The Chapter on Kings

1. Ghaṭikārasuttaṃ

1. The Ghaṭikāra Sutta

282. [M 2.0236] Evaṃ [T 2.0374][V 2.0247][P 2.0045] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā kosalesu cārikaṃ carati mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ. Atha kho bhagavā maggā okkamma aññatarasmiṃ padese sitaṃ pātvākāsi. Atha kho āyasmato ānandassa etadahosi – “ko nu kho hetu, ko paccayo bhagavato sitassa pātukammāya? Na akāraṇena na akāraṇe (sī.) tathāgatā sitaṃ pātukarontī”ti. Atha kho āyasmā ānando ekaṃsaṃ cīvaraṃ uttarāsaṅga (syā. kaṃ.) katvā yena bhagavā tenañjaliṃ paṇāmetvā bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “ko nu kho, bhante, hetu, ko paccayo bhagavato sitassa pātukammāya? Na akāraṇena tathāgatā sitaṃ pātukarontī”ti. “Bhūtapubbaṃ, ānanda, imasmiṃ padese vegaḷiṅgaṃ vehaliṅgaṃ (sī.), vebhaligaṃ (syā. kaṃ.), vebhaliṅgaṃ (pī.) nāma gāmanigamo ahosi iddho ceva phīto ca bahujano ākiṇṇamanusso. Vegaḷiṅgaṃ kho, ānanda, gāmanigamaṃ kassapo bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho upanissāya vihāsi. Idha sudaṃ, ānanda, kassapassa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa ārāmo ahosi. Idha sudaṃ, ānanda, kassapo bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho nisinnako bhikkhusaṅghaṃ ovadatī”ti. Atha [T 2.0375] kho āyasmā ānando catugguṇaṃ saṅghāṭiṃ paññapetvā bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “tena hi, bhante, bhagavā nisīdatu ettha. Ayaṃ bhūmipadeso dvīhi arahantehi sammāsambuddhehi paribhutto bhavissatī”ti. Nisīdi bhagavā paññatte āsane. Nisajja kho bhagavā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi –

282. Thus have I heard. At one time, the Blessed One was journeying in the Kosalan country with a great Saṅgha of monks. Then the Blessed One, stepping aside from the road, showed a smile at a certain spot. Then this thought occurred to the Venerable Ānanda: “What, indeed, is the cause, what is the reason for the Blessed One’s showing a smile? The Tathāgatas do not show a smile without a reason.” Then the Venerable Ānanda, having arranged his upper robe over one shoulder and extending his joined palms toward the Blessed One, said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, what, indeed, is the cause, what is the reason for the Blessed One’s showing a smile? The Tathāgatas do not show a smile without a reason.” “Formerly, Ānanda, in this very spot, there was a market town named Vegaḷiṅga, which was prosperous, flourishing, populous, and teeming with people. Ānanda, the Blessed One Kassapa, the Arahant, the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One, dwelt depending on the market town of Vegaḷiṅga. Here, Ānanda, was the monastery of the Blessed One Kassapa, the Arahant, the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One. Here, Ānanda, the Blessed One Kassapa, the Arahant, the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One, being seated, would instruct the Saṅgha of monks.” Then the Venerable Ānanda, having spread out his outer robe folded in four, said this to the Blessed One: “If that is so, venerable sir, let the Blessed One be seated here. This plot of ground will have been used by two Arahants, Perfectly Self-Enlightened Ones.” The Blessed One sat down on the prepared seat. Having sat down, the Blessed One addressed the Venerable Ānanda:

“Bhūtapubbaṃ, ānanda, imasmiṃ padese vegaḷiṅgaṃ nāma gāmanigamo ahosi iddho ceva phīto ca bahujano ākiṇṇamanusso. Vegaḷiṅgaṃ kho, ānanda, gāmanigamaṃ kassapo bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho upanissāya vihāsi. Idha sudaṃ, ānanda, kassapassa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa [V 2.0248] ārāmo ahosi. Idha sudaṃ, ānanda, kassapo bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho nisinnako bhikkhusaṅghaṃ [P 2.0046] ovadati.

“Formerly, Ānanda, in this spot, there was a market town named Vegaḷiṅga, prosperous, flourishing, populous, and crowded with people. Ānanda, the Blessed One Kassapa, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, lived in dependence on the market town of Vegaḷiṅga. Right here, Ānanda, was the monastery of the Blessed One Kassapa, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One. Right here, Ānanda, the Blessed One Kassapa, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, while seated, used to instruct the Saṅgha of monks.”

283. “Vegaḷiṅge kho, ānanda, gāmanigame ghaṭikāro ghaṭīkāro (sī. pī.) nāma kumbhakāro kassapassa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa upaṭṭhāko ahosi [M 2.0237] aggupaṭṭhāko. Ghaṭikārassa kho, ānanda, kumbhakārassa jotipālo nāma māṇavo sahāyo ahosi piyasahāyo. Atha kho, ānanda, ghaṭikāro kumbhakāro jotipālaṃ māṇavaṃ āmantesi – ‘āyāma, samma jotipāla, kassapaṃ bhagavantaṃ arahantaṃ sammāsambuddhaṃ dassanāya upasaṅkamissāma. Sādhusammatañhi me tassa bhagavato dassanaṃ arahato sammāsambuddhassā’ti. Evaṃ vutte, ānanda, jotipālo māṇavo ghaṭikāraṃ kumbhakāraṃ etadavoca – ‘alaṃ, samma ghaṭikāra. Kiṃ pana tena muṇḍakena samaṇakena [T 2.0376] diṭṭhenā’ti? Dutiyampi kho, ānanda…pe… tatiyampi kho, ānanda, ghaṭikāro kumbhakāro jotipālaṃ māṇavaṃ etadavoca – ‘āyāma, samma jotipāla, kassapaṃ bhagavantaṃ arahantaṃ sammāsambuddhaṃ dassanāya upasaṅkamissāma. Sādhusammatañhi me tassa bhagavato dassanaṃ arahato sammāsambuddhassā’ti. Tatiyampi kho, ānanda, jotipālo māṇavo ghaṭikāraṃ kumbhakāraṃ etadavoca – ‘alaṃ, samma ghaṭikāra. Kiṃ pana tena muṇḍakena samaṇakena diṭṭhenā’ti? ‘Tena hi, samma jotipāla, sottisināniṃ sottiṃ sināniṃ (sī. pī.), sottisinānaṃ (syā. kaṃ. ka.) ādāya āhara (ka.) nadiṃ gamissāma sināyitu’nti. ‘Evaṃ sammā’ti kho, ānanda, jotipālo māṇavo ghaṭikārassa kumbhakārassa paccassosi. Atha kho, ānanda, ghaṭikāro ca kumbhakāro jotipālo ca māṇavo sottisināniṃ ādāya nadiṃ agamaṃsu sināyituṃ’.

283. “In the market town of Vegaḷiṅga, Ānanda, there was a potter named Ghaṭikāra who was the attendant, the chief attendant, of the Blessed One Kassapa, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One. The potter Ghaṭikāra, Ānanda, had a friend, a dear friend, the young man Jotipāla. Then, Ānanda, the potter Ghaṭikāra addressed the young man Jotipāla: ‘Come, friend Jotipāla, let us approach the Blessed One Kassapa, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, for a visit. For the sight of that Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, is deemed excellent by me.’ When this was said, Ānanda, the young man Jotipāla said this to the potter Ghaṭikāra: ‘Enough, friend Ghaṭikāra. What is the use of seeing that shaven-headed recluse?’ A second time, Ānanda… A third time, Ānanda, the potter Ghaṭikāra said this to the young man Jotipāla: ‘Come, friend Jotipāla, let us approach the Blessed One Kassapa, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, for a visit. For the sight of that Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, is deemed excellent by me.’ A third time, Ānanda, the young man Jotipāla said this to the potter Ghaṭikāra: ‘Enough, friend Ghaṭikāra. What is the use of seeing that shaven-headed recluse?’ ‘If that is so, friend Jotipāla, let us take bathing powder and string and go to the river to bathe.’ ‘So be it, friend,’ Ānanda, the young man Jotipāla replied to the potter Ghaṭikāra. Then, Ānanda, the potter Ghaṭikāra and the young man Jotipāla, having taken bathing powder and string, went to the river to bathe.”

284. “Atha kho, ānanda, ghaṭikāro kumbhakāro jotipālaṃ māṇavaṃ āmantesi – ‘ayaṃ, samma jotipāla, kassapassa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa avidūre ārāmo. Āyāma, samma jotipāla, kassapaṃ bhagavantaṃ arahantaṃ sammāsambuddhaṃ dassanāya upasaṅkamissāma. Sādhusammatañhi me tassa bhagavato dassanaṃ arahato sammāsambuddhassā’ti. Evaṃ vutte, ānanda, jotipālo māṇavo ghaṭikāraṃ kumbhakāraṃ etadavoca – ‘alaṃ, samma ghaṭikāra. Kiṃ pana tena [P 2.0047] muṇḍakena samaṇakena [T 2.0377] diṭṭhenā’ti? Dutiyampi kho, ānanda…pe… tatiyampi kho, ānanda, ghaṭikāro kumbhakāro jotipālaṃ māṇavaṃ etadavoca – ‘ayaṃ, samma jotipāla, kassapassa bhagavato [V 2.0249] arahato sammāsambuddhassa avidūre ārāmo. Āyāma, samma jotipāla, kassapaṃ bhagavantaṃ arahantaṃ sammāsambuddhaṃ dassanāya [M 2.0238] upasaṅkamissāma. Sādhusammatañhi me tassa bhagavato dassanaṃ arahato sammāsambuddhassā’ti. Tatiyampi kho, ānanda, jotipālo māṇavo ghaṭikāraṃ kumbhakāraṃ etadavoca – ‘alaṃ, samma ghaṭikāra. Kiṃ pana tena muṇḍakena samaṇakena diṭṭhenā’ti? Atha kho, ānanda, ghaṭikāro kumbhakāro jotipālaṃ māṇavaṃ ovaṭṭikāyaṃ parāmasitvā etadavoca – ‘ayaṃ, samma jotipāla, kassapassa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa avidūre ārāmo. Āyāma, samma jotipāla, kassapaṃ bhagavantaṃ arahantaṃ sammāsambuddhaṃ dassanāya upasaṅkamissāma. Sādhusammatañhi me tassa bhagavato dassanaṃ arahato sammāsambuddhassā’ti. Atha kho, ānanda, jotipālo māṇavo ovaṭṭikaṃ vinivaṭṭetvā viniveṭhetvā (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) ghaṭikāraṃ kumbhakāraṃ etadavoca – ‘alaṃ, samma ghaṭikāra. Kiṃ pana tena muṇḍakena samaṇakena diṭṭhenā’ti? Atha kho, ānanda, ghaṭikāro kumbhakāro jotipālaṃ māṇavaṃ sīsaṃnhātaṃ sasīsaṃ nahātaṃ (sī.), sīsanhātaṃ (syā. kaṃ.) kesesu parāmasitvā etadavoca – ‘ayaṃ, samma jotipāla, kassapassa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa avidūre ārāmo. Āyāma, samma jotipāla, kassapaṃ bhagavantaṃ arahantaṃ sammāsambuddhaṃ dassanāya upasaṅkamissāma[T 2.0378]. Sādhusammatañhi me tassa bhagavato dassanaṃ arahato sammāsambuddhassā’ti. Atha kho, ānanda, jotipālassa māṇavassa etadahosi – ‘acchariyaṃ vata, bho, abbhutaṃ vata, bho! Yatra hi nāmāyaṃ ghaṭikāro kumbhakāro ittarajacco samāno amhākaṃ sīsaṃnhātānaṃ kesesu parāmasitabbaṃ maññissati; na vatidaṃ kira orakaṃ maññe bhavissatī’ti; ghaṭikāraṃ kumbhakāraṃ etadavoca – ‘yāvatādohipi yāvetadohipi (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.), samma ghaṭikārā’ti? ‘Yāvatādohipi, samma jotipāla. Tathā hi pana me [P 2.0048] sādhusammataṃ tassa bhagavato dassanaṃ arahato sammāsambuddhassā’ti. ‘Tena hi, samma ghaṭikāra, muñca; gamissāmā’ti.

284. “Then, Ānanda, the potter Ghaṭikāra addressed the young man Jotipāla: ‘Friend Jotipāla, not far from here is the monastery of the Blessed One Kassapa, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One. Come, friend Jotipāla, let us approach the Blessed One Kassapa, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, for a visit. For the sight of that Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, is deemed excellent by me.’ When this was said, Ānanda, the young man Jotipāla said this to the potter Ghaṭikāra: ‘Enough, friend Ghaṭikāra. What is to be gained by seeing that shaven-headed ascetic?’ For a second time, Ānanda… And for a third time, Ānanda, the potter Ghaṭikāra said this to the young man Jotipāla: ‘Friend Jotipāla, not far from here is the monastery of the Blessed One Kassapa, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One. Come, friend Jotipāla, let us approach the Blessed One Kassapa, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, for a visit. For the sight of that Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, is deemed excellent by me.’ For a third time, Ānanda, the young man Jotipāla said this to the potter Ghaṭikāra: ‘Enough, friend Ghaṭikāra. What is to be gained by seeing that shaven-headed ascetic?’ Then, Ānanda, the potter Ghaṭikāra, having grasped the young man Jotipāla by his loincloth, said this: ‘Friend Jotipāla, not far from here is the monastery of the Blessed One Kassapa, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One. Come, friend Jotipāla, let us approach the Blessed One Kassapa, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, for a visit. For the sight of that Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, is deemed excellent by me.’ Then, Ānanda, the young man Jotipāla, having shaken off his loincloth, said this to the potter Ghaṭikāra: ‘Enough, friend Ghaṭikāra. What is to be gained by seeing that shaven-headed ascetic?’ Then, Ānanda, the potter Ghaṭikāra, having grasped by the hair the young man Jotipāla who had just washed his head, said this: ‘Friend Jotipāla, not far from here is the monastery of the Blessed One Kassapa, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One. Come, friend Jotipāla, let us approach the Blessed One Kassapa, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, for a visit. For the sight of that Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, is deemed excellent by me.’ Then, Ānanda, this thought occurred to the young man Jotipāla: ‘It is wonderful, sirs, it is astonishing, sirs! That this potter Ghaṭikāra, being of low birth, should think to grasp the hair of one of us who has just washed his head! Surely, I think, this will not be an inferior matter.’ He said this to the potter Ghaṭikāra: ‘To this extent, friend Ghaṭikāra?’ ‘To this extent, friend Jotipāla. For so it is that the sight of that Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, is deemed excellent by me.’ ‘In that case, friend Ghaṭikāra, let go; we shall go.’”

285. “Atha kho, ānanda, ghaṭikāro ca kumbhakāro jotipālo ca māṇavo yena kassapo bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā ghaṭikāro kumbhakāro kassapaṃ bhagavantaṃ arahantaṃ sammāsambuddhaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Jotipālo pana māṇavo kassapena [M 2.0239] bhagavatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho, ānanda, ghaṭikāro kumbhakāro kassapaṃ bhagavantaṃ arahantaṃ sammāsambuddhaṃ etadavoca – ‘ayaṃ me, bhante, jotipālo māṇavo sahāyo piyasahāyo. Imassa bhagavā dhammaṃ desetū’ti. Atha kho, ānanda, kassapo bhagavā [V 2.0250] arahaṃ sammāsambuddho ghaṭikārañca [T 2.0379] kumbhakāraṃ jotipālañca māṇavaṃ dhammiyā kathāya sandassesi samādapesi samuttejesi sampahaṃsesi. Atha kho, ānanda, ghaṭikāro ca kumbhakāro jotipālo ca māṇavo kassapena bhagavatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena dhammiyā kathāya sandassitā samādapitā samuttejitā sampahaṃsitā kassapassa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa bhāsitaṃ abhinanditvā anumoditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā kassapaṃ bhagavantaṃ arahantaṃ sammāsambuddhaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā pakkamiṃsu.

285. Then, Ānanda, the potter Ghaṭikāra and the young man Jotipāla approached the Blessed One Kassapa, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One. Having approached, the potter Ghaṭikāra paid homage to the Blessed One Kassapa, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, and sat down to one side. The young man Jotipāla, however, exchanged greetings with the Blessed One Kassapa, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One. After concluding the courteous and memorable talk, he sat down to one side. Seated to one side, Ānanda, the potter Ghaṭikāra said this to the Blessed One Kassapa, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One: ‘Venerable sir, this young man Jotipāla is my friend, my dear friend. May the Blessed One teach him the Dhamma.’ Then, Ānanda, the Blessed One Kassapa, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, instructed, inspired, enthused, and gladdened the potter Ghaṭikāra and the young man Jotipāla with a talk on the Dhamma. Then, Ānanda, the potter Ghaṭikāra and the young man Jotipāla, having been instructed, inspired, enthused, and gladdened by the Blessed One Kassapa, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, with a talk on the Dhamma, delighted in and rejoiced at the words of the Blessed One Kassapa, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One. Rising from their seats, they paid homage to the Blessed One Kassapa, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, and having circumambulated him keeping him to their right, they departed.

286. “Atha kho, ānanda, jotipālo māṇavo ghaṭikāraṃ kumbhakāraṃ etadavoca – ‘imaṃ nu tvaṃ, samma ghaṭikāra, dhammaṃ suṇanto atha ca pana agārasmā anagāriyaṃ na pabbajissasī’ti? ‘Nanu maṃ, samma jotipāla, jānāsi, andhe jiṇṇe mātāpitaro posemī’ti? ‘Tena hi, samma ghaṭikāra, ahaṃ agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajissāmī’ti. Atha kho, ānanda, ghaṭikāro ca kumbhakāro jotipālo ca māṇavo yena kassapo bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho tenupasaṅkamiṃsu[P 2.0049]; upasaṅkamitvā kassapaṃ bhagavantaṃ arahantaṃ sammāsambuddhaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu.
