Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho, ānanda, ghaṭikāro kumbhakāro kassapaṃ bhagavantaṃ arahantaṃ sammāsambuddhaṃ etadavoca – ‘ayaṃ me, bhante, jotipālo māṇavo sahāyo piyasahāyo. Imaṃ bhagavā pabbājetū’ti. Alattha kho, ānanda, jotipālo māṇavo [T 2.0380] kassapassa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa santike pabbajjaṃ, alattha upasampadaṃ.

286. Then, Ānanda, the young man Jotipāla said to the potter Ghaṭikāra: ‘Friend Ghaṭikāra, having heard this Dhamma, will you not go forth from the household life into homelessness?’ ‘Friend Jotipāla, do you not know that I support my blind and aged parents?’ ‘Well then, friend Ghaṭikāra, I will go forth from the household life into homelessness.’ Then, Ānanda, the potter Ghaṭikāra and the young man Jotipāla approached the Blessed One Kassapa, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One. Having approached, they paid homage to the Blessed One Kassapa, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, Ānanda, the potter Ghaṭikāra said to the Blessed One Kassapa, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One: ‘Venerable sir, this young man Jotipāla is my companion and dear friend. May the Blessed One ordain him.’ The young man Jotipāla, Ānanda, received the going forth in the presence of the Blessed One Kassapa, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One; he received the higher ordination.

287. “Atha kho, ānanda, kassapo bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho acirūpasampanne jotipāle māṇave aḍḍhamāsupasampanne vegaḷiṅge yathābhirantaṃ viharitvā yena bārāṇasī tena cārikaṃ pakkāmi. Anupubbena cārikaṃ caramāno yena bārāṇasī tadavasari. Tatra sudaṃ, ānanda, kassapo bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho bārāṇasiyaṃ viharati isipatane migadāye[M 2.0240]. Assosi kho, ānanda, kikī kāsirājā – ‘kassapo kira bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho bārāṇasiṃ anuppatto bārāṇasiyaṃ viharati isipatane migadāye’ti. Atha kho, ānanda, kikī kāsirājā bhadrāni bhadrāni yānāni yojāpetvā bhadraṃ bhadraṃ bhadraṃ (ka.) yānaṃ abhiruhitvā bhadrehi bhadrehi yānehi bārāṇasiyā niyyāsi mahaccarājānubhāvena mahaccā rājānubhāvena (sī.), mahatā rājānubhāvena (pī.) kassapaṃ bhagavantaṃ arahantaṃ sammāsambuddhaṃ dassanāya. Yāvatikā yānassa bhūmi yānena gantvā yānā paccorohitvā pattikova [V 2.0251] yena kassapo bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā kassapaṃ bhagavantaṃ arahantaṃ sammāsambuddhaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho, ānanda, kikiṃ kāsirājānaṃ kassapo bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho dhammiyā kathāya sandassesi samādapesi samuttejesi sampahaṃsesi. Atha kho, ānanda, kikī kāsirājā [T 2.0381] kassapena bhagavatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena dhammiyā kathāya sandassito samādapito samuttejito sampahaṃsito kassapaṃ bhagavantaṃ arahantaṃ sammāsambuddhaṃ etadavoca – ‘adhivāsetu [P 2.0050] me, bhante, bhagavā svātanāya bhattaṃ saddhiṃ bhikkhusaṅghenā’ti. Adhivāsesi kho, ānanda, kassapo bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho tuṇhībhāvena. Atha kho, ānanda, kikī kāsirājā kassapassa bhagavato sammāsambuddhassa adhivāsanaṃ viditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā kassapaṃ bhagavantaṃ arahantaṃ sammāsambuddhaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā pakkāmi. Atha kho, ānanda, kikī kāsirājā tassā rattiyā accayena sake nivesane paṇītaṃ khādanīyaṃ bhojanīyaṃ paṭiyādāpetvā paṇḍupuṭakassa paṇḍumuṭīkassa (sī. pī.), paṇḍumudikassa (syā. kaṃ.) sālino vigatakāḷakaṃ anekasūpaṃ anekabyañjanaṃ, kassapassa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa kālaṃ ārocāpesi – ‘kālo, bhante, niṭṭhitaṃ bhatta’nti.

287. Then, Ānanda, the Blessed One Kassapa, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, having stayed at Vegaḷiṅga for as long as he pleased, when the young man Jotipāla had been ordained for half a month, set out on a journey to Bārāṇasī. Traveling stage by stage, he arrived at Bārāṇasī. There, Ānanda, the Blessed One Kassapa, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, stayed in the deer park at Isipatana near Bārāṇasī. King Kikī of Kāsi heard: ‘The Blessed One Kassapa, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, has, it is said, arrived at Bārāṇasī and is staying in the deer park at Isipatana.’ Then, Ānanda, King Kikī of Kāsi had fine carriages harnessed, mounted a fine carriage, and with great royal majesty, he set out from Bārāṇasī with his fine carriages to see the Blessed One Kassapa, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One. He went as far as the carriage could go, then dismounted from the carriage and approached the Blessed One Kassapa, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, on foot. Having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One Kassapa, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, Ānanda, the Blessed One Kassapa, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, instructed, inspired, enthused, and gladdened King Kikī of Kāsi with a talk on the Dhamma. Then, Ānanda, King Kikī of Kāsi, having been instructed, inspired, enthused, and gladdened by the Blessed One Kassapa, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One with a talk on the Dhamma, said to him, ‘Venerable sir, may the Blessed One accept tomorrow’s meal from me together with the Sangha of bhikkhus.’ The Blessed One Kassapa, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, accepted in silence. Then, Ānanda, King Kikī, understanding the acceptance of the Blessed One Kassapa, the Perfectly Enlightened One, rose from his seat, paid homage to the Blessed One Kassapa, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, circumambulated him, and departed. When the night had passed, Ānanda, King Kikī had excellent food, both hard and soft, prepared in his own residence—rice of the sālī variety, dried in bundles and free of black grains, with many soups and many curries—and had the time announced to the Blessed One Kassapa, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One: ‘It is time, venerable sir, the meal is ready.’

288. “Atha kho, ānanda, kassapo bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya yena kikissa kāsirañño nivesanaṃ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi saddhiṃ bhikkhusaṅghena. Atha kho, ānanda, kikī kāsirājā buddhappamukhaṃ bhikkhusaṅghaṃ paṇītena khādanīyena bhojanīyena sahatthā santappesi sampavāresi. Atha [M 2.0241] kho, ānanda, kikī kāsirājā kassapaṃ bhagavantaṃ [T 2.0382] arahantaṃ sammāsambuddhaṃ bhuttāviṃ onītapattapāṇiṃ aññataraṃ nīcaṃ āsanaṃ gahetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho, ānanda, kikī kāsirājā kassapaṃ bhagavantaṃ arahantaṃ sammāsambuddhaṃ etadavoca – ‘adhivāsetu me, bhante, bhagavā bārāṇasiyaṃ vassāvāsaṃ; evarūpaṃ saṅghassa upaṭṭhānaṃ bhavissatī’ti. ‘Alaṃ, mahārāja. Adhivuttho me vassāvāso’ti. Dutiyampi kho, ānanda… tatiyampi kho, ānanda, kikī kāsirājā kassapaṃ bhagavantaṃ arahantaṃ sammāsambuddhaṃ etadavoca – ‘adhivāsetu me, bhante, bhagavā bārāṇasiyaṃ vassāvāsaṃ; evarūpaṃ saṅghassa upaṭṭhānaṃ bhavissatī’ti. ‘Alaṃ, mahārāja. Adhivuttho me vassāvāso’ti. Atha kho, ānanda, kikissa kāsirañño ‘na me kassapo bhagavā arahaṃ [P 2.0051] sammāsambuddho adhivāseti bārāṇasiyaṃ vassāvāsa’nti ahudeva aññathattaṃ[V 2.0252], ahu domanassaṃ. Atha kho, ānanda, kikī kāsirājā kassapaṃ bhagavantaṃ arahantaṃ sammāsambuddhaṃ etadavoca – ‘atthi nu kho, bhante, añño koci mayā upaṭṭhākataro’ti?

288. Then, Ānanda, the Blessed One Kassapa, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, having dressed in the morning, took his bowl and robe and went to the residence of Kikī, the king of Kāsi. Having approached, he sat down on the prepared seat together with the community of monks. Then, Ānanda, Kikī, the king of Kāsi, with his own hands served and satisfied the community of monks headed by the Buddha with excellent hard and soft food. Then, Ānanda, when the Blessed One Kassapa, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, had finished his meal and withdrawn his hand from the bowl, Kikī, the king of Kāsi, took a low seat and sat to one side. Seated to one side, Ānanda, Kikī, the king of Kāsi, said this to the Blessed One Kassapa, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One: ‘Venerable sir, may the Blessed One consent to spend the rains residence in Bārāṇasī; in this way there will be service to the Saṅgha.’ ‘Enough, great king. I have already consented to a rains residence.’ For a second time, Ānanda… For a third time, Ānanda, Kikī, the king of Kāsi, said this to the Blessed One Kassapa, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One: ‘Venerable sir, may the Blessed One consent to spend the rains residence in Bārāṇasī; in this way there will be service to the Saṅgha.’ ‘Enough, great king. I have already consented to a rains residence.’ Then, Ānanda, for Kikī, the king of Kāsi, because of the thought, ‘The Blessed One Kassapa, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, does not consent to my invitation to spend the rains residence in Bārāṇasī,’ there arose a change of mind, there arose displeasure. Then, Ānanda, Kikī, the king of Kāsi, said this to the Blessed One Kassapa, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One: ‘Venerable sir, is there anyone who is a greater supporter than I?’

“‘Atthi, mahārāja, vegaḷiṅgaṃ nāma gāmanigamo. Tattha ghaṭikāro nāma kumbhakāro; so me upaṭṭhāko aggupaṭṭhāko. Tuyhaṃ kho pana, mahārāja, na me kassapo bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho adhivāseti bārāṇasiyaṃ vassāvāsanti attheva atthi (sī. pī.) aññathattaṃ, atthi domanassaṃ. Tayidaṃ ghaṭikārassa kumbhakārassa ghaṭikāre kumbhakāre (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) natthi ca na ca bhavissati. Ghaṭikāro kho, mahārāja, kumbhakāro buddhaṃ saraṇaṃ gato, dhammaṃ saraṇaṃ [T 2.0383] gato, saṅghaṃ saraṇaṃ gato. Ghaṭikāro kho, mahārāja, kumbhakāro pāṇātipātā paṭivirato, adinnādānā paṭivirato, kāmesumicchācārā paṭivirato, musāvādā paṭivirato, surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā paṭivirato. Ghaṭikāro kho, mahārāja, kumbhakāro buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgato, dhamme aveccappasādena samannāgato, saṅghe aveccappasādena samannāgato, ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgato. Ghaṭikāro kho, mahārāja, kumbhakāro dukkhe nikkaṅkho, dukkhasamudaye nikkaṅkho, dukkhanirodhe nikkaṅkho, dukkhanirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāya nikkaṅkho. Ghaṭikāro kho, mahārāja, kumbhakāro ekabhattiko brahmacārī sīlavā kalyāṇadhammo. Ghaṭikāro kho, mahārāja, kumbhakāro nikkhittamaṇisuvaṇṇo apetajātarūparajato[M 2.0242]. Ghaṭikāro kho, mahārāja, kumbhakāro pannamusalo na sahatthā pathaviṃ khaṇati kumbhakāro na musalena na sahatthā paṭhaviṃ khaṇati (syā. kaṃ. pī.), kumbhakāro na musalena sahatthā pathaviñca khaṇati (ka.). Yaṃ hoti kūlapaluggaṃ vā mūsikukkaro mūsikukkuro (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) vā taṃ kājena āharitvā bhājanaṃ karitvā evamāha – “ettha yo icchati taṇḍulapaṭibhastāni taṇḍula pabhivattāni (sī. pī.) vā muggapaṭibhastāni vā kaḷāyapaṭibhastāni vā nikkhipitvā yaṃ icchati taṃ haratū”ti. Ghaṭikāro kho, mahārāja, kumbhakāro andhe jiṇṇe [P 2.0052] mātāpitaro poseti. Ghaṭikāro kho, mahārāja, kumbhakāro pañcannaṃ orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā opapātiko tattha parinibbāyī anāvattidhammo tasmā lokā.

‘There is, great king, a village-town named Vegaḷiṅga. There, there is a potter named Ghaṭikāra; he is my supporter, my chief supporter. But for you, great king, because of the thought, ‘The Blessed One Kassapa, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, does not consent to my invitation to spend the rains residence in Bārāṇasī,’ there is indeed a change of mind, there is displeasure. This does not exist for Ghaṭikāra the potter, nor will it ever exist. Ghaṭikāra the potter, great king, has gone for refuge to the Buddha, has gone for refuge to the Dhamma, has gone for refuge to the Saṅgha. Ghaṭikāra the potter, great king, abstains from the destruction of life, abstains from taking what is not given, abstains from misconduct in sensual pleasures, abstains from false speech, and abstains from liquor, wine, and intoxicants which are a cause for negligence. Ghaṭikāra the potter, great king, is endowed with unwavering confidence in the Buddha, endowed with unwavering confidence in the Dhamma, endowed with unwavering confidence in the Saṅgha, and is endowed with the virtues dear to the noble ones. Ghaṭikāra the potter, great king, is without doubt concerning suffering, without doubt concerning the origin of suffering, without doubt concerning the cessation of suffering, and without doubt concerning the path leading to the cessation of suffering. Ghaṭikāra the potter, great king, eats only one meal a day, practices the holy life, is virtuous, and of a lovely nature. Ghaṭikāra the potter, great king, has put aside gems and gold and has abstained from gold and silver. Ghaṭikāra the potter, great king, has laid down the pestle and does not dig the earth with his own hands. Whatever earth has crumbled from a bank or been dug up by mice, he brings it with a carrying pole, makes a vessel, and says this: “Let whoever wishes deposit here a measure of rice, or a measure of mung beans, or a measure of peas, and take whatever they wish.” Ghaṭikāra the potter, great king, supports his blind, aged parents. Ghaṭikāra the potter, great king, due to the complete destruction of the five lower fetters, is one of spontaneous rebirth, who will attain final Nibbāna there, not liable to return from that world.’

289. “‘Ekamidāhaṃ[T 2.0384], mahārāja, samayaṃ vegaḷiṅge nāma gāmanigame viharāmi. Atha khvāhaṃ, mahārāja, pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya yena ghaṭikārassa kumbhakārassa mātāpitaro tenupasaṅkamiṃ; upasaṅkamitvā ghaṭikārassa kumbhakārassa mātāpitaro etadavocaṃ – “handa, ko nu kho ayaṃ bhaggavo gato”ti? “Nikkhanto kho te, bhante, upaṭṭhāko antokumbhiyā odanaṃ gahetvā pariyogā sūpaṃ gahetvā paribhuñjā”ti. Atha khvāhaṃ, mahārāja, kumbhiyā [V 2.0253] odanaṃ gahetvā pariyogā sūpaṃ gahetvā paribhuñjitvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkamiṃ pakkāmiṃ (syā. kaṃ. pī.). Atha kho, mahārāja, ghaṭikāro kumbhakāro yena mātāpitaro tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā mātāpitaro etadavoca – “ko kumbhiyā odanaṃ gahetvā pariyogā sūpaṃ gahetvā paribhuñjitvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkanto”ti? “Kassapo, tāta, bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho kumbhiyā odanaṃ gahetvā pariyogā sūpaṃ gahetvā paribhuñjitvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkanto”ti? Atha kho, mahārāja, ghaṭikārassa kumbhakārassa etadahosi – “lābhā vata me, suladdhaṃ vata me, yassa me kassapo bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho evaṃ abhivissattho”ti. Atha kho, mahārāja, ghaṭikāraṃ kumbhakāraṃ aḍḍhamāsaṃ pītisukhaṃ na vijahati na vijahi (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.), sattāhaṃ mātāpitūnaṃ.

289. ‘At one time, great king, I was dwelling in a village-town named Vegaḷiṅga. Then, great king, in the morning, having dressed and taken my bowl and robe, I approached the parents of Ghaṭikāra the potter and said, “Well now, where has this Bhaggava gone?” “Venerable sir, your attendant has gone out. Please take rice from the rice-pot and soup from the curry-pot and eat.” Then, great king, I took rice from the rice-pot and soup from the curry-pot, ate, rose from my seat, and departed. Then, great king, Ghaṭikāra the potter approached his parents and asked, “Who took rice from the rice-pot and soup from the curry-pot, ate, and then rose from his seat and departed?” “Dear son, it was the Blessed One Kassapa, the Arahant, the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One, who took rice from the rice-pot and soup from the curry-pot, ate, and then rose from his seat and departed.” Then, great king, this thought occurred to Ghaṭikāra the potter: “It is a gain for me, indeed, a great gain for me, that the Blessed One Kassapa, the Arahant, the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One, is so very familiar with me.” Then, great king, joy and happiness did not leave Ghaṭikāra the potter for half a month, nor his parents for seven days.’

290. “‘Ekamidāhaṃ, mahārāja, samayaṃ tattheva vegaḷiṅge nāma gāmanigame viharāmi. Atha khvāhaṃ, mahārāja, pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya [T 2.0385] yena [M 2.0243] ghaṭikārassa kumbhakārassa mātāpitaro tenupasaṅkamiṃ; upasaṅkamitvā ghaṭikārassa kumbhakārassa mātāpitaro etadavocaṃ – “handa, ko nu kho ayaṃ bhaggavo gato”ti? “Nikkhanto kho te, bhante, upaṭṭhāko anto kaḷopiyā kummāsaṃ gahetvā pariyogā sūpaṃ gahetvā paribhuñjā”ti. Atha khvāhaṃ, mahārāja, kaḷopiyā kummāsaṃ gahetvā pariyogā sūpaṃ [P 2.0053] gahetvā paribhuñjitvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkamiṃ. Atha kho, mahārāja, ghaṭikāro kumbhakāro yena mātāpitaro tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā mātāpitaro etadavoca – “ko kaḷopiyā kummāsaṃ gahetvā pariyogā sūpaṃ gahetvā paribhuñjitvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkanto”ti? “Kassapo, tāta, bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho kaḷopiyā kummāsaṃ gahetvā pariyogā sūpaṃ gahetvā paribhuñjitvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkanto”ti. Atha kho, mahārāja, ghaṭikārassa kumbhakārassa etadahosi – “lābhā vata me, suladdhaṃ vata me, yassa me kassapo bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho evaṃ abhivissattho”ti. Atha kho, mahārāja, ghaṭikāraṃ kumbhakāraṃ aḍḍhamāsaṃ pītisukhaṃ na vijahati, sattāhaṃ mātāpitūnaṃ.

290. ‘At one time, great king, I was dwelling in that very same village-town named Vegaḷiṅga. Then, great king, in the morning, having dressed and taken my bowl and robe, I approached the parents of Ghaṭikāra the potter and said to them: “Well now, where has this Bhaggava gone?” “Venerable sir, your attendant has gone out. Please take barley cake from the basket and soup from the curry-pot and eat.” Then, great king, I took barley cake from the basket and soup from the curry-pot, ate, rose from my seat, and departed. Then, great king, Ghaṭikāra the potter approached his parents and asked them: “Who took barley cake from the basket and soup from the curry-pot, ate, rose from his seat, and departed?” “Dear son, it was the Blessed One Kassapa, the Arahant, the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One, who took barley cake from the basket and soup from the curry-pot, ate, rose from his seat, and departed.” Then, great king, this thought occurred to Ghaṭikāra the potter: “It is a gain for me, indeed, a great gain for me, that the Blessed One Kassapa, the Arahant, the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One, is so very familiar with me.” Then, great king, joy and happiness did not leave Ghaṭikāra the potter for half a month, nor his parents for seven days.’

291. “‘Ekamidāhaṃ, mahārāja, samayaṃ tattheva vegaḷiṅge nāma gāmanigame viharāmi. Tena kho pana samayena kuṭi gandhakuṭi (sī.) ovassati. Atha khvāhaṃ, mahārāja, bhikkhū āmantesiṃ – “gacchatha, bhikkhave, ghaṭikārassa kumbhakārassa nivesane tiṇaṃ jānāthā”ti. Evaṃ vutte, mahārāja, te [T 2.0386] bhikkhū maṃ etadavocuṃ – “natthi kho, bhante, ghaṭikārassa kumbhakārassa nivesane tiṇaṃ, atthi ca khvāssa āvesane [V 2.0254] āvesanaṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) tiṇacchadana” navacchadanaṃ (sī.) nti. “Gacchatha, bhikkhave, ghaṭikārassa kumbhakārassa āvesanaṃ uttiṇaṃ karothā”ti. Atha kho te, mahārāja, bhikkhū ghaṭikārassa kumbhakārassa āvesanaṃ uttiṇamakaṃsu. Atha kho, mahārāja, ghaṭikārassa kumbhakārassa mātāpitaro te bhikkhū etadavocuṃ – “ke āvesanaṃ uttiṇaṃ karontī”ti? “Bhikkhū, bhagini, kassapassa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa kuṭi ovassatī”ti. “Haratha, bhante, haratha, bhadramukhā”ti. Atha kho, mahārāja, ghaṭikāro kumbhakāro yena mātāpitaro tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā mātāpitaro etadavoca – “ke āvesanaṃ uttiṇamakaṃsū”ti? “Bhikkhū, tāta, kassapassa kira bhagavato [M 2.0244] arahato sammāsambuddhassa kuṭi ovassatī”ti. Atha kho, mahārāja, ghaṭikārassa kumbhakārassa etadahosi – “lābhā vata me, suladdhaṃ vata me, yassa me kassapo bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho evaṃ abhivissattho”ti. Atha kho, mahārāja ghaṭikāraṃ kumbhakāraṃ [P 2.0054] aḍḍhamāsaṃ pītisukhaṃ na vijahati, sattāhaṃ mātāpitūnaṃ. Atha kho, mahārāja, āvesanaṃ sabbantaṃ temāsaṃ ākāsacchadanaṃ aṭṭhāsi, na devotivassi na cātivassi (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.). Evarūpo ca, mahārāja, ghaṭikāro kumbhakāro’ti. ‘Lābhā, bhante, ghaṭikārassa kumbhakārassa, suladdhā, bhante, ghaṭikārassa kumbhakārassa yassa bhagavā evaṃ abhivissattho’”ti.

291. ‘At one time, great king, I was dwelling in that very same village-town named Vegaḷiṅga. At that time, my hut was leaking. Then, great king, I addressed the monks: ‘Go, monks, and find out about grass at the house of Ghaṭikāra the potter.’ When this was said, great king, those monks replied to me: ‘Venerable sir, there is no grass at the house of Ghaṭikāra the potter, but there is a grass roof on his workshop.’ ‘Go, monks, and un-thatch the workshop of Ghaṭikāra the potter.’ Then, great king, those monks un-thatched the workshop of Ghaṭikāra the potter. Then, great king, the parents of Ghaṭikāra the potter said to those monks: ‘Who is un-thatching the workshop?’ ‘It is the monks, sister. The hut of the Blessed One Kassapa, the Arahant, the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One, is leaking.’ ‘Take it, venerable sirs, take it, good sirs.’ Then, great king, Ghaṭikāra the potter approached his parents and asked: ‘Who un-thatched the workshop?’ ‘Dear son, it is said the monks did; the hut of the Blessed One Kassapa, the Arahant, the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One, is leaking.’ Then, great king, this thought occurred to Ghaṭikāra the potter: ‘It is a gain for me, indeed, a great gain for me, that the Blessed One Kassapa, the Arahant, the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One, is so very familiar with me!’ Then, great king, joy and happiness did not leave Ghaṭikāra the potter for half a month, nor his parents for seven days. And, great king, that entire workshop remained with the sky for its roof for three months, and the god did not rain upon it. Such, great king, was Ghaṭikāra the potter.’ ‘It is a gain, venerable sir, for Ghaṭikāra the potter, a great good fortune, venerable sir, for Ghaṭikāra the potter, that the Blessed One is so very familiar with him!’

292. “Atha [T 2.0387] kho, ānanda, kikī kāsirājā ghaṭikārassa kumbhakārassa pañcamattāni taṇḍulavāhasatāni pāhesi paṇḍupuṭakassa sālino tadupiyañca sūpeyyaṃ. Atha kho te, ānanda, rājapurisā ghaṭikāraṃ kumbhakāraṃ upasaṅkamitvā etadavocuṃ – ‘imāni kho, bhante, pañcamattāni taṇḍulavāhasatāni kikinā kāsirājena pahitāni paṇḍupuṭakassa sālino tadupiyañca sūpeyyaṃ. Tāni, bhante, paṭiggaṇhathā’ti patiggaṇhātūti (sī. pī.), paṭiggaṇhātūti (syā. kaṃ.). ‘Rājā kho bahukicco bahukaraṇīyo. Alaṃ me! Raññova hotū’ti. Siyā kho pana te, ānanda, evamassa – ‘añño nūna tena samayena jotipālo māṇavo ahosī’ti. Na kho panetaṃ, ānanda, evaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ. Ahaṃ tena samayena jotipālo māṇavo ahosi”nti.

292. Then, Ānanda, King Kikī of Kāsī sent to Ghaṭikāra the potter five hundred cartloads of Sāli rice, dried in bundles, and suitable side dishes. Then, Ānanda, those royal men approached Ghaṭikāra the potter and said this: ‘Venerable sir, these five hundred cartloads of Sāli rice, dried in bundles, and suitable side dishes have been sent by King Kikī of Kāsī. Venerable sir, please accept them.’ ‘The king has many duties and many things to do. Enough for me! Let it be for the king himself.’ It might occur to you, Ānanda: ‘Surely, at that time, the young man Jotipāla was someone else?’ But it should not be seen like this, Ānanda. At that time, I myself was the young man Jotipāla.

Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamano āyasmā ānando bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandīti.

Thus spoke the Blessed One. The Venerable Ānanda, pleased, rejoiced at the Blessed One's words.

Ghaṭikārasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ paṭhamaṃ.

The first Ghaṭikāra Sutta is concluded.

2. Raṭṭhapālasuttaṃ

2. The Raṭṭhapāla Sutta

293. Evaṃ [T 2.0388][V 2.0255] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā kurūsu cārikaṃ caramāno mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ yena thullakoṭṭhikaṃ thūlakoṭṭhikaṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) nāma kurūnaṃ nigamo tadavasari. Assosuṃ kho thullakoṭṭhikā thūlakoṭṭhitakā (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) brāhmaṇagahapatikā – “samaṇo [M 2.0245] khalu, bho, gotamo sakyaputto sakyakulā pabbajito kurūsu cārikaṃ [P 2.0055] caramāno mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ thullakoṭṭhikaṃ anuppatto. Taṃ kho pana bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ evaṃ kalyāṇo kittisaddo abbhuggato – ‘itipi so bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho vijjācaraṇasampanno sugato lokavidū anuttaro purisadammasārathi satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavā’ti. So imaṃ lokaṃ sadevakaṃ samārakaṃ sabrahmakaṃ sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiṃ pajaṃ sadevamanussaṃ sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā pavedeti. So dhammaṃ deseti ādikalyāṇaṃ majjhekalyāṇaṃ pariyosānakalyāṇaṃ sātthaṃ sabyañjanaṃ, kevalaparipuṇṇaṃ parisuddhaṃ brahmacariyaṃ pakāseti. Sādhu kho pana tathārūpānaṃ arahataṃ dassanaṃ hotī”ti. Atha kho thullakoṭṭhikā brāhmaṇagahapatikā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā appekacce bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu; appekacce bhagavatā saddhiṃ sammodiṃsu, sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu; appekacce yena bhagavā tenañjaliṃ paṇāmetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu; appekacce [T 2.0389] bhagavato santike nāmagottaṃ sāvetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu; appekacce tuṇhībhūtā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Ekamantaṃ nisinne kho thullakoṭṭhike brāhmaṇagahapatike bhagavā dhammiyā kathāya sandassesi samādapesi samuttejesi sampahaṃsesi.

293. Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One was wandering on tour in the Kuru country with a large Saṅgha of bhikkhus when he arrived at Thullakoṭṭhika, a market town of the Kurus. The brahmin householders of Thullakoṭṭhika heard: “It is said that the ascetic Gotama, the Sakyan son who went forth from the Sakyan clan, while wandering on tour in the Kuru country with a large Saṅgha of bhikkhus, has arrived at Thullakoṭṭhika. A good report of that Blessed Gotama has spread far and wide: ‘That Blessed One is an arahant, a perfectly enlightened one, perfect in knowledge and conduct, a sublime one, a knower of the worlds, an unsurpassed guide for those who wish to be trained, a teacher of gods and humans, an enlightened one, a blessed one.’ He makes known this world with its gods, its Māras, and its Brahmās, this generation with its ascetics and brahmins, with its gods and humans, having realized it himself through direct knowledge. He teaches the Dhamma that is good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, with its meaning and its phrasing; he proclaims the holy life, which is utterly complete and pure. It is good to see such arahants.” Then the brahmin householders of Thullakoṭṭhika went to the Blessed One. Having approached, some paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Some exchanged greetings with the Blessed One, and after concluding their friendly and memorable conversation, sat down to one side. Some raised their joined hands in salutation toward the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Some announced their name and clan in the Blessed One’s presence and sat down to one side. Some, remaining silent, sat down to one side. The Blessed One instructed, roused, inspired, and gladdened the brahmin householders of Thullakoṭṭhika, who were sitting to one side, with a talk on the Dhamma.

294. Tena kho pana samayena raṭṭhapālo nāma kulaputto tasmiṃyeva thullakoṭṭhike aggakulassa aggakulikassa (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) putto tissaṃ parisāyaṃ nisinno hoti. Atha kho raṭṭhapālassa kulaputtassa etadahosi – “yathā yathā khvāhaṃ bhagavatā dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānāmi yathā yathā kho bhagavā dhammaṃ deseti (sī.), nayidaṃ sukaraṃ agāraṃ ajjhāvasatā ekantaparipuṇṇaṃ ekantaparisuddhaṃ saṅkhalikhitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ carituṃ. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ kesamassuṃ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajeyya”nti. Atha kho thullakoṭṭhikā brāhmaṇagahapatikā bhagavatā dhammiyā kathāya sandassitā samādapitā samuttejitā sampahaṃsitā [V 2.0256] bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinanditvā anumoditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā [P 2.0056] bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā pakkamiṃsu. Atha kho raṭṭhapālo kulaputto acirapakkantesu thullakoṭṭhikesu [M 2.0246] brāhmaṇagahapatikesu yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho raṭṭhapālo kulaputto bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “yathā yathāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavatā dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānāmi, nayidaṃ sukaraṃ agāraṃ ajjhāvasatā ekantaparipuṇṇaṃ ekantaparisuddhaṃ saṅkhalikhitaṃ [T 2.0390] brahmacariyaṃ carituṃ. Icchāmahaṃ, bhante, kesamassuṃ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajituṃ. Labheyyāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavato santike pabbajjaṃ, labheyyaṃ upasampadaṃ. Pabbājetu maṃ bhagavā”ti ettha “labheyyāhaṃ…pe… upasampadaṃ”ti vākyadvayaṃ sabbesupi mūlapotthakesu dissati, pārājikapāḷiyaṃ pana sudinnabhāṇavāre etaṃ natthi. “pabbājetu maṃ bhagavā”ti idaṃ pana vākyaṃ marammapotthake yeva dissati, pārājikapāḷiyañca tadeva atthi. “Anuññātosi pana tvaṃ, raṭṭhapāla, mātāpitūhi agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajjāyā”ti? “Na khohaṃ, bhante, anuññāto mātāpitūhi agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajjāyā”ti. “Na kho, raṭṭhapāla, tathāgatā ananuññātaṃ mātāpitūhi puttaṃ pabbājentī”ti. “Svāhaṃ, bhante, tathā karissāmi yathā maṃ mātāpitaro anujānissanti agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajjāyā”ti.

294. Now at that time a clansman named Raṭṭhapāla, the son of the foremost family in that same Thullakoṭṭhika, was sitting in the assembly. Then Raṭṭhapāla the clansman thought: "As I understand the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One, it is not easy for one living at home to lead the perfectly complete, perfectly pure holy life, bright as a polished conch. What if I were to shave off my hair and beard, put on the saffron robes, and go forth from the household life into homelessness?" Then the brahmin householders of Thullakoṭṭhika, having been instructed, encouraged, roused, and gladdened by the Blessed One with a Dhamma talk, rejoiced in and approved of the Blessed One’s statement. They rose from their seats, paid homage to the Blessed One, circumambulated him with their right side towards him, and departed. Then, not long after the brahmin householders of Thullakoṭṭhika had departed, Raṭṭhapāla the clansman approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Sitting to one side, Raṭṭhapāla the clansman said to the Blessed One: "As I understand the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One, venerable sir, it is not easy for one living at home to lead the perfectly complete, perfectly pure holy life, bright as a polished conch. I wish, venerable sir, to shave off my hair and beard, put on the saffron robes, and go forth from the household life into homelessness. May I receive the going forth in the Blessed One’s presence, may I receive the full ordination. Let the Blessed One give me the going forth." "But, Raṭṭhapāla, have you obtained permission from your parents to go forth from the household life into homelessness?" "No, venerable sir, I have not obtained permission from my parents to go forth from the household life into homelessness." "Raṭṭhapāla, the Tathāgatas do not give the going forth to a son whose parents have not given their permission." "Then, venerable sir, I will act in such a way that my parents will give me permission to go forth from the household life into homelessness."

295. Atha kho raṭṭhapālo kulaputto uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā yena mātāpitaro tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā mātāpitaro etadavoca – “ammatātā, yathā yathāhaṃ bhagavatā dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānāmi, nayidaṃ sukaraṃ agāraṃ ajjhāvasatā ekantaparipuṇṇaṃ ekantaparisuddhaṃ saṅkhalikhitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ carituṃ. Icchāmahaṃ kesamassuṃ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajituṃ. Anujānātha maṃ agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajjāyā”ti. Evaṃ vutte, raṭṭhapālassa kulaputtassa mātāpitaro raṭṭhapālaṃ kulaputtaṃ etadavocuṃ – “tvaṃ khosi, tāta raṭṭhapāla, amhākaṃ ekaputtako piyo manāpo sukhedhito sukhaparibhato sukhaparihato (syā. kaṃ. ka.) (ehi tvaṃ tāta raṭṭhapāla bhuñja ca piva ca paricāre hi ca, bhuñjanto pivanto paricārento kāme paribhuñjanto puññāni karonto abhiramassu, na taṃ mayaṃ anujānāma agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajjāya,) sabbattha dissati, sudinnakaṇḍe pana natthi, aṭṭhakathāsupi na dassitaṃ. Na tvaṃ, tāta raṭṭhapāla[T 2.0391], kassaci dukkhassa jānāsi. Maraṇenapi [P 2.0057] te mayaṃ akāmakā vinā bhavissāma. Kiṃ pana mayaṃ [M 2.0247] taṃ jīvantaṃ anujānissāma agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajjāyā”ti? Dutiyampi kho raṭṭhapālo kulaputto…pe… tatiyampi kho raṭṭhapālo kulaputto mātāpitaro etadavoca – “ammatātā, yathā yathāhaṃ bhagavatā dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānāmi, nayidaṃ sukaraṃ agāraṃ ajjhāvasatā ekantaparipuṇṇaṃ ekantaparisuddhaṃ saṅkhalikhitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ carituṃ. Icchāmahaṃ kesamassuṃ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajituṃ. Anujānātha maṃ agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajjāyā”ti. Tatiyampi kho [V 2.0257] raṭṭhapālassa kulaputtassa mātāpitaro raṭṭhapālaṃ kulaputtaṃ etadavocuṃ – “tvaṃ khosi, tāta raṭṭhapāla, amhākaṃ ekaputtako piyo manāpo sukhedhito sukhaparibhato. Na tvaṃ, tāta raṭṭhapāla, kassaci dukkhassa jānāsi. Maraṇenapi te mayaṃ akāmakā vinā bhavissāma. Kiṃ pana mayaṃ taṃ jīvantaṃ anujānissāma [T 2.0392] agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajjāyā”ti?

295. Then the clansman Raṭṭhapāla rose from his seat, paid homage to the Blessed One, circumambulated him keeping his right side toward him, and approached his parents. Having approached, he said this to his parents: “Mother, Father, as I understand the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One, it is not easy for one living at home to lead the holy life that is utterly complete, utterly pure, like a polished conch shell. I wish to shave off my hair and beard, put on the ochre robes, and go forth from the household life into homelessness. Permit me to go forth from the household life into homelessness.” When this was said, the parents of the clansman Raṭṭhapāla said this to the clansman Raṭṭhapāla: “Dear Raṭṭhapāla, you are our only son, dear and beloved, raised in comfort, brought up in comfort. You, dear Raṭṭhapāla, do not know of any suffering. Even by death, we will be separated from you against our will. How then could we, while you are living, permit you to go forth from the household life into homelessness?” A second time, the clansman Raṭṭhapāla… and a third time, the clansman Raṭṭhapāla said this to his parents: “Mother, Father, as I understand the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One, it is not easy for one living at home to lead the holy life that is utterly complete, utterly pure, like a polished conch shell. I wish to shave off my hair and beard, put on the ochre robes, and go forth from the household life into homelessness. Permit me to go forth from the household life into homelessness.” A third time, the parents of the clansman Raṭṭhapāla said this to the clansman Raṭṭhapāla: “Dear Raṭṭhapāla, you are our only son, dear and beloved, raised in comfort, brought up in comfort. You, dear Raṭṭhapāla, do not know of any suffering. Even by death, we will be separated from you against our will. How then could we, while you are living, permit you to go forth from the household life into homelessness?”

296. Atha kho raṭṭhapālo kulaputto – “na maṃ mātāpitaro anujānanti agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajjāyā”ti tattheva anantarahitāya bhūmiyā nipajji – “idheva me maraṇaṃ bhavissati pabbajjā vā”ti. Atha kho raṭṭhapālo kulaputto ekampi bhattaṃ na bhuñji, dvepi bhattāni na bhuñji, tīṇipi bhattāni na bhuñji, cattāripi bhattāni na bhuñji, pañcapi bhattāni na bhuñji, chapi bhattāni na bhuñji, sattapi bhattāni na bhuñji. Atha [P 2.0058] kho raṭṭhapālassa kulaputtassa mātāpitaro raṭṭhapālaṃ kulaputtaṃ etadavocuṃ – “tvaṃ khosi, tāta raṭṭhapāla, amhākaṃ ekaputtako piyo manāpo sukhedhito sukhaparibhato. Na tvaṃ, tāta raṭṭhapāla, kassaci, dukkhassa jānāsi “maraṇenapi te…pe… pabbajjāyā”ti vākyadvayaṃ sī. syā. kaṃ. pī. potthakesu dutiyaṭṭhāne yeva dissati, pārājikapāḷiyaṃ pana paṭhamaṭṭhāne yeva dissati. tasmā idha dutiyaṭṭhāne punāgataṃ adhikaṃ viya dissati. Maraṇenapi te mayaṃ akāmakā vinā bhavissāma. Kiṃ pana mayaṃ taṃ jīvantaṃ anujānissāma agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajjāya. Uṭṭhehi, tāta raṭṭhapāla, bhuñja ca piva ca paricārehi ca; bhuñjanto pivanto paricārento kāme paribhuñjanto puññāni karonto abhiramassu. Na taṃ mayaṃ anujānāma agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajjāya “maraṇenapi te…pe… pabbajāyā”ti vākyadvayaṃ sī. syā. kaṃ. pī. potthakesu dutiyaṭṭhāne yeva dissati, pārājikapāḷiyaṃ pana paṭhamaṭṭhāne yeva dissati. tasmā idha dutiyaṭṭhāne punāgataṃ adhikaṃ viya dissati. Maraṇenapi te mayaṃ akāmakā vinā bhavissāma. Kiṃ pana mayaṃ taṃ jīvantaṃ anujānissāma agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajjāyā”ti? Evaṃ vutte, raṭṭhapālo kulaputto tuṇhī ahosi. Dutiyampi kho raṭṭhapālassa kulaputtassa mātāpitaro [M 2.0248] raṭṭhapālaṃ [T 2.0393] kulaputtaṃ etadavocuṃ…pe… dutiyampi kho raṭṭhapālo kulaputto tuṇhī ahosi. Tatiyampi kho raṭṭhapālassa kulaputtassa mātāpitaro raṭṭhapālaṃ kulaputtaṃ etadavocuṃ – “tvaṃ khosi, tāta raṭṭhapāla, amhākaṃ ekaputtako piyo manāpo sukhedhito sukhaparibhato. Na tvaṃ, tāta raṭṭhapāla, kassaci dukkhassa jānāsi. Maraṇenapi te mayaṃ akāmakā vinā bhavissāma, kiṃ pana mayaṃ taṃ jīvantaṃ anujānissāma agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajjāya. Uṭṭhehi, tāta raṭṭhapāla, bhuñja ca piva ca paricārehi ca; bhuñjanto pivanto paricārento kāme paribhuñjanto puññāni karonto abhiramassu. Na taṃ mayaṃ anujānāma agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajjāya. Maraṇenapi te mayaṃ akāmakā vinā bhavissāma[V 2.0258]. Kiṃ pana mayaṃ taṃ jīvantaṃ anujānissāma agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajjāyā”ti? Tatiyampi kho raṭṭhapālo kulaputto tuṇhī ahosi.

296. Then the clansman Raṭṭhapāla, thinking, “My parents do not permit me to go forth from the household life into homelessness,” lay down right there on the bare ground, thinking, “Here there will be either my death or the going forth.” Then the clansman Raṭṭhapāla did not eat one meal, nor two meals, nor three meals, nor four meals, nor five meals, nor six meals, nor seven meals. Then the parents of the clansman Raṭṭhapāla said this to the clansman Raṭṭhapāla: “Dear Raṭṭhapāla, you are our only son, dear and beloved, raised in comfort, brought up in comfort. You, dear Raṭṭhapāla, do not know of any suffering. Even by death, we will be separated from you against our will. How then could we, while you are living, permit you to go forth from the household life into homelessness? Rise, dear Raṭṭhapāla, eat, drink, and enjoy yourself; eating, drinking, enjoying yourself, indulging in sensual pleasures, and making merit, you should delight. We do not permit you to go forth from the household life into homelessness. Even by death, we will be separated from you against our will. How then could we, while you are living, permit you to go forth from the household life into homelessness?” When this was said, the clansman Raṭṭhapāla was silent. A second time, the parents of the clansman Raṭṭhapāla said this to the clansman Raṭṭhapāla… and a second time, the clansman Raṭṭhapāla was silent. A third time, the parents of the clansman Raṭṭhapāla said this to the clansman Raṭṭhapāla: “Dear Raṭṭhapāla, you are our only son, dear and beloved, raised in comfort, brought up in comfort. You, dear Raṭṭhapāla, do not know of any suffering. Even by death, we will be separated from you against our will; how then could we, while you are living, permit you to go forth from the household life into homelessness? Rise, dear Raṭṭhapāla, eat, drink, and enjoy yourself; eating, drinking, enjoying yourself, indulging in sensual pleasures, and making merit, you should delight. We do not permit you to go forth from the household life into homelessness. Even by death, we will be separated from you against our will. How then could we, while you are living, permit you to go forth from the household life into homelessness?” A third time, the clansman Raṭṭhapāla was silent.

297. Atha [P 2.0059] kho raṭṭhapālassa kulaputtassa sahāyakā yena raṭṭhapālo kulaputto tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā raṭṭhapālaṃ kulaputtaṃ etadavocuṃ – “tvaṃ khosi tvaṃ kho (sī. pī.), samma raṭṭhapāla, mātāpitūnaṃ ekaputtako piyo manāpo sukhedhito sukhaparibhato. Na tvaṃ, samma raṭṭhapāla, kassaci dukkhassa jānāsi. Maraṇenapi te mātāpitaro akāmakā vinā bhavissanti. Kiṃ pana te taṃ jīvantaṃ anujānissanti agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajjāya. Uṭṭhehi, samma raṭṭhapāla, bhuñja ca piva ca paricārehi ca; bhuñjanto pivanto paricārento kāme paribhuñjanto puññāni karonto abhiramassu. Na taṃ mātāpitaro anujānissanti anujānanti (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajjāya. Maraṇenapi te mātāpitaro akāmakā vinā bhavissanti. Kiṃ pana te taṃ jīvantaṃ anujānissanti [T 2.0394] agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajjāyā”ti? Evaṃ vutte, raṭṭhapālo kulaputto tuṇhī ahosi. Dutiyampi kho… tatiyampi kho raṭṭhapālassa kulaputtassa sahāyakā raṭṭhapālaṃ kulaputtaṃ etadavocuṃ – “tvaṃ khosi, samma raṭṭhapāla, mātāpitūnaṃ ekaputtako piyo manāpo sukhedhito sukhaparibhato, na tvaṃ, samma raṭṭhapāla, kassaci dukkhassa jānāsi, maraṇenapi te mātāpitaro akāmakā vinā bhavissanti. Kiṃ pana te taṃ jīvantaṃ anujānissanti agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajjāya? Uṭṭhehi, samma raṭṭhapāla, bhuñja ca piva ca paricārehi ca, bhuñjanto pivanto paricārento kāme paribhuñjanto puññāni [M 2.0249] karonto abhiramassu. Na taṃ mātāpitaro anujānissanti agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajjāya, maraṇenapi te mātāpitaro akāmakā vinā bhavissanti. Kiṃ pana te taṃ jīvantaṃ anujānissanti agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajjāyā”ti? Tatiyampi kho raṭṭhapālo kulaputto tuṇhī ahosi.

297. Then the friends of the clansman Raṭṭhapāla approached him and said: “Dear friend Raṭṭhapāla, you are your parents' only son, beloved and dear to their hearts, raised in comfort, nurtured in comfort. You have known no suffering. Even against their will, your parents will be parted from you by death. How then could they permit you to go forth from the household life into homelessness while you are still alive? Get up, dear friend Raṭṭhapāla, eat, drink, and enjoy yourself; while eating, drinking, and enjoying yourself, indulging in sensual pleasures and performing meritorious deeds, you should delight. Your parents will not permit you to go forth from the household life into homelessness. Even against their will, your parents will be parted from you by death. How then could they permit you to go forth from the household life into homelessness while you are still alive?” When this was said, the clansman Raṭṭhapāla remained silent. For a second time, and again for a third time, the friends of the clansman Raṭṭhapāla said this to him: “Dear friend Raṭṭhapāla, you are your parents' only son, beloved and dear to their hearts, raised in comfort, nurtured in comfort. You have known no suffering. Even against their will, your parents will be parted from you by death. How then could they permit you to go forth from the household life into homelessness while you are still alive? Get up, dear friend Raṭṭhapāla, eat, drink, and enjoy yourself; while eating, drinking, and enjoying yourself, indulging in sensual pleasures and performing meritorious deeds, you should delight. Your parents will not permit you to go forth from the household life into homelessness. Even against their will, your parents will be parted from you by death. How then could they permit you to go forth from the household life into homelessness while you are still alive?” For a third time, the clansman Raṭṭhapāla remained silent.

298. Atha kho raṭṭhapālassa kulaputtassa sahāyakā yena raṭṭhapālassa kulaputtassa mātāpitaro tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā raṭṭhapālassa kulaputtassa mātāpitaro etadavocuṃ – “ammatātā, eso raṭṭhapālo kulaputto tattheva anantarahitāya bhūmiyā nipanno – ‘idheva me maraṇaṃ bhavissati [P 2.0060] pabbajjā vā’ti. Sace tumhe raṭṭhapālaṃ kulaputtaṃ nānujānissatha agārasmā anagāriyaṃ [V 2.0259] pabbajjāya, tattheva tatthevassa (sī.) maraṇaṃ āgamissati. Sace pana tumhe raṭṭhapālaṃ kulaputtaṃ anujānissatha agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajjāya, pabbajitampi naṃ dakkhissatha. Sace raṭṭhapālo kulaputto nābhiramissati agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajjāya, kā tassa kā cassa (sī.) aññā gati bhavissati? Idheva [T 2.0395] paccāgamissati. Anujānātha raṭṭhapālaṃ kulaputtaṃ agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajjāyā”ti. “Anujānāma, tātā, raṭṭhapālaṃ kulaputtaṃ agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajjāya. Pabbajitena ca pana pana te (syā. kaṃ. ka.) mātāpitaro uddassetabbā”ti. Atha kho raṭṭhapālassa kulaputtassa sahāyakā yena raṭṭhapālo kulaputto tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā raṭṭhapālaṃ kulaputtaṃ etadavocuṃ – “uṭṭhehi, samma raṭṭhapāla “tvaṃ khosi samma raṭṭhapāla mātāpitūnaṃ ekaputtako piyo manāpo sukhedhito sukhaparihato, na tvaṃ samma raṭṭhapāla kassaci dukkhassa jānāsi, uṭṭhehi samma raṭṭhapāla bhuñja ca piva ca paricārehi ca, bhuñjanto pivanto paricārento kāme paribhuñjanto puññāni karonto abhiramassu, (sī. pī. ka.), anuññātosi mātāpitūhi agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajjāya. Pabbajitena ca pana te mātāpitaro uddassetabbā”ti.

298. Then the friends of the clansman Raṭṭhapāla approached Raṭṭhapāla's parents and said to them: “Mother and father, this clansman Raṭṭhapāla is lying there on the bare ground, resolving, ‘Right here my death will be, or my ordination will be.’ If you do not permit the clansman Raṭṭhapāla to go forth from the household life into homelessness, he will meet his death right there. But if you permit the clansman Raṭṭhapāla to go forth from the household life into homelessness, you will see him even after he has gone forth. And if the clansman Raṭṭhapāla does not find delight in going forth from the household life into homelessness, what other destination will there be for him? He will return right here. Permit the clansman Raṭṭhapāla to go forth from the household life into homelessness.” “We permit, my dears, the clansman Raṭṭhapāla to go forth from the household life into homelessness. But having gone forth, he must visit his parents.” Then the friends of the clansman Raṭṭhapāla approached Raṭṭhapāla and said to him: “Get up, dear friend Raṭṭhapāla, you have been permitted by your parents to go forth from the household life into homelessness. But having gone forth, you must visit your parents.”

299. Atha kho raṭṭhapālo kulaputto uṭṭhahitvā balaṃ gāhetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho raṭṭhapālo kulaputto bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “anuññāto ahaṃ, bhante, mātāpitūhi agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajjāya. Pabbājetu maṃ bhagavā”ti. Alattha kho raṭṭhapālo kulaputto bhagavato [M 2.0250] santike pabbajjaṃ, alattha upasampadaṃ. Atha kho bhagavā acirūpasampanne āyasmante raṭṭhapāle aḍḍhamāsūpasampanne thullakoṭṭhike yathābhirantaṃ viharitvā yena sāvatthi tena cārikaṃ pakkāmi. Anupubbena cārikaṃ caramāno yena sāvatthi tadavasari. Tatra sudaṃ bhagavā [P 2.0061] sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Atha kho āyasmā raṭṭhapālo eko vūpakaṭṭho appamatto ātāpī pahitatto viharanto nacirasseva – yassatthāya [T 2.0396] kulaputtā sammadeva agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajanti tadanuttaraṃ – brahmacariyapariyosānaṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja vihāsi. ‘Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti abbhaññāsi. Aññataro kho panāyasmā raṭṭhapālo arahataṃ ahosi.

299. Then the clansman Raṭṭhapāla, having risen and gathered his strength, approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Sitting to one side, the clansman Raṭṭhapāla said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, I have been permitted by my parents to go forth from the household life into homelessness. May the Blessed One grant me the going forth.” The clansman Raṭṭhapāla obtained the going forth in the presence of the Blessed One, and he obtained the higher ordination. Then, when the Venerable Raṭṭhapāla had been fully ordained for not long, for half a month, the Blessed One, having dwelt at Thullakoṭṭhika for as long as he wished, set out on a journey toward Sāvatthī. Journeying stage by stage, he arrived at Sāvatthī. There the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. Then the Venerable Raṭṭhapāla, dwelling alone, in seclusion, diligent, ardent, and with a resolute mind, not long after, dwelt having realized for himself with direct knowledge in this very life that unsurpassed culmination of the holy life for the sake of which clansmen rightly go forth from the household life into homelessness, having made it manifest and attained it. He knew directly: “Destroyed is birth, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this state of being.” And the Venerable Raṭṭhapāla became one of the Arahants.

Atha kho āyasmā raṭṭhapālo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā raṭṭhapālo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “icchāmahaṃ, bhante, mātāpitaro uddassetuṃ, sace maṃ bhagavā anujānātī”ti. Atha kho bhagavā āyasmato raṭṭhapālassa cetasā ceto paricca cetoparivitakkaṃ (sī. pī.) manasākāsi. Yathā yadā (sī. pī.) bhagavā aññāsi [V 2.0260] – “abhabbo kho raṭṭhapālo kulaputto sikkhaṃ paccakkhāya hīnāyāvattitu”nti, atha kho bhagavā āyasmantaṃ raṭṭhapālaṃ etadavoca – “yassadāni tvaṃ, raṭṭhapāla, kālaṃ maññasī”ti. Atha kho āyasmā raṭṭhapālo uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā senāsanaṃ saṃsāmetvā pattacīvaramādāya yena thullakoṭṭhikaṃ tena cārikaṃ pakkāmi. Anupubbena cārikaṃ caramāno yena thullakoṭṭhiko tadavasari. Tatra sudaṃ āyasmā raṭṭhapālo thullakoṭṭhike viharati rañño korabyassa migacīre. Atha kho āyasmā raṭṭhapālo pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya thullakoṭṭhikaṃ piṇḍāya pāvisi. Thullakoṭṭhike sapadānaṃ piṇḍāya caramāno yena sakapitu nivesanaṃ [T 2.0397] tenupasaṅkami. Tena kho pana samayena āyasmato raṭṭhapālassa pitā majjhimāya dvārasālāya ullikhāpeti. Addasā kho āyasmato raṭṭhapālassa pitā āyasmantaṃ raṭṭhapālaṃ dūratova āgacchantaṃ. Disvāna etadavoca – “imehi muṇḍakehi samaṇakehi amhākaṃ ekaputtako piyo manāpo pabbājito”ti[P 2.0062]. Atha kho āyasmā raṭṭhapālo [M 2.0251] sakapitu nivesane neva dānaṃ alattha na paccakkhānaṃ; aññadatthu akkosameva alattha. Tena kho pana samayena āyasmato raṭṭhapālassa ñātidāsī ābhidosikaṃ kummāsaṃ chaḍḍetukāmā hoti. Atha kho āyasmā raṭṭhapālo taṃ ñātidāsiṃ etadavoca – “sacetaṃ, bhagini, chaḍḍanīyadhammaṃ, idha me patte ākirā”ti. Atha kho āyasmato raṭṭhapālassa ñātidāsī taṃ ābhidosikaṃ kummāsaṃ āyasmato raṭṭhapālassa patte ākirantī hatthānañca pādānañca sarassa ca nimittaṃ aggahesi.

Then the Venerable Raṭṭhapāla went to where the Blessed One was; having gone, he paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the Venerable Raṭṭhapāla said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, I wish to see my parents, if the Blessed One would permit me.” Then the Blessed One, having encompassed the Venerable Raṭṭhapāla’s mind with his own mind, reflected and knew thus: “The clansman Raṭṭhapāla is incapable of renouncing the training and reverting to the lower life.” Then the Blessed One said this to the Venerable Raṭṭhapāla: “Raṭṭhapāla, it is now time for whatever you deem fit.” Then the Venerable Raṭṭhapāla, rising from his seat, paid homage to the Blessed One, circumambulated him to the right, put his lodging in order, took his bowl and robes, and set out on tour towards Thullakoṭṭhika. Wandering on tour by stages, he arrived at Thullakoṭṭhika. There, indeed, the Venerable Raṭṭhapāla stayed in Thullakoṭṭhika, in King Korabya’s deer park, Migacīra. Then, in the morning, the Venerable Raṭṭhapāla dressed, took his bowl and robes, and entered Thullakoṭṭhika for alms. While wandering for alms from house to house in Thullakoṭṭhika, he went to his own father’s residence. At that time, the Venerable Raṭṭhapāla’s father was having his hair dressed in the central gatehouse. The Venerable Raṭṭhapāla’s father saw the Venerable Raṭṭhapāla coming from afar. Having seen him, he said this: “By these shaven-headed ascetics, our only son, dear and beloved, has been made to go forth.” Then, at his father’s residence, the Venerable Raṭṭhapāla received neither an offering nor a refusal; on the contrary, he received only abuse. At that time, a female slave of the Venerable Raṭṭhapāla’s kin wished to throw away some stale barley-gruel. Then the Venerable Raṭṭhapāla said this to that female slave: “Sister, if that is to be discarded, then pour it into my bowl here.” Then, as the female slave of the Venerable Raṭṭhapāla’s kin was pouring the stale barley-gruel into the Venerable Raṭṭhapāla’s bowl, she took note of the signs of his hands, feet, and voice.

300. Atha kho āyasmato raṭṭhapālassa ñātidāsī yenāyasmato raṭṭhapālassa mātā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmato raṭṭhapālassa mātaraṃ etadavoca – “yaggheyye, jāneyyāsi – ‘ayyaputto raṭṭhapālo anuppatto’”ti. “Sace, je, saccaṃ bhaṇasi, adāsiṃ taṃ karomī”ti saccaṃ vadasi, adāsī bhavasīti (sī. pī.), saccaṃ vadasi, adāsī bhavissasi (ka.). Atha kho āyasmato raṭṭhapālassa mātā yenāyasmato raṭṭhapālassa pitā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmato [T 2.0398] raṭṭhapālassa pitaraṃ etadavoca – “yagghe, gahapati, jāneyyāsi – ‘raṭṭhapālo kira kulaputto anuppatto’”ti? Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā raṭṭhapālo taṃ ābhidosikaṃ kummāsaṃ aññataraṃ kuṭṭamūlaṃ kuḍḍaṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) nissāya paribhuñjati. Atha kho āyasmato raṭṭhapālassa pitā yenāyasmā raṭṭhapālo tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ raṭṭhapālaṃ etadavoca – “atthi nāma, tāta raṭṭhapāla, ābhidosikaṃ kummāsaṃ paribhuñjissasi? Nanu, tāta raṭṭhapāla, sakaṃ gehaṃ gantabba”nti? “Kuto no, gahapati, amhākaṃ gehaṃ agārasmā [V 2.0261] anagāriyaṃ pabbajitānaṃ? Anagārā mayaṃ, gahapati. Agamamha kho [P 2.0063] te, gahapati, gehaṃ, tattha neva dānaṃ alatthamha na paccakkhānaṃ; aññadatthu akkosameva alatthamhā”ti. “Ehi, tāta raṭṭhapāla, gharaṃ gamissāmā”ti. “Alaṃ, gahapati, kataṃ me ajja bhattakiccaṃ”. “Tena hi, tāta raṭṭhapāla, adhivāsehi svātanāya bhatta”nti. Adhivāsesi kho āyasmā raṭṭhapālo tuṇhībhāvena. Atha kho āyasmato raṭṭhapālassa pitā āyasmato raṭṭhapālassa adhivāsanaṃ viditvā yena sakaṃ nivesanaṃ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā mahantaṃ hiraññasuvaṇṇassa [T 2.0399] puñjaṃ kārāpetvā kilañjehi [M 2.0252] paṭicchādetvā āyasmato raṭṭhapālassa purāṇadutiyikā āmantesi – “etha tumhe, vadhuyo, yena alaṅkārena alaṅkatā pubbe raṭṭhapālassa kulaputtassa piyā hotha manāpā tena alaṅkārena alaṅkarothā”ti.

300. Then the female slave of the Venerable Raṭṭhapāla’s kin went to where the Venerable Raṭṭhapāla’s mother was; having gone, she said this to the Venerable Raṭṭhapāla’s mother: “Pray, madam, know this: ‘The master’s son, Raṭṭhapāla, has arrived.’” “If, girl, you speak the truth, I will make you a free woman.” Then the Venerable Raṭṭhapāla’s mother went to where the Venerable Raṭṭhapāla’s father was; having gone, she said this to the Venerable Raṭṭhapāla’s father: “Pray, householder, know this: ‘The clansman Raṭṭhapāla has reportedly arrived.’” Now at that time, the Venerable Raṭṭhapāla was eating that stale barley-gruel while leaning against the base of a certain wall. Then the Venerable Raṭṭhapāla’s father went to where the Venerable Raṭṭhapāla was; having gone, he said this to the Venerable Raṭṭhapāla: “Is it possible, dear Raṭṭhapāla, that you would eat stale barley-gruel? Should you not, dear Raṭṭhapāla, go to your own home?” “Householder, from where is there a home for us who have gone forth from the household life into homelessness? We are homeless, householder. We did go to your home, householder, and there we received neither an offering nor a refusal; on the contrary, we received only abuse.” “Come, dear Raṭṭhapāla, let us go home.” “Enough, householder, my meal for today is finished.” “In that case, dear Raṭṭhapāla, please consent to a meal for tomorrow.” The Venerable Raṭṭhapāla consented by his silence. Then the Venerable Raṭṭhapāla’s father, having understood the Venerable Raṭṭhapāla’s consent, went to his own residence. Having gone, he had a great heap of gold and bullion prepared, covered it with mats, and addressed the Venerable Raṭṭhapāla’s former wives: “Come, ladies, adorn yourselves with those ornaments with which you were formerly dear and pleasing to the clansman Raṭṭhapāla.”

301. Atha kho āyasmato raṭṭhapālassa pitā tassā rattiyā accayena sake nivesane paṇītaṃ khādanīyaṃ bhojanīyaṃ paṭiyādāpetvā āyasmato raṭṭhapālassa kālaṃ ārocesi – “kālo, tāta raṭṭhapāla, niṭṭhitaṃ bhatta”nti. Atha kho āyasmā raṭṭhapālo pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya yena sakapitu nivesanaṃ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi. Atha kho āyasmato raṭṭhapālassa pitā taṃ hiraññasuvaṇṇassa puñjaṃ vivarāpetvā āyasmantaṃ raṭṭhapālaṃ etadavoca – “idaṃ te, tāta raṭṭhapāla, mātu mattikaṃ dhanaṃ, aññaṃ pettikaṃ, aññaṃ pitāmahaṃ. Sakkā, tāta raṭṭhapāla, bhoge ca bhuñjituṃ puññāni ca kātuṃ. Ehi tvaṃ, tāta raṭṭhapāla raṭṭhapāla sikkhaṃ paccakkhāya (sabbattha)[P 2.0064], hīnāyāvattitvā bhoge ca bhuñjassu puññāni ca karohī”ti. “Sace me tvaṃ, gahapati, vacanaṃ kareyyāsi, imaṃ hiraññasuvaṇṇassa puñjaṃ sakaṭe āropetvā nibbāhāpetvā [T 2.0400] majjhegaṅgāya nadiyā sote opilāpeyyāsi. Taṃ kissa hetu? Ye uppajjissanti hi te, gahapati, tatonidānaṃ sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā”ti. Atha kho āyasmato raṭṭhapālassa purāṇadutiyikā paccekaṃ pādesu gahetvā āyasmantaṃ raṭṭhapālaṃ etadavocuṃ – “kīdisā nāma tā, ayyaputta, accharāyo yāsaṃ tvaṃ hetu brahmacariyaṃ carasī”ti? “Na kho mayaṃ, bhaginī, accharānaṃ hetu brahmacariyaṃ carāmā”ti. “Bhaginivādena no ayyaputto raṭṭhapālo samudācaratī”ti tā tattheva mucchitā papatiṃsu. Atha kho āyasmā raṭṭhapālo pitaraṃ etadavoca – “sace, gahapati, bhojanaṃ dātabbaṃ, detha; mā no viheṭhethā”ti. “Bhuñja, tāta raṭṭhapāla, niṭṭhitaṃ bhatta”nti. Atha kho āyasmato raṭṭhapālassa [V 2.0262] pitā āyasmantaṃ raṭṭhapālaṃ paṇītena khādanīyena bhojanīyena sahatthā santappesi sampavāresi.

301. Then, when that night had passed, the Venerable Raṭṭhapāla’s father had choice solid and soft food prepared in his own house and announced the time to the Venerable Raṭṭhapāla, saying: “It is time, dear Raṭṭhapāla, the meal is ready.” Then, in the morning, the Venerable Raṭṭhapāla dressed, took his bowl and robe, and went to his father’s house. Having arrived, he sat down on the prepared seat. Then the Venerable Raṭṭhapāla’s father had the heap of gold and silver uncovered and said to him: “This, dear Raṭṭhapāla, is your mother’s wealth, another is your father’s, and another your grandfather’s. It is possible, dear Raṭṭhapāla, to enjoy riches and to make merit. Come, dear Raṭṭhapāla, revert to the low life, enjoy riches, and make merit.” “Householder, if you would do as I say, you should load this heap of gold and silver onto a cart, have it hauled away, and sink it in the current in the middle of the river Ganges. For what reason? Because from that as a cause, householder, sorrow, lamentation, pain, displeasure, and despair will arise for you.” Then the Venerable Raṭṭhapāla’s former wives each took him by the feet and said: “What kind of celestial nymphs are they, my lord, for whose sake you lead the holy life?” “Sisters, we do not lead the holy life for the sake of celestial nymphs.” “Our lord Raṭṭhapāla addresses us as ‘sisters’!” Saying this, they fainted right there. Then the Venerable Raṭṭhapāla said to his father: “Householder, if food is to be given, give it; do not harass us.” “Eat, dear Raṭṭhapāla, the meal is finished.” Then the Venerable Raṭṭhapāla’s father, with his own hands, served him with choice solid and soft food until he was satisfied and indicated he had had enough.

302. Atha kho āyasmā raṭṭhapālo bhuttāvī onītapattapāṇī ṭhitakova imā gāthā abhāsi –

302. Then the Venerable Raṭṭhapāla, having eaten and withdrawn his hand from the bowl, while standing, uttered these verses:

“Passa [M 2.0253] cittīkataṃ bimbaṃ, arukāyaṃ samussitaṃ;

Āturaṃ bahusaṅkappaṃ, yassa natthi dhuvaṃ ṭhiti.

“See this decorated image, a body of sores, heaped up, afflicted, and much thought-of, for which there is no permanent stability.

“Passa cittīkataṃ rūpaṃ, maṇinā kuṇḍalena ca;

Aṭṭhi tacena onaddhaṃ, saha vatthebhi sobhati.

“See this decorated form, with jewels and earrings; a skeleton bound with skin, it shines only with its clothes.

“Alattakakatā pādā, mukhaṃ cuṇṇakamakkhitaṃ;

Alaṃ [T 2.0401] bālassa mohāya, no ca pāragavesino.

“Feet dyed with lac, a face smeared with powder—enough to delude a fool, but not one who seeks the far shore.

“Aṭṭhāpadakatā [P 2.0065] kesā, nettā añjanamakkhitā;

Alaṃ bālassa mohāya, no ca pāragavesino.

“Hair styled in eight braids, eyes smeared with eyeliner—enough to delude a fool, but not one who seeks the far shore.

“Añjanīva navā añjanīvaṇṇavā (ka.) cittā, pūtikāyo alaṅkato;

Alaṃ bālassa mohāya, no ca pāragavesino.

“Like a new, decorated eyeliner box, this putrid body is adorned—enough to delude a fool, but not one who seeks the far shore.

“Odahi migavo pāsaṃ, nāsadā vākaraṃ migo;

Bhutvā nivāpaṃ gacchāma gacchāmi (syā. ka.), kandante migabandhake”ti.

“The hunter set the snare, but the deer did not approach the trap. Having eaten the fodder, we depart, while the deer-binders lament.”

Atha kho āyasmā raṭṭhapālo ṭhitakova imā gāthā bhāsitvā yena rañño korabyassa migacīraṃ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā aññatarasmiṃ rukkhamūle divāvihāraṃ nisīdi.

Then the Venerable Raṭṭhapāla, while standing, having uttered these verses, went to King Korabya’s Migacīra park. Having arrived, he sat down at the root of a certain tree for the day's abiding.

303. Atha [V 2.0263] kho rājā korabyo migavaṃ āmantesi – “sodhehi, samma migava, migacīraṃ uyyānabhūmiṃ; gacchāma subhūmiṃ dassanāyā”ti. “Evaṃ, devā”ti kho migavo rañño korabyassa paṭissutvā migacīraṃ sodhento addasa āyasmantaṃ raṭṭhapālaṃ aññatarasmiṃ rukkhamūle divāvihāraṃ nisinnaṃ. Disvāna yena rājā korabyo tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā rājānaṃ korabyaṃ etadavoca – “suddhaṃ kho te, deva, migacīraṃ. Atthi cettha raṭṭhapālo nāma kulaputto imasmiṃyeva thullakoṭṭhike aggakulassa putto yassa tvaṃ abhiṇhaṃ kittayamāno ahosi, so aññatarasmiṃ rukkhamūle divāvihāraṃ nisinno”ti. “Tena hi, samma migava, alaṃ dānajja uyyānabhūmiyā. Tameva dāni mayaṃ bhavantaṃ raṭṭhapālaṃ payirupāsissāmā”ti. Atha [T 2.0402] kho rājā korabyo “yaṃ tattha khādanīyaṃ bhojanīyaṃ paṭiyattaṃ taṃ sabbaṃ vissajjethā”ti vatvā bhadrāni bhadrāni yānāni yojāpetvā bhadraṃ yānaṃ abhiruhitvā bhadrehi bhadrehi yānehi thullakoṭṭhikamhā niyyāsi [M 2.0254] mahaccarājānubhāvena mahaccā rājānubhāvena (sī.) āyasmantaṃ raṭṭhapālaṃ dassanāya. Yāvatikā yānassa bhūmi yānena gantvā yānā paccorohitvā pattikova ussaṭāya ussaṭāya parisāya yenāyasmā raṭṭhapālo tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmatā raṭṭhapālena [P 2.0066] saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhito kho rājā korabyo āyasmantaṃ raṭṭhapālaṃ etadavoca – “idha bhavaṃ raṭṭhapāla hatthatthare kaṭṭhatthare (syā. kaṃ.) nisīdatū”ti. “Alaṃ, mahārāja, nisīda tvaṃ; nisinno ahaṃ sake āsane”ti. Nisīdi rājā korabyo paññatte āsane. Nisajja kho rājā korabyo āyasmantaṃ raṭṭhapālaṃ etadavoca –

303. Then King Korabya addressed the park-keeper Migava: “Clean the Migacīra park grounds, my dear Migava; we shall go to see the beautiful grounds.” “Yes, Your Majesty,” replied Migava to King Korabya, and while cleaning the Migacīra park, he saw the Venerable Raṭṭhapāla seated at the root of a certain tree for the day's abiding. Having seen him, he approached King Korabya and said: “Your Migacīra park is clean, Your Majesty. And here there is the clansman named Raṭṭhapāla, the son of the foremost family in this very Thullakoṭṭhita, whom you have constantly praised; he is seated at the root of a certain tree for the day's abiding.” “In that case, my dear Migava, enough of the park grounds for today. We will now attend upon the Venerable Raṭṭhapāla himself.” Then King Korabya said, “Distribute all the solid and soft food that has been prepared there,” and having had the finest carriages harnessed, he mounted a fine carriage and, with the great majesty of a king, set out from Thullakoṭṭhita with his finest carriages to see the Venerable Raṭṭhapāla. He went by carriage as far as the ground was passable for a carriage, then dismounted and proceeded on foot with a large retinue to where the Venerable Raṭṭhapāla was. Having approached, he exchanged courteous greetings with the Venerable Raṭṭhapāla. After concluding the courteous and memorable conversation, he stood to one side. Standing to one side, King Korabya said to the Venerable Raṭṭhapāla: “Let the Venerable Raṭṭhapāla sit here on the elephant rug.” “Enough, great king, you sit down; I am seated on my own seat.” King Korabya sat down on the prepared seat. Having sat down, King Korabya said to the Venerable Raṭṭhapāla:

304. “Cattārimāni, bho raṭṭhapāla, pārijuññāni yehi pārijuññehi samannāgatā idhekacce kesamassuṃ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajanti. Katamāni cattāri? Jarāpārijuññaṃ, byādhipārijuññaṃ, bhogapārijuññaṃ, ñātipārijuññaṃ. Katamañca, bho raṭṭhapāla, jarāpārijuññaṃ? Idha, bho raṭṭhapāla[T 2.0403], ekacco jiṇṇo hoti vuḍḍho mahallako addhagato vayoanuppatto. So iti paṭisañcikkhati – ‘ahaṃ khomhi etarahi jiṇṇo vuḍḍho mahallako addhagato vayoanuppatto. Na kho pana mayā sukaraṃ anadhigataṃ vā bhogaṃ adhigantuṃ adhigataṃ vā bhogaṃ phātiṃ kātuṃ phātikattuṃ (sī.). Yaṃnūnāhaṃ kesamassuṃ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajeyya’nti. So tena jarāpārijuññena samannāgato kesamassuṃ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ [V 2.0264] pabbajati. Idaṃ vuccati, bho raṭṭhapāla, jarāpārijuññaṃ. Bhavaṃ kho pana raṭṭhapālo etarahi daharo yuvā susukāḷakeso bhadrena yobbanena samannāgato paṭhamena vayasā. Taṃ bhoto raṭṭhapālassa jarāpārijuññaṃ natthi. Kiṃ bhavaṃ raṭṭhapālo ñatvā vā disvā vā sutvā vā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajito?

304. “There are, Raṭṭhapāla, these four kinds of decline, possessed of which, some people in this world shave off their hair and beard, put on ochre robes, and go forth from the household life into homelessness. What are the four? The decline of old age, the decline of sickness, the decline of wealth, and the decline of relatives. And what, Raṭṭhapāla, is the decline of old age? Here, Raṭṭhapāla, someone is old, grown old, aged, far-gone in years, having reached the final stage of life. He reflects thus: ‘I am now old, grown old, aged, far-gone in years, having reached the final stage of life. It is not easy for me to acquire wealth I have not yet acquired or to make my acquired wealth increase. What if I were to shave off my hair and beard, put on ochre robes, and go forth from the household life into homelessness?’ So, possessed of that decline of old age, he shaves off his hair and beard, puts on ochre robes, and goes forth from the household life into homelessness. This, Raṭṭhapāla, is called the decline of old age. But you, venerable Raṭṭhapāla, are now young, a youth with glossy black hair, endowed with blessed youth, in the prime of life. For you, venerable Raṭṭhapāla, that decline of old age does not exist. What have you known, seen, or heard that you have gone forth from the household life into homelessness?”

“Katamañca, bho raṭṭhapāla, byādhipārijuññaṃ? Idha, bho raṭṭhapāla, ekacco ābādhiko hoti dukkhito bāḷhagilāno. So iti paṭisañcikkhati [M 2.0255] – ‘ahaṃ khomhi etarahi ābādhiko dukkhito bāḷhagilāno. Na kho pana mayā sukaraṃ anadhigataṃ vā bhogaṃ adhigantuṃ adhigataṃ vā bhogaṃ phātiṃ kātuṃ[P 2.0067]. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ kesamassuṃ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajeyya’nti. So [T 2.0404] tena byādhipārijuññena samannāgato kesamassuṃ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajati. Idaṃ vuccati, bho raṭṭhapāla, byādhipārijuññaṃ. Bhavaṃ kho pana raṭṭhapālo etarahi appābādho appātaṅko samavepākiniyā gahaṇiyā samannāgato nātisītāya nāccuṇhāya. Taṃ bhoto raṭṭhapālassa byādhipārijuññaṃ natthi. Kiṃ bhavaṃ raṭṭhapālo ñatvā vā disvā vā sutvā vā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajito?

“And what, Raṭṭhapāla, is the decline of sickness? Here, Raṭṭhapāla, someone is afflicted with illness, suffering, and gravely sick. He reflects thus: ‘I am now afflicted with illness, suffering, and gravely sick. It is not easy for me to acquire wealth I have not yet acquired or to make my acquired wealth increase. What if I were to shave off my hair and beard, put on ochre robes, and go forth from the household life into homelessness?’ So, possessed of that decline of sickness, he shaves off his hair and beard, puts on ochre robes, and goes forth from the household life into homelessness. This, Raṭṭhapāla, is called the decline of sickness. But you, venerable Raṭṭhapāla, are now free from illness and affliction, endowed with a balanced digestive faculty that is not too cold and not too hot. For you, venerable Raṭṭhapāla, that decline of sickness does not exist. What have you known, seen, or heard that you have gone forth from the household life into homelessness?”

“Katamañca[V 2.0265], bho raṭṭhapāla, bhogapārijuññaṃ? Idha, bho raṭṭhapāla, ekacco aḍḍho hoti mahaddhano mahābhogo. Tassa te bhogā anupubbena parikkhayaṃ gacchanti. So iti paṭisañcikkhati – ‘ahaṃ kho pubbe aḍḍho ahosiṃ mahaddhano mahābhogo. Tassa me te bhogā anupubbena parikkhayaṃ gatā. Na kho pana mayā sukaraṃ anadhigataṃ vā bhogaṃ adhigantuṃ adhigataṃ vā bhogaṃ phātiṃ kātuṃ. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ kesamassuṃ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajeyya’nti. So tena bhogapārijuññena samannāgato kesamassuṃ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajati. Idaṃ vuccati, bho raṭṭhapāla, bhogapārijuññaṃ. Bhavaṃ kho pana raṭṭhapālo imasmiṃyeva thullakoṭṭhike aggakulassa putto. Taṃ bhoto raṭṭhapālassa bhogapārijuññaṃ natthi. Kiṃ bhavaṃ raṭṭhapālo ñatvā vā disvā vā sutvā vā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajito?

“And what, Raṭṭhapāla, is the decline of wealth? Here, Raṭṭhapāla, someone is wealthy, with great riches and vast possessions. His wealth gradually goes to ruin. He reflects thus: ‘Formerly, I was wealthy, with great riches and vast possessions. But that wealth of mine has gradually gone to ruin. It is not easy for me to acquire wealth I have not yet acquired or to make my acquired wealth increase. What if I were to shave off my hair and beard, put on ochre robes, and go forth from the household life into homelessness?’ So, possessed of that decline of wealth, he shaves off his hair and beard, puts on ochre robes, and goes forth from the household life into homelessness. This, Raṭṭhapāla, is called the decline of wealth. But you, venerable Raṭṭhapāla, are the son of the foremost family in this very Thullakoṭṭhika. For you, venerable Raṭṭhapāla, that decline of wealth does not exist. What have you known, seen, or heard that you have gone forth from the household life into homelessness?”

“Katamañca[T 2.0405], bho raṭṭhapāla, ñātipārijuññaṃ? Idha, bho raṭṭhapāla, ekaccassa bahū honti mittāmaccā ñātisālohitā. Tassa te ñātakā anupubbena parikkhayaṃ gacchanti. So iti paṭisañcikkhati – ‘mamaṃ kho pubbe bahū ahesuṃ mittāmaccā ñātisālohitā. Tassa me te anupubbena parikkhayaṃ gatā. Na kho pana mayā sukaraṃ anadhigataṃ vā bhogaṃ adhigantuṃ adhigataṃ vā bhogaṃ phātiṃ kātuṃ. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ kesamassuṃ [P 2.0068] ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajeyya’nti. So [M 2.0256] tena ñātipārijuññena samannāgato kesamassuṃ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajati. Idaṃ vuccati, bho raṭṭhapāla, ñātipārijuññaṃ. Bhoto kho pana raṭṭhapālassa imasmiṃyeva thullakoṭṭhike bahū mittāmaccā ñātisālohitā. Taṃ bhoto raṭṭhapālassa ñātipārijuññaṃ natthi. Kiṃ bhavaṃ raṭṭhapālo ñatvā vā disvā vā sutvā vā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajito?

“And what, Raṭṭhapāla, is the decline of relatives? Here, Raṭṭhapāla, someone has many friends and companions, kinsmen and blood relatives. Those relatives of his gradually dwindle away. He reflects thus: ‘Formerly, I had many friends and companions, kinsmen and blood relatives. But they have gradually dwindled away. It is not easy for me to acquire wealth I have not yet acquired or to make my acquired wealth increase. What if I were to shave off my hair and beard, put on ochre robes, and go forth from the household life into homelessness?’ So, possessed of that decline of relatives, he shaves off his hair and beard, puts on ochre robes, and goes forth from the household life into homelessness. This, Raṭṭhapāla, is called the decline of relatives. But for you, venerable Raṭṭhapāla, there are many friends and companions, kinsmen and blood relatives in this very Thullakoṭṭhika. For you, venerable Raṭṭhapāla, that decline of relatives does not exist. What have you known, seen, or heard that you have gone forth from the household life into homelessness?”

“Imāni kho, bho raṭṭhapāla, cattāri pārijuññāni, yehi pārijuññehi samannāgatā idhekacce kesamassuṃ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajanti. Tāni bhoto raṭṭhapālassa natthi. Kiṃ bhavaṃ raṭṭhapālo ñatvā vā disvā vā sutvā vā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajito”ti?

“These, Raṭṭhapāla, are the four declines, possessed of which, some people in this world shave off their hair and beard, put on ochre robes, and go forth from the household life into homelessness. For you, venerable Raṭṭhapāla, those declines do not exist. What have you known, seen, or heard that you have gone forth from the household life into homelessness?”

305. “Atthi kho, mahārāja, tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā [T 2.0406] sammāsambuddhena cattāro dhammuddesā uddiṭṭhā, ye ahaṃ yamahaṃ (syā. kaṃ. ka.) ñatvā ca disvā ca sutvā ca agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajito. Katame cattāro? ‘Upaniyyati loko addhuvo’ti kho, mahārāja, tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena paṭhamo dhammuddeso uddiṭṭho, yamahaṃ ñatvā ca disvā sutvā ca agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajito. ‘Atāṇo loko anabhissaro’ti kho, mahārāja, tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena dutiyo dhammuddeso uddiṭṭho, yamahaṃ ñatvā ca disvā sutvā ca agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajito. ‘Assako loko, sabbaṃ pahāya gamanīya’nti kho, mahārāja, tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena tatiyo dhammuddeso uddiṭṭho, yamahaṃ ñatvā ca disvā sutvā ca agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajito. ‘Ūno loko atitto taṇhādāso’ti kho, mahārāja, tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena catuttho dhammuddeso uddiṭṭho, yamahaṃ ñatvā ca disvā sutvā [V 2.0266] ca agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajito. Ime kho, mahārāja, tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena [P 2.0069] cattāro dhammuddesā uddiṭṭhā, ye ahaṃ ñatvā ca disvā sutvā ca agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajito”ti.

305. “Great king, there are four summaries of the Dhamma that have been declared by the Blessed One—who knows and sees, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One—which I, having known, seen, and heard, went forth from the household life into homelessness. What are the four? ‘The world is swept away, it is not lasting,’ great king—this is the first summary of the Dhamma declared by the Blessed One, who knows and sees, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, which I, having known, seen, and heard, went forth from the household life into homelessness. ‘The world is without refuge, without a protector,’ great king—this is the second summary of the Dhamma declared by the Blessed One, who knows and sees, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, which I, having known, seen, and heard, went forth from the household life into homelessness. ‘The world has nothing of its own; one must go on, leaving everything behind,’ great king—this is the third summary of the Dhamma declared by the Blessed One, who knows and sees, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, which I, having known, seen, and heard, went forth from the household life into homelessness. ‘The world is deficient, insatiable, a slave to craving,’ great king—this is the fourth summary of the Dhamma declared by the Blessed One, who knows and sees, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, which I, having known, seen, and heard, went forth from the household life into homelessness. These, great king, are the four summaries of the Dhamma declared by the Blessed One—who knows and sees, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One—which I, having known, seen, and heard, went forth from the household life into homelessness.”

306. “‘Upaniyyati [M 2.0257] loko addhuvo’ti – bhavaṃ raṭṭhapālo āha. Imassa[T 2.0407], bho raṭṭhapāla, bhāsitassa kathaṃ attho daṭṭhabbo”ti? “Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, mahārāja, tvaṃ vīsativassuddesikopi paṇṇavīsativassuddesikopi hatthismimpi katāvī assasmimpi katāvī rathasmimpi katāvī dhanusmimpi katāvī tharusmimpi katāvī ūrubalī bāhubalī alamatto saṅgāmāvacaro”ti? “Ahosiṃ ahaṃ, bho raṭṭhapāla, vīsativassuddesikopi paṇṇavīsativassuddesikopi hatthismimpi katāvī assasmimpi katāvī rathasmimpi katāvī dhanusmimpi katāvī tharusmimpi katāvī ūrubalī bāhubalī alamatto saṅgāmāvacaro. Appekadāhaṃ, bho raṭṭhapāla, iddhimāva maññe na iddhimā maññe na (syā. kaṃ.), iddhimā ca maññe (sī.), na viya maññe (ka.) attano balena samasamaṃ samanupassāmī”ti. “Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, mahārāja, evameva tvaṃ etarahi ūrubalī bāhubalī alamatto saṅgāmāvacaro”ti? “No hidaṃ, bho raṭṭhapāla. Etarahi jiṇṇo vuḍḍho mahallako addhagato vayoanuppatto āsītiko me vayo vattati. Appekadāhaṃ, bho raṭṭhapāla, ‘idha pādaṃ karissāmī’ti aññeneva pādaṃ karomī”ti. “Idaṃ kho taṃ, mahārāja, tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena sandhāya bhāsitaṃ – ‘upaniyyati loko addhuvo’ti, yamahaṃ ñatvā ca disvā sutvā ca agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajito”ti. “Acchariyaṃ, bho raṭṭhapāla, abbhutaṃ, bho raṭṭhapāla! Yāva subhāsitaṃ cidaṃ tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena – ‘upaniyyati loko addhuvo’ti. Upaniyyati hi[T 2.0408], bho raṭṭhapāla, loko addhuvo.

306. “‘The world is swept away, it is not lasting’—so said the Venerable Raṭṭhapāla.” “How, Venerable Raṭṭhapāla, should the meaning of this statement be understood?” “What do you think, great king? When you were about twenty or twenty-five years of age, were you not skilled in elephantry, skilled in horsemanship, skilled in chariot-driving, skilled in archery, skilled in swordsmanship, strong of thigh, strong of arm, capable, and a frequenter of battlefields?” “Indeed, Venerable Raṭṭhapāla, when I was about twenty or twenty-five years of age, I was skilled in elephantry, skilled in horsemanship, skilled in chariot-driving, skilled in archery, skilled in swordsmanship, strong of thigh, strong of arm, capable, and a frequenter of battlefields. Sometimes, Venerable Raṭṭhapāla, I thought myself as if possessed of magical power; I did not see anyone equal to myself in strength.” “What do you think, great king? Are you now, in the same way, strong of thigh, strong of arm, capable, and a frequenter of battlefields?” “Not so, Venerable Raṭṭhapāla. Now I am decrepit, old, aged, far-gone in years, having reached the final stage of life; my age is eighty years. Sometimes, Venerable Raṭṭhapāla, intending to place my foot here, I place my foot elsewhere.” “It was with reference to this, great king, that the Blessed One, who knows and sees, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, said: ‘The world is swept away, it is not lasting.’ It was after knowing, seeing, and hearing this that I went forth from the household life into homelessness.” “It is wonderful, Venerable Raṭṭhapāla, it is marvelous, Venerable Raṭṭhapāla! How well-spoken indeed was this by the Blessed One, who knows and sees, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One: ‘The world is swept away, it is not lasting.’ For indeed, Venerable Raṭṭhapāla, the world is swept away; it is not lasting.”

“Saṃvijjante kho, bho raṭṭhapāla, imasmiṃ rājakule hatthikāyāpi assakāyāpi rathakāyāpi pattikāyāpi, amhākaṃ āpadāsu pariyodhāya [P 2.0070] vattissanti. ‘Atāṇo loko anabhissaro’ti – bhavaṃ raṭṭhapālo āha. Imassa pana, bho raṭṭhapāla, bhāsitassa kathaṃ attho daṭṭhabbo”ti? “Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, mahārāja, atthi te koci anusāyiko ābādho”ti? “Atthi me, bho raṭṭhapāla, anusāyiko ābādho. Appekadā maṃ, bho raṭṭhapāla, mittāmaccā ñātisālohitā [V 2.0267] parivāretvā ṭhitā honti – ‘idāni rājā korabyo kālaṃ karissati, idāni rājā korabyo kālaṃ karissatī’”ti. “Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, mahārāja, labhasi tvaṃ [M 2.0258] te mittāmacce ñātisālohite – ‘āyantu me bhonto mittāmaccā ñātisālohitā, sabbeva santā imaṃ vedanaṃ saṃvibhajatha, yathāhaṃ lahukatarikaṃ vedanaṃ vediyeyya’nti – udāhu tvaṃyeva taṃ vedanaṃ vediyasī”ti? “Nāhaṃ, bho raṭṭhapāla, labhāmi te mittāmacce ñātisālohite – ‘āyantu me bhonto mittāmaccā ñātisālohitā, sabbeva santā imaṃ vedanaṃ saṃvibhajatha, yathāhaṃ lahukatarikaṃ vedanaṃ vediyeyya’nti.
