360. “Venerable Ānanda, what then is the bodily conduct that is censurable by wise ascetics and brahmins?” “Great King, it is that bodily conduct which is unwholesome.”

“Katamo [V 2.0324] pana, bhante, kāyasamācāro akusalo”? “Yo kho, mahārāja, kāyasamācāro sāvajjo”.

“Venerable sir, what then is unwholesome bodily conduct?” “Great King, it is that bodily conduct which is blameworthy.”

“Katamo pana, bhante, kāyasamācāro sāvajjo”? “Yo kho, mahārāja, kāyasamācāro sabyābajjho” sabyāpajjho (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.), sabyāpajjo (ka.).

“Venerable sir, what then is blameworthy bodily conduct?” “Great King, it is that bodily conduct which is with affliction.”

“Katamo [M 2.0317] pana, bhante, kāyasamācāro sabyābajjho”? “Yo kho, mahārāja, kāyasamācāro dukkhavipāko”.

“Venerable sir, what then is bodily conduct that is with affliction?” “Great King, it is that bodily conduct which has a painful result.”

“Katamo pana, bhante, kāyasamācāro dukkhavipāko”? “Yo kho, mahārāja, kāyasamācāro attabyābādhāyapi saṃvattati, parabyābādhāyapi saṃvattati, ubhayabyābādhāyapi saṃvattati tassa akusalā dhammā abhivaḍḍhanti, kusalā dhammā parihāyanti; evarūpo kho, mahārāja, kāyasamācāro opārambho samaṇehi brāhmaṇehi viññūhī”ti.

“Venerable sir, what then is bodily conduct that has a painful result?” “Great King, it is that bodily conduct which conduces to one's own affliction, to the affliction of others, and to the affliction of both. For that person, unwholesome states increase and wholesome states diminish. Such bodily conduct, Great King, is censurable by wise ascetics and brahmins.”

“Katamo pana, bhante ānanda, vacīsamācāro…pe… manosamācāro opārambho samaṇehi brāhmaṇehi viññūhī”ti? “Yo kho, mahārāja, manosamācāro akusalo”.

“Venerable Ānanda, what then is the verbal conduct… what then is the mental conduct that is censurable by wise ascetics and brahmins?” “Great King, it is that mental conduct which is unwholesome.”

“Katamo pana, bhante, manosamācāro akusalo”? “Yo [P 2.0115] kho, mahārāja, manosamācāro sāvajjo”.

“Venerable sir, what then is unwholesome mental conduct?” “Great King, it is that mental conduct which is blameworthy.”

“Katamo pana, bhante, manosamācāro sāvajjo”? “Yo kho, mahārāja, manosamācāro sabyābajjho”.

“Venerable sir, what then is blameworthy mental conduct?” “Great King, it is that mental conduct which is with affliction.”

“Katamo [T 2.0502] pana, bhante, manosamācāro sabyābajjho”? “Yo kho, mahārāja, manosamācāro dukkhavipāko”.

“Venerable sir, what then is mental conduct that is with affliction?” “Great King, it is that mental conduct which has a painful result.”

“Katamo pana, bhante, manosamācāro dukkhavipāko”? “Yo kho, mahārāja, manosamācāro [V 2.0325] attabyābādhāyapi saṃvattati, parabyābādhāyapi saṃvattati, ubhayabyābādhāyapi saṃvattati tassa akusalā dhammā abhivaḍḍhanti, kusalā dhammā parihāyanti; evarūpo kho, mahārāja, manosamācāro opārambho samaṇehi brāhmaṇehi viññūhī”ti.

“Venerable sir, what then is mental conduct that has a painful result?” “Great King, it is that mental conduct which conduces to one's own affliction, to the affliction of others, and to the affliction of both. For that person, unwholesome states increase and wholesome states diminish. Such mental conduct, Great King, is censurable by wise ascetics and brahmins.”

“Kiṃ nu kho, bhante ānanda, so bhagavā sabbesaṃyeva akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānaṃ vaṇṇetī”ti? “Sabbākusaladhammapahīno kho, mahārāja, tathāgato kusaladhammasamannāgato”ti.

“Venerable Ānanda, does that Blessed One then praise the abandoning of all unwholesome states whatsoever?” “Great King, the Tathāgata has indeed abandoned all unwholesome states and is endowed with wholesome states.”

361. “Katamo pana, bhante ānanda, kāyasamācāro anopārambho samaṇehi brāhmaṇehi viññūhī”ti? “Yo kho, mahārāja, kāyasamācāro kusalo”.

361. “Venerable Ānanda, what then is the bodily conduct that is irreproachable by wise ascetics and brahmins?” “Great King, it is that bodily conduct which is wholesome.”

“Katamo [M 2.0318] pana, bhante, kāyasamācāro kusalo”? “Yo kho, mahārāja, kāyasamācāro anavajjo”.

“Venerable sir, what then is wholesome bodily conduct?” “Great King, it is that bodily conduct which is blameless.”

“Katamo pana, bhante, kāyasamācāro anavajjo”? “Yo kho, mahārāja, kāyasamācāro abyābajjho”.

“Venerable sir, what then is blameless bodily conduct?” “Great King, it is that bodily conduct which is without affliction.”

“Katamo pana, bhante, kāyasamācāro abyābajjho”? “Yo kho, mahārāja, kāyasamācāro sukhavipāko”.

“Venerable sir, what then is bodily conduct that is without affliction?” “Great King, it is that bodily conduct which has a pleasant result.”

“Katamo pana, bhante, kāyasamācāro sukhavipāko”?

“Venerable sir, what then is bodily conduct that has a pleasant result?”

“Yo kho, mahārāja, kāyasamācāro nevattabyābādhāyapi saṃvattati, na parabyābādhāyapi saṃvattati, na ubhayabyābādhāyapi saṃvattati tassa akusalā dhammā parihāyanti, kusalā dhammā [T 2.0503] abhivaḍḍhanti; evarūpo kho, mahārāja, kāyasamācāro anopārambho samaṇehi brāhmaṇehi viññūhī”ti.

“Great King, it is that bodily conduct which conduces neither to one's own affliction, nor to the affliction of others, nor to the affliction of both. For that person, unwholesome states diminish and wholesome states increase. Such bodily conduct, Great King, is irreproachable by wise ascetics and brahmins.”

“Katamo pana, bhante ānanda, vacīsamācāro…pe… manosamācāro anopārambho samaṇehi brāhmaṇehi viññūhī”ti? “Yo kho, mahārāja, manosamācāro kusalo”.

“Venerable Ānanda, what then is the verbal conduct… what then is the mental conduct that is irreproachable by wise ascetics and brahmins?” “Great King, it is that mental conduct which is wholesome.”

“Katamo [V 2.0326][P 2.0116] pana, bhante, manosamācāro kusalo”? “Yo kho, mahārāja, manosamācāro anavajjo”.

“Venerable sir, what then is wholesome mental conduct?” “Great King, it is that mental conduct which is blameless.”

“Katamo pana, bhante, manosamācāro anavajjo”? “Yo kho, mahārāja, manosamācāro abyābajjho”.

“Venerable sir, what then is blameless mental conduct?” “Great King, it is that mental conduct which is without affliction.”

“Katamo pana, bhante, manosamācāro abyābajjho”? “Yo kho, mahārāja, manosamācāro sukhavipāko”.

“Venerable sir, what then is mental conduct that is without affliction?” “Great King, it is that mental conduct which has a pleasant result.”

“Katamo pana, bhante, manosamācāro sukhavipāko”? “Yo kho, mahārāja, manosamācāro nevattabyābādhāyapi saṃvattati, na parabyābādhāyapi saṃvattati, na ubhayabyābādhāyapi saṃvattati. Tassa akusalā dhammā parihāyanti, kusalā dhammā abhivaḍḍhanti. Evarūpo kho, mahārāja, manosamācāro anopārambho samaṇehi brāhmaṇehi viññūhī”ti.

“Venerable sir, what then is mental conduct that has a pleasant result?” “Great King, it is that mental conduct which conduces neither to one's own affliction, nor to the affliction of others, nor to the affliction of both. For that person, unwholesome states diminish and wholesome states increase. Such mental conduct, Great King, is irreproachable by wise ascetics and brahmins.”

“Kiṃ pana, bhante ānanda, so bhagavā sabbesaṃyeva kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ upasampadaṃ vaṇṇetī”ti? “Sabbākusaladhammapahīno kho, mahārāja, tathāgato kusaladhammasamannāgato”ti.

“Venerable Ānanda, does that Blessed One then praise the accomplishment of all wholesome states whatsoever?” “Great King, the Tathāgata has indeed abandoned all unwholesome states and is endowed with wholesome states.”

362. “Acchariyaṃ[M 2.0319], bhante, abbhutaṃ, bhante! Yāva subhāsitaṃ cidaṃ subhāsitamidaṃ (sī.), bhante, āyasmatā ānandena. Iminā ca mayaṃ, bhante, āyasmato ānandassa subhāsitena attamanābhiraddhā. Evaṃ attamanābhiraddhā ca mayaṃ[T 2.0504], bhante, āyasmato ānandassa subhāsitena. Sace, bhante, āyasmato ānandassa hatthiratanaṃ kappeyya, hatthiratanampi mayaṃ āyasmato ānandassa dadeyyāma. Sace, bhante, āyasmato ānandassa assaratanaṃ kappeyya, assaratanampi mayaṃ āyasmato ānandassa dadeyyāma. Sace, bhante, āyasmato ānandassa gāmavaraṃ kappeyya, gāmavarampi mayaṃ āyasmato ānandassa dadeyyāma. Api ca, bhante, mayampetaṃ mayameva taṃ (sī.), mayampanetaṃ (syā. kaṃ.) jānāma – ‘netaṃ āyasmato ānandassa kappatī’ti. Ayaṃ me, bhante, bāhitikā raññā māgadhena ajātasattunā vedehiputtena vatthanāḷiyā chattanāḷiyā (syā. kaṃ. pī.) pakkhipitvā pahitā soḷasasamā āyāmena, aṭṭhasamā vitthārena[V 2.0327]. Taṃ, bhante, āyasmā ānando paṭiggaṇhātu anukampaṃ upādāyā”ti. “Alaṃ, mahārāja, paripuṇṇaṃ me ticīvara”nti.

362. “Wonderful, Venerable Sir! Marvelous, Venerable Sir! How well spoken this is by the Venerable Ānanda. And we, Venerable Sir, are pleased and delighted with the Venerable Ānanda’s well-spoken words. Indeed, being so pleased and delighted with the Venerable Ānanda’s well-spoken words, Venerable Sir, if an elephant-treasure were fitting for the Venerable Ānanda, we would give the Venerable Ānanda an elephant-treasure. If a horse-treasure were fitting for the Venerable Ānanda, we would give the Venerable Ānanda a horse-treasure. If a choice village were fitting for the Venerable Ānanda, we would give the Venerable Ānanda a choice village. Moreover, Venerable Sir, we know this: ‘This is not fitting for the Venerable Ānanda.’ This, Venerable Sir, is a Bāhitika cloth sent to me by King Ajātasattu of Magadha, son of the Videhan queen, placed in a cloth wrapping—sixteen cubits in length and eight cubits in width. Venerable Sir, may the Venerable Ānanda accept it out of compassion.” “Enough, Great King. My three robes are complete.”

“Ayaṃ[P 2.0117], bhante, aciravatī nadī diṭṭhā āyasmatā ceva ānandena amhehi ca. Yadā uparipabbate mahāmegho abhippavuṭṭho hoti, athāyaṃ aciravatī nadī ubhato kūlāni saṃvissandantī gacchati; evameva kho, bhante, āyasmā ānando imāya bāhitikāya attano ticīvaraṃ karissati. Yaṃ panāyasmato ānandassa purāṇaṃ ticīvaraṃ taṃ sabrahmacārīhi saṃvibhajissati. Evāyaṃ amhākaṃ dakkhiṇā saṃvissandantī maññe gamissati. Paṭiggaṇhātu, bhante, āyasmā ānando bāhitika”nti. Paṭiggahesi kho āyasmā ānando [T 2.0505] bāhitikaṃ.

“Venerable Sir, this Aciravatī River has been seen by the Venerable Ānanda and by us. When a great rain cloud pours down on the mountaintop, then this Aciravatī River flows, overflowing both banks. In the same way, Venerable Sir, the Venerable Ānanda will make his own triple robe from this Bāhitika cloth. And whatever old triple robe the Venerable Ānanda has, he will share it with his fellows in the holy life. Thus, our offering, I think, will flow forth. Venerable Sir, may the Venerable Ānanda accept the Bāhitika cloth.” The Venerable Ānanda accepted the Bāhitika cloth.

Atha kho rājā pasenadi kosalo āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ etadavoca – “handa ca dāni mayaṃ, bhante ānanda, gacchāma; bahukiccā mayaṃ bahukaraṇīyā”ti. “Yassadāni tvaṃ, mahārāja, kālaṃ maññasī”ti. Atha kho rājā pasenadi kosalo āyasmato ānandassa bhāsitaṃ abhinanditvā anumoditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā pakkāmi.

Then King Pasenadi of Kosala said to the Venerable Ānanda: “Well then, Venerable Ānanda, we shall now depart; we have much to do, many duties to attend to.” “Great King, you may now depart at the time you think fit.” Then King Pasenadi of Kosala, having rejoiced in and approved of the Venerable Ānanda’s words, rose from his seat, paid homage to the Venerable Ānanda, circumambulated him, keeping him to the right, and departed.

363. Atha [M 2.0320] kho āyasmā ānando acirapakkantassa rañño pasenadissa kosalassa yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā ānando yāvatako ahosi raññā pasenadinā kosalena saddhiṃ kathāsallāpo taṃ sabbaṃ bhagavato ārocesi. Tañca bāhitikaṃ bhagavato pādāsi. Atha kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – “lābhā, bhikkhave, rañño pasenadissa kosalassa, suladdhalābhā, bhikkhave, rañño pasenadissa kosalassa; yaṃ rājā pasenadi kosalo labhati ānandaṃ dassanāya, labhati payirupāsanāyā”ti.

363. Then, soon after King Pasenadi of Kosala had departed, the Venerable Ānanda approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the Venerable Ānanda reported to the Blessed One the entire conversation he had with King Pasenadi of Kosala. He also presented the Bāhitika cloth to the Blessed One. Then the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus: “It is a gain, bhikkhus, for King Pasenadi of Kosala; it is a great gain, bhikkhus, for King Pasenadi of Kosala, that King Pasenadi of Kosala gets to see Ānanda and gets to attend upon him.”

Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamanā te bhikkhū bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandunti.

This the Blessed One said. Pleased, those bhikkhus delighted in the Blessed One’s words.

Bāhitikasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ aṭṭhamaṃ.

The Bāhitika Sutta, the eighth, is concluded.

9. Dhammacetiyasuttaṃ

9. The Discourse on Monuments to the Dhamma

364. Evaṃ [T 2.0506][V 2.0328][P 2.0118] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sakkesu viharati medāḷupaṃ metaḷūpaṃ (sī.), medaḷumpaṃ (pī.) nāma sakyānaṃ nigamo. Tena kho pana samayena rājā pasenadi kosalo nagarakaṃ anuppatto hoti kenacideva karaṇīyena. Atha kho rājā pasenadi kosalo dīghaṃ kārāyanaṃ āmantesi – “yojehi, samma kārāyana, bhadrāni bhadrāni yānāni, uyyānabhūmiṃ gacchāma subhūmiṃ dassanāyā”ti subhūmidassanāyāti (dī. ni. 2.43). “Evaṃ, devā”ti kho dīgho kārāyano rañño pasenadissa kosalassa paṭissutvā bhadrāni bhadrāni yānāni yojāpetvā rañño pasenadissa kosalassa paṭivedesi – “yuttāni kho te, deva, bhadrāni bhadrāni yānāni. Yassadāni kālaṃ maññasī”ti. Atha kho rājā pasenadi kosalo bhadraṃ yānaṃ abhiruhitvā bhadrehi bhadrehi yānehi nagarakamhā niyyāsi mahaccā rājānubhāvena. Yena ārāmo tena pāyāsi. Yāvatikā yānassa bhūmi yānena gantvā yānā paccorohitvā pattikova ārāmaṃ pāvisi. Addasā kho rājā pasenadi kosalo ārāme jaṅghāvihāraṃ anucaṅkamamāno anuvicaramāno [M 2.0321] rukkhamūlāni pāsādikāni pasādanīyāni appasaddāni appanigghosāni vijanavātāni manussarāhasseyyakāni manussarāhaseyyakāni (sī. pī.) paṭisallānasāruppāni. Disvāna bhagavantaṃyeva ārabbha sati udapādi – “imāni kho tāni rukkhamūlāni pāsādikāni pasādanīyāni appasaddāni [T 2.0507] appanigghosāni vijanavātāni manussarāhasseyyakāni paṭisallānasāruppāni, yattha sudaṃ mayaṃ taṃ bhagavantaṃ payirupāsāma arahantaṃ sammāsambuddha”nti.

364. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling among the Sakyans in a market town of the Sakyans named Medāḷupa. Now at that time, King Pasenadi of Kosala had arrived at Nagaraka on some business. Then King Pasenadi of Kosala addressed Dīgha Kārāyana: “Good Kārāyana, harness the finest carriages. Let us go to the park grounds to see the beautiful grounds.” “As you say, Your Majesty,” Dīgha Kārāyana replied. Having had the finest carriages harnessed, he informed King Pasenadi of Kosala: “The finest carriages are harnessed for you, Your Majesty. Now is the time for what you deem fit.” Then King Pasenadi of Kosala mounted a fine carriage and, with the finest carriages, departed from Nagaraka with great royal majesty. He proceeded toward the park. He went by carriage as far as the ground was passable for a carriage, then dismounted and entered the park on foot. In the park, while walking and wandering about, King Pasenadi of Kosala saw the roots of trees that were inspiring, confidence-inspiring, quiet, with little noise, secluded from people, suitable for privacy, and fit for solitude. Upon seeing them, mindfulness arose in him directed toward the Blessed One: “These roots of trees are indeed inspiring, confidence-inspiring, quiet, with little noise, secluded from people, suitable for privacy, and fit for solitude, just like those places where we used to attend upon that Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One.”

365. Atha kho rājā pasenadi kosalo dīghaṃ kārāyanaṃ āmantesi – “imāni kho, samma kārāyana, tāni rukkhamūlāni pāsādikāni pasādanīyāni appasaddāni appanigghosāni vijanavātāni manussarāhasseyyakāni paṭisallānasāruppāni, yattha sudaṃ mayaṃ taṃ bhagavantaṃ payirupāsāma arahantaṃ sammāsambuddhaṃ. Kahaṃ nu kho, samma kārāyana, etarahi so bhagavā [P 2.0119] viharati arahaṃ sammāsambuddho”ti? “Atthi, mahārāja, medāḷupaṃ nāma sakyānaṃ nigamo. Tattha so bhagavā etarahi viharati arahaṃ sammāsambuddho”ti. “Kīvadūre kīvadūro (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) pana, samma kārāyana[V 2.0329], nagarakamhā medāḷupaṃ nāma sakyānaṃ nigamo hotī”ti? “Na dūre, mahārāja; tīṇi yojanāni; sakkā divasāvasesena gantu”nti. “Tena hi, samma kārāyana, yojehi bhadrāni bhadrāni yānāni, gamissāma mayaṃ taṃ bhagavantaṃ dassanāya arahantaṃ sammāsambuddha”nti. “Evaṃ, devā”ti kho dīgho kārāyano rañño pasenadissa kosalassa paṭissutvā bhadrāni bhadrāni yānāni yojāpetvā rañño pasenadissa kosalassa paṭivedesi – “yuttāni kho te, deva, bhadrāni bhadrāni yānāni. Yassadāni kālaṃ maññasī”ti. Atha kho rājā pasenadi kosalo bhadraṃ yānaṃ abhiruhitvā bhadrehi bhadrehi yānehi nagarakamhā yena medāḷupaṃ nāma sakyānaṃ [T 2.0508] nigamo tena pāyāsi. Teneva divasāvasesena medāḷupaṃ nāma sakyānaṃ nigamaṃ sampāpuṇi. Yena ārāmo tena pāyāsi. Yāvatikā yānassa bhūmi yānena gantvā yānā paccorohitvā pattikova ārāmaṃ pāvisi.

365. Then King Pasenadi of Kosala addressed Dīgha Kārāyana: “Good Kārāyana, these roots of trees are inspiring, confidence-inspiring, quiet, with little noise, secluded from people, suitable for privacy, and fit for solitude, just like those places where we used to attend upon that Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One. Where, I wonder, good Kārāyana, is that Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, now dwelling?” “There is, Great King, a market town of the Sakyans named Medāḷupa. That Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, is now dwelling there.” “But how far, good Kārāyana, is the market town of the Sakyans named Medāḷupa from Nagaraka?” “Not far, Great King; three yojanas. It is possible to go there with the remainder of the day.” “In that case, good Kārāyana, harness the finest carriages. We shall go to see that Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One.” “As you say, Your Majesty,” Dīgha Kārāyana replied to King Pasenadi of Kosala. Having had the finest carriages harnessed, he informed the king: “The finest carriages are harnessed for you, Your Majesty. Now is the time for what you deem fit.” Then King Pasenadi of Kosala mounted a fine carriage and, with the finest carriages, set out from Nagaraka toward the market town of the Sakyans named Medāḷupa. With the remainder of that very day, he reached the market town of the Sakyans named Medāḷupa. He proceeded to the park. He went by carriage as far as the ground was passable for a carriage, then dismounted from the carriage and entered the park on foot.

366. Tena kho pana samayena sambahulā bhikkhū abbhokāse caṅkamanti. Atha kho rājā pasenadi kosalo yena te bhikkhū tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā te bhikkhū etadavoca – “kahaṃ nu kho, bhante, etarahi [M 2.0322] so bhagavā viharati arahaṃ sammāsambuddho? Dassanakāmā hi mayaṃ taṃ bhagavantaṃ arahantaṃ sammāsambuddha”nti. “Eso, mahārāja, vihāro saṃvutadvāro. Tena appasaddo upasaṅkamitvā ataramāno āḷindaṃ pavisitvā ukkāsitvā aggaḷaṃ ākoṭehi. Vivarissati bhagavā te dvāra”nti. Atha kho rājā pasenadi kosalo tattheva khaggañca uṇhīsañca dīghassa kārāyanassa pādāsi. Atha kho dīghassa kārāyanassa etadahosi – “rahāyati kho dāni rājā mahārājā (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.), idheva tenidheva (sī.) dāni mayā ṭhātabba”nti. Atha kho rājā pasenadi kosalo yena so vihāro saṃvutadvāro tena appasaddo upasaṅkamitvā ataramāno āḷindaṃ pavisitvā ukkāsitvā aggaḷaṃ ākoṭesi. Vivari bhagavā dvāraṃ. Atha kho rājā pasenadi kosalo vihāraṃ [P 2.0120] pavisitvā bhagavato pādesu sirasā nipatitvā bhagavato pādāni mukhena ca paricumbati, pāṇīhi ca parisambāhati, nāmañca sāveti – “rājāhaṃ, bhante, pasenadi kosalo; rājāhaṃ, bhante, pasenadi [T 2.0509] kosalo”ti.

366. Now at that time, a number of bhikkhus were walking up and down in the open. Then King Pasenadi of Kosala approached those bhikkhus. Having approached, he said to them: “Venerable sirs, where, I wonder, is the Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, now dwelling? For we are desirous of seeing that Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One.” “That, Great King, is the dwelling with the closed door. Approach it quietly, without hurrying, enter the porch, clear your throat, and knock on the door bolt. The Blessed One will open the door for you.” Then King Pasenadi of Kosala right there gave his sword and turban to Dīgha Kārāyana. Then this thought occurred to Dīgha Kārāyana: “The king now seeks privacy. I should stay right here.” Then King Pasenadi of Kosala approached that dwelling with the closed door quietly, without hurrying, entered the porch, cleared his throat, and knocked on the door bolt. The Blessed One opened the door. Then King Pasenadi of Kosala entered the dwelling, fell with his head at the Blessed One’s feet, kissed the Blessed One’s feet with his mouth and massaged them with his hands, and announced his name: “I, venerable sir, am King Pasenadi of Kosala; I, venerable sir, am King Pasenadi of Kosala.”

367. “Kiṃ pana tvaṃ, mahārāja, atthavasaṃ sampassamāno imasmiṃ sarīre evarūpaṃ paramanipaccakāraṃ karosi, mittūpahāraṃ cittūpahāraṃ (sī.) upadaṃsesī”ti? “Atthi kho me, bhante, bhagavati dhammanvayo [V 2.0330] – ‘hoti sammāsambuddho bhagavā, svākkhāto bhagavatā dhammo, suppaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho’ti. Idhāhaṃ, bhante, passāmi eke samaṇabrāhmaṇe pariyantakataṃ brahmacariyaṃ carante dasapi vassāni, vīsampi vassāni, tiṃsampi vassāni, cattārīsampi vassāni. Te aparena samayena sunhātā suvilittā kappitakesamassū pañcahi kāmaguṇehi samappitā samaṅgībhūtā paricārenti. Idha panāhaṃ, bhante, bhikkhū passāmi yāvajīvaṃ āpāṇakoṭikaṃ paripuṇṇaṃ parisuddhaṃ brahmacariyaṃ carante. Na kho panāhaṃ, bhante, ito bahiddhā aññaṃ evaṃ paripuṇṇaṃ parisuddhaṃ brahmacariyaṃ samanupassāmi. Ayampi kho me, bhante, bhagavati dhammanvayo hoti – ‘sammāsambuddho bhagavā, svākkhāto bhagavatā dhammo, suppaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho”ti.

367. “Great King, seeing what special benefit do you perform such supreme reverence towards this body and show this offering of affection?” “Venerable sir, I have this inference based on the Dhamma regarding the Blessed One: ‘The Blessed One is a Perfectly Enlightened One; the Dhamma is well-expounded by the Blessed One; the Saṅgha of the Blessed One’s disciples is practicing the good way.’ Here, venerable sir, I see some ascetics and brahmins who practice a holy life with a set limit for ten years, twenty years, thirty years, or forty years. Then, at a later time, well-bathed, well-anointed, with hair and beard trimmed, they enjoy themselves, provided and endowed with the five strands of sensual pleasure. But here, venerable sir, I see bhikkhus who practice the holy life that is complete and pure for their entire lives, to their last breath. Indeed, venerable sir, outside of this Dispensation I do not see any other holy life so complete and pure. This too, venerable sir, is my inference based on the Dhamma regarding the Blessed One: ‘The Blessed One is a Perfectly Enlightened One; the Dhamma is well-expounded by the Blessed One; the Saṅgha of the Blessed One’s disciples is practicing the good way.’”

368. “Puna caparaṃ, bhante, rājānopi rājūhi vivadanti, khattiyāpi khattiyehi vivadanti, brāhmaṇāpi brāhmaṇehi vivadanti, gahapatayopi gahapatīhi [M 2.0323] vivadanti, mātāpi puttena vivadati, puttopi mātarā vivadati, pitāpi puttena vivadati, puttopi pitarā vivadati, bhātāpi bhaginiyā vivadati[T 2.0510], bhaginīpi bhātarā vivadati, sahāyopi sahāyena vivadati. Idha panāhaṃ, bhante, bhikkhū passāmi samagge sammodamāne avivadamāne khīrodakībhūte aññamaññaṃ [P 2.0121] piyacakkhūhi sampassante viharante. Na kho panāhaṃ, bhante, ito bahiddhā aññaṃ evaṃ samaggaṃ parisaṃ samanupassāmi. Ayampi kho me, bhante, bhagavati dhammanvayo hoti – ‘sammāsambuddho bhagavā, svākkhāto bhagavatā dhammo, suppaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho’ti.

368. “Furthermore, venerable sir, kings dispute with kings, khattiyas dispute with khattiyas, brahmins dispute with brahmins, householders dispute with householders, a mother disputes with her son, a son disputes with his mother, a father disputes with his son, a son disputes with his father, a brother disputes with his sister, a sister disputes with her brother, and a friend disputes with a friend. But here, venerable sir, I see bhikkhus dwelling in harmony, rejoicing together, without disputing, having become like milk and water, regarding one another with loving eyes. Indeed, venerable sir, outside of this Dispensation I do not see any other assembly so harmonious. This too, venerable sir, is my inference based on the Dhamma regarding the Blessed One: ‘The Blessed One is a Perfectly Enlightened One; the Dhamma is well-expounded by the Blessed One; the Saṅgha of the Blessed One’s disciples is practicing the good way.’”

369. “Puna caparāhaṃ, bhante, ārāmena ārāmaṃ, uyyānena uyyānaṃ anucaṅkamāmi anuvicarāmi. Sohaṃ tattha passāmi eke samaṇabrāhmaṇe kise lūkhe dubbaṇṇe uppaṇḍuppaṇḍukajāte dhamanisanthatagatte, na viya maññe cakkhuṃ bandhante janassa dassanāya. Tassa mayhaṃ, bhante, etadahosi – ‘addhā ime āyasmanto anabhiratā vā brahmacariyaṃ caranti, atthi vā tesaṃ kiñci pāpaṃ kammaṃ kataṃ paṭicchannaṃ; tathā hi ime āyasmanto kisā lūkhā dubbaṇṇā uppaṇḍuppaṇḍukajātā dhamanisanthatagattā, na viya maññe cakkhuṃ bandhanti janassa dassanāyā’ti. Tyāhaṃ upasaṅkamitvā evaṃ vadāmi – ‘kiṃ nu kho tumhe āyasmanto kisā lūkhā dubbaṇṇā uppaṇḍuppaṇḍukajātā dhamanisanthatagattā, na viya maññe cakkhuṃ bandhatha janassa dassanāyā’ti? Te evamāhaṃsu – ‘bandhukarogo no paṇḍukarogino (ka.), mahārājā’ti. Idha panāhaṃ, bhante, bhikkhū [T 2.0511] passāmi [V 2.0331] haṭṭhapahaṭṭhe udaggudagge abhiratarūpe pīṇindriye pīṇitindriye (sī. pī.) appossukke pannalome paradattavutte migabhūtena cetasā viharante. Tassa mayhaṃ, bhante, etadahosi – ‘addhā ime āyasmanto tassa bhagavato sāsane uḷāraṃ pubbenāparaṃ visesaṃ jānanti; tathā hi ime āyasmanto haṭṭhapahaṭṭhā udaggudaggā abhiratarūpā pīṇindriyā appossukkā pannalomā paradattavuttā migabhūtena cetasā viharantī’ti. Ayampi kho me, bhante, bhagavati dhammanvayo hoti – ‘sammāsambuddho bhagavā, svākkhāto bhagavatā dhammo, suppaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho’ti.

369. “Furthermore, venerable sir, I wander and roam from park to park, and from garden to garden. There I see some ascetics and brahmins who are emaciated, wretched, unsightly, and pallid, with bodies covered in veins, not, I think, captivating the eye for people to see. To me, venerable sir, this occurred: ‘Surely, these venerable ones are practicing the holy life without delight, or they have some evil deed that has been done and is concealed; that is why these venerable ones are emaciated, wretched, unsightly, and pallid, with bodies covered in veins, not, I think, captivating the eye for people to see.’ I approach them and say: ‘Venerable sirs, why are you emaciated, wretched, unsightly, and pallid, with bodies covered in veins, not, I think, captivating the eye for people to see?’ They reply: ‘We have a hereditary disease, great king.’ But here, venerable sir, I see bhikkhus who are joyful and elated, exultant, delighted, with gratified faculties, untroubled, with hair laid down, living on what is given by others, and dwelling with a mind like a wild deer's. To me, venerable sir, this occurred: ‘Surely, these venerable ones know a great and progressive distinction in the Blessed One’s Dispensation; that is why these venerable ones are joyful and elated, exultant, delighted, with gratified faculties, untroubled, with hair laid down, living on what is given by others, and dwelling with a mind like a wild deer's.’ This too, venerable sir, is my inference based on the Dhamma regarding the Blessed One: ‘The Blessed One is a Perfectly Self-Enlightened One; the Dhamma is well-expounded by the Blessed One; the Saṅgha of the Blessed One’s disciples is practicing the good way.’”

370. “Puna caparāhaṃ, bhante, rājā khattiyo muddhāvasitto; pahomi [P 2.0122] ghātetāyaṃ vā ghātetuṃ, jāpetāyaṃ vā jāpetuṃ, pabbājetāyaṃ vā pabbājetuṃ[M 2.0324]. Tassa mayhaṃ, bhante, aḍḍakaraṇe nisinnassa antarantarā kathaṃ opātenti. Sohaṃ na labhāmi – ‘mā me bhonto aḍḍakaraṇe nisinnassa antarantarā kathaṃ opātetha opātentu (sī.) upariselasutte pana “opātethā”tiyeva dissati, kathāpariyosānaṃ me bhonto āgamentū’ti. Tassa mayhaṃ, bhante, antarantarā kathaṃ opātenti. Idha panāhaṃ, bhante, bhikkhū passāmi; yasmiṃ samaye bhagavā anekasatāya parisāya dhammaṃ deseti, neva tasmiṃ samaye bhagavato sāvakānaṃ khipitasaddo vā hoti ukkāsitasaddo vā. Bhūtapubbaṃ, bhante, bhagavā anekasatāya parisāya dhammaṃ deseti. Tatraññataro bhagavato sāvako ukkāsi. Tamenaṃ aññataro sabrahmacārī [T 2.0512] jaṇṇukena ghaṭṭesi – ‘appasaddo āyasmā hotu, māyasmā saddamakāsi; satthā no bhagavā dhammaṃ desetī’ti. Tassa mayhaṃ, bhante, etadahosi – ‘acchariyaṃ vata, bho, abbhutaṃ vata, bho! Adaṇḍena vata kira, bho, asatthena evaṃ suvinītā parisā bhavissatī’ti! Na kho panāhaṃ, bhante, ito bahiddhā aññaṃ evaṃ suvinītaṃ parisaṃ samanupassāmi. Ayampi kho me, bhante, bhagavati dhammanvayo hoti – ‘sammāsambuddho bhagavā, svākkhāto bhagavatā dhammo, suppaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho’ti.

370. “Furthermore, venerable sir, I am a consecrated khattiya king; I am able to have executed those who deserve execution, to have fined those who deserve to be fined, and to have banished those who deserve to be banished. Yet, venerable sir, while I am sitting in the judgment hall, they interrupt my speech. I do not get the opportunity to say, ‘Sirs, do not interrupt my speech while I am sitting in the judgment hall; sirs, please wait until the conclusion of my speech.’ But, venerable sir, they do interrupt my speech. Here, however, venerable sir, I see the bhikkhus; when the Blessed One is teaching the Dhamma to an assembly of many hundreds, at that time there is not even the sound of a sneeze or a cough among the Blessed One’s disciples. Once in the past, venerable sir, the Blessed One was teaching the Dhamma to an assembly of many hundreds. There, a certain disciple of the Blessed One coughed. A certain fellow monk nudged him with his knee, saying: ‘Venerable one, be quiet; venerable one, do not make a sound. The Blessed One, our Teacher, is teaching the Dhamma.’ Then, venerable sir, this thought occurred to me: ‘Oh, it is wonderful! Oh, it is astonishing! Indeed, without a rod, without a weapon, an assembly will be so well-disciplined!’ I do not see, venerable sir, any other assembly outside of this Dispensation that is so well-disciplined. This too, venerable sir, is my inference based on the Dhamma regarding the Blessed One: ‘The Blessed One is a Perfectly Self-Enlightened One; the Dhamma is well-expounded by the Blessed One; the Saṅgha of the Blessed One’s disciples is practicing the good way.’”

371. “Puna caparāhaṃ, bhante, passāmi idhekacce khattiyapaṇḍite nipuṇe kataparappavāde vālavedhirūpe. Te bhindantā vobhindantā (sī.) maññe caranti paññāgatena diṭṭhigatāni. Te suṇanti – ‘samaṇo khalu, bho, gotamo amukaṃ nāma gāmaṃ vā nigamaṃ vā osarissatī’ti. Te pañhaṃ abhisaṅkharonti – ‘imaṃ mayaṃ pañhaṃ samaṇaṃ gotamaṃ upasaṅkamitvā pucchissāma. Evaṃ ce no puṭṭho evaṃ byākarissati, evamassa mayaṃ vādaṃ āropessāma; evaṃ cepi no puṭṭho evaṃ byākarissati, evampissa mayaṃ vādaṃ [V 2.0332] āropessāmā’ti. Te suṇanti – ‘samaṇo khalu, bho, gotamo amukaṃ nāma gāmaṃ vā nigamaṃ vā osaṭo’ti. Te yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamanti. Te bhagavā dhammiyā kathāya sandasseti samādapeti samuttejeti sampahaṃseti[P 2.0123]. Te bhagavatā dhammiyā kathāya sandassitā samādapitā samuttejitā sampahaṃsitā na ceva bhagavantaṃ pañhaṃ [T 2.0513] pucchanti, kuto vādaṃ āropessanti? Aññadatthu bhagavato sāvakā sampajjanti. Ayampi kho me, bhante, bhagavati dhammanvayo hoti – ‘sammāsambuddho [M 2.0325] bhagavā, svākkhāto bhagavatā dhammo, suppaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho’ti.

371. “Furthermore, venerable sir, I see here certain wise khattiyas who are subtle, skilled in the doctrines of others, and like archers who can split a horse-hair. They wander about as if shattering wrong views with their wisdom. They hear: ‘Sirs, the ascetic Gotama will be arriving at such and such a village or town.’ They formulate a question: ‘We will approach the ascetic Gotama and ask him this question. If, when asked, he answers us in this way, we will find fault with his statement in this way; and if, when asked, he answers us in that way, we will find fault with his statement in that way.’ They hear: ‘Sirs, the ascetic Gotama has arrived at such and such a village or town.’ They approach the Blessed One. The Blessed One instructs, encourages, inspires, and gladdens them with a talk on the Dhamma. Having been instructed, encouraged, inspired, and gladdened by the Blessed One with a talk on the Dhamma, they do not even ask the Blessed One the question, how then could they find fault with his statement? On the contrary, they become the Blessed One’s disciples. This too, venerable sir, is my inference based on the Dhamma regarding the Blessed One: ‘The Blessed One is a Perfectly Self-Enlightened One; the Dhamma is well-expounded by the Blessed One; the Saṅgha of the Blessed One’s disciples is practicing the good way.’”

372. “Puna caparāhaṃ, bhante, passāmi idhekacce brāhmaṇapaṇḍite…pe… gahapatipaṇḍite…pe… samaṇapaṇḍite nipuṇe kataparappavāde vālavedhirūpe. Te bhindantā maññe caranti paññāgatena diṭṭhigatāni. Te suṇanti – ‘samaṇo khalu, bho, gotamo amukaṃ nāma gāmaṃ vā nigamaṃ vā osarissatī’ti. Te pañhaṃ abhisaṅkharonti – ‘imaṃ mayaṃ pañhaṃ samaṇaṃ gotamaṃ upasaṅkamitvā pucchissāma. Evaṃ ce no puṭṭho evaṃ byākarissati, evamassa mayaṃ vādaṃ āropessāma; evaṃ cepi no puṭṭho evaṃ byākarissati, evampissa mayaṃ vādaṃ āropessāmā’ti. Te suṇanti – ‘samaṇo khalu, bho, gotamo amukaṃ nāma gāmaṃ vā nigamaṃ vā osaṭo’ti. Te yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamanti. Te bhagavā dhammiyā kathāya sandasseti samādapeti samuttejeti sampahaṃseti. Te bhagavatā dhammiyā kathāya sandassitā samādapitā samuttejitā sampahaṃsitā na ceva bhagavantaṃ pañhaṃ pucchanti, kuto vādaṃ āropessanti? Aññadatthu bhagavantaṃyeva okāsaṃ yācanti agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajjāya. Te bhagavā pabbājeti. Te tathāpabbajitā [T 2.0514] samānā ekā vūpakaṭṭhā appamattā ātāpino pahitattā viharantā nacirasseva – yassatthāya kulaputtā sammadeva agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajanti tadanuttaraṃ – brahmacariyapariyosānaṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharanti. Te evamāhaṃsu – ‘manaṃ vata, bho, anassāma; manaṃ vata, bho, panassāma’. Mayañhi pubbe assamaṇāva samānā samaṇāmhāti paṭijānimhā, abrāhmaṇāva samānā brāhmaṇāmhāti paṭijānimhā, anarahantova samānā arahantāmhāti paṭijānimhā. ‘Idāni khomha samaṇā, idāni khomha brāhmaṇā, idāni khomha arahanto’ti. Ayampi kho me, bhante, bhagavati dhammanvayo hoti – ‘sammāsambuddho bhagavā, svākkhāto bhagavatā dhammo, suppaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho’ti.

372. Furthermore, venerable sir, I see here certain wise brahmins… wise householders… wise ascetics who are subtle, skilled in the doctrines of others, and like archers who can split a horse-hair. They wander about as if shattering wrong views with their wisdom. They hear: ‘Sirs, the ascetic Gotama will be arriving at such and such a village or town.’ They formulate a question: ‘We will approach the ascetic Gotama and ask him this question. If, when asked, he answers us in this way, we will find fault with his statement in this way; and if, when asked, he answers us in that way, we will find fault with his statement in that way.’ They hear: ‘Sirs, the ascetic Gotama has arrived at such and such a village or town.’ They approach the Blessed One. The Blessed One instructs, encourages, inspires, and gladdens them with a talk on the Dhamma. Having been instructed, encouraged, inspired, and gladdened by the Blessed One with a talk on the Dhamma, they do not even ask the Blessed One the question, how then could they find fault with his statement? On the contrary, they ask the Blessed One himself for the opportunity to go forth from the household life into homelessness. The Blessed One gives them the going forth. Having thus gone forth, dwelling secluded, diligent, ardent, and resolute, before long they realize for themselves with direct knowledge, in this very life, that unsurpassed culmination of the holy life for which clansmen rightly go forth from the household life into homelessness, and having attained it, they dwell therein. They say thus: ‘Oh, sirs, we were nearly lost! Oh, sirs, we were nearly ruined! For previously, while not being ascetics, we claimed, “We are ascetics.” While not being brahmins, we claimed, “We are brahmins.” While not being arahants, we claimed, “We are arahants.” But now, indeed, we are ascetics. Now, indeed, we are brahmins. Now, indeed, we are arahants.’ This too, venerable sir, is for me an inference from the Dhamma concerning the Blessed One: ‘The Blessed One is a Perfectly Enlightened One, the Dhamma is well-proclaimed by the Blessed One, the Saṅgha of the Blessed One’s disciples is practicing the good way.’

373. “Puna [V 2.0333] caparāhaṃ, bhante, ime isidattapurāṇā thapatayo mamabhattā mamayānā, ahaṃ nesaṃ jīvikāya jīvitassa (sī.), jīvikaṃ (sī. aṭṭha.), jīvitaṃ (syā. kaṃ. pī. ka.) dātā, yasassa āhattā; atha [M 2.0326] ca pana no tathā mayi nipaccakāraṃ [P 2.0124] karonti yathā bhagavati. Bhūtapubbāhaṃ, bhante, senaṃ abbhuyyāto samāno ime ca isidattapurāṇā thapatayo vīmaṃsamāno aññatarasmiṃ sambādhe āvasathe vāsaṃ upagacchiṃ. Atha kho, bhante, ime isidattapurāṇā thapatayo bahudeva rattiṃ dhammiyā kathāya vītināmetvā, yato ahosi bhagavā [T 2.0515] assosuṃ kho bhagavantaṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) tato sīsaṃ katvā maṃ pādato karitvā nipajjiṃsu. Tassa mayhaṃ, bhante, etadahosi – ‘acchariyaṃ vata, bho, abbhutaṃ vata, bho! Ime isidattapurāṇā thapatayo mamabhattā mamayānā, ahaṃ nesaṃ jīvikāya dātā, yasassa āhattā; atha ca pana no tathā mayi nipaccakāraṃ karonti yathā bhagavati. Addhā ime āyasmanto tassa bhagavato sāsane uḷāraṃ pubbenāparaṃ visesaṃ jānantī’ti. Ayampi kho me, bhante, bhagavati dhammanvayo hoti – ‘sammāsambuddho bhagavā, svākkhāto bhagavatā dhammo, suppaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho’ti.

373. Furthermore, venerable sir, these carpenters Isidatta and Purāṇa are sustained by my food and use my vehicles; I am the giver of their livelihood and the bringer of their renown. Yet they do not show me the same reverence as they do to the Blessed One. Once, venerable sir, when I had gone forth on a military campaign, while observing these carpenters Isidatta and Purāṇa, I took up lodging in a certain cramped dwelling. Then, venerable sir, these carpenters Isidatta and Purāṇa, having spent much of the night in discussion on the Dhamma, lay down placing their heads in the direction where the Blessed One was and their feet towards me. To me, venerable sir, this thought occurred: ‘It is wonderful, sirs, it is astonishing, sirs! These carpenters Isidatta and Purāṇa are sustained by my food and use my vehicles; I am the giver of their livelihood and the bringer of their renown. Yet they do not show me the same reverence as they do to the Blessed One. Surely these venerable ones know some great and subsequent distinction in the Blessed One’s Dispensation.’ This too, venerable sir, is my reasoning according to the Dhamma concerning the Blessed One: ‘The Blessed One is a Perfectly Enlightened One, the Dhamma is well-expounded by the Blessed One, the Saṅgha of the Blessed One’s disciples has practiced well.’

374. “Puna caparaṃ, bhante, bhagavāpi khattiyo, ahampi khattiyo; bhagavāpi kosalo, ahampi kosalo; bhagavāpi āsītiko, ahampi āsītiko. Yampi, bhante, bhagavāpi khattiyo ahampi khattiyo, bhagavāpi kosalo ahampi kosalo, bhagavāpi āsītiko ahampi āsītiko; imināvārahāmevāhaṃ imināpāhaṃ (ka.), bhante, bhagavati paramanipaccakāraṃ kātuṃ, mittūpahāraṃ upadaṃsetuṃ. Handa, ca dāni mayaṃ, bhante, gacchāma; bahukiccā mayaṃ bahukaraṇīyā”ti. “Yassadāni tvaṃ, mahārāja, kālaṃ maññasī”ti. Atha kho rājā pasenadi kosalo uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā pakkāmi. Atha kho bhagavā acirapakkantassa rañño pasenadissa kosalassa bhikkhū āmantesi – “eso, bhikkhave, rājā pasenadi kosalo dhammacetiyāni [T 2.0516] bhāsitvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkanto. Uggaṇhatha, bhikkhave, dhammacetiyāni; pariyāpuṇātha, bhikkhave[P 2.0125], dhammacetiyāni; dhāretha, bhikkhave, dhammacetiyāni. Atthasaṃhitāni, bhikkhave, dhammacetiyāni ādibrahmacariyakānī”ti.

374. Furthermore, venerable sir, the Blessed One is a khattiya, and I too am a khattiya; the Blessed One is a Kosalan, and I too am a Kosalan; the Blessed One is eighty years old, and I too am eighty years old. In that the Blessed One is a khattiya and I too am a khattiya, the Blessed One is a Kosalan and I too am a Kosalan, the Blessed One is eighty years old and I too am eighty years old—for this reason, venerable sir, it is fitting for me to pay the utmost reverence to the Blessed One and to show a friendly offering. And now, venerable sir, we shall depart; we have many duties, much to do.” “Now, great king, is the time for you to do as you see fit.” Then King Pasenadi of Kosala rose from his seat, paid homage to the Blessed One, circumambulated him keeping his right side toward him, and departed. Soon after King Pasenadi of Kosala had departed, the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus, this King Pasenadi of Kosala, having spoken these monuments to the Dhamma, has risen from his seat and departed. Learn these monuments to the Dhamma, bhikkhus; master these monuments to the Dhamma; bear in mind these monuments to the Dhamma. These monuments to the Dhamma are connected with benefit, bhikkhus, and are fundamental to the holy life.”

Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamanā te bhikkhū bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandunti.

The Blessed One said this. Pleased, those bhikkhus delighted in the Blessed One’s words.

Dhammacetiyasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ navamaṃ.

The Dhammacetiya Sutta, the ninth, is concluded.

10. Kaṇṇakatthalasuttaṃ

10. The Discourse at Kaṇṇakatthala

375. Evaṃ [T 2.0517][M 2.0327][V 2.0334] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā uruññāyaṃ ujuññāyaṃ (sī. pī.), udaññāyaṃ (syā. kaṃ.) viharati kaṇṇakatthale migadāye. Tena kho pana samayena rājā pasenadi kosalo uruññaṃ anuppatto hoti kenacideva karaṇīyena. Atha kho rājā pasenadi kosalo aññataraṃ purisaṃ āmantesi – “ehi tvaṃ, ambho purisa, yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkama; upasaṅkamitvā mama vacanena bhagavato pāde sirasā vandāhi, appābādhaṃ appātaṅkaṃ lahuṭṭhānaṃ balaṃ phāsuvihāraṃ puccha – ‘rājā, bhante, pasenadi kosalo bhagavato pāde sirasā vandati, appābādhaṃ appātaṅkaṃ lahuṭṭhānaṃ balaṃ phāsuvihāraṃ pucchatī’ti. Evañca vadehi – ‘ajja kira, bhante, rājā pasenadi kosalo pacchābhattaṃ bhuttapātarāso bhagavantaṃ dassanāya upasaṅkamissatī’”ti. “Evaṃ, devā”ti kho so puriso rañño pasenadissa kosalassa paṭissutvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho so puriso bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “rājā, bhante, pasenadi kosalo bhagavato pāde sirasā vandati, appābādhaṃ appātaṅkaṃ lahuṭṭhānaṃ balaṃ phāsuvihāraṃ pucchati; evañca vadeti – ‘ajja kira bhante, rājā pasenadi kosalo pacchābhattaṃ bhuttapātarāso bhagavantaṃ dassanāya upasaṅkamissatī’”ti. Assosuṃ [T 2.0518] kho somā ca bhaginī sakulā ca bhaginī – “ajja kira [P 2.0126] rājā pasenadi kosalo pacchābhattaṃ bhuttapātarāso bhagavantaṃ dassanāya upasaṅkamissatī”ti. Atha kho somā ca bhaginī sakulā ca bhaginī rājānaṃ pasenadiṃ kosalaṃ bhattābhihāre upasaṅkamitvā etadavocuṃ – “tena hi, mahārāja, amhākampi vacanena bhagavato pāde sirasā vandāhi, appābādhaṃ appātaṅkaṃ lahuṭṭhānaṃ balaṃ phāsuvihāraṃ puccha – ‘somā ca, bhante, bhaginī sakulā ca bhaginī bhagavato pāde sirasā vandati, appābādhaṃ appātaṅkaṃ lahuṭṭhānaṃ balaṃ phāsuvihāraṃ pucchatī’”ti.

375. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Uruññā, in the Kaṇṇakatthala deer sanctuary. Now at that time King Pasenadi of Kosala had arrived at Uruññā on some business. Then King Pasenadi of Kosala addressed a certain man: "Come, good man, go to the Blessed One. Having approached, in my name, pay homage at the Blessed One’s feet with your head, and inquire about his freedom from illness, freedom from affliction, lightness of body, strength, and comfortable abiding: 'Venerable sir, King Pasenadi of Kosala pays homage at the Blessed One’s feet with his head and inquires about his freedom from illness, freedom from affliction, lightness of body, strength, and comfortable abiding.' And say this: 'Venerable sir, today, after his morning meal, King Pasenadi of Kosala will come to see the Blessed One.'" "Very well, Your Majesty," that man replied to King Pasenadi of Kosala. He then went to the Blessed One, paid homage, and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, that man said to the Blessed One: "Venerable sir, King Pasenadi of Kosala pays homage at the Blessed One’s feet with his head and inquires about his freedom from illness, freedom from affliction, lightness of body, strength, and comfortable abiding. And he says this: 'Venerable sir, today, after his morning meal, King Pasenadi of Kosala will come to see the Blessed One.'" The sister Somā and the sister Sakulā heard: "Today, it seems, after his morning meal, King Pasenadi of Kosala will come to see the Blessed One." Then the sister Somā and the sister Sakulā approached King Pasenadi of Kosala where the meal was being served and said this: "In that case, great king, on our behalf too, pay homage at the Blessed One’s feet with your head and inquire about his freedom from illness, freedom from affliction, lightness of body, strength, and comfortable abiding: 'Venerable sir, the sister Somā and the sister Sakulā pay homage at the Blessed One’s feet with their heads and inquire about his freedom from illness, freedom from affliction, lightness of body, strength, and comfortable abiding.'"

376. Atha kho rājā pasenadi kosalo pacchābhattaṃ bhuttapātarāso yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho rājā [V 2.0335] pasenadi kosalo [M 2.0328] bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “somā ca, bhante, bhaginī sakulā ca bhaginī bhagavato pāde sirasā vandati vandanti (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.), appābādhaṃ appātaṅkaṃ lahuṭṭhānaṃ balaṃ phāsuvihāraṃ pucchatī”ti pucchantīti (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.). “Kiṃ pana, mahārāja, somā ca bhaginī sakulā ca bhaginī aññaṃ dūtaṃ nālatthu”nti? “Assosuṃ kho, bhante, somā ca bhaginī sakulā ca bhaginī – ‘ajja kira rājā pasenadi kosalo pacchābhattaṃ bhuttapātarāso bhagavantaṃ dassanāya upasaṅkamissatī’ti. Atha kho, bhante, somā ca bhaginī sakulā ca bhaginī maṃ bhattābhihāre upasaṅkamitvā etadavocuṃ – ‘tena hi, mahārāja, amhākampi vacanena bhagavato pāde sirasā vandāhi, appābādhaṃ [T 2.0519] appātaṅkaṃ lahuṭṭhānaṃ balaṃ phāsuvihāraṃ puccha – somā ca bhaginī sakulā ca bhaginī bhagavato pāde sirasā vandati, appābādhaṃ appātaṅkaṃ lahuṭṭhānaṃ balaṃ phāsuvihāraṃ pucchatī’”ti. “Sukhiniyo hontu tā, mahārāja, somā ca bhaginī sakulā ca bhaginī”ti.

376. Then King Pasenadi of Kosala, after his morning meal, went to the Blessed One. Having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, King Pasenadi of Kosala said to the Blessed One: "Venerable sir, the sister Somā and the sister Sakulā pay homage at the Blessed One’s feet with their heads and inquire about his freedom from illness, freedom from affliction, lightness of body, strength, and comfortable abiding." "But why, great king, could the sister Somā and the sister Sakulā not find another messenger?" "Venerable sir, the sister Somā and the sister Sakulā heard: ‘Today, it seems, after his morning meal, King Pasenadi of Kosala will come to see the Blessed One.’ Then, venerable sir, the sister Somā and the sister Sakulā approached me where the meal was being served and said this: ‘In that case, great king, on our behalf too, pay homage at the Blessed One’s feet with your head and inquire about his freedom from illness, freedom from affliction, lightness of body, strength, and comfortable abiding: “Venerable sir, the sister Somā and the sister Sakulā pay homage at the Blessed One’s feet with their heads and inquire about his freedom from illness, freedom from affliction, lightness of body, strength, and comfortable abiding.”’" "May they be happy, great king, the sister Somā and the sister Sakulā."

377. Atha kho rājā pasenadi kosalo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “sutaṃ metaṃ, bhante, samaṇo gotamo evamāha – ‘natthi so samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā yo sabbaññū sabbadassāvī aparisesaṃ ñāṇadassanaṃ paṭijānissati, netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjatī’ti. Ye te, bhante, evamāhaṃsu – ‘samaṇo gotamo evamāha [P 2.0127] – natthi so samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā yo sabbaññū sabbadassāvī aparisesaṃ ñāṇadassanaṃ paṭijānissati, netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjatī’ti; kacci te, bhante, bhagavato vuttavādino, na ca bhagavantaṃ abhūtena abbhācikkhanti, dhammassa cānudhammaṃ byākaronti, na ca koci sahadhammiko vādānuvādo gārayhaṃ ṭhānaṃ āgacchatī”ti? “Ye te, mahārāja, evamāhaṃsu – ‘samaṇo gotamo evamāha – natthi so samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā yo sabbaññū sabbadassāvī aparisesaṃ ñāṇadassanaṃ paṭijānissati, netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjatī’ti; na me te vuttavādino, abbhācikkhanti ca pana maṃ te asatā abhūtenā”ti.

377. Then King Pasenadi of Kosala said to the Blessed One: "Venerable sir, I have heard this: ‘The recluse Gotama says thus: “There is no recluse or brahmin who, being all-knowing and all-seeing, will claim knowledge and vision without remainder—that is not possible.”’ Venerable sir, those who say thus: ‘The recluse Gotama says—there is no recluse or brahmin who, being all-knowing and all-seeing, will claim knowledge and vision without remainder—that is not possible’; do they, venerable sir, speak in accordance with the Blessed One's words, and do they not misrepresent the Blessed One with what is untrue? Do they explain the Dhamma in accordance with the Dhamma, and does no legitimate, consequential point of debate give grounds for censure?" "Great king, those who say thus: ‘The recluse Gotama says—there is no recluse or brahmin who, being all-knowing and all-seeing, will claim knowledge and vision without remainder—that is not possible’; they do not speak in accordance with my words. On the contrary, they misrepresent me with what is non-existent and untrue."

378. Atha kho rājā pasenadi kosalo viṭaṭūbhaṃ senāpatiṃ āmantesi – “ko nu kho, senāpati, imaṃ kathāvatthuṃ rājantepure abbhudāhāsī”ti? “Sañjayo, mahārāja, brāhmaṇo ākāsagotto”ti. Atha [T 2.0520] kho rājā pasenadi kosalo aññataraṃ purisaṃ āmantesi – “ehi tvaṃ[M 2.0329], ambho purisa, mama vacanena sañjayaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ ākāsagottaṃ āmantehi – ‘rājā taṃ, bhante, pasenadi kosalo āmantetī’”ti. “Evaṃ, devā”ti kho so puriso rañño pasenadissa [V 2.0336] kosalassa paṭissutvā yena sañjayo brāhmaṇo ākāsagotto tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā sañjayaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ ākāsagottaṃ etadavoca – “rājā taṃ, bhante, pasenadi kosalo āmantetī”ti. Atha kho rājā pasenadi kosalo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “siyā nu kho, bhante, bhagavatā aññadeva kiñci sandhāya bhāsitaṃ, tañca jano aññathāpi paccāgaccheyya paccāgaccheyyāti, abhijānāmi mahārāja vācaṃ bhāsitāti (sī.). Yathā kathaṃ pana, bhante, bhagavā abhijānāti vācaṃ bhāsitā”ti? “Evaṃ kho ahaṃ, mahārāja, abhijānāmi vācaṃ bhāsitā – ‘natthi so samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā yo sakideva sabbaṃ ñassati, sabbaṃ dakkhiti, netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjatī’”ti. “Heturūpaṃ, bhante, bhagavā āha; saheturūpaṃ, bhante, bhagavā āha – ‘natthi so samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā yo [P 2.0128] sakideva sabbaṃ ñassati, sabbaṃ dakkhiti, netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjatī’”ti. “Cattārome, bhante, vaṇṇā – khattiyā, brāhmaṇā, vessā, suddā. Imesaṃ nu kho, bhante, catunnaṃ vaṇṇānaṃ siyā viseso siyā nānākaraṇa”nti? “Cattārome, mahārāja, vaṇṇā – khattiyā, brāhmaṇā, vessā, suddā. Imesaṃ kho, mahārāja, catunnaṃ vaṇṇānaṃ dve vaṇṇā [T 2.0521] aggamakkhāyanti – khattiyā ca brāhmaṇā ca – yadidaṃ abhivādanapaccuṭṭhānaañjalikammasāmīcikammānī”ti sāmicikammānanti (sī.). “Nāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavantaṃ diṭṭhadhammikaṃ pucchāmi; samparāyikāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavantaṃ pucchāmi. Cattārome, bhante, vaṇṇā – khattiyā, brāhmaṇā, vessā, suddā. Imesaṃ nu kho, bhante, catunnaṃ vaṇṇānaṃ siyā viseso siyā nānākaraṇa”nti?

378. Then King Pasenadi of Kosala addressed General Viṭaṭūbha: 'General, who was it that initiated this topic of discussion in the royal palace?' 'Great king, it was the brahmin Sañjaya Ākāsagotta.' Then King Pasenadi of Kosala addressed a certain man: 'Come, my good man, go at my word and summon the brahmin Sañjaya Ākāsagotta, saying, 'The king, sir, Pasenadi of Kosala summons you.'' 'Yes, lord,' that man replied to King Pasenadi of Kosala. Then he approached the brahmin Sañjaya Ākāsagotta and said, 'The king, sir, Pasenadi of Kosala summons you.' Then King Pasenadi of Kosala said to the Blessed One: 'Lord, could it be that the Blessed One spoke having some other meaning in mind, but people understood it differently? How, lord, does the Blessed One recall the words that have been spoken?' 'Great king, I recall the words that have been spoken thus: 'There is no ascetic or brahmin who could know everything all at once, see everything all at once—this is not possible.'' 'The Blessed One speaks with reason, lord; the Blessed One speaks with a cause: 'There is no ascetic or brahmin who could know everything all at once, see everything all at once—this is not possible.'' 'Lord, there are these four classes—khattiyas, brahmins, vessas, and suddas. Among these four classes, lord, might there be any distinction or difference?' 'Great king, there are these four classes—khattiyas, brahmins, vessas, and suddas. Among these four classes, great king, two are said to be foremost—the khattiyas and the brahmins—that is, in terms of paying homage, rising up to greet, offering reverential salutations, and performing acts of respect.' 'Lord, I am not asking the Blessed One about matters pertaining to this present life; I am asking the Blessed One about the future life. Lord, there are these four classes—khattiyas, brahmins, vessas, and suddas. Among these four classes, lord, might there be any distinction or difference?'

379. “Pañcimāni, mahārāja, padhāniyaṅgāni. Katamāni pañca? Idha, mahārāja, bhikkhu saddho hoti, saddahati tathāgatassa bodhiṃ – ‘itipi so bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho vijjācaraṇasampanno sugato lokavidū anuttaro purisadammasārathi satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavā’ti; appābādho hoti appātaṅko samavepākiniyā gahaṇiyā samannāgato nātisītāya nāccuṇhāya majjhimāya padhānakkhamāya; asaṭho hoti amāyāvī yathābhūtaṃ attānaṃ āvikattā satthari vā viññūsu vā sabrahmacārīsu; āraddhavīriyo viharati akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ [M 2.0330] pahānāya, kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ upasampadāya, thāmavā daḷhaparakkamo anikkhittadhuro kusalesu dhammesu; paññavā hoti udayatthagāminiyā paññāya samannāgato ariyāya nibbedhikāya sammādukkhakkhayagāminiyā – imāni kho, mahārāja, pañca padhāniyaṅgāni. Cattārome, mahārāja, vaṇṇā – khattiyā, brāhmaṇā, vessā, suddā. Te cassu imehi pañcahi padhāniyaṅgehi samannāgatā[V 2.0337]; ettha pana nesaṃ assa [T 2.0522] dīgharattaṃ hitāya sukhāyā”ti. “Cattārome, bhante, vaṇṇā – khattiyā, brāhmaṇā, vessā, suddā[P 2.0129]. Te cassu imehi pañcahi padhāniyaṅgehi samannāgatā; ettha pana nesaṃ, bhante, siyā viseso siyā nānākaraṇa”nti? “Ettha kho nesāhaṃ, mahārāja, padhānavemattataṃ vadāmi. Seyyathāpissu, mahārāja, dve hatthidammā vā assadammā vā godammā vā sudantā suvinītā, dve hatthidammā vā assadammā vā godammā vā adantā avinītā. Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, mahārāja, ye te dve hatthidammā vā assadammā vā godammā vā sudantā suvinītā, api nu te dantāva dantakāraṇaṃ gaccheyyuṃ, dantāva dantabhūmiṃ sampāpuṇeyyu”nti? “Evaṃ, bhante”. “Ye pana te dve hatthidammā vā assadammā vā godammā vā adantā avinītā, api nu te adantāva dantakāraṇaṃ gaccheyyuṃ, adantāva dantabhūmiṃ sampāpuṇeyyuṃ, seyyathāpi te dve hatthidammā vā assadammā vā godammā vā sudantā suvinītā”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”. “Evameva kho, mahārāja, yaṃ taṃ saddhena pattabbaṃ appābādhena asaṭhena amāyāvinā āraddhavīriyena paññavatā taṃ vata taṃ tathā so (ka.) assaddho bahvābādho saṭho māyāvī kusīto duppañño pāpuṇissatīti – netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjatī”ti.

379. Great king, there are these five factors of striving. What five? Here, great king, a bhikkhu has faith; he believes in the enlightenment of the Tathagata: 'Thus is the Blessed One an Arahant, perfectly self-enlightened, consummate in knowledge and conduct, well-gone, knower of the world, unexcelled trainer of persons to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, the Buddha, the Blessed One.' He is free from illness and affliction, possessing an even digestion that is neither too cold nor too hot but moderate and fit for striving. He is not deceitful and not fraudulent, revealing himself as he truly is to the Teacher or to his wise companions in the holy life. He dwells with aroused persistence for abandoning unwholesome states and for the undertaking of wholesome states; he is strong, of firm exertion, not shirking his duty in regard to wholesome states. He is discerning, endowed with the noble, penetrating discernment that leads to arising and passing away, that leads to the right destruction of suffering. These, great king, are the five factors of striving. There are these four classes, great king: khattiyas, brahmins, vessas, and suddas. If they were endowed with these five factors of striving, it would be for their long-term welfare and happiness." "Lord, there are these four classes—khattiyas, brahmins, vessas, and suddas. If they were endowed with these five factors of striving, would there be any distinction or difference among them in this regard?" "In this, great king, I declare there is a difference in their striving. Suppose, great king, there were two elephants, horses, or oxen that were well-tamed and well-trained, and two elephants, horses, or oxen that were untamed and untrained. What do you think, great king? Would those two elephants, horses, or oxen that were well-tamed and well-trained, being tamed, perform the work of the tamed and reach the domain of the tamed?" "Yes, lord." "But as for those two elephants, horses, or oxen that were untamed and untrained, would they, being untamed, perform the work of the tamed and reach the domain of the tamed, just like those two elephants, horses, or oxen that were well-tamed and well-trained?" "No, lord." "In the same way, great king, that which is to be attained by one with faith, free from illness, not deceitful, not fraudulent, with aroused persistence, and discerning—that one who is faithless, often ill, deceitful, fraudulent, lazy, and undiscerning would attain it—this is not possible."

380. “Heturūpaṃ, bhante, bhagavā āha; saheturūpaṃ, bhante, bhagavā āha. Cattārome, bhante, vaṇṇā – khattiyā, brāhmaṇā, vessā[T 2.0523], suddā. Te cassu imehi pañcahi padhāniyaṅgehi samannāgatā te cassu sammappadhānā; ettha pana nesaṃ, bhante, siyā viseso siyā nānākaraṇa”nti? “Ettha kho ettha kho pana (sī.) nesāhaṃ, mahārāja, na kiñci nānākaraṇaṃ vadāmi – yadidaṃ vimuttiyā vimuttiṃ. Seyyathāpi, mahārāja, puriso sukkhaṃ sākakaṭṭhaṃ ādāya aggiṃ abhinibbatteyya, tejo pātukareyya[M 2.0331]; athāparo puriso sukkhaṃ sālakaṭṭhaṃ ādāya [P 2.0130] aggiṃ abhinibbatteyya, tejo pātukareyya; athāparo puriso sukkhaṃ ambakaṭṭhaṃ ādāya aggiṃ abhinibbatteyya, tejo pātukareyya; athāparo puriso sukkhaṃ udumbarakaṭṭhaṃ ādāya aggiṃ abhinibbatteyya, tejo pātukareyya. Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, mahārāja, siyā nu kho tesaṃ aggīnaṃ nānādāruto abhinibbattānaṃ kiñci nānākaraṇaṃ acciyā vā acciṃ, vaṇṇena vā vaṇṇaṃ, ābhāya vā ābha”nti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”. “Evameva kho, mahārāja, yaṃ taṃ tejaṃ vīriyā nimmathitaṃ padhānābhinibbattaṃ viriyaṃ nippharati, taṃ pacchābhinibbattaṃ (sī.), nāhaṃ tattha kiñci nānākaraṇaṃ vadāmi – yadidaṃ vimuttiyā vimutti”nti. “Heturūpaṃ, bhante, bhagavā āha; saheturūpaṃ, bhante, bhagavā āha. Kiṃ [V 2.0338] pana, bhante, atthi devā”ti? “Kiṃ pana tvaṃ, mahārāja, evaṃ vadesi – ‘kiṃ pana, bhante, atthi devā’”ti? “Yadi vā te, bhante, devā āgantāro itthattaṃ yadi vā anāgantāro itthattaṃ”? “Ye te, mahārāja, devā sabyābajjhā te devā āgantāro itthattaṃ, ye te devā abyābajjhā te devā anāgantāro itthatta”nti.

380. “Venerable sir, the Blessed One has spoken of that which has a cause; venerable sir, the Blessed One has spoken of that which is together with its cause. Venerable sir, there are these four castes: warriors, brahmins, merchants, and workers. If they were endowed with these five factors of striving and were possessed of right exertion, would there be any distinction, any difference among them in this regard?” “In this regard, great king, I declare there is no difference whatsoever, that is, between one liberation and another. Suppose, great king, a man, taking dry teak wood, were to produce a fire and bring forth heat; and then another man, taking dry sal wood, were to produce a fire and bring forth heat; and then another man, taking dry mango wood, were to produce a fire and bring forth heat; and then another man, taking dry fig wood, were to produce a fire and bring forth heat. What do you think, great king? Among those fires produced from different kinds of wood, would there be any difference whatsoever with respect to flame from flame, color from color, or radiance from radiance?” “No, venerable sir.” “In the same way, great king, with regard to that radiance which is churned out by energy and produced by striving, I declare there is no difference whatsoever—that is, between one liberation and another.” “Venerable sir, the Blessed One has spoken of that which has a cause; venerable sir, the Blessed One has spoken of that which is together with its cause. But, venerable sir, do devas exist?” “Why, great king, do you say this: ‘But, venerable sir, do devas exist?’” “It is whether, venerable sir, those devas are returners to this state or non-returners to this state.” “Great king, those devas who are afflicted are returners to this state; those devas who are unafflicted are non-returners to this state.”

381. Evaṃ [T 2.0524] vutte, viṭṭūbho senāpati bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “ye te, bhante, devā sabyābajjhā āgantāro itthattaṃ te devā, ye te devā abyābajjhā anāgantāro itthattaṃ te deve tamhā ṭhānā cāvessanti vā pabbājessanti vā”ti?

381. When this was said, General Viṭṭūbha said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, will those devas who are afflicted and are returners to this state cause those devas who are unafflicted and are non-returners to this state to move from that place or banish them?”

Atha kho āyasmato ānandassa etadahosi – “ayaṃ kho viṭaṭūbho senāpati rañño pasenadissa kosalassa putto; ahaṃ bhagavato putto. Ayaṃ kho kālo yaṃ putto puttena manteyyā”ti. Atha kho āyasmā ānando viṭaṭūbhaṃ senāpatiṃ āmantesi – “tena hi, senāpati, taṃ yevettha paṭipucchissāmi; yathā te khameyya tathā naṃ byākareyyāsi. Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, senāpati, yāvatā rañño pasenadissa kosalassa vijitaṃ yattha ca rājā pasenadi kosalo issariyādhipaccaṃ [P 2.0131] rajjaṃ kāreti, pahoti tattha rājā pasenadi kosalo samaṇaṃ vā brāhmaṇaṃ vā puññavantaṃ vā apuññavantaṃ vā brahmacariyavantaṃ vā abrahmacariyavantaṃ vā tamhā ṭhānā cāvetuṃ vā pabbājetuṃ vā”ti? “Yāvatā, bho, rañño pasenadissa kosalassa vijitaṃ yattha ca rājā pasenadi [T 2.0525] kosalo issariyādhipaccaṃ rajjaṃ kāreti, pahoti tattha rājā pasenadi kosalo [M 2.0332] samaṇaṃ vā brāhmaṇaṃ vā puññavantaṃ vā apuññavantaṃ vā brahmacariyavantaṃ vā abrahmacariyavantaṃ vā tamhā ṭhānā cāvetuṃ vā pabbājetuṃ vā”ti.

Then this thought occurred to the Venerable Ānanda: “This General Viṭaṭūbha is the son of King Pasenadi of Kosala, and I am the son of the Blessed One. This is the time for a son to confer with a son.” Then the Venerable Ānanda addressed General Viṭaṭūbha: “In that case, General, I will question you in return on this very matter. As it seems fitting to you, so you should explain it. What do you think, General? Insofar as the territory of King Pasenadi of Kosala extends, and where King Pasenadi of Kosala exercises sovereignty and dominion, is King Pasenadi of Kosala able there to cause a recluse or a brahmin—whether meritorious or demeritorious, whether living the holy life or not living the holy life—to move from that place or to banish them?” “Sir, insofar as the territory of King Pasenadi of Kosala extends, and where King Pasenadi of Kosala exercises sovereignty and dominion, King Pasenadi of Kosala is able there to cause a recluse or a brahmin—whether meritorious or demeritorious, whether living the holy life or not living the holy life—to move from that place or to banish them.”

“Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, senāpati, yāvatā rañño pasenadissa kosalassa avijitaṃ yattha ca rājā pasenadi kosalo na issariyādhipaccaṃ rajjaṃ kāreti, tattha pahoti rājā pasenadi kosalo samaṇaṃ vā brāhmaṇaṃ vā puññavantaṃ vā apuññavantaṃ vā brahmacariyavantaṃ vā abrahmacariyavantaṃ vā tamhā ṭhānā cāvetuṃ vā pabbājetuṃ vā”ti? “Yāvatā, bho, rañño pasenadissa kosalassa avijitaṃ yattha ca rājā pasenadi kosalo na issariyādhipaccaṃ rajjaṃ kāreti, na tattha pahoti rājā [V 2.0339] pasenadi kosalo samaṇaṃ vā brāhmaṇaṃ vā puññavantaṃ vā apuññavantaṃ vā brahmacariyavantaṃ vā abrahmacariyavantaṃ vā tamhā ṭhānā cāvetuṃ vā pabbājetuṃ vā”ti.

“What do you think, General? Insofar as the territory not conquered by King Pasenadi of Kosala extends, and where King Pasenadi of Kosala does not exercise sovereignty and dominion, is King Pasenadi of Kosala able there to cause a recluse or a brahmin—whether meritorious or demeritorious, whether living the holy life or not living the holy life—to move from that place or to banish them?” “Sir, insofar as the territory not conquered by King Pasenadi of Kosala extends, and where King Pasenadi of Kosala does not exercise sovereignty and dominion, King Pasenadi of Kosala is not able there to cause a recluse or a brahmin—whether meritorious or demeritorious, whether living the holy life or not living the holy life—to move from that place or to banish them.”

“Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, senāpati, sutā te devā tāvatiṃsā”ti? “Evaṃ, bho. Sutā me devā tāvatiṃsā. Idhāpi bhotā raññā pasenadinā kosalena sutā devā tāvatiṃsā”ti. “Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, senāpati, pahoti rājā pasenadi kosalo deve tāvatiṃse tamhā ṭhānā cāvetuṃ vā pabbājetuṃ vā”ti? “Dassanampi, bho, rājā pasenadi kosalo deve tāvatiṃse nappahoti, kuto pana tamhā ṭhānā cāvessati vā pabbājessati vā”ti? “Evameva kho, senāpati, ye te devā sabyābajjhā āgantāro itthattaṃ te devā, ye te devā abyābajjhā anāgantāro itthattaṃ te deve dassanāyapi nappahonti; kuto pana tamhā ṭhānā cāvessanti vā pabbājessanti vā”ti?

“What do you think, General, have you heard of the Tāvatiṃsa devas?” “Yes, sir. I have heard of the Tāvatiṃsa devas. And the noble King Pasenadi of Kosala has also heard of the Tāvatiṃsa devas.” “What do you think, General? Is King Pasenadi of Kosala able to cause the Tāvatiṃsa devas to move from that place or to banish them?” “Sir, King Pasenadi of Kosala is not even able to see the Tāvatiṃsa devas, so how could he cause them to move from that place or banish them?” “In the same way, General, those devas who are afflicted and are returners to this state are not even able to see those devas who are unafflicted and are non-returners to this state. How then could they cause them to move from that place or banish them?”

382. Atha kho rājā pasenadi kosalo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “konāmo ayaṃ, bhante, bhikkhū”ti? “Ānando [T 2.0526] nāma, mahārājā”ti. “Ānando vata, bho, ānandarūpo vata, bho! Heturūpaṃ, bhante[P 2.0132], āyasmā ānando āha; saheturūpaṃ, bhante, āyasmā ānando āha. Kiṃ pana, bhante, atthi brahmā”ti? “Kiṃ pana tvaṃ, mahārāja, evaṃ vadesi – ‘kiṃ pana, bhante, atthi brahmā’”ti? “Yadi vā so, bhante, brahmā āgantā itthattaṃ, yadi vā anāgantā itthatta”nti? “Yo so, mahārāja, brahmā sabyābajjho so brahmā āgantā itthattaṃ, yo so brahmā abyābajjho so brahmā anāgantā itthatta”nti. Atha kho aññataro puriso rājānaṃ pasenadiṃ [M 2.0333] kosalaṃ etadavoca – “sañjayo, mahārāja, brāhmaṇo ākāsagotto āgato”ti. Atha kho rājā pasenadi kosalo sañjayaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ ākāsagottaṃ etadavoca – “ko nu kho, brāhmaṇa, imaṃ kathāvatthuṃ rājantepure abbhudāhāsī”ti? “Viṭaṭūbho, mahārāja, senāpatī”ti. Viṭaṭūbho senāpati evamāha – “sañjayo, mahārāja, brāhmaṇo ākāsagotto”ti. Atha kho aññataro puriso rājānaṃ pasenadiṃ kosalaṃ etadavoca – “yānakālo, mahārājā”ti.

382. Then King Pasenadi of Kosala said to the Blessed One: 'Venerable Sir, what is the name of this bhikkhu?' 'His name is Ānanda, great king.' 'Indeed, sirs, he is a delight! Indeed, sirs, his nature is delightful! Venerable Sir, the Venerable Ānanda has spoken what is causal in nature; Venerable Sir, the Venerable Ānanda has spoken with sound reasoning. But, Venerable Sir, does Brahmā exist?' 'Why, great king, do you say thus: "But, Venerable Sir, does Brahmā exist?"' 'Venerable Sir, is that Brahmā one who will return to this state of existence, or one who will not return to this state of existence?' 'Great king, that Brahmā who is subject to affliction is one who will return to this state of existence; that Brahmā who is not subject to affliction is one who will not return to this state of existence.' Then a certain man said to King Pasenadi of Kosala: 'Great king, the brahmin Sañjaya of the Ākāsagotta clan has arrived.' Then King Pasenadi of Kosala said to the brahmin Sañjaya of the Ākāsagotta clan: 'Who, brahmin, brought up this topic of conversation in the inner royal palace?' 'It was General Viṭaṭūbha, great king.' General Viṭaṭūbha said: 'It was Sañjaya, the brahmin of the Ākāsagotta clan, great king.' Then a certain man said to King Pasenadi of Kosala: 'It is time to depart, great king.'

Atha kho rājā pasenadi kosalo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “sabbaññutaṃ mayaṃ, bhante, bhagavantaṃ [V 2.0340] apucchimhā, sabbaññutaṃ bhagavā byākāsi; tañca panamhākaṃ ruccati ceva khamati ca, tena camhā attamanā. Cātuvaṇṇisuddhiṃ mayaṃ, bhante, bhagavantaṃ apucchimhā, cātuvaṇṇisuddhiṃ [T 2.0527] bhagavā byākāsi; tañca panamhākaṃ ruccati ceva khamati ca, tena camhā attamanā. Adhideve mayaṃ, bhante, bhagavantaṃ apucchimhā, adhideve bhagavā byākāsi; tañca panamhākaṃ ruccati ceva khamati ca, tena camhā attamanā. Adhibrahmānaṃ mayaṃ, bhante, bhagavantaṃ apucchimhā, adhibrahmānaṃ bhagavā byākāsi; tañca panamhākaṃ ruccati ceva khamati ca, tena camhā attamanā. Yaṃ yadeva ca mayaṃ bhagavantaṃ apucchimhā taṃ tadeva bhagavā byākāsi; tañca panamhākaṃ ruccati ceva khamati ca, tena camhā attamanā. Handa, ca [P 2.0133] dāni mayaṃ, bhante, gacchāma; bahukiccā mayaṃ bahukaraṇīyā”ti. “Yassadāni tvaṃ, mahārāja, kālaṃ maññasī”ti. Atha kho rājā pasenadi kosalo bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinanditvā anumoditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā pakkāmīti.

Then King Pasenadi of Kosala said to the Blessed One: 'Venerable Sir, we asked the Blessed One about omniscience, and the Blessed One explained omniscience; and that is both pleasing and acceptable to us, and by it we are gladdened. Venerable Sir, we asked the Blessed One about the purity of the four castes, and the Blessed One explained the purity of the four castes; and that is both pleasing and acceptable to us, and by it we are gladdened. Venerable Sir, we asked the Blessed One about the supreme devas, and the Blessed One explained the supreme devas; and that is both pleasing and acceptable to us, and by it we are gladdened. Venerable Sir, we asked the Blessed One about the supreme Brahmā, and the Blessed One explained the supreme Brahmā; and that is both pleasing and acceptable to us, and by it we are gladdened. And whatever we asked the Blessed One, that very thing the Blessed One explained; and that is both pleasing and acceptable to us, and by it we are gladdened. And now, Venerable Sir, we shall depart; we have many duties and much to do.' 'Great king, you may do so at the time you deem fit.' Then King Pasenadi of Kosala, having greatly delighted in and rejoiced at the Blessed One's words, rose from his seat, paid homage to the Blessed One, circumambulated him keeping his right side toward him, and departed.

Kaṇṇakatthalasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ dasamaṃ.

The tenth, the Kaṇṇakatthala Sutta, is concluded.

Rājavaggo niṭṭhito catuttho.

The fourth, the Chapter on Kings, is concluded.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary:

Ghaṭikāro raṭṭhapālo, maghadevo madhuriyaṃ;

Bodhi aṅgulimālo ca, piyajātaṃ bāhitikaṃ;

Dhammacetiyasuttañca, dasamaṃ kaṇṇakatthalaṃ.

Ghaṭikāra, Raṭṭhapāla, Maghadeva, Madhurā; Bodhi and Aṅgulimāla, Piyajāta, Bāhitika; the Dhammacetiya Sutta, and the tenth, Kaṇṇakatthala.

5. Brāhmaṇavaggo

5. The Brahmin Chapter

1. Brahmāyusuttaṃ

The Brahmāyu Sutta

383. Evaṃ [T 2.0528][M 2.0334][V 2.0341] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā videhesu cārikaṃ carati mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ pañcamattehi bhikkhusatehi. Tena kho pana samayena brahmāyu brāhmaṇo mithilāyaṃ paṭivasati jiṇṇo vuḍḍho mahallako addhagato vayoanuppatto, vīsavassasatiko jātiyā, tiṇṇaṃ vedānaṃ bedānaṃ (ka.) pāragū sanighaṇḍukeṭubhānaṃ sākkharappabhedānaṃ itihāsapañcamānaṃ, padako, veyyākaraṇo, lokāyatamahāpurisalakkhaṇesu anavayo. Assosi kho brahmāyu brāhmaṇo – “samaṇo khalu bho, gotamo sakyaputto sakyakulā pabbajito videhesu cārikaṃ carati mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ pañcamattehi bhikkhusatehi. Taṃ kho pana bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ evaṃ kalyāṇo kittisaddo abbhuggato – ‘itipi so bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho vijjācaraṇasampanno sugato lokavidū anuttaro purisadammasārathi satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavāti. So imaṃ lokaṃ sadevakaṃ samārakaṃ sabrahmakaṃ sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiṃ pajaṃ sadevamanussaṃ sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā pavedeti. So dhammaṃ deseti ādikalyāṇaṃ majjhekalyāṇaṃ pariyosānakalyāṇaṃ sātthaṃ sabyañjanaṃ, kevalaparipuṇṇaṃ parisuddhaṃ brahmacariyaṃ pakāseti. Sādhu [T 2.0529] kho pana tathārūpānaṃ arahataṃ dassanaṃ hotī’”ti.

Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was traveling in the Videha country with a large Saṅgha of bhikkhus, with five hundred bhikkhus. Now at that time, the brahmin Brahmāyu was living in Mithilā. He was old, aged, burdened with years, advanced in life, and had come to the last stage; he was one hundred and twenty years old. He was a master of the three Vedas with their vocabularies, ritual texts, phonology, and etymology, and with history as the fifth; he was a philologist and grammarian, and was perfectly versed in cosmology and the marks of a great man. The brahmin Brahmāyu heard: “The ascetic Gotama, it seems, a Sakyan son who has gone forth from the Sakyan clan, is traveling in the Videha country with a large Saṅgha of bhikkhus, with five hundred bhikkhus. Now regarding that venerable Gotama, such a good report has spread: ‘That Blessed One is an Arahant, a Perfectly Self-Enlightened One, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, the Well-Farer, knower of the world, unsurpassed trainer of persons to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, the Buddha, the Blessed One.’ He, having realized it for himself with direct knowledge, makes known this world with its devas, its Māras, and its Brahmās, this generation with its ascetics and brahmins, its devas and humans. He teaches the Dhamma which is good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, with the right meaning and phrasing; he reveals the holy life that is perfectly complete and pure. It is good, indeed, to see such Arahants.”

384. Tena [P 2.0134] kho pana samayena brahmāyussa brāhmaṇassa uttaro nāma māṇavo antevāsī hoti tiṇṇaṃ vedānaṃ pāragū sanighaṇḍukeṭubhānaṃ sākkharappabhedānaṃ itihāsapañcamānaṃ, padako, veyyākaraṇo, lokāyatamahāpurisalakkhaṇesu anavayo. Atha kho brahmāyu brāhmaṇo uttaraṃ māṇavaṃ āmantesi – “ayaṃ, tāta uttara, samaṇo gotamo sakyaputto sakyakulā pabbajito videhesu [V 2.0342] cārikaṃ carati mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ pañcamattehi bhikkhusatehi. Taṃ kho pana bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ evaṃ kalyāṇo kittisaddo abbhuggato – ‘itipi so bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho…pe… sādhu kho pana tathārūpānaṃ arahataṃ dassanaṃ [M 2.0335] hotī’ti. Ehi tvaṃ, tāta uttara, yena samaṇo gotamo tenupasaṅkama; upasaṅkamitvā samaṇaṃ gotamaṃ jānāhi yadi vā taṃ bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ tathā santaṃyeva saddo abbhuggato, yadi vā no tathā; yadi vā so bhavaṃ gotamo tādiso, yadi vā na tādiso. Tathā mayaṃ taṃ bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ vedissāmā”ti. “Yathā kathaṃ panāhaṃ, bho, taṃ bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ jānissāmi yadi vā taṃ bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ tathā santaṃyeva saddo abbhuggato, yadi vā no tathā; yadi vā so bhavaṃ gotamo tādiso, yadi vā na tādiso”ti. “Āgatāni kho, tāta uttara, amhākaṃ mantesu dvattiṃsamahāpurisalakkhaṇāni, yehi samannāgatassa mahāpurisassa dveyeva gatiyo bhavanti anaññā[T 2.0530]. Sace agāraṃ ajjhāvasati, rājā hoti cakkavattī dhammiko dhammarājā cāturanto vijitāvī janapadatthāvariyappatto sattaratanasamannāgato. Tassimāni satta ratanāni bhavanti, seyyathidaṃ – cakkaratanaṃ, hatthiratanaṃ, assaratanaṃ, maṇiratanaṃ, itthiratanaṃ, gahapatiratanaṃ, pariṇāyakaratanameva sattamaṃ. Parosahassaṃ kho panassa puttā bhavanti sūrā vīraṅgarūpā parasenappamaddanā. So imaṃ pathaviṃ sāgarapariyantaṃ adaṇḍena asatthena dhammena dhammena samena (ka.) abhivijiya ajjhāvasati. Sace kho pana agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajati, arahaṃ hoti sammāsambuddho loke vivaṭṭacchado. Ahaṃ kho pana, tāta uttara, mantānaṃ dātā; tvaṃ mantānaṃ paṭiggahetā”ti.

384. Now at that time, the brahmin Brahmāyu had a student, a young man named Uttara, who was a master of the three Vedas with their vocabularies, ritual texts, phonology, and etymology, and history as the fifth; he was a philologist and grammarian, and was perfectly versed in cosmology and the marks of a great man. Then the brahmin Brahmāyu addressed the young man Uttara: ‘Dear Uttara, this ascetic Gotama, a Sakyan son who has gone forth from the Sakyan clan, is traveling in the Videha country with a large Saṅgha of bhikkhus, with five hundred bhikkhus. Now regarding that venerable Gotama, such a good report has spread: “That Blessed One is an Arahant, a Perfectly Self-Enlightened One... It is good, indeed, to see such Arahants.” Come, dear Uttara, go to where the ascetic Gotama is. Having gone, find out about the ascetic Gotama: whether the good report that has spread about the venerable Gotama is true or not, and whether the venerable Gotama is like that or not. In this way, we will come to know about that venerable Gotama.’ ‘But how, sir, shall I know about that venerable Gotama: whether the good report that has spread about him is true or not, and whether the venerable Gotama is like that or not?’ ‘Dear Uttara, in our sacred texts have come down the thirty-two marks of a great man, and for a great man endowed with them, only two destinies are possible, no other. If he lives the household life, he becomes a wheel-turning monarch, a righteous king of the Dhamma, a conqueror of the four quarters, who has established the security of his country and possesses the seven treasures. These are his seven treasures: the wheel-treasure, the elephant-treasure, the horse-treasure, the jewel-treasure, the woman-treasure, the householder-treasure, and the counselor-treasure as the seventh. He has more than a thousand sons who are brave, heroic in form, crushers of enemy armies. He dwells having conquered this earth to its ocean boundaries, without rod or weapon, by means of the Dhamma. But if he goes forth from the household life into homelessness, he becomes an Arahant, a Perfectly Self-Enlightened One, who has drawn back the veil in the world. And I, dear Uttara, am the giver of the sacred texts; you are the receiver.’

385. “Evaṃ, bho”ti kho uttaro māṇavo brahmāyussa brāhmaṇassa paṭissutvā uṭṭhāyāsanā brahmāyuṃ brāhmaṇaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā videhesu yena bhagavā tena cārikaṃ [P 2.0135] pakkāmi. Anupubbena cārikaṃ caramāno yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho uttaro māṇavo bhagavato kāye dvattiṃsamahāpurisalakkhaṇāni samannesi. Addasā [V 2.0343] kho uttaro māṇavo bhagavato kāye dvattiṃsamahāpurisalakkhaṇāni, yebhuyyena thapetvā dve.
