Dvīsu mahāpurisalakkhaṇesu kaṅkhati [T 2.0531] vicikicchati nādhimuccati na sampasīdati – kosohite ca vatthaguyhe, pahūtajivhatāya ca. Atha kho bhagavato etadahosi – “passati kho me ayaṃ uttaro māṇavo dvattiṃsamahāpurisalakkhaṇāni[M 2.0336], yebhuyyena thapetvā dve. Dvīsu mahāpurisalakkhaṇesu kaṅkhati vicikicchati nādhimuccati na sampasīdati – kosohite ca vatthaguyhe, pahūtajivhatāya cā”ti. Atha kho bhagavā tathārūpaṃ iddhābhisaṅkhāraṃ abhisaṅkhāsi yathā addasa uttaro māṇavo bhagavato kosohitaṃ vatthaguyhaṃ. Atha kho bhagavā jivhaṃ ninnāmetvā ubhopi kaṇṇasotāni anumasi paṭimasi parimasi (sī. ka.); ubhopi nāsikasotāni nāsikāsotāni (sī.) anumasi paṭimasi; kevalampi nalāṭamaṇḍalaṃ jivhāya chādesi. Atha kho uttarassa māṇavassa etadahosi – “samannāgato kho samaṇo gotamo dvattiṃsamahāpurisalakkhaṇehi. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ samaṇaṃ gotamaṃ anubandheyyaṃ, iriyāpathamassa passeyya”nti. Atha kho uttaro māṇavo sattamāsāni bhagavantaṃ anubandhi chāyāva anapāyinī anupāyinī (syā. kaṃ. ka.).

385. The young man Uttara assented to the brahmin Brahmāyu, saying, 'Very well, venerable sir.' Rising from his seat, he paid homage to the brahmin Brahmāyu, circumambulated him respectfully, and set out on a journey in the Videha country to where the Blessed One was. Traveling in stages, he approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he exchanged joyful greetings with the Blessed One. After concluding the joyful and memorable talk, he sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the young man Uttara investigated the Blessed One’s body for the thirty-two marks of a great man. Indeed, the young man Uttara saw on the Blessed One’s body the thirty-two marks of a great man, for the most part, excepting two. Regarding two of the marks of a great man, he was doubtful, uncertain, could not decide, and was not satisfied: regarding the male organ concealed in a sheath and the long, broad tongue. Then this thought occurred to the Blessed One: 'This young man Uttara sees on my body the thirty-two marks of a great man, for the most part, excepting two. Regarding two of the marks of a great man, he is doubtful, uncertain, could not decide, and is not satisfied: regarding the male organ concealed in a sheath and the long, broad tongue.' Then the Blessed One performed such a feat of psychic power that the young man Uttara saw the Blessed One’s male organ concealed in a sheath. Then, the Blessed One, having extended his tongue, touched and stroked both ear orifices, touched and stroked both nostril orifices, and covered the entire orb of his forehead with his tongue. Then this thought occurred to the young man Uttara: 'The ascetic Gotama is indeed endowed with the thirty-two marks of a great man. Let me now follow the ascetic Gotama and observe his deportment.' Then, for seven months, the young man Uttara followed the Blessed One like an inseparable shadow.

386. Atha kho uttaro māṇavo sattannaṃ māsānaṃ accayena videhesu yena mithilā tena cārikaṃ pakkāmi. Anupubbena cārikaṃ caramāno yena mithilā yena brahmāyu brāhmaṇo tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā brahmāyuṃ brāhmaṇaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ [T 2.0532] nisinnaṃ kho uttaraṃ māṇavaṃ brahmāyu brāhmaṇo etadavoca – “kacci, tāta uttara, taṃ bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ tathā santaṃyeva saddo abbhuggato[P 2.0136], no aññathā? Kacci pana so bhavaṃ gotamo tādiso, no aññādiso”ti? “Tathā santaṃyeva, bho, taṃ bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ saddo abbhuggato, no aññathā; tādisova tādisova bho (sī. pī.), tādiso ca kho (syā. kaṃ. ka.) so bhavaṃ gotamo, no aññādiso. Samannāgato ca samannāgato ca bho (sabbattha) so bhavaṃ gotamo dvattiṃsamahāpurisalakkhaṇehi.

386. Then, after the passing of seven months, the young man Uttara set out on a journey in the Videha country towards Mithilā. Traveling in stages, he approached Mithilā, where the brahmin Brahmāyu was. Having approached, he paid homage to the brahmin Brahmāyu and sat down to one side. To the young man Uttara, who was seated to one side, the brahmin Brahmāyu said this: 'Is it so, dear Uttara, that the fame of the venerable Gotama has arisen based on his actual qualities, and not otherwise? And is the venerable Gotama indeed like that, and not different?' 'Indeed, venerable sir, the fame of the venerable Gotama has arisen based on his actual qualities, and not otherwise. The venerable Gotama is indeed like that, and not different. And the venerable Gotama is endowed with the thirty-two marks of a great man.'

“Suppatiṭṭhitapādo kho pana bhavaṃ gotamo; idampi tassa bhoto gotamassa mahāpurisassa mahāpurisalakkhaṇaṃ bhavati.

Indeed, the venerable Gotama has well-placed feet. This, too, of the venerable Gotama, is a mark of a great man.

“Heṭṭhā kho pana tassa bhoto gotamassa pādatalesu cakkāni jātāni sahassārāni sanemikāni sanābhikāni sabbākāraparipūrāni…

Indeed, on the soles of the venerable Gotama's feet, wheels have appeared with a thousand spokes, with rims and hubs, complete in every aspect.

“Āyatapaṇhi [M 2.0337][V 2.0344] kho pana so bhavaṃ gotamo…

Indeed, the venerable Gotama has long heels.

“Dīghaṅguli kho pana so bhavaṃ gotamo…

Indeed, the venerable Gotama has long fingers and toes.

“Mudutalunahatthapādo kho pana so bhavaṃ gotamo…

Indeed, the venerable Gotama has soft and tender palms and soles.

“Jālahatthapādo kho pana so bhavaṃ gotamo…

Indeed, the venerable Gotama has webbed hands and feet.

“Ussaṅkhapādo kho pana so bhavaṃ gotamo…

Indeed, the venerable Gotama has high insteps.

“Eṇijaṅgho kho pana so bhavaṃ gotamo…

Indeed, the venerable Gotama has shanks like those of an Eṇī deer.

“Ṭhitako kho pana so bhavaṃ gotamo anonamanto ubhohi pāṇitalehi jaṇṇukāni parimasati parimajjati…

Indeed, the venerable Gotama, while standing and without bending, can touch and stroke his knees with both palms.

“Kosohitavatthaguyho kho pana so bhavaṃ gotamo…

Indeed, the venerable Gotama has his male organ concealed in a sheath.

“Suvaṇṇavaṇṇo kho pana so bhavaṃ gotamo kañcanasannibhattaco…

Indeed, the venerable Gotama has a golden complexion, his skin like burnished gold.

“Sukhumacchavi kho pana so bhavaṃ gotamo. Sukhumattā chaviyā rajojallaṃ kāye na upalimpati…

Indeed, the venerable Gotama has fine skin. Because of the fineness of his skin, dust and dirt do not adhere to his body.

“Ekekalomo kho pana so bhavaṃ [T 2.0533] gotamo; ekekāni lomāni lomakūpesu jātāni…

Indeed, the venerable Gotama has one hair per pore; single hairs grow in each hair follicle.

“Uddhaggalomo kho pana so bhavaṃ gotamo; uddhaggāni lomāni jātāni nīlāni añjanavaṇṇāni kuṇḍalāvaṭṭāni dakkhiṇāvaṭṭakajātāni…

Indeed, the venerable Gotama has body-hairs that grow upwards; the hairs that grow are directed upwards, are blue-black like collyrium, curled in rings, and turn to the right.

“Brahmujugatto kho pana so bhavaṃ gotamo…

Indeed, the venerable Gotama has a body as straight as Brahmā's.

“Sattussado kho pana so bhavaṃ gotamo…

Indeed, the venerable Gotama has seven convexities.

“Sīhapubbaddhakāyo [V 2.0345] kho pana so bhavaṃ gotamo…

Indeed, the venerable Gotama has the front half of his body like a lion's.

“Citantaraṃso kho pana so bhavaṃ gotamo…

Indeed, the venerable Gotama has the space between his shoulders well-filled.

“Nigrodhaparimaṇḍalo kho pana so bhavaṃ gotamo; yāvatakvassa kāyo tāvatakvassa byāmo, yāvatakvassa byāmo tāvatakvassa kāyo…

Indeed, the venerable Gotama has the proportions of a banyan tree: his height is equal to his arm-span, and his arm-span is equal to his height.

“Samavaṭṭakkhandho kho pana so bhavaṃ gotamo…

Indeed, the venerable Gotama has an evenly rounded neck.

“Rasaggasaggī kho pana so bhavaṃ gotamo…

Indeed, the venerable Gotama has a supreme faculty of taste.

“Sīhahanu [M 2.0338] kho pana [P 2.0137] so bhavaṃ gotamo…

Indeed, the venerable Gotama has a jaw like a lion's.

“Cattālīsadanto kho pana so bhavaṃ gotamo…

Indeed, the venerable Gotama has forty teeth.

“Samadanto kho pana so bhavaṃ gotamo…

Indeed, the venerable Gotama has even teeth.

“Aviraḷadanto kho pana so bhavaṃ gotamo…

Indeed, the venerable Gotama has teeth without gaps.

“Susukkadāṭho kho pana so bhavaṃ gotamo…

Indeed, the venerable Gotama has brilliant white canine teeth.

“Pahūtajivho kho pana so bhavaṃ gotamo…

Indeed, the venerable Gotama has a long and broad tongue.

“Brahmassaro kho pana so bhavaṃ gotamo karavikabhāṇī…

Indeed, the venerable Gotama has a voice like Brahmā's, with the melodious call of the Karavīka bird.

“Abhinīlanetto kho pana so bhavaṃ gotamo…

Indeed, the venerable Gotama has deep blue eyes.

“Gopakhumo [V 2.0346] kho pana so bhavaṃ gotamo…

Indeed, the venerable Gotama has eyelashes like those of a calf.

“Uṇṇā kho panassa bhoto gotamassa bhamukantare jātā odātā mudutūlasannibhā…

Indeed, an ūrṇā has grown between the venerable Gotama's eyebrows, white and soft like cotton wool.

“Uṇhīsasīso kho pana so bhavaṃ gotamo; idampi tassa bhoto gotamassa mahāpurisassa mahāpurisalakkhaṇaṃ bhavati.

Indeed, the venerable Gotama has a head like a royal turban. This, too, of the venerable Gotama, is a mark of a great man.

“Imehi kho, bho, so bhavaṃ gotamo dvattiṃsamahāpurisalakkhaṇehi samannāgato.

Indeed, sirs, that venerable Gotama is endowed with these thirty-two marks of a great man.

387. “Gacchanto kho pana so bhavaṃ gotamo dakkhiṇeneva pādena [T 2.0534] paṭhamaṃ pakkamati. So nātidūre pādaṃ uddharati, nāccāsanne pādaṃ nikkhipati; so nātisīghaṃ gacchati, nātisaṇikaṃ gacchati; na ca adduvena adduvaṃ saṅghaṭṭento gacchati, na ca gopphakena gopphakaṃ saṅghaṭṭento gacchati. So gacchanto na satthiṃ unnāmeti, na satthiṃ onāmeti; na satthiṃ sannāmeti, na satthiṃ vināmeti. Gacchato kho pana tassa bhoto gotamassa adharakāyova aḍḍhakāyova (ka.), āraddhakāyova (syā. kaṃ.) iñjati, na ca kāyabalena gacchati. Apalokento kho pana so bhavaṃ gotamo sabbakāyeneva apaloketi; so na uddhaṃ ulloketi, na adho oloketi; na ca vipekkhamāno gacchati, yugamattañca pekkhati; tato cassa uttari anāvaṭaṃ ñāṇadassanaṃ bhavati. So antaragharaṃ pavisanto na kāyaṃ unnāmeti[M 2.0339], na kāyaṃ onāmeti; na kāyaṃ sannāmeti, na [P 2.0138] kāyaṃ vināmeti. So nātidūre nāccāsanne āsanassa parivattati, na ca pāṇinā ālambitvā āsane nisīdati, na ca āsanasmiṃ kāyaṃ pakkhipati. So antaraghare nisinno samāno na hatthakukkuccaṃ āpajjati, na pādakukkuccaṃ āpajjati; na adduvena adduvaṃ āropetvā nisīdati; na ca gopphakena gopphakaṃ āropetvā nisīdati; na ca pāṇinā hanukaṃ upadahitvā upādiyitvā (sī. pī.) nisīdati. So antaraghare nisinno samāno na chambhati na kampati na vedhati na paritassati. So achambhī akampī avedhī aparitassī vigatalomahaṃso. Vivekavatto ca so bhavaṃ gotamo antaraghare nisinno hoti. So pattodakaṃ paṭiggaṇhanto [T 2.0535] na pattaṃ unnāmeti, na pattaṃ onāmeti; na pattaṃ sannāmeti, na pattaṃ vināmeti. So pattodakaṃ paṭiggaṇhāti nātithokaṃ nātibahuṃ. So na khulukhulukārakaṃ bulubulukārakaṃ (sī.) pattaṃ dhovati, na samparivattakaṃ pattaṃ dhovati, na [V 2.0347] pattaṃ bhūmiyaṃ nikkhipitvā hatthe dhovati; hatthesu dhotesu patto dhoto hoti, patte dhote hatthā dhotā honti. So pattodakaṃ chaḍḍeti nātidūre nāccāsanne, na ca vicchaḍḍayamāno. So odanaṃ paṭiggaṇhanto na pattaṃ unnāmeti, na pattaṃ onāmeti; na pattaṃ sannāmeti, na pattaṃ vināmeti. So odanaṃ paṭiggaṇhāti nātithokaṃ nātibahuṃ. Byañjanaṃ kho pana bhavaṃ gotamo byañjanamattāya āhāreti, na ca byañjanena ālopaṃ atināmeti. Dvattikkhattuṃ kho bhavaṃ gotamo mukhe ālopaṃ samparivattetvā ajjhoharati; na cassa kāci odanamiñjā asambhinnā kāyaṃ pavisati, na cassa kāci odanamiñjā mukhe avasiṭṭhā hoti; athāparaṃ ālopaṃ upanāmeti. Rasapaṭisaṃvedī kho pana so bhavaṃ gotamo āhāraṃ āhāreti, no ca rasarāgapaṭisaṃvedī.

387. Indeed, when that venerable Gotama walks, he steps forward with his right foot first. He does not lift his foot too far, nor place it too near. He walks neither too fast nor too slow. He does not walk with knee striking against knee, nor with ankle striking against ankle. When walking, he does not raise his thigh, nor lower his thigh, nor draw his thigh in, nor thrust his thigh out. When that venerable Gotama walks, only his lower body moves; he does not walk by swaying his body. When looking around, that venerable Gotama looks around with his whole body. He does not look upward, nor does he look downward. He does not go along looking about, but looks a yoke’s length ahead; and beyond that, his knowledge and vision is unobstructed. When entering a house, he does not raise his body, nor lower his body, nor hunch his body, nor arch his body. He turns neither too far from nor too near to a seat. He does not sit down supporting himself with his hand, nor does he throw his body onto the seat. When seated indoors, he does not fidget with his hands, nor does he fidget with his feet. He does not sit with one knee placed upon the other, nor with one ankle placed upon the other. He does not sit supporting his chin with his hand. When seated indoors, that venerable Gotama is not startled, does not tremble, does not shake, and is not agitated. He is without fear, unshaken, untrembling, not agitated, and the hair of his body does not stand on end. And that venerable Gotama, when seated indoors, has his mind inclined to seclusion. When receiving water for his bowl, he does not raise the bowl, nor lower the bowl, nor incline the bowl inwards, nor incline the bowl outwards. He receives the bowl-water in a quantity that is neither too little nor too much. He does not wash the bowl making a ‘khulu-khulu’ sound, nor does he wash the bowl by turning it over and over. He does not place the bowl on the ground to wash his hands; when the hands are washed, the bowl is washed, and when the bowl is washed, the hands are washed. He discards the bowl-water neither too far nor too near, and not by scattering it. When receiving rice, he does not raise the bowl, nor lower the bowl, nor incline the bowl inwards, nor incline the bowl outwards. He receives the rice in a quantity that is neither too little nor too much. The venerable Gotama partakes of the curry in proportion to the rice, and does not let the curry overwhelm the mouthful. The venerable Gotama turns the mouthful over in his mouth two or three times before swallowing. No unbroken grain of rice enters his body, and no grain of rice remains in his mouth when he brings forward the next mouthful. Indeed, that venerable Gotama partakes of food experiencing the taste, but not experiencing craving for the taste.

“Aṭṭhaṅgasamannāgataṃ aṭṭhaṅgasamannāgato (ka.) kho pana so bhavaṃ gotamo āhāraṃ āhāreti – neva davāya, na madāya na maṇḍanāya na vibhūsanāya, yāvadeva imassa kāyassa ṭhitiyā yāpanāya, vihiṃsūparatiyā brahmacariyānuggahāya – ‘iti purāṇañca [P 2.0139] vedanaṃ paṭihaṅkhāmi navañca vedanaṃ na uppādessāmi, yātrā ca me [T 2.0536] bhavissati anavajjatā ca phāsuvihāro cā’ti[M 2.0340]. So bhuttāvī pattodakaṃ paṭiggaṇhanto na pattaṃ unnāmeti, na pattaṃ onāmeti; na pattaṃ sannāmeti, na pattaṃ vināmeti. So pattodakaṃ paṭiggaṇhāti nātithokaṃ nātibahuṃ. So na khulukhulukārakaṃ pattaṃ dhovati, na samparivattakaṃ pattaṃ dhovati, na pattaṃ bhūmiyaṃ nikkhipitvā hatthe dhovati; hatthesu dhotesu patto dhoto hoti, patte dhote hatthā dhotā honti. So pattodakaṃ chaḍḍeti nātidūre nāccāsanne, na ca vicchaḍḍayamāno. So bhuttāvī na pattaṃ bhūmiyaṃ nikkhipati nātidūre nāccāsanne, na ca anatthiko pattena hoti, na ca ativelānurakkhī pattasmiṃ. So bhuttāvī muhuttaṃ tuṇhī nisīdati, na ca anumodanassa kālamatināmeti. So bhuttāvī anumodati, na taṃ bhattaṃ garahati, na aññaṃ bhattaṃ paṭikaṅkhati; aññadatthu dhammiyā kathāya taṃ parisaṃ sandasseti samādapeti samuttejeti sampahaṃseti. So taṃ parisaṃ dhammiyā kathāya sandassetvā samādapetvā samuttejetvā sampahaṃsetvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkamati. So nātisīghaṃ gacchati, nātisaṇikaṃ gacchati, na ca muccitukāmo gacchati; na ca tassa bhoto gotamassa kāye cīvaraṃ accukkaṭṭhaṃ hoti na ca accokkaṭṭhaṃ, na ca kāyasmiṃ allīnaṃ na ca kāyasmā apakaṭṭhaṃ; na ca tassa bhoto gotamassa kāyamhā vāto cīvaraṃ apavahati; na ca tassa bhoto [V 2.0348] gotamassa kāye rajojallaṃ upalimpati[T 2.0537]. So ārāmagato nisīdati paññatte āsane. Nisajja pāde pakkhāleti; na ca so bhavaṃ gotamo pādamaṇḍanānuyogamanuyutto viharati. So pāde pakkhāletvā nisīdati pallaṅkaṃ ābhujitvā ujuṃ kāyaṃ paṇidhāya parimukhaṃ satiṃ upaṭṭhapetvā. So neva attabyābādhāya ceteti, na parabyābādhāya ceteti, na ubhayabyābādhāya ceteti; attahitaparahitaubhayahitasabbalokahitameva [P 2.0140] so bhavaṃ gotamo cintento nisinno hoti. So ārāmagato parisati dhammaṃ deseti, na taṃ parisaṃ ussādeti, na taṃ parisaṃ apasādeti; aññadatthu dhammiyā kathāya taṃ parisaṃ sandasseti samādapeti samuttejeti sampahaṃseti.

Indeed, the venerable Gotama partakes of food endowed with eight factors: not for amusement, not for intoxication, not for beautification, not for adornment, but only for the maintenance and sustenance of this body, for the cessation of discomfort, and for the support of the holy life, thinking: ‘Thus I shall ward off old feelings and not allow new feelings to arise, and there will be for me sustenance, blamelessness, and a comfortable abiding.’ Having eaten, while accepting the bowl-rinsing water, he does not raise the bowl up, nor bend it down; he does not bend it inwards, nor bend it outwards. He accepts bowl-rinsing water that is not too little and not too much. He does not wash the bowl making a ‘khulukhulu’ sound, nor does he wash the bowl turning it over and over, nor does he place the bowl on the ground to wash his hands; when the hands are washed, the bowl is washed, and when the bowl is washed, the hands are washed. He discards the bowl-rinsing water neither too far nor too near, and without scattering it. Having eaten, he does not place the bowl on the ground too far or too near; nor is he unconcerned with the bowl, nor is he excessively protective of it. Having eaten, he sits silently for a moment and does not let the time for the blessing pass. Having eaten, he gives the blessing; he does not disparage that meal, nor does he long for another meal; but rather, with a talk on the Dhamma, he instructs, encourages, incites, and gladdens that assembly. Having instructed, encouraged, incited, and gladdened that assembly with a talk on the Dhamma, he rises from his seat and departs. He goes neither too quickly nor too slowly, and not as one desiring to be released. On the venerable Gotama’s body, the robe is not worn too high up or too low down, nor is it clinging to his body or far from his body; the wind does not carry the robe away from the venerable Gotama’s body, nor does dust and dirt smear his body. Having gone to the monastery, he sits on a prepared seat. Having sat down, he washes his feet; the venerable Gotama does not dwell engaged in the practice of adorning his feet. Having washed his feet, he sits, having folded his legs crosswise, holding his body erect, and establishing mindfulness before him. He does not intend for his own affliction, nor for the affliction of others, nor for the affliction of both; the venerable Gotama sits thinking only of his own welfare, the welfare of others, the welfare of both, and the welfare of the entire world. Having gone to the monastery, he teaches the Dhamma to the assembly; he does not exalt that assembly, nor does he disparage it; but rather, with a talk on the Dhamma, he instructs, encourages, incites, and gladdens that assembly.

“Aṭṭhaṅgasamannāgato kho panassa bhoto gotamassa mukhato ghoso niccharati – vissaṭṭho ca, viññeyyo ca, mañju ca, savanīyo ca, bindu ca, avisārī ca, gambhīro ca, ninnādī ca. Yathāparisaṃ kho pana so bhavaṃ [M 2.0341] gotamo sarena viññāpeti, na cassa bahiddhā parisāya ghoso niccharati. Te tena bhotā gotamena dhammiyā kathāya sandassitā samādapitā samuttejitā sampahaṃsitā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkamanti avalokayamānāyeva apalokayamānāyeva (sī. ka.) avijahitattā avijahantābhāvena (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.). Addasāma kho mayaṃ, bho, taṃ bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ gacchantaṃ, addasāma ṭhitaṃ, addasāma antaragharaṃ pavisantaṃ, addasāma antaraghare nisinnaṃ tuṇhībhūtaṃ, addasāma antaraghare bhuñjantaṃ, addasāma bhuttāviṃ nisinnaṃ tuṇhībhūtaṃ, addasāma bhuttāviṃ anumodantaṃ, addasāma ārāmaṃ [T 2.0538] gacchantaṃ, addasāma ārāmagataṃ nisinnaṃ tuṇhībhūtaṃ, addasāma ārāmagataṃ parisati dhammaṃ desentaṃ. Ediso ca ediso ca so bhavaṃ gotamo, tato ca bhiyyo”ti.

Indeed, from the mouth of the venerable Gotama issues a voice endowed with eight qualities: it is clear, intelligible, pleasing, audible, articulate, unbroken, deep, and resonant. The venerable Gotama makes himself understood with a voice appropriate to the assembly, and his voice does not go outside the assembly. Those who have been instructed, encouraged, incited, and gladdened by the venerable Gotama with a talk on the Dhamma rise from their seats and depart, only while looking back, as if unable to leave him. Indeed, sir, we have seen the venerable Gotama going; we have seen him standing; we have seen him entering a house; we have seen him sitting silently inside a house; we have seen him eating inside a house; we have seen him sitting silently after eating; we have seen him giving the blessing after eating; we have seen him going to the monastery; we have seen him sitting silently, having gone to the monastery; we have seen him teaching the Dhamma to an assembly, having gone to the monastery. Such and such is the venerable Gotama, and even more than that.

388. Evaṃ vutte, brahmāyu brāhmaṇo uṭṭhāyāsanā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā yena bhagavā tenañjaliṃ paṇāmetvā tikkhattuṃ udānaṃ udāneti –

388. When this was said, the brahmin Brahmāyu rose from his seat, arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, extended his joined palms in the direction of the Blessed One, and three times uttered this inspired utterance:

“Namo tassa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa.

Homage to that Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One.

“Namo tassa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa.

Homage to that Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One.

“Namo [V 2.0349] tassa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassā”ti.

Homage to that Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One.

“Appeva nāma mayaṃ kadāci karahaci tena bhotā gotamena samāgaccheyyāma? Appeva nāma siyā kocideva kathāsallāpo”ti!

Oh, that we might, sometime or other, meet with the venerable Gotama! Oh, that there might be some conversation!

389. Atha kho bhagavā videhesu anupubbena cārikaṃ caramāno yena mithilā tadavasari. Tatra sudaṃ bhagavā mithilāyaṃ viharati maghadevambavane. Assosuṃ kho mithileyyakā methileyyakā (sī. pī.) brāhmaṇagahapatikā – “samaṇo khalu, bho, gotamo [P 2.0141] sakyaputto sakyakulā pabbajito videhesu cārikaṃ caramāno mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ pañcamattehi bhikkhusatehi mithilaṃ anuppatto, mithilāyaṃ viharati maghadevambavane. Taṃ kho pana bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ evaṃ kalyāṇo kittisaddo abbhuggato – ‘itipi so bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho vijjācaraṇasampanno sugato lokavidū anuttaro purisadammasārathi satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavāti. So imaṃ lokaṃ sadevakaṃ samārakaṃ sabrahmakaṃ sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiṃ [M 2.0342] pajaṃ sadevamanussaṃ sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā pavedeti[T 2.0539]. So dhammaṃ deseti ādikalyāṇaṃ majjhekalyāṇaṃ pariyosānakalyāṇaṃ sātthaṃ sabyañjanaṃ, kevalaparipuṇṇaṃ parisuddhaṃ brahmacariyaṃ pakāseti. Sādhu kho pana tathārūpānaṃ arahataṃ dassanaṃ hotī’”ti.

389. Then the Blessed One, traveling stage by stage in the Videha country, arrived at Mithilā. There the Blessed One stayed in the Maghadeva Mango Grove. The brahmins and householders of Mithilā heard: “The ascetic Gotama, the son of the Sakyans, who has gone forth from the Sakyan clan, has been traveling in the Videha country with a large Saṅgha of bhikkhus, with about five hundred bhikkhus, and has arrived at Mithilā. He is staying in the Maghadeva Mango Grove. A good report about the Venerable Gotama has been circulating: ‘Indeed, the Blessed One is an Arahant, a Perfectly Self-Enlightened One, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, the Well-Gone One, knower of the world, unexcelled trainer of persons to be tamed, teacher of devas and humans, the Enlightened One, the Blessed One. Having realized with his own direct knowledge this world with its devas, Māras, and Brahmās, this generation with its recluses and brahmins, its devas and humans, he makes it known to others. He teaches the Dhamma that is good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, with its meaning and phrasing, and he reveals the perfectly complete and purified holy life. It is good to see such Arahants.’”

Atha kho mithileyyakā brāhmaṇagahapatikā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā appekacce bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu; appekacce bhagavatā saddhiṃ sammodiṃsu, sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu; appekacce yena bhagavā tenañjaliṃ paṇāmetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu; appekacce bhagavato santike nāmagottaṃ sāvetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu; appekacce tuṇhībhūtā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu.

Then the brahmins and householders of Mithilā approached the Blessed One. Having approached, some paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side; some exchanged greetings with the Blessed One, and when that courteous and amiable talk was concluded, sat down to one side; some raised their joined hands in salutation towards the Blessed One and sat down to one side; some announced their name and clan in the presence of the Blessed One and sat down to one side; some kept silent and sat down to one side.

390. Assosi kho brahmāyu brāhmaṇo – “samaṇo khalu, bho, gotamo sakyaputto sakyakulā pabbajito mithilaṃ anuppatto, mithilāyaṃ viharati maghadevambavane”ti. Atha kho brahmāyu brāhmaṇo sambahulehi sāvakehi saddhiṃ yena maghadevambavanaṃ tenupasaṅkami. Atha kho brahmāyuno brāhmaṇassa avidūre ambavanassa etadahosi – “na kho metaṃ patirūpaṃ yohaṃ pubbe appaṭisaṃvidito [V 2.0350] samaṇaṃ gotamaṃ dassanāya upasaṅkameyya”nti. Atha kho brahmāyu brāhmaṇo aññataraṃ māṇavakaṃ āmantesi – “ehi tvaṃ, māṇavaka, yena samaṇo gotamo tenupasaṅkama; upasaṅkamitvā mama vacanena samaṇaṃ gotamaṃ appābādhaṃ appātaṅkaṃ lahuṭṭhānaṃ balaṃ phāsuvihāraṃ puccha – ‘brahmāyu, bho gotama, brāhmaṇo bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ appābādhaṃ appātaṅkaṃ lahuṭṭhānaṃ balaṃ phāsuvihāraṃ pucchatī’ti. Evañca vadehi – ‘brahmāyu, bho [T 2.0540] gotama, brāhmaṇo jiṇṇo vuḍḍho mahallako addhagato vayoanuppatto, vīsavassasatiko jātiyā, tiṇṇaṃ vedānaṃ pāragū sanighaṇḍukeṭubhānaṃ sākkharappabhedānaṃ itihāsapañcamānaṃ, padako, veyyākaraṇo, lokāyatamahāpurisalakkhaṇesu anavayo. Yāvatā, bho, brāhmaṇagahapatikā mithilāyaṃ paṭivasanti, brahmāyu tesaṃ brāhmaṇo aggamakkhāyati – yadidaṃ bhogehi; brahmāyu tesaṃ brāhmaṇo aggamakkhāyati – yadidaṃ mantehi; brahmāyu [P 2.0142] tesaṃ brāhmaṇo aggamakkhāyati – yadidaṃ āyunā ceva yasasā ca. So bhoto gotamassa dassanakāmo’”ti.

390. The brahmin Brahmāyu heard: “Indeed, the ascetic Gotama, the son of the Sakyans, who has gone forth from the Sakyan clan, has arrived at Mithilā and is dwelling in the Maghadeva Mango Grove.” Then the brahmin Brahmāyu, together with many disciples, approached the Maghadeva Mango Grove. Then, when the brahmin Brahmāyu was not far from the mango grove, this thought occurred to him: “It would not be proper for me to approach the ascetic Gotama without first being introduced.” Then the brahmin Brahmāyu addressed a certain young man: “Come, young man, approach the ascetic Gotama. Having approached, ask the ascetic Gotama in my name whether he is free from illness and affliction, light in his movements, strong, and dwelling comfortably—saying: ‘Venerable Gotama, the brahmin Brahmāyu asks whether you are free from illness and affliction, light in your movements, strong, and dwelling comfortably.’ And say this: ‘Venerable Gotama, the brahmin Brahmāyu is old, aged, burdened with years, advanced in life, having reached the final stage of life, being one hundred and twenty years old by birth. He is a master of the three Vedas, with the glossaries, treatises on rhetoric, and phonology, and with the histories as a fifth; a master of the verses and of grammar, he is unerring concerning natural philosophy and the marks of a great man. As many brahmins and householders as dwell in Mithilā, Brahmāyu is declared foremost among them—that is, in regard to wealth, in regard to the mantras, and in regard to both longevity and fame. He wishes to see the Venerable Gotama.’”

“Evaṃ[M 2.0343], bho”ti kho so māṇavako brahmāyussa brāhmaṇassa paṭissutvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhito kho so māṇavako bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “brahmāyu, bho gotama, brāhmaṇo bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ appābādhaṃ appātaṅkaṃ lahuṭṭhānaṃ balaṃ phāsuvihāraṃ pucchati; evañca vadeti – ‘brahmāyu, bho gotama, brāhmaṇo jiṇṇo vuḍḍho mahallako addhagato vayoanuppatto, vīsavassasatiko jātiyā, tiṇṇaṃ vedānaṃ pāragū sanighaṇḍukeṭubhānaṃ sākkharappabhedānaṃ itihāsapañcamānaṃ, padako, veyyākaraṇo, lokāyatamahāpurisalakkhaṇesu [T 2.0541] anavayo. Yāvatā, bho, brāhmaṇagahapatikā mithilāyaṃ paṭivasanti, brahmāyu tesaṃ brāhmaṇo aggamakkhāyati – yadidaṃ bhogehi; brahmāyu tesaṃ brāhmaṇo aggamakkhāyati – yadidaṃ mantehi; brahmāyu tesaṃ brāhmaṇo aggamakkhāyati – yadidaṃ āyunā ceva yasasā ca. So bhoto gotamassa dassanakāmo’”ti. “Yassadāni, māṇava, brahmāyu brāhmaṇo kālaṃ maññatī”ti. Atha kho so māṇavako yena brahmāyu brāhmaṇo tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā brahmāyuṃ brāhmaṇaṃ etadavoca – “katāvakāso khomhi bhavatā samaṇena gotamena. Yassadāni bhavaṃ kālaṃ maññatī”ti.

“Yes, sir,” replied the young man to the brahmin Brahmāyu, and he approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he exchanged greetings with the Blessed One. And when that courteous and amiable talk was concluded, he stood to one side. Standing to one side, the young man said to the Blessed One: “Venerable Gotama, the brahmin Brahmāyu asks after your health—whether you are free from illness, free from affliction, light in your movements, strong, and dwelling comfortably. And he says this: ‘Venerable Gotama, the brahmin Brahmāyu is old, aged, burdened with years, advanced in life, having reached the final stage of life; he is one hundred and twenty years old by birth, a master of the three Vedas, with the glossaries, treatises on rhetoric, and phonology, and with the histories as a fifth; a master of the verses and of grammar, and unerring concerning natural philosophy and the marks of a great man. As many brahmins and householders as dwell in Mithilā, Brahmāyu is declared foremost among them—that is, in regard to wealth, in regard to the mantras, and in regard to both longevity and fame. He wishes to see the Venerable Gotama.’ ” “Let the brahmin Brahmāyu come when he deems it the time, young man,” replied the Blessed One. Then the young man returned to the brahmin Brahmāyu and said: “I have made an opportunity for you with the ascetic Gotama, sir. Let the venerable one come when he deems it the time.”

391. Atha [V 2.0351] kho brahmāyu brāhmaṇo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami. Addasā kho sā parisā brahmāyuṃ brāhmaṇaṃ dūratova āgacchantaṃ. Disvāna oramiya oramattha (syā. kaṃ. pī.), oramatha, oramati (ka.), atha naṃ (sī.), oramiyāti pana tvāpaccayantatathasaṃvaṇṇanānurūpaṃ visodhitapadaṃ okāsamakāsi yathā taṃ ñātassa yasassino. Atha kho brahmāyu brāhmaṇo taṃ parisaṃ etadavoca – “alaṃ, bho! Nisīdatha tumhe sake āsane. Idhāhaṃ samaṇassa gotamassa santike nisīdissāmī”ti.

391. Then the brahmin Brahmāyu approached the Blessed One. The assembly saw the brahmin Brahmāyu coming from afar. Seeing him, they moved aside and made space for him, as was fitting for one who was known and famous. Then the brahmin Brahmāyu addressed that assembly: “Enough, sirs! Sit on your own seats. Here I will sit near the ascetic Gotama.”

Atha kho brahmāyu brāhmaṇo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho brahmāyu brāhmaṇo bhagavato [M 2.0344] kāye [P 2.0143] dvattiṃsamahāpurisalakkhaṇāni samannesi. Addasā kho brahmāyu brāhmaṇo bhagavato [T 2.0542] kāye dvattiṃsamahāpurisalakkhaṇāni, yebhuyyena ṭhapetvā dve. Dvīsu mahāpurisalakkhaṇesu kaṅkhati vicikicchati nādhimuccati na sampasīdati – kosohite ca vatthaguyhe, pahūtajivhatāya ca. Atha kho brahmāyu brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṃ gāthāhi ajjhabhāsi –

Then the brahmin Brahmāyu approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he exchanged joyful and memorable greetings with the Blessed One. When that courteous talk was concluded, he sat down to one side. Sitting to one side, the brahmin Brahmāyu investigated the thirty-two marks of a great man on the Blessed One’s body. The brahmin Brahmāyu saw on the Blessed One’s body the thirty-two marks of a great man for the most part, except for two. Regarding two of the marks of a great man he was doubtful and uncertain, he could not be confident or clear: the sheath-enclosed male organ and the large tongue. Then the brahmin Brahmāyu addressed the Blessed One with verses:

“Ye me dvattiṃsāti sutā, mahāpurisalakkhaṇā;

Duve tesaṃ na passāmi, bhoto kāyasmiṃ gotama.

“The thirty-two marks of a great man that I have heard of—two of them I do not see on your body, Gotama.

“Kacci kosohitaṃ bhoto, vatthaguyhaṃ naruttama;

Nārīsamānasavhayā, kacci jivhā na dassakā nārīsahanāma savhayā, kacci jivhā narassikā; (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.).

“O supreme among men, is your male organ enclosed in a sheath? And is your tongue, which has a feminine designation, not visible?

“Kacci pahūtajivhosi, yathā taṃ jāniyāmase;

Ninnāmayetaṃ pahūtaṃ, kaṅkhaṃ vinaya no ise.

“Do you have a large tongue? So that we may know, please extend that large tongue. Dispel our doubt, O Sage.

“Diṭṭhadhammahitatthāya, samparāyasukhāya ca;

Katāvakāsā pucchāma, yaṃ kiñci abhipatthita”nti.

“For the sake of welfare in this present life, and for the sake of happiness in the next life, having been given the opportunity, we ask whatever we desire.”

392. Atha kho bhagavato etadahosi – “passati kho me ayaṃ brahmāyu brāhmaṇo dvattiṃsamahāpurisalakkhaṇāni, yebhuyyena ṭhapetvā dve. Dvīsu mahāpurisalakkhaṇesu kaṅkhati vicikicchati nādhimuccati na sampasīdati – kosohite ca vatthaguyhe, pahūtajivhatāya cā”ti[V 2.0352]. Atha kho bhagavā tathārūpaṃ iddhābhisaṅkhāraṃ abhisaṅkhāsi yathā addasa brahmāyu brāhmaṇo bhagavato kosohitaṃ vatthaguyhaṃ. Atha kho bhagavā jivhaṃ ninnāmetvā ubhopi kaṇṇasotāni anumasi paṭimasi; ubhopi nāsikasotāni [T 2.0543] anumasi paṭimasi; kevalampi nalāṭamaṇḍalaṃ jivhāya chādesi. Atha kho bhagavā brahmāyuṃ brāhmaṇaṃ gāthāhi paccabhāsi –

392. Then this thought occurred to the Blessed One: “This brahmin Brahmāyu sees the thirty-two marks of a great man on me for the most part, except for two. Regarding two of the marks of a great man he is doubtful and uncertain, he cannot be confident or clear: the sheath-enclosed male organ and the large tongue.” Then the Blessed One performed a feat of psychic power in such a way that the brahmin Brahmāyu saw the Blessed One’s sheath-enclosed male organ. Then the Blessed One, having extended his tongue, touched back and forth both ear-holes; he touched back and forth both nostrils; and he covered the entire surface of his forehead with his tongue. Then the Blessed One replied to the brahmin Brahmāyu in verses:

“Ye te dvattiṃsāti sutā, mahāpurisalakkhaṇā;

Sabbe te mama kāyasmiṃ, mā te mā vo (ka.) kaṅkhāhu brāhmaṇa.

“The thirty-two marks of a great man that you have heard of—all of them are on my body. Let there be no doubt for you, brahmin.

“Abhiññeyyaṃ abhiññātaṃ, bhāvetabbañca bhāvitaṃ;

Pahātabbaṃ pahīnaṃ me, tasmā buddhosmi brāhmaṇa.

“What is to be directly known has been directly known by me; what is to be developed has been developed; what is to be abandoned has been abandoned. Therefore, brahmin, I am the Buddha.

“Diṭṭhadhammahitatthāya[M 2.0345][P 2.0144], samparāyasukhāya ca;

Katāvakāso pucchassu, yaṃ kiñci abhipatthita”nti.

“For the sake of welfare in this present life, and for the sake of happiness in the next life, having been given the opportunity, ask whatever you desire.”

393. Atha kho brahmāyussa brāhmaṇassa etadahosi – “katāvakāso khomhi samaṇena gotamena. Kiṃ nu kho ahaṃ samaṇaṃ gotamaṃ puccheyyaṃ – ‘diṭṭhadhammikaṃ vā atthaṃ samparāyikaṃ vā’”ti. Atha kho brahmāyussa brāhmaṇassa etadahosi – “kusalo kho ahaṃ diṭṭhadhammikānaṃ atthānaṃ. Aññepi maṃ diṭṭhadhammikaṃ atthaṃ pucchanti. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ samaṇaṃ gotamaṃ samparāyikaṃyeva atthaṃ puccheyya”nti. Atha kho brahmāyu brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṃ gāthāhi ajjhabhāsi –

393. Then this thought occurred to the brahmin Brahmāyu: “I have been given an opportunity by the ascetic Gotama. What, I wonder, should I ask the ascetic Gotama—a matter concerning the present life, or a matter concerning the next life?” Then this thought occurred to the brahmin Brahmāyu: “I am indeed skilled in matters concerning the present life. Others also ask me about matters concerning the present life. It would be good if I were to ask the ascetic Gotama only about a matter concerning the next life.” Then the brahmin Brahmāyu addressed the Blessed One in verses:

“Kathaṃ kho brāhmaṇo hoti, kathaṃ bhavati vedagū;

Tevijjo bho kathaṃ hoti, sotthiyo kinti vuccati.

“How, sir, does one become a brahmin? How does one become one who has gone to the end of knowledge? How, sir, does one become a possessor of the threefold knowledge? Who is called one who is blessed?

“Arahaṃ bho kathaṃ hoti, kathaṃ bhavati kevalī;

Muni ca bho kathaṃ hoti, buddho kinti pavuccatī”ti.

“How, sir, does one become an Arahant? How does one become perfected? How, sir, does one become a sage? And who is called a Buddha?”

394. Atha [T 2.0544] kho bhagavā brahmāyuṃ brāhmaṇaṃ gāthāhi paccabhāsi –

394. Then the Blessed One replied to the brahmin Brahmāyu in verses:

“Pubbenivāsaṃ [V 2.0353] yo vedi, saggāpāyañca passati;

Atho jātikkhayaṃ patto, abhiññā vosito muni.

“One who knows their former abodes, sees heaven and the states of loss, and has reached the destruction of birth, is a sage who has reached the culmination through direct knowledge.

“Cittaṃ visuddhaṃ jānāti, muttaṃ rāgehi sabbaso;

Pahīnajātimaraṇo, brahmacariyassa kevalī;

Pāragū sabbadhammānaṃ, buddho tādī pavuccatī”ti.

“One who knows the purified mind, completely freed from passions; who has abandoned birth and death, perfected in the holy life; who has gone to the far shore of all phenomena—such a one is called a Buddha.”

Evaṃ vutte, brahmāyu brāhmaṇo uṭṭhāyāsanā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā bhagavato pādesu sirasā nipatitvā bhagavato pādāni mukhena ca paricumbati, pāṇīhi ca parisambāhati, nāmañca sāveti – “brahmāyu ahaṃ, bho gotama, brāhmaṇo; brahmāyu ahaṃ, bho gotama, brāhmaṇo”ti. Atha kho sā parisā acchariyabbhutacittajātā ahosi – “acchariyaṃ vata, bho, abbhutaṃ vata, bho! Yatra hi nāmāyaṃ brahmāyu brāhmaṇo ñāto yasassī evarūpaṃ paramanipaccakāraṃ karissatī”ti. Atha kho bhagavā brahmāyuṃ brāhmaṇaṃ etadavoca [P 2.0145] – “alaṃ, brāhmaṇa, uṭṭhaha nisīda tvaṃ sake āsane yato te mayi cittaṃ pasanna”nti. Atha kho brahmāyu brāhmaṇo uṭṭhahitvā sake āsane nisīdi.

When this was said, the brahmin Brahmāyu rose from his seat, arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, prostrated with his head at the Blessed One’s feet, kissed the Blessed One's feet with his mouth, and massaged them with his hands, announcing his name: “I am Brahmāyu, Master Gotama, a brahmin; I am Brahmāyu, Master Gotama, a brahmin.” Then that assembly was filled with an amazing and unprecedented thought: “It is wonderful, sirs, it is truly amazing! That this brahmin Brahmāyu, who is so well-known and famous, should perform such an act of utmost reverence.” Then the Blessed One said to the brahmin Brahmāyu: “Enough, brahmin. Rise and sit in your own seat, since your mind has faith in me.” Then the brahmin Brahmāyu, having risen, sat down in his own seat.

395. Atha [M 2.0346] kho bhagavā brahmāyussa brāhmaṇassa anupubbiṃ kathaṃ kathesi, seyyathidaṃ – dānakathaṃ, sīlakathaṃ, saggakathaṃ; kāmānaṃ ādīnavaṃ okāraṃ saṃkilesaṃ nekkhamme ānisaṃsaṃ pakāsesi. Yadā bhagavā [T 2.0545] aññāsi brahmāyuṃ brāhmaṇaṃ kallacittaṃ muducittaṃ vinīvaraṇacittaṃ udaggacittaṃ pasannacittaṃ, atha yā buddhānaṃ sāmukkaṃsikā dhammadesanā taṃ pakāsesi – dukkhaṃ, samudayaṃ, nirodhaṃ, maggaṃ. Seyyathāpi nāma suddhaṃ vatthaṃ apagatakāḷakaṃ sammadeva rajanaṃ paṭiggaṇheyya, evameva brahmāyussa brāhmaṇassa tasmiṃyeva āsane virajaṃ vītamalaṃ dhammacakkhuṃ udapādi – “yaṃ kiñci samudayadhammaṃ sabbaṃ taṃ nirodhadhamma”nti. Atha kho brahmāyu brāhmaṇo diṭṭhadhammo pattadhammo viditadhammo pariyogāḷhadhammo tiṇṇavicikiccho vigatakathaṃkatho vesārajjappatto aparappaccayo satthusāsane bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “abhikkantaṃ, bho gotama, abhikkantaṃ, bho gotama! Seyyathāpi, bho gotama, nikkujjitaṃ vā ukkujjeyya, paṭicchannaṃ vā vivareyya, mūḷhassa vā maggaṃ ācikkheyya, andhakāre vā telapajjotaṃ dhāreyya – cakkhumanto rūpāni dakkhantīti – evamevaṃ bhotā [V 2.0354] gotamena anekapariyāyena dhammo pakāsito. Esāhaṃ bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāmi dhammañca bhikkhusaṅghañca. Upāsakaṃ maṃ bhavaṃ gotamo dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṃ saraṇaṃ gataṃ. Adhivāsetu ca me bhavaṃ gotamo svātanāya bhattaṃ saddhiṃ bhikkhusaṅghenā”ti. Adhivāsesi bhagavā tuṇhībhāvena. Atha kho brahmāyu brāhmaṇo bhagavato adhivāsanaṃ viditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā pakkāmi[T 2.0546]. Atha kho brahmāyu brāhmaṇo tassā rattiyā accayena sake nivesane paṇītaṃ khādanīyaṃ bhojanīyaṃ paṭiyādāpetvā bhagavato kālaṃ ārocāpesi – “kālo, bho gotama, niṭṭhitaṃ bhatta”nti.

395. Then the Blessed One gave the brahmin Brahmāyu a progressive discourse—that is, a discourse on giving, on virtue, on heaven; he explained the danger, baseness, and defilement of sensual pleasures and the benefit of renunciation. When the Blessed One knew that Brahmāyu the brahmin had a receptive mind, a pliant mind, a mind free from hindrances, an uplifted mind, and a confident mind, he then revealed that Dhamma teaching which is the special dispensation of the Buddhas: suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path. Just as a clean cloth free from black stains would rightly take up dye, even so, for the brahmin Brahmāyu, right in that very seat, the dust-free, stainless Dhamma-eye arose: “Whatever has the nature to arise, all that has the nature to cease.” Then the brahmin Brahmāyu, having seen the Dhamma, attained the Dhamma, understood the Dhamma, penetrated the Dhamma, having crossed over doubt, being free from perplexity, having attained confidence, not reliant on another in the Teacher’s Dispensation, said this to the Blessed One: “Excellent, Master Gotama! Excellent, Master Gotama! Just as, Master Gotama, one might set upright what was overturned, or reveal what was hidden, or point out the way to one who was lost, or hold up an oil lamp in the darkness so that those with eyes might see forms—even so has the Dhamma been made clear in many ways by Master Gotama. I go to Master Gotama for refuge, and to the Dhamma, and to the Bhikkhu Saṅgha. May Master Gotama remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge from this day forth, for as long as life lasts. And may Master Gotama consent to my meal for tomorrow, together with the Bhikkhu Saṅgha.” The Blessed One consented by silence. Then the brahmin Brahmāyu, having understood the Blessed One’s consent, rose from his seat, paid homage to the Blessed One, circumambulated him keeping him to the right, and departed. Then, at the passing of that night, the brahmin Brahmāyu, having had excellent food, both hard and soft, prepared in his own residence, had the time announced to the Blessed One: “It is time, Master Gotama, the meal is ready.”

Atha [P 2.0146] kho bhagavā pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya yena brahmāyussa brāhmaṇassa nivesanaṃ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi saddhiṃ bhikkhusaṅghena. Atha kho brahmāyu brāhmaṇo sattāhaṃ buddhappamukhaṃ bhikkhusaṅghaṃ paṇītena khādanīyena bhojanīyena sahatthā santappesi sampavāresi. Atha kho bhagavā tassa sattāhassa accayena videhesu cārikaṃ pakkāmi. Atha kho brahmāyu brāhmaṇo acirapakkantassa bhagavato kālamakāsi. Atha kho sambahulā [M 2.0347] bhikkhū yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Ekamantaṃ nisinnā kho te bhikkhū bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ – “brahmāyu, bhante, brāhmaṇo kālaṅkato. Tassa kā gati, ko abhisamparāyo”ti? “Paṇḍito, bhikkhave, brahmāyu brāhmaṇo paccapādi dhammassānudhammaṃ, na ca maṃ dhammādhikaraṇaṃ vihesesi. Brahmāyu, bhikkhave, brāhmaṇo pañcannaṃ orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā opapātiko hoti, tattha parinibbāyī, anāvattidhammo tasmā lokā”ti.

Then the Blessed One, in the morning time, having dressed, took his bowl and robe and went to the residence of the brahmin Brahmāyu. Having approached, he sat down on the prepared seat together with the Bhikkhu Saṅgha. Then the brahmin Brahmāyu, for seven days, with his own hands served and satisfied the Bhikkhu Saṅgha headed by the Buddha with excellent hard and soft food. Then, at the passing of those seven days, the Blessed One departed on a wandering in the Videha country. Not long after the Blessed One had departed, the brahmin Brahmāyu passed away. Then a number of bhikkhus approached the Blessed One; having approached, they paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Sitting to one side, those bhikkhus said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, the brahmin Brahmāyu has passed away. What is his destination, what is his future course?” “Bhikkhus, the brahmin Brahmāyu was wise. He practiced the Dhamma in accordance with the Dhamma, and did not trouble me on account of the Dhamma. Bhikkhus, the brahmin Brahmāyu, through the destruction of the five lower fetters, is one of spontaneous birth; there he will attain final Nibbāna, not being of a nature to return from that world.”

Idamavoca [T 2.0547] bhagavā. Attamanā te bhikkhū bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandunti.

The Blessed One said this. Those bhikkhus, delighted, rejoiced at the Blessed One's words.

Brahmāyusuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ paṭhamaṃ.

The Brahmāyu Sutta, the first, is concluded.

2. Selasuttaṃ

2. The Sela Sutta

396. Evaṃ [V 2.0355] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā aṅguttarāpesu cārikaṃ caramāno mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ aḍḍhateḷasehi bhikkhusatehi yena āpaṇaṃ nāma aṅguttarāpānaṃ nigamo tadavasari. Assosi kho keṇiyo jaṭilo – “samaṇo khalu, bho, gotamo sakyaputto sakyakulā pabbajito aṅguttarāpesu cārikaṃ caramāno mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ aḍḍhateḷasehi bhikkhusatehi āpaṇaṃ anuppatto. Taṃ kho pana bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ evaṃ kalyāṇo kittisaddo abbhuggato – ‘itipi so bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho vijjācaraṇasampanno sugato lokavidū anuttaro purisadammasārathi satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavāti. So imaṃ lokaṃ sadevakaṃ samārakaṃ sabrahmakaṃ sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiṃ pajaṃ sadevamanussaṃ sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā pavedeti. So dhammaṃ deseti ādikalyāṇaṃ majjhekalyāṇaṃ pariyosānakalyāṇaṃ sātthaṃ sabyañjanaṃ, kevalaparipuṇṇaṃ parisuddhaṃ brahmacariyaṃ pakāseti. Sādhu kho pana tathārūpānaṃ arahataṃ dassanaṃ hotī’”ti.

396. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was traveling through the Aṅguttarāpa country with a large Saṅgha of bhikkhus, numbering twelve hundred and fifty, when he arrived at Āpaṇa, a market town of the Aṅguttarāpas. The matted-hair ascetic Keṇiya heard: “Indeed, good sirs, the ascetic Gotama, the son of the Sakyans, who went forth from the Sakyan clan, is traveling through the Aṅguttarāpa country with a large Saṅgha of bhikkhus, numbering twelve hundred and fifty, and has arrived at Āpaṇa. And regarding that venerable Gotama, such a glorious report has spread: ‘Indeed, that Blessed One is an Arahant, a Perfectly Self-Enlightened One, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, the Well-Gone, knower of the world, unsurpassed leader of persons to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, the Enlightened One, the Blessed One.’ He makes known this world with its devas, Māras, and Brahmās, this generation with its ascetics and brahmins, its devas and humans, having realized it himself with direct knowledge. He teaches the Dhamma that is good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, with meaning and phrasing, and proclaims the holy life that is entirely complete and pure. It is indeed good to see such Arahants.”

Atha kho keṇiyo jaṭilo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā [M 2.0348] ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho keṇiyaṃ jaṭilaṃ bhagavā dhammiyā kathāya sandassesi samādapesi samuttejesi sampahaṃsesi[T 2.0549]. Atha kho keṇiyo jaṭilo bhagavatā dhammiyā kathāya sandassito samādapito samuttejito sampahaṃsito bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “adhivāsetu me bhavaṃ gotamo svātanāya bhattaṃ saddhiṃ bhikkhusaṅghenā”ti. Evaṃ vutte, bhagavā keṇiyaṃ jaṭilaṃ etadavoca – “mahā kho, keṇiya, bhikkhusaṅgho aḍḍhateḷasāni bhikkhusatāni, tvañca brāhmaṇesu abhippasanno”ti. Dutiyampi kho keṇiyo jaṭilo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “kiñcāpi kho, bho gotama, mahā bhikkhusaṅgho aḍḍhateḷasāni bhikkhusatāni, ahañca brāhmaṇesu abhippasanno; adhivāsetu me bhavaṃ gotamo svātanāya bhattaṃ saddhiṃ bhikkhusaṅghenā”ti. Dutiyampi kho bhagavā keṇiyaṃ jaṭilaṃ etadavoca – “mahā kho, keṇiya, bhikkhusaṅgho aḍḍhateḷasāni bhikkhusatāni, tvañca brāhmaṇesu abhippasanno”ti. Tatiyampi kho keṇiyo jaṭilo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “kiñcāpi kho, bho gotama, mahā bhikkhusaṅgho aḍḍhateḷasāni bhikkhusatāni, ahañca brāhmaṇesu abhippasanno; adhivāsetu me bhavaṃ gotamo svātanāya bhattaṃ saddhiṃ bhikkhusaṅghenā”ti[V 2.0356]. Adhivāsesi bhagavā tuṇhībhāvena. Atha kho keṇiyo jaṭilo bhagavato adhivāsanaṃ viditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā yena sako assamo tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā mittāmacce ñātisālohite āmantesi – “suṇantu me bhonto, mittāmaccā ñātisālohitā; samaṇo me gotamo nimantito svātanāya bhattaṃ saddhiṃ bhikkhusaṅghena. Yena me kāyaveyyāvaṭikaṃ kāyaveyāvaṭṭikaṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ.), kāyaveyyāvatikaṃ (ka.) kareyyāthā”ti. “Evaṃ, bho”ti kho [T 2.0550] keṇiyassa jaṭilassa mittāmaccā ñātisālohitā keṇiyassa jaṭilassa paṭissutvā appekacce uddhanāni khaṇanti, appekacce kaṭṭhāni phālenti, appekacce bhājanāni dhovanti, appekacce udakamaṇikaṃ patiṭṭhāpenti, appekacce āsanāni paññapenti. Keṇiyo pana jaṭilo sāmaṃyeva maṇḍalamālaṃ paṭiyādeti.

Then the matted-hair ascetic Keṇiya approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he exchanged greetings with the Blessed One. When this courteous and memorable talk was concluded, he sat down to one side. As he was sitting to one side, the Blessed One instructed, established, roused, and gladdened the matted-hair ascetic Keṇiya with a Dhamma talk. Then the matted-hair ascetic Keṇiya, having been instructed, established, roused, and gladdened by the Blessed One with a Dhamma talk, said to the Blessed One: “May the venerable Gotama consent to accept a meal from me tomorrow together with the Saṅgha of bhikkhus.” When this was said, the Blessed One said to the matted-hair ascetic Keṇiya: “The Saṅgha of bhikkhus is large, Keṇiya, numbering twelve hundred and fifty bhikkhus, and you are greatly devoted to the brahmins.” A second time the matted-hair ascetic Keṇiya said to the Blessed One: “Even though, venerable Gotama, the Saṅgha of bhikkhus is large, numbering twelve hundred and fifty bhikkhus, and I am greatly devoted to the brahmins; may the venerable Gotama consent to accept a meal from me tomorrow together with the Saṅgha of bhikkhus.” A second time the Blessed One said to the matted-hair ascetic Keṇiya: “The Saṅgha of bhikkhus is large, Keṇiya, numbering twelve hundred and fifty bhikkhus, and you are greatly devoted to the brahmins.” A third time the matted-hair ascetic Keṇiya said to the Blessed One: “Even though, venerable Gotama, the Saṅgha of bhikkhus is large, numbering twelve hundred and fifty bhikkhus, and I am greatly devoted to the brahmins; may the venerable Gotama consent to accept a meal from me tomorrow together with the Saṅgha of bhikkhus.” The Blessed One consented by silence. Then the matted-hair ascetic Keṇiya, understanding the Blessed One's consent, rose from his seat and went to his own hermitage. Having gone there, he addressed his friends, companions, relatives, and kin: “Listen to me, venerable sirs, friends, companions, relatives, and kin; the ascetic Gotama has been invited by me for a meal tomorrow together with the Saṅgha of bhikkhus. Therefore, you should perform the physical services for me.” “Yes, venerable sir,” replied Keṇiya's friends, companions, relatives, and kin to the matted-hair ascetic Keṇiya, and some dug ovens, some split wood, some washed vessels, some set up a large water jar, and some prepared seats. Keṇiya the matted-hair ascetic himself prepared a circular pavilion.

397. Tena kho pana samayena selo brāhmaṇo āpaṇe paṭivasati tiṇṇaṃ vedānaṃ pāragū sanighaṇḍukeṭubhānaṃ sākkharappabhedānaṃ itihāsapañcamānaṃ[M 2.0349], padako, veyyākaraṇo, lokāyatamahāpurisalakkhaṇesu anavayo, tīṇi ca māṇavakasatāni mante vāceti. Tena kho pana samayena keṇiyo jaṭilo sele brāhmaṇe abhippasanno hoti. Atha kho selo brāhmaṇo tīhi māṇavakasatehi parivuto jaṅghāvihāraṃ anucaṅkamamāno anuvicaramāno yena keṇiyassa jaṭilassa assamo tenupasaṅkami. Addasā kho selo brāhmaṇo keṇiyassa jaṭilassa assame appekacce uddhanāni khaṇante, appekacce kaṭṭhāni phālente, appekacce bhājanāni dhovante, appekacce udakamaṇikaṃ patiṭṭhāpente, appekacce āsanāni paññapente, keṇiyaṃ pana jaṭilaṃ sāmaṃyeva maṇḍalamālaṃ paṭiyādentaṃ. Disvāna keṇiyaṃ jaṭilaṃ etadavoca – “kiṃ nu bhoto keṇiyassa āvāho vā bhavissati vivāho vā bhavissati mahāyañño vā paccupaṭṭhito, rājā vā māgadho seniyo bimbisāro nimantito svātanāya saddhiṃ balakāyenā”ti? “Na me, bho sela, āvāho [T 2.0551] bhavissati napi vivāho bhavissati napi rājā māgadho seniyo bimbisāro nimantito svātanāya saddhiṃ balakāyena; api ca kho me mahāyañño paccupaṭṭhito. Atthi, bho, samaṇo gotamo sakyaputto sakyakulā pabbajito aṅguttarāpesu cārikaṃ caramāno mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ aḍḍhateḷasehi bhikkhusatehi āpaṇaṃ anuppatto. Taṃ kho pana bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ evaṃ kalyāṇo kittisaddo abbhuggato – ‘itipi so bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho vijjācaraṇasampanno sugato lokavidū anuttaro purisadammasārathi satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavā’ti. So me nimantito svātanāya bhattaṃ saddhiṃ bhikkhusaṅghenā”ti.

397. Now at that time, the brahmin Sela was dwelling in Āpaṇa. He was a master of the three Vedas, along with the Nighaṇḍu, the Ketubha, and the Akkharappabheda, with the Itihāsa as the fifth. He was a reciter of the verses, an expert in grammar, and was completely skilled in the Lokāyata treatise and the marks of a great man. He taught the Vedas to three hundred young students. Now at that time, the matted-hair ascetic Keṇiya was exceedingly devoted to the brahmin Sela. Then the brahmin Sela, surrounded by three hundred young students, while walking back and forth and wandering about for exercise, approached the hermitage of the matted-hair ascetic Keṇiya. In the hermitage of the matted-hair ascetic Keṇiya, the brahmin Sela saw some digging ovens, some splitting firewood, some washing vessels, some setting up water pots, and some preparing seats, while he saw the matted-hair ascetic Keṇiya himself preparing the circular pavilion. Having seen him, he said this to the matted-hair ascetic Keṇiya: “What is the matter, Master Keṇiya? Will there be a wedding where a bride is taken, or a wedding where a bride is given? Or is a great sacrifice being prepared? Or has the King of Magadha, Seniya Bimbisāra, been invited for tomorrow along with his retinue?” “There will be no wedding for me where a bride is taken, Master Sela, nor one where a bride is given, nor has the King of Magadha, Seniya Bimbisāra, been invited for tomorrow along with his retinue. But indeed, a great sacrifice has been prepared by me. There is, sir, the ascetic Gotama, a son of the Sakyans, who has gone forth from the Sakyan clan. He is wandering in the country of the Aṅguttarāpas with a great Saṅgha of bhikkhus, with twelve hundred and fifty bhikkhus, and has arrived at Āpaṇa. Regarding that Master Gotama, this good report of his fame has spread: ‘That Blessed One is an Arahant, a Perfectly Self-Enlightened One, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, the Fortunate One, the Knower of the World, the Unsurpassed Leader of persons to be tamed, the Teacher of gods and humans, the Enlightened One, the Blessed One.’ He has been invited by me for tomorrow’s meal, together with the Saṅgha of bhikkhus.”

“Buddhoti [V 2.0357] – bho keṇiya, vadesi”?

“Do you say, ‘Buddha,’ Master Keṇiya?”

“Buddhoti – bho sela, vadāmi”.

“I do say, ‘Buddha,’ Master Sela.”

“Buddhoti – bho keṇiya, vadesi”?

“Do you say, ‘Buddha,’ Master Keṇiya?”

“Buddhoti – bho sela, vadāmī”ti.

“I do say, ‘Buddha,’ Master Sela.”

398. Atha kho selassa brāhmaṇassa etadahosi – “ghosopi kho eso dullabho lokasmiṃ – yadidaṃ ‘buddho’ti yadidaṃ buddho buddhoti (ka.). Āgatāni kho panamhākaṃ mantesu dvattiṃsamahāpurisalakkhaṇāni, yehi samannāgatassa mahāpurisassa [M 2.0350] dveyeva gatiyo bhavanti anaññā. Sace agāraṃ ajjhāvasati, rājā hoti cakkavattī dhammiko dhammarājā cāturanto vijitāvī janapadatthāvariyappatto sattaratanasamannāgato. Tassimāni satta ratanāni bhavanti, seyyathidaṃ – cakkaratanaṃ, hatthiratanaṃ, assaratanaṃ, maṇiratanaṃ, itthiratanaṃ, gahapatiratanaṃ, pariṇāyakaratanameva sattamaṃ. Parosahassaṃ kho panassa puttā bhavanti sūrā vīraṅgarūpā parasenappamaddanā. So [T 2.0552] imaṃ pathaviṃ sāgarapariyantaṃ adaṇḍena asatthena dhammena abhivijiya ajjhāvasati. Sace pana agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajati, arahaṃ hoti sammāsambuddho loke vivaṭṭacchado”.

398. Then this thought occurred to the brahmin Sela: “Indeed, this sound is rare in the world—that is, the word ‘Buddha.’ Moreover, in our Vedas, the thirty-two marks of a great man have been handed down, and for a great man endowed with these, there are only two destinies, and no other. If he dwells in the household life, he becomes a king, a wheel-turning monarch, a righteous one, a king of righteousness, ruler of the four quarters, a conqueror, one who has attained stability in his country, and endowed with the seven treasures. These are his seven treasures: the wheel-treasure, the elephant-treasure, the horse-treasure, the jewel-treasure, the woman-treasure, the householder-treasure, and the heir-apparent-treasure as the seventh. Furthermore, he has over a thousand sons who are valiant, heroic in form, and crushers of the armies of others. Having conquered this earth, bounded by the ocean, he dwells ruling it by righteousness, without rod and without weapon. But if he goes forth from the household life into homelessness, he becomes an Arahant, a Perfectly Enlightened One in the world, one who has drawn back the veil.”

“Kahaṃ pana, bho keṇiya, etarahi so bhavaṃ gotamo viharati arahaṃ sammāsambuddho”ti? Evaṃ vutte, keṇiyo jaṭilo dakkhiṇaṃ bāhuṃ paggahetvā selaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ etadavoca – “yenesā, bho sela, nīlavanarājī”ti. Atha kho selo brāhmaṇo tīhi māṇavakasatehi saddhiṃ yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami. Atha kho selo brāhmaṇo te māṇavake āmantesi – “appasaddā bhonto āgacchantu pade padaṃ pāde pādaṃ (sī.) nikkhipantā; durāsadā dūrasaddā (ka.) hi te bhagavanto sīhāva ekacarā. Yadā cāhaṃ, bho, samaṇena gotamena saddhiṃ manteyyaṃ, mā me bhonto antarantarā kathaṃ opātetha. Kathāpariyosānaṃ me bhavanto āgamentū”ti. Atha kho selo brāhmaṇo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho selo brāhmaṇo bhagavato kāye dvattiṃsamahāpurisalakkhaṇāni samannesi.

“But where, Master Keṇiya, is that Master Gotama, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, now dwelling?” When this was said, the matted-hair ascetic Keṇiya, raising his right arm, said this to the brahmin Sela: “Over there, Master Sela, where that line of dark-green forest is.” Then the brahmin Sela, together with three hundred young students, approached the Blessed One. Then the brahmin Sela addressed those young students: “Sirs, come without making a sound, placing foot after foot. For those Blessed Ones are difficult to approach, like lions that wander alone. And when I, sirs, am conversing with the ascetic Gotama, do not interrupt my speech. You should wait for the conclusion of my talk.” Then the brahmin Sela approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he exchanged courteous greetings with the Blessed One. When this courteous and amiable talk was concluded, he sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the brahmin Sela searched for the thirty-two marks of a great man on the Blessed One’s body.

Addasā kho selo brāhmaṇo bhagavato kāye dvattiṃsamahāpurisalakkhaṇāni, yebhuyyena ṭhapetvā dve. Dvīsu mahāpurisalakkhaṇesu kaṅkhati vicikicchati nādhimuccati na sampasīdati – kosohite [V 2.0358] ca vatthaguyhe, pahūtajivhatāya ca. Atha [T 2.0553] kho bhagavato etadahosi – “passati kho me ayaṃ selo brāhmaṇo dvattiṃsamahāpurisalakkhaṇāni, yebhuyyena ṭhapetvā dve. Dvīsu mahāpurisalakkhaṇesu kaṅkhati vicikicchati nādhimuccati na sampasīdati – kosohite [M 2.0351] ca vatthaguyhe, pahūtajivhatāya cā”ti. Atha kho bhagavā tathārūpaṃ iddhābhisaṅkhāraṃ abhisaṅkhāsi, yathā addasa selo brāhmaṇo bhagavato kosohitaṃ vatthaguyhaṃ. Atha kho bhagavā jivhaṃ ninnāmetvā ubhopi kaṇṇasotāni anumasi paṭimasi; ubhopi nāsikasotāni anumasi paṭimasi; kevalampi nalāṭamaṇḍalaṃ jivhāya chādesi. Atha kho selassa brāhmaṇassa etadahosi – “samannāgato kho samaṇo gotamo dvattiṃsamahāpurisalakkhaṇehi paripuṇṇehi, no aparipuṇṇehi; no ca kho naṃ jānāmi buddho vā no vā. Sutaṃ kho pana metaṃ brāhmaṇānaṃ vuddhānaṃ mahallakānaṃ ācariyapācariyānaṃ bhāsamānānaṃ – ‘ye te bhavanti arahanto sammāsambuddhā te sake vaṇṇe bhaññamāne attānaṃ pātukarontī’ti. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ samaṇaṃ gotamaṃ sammukhā sāruppāhi gāthāhi abhitthaveyya”nti.

The brahmin Sela saw on the Blessed One's body the thirty-two marks of a great man for the most part, except for two. Regarding two of the marks of a great man, he was doubtful, perplexed, unconvinced, and unsatisfied: that of the male organ enclosed in a sheath, and that of the great breadth of the tongue. Then this thought occurred to the Blessed One: 'This brahmin Sela sees on me the thirty-two marks of a great man for the most part, except for two. Regarding two of the marks of a great man, he is doubtful, perplexed, unconvinced, and unsatisfied: that of the male organ enclosed in a sheath, and that of the great breadth of the tongue.' Then the Blessed One performed such a feat of psychic power that the brahmin Sela saw the Blessed One's male organ enclosed in a sheath. Then the Blessed One, extending his tongue, stroked and touched both ear-holes, stroked and touched both nostrils, and covered the entire orb of his forehead with his tongue. Then this thought occurred to the brahmin Sela: 'The ascetic Gotama is endowed with the thirty-two marks of a great man, complete and not incomplete. Yet I do not know whether he is a Buddha or not. But I have heard this from aged, venerable brahmins, teachers and their teachers, who said: "Those who are Arahants, Perfectly Enlightened Ones, reveal themselves when their own praise is spoken." What if I were to praise the ascetic Gotama in his presence with suitable verses?'

399. Atha kho selo brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṃ sammukhā sāruppāhi gāthāhi abhitthavi –

399. Then the brahmin Sela praised the Blessed One in his presence with suitable verses:

“Paripuṇṇakāyo suruci, sujāto cārudassano;

Suvaṇṇavaṇṇosi bhagavā, susukkadāṭhosi vīriyavā viriyavā (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.).

“You have a perfect body, are of fine radiance, well-born, and pleasing to see; you are of golden complexion, O Blessed One, you have brilliant white canine teeth and are full of energy.

“Narassa hi sujātassa, ye bhavanti viyañjanā;

Sabbe te tava kāyasmiṃ, mahāpurisalakkhaṇā.

“Whatever marks there are for a well-born man, all those marks of a great man are present on your body.

“Pasannanetto [T 2.0554] sumukho, brahā brahmā (syā. kaṃ. ka.) uju patāpavā;

Majjhe samaṇasaṅghassa, ādiccova virocasi.

“With serene eyes and a beautiful face, you are majestic, upright, and radiant; in the midst of the assembly of ascetics, you shine like the sun.

“Kalyāṇadassano bhikkhu, kañcanasannibhattaco;

Kiṃ te samaṇabhāvena, evaṃ uttamavaṇṇino.

“O monk, beautiful to see, with skin like gold; for one of such supreme complexion as you, what is the purpose of the ascetic life?

“Rājā arahasi bhavituṃ, cakkavattī rathesabho;

Cāturanto vijitāvī, jambusaṇḍassa jambumaṇḍassa (ka.) issaro.

“You are worthy to be a king, a wheel-turning monarch, a bull among charioteers; a conqueror of the four quarters, the lord of the continent of Jambu.

“Khattiyā [V 2.0359] bhogirājāno, anuyantā anuyuttā (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) bhavantu te;

Rājābhirājā manujindo, rajjaṃ kārehi gotama”.

“May Khattiya kings, possessors of wealth, become your followers. O king of kings, lord of men, exercise your sovereignty, Gotama.”

“Rājāhamasmi [M 2.0352] selāti, dhammarājā anuttaro;

Dhammena cakkaṃ vattemi, cakkaṃ appaṭivattiyaṃ”.

“I am a king, Sela,” said the Blessed One, “an unsurpassed King of Dhamma. By Dhamma I turn the wheel, a wheel that cannot be turned back.”

“Sambuddho paṭijānāsi, dhammarājā anuttaro;

‘Dhammena cakkaṃ vattemi’, iti bhāsasi gotama.

“You claim to be a Perfectly Enlightened One, an unsurpassed King of Dhamma. ‘By Dhamma I turn the wheel,’ so you say, Gotama.

“Ko nu senāpati bhoto, sāvako satthuranvayo;

Ko te tamanuvatteti, dhammacakkaṃ pavattitaṃ”.

“Who is your general, the disciple who follows the Teacher? Who keeps turning this Wheel of Dhamma that has been set in motion by you?”

“Mayā pavattitaṃ cakkaṃ, (selāti bhagavā dhammacakkaṃ anuttaraṃ;

Sāriputto anuvatteti, anujāto tathāgataṃ.

“The wheel set in motion by me,” said the Blessed One, “Sela, the unsurpassed Wheel of Dhamma, is kept turning by Sāriputta, who follows the Tathāgata.

“Abhiññeyyaṃ abhiññātaṃ, bhāvetabbañca bhāvitaṃ;

Pahātabbaṃ pahīnaṃ me, tasmā buddhosmi brāhmaṇa.

“What should be directly known has been directly known by me; what should be developed has been developed; what should be abandoned has been abandoned. Therefore, brahmin, I am a Buddha.

“Vinayassu mayi kaṅkhaṃ, adhimuccassu brāhmaṇa;

Dullabhaṃ dassanaṃ hoti, sambuddhānaṃ abhiṇhaso.

“Dispel your doubt in me; be convinced, brahmin. The frequent sight of Perfectly Enlightened Ones is difficult to obtain.

“Yesaṃ [T 2.0555] ve dullabho loke, pātubhāvo abhiṇhaso;

Sohaṃ brāhmaṇa sambuddho, sallakatto anuttaro.

“Of those whose frequent appearance in the world is difficult to obtain—I, brahmin, am one such Perfectly Enlightened One, the unsurpassed remover of the dart.

“Brahmabhūto atitulo, mārasenappamaddano;

Sabbāmitte vasī katvā, modāmi akutobhayo”.

“Become supreme, incomparable, the crusher of Māra’s army; having brought all enemies under my control, I rejoice, fearless from any quarter.”

“Imaṃ bhonto nisāmetha, yathā bhāsati cakkhumā;

Sallakatto mahāvīro, sīhova nadatī vane.

“Sirs, listen to this, to how the One with the Eye speaks. The remover of the dart, the great hero, roars like a lion in the forest.

“Brahmabhūtaṃ [V 2.0360] atitulaṃ, mārasenappamaddanaṃ;

Ko disvā nappasīdeyya, api kaṇhābhijātiko.

“Having seen him—become supreme, incomparable, the crusher of Māra’s army—who would not be inspired with faith, even one of dark birth?

“Yo maṃ icchati anvetu, yo vā nicchati gacchatu;

Idhāhaṃ pabbajissāmi, varapaññassa santike”.

“Whoever wishes may follow me; whoever does not wish may go. Here I shall go forth in the presence of the one of excellent wisdom.”

“Etañce evañce (syā. kaṃ.) ruccati bhoto, sammāsambuddhasāsanaṃ sammāsambuddhasāsane (katthaci suttanipāte);

Mayampi pabbajissāma, varapaññassa santike”.

“Sir, if this teaching of the Perfectly Enlightened One pleases you, we too shall go forth in the presence of the one of excellent wisdom.”

“Brāhmaṇā tisatā ime, yācanti pañjalīkatā;

Brahmacariyaṃ carissāma, bhagavā tava santike”.

“These three hundred brahmins, with hands raised in reverence, ask: ‘We shall live the holy life in your presence, O Blessed One.’”

“Svākkhātaṃ [M 2.0353] brahmacariyaṃ, (selāti bhagavā sandiṭṭhikamakālikaṃ;

Yattha amoghā pabbajjā, appamattassa sikkhato”ti.

“The holy life is well-expounded,” said the Blessed One, “Sela, visible here and now, immediate, wherein the going forth is not in vain for one who trains diligently.”

Alattha kho selo brāhmaṇo sapariso bhagavato santike pabbajjaṃ, alattha upasampadaṃ.

The brahmin Sela, together with his assembly, obtained the going forth and the higher ordination in the presence of the Blessed One.

400. Atha kho keṇiyo jaṭilo tassā rattiyā accayena sake assame paṇītaṃ khādanīyaṃ bhojanīyaṃ paṭiyādāpetvā bhagavato kālaṃ [T 2.0556] ārocāpesi – “kālo, bho gotama, niṭṭhitaṃ bhatta”nti. Atha kho bhagavā pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya yena keṇiyassa jaṭilassa assamo tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi saddhiṃ bhikkhusaṅghena. Atha kho keṇiyo jaṭilo buddhappamukhaṃ bhikkhusaṅghaṃ paṇītena khādanīyena bhojanīyena sahatthā santappesi, sampavāresi. Atha kho keṇiyo jaṭilo bhagavantaṃ bhuttāviṃ onītapattapāṇiṃ aññataraṃ nīcaṃ āsanaṃ gahetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho keṇiyaṃ jaṭilaṃ bhagavā imāhi gāthāhi anumodi –

400. Then, when that night had passed, the matted-hair ascetic Keṇiya had excellent hard and soft food prepared in his own hermitage and had the time announced to the Blessed One: “It is time, Master Gotama, the meal is ready.” Then the Blessed One, having dressed in the morning, took his bowl and robe and went to the hermitage of the matted-hair ascetic Keṇiya. Having arrived, he sat down on the prepared seat together with the Saṅgha of monks. Then the matted-hair ascetic Keṇiya, with his own hands, served and satisfied the Saṅgha of monks headed by the Buddha with excellent hard and soft food. When the Blessed One had finished his meal and had removed his hand from the bowl, the matted-hair ascetic Keṇiya took a lower seat and sat to one side. To Keṇiya, seated to one side, the Blessed One expressed his appreciation with these verses:

“Aggihuttamukhā yaññā, sāvittī chandaso mukhaṃ;

Rājā mukhaṃ manussānaṃ, nadīnaṃ sāgaro mukhaṃ.

“The fire-oblation is the chief of sacrifices; the Sāvittī is the chief of meters. A king is the chief of humans, and the ocean is the chief of rivers.

“Nakkhattānaṃ [V 2.0361] mukhaṃ cando, ādicco tapataṃ mukhaṃ;

Puññaṃ ākaṅkhamānānaṃ, saṅgho ve yajataṃ mukha”nti.

“The moon is the chief among constellations; the sun is the chief among those that shine; for those desiring merit who make offerings, the Saṅgha is indeed the chief.”

Atha kho bhagavā keṇiyaṃ jaṭilaṃ imāhi gāthāhi anumoditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkāmi.

Then the Blessed One, having expressed his appreciation to Keṇiya the matted-hair ascetic with these verses, rose from his seat and departed.

Atha kho āyasmā selo sapariso eko vūpakaṭṭho appamatto ātāpī pahitatto viharanto nacirasseva – yassatthāya kulaputtā sammadeva agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajanti tadanuttaraṃ – brahmacariyapariyosānaṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja vihāsi. ‘Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti abbhaññāsi. Aññataro kho panāyasmā selo [T 2.0557] sapariso arahataṃ ahosi. Atha kho āyasmā selo sapariso yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā ekaṃsaṃ cīvaraṃ katvā yena bhagavā tenañjaliṃ paṇāmetvā bhagavantaṃ gāthāhi ajjhabhāsi –

Then the Venerable Sela, together with his retinue, dwelling alone, withdrawn, heedful, ardent, and resolute, not long after—in this very life, for himself, with direct knowledge—realized, attained, and dwelt in that unsurpassed culmination of the holy life for which clansmen rightly go forth from the household life into homelessness. He knew: ‘Birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is no more of this state of being.’ And the Venerable Sela, together with his retinue, became one of the Arahants. Then the Venerable Sela, together with his retinue, approached the Blessed One; having approached, he arranged his robe over one shoulder, extended his joined palms toward the Blessed One, and addressed the Blessed One with verses:

“Yaṃ [M 2.0354] taṃ saraṇamāgamma, ito aṭṭhami cakkhumā;

Sattarattena anuttarena (ka.) bhagavā, dantamha tava sāsane.

“O One with Vision, it is the eighth day since we came to you for refuge. Within seven nights, O Blessed One, we have been tamed in your dispensation.

“Tuvaṃ buddho tuvaṃ satthā, tuvaṃ mārābhibhū muni;

Tuvaṃ anusaye chetvā, tiṇṇo tāresimaṃ pajaṃ.

“You are the Buddha, you are the Teacher, you are the Muni who has overcome Māra. You, having cut off the underlying tendencies, have crossed over and you ferry this multitude of beings across.

“Upadhī te samatikkantā, āsavā te padālitā;

Sīhova anupādāno, pahīnabhayabheravo.

“You have completely overcome attachments; your taints have been shattered. Like a lion, without clinging, you have abandoned fear and dread.

“Bhikkhavo tisatā ime, tiṭṭhanti pañjalīkatā;

Pāde vīra pasārehi, nāgā vandantu satthuno”ti.

“These three hundred monks stand with their palms joined in reverence. O Hero, extend your feet; let the great beings venerate the Teacher.”

Selasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ dutiyaṃ.

The Sela Sutta, the second, is concluded.

3. Assalāyanasuttaṃ

3. The Assalāyana Sutta

401. Evaṃ [T 2.0558][V 2.0362][P 2.0147] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena nānāverajjakānaṃ brāhmaṇānaṃ pañcamattāni brāhmaṇasatāni sāvatthiyaṃ paṭivasanti kenacideva karaṇīyena. Atha kho tesaṃ brāhmaṇānaṃ etadahosi – “ayaṃ kho samaṇo gotamo cātuvaṇṇiṃ suddhiṃ paññapeti. Ko nu kho pahoti samaṇena gotamena saddhiṃ asmiṃ vacane paṭimantetu”nti? Tena kho pana samayena assalāyano nāma māṇavo sāvatthiyaṃ paṭivasati daharo, vuttasiro, soḷasavassuddesiko jātiyā, tiṇṇaṃ vedānaṃ pāragū sanighaṇḍukeṭubhānaṃ sākkharappabhedānaṃ itihāsapañcamānaṃ, padako, veyyākaraṇo, lokāyatamahāpurisalakkhaṇesu anavayo. Atha kho tesaṃ brāhmaṇānaṃ etadahosi – “ayaṃ kho assalāyano māṇavo sāvatthiyaṃ paṭivasati daharo, vuttasiro, soḷasavassuddesiko jātiyā, tiṇṇaṃ vedānaṃ pāragū…pe… anavayo. So kho pahoti samaṇena gotamena saddhiṃ asmiṃ vacane paṭimantetu”nti.

401. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling in Sāvatthī, at Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. At that time, about five hundred brahmins from various countries were residing in Sāvatthī for some purpose. Then this thought occurred to those brahmins: “This ascetic Gotama proclaims the purity of the four castes. Who, I wonder, is able to debate with the ascetic Gotama regarding this statement?” Now at that time, a young man named Assalāyana was residing in Sāvatthī. He was young, with his hair freshly cut, sixteen years of age by birth, a master of the three Vedas with their glossaries and ritual manuals, phonology and etymology, and history as the fifth. He was a master of philology and grammar, and was fully skilled in cosmology and the science of the marks of a great man. Then this thought occurred to those brahmins: “This young man Assalāyana resides in Sāvatthī. He is young... fully skilled. He is able to debate with the ascetic Gotama regarding this statement.”

Atha kho te brāhmaṇā yena assalāyano māṇavo tenupaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā assalāyanaṃ māṇavaṃ etadavocuṃ – “ayaṃ, bho assalāyana[M 2.0355], samaṇo gotamo cātuvaṇṇiṃ suddhiṃ paññapeti. Etu bhavaṃ assalāyano samaṇena gotamena saddhiṃ asmiṃ vacane paṭimantetū”ti paṭimantetunti (pī. ka.).

Then those brahmins approached the young man Assalāyana; having approached, they said this to the young man Assalāyana: “Venerable Assalāyana, this ascetic Gotama proclaims the purity of the four castes. Let the venerable Assalāyana come and debate with the ascetic Gotama regarding this statement.”

Evaṃ vutte, assalāyano māṇavo te brāhmaṇe etadavoca [T 2.0559] – “samaṇo khalu, bho, gotamo dhammavādī; dhammavādino ca pana duppaṭimantiyā bhavanti. Nāhaṃ sakkomi samaṇena gotamena saddhiṃ asmiṃ vacane paṭimantetu”nti. Dutiyampi kho te brāhmaṇā assalāyanaṃ māṇavaṃ etadavocuṃ – “ayaṃ, bho assalāyana, samaṇo gotamo cātuvaṇṇiṃ suddhiṃ paññapeti. Etu bhavaṃ assalāyano samaṇena gotamena [P 2.0148] saddhiṃ asmiṃ vacane paṭimantetu paṭimantetuṃ (sī. pī. ka.). Caritaṃ kho pana bhotā assalāyanena paribbājaka”nti. Dutiyampi kho assalāyano māṇavo te brāhmaṇe etadavoca – “samaṇo khalu, bho, gotamo dhammavādī; dhammavādino ca pana duppaṭimantiyā bhavanti[V 2.0363]. Nāhaṃ sakkomi samaṇena gotamena saddhiṃ asmiṃ vacane paṭimantetu”nti. Tatiyampi kho te brāhmaṇā assalāyanaṃ māṇavaṃ etadavocuṃ – “ayaṃ, bho assalāyana, samaṇo gotamo cātuvaṇṇiṃ suddhiṃ paññapeti. Etu bhavaṃ assalāyano samaṇena gotamena saddhiṃ asmiṃ vacane paṭimantetu paṭimantetuṃ (sī. pī. ka.). Caritaṃ kho pana bhotā assalāyanena paribbājakaṃ. Mā bhavaṃ assalāyano ayuddhaparājitaṃ parājayī”ti.

When this was said, the young man Assalāyana said this to those brahmins: “Sirs, the ascetic Gotama is indeed a speaker of truth, and speakers of truth are difficult to debate. I am not able to debate with the ascetic Gotama regarding this statement.” For a second time, those brahmins said this to the young man Assalāyana: “Venerable Assalāyana, this ascetic Gotama proclaims the purity of the four castes. Let the venerable Assalāyana come and debate with the ascetic Gotama regarding this statement. For the venerable Assalāyana has practiced the way of the wanderers.” For a second time, the young man Assalāyana said this to those brahmins: “Sirs, the ascetic Gotama is indeed a speaker of truth, and speakers of truth are difficult to debate. I am not able to debate with the ascetic Gotama regarding this statement.” For a third time, those brahmins said this to the young man Assalāyana: “Venerable Assalāyana, this ascetic Gotama proclaims the purity of the four castes. Let the venerable Assalāyana come and debate with the ascetic Gotama regarding this statement. For the venerable Assalāyana has practiced the way of the wanderers. Let the venerable Assalāyana not be defeated without a fight!”

Evaṃ vutte, assalāyano māṇavo te brāhmaṇe etadavoca – “addhā kho ahaṃ bhavanto na labhāmi. Samaṇo khalu, bho, gotamo dhammavādī; dhammavādino ca pana duppaṭimantiyā bhavanti. Nāhaṃ sakkomi samaṇena gotamena saddhiṃ asmiṃ vacane paṭimantetunti. Api cāhaṃ bhavantānaṃ vacanena gamissāmī”ti.

When this was said, the young man Assalāyana said this to those brahmins: “Indeed, sirs, I cannot persuade you. The ascetic Gotama is indeed a speaker of truth, and speakers of truth are difficult to debate. I am not able to debate with the ascetic Gotama regarding this statement. Nevertheless, I will go on your word.”

402. Atha kho assalāyano māṇavo mahatā brāhmaṇagaṇena saddhiṃ [T 2.0560] yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho assalāyano māṇavo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “brāhmaṇā, bho gotama, evamāhaṃsu – ‘brāhmaṇova seṭṭho vaṇṇo, hīno añño vaṇṇo; brāhmaṇova sukko vaṇṇo, kaṇho añño vaṇṇo; brāhmaṇova sujjhanti, no abrāhmaṇā; brāhmaṇāva brahmuno puttā [M 2.0356] orasā mukhato jātā brahmajā brahmanimmitā brahmadāyādā’ti. Idha bhavaṃ gotamo kimāhā”ti? “Dissanti dissante (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) kho pana, assalāyana, brāhmaṇānaṃ brāhmaṇiyo utuniyopi gabbhiniyopi vijāyamānāpi pāyamānāpi. Te ca brāhmaṇiyonijāva samānā evamāhaṃsu – ‘brāhmaṇova seṭṭho vaṇṇo, hīno añño vaṇṇo; brāhmaṇova sukko vaṇṇo, kaṇho añño vaṇṇo; brāhmaṇāva sujjhanti, no abrāhmaṇā; brāhmaṇāva brahmuno puttā orasā mukhato jātā brahmajā brahmanimmitā brahmadāyādā’”ti. “Kiñcāpi [P 2.0149] bhavaṃ gotamo evamāha, atha khvettha brāhmaṇā evametaṃ maññanti – ‘brāhmaṇova seṭṭho vaṇṇo, hīno añño vaṇṇo…pe… brahmadāyādā’”ti.
