Just as, Venerable Udena, one might set upright what has been overturned, or reveal what is hidden, or show the path to one who is lost, or hold up an oil lamp in the darkness so that those with eyes may see forms—in the very same way has the Dhamma been made clear in many ways by the Venerable Udena. I go for refuge to the Venerable Udena, to the Dhamma, and to the Saṅgha of bhikkhus. May the Venerable Udena remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge from this day forward, for as long as life lasts.' 'Do not go for refuge to me, brahmin. Go for refuge to that same Blessed One to whom I have gone for refuge.' 'But where, Venerable Udena, does that Venerable Gotama, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, now dwell?' 'That Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, has now attained Parinibbāna, brahmin.'

“Sacepi sace hi (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) mayaṃ, bho udena, suṇeyyāma taṃ bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ dasasu yojanesu, dasapi mayaṃ yojanāni gaccheyyāma [T 2.0589] taṃ bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ dassanāya [M 2.0375] arahantaṃ sammāsambuddhaṃ. Sacepi sace (sī. pī.), sace hi (syā. kaṃ.) mayaṃ, bho udena, suṇeyyāma taṃ bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ vīsatiyā yojanesu… tiṃsāya yojanesu… cattārīsāya yojanesu… paññāsāya yojanesu, paññāsampi mayaṃ yojanāni gaccheyyāma taṃ bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ dassanāya arahantaṃ sammāsambuddhaṃ. Yojanasate cepi yojanasatepi (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) mayaṃ[P 2.0163], bho udena, suṇeyyāma taṃ bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ, yojanasatampi mayaṃ gaccheyyāma taṃ bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ dassanāya arahantaṃ sammāsambuddhaṃ.

Venerable Udena, if we were to hear that the Venerable Gotama was ten yojanas away, we would travel those ten yojanas to see that Venerable Gotama, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One. Venerable Udena, if we were to hear that the Venerable Gotama was twenty yojanas away… thirty yojanas away… forty yojanas away… fifty yojanas away, we would travel those fifty yojanas to see that Venerable Gotama, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One. And Venerable Udena, if we were to hear that the Venerable Gotama was a hundred yojanas away, we would travel even a hundred yojanas to see that Venerable Gotama, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One.

“Yato ca kho, bho udena, parinibbuto so bhavaṃ gotamo, parinibbutampi mayaṃ taṃ bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāma dhammañca bhikkhusaṅghañca. Upāsakaṃ maṃ bhavaṃ udeno dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṃ saraṇaṃ gataṃ. Atthi ca me, bho udena, aṅgarājā devasikaṃ niccabhikkhaṃ dadāti[V 2.0382], tato ahaṃ bhoto udenassa ekaṃ niccabhikkhaṃ dadāmī”ti. “Kiṃ pana te, brāhmaṇa, aṅgarājā devasikaṃ niccabhikkhaṃ dadātī”ti? “Pañca, bho udena, kahāpaṇasatānī”ti. “Na kho no, brāhmaṇa, kappati jātarūparajataṃ paṭiggahetu”nti. “Sace taṃ bhoto udenassa na kappati vihāraṃ bhoto udenassa kārāpessāmī”ti. “Sace kho me tvaṃ, brāhmaṇa, vihāraṃ, kārāpetukāmo, pāṭaliputte saṅghassa upaṭṭhānasālaṃ kārāpehī”ti. “Imināpāhaṃ bhoto udenassa bhiyyosomattāya attamano abhiraddho yaṃ maṃ bhavaṃ udeno saṅghe dāne samādapeti. Esāhaṃ, bho udena, etissā ca niccabhikkhāya aparāya ca niccabhikkhāya pāṭaliputte saṅghassa upaṭṭhānasālaṃ kārāpessāmī”ti. Atha [T 2.0590] kho ghoṭamukho brāhmaṇo etissā ca niccabhikkhāya aparāya ca niccabhikkhāya pāṭaliputte saṅghassa upaṭṭhānasālaṃ kārāpesi. Sā etarahi ‘ghoṭamukhī’ti vuccatīti.

“Since, Venerable Udena, the Master Gotama has attained final Nibbāna, we go for refuge to that Master Gotama who has attained final Nibbāna, and to the Dhamma, and to the Bhikkhu Saṅgha. May the Venerable Udena remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge from this day forward for as long as life lasts. Moreover, Venerable Udena, the king of Aṅga gives me a daily regular provision; from that, I will give one regular provision to the Venerable Udena.” “But, brahmin, what daily regular provision does the king of Aṅga give you?” “Five hundred kahāpaṇas, Venerable Udena.” “It is not allowable for us, brahmin, to accept gold and silver.” “If that is not allowable for the Venerable Udena, I will have a monastery built for the Venerable Udena.” “If you wish to have a monastery built for me, brahmin, then have an assembly hall built for the Saṅgha in Pāṭaliputta.” “By this I am even more pleased and delighted with the Venerable Udena, that the Venerable Udena encourages me in giving to the Saṅgha. I, Venerable Udena, with this regular provision and with another regular provision, will have an assembly hall built for the Saṅgha in Pāṭaliputta.” Then the brahmin Ghoṭamukha, with that regular provision and with another regular provision, had an assembly hall built for the Saṅgha in Pāṭaliputta. It is now called ‘Ghoṭamukhī’.”

Ghoṭamukhasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ catutthaṃ.

The Ghoṭamukha Sutta, the fourth, is concluded.

5. Caṅkīsuttaṃ

5. The Caṅkī Sutta

422. Evaṃ [T 2.0591][V 2.0383][P 2.0164] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā kosalesu cārikaṃ caramāno mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ yena opāsādaṃ nāma kosalānaṃ [M 2.0376] brāhmaṇagāmo tadavasari. Tatra sudaṃ bhagavā opāsāde viharati uttarena opāsādaṃ devavane sālavane. Tena kho pana samayena caṅkī brāhmaṇo opāsādaṃ ajjhāvasati sattussadaṃ satiṇakaṭṭhodakaṃ sadhaññaṃ rājabhoggaṃ raññā pasenadinā kosalena dinnaṃ rājadāyaṃ brahmadeyyaṃ. Assosuṃ kho opāsādakā brāhmaṇagahapatikā – “samaṇo khalu, bho, gotamo sakyaputto sakyakulā pabbajito kosalesu cārikaṃ caramāno mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ opāsādaṃ anuppatto, opāsāde viharati uttarena opāsādaṃ devavane sālavane. Taṃ kho pana bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ evaṃ kalyāṇo kittisaddo abbhuggato – ‘itipi so bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho vijjācaraṇasampanno sugato lokavidū anuttaro purisadammasārathi satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavā’ti. So imaṃ lokaṃ sadevakaṃ samārakaṃ sabrahmakaṃ sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiṃ pajaṃ sadevamanussaṃ sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā pavedeti. So dhammaṃ deseti ādikalyāṇaṃ majjhekalyāṇaṃ pariyosānakalyāṇaṃ sātthaṃ [T 2.0592] sabyañjanaṃ, kevalaparipuṇṇaṃ parisuddhaṃ brahmacariyaṃ pakāseti. Sādhu kho pana tathārūpānaṃ arahataṃ dassanaṃ hotī”ti.

422. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was wandering on tour in the Kosala country with a large Saṅgha of bhikkhus and arrived at Opāsāda, a brahmin village of the Kosalans. There the Blessed One stayed in the Devavana Sāla Grove to the north of Opāsāda. At that time, the brahmin Caṅkī was living in Opāsāda, a populous place, with plentiful grass, wood, and water, with abundant grain, a royal fief granted by King Pasenadi of Kosala, a royal grant, a gift of excellence. The brahmin householders of Opāsāda heard: “The ascetic Gotama, it seems, a son of the Sakyans who went forth from the Sakyan clan, while wandering on tour in the Kosala country with a large Saṅgha of bhikkhus, has arrived at Opāsāda and is staying in the Devavana Sāla Grove to the north of Opāsāda. A fine report of that Master Gotama has spread in this way: ‘That Blessed One is an Arahant, a Perfectly Enlightened One, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, the Fortunate One, knower of the world, supreme trainer of persons to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, the Buddha, the Blessed One.’ He, having realized it for himself through direct knowledge, makes known this world with its devas, its Māras, and its Brahmās, this generation with its ascetics and brahmins, its devas and humans. He teaches the Dhamma that is good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, with its meaning and phrasing; he reveals a spiritual life that is entirely complete and pure. It is indeed good to see such Arahants.”

423. Atha kho opāsādakā brāhmaṇagahapatikā opāsādā nikkhamitvā saṅghasaṅghī gaṇībhūtā uttarenamukhā gacchanti yena devavanaṃ sālavanaṃ. Tena kho pana samayena caṅkī brāhmaṇo uparipāsāde divāseyyaṃ upagato. Addasā kho caṅkī brāhmaṇo opāsādake brāhmaṇagahapatike opāsādā nikkhamitvā saṅghasaṅghī gaṇībhūte uttarena mukhaṃ yena devavanaṃ sālavanaṃ tenupasaṅkamante. Disvā khattaṃ āmantesi – “kiṃ nu kho, bho khatte, opāsādakā brāhmaṇagahapatikā opāsādā nikkhamitvā saṅghasaṅghī gaṇībhūtā uttarenamukhā gacchanti yena devavanaṃ sālavana”nti? “Atthi, bho caṅkī, samaṇo gotamo sakyaputto sakyakulā pabbajito kosalesu cārikaṃ caramāno mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ opāsādaṃ anuppatto, opāsāde [V 2.0384] viharati uttarena opāsādaṃ devavane sālavane. Taṃ kho pana bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ evaṃ kalyāṇo kittisaddo abbhuggato – ‘itipi so bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho vijjācaraṇasampanno sugato lokavidū anuttaro purisadammasārathi satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavā’ti. Tamete bhavantaṃ [M 2.0377] gotamaṃ dassanāya gacchantī”ti. “Tena hi, bho khatte, yena opāsādakā brāhmaṇagahapatikā tenupasaṅkama; upasaṅkamitvā opāsādake [T 2.0593] brāhmaṇagahapatike evaṃ vadehi – ‘caṅkī, bho, brāhmaṇo evamāha – āgamentu kira bhonto, caṅkīpi brāhmaṇo samaṇaṃ gotamaṃ dassanāya upasaṅkamissatī’”ti. “Evaṃ, bho”ti kho so khatto caṅkissa brāhmaṇassa paṭissutvā [P 2.0165] yena opāsādakā brāhmaṇagahapatikā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā opāsādake brāhmaṇagahapatike etadavoca – “caṅkī, bho, brāhmaṇo evamāha – ‘āgamentu kira bhonto, caṅkīpi brāhmaṇo samaṇaṃ gotamaṃ dassanāya upasaṅkamissatī’”ti.

423. Then the brahmin householders of Opāsāda, having left Opāsāda, formed into groups and crowds and went, facing north, toward the Devavana Sāla Grove. At that time, the brahmin Caṅkī had gone up to the upper terrace of his palace for his midday rest. The brahmin Caṅkī saw the brahmin householders of Opāsāda leaving Opāsāda, formed into groups and crowds, approaching the Devavana Sāla Grove, facing north. Seeing them, he addressed his attendant: “Why, good attendant, are the brahmin householders of Opāsāda leaving Opāsāda, formed into groups and crowds, and going, facing north, toward the Devavana Sāla Grove?” “Sir Caṅkī, there is the ascetic Gotama, a son of the Sakyans who went forth from the Sakyan clan. While wandering on tour in the Kosala country with a large Saṅgha of bhikkhus, he has arrived at Opāsāda and is staying in the Devavana Sāla Grove to the north of Opāsāda. A fine report of that Master Gotama has spread in this way: ‘That Blessed One is an Arahant, a Perfectly Enlightened One, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, the Fortunate One, knower of the world, supreme trainer of persons to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, the Buddha, the Blessed One.’ They are going to see that Master Gotama.” “In that case, good attendant, go to the brahmin householders of Opāsāda and, having approached them, speak to them thus: ‘The brahmin Caṅkī, sirs, says this: “May the venerable ones please wait. The brahmin Caṅkī will also come to see the ascetic Gotama.”’” “Yes, sir,” the attendant replied to the brahmin Caṅkī. He went to the brahmin householders of Opāsāda and, having approached them, said this: “The brahmin Caṅkī, sirs, says this: ‘May the venerable ones please wait. The brahmin Caṅkī will also come to see the ascetic Gotama.’”

424. Tena kho pana samayena nānāverajjakānaṃ brāhmaṇānaṃ pañcamattāni brāhmaṇasatāni opāsāde paṭivasanti kenacideva karaṇīyena. Assosuṃ kho te brāhmaṇā – “caṅkī kira brāhmaṇo samaṇaṃ gotamaṃ dassanāya upasaṅkamissatī”ti. Atha kho te brāhmaṇā yena caṅkī brāhmaṇo tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā caṅkiṃ brāhmaṇaṃ etadavocuṃ – “saccaṃ kira bhavaṃ caṅkī samaṇaṃ gotamaṃ dassanāya upasaṅkamissatī”ti? “Evaṃ kho me, bho, hoti – ‘ahaṃ samaṇaṃ gotamaṃ dassanāya upasaṅkamissāmī’”ti. “Mā bhavaṃ caṅkī samaṇaṃ gotamaṃ dassanāya upasaṅkami. Na arahati bhavaṃ caṅkī samaṇaṃ gotamaṃ dassanāya upasaṅkamituṃ; samaṇotveva gotamo arahati bhavantaṃ caṅkiṃ dassanāya upasaṅkamituṃ. Bhavañhi caṅkī ubhato sujāto mātito ca pitito ca saṃsuddhagahaṇiko yāva sattamā pitāmahayugā akkhitto anupakkuṭṭho jātivādena. Yampi bhavaṃ caṅkī ubhato sujāto mātito ca pitito ca saṃsuddhagahaṇiko yāva sattamā pitāmahayugā akkhitto anupakkuṭṭho [T 2.0594] jātivādena, imināpaṅgena na arahati bhavaṃ caṅkī samaṇaṃ gotamaṃ dassanāya upasaṅkamituṃ; samaṇotveva gotamo arahati bhavantaṃ caṅkiṃ dassanāya upasaṅkamituṃ. Bhavañhi caṅkī aḍḍho mahaddhano mahābhogo…pe… bhavañhi caṅkī tiṇṇaṃ vedānaṃ pāragū sanighaṇḍukeṭubhānaṃ sākkharappabhedānaṃ itihāsapañcamānaṃ, padako, veyyākaraṇo, lokāyatamahāpurisalakkhaṇesu anavayo…pe… bhavañhi caṅkī abhirūpo dassanīyo pāsādiko paramāya vaṇṇapokkharatāya samannāgato [M 2.0378] brahmavaṇṇī brahmavacchasī brahmavaccasī (sī. pī.) akhuddāvakāso [V 2.0385] dassanāya…pe… bhavañhi caṅkī sīlavā vuddhasīlī vuddhasīlena samannāgato…pe… bhavañhi caṅkī kalyāṇavāco kalyāṇavākkaraṇo [P 2.0166] poriyā vācāya samannāgato vissaṭṭhāya anelagalāya atthassa viññāpaniyā…pe… bhavañhi caṅkī bahūnaṃ ācariyapācariyo, tīṇi māṇavakasatāni mante vāceti…pe… bhavañhi caṅkī rañño pasenadissa kosalassa sakkato garukato mānito pūjito apacito…pe… bhavañhi caṅkī brāhmaṇassa pokkharasātissa sakkato garukato mānito pūjito apacito…pe… bhavañhi caṅkī opāsādaṃ ajjhāvasati sattussadaṃ satiṇakaṭṭhodakaṃ sadhaññaṃ rājabhoggaṃ raññā pasenadinā kosalena dinnaṃ rājadāyaṃ brahmadeyyaṃ. Yampi bhavaṃ caṅkī opāsādaṃ ajjhāvasati sattussadaṃ satiṇakaṭṭhodakaṃ [T 2.0595] sadhaññaṃ rājabhoggaṃ raññā pasenadinā kosalena dinnaṃ rājadāyaṃ brahmadeyyaṃ, imināpaṅgena na arahati bhavaṃ caṅkī samaṇaṃ gotamaṃ dassanāya upasaṅkamituṃ; samaṇotveva gotamo arahati bhavantaṃ caṅkiṃ dassanāya upasaṅkamitu”nti.

424. Now at that time, five hundred brahmins from various kingdoms were residing at Opāsāda on some business. They heard: “It is said that the brahmin Caṅkī will visit the ascetic Gotama.” Then those brahmins approached the brahmin Caṅkī and said to him: “Is it true, venerable Caṅkī, that you will visit the ascetic Gotama?” “Indeed, sirs, it is my intention to visit the ascetic Gotama.” “Venerable Caṅkī, do not visit the ascetic Gotama. It is not fitting for venerable Caṅkī to visit the ascetic Gotama; rather, the ascetic Gotama should visit venerable Caṅkī. For venerable Caṅkī is well-born on both sides, from mother and father, of pure maternal lineage back for seven generations of ancestors, unassailed and unreproached regarding birth. In that venerable Caṅkī is well-born on both sides, from mother and father, of pure maternal lineage back for seven generations of ancestors, unassailed and unreproached regarding birth, for this reason, too, it is not fitting for venerable Caṅkī to visit the ascetic Gotama; rather, the ascetic Gotama should visit venerable Caṅkī. For venerable Caṅkī is rich, with great wealth and abundant possessions... For venerable Caṅkī is a master of the three Vedas, along with their glossaries, ritual treatises, phonology, and etymology, with the histories as the fifth; he is versed in the word-lore and grammar, and flawless in cosmology and the marks of a Great Man... For venerable Caṅkī is handsome, attractive, graceful, possessing supreme beauty of complexion, of Brahma-like complexion and Brahma-like presence, not insignificant to behold... For venerable Caṅkī is virtuous, of mature virtue, endowed with this mature virtue... For venerable Caṅkī has good speech and a fine delivery, endowed with a refined voice that is clear, fluent, and makes the meaning known... For venerable Caṅkī is a teacher and master teacher to many, instructing three hundred young brahmins in the hymns... For venerable Caṅkī is honored, respected, revered, venerated, and esteemed by King Pasenadi of Kosala... For venerable Caṅkī is honored, respected, revered, venerated, and esteemed by the brahmin Pokkharasāti... For venerable Caṅkī dwells in Opāsāda, teeming with life, with grass, wood, and water, abundant grain, a royal possession given by King Pasenadi of Kosala, a royal gift, a magnificent gift. In that venerable Caṅkī dwells in Opāsāda, teeming with life, with grass, wood, and water, abundant grain, a royal possession given by King Pasenadi of Kosala, a royal gift, a magnificent gift, for this reason, too, it is not fitting for venerable Caṅkī to visit the ascetic Gotama; rather, the ascetic Gotama should visit venerable Caṅkī.”

425. Evaṃ vutte, caṅkī brāhmaṇo te brāhmaṇe etadavoca – “tena hi, bho, mamapi suṇātha, yathā mayameva arahāma taṃ samaṇaṃ gotamaṃ dassanāya upasaṅkamituṃ; natveva arahati so bhavaṃ gotamo amhākaṃ dassanāya upasaṅkamituṃ. Samaṇo khalu, bho, gotamo ubhato sujāto mātito ca pitito ca saṃsuddhagahaṇiko yāva sattamā pitāmahayugā akkhitto anupakkuṭṭho jātivādena. Yampi, bho, samaṇo gotamo ubhato sujāto mātito ca pitito ca saṃsuddhagahaṇiko yāva sattamā pitāmahayugā akkhitto anupakkuṭṭho jātivādena, imināpaṅgena na arahati so bhavaṃ gotamo amhākaṃ dassanāya upasaṅkamituṃ; atha kho mayameva arahāma taṃ bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ dassanāya upasaṅkamituṃ ettha dī. ni. 1.304 aññampi guṇapadaṃ dissati. Samaṇo khalu, bho, gotamo pahūtaṃ hiraññasuvaṇṇaṃ ohāya pabbajito bhūmigatañca vehāsaṭṭhañca…pe… samaṇo khalu, bho, gotamo daharova samāno yuvā susukāḷakeso bhadrena yobbanena samannāgato paṭhamena vayasā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajito…pe… samaṇo khalu, bho, gotamo akāmakānaṃ [M 2.0379] mātāpitūnaṃ assumukhānaṃ rudantānaṃ kesamassuṃ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajito…pe… samaṇo khalu, bho, gotamo abhirūpo dassanīyo pāsādiko paramāya vaṇṇapokkharatāya [T 2.0596] samannāgato brahmavaṇṇī [P 2.0167] brahmavacchasī akhuddāvakāso dassanāya…pe… samaṇo khalu, bho, gotamo sīlavā ariyasīlī kusalasīlī kusalena sīlena [V 2.0386] samannāgato…pe… samaṇo khalu, bho, gotamo kalyāṇavāco kalyāṇavākkaraṇo poriyā vācāya samannāgato vissaṭṭhāya anelagalāya atthassa viññāpaniyā…pe… samaṇo khalu, bho, gotamo bahūnaṃ ācariyapācariyo…pe… samaṇo khalu, bho, gotamo khīṇakāmarāgo vigatacāpallo…pe… samaṇo khalu, bho, gotamo kammavādī kiriyavādī apāpapurekkhāro brahmaññāya pajāya…pe… samaṇo khalu, bho, gotamo uccā kulā pabbajito asambhinnā khattiyakulā…pe… samaṇo khalu, bho, gotamo aḍḍhā kulā pabbajito mahaddhanā mahābhogā…pe… samaṇaṃ khalu, bho, gotamaṃ tiroraṭṭhā tirojanapadā saṃpucchituṃ āgacchanti…pe… samaṇaṃ khalu, bho, gotamaṃ anekāni devatāsahassāni pāṇehi saraṇaṃ gatāni…pe… samaṇaṃ khalu, bho, gotamaṃ evaṃ kalyāṇo kittisaddo abbhuggato – ‘itipi so bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho vijjācaraṇasampanno sugato lokavidū anuttaro purisadammasārathi satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavā’ti…pe… samaṇo khalu, bho, gotamo dvattiṃsamahāpurisalakkhaṇehi samannāgato…pe… etthāpi dī. ni. 1.304 aññānipi guṇapadānaṃ dissanti samaṇaṃ khalu, bho, gotamaṃ rājā māgadho seniyo bimbisāro saputtadāro pāṇehi saraṇaṃ gato…pe… samaṇaṃ khalu, bho, gotamaṃ rājā pasenadi kosalo saputtadāro pāṇehi saraṇaṃ gato…pe… samaṇaṃ khalu, bho, gotamaṃ brāhmaṇo pokkharasāti saputtadāro [T 2.0597] pāṇehi saraṇaṃ gato…pe… samaṇo khalu, bho, gotamo opāsādaṃ anuppatto opāsāde viharati uttarena opāsādaṃ devavane sālavane. Ye kho te samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā amhākaṃ gāmakkhettaṃ āgacchanti, atithī no te honti. Atithī kho panamhehi sakkātabbā garukātabbā mānetabbā pūjetabbā. Yampi samaṇo gotamo opāsādaṃ anuppatto [M 2.0380] opāsāde viharati uttarena opāsādaṃ devavane sālavane, atithimhākaṃ samaṇo gotamo. Atithi kho panamhehi sakkātabbo garukātabbo mānetabbo pūjetabbo. Imināpaṅgena [P 2.0168] na arahati so bhavaṃ gotamo amhākaṃ dassanāya upasaṅkamituṃ; atha kho mayameva arahāma taṃ bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ dassanāya upasaṅkamituṃ. Ettake kho ahaṃ, bho, tassa bhoto gotamassa vaṇṇe pariyāpuṇāmi, no ca kho so bhavaṃ gotamo ettakavaṇṇo; aparimāṇavaṇṇo hi so bhavaṃ gotamo. Ekamekenapi tena ekamekenapi bho (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) aṅgena samannāgato na arahati, so, bhavaṃ gotamo amhākaṃ dassanāya upasaṅkamituṃ; atha kho mayameva arahāma taṃ bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ dassanāya upasaṅkamitunti. Tena hi, bho, sabbeva mayaṃ samaṇaṃ gotamaṃ dassanāya upasaṅkamissāmā”ti.

425. When this was said, the brahmin Caṅkī addressed those brahmins: 'Well then, sirs, listen to me as to why we should be the ones to go and see the ascetic Gotama, and why he would not be the one to come and see us. For, sirs, the ascetic Gotama is well-born on both sides, of pure descent through the maternal and paternal line back to the seventh generation, unblemished and irreproachable in birth. Since the ascetic Gotama is well-born on both sides, of pure descent back to the seventh generation, unblemished and irreproachable in birth, for this reason he would not be the one to come and see us; rather, we should be the ones to go and see him. For, sirs, the ascetic Gotama has gone forth, having abandoned much gold and silver, both buried and above ground… For, sirs, the ascetic Gotama went forth while still young, a black-haired young man endowed with the blessing of youth, in the first stage of life… For, sirs, the ascetic Gotama shaved off his hair and beard, put on the ochre robes, and went forth from the household life into homelessness, though his unwilling parents wept with tearful faces… For, sirs, the ascetic Gotama is handsome, good-looking, inspiring confidence, endowed with supreme beauty of complexion, with a Brahma-like complexion, with a body like Brahma's, and his presence is of no small account to behold… For, sirs, the ascetic Gotama is virtuous, possessing noble virtue, wholesome virtue, endowed with wholesome virtue… For, sirs, the ascetic Gotama is a good speaker, with a good delivery, possessing urbane speech that is distinct, not slurred, and makes the meaning clear… For, sirs, the ascetic Gotama is the teacher of many teachers… For, sirs, the ascetic Gotama is free from sensual lust, free from fickleness… For, sirs, the ascetic Gotama is a proponent of kamma, a proponent of action, and he promotes what is blameless for the brahminical folk… For, sirs, the ascetic Gotama went forth from a high family, from an unmixed khattiya clan… For, sirs, the ascetic Gotama went forth from a wealthy family, with abundant riches and resources… For, sirs, people come from other kingdoms and districts to question the ascetic Gotama… For, sirs, many thousands of deities have gone for refuge to the ascetic Gotama with their very lives… For, sirs, such a glorious report has spread about the ascetic Gotama: ‘Indeed, the Blessed One is an Arahant, a Perfectly Enlightened One, accomplished in true knowledge and conduct, the Well-Gone One, knower of the world, unsurpassed trainer of persons to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, the Enlightened One, the Blessed One.’… For, sirs, the ascetic Gotama is endowed with the thirty-two marks of a great man… For, sirs, King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha, along with his wife and children, has gone for refuge to the ascetic Gotama with his very life… For, sirs, King Pasenadi of Kosala, along with his wife and children, has gone for refuge to the ascetic Gotama with his very life… For, sirs, the brahmin Pokkharasāti, along with his wife and children, has gone for refuge to the ascetic Gotama with his very life… For, sirs, the ascetic Gotama has arrived at Opāsāda and is staying in the Sāla Grove of the Devas, north of Opāsāda. Whatever ascetics or brahmins come to our village territory are our guests. And guests should be honored, respected, revered, and venerated by us. Since the ascetic Gotama has arrived at Opāsāda and is staying there, he is our guest. And a guest should be honored, respected, revered, and venerated by us. For this reason too, the Venerable Gotama would not be the one to come and see us; rather, we should be the ones to go and see him. These, sirs, are the virtues I have learned about the Venerable Gotama, but the Venerable Gotama’s virtues are not limited to these. For the Venerable Gotama’s virtues are immeasurable. Even if he were endowed with just one of these qualities, he would not be the one to come and see us; rather, we should be the ones to go and see him.' Then they said: 'In that case, sir, let us all go to see the ascetic Gotama.'

426. Atha [V 2.0387] kho caṅkī brāhmaṇo mahatā brāhmaṇagaṇena saddhiṃ yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Tena kho pana samayena [T 2.0598] bhagavā vuddhehi vuddhehi brāhmaṇehi saddhiṃ kiñci kiñci kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā nisinno hoti. Tena kho pana samayena kāpaṭiko kāpaṭhiko (sī. pī.), kāpadiko (syā. kaṃ.) nāma māṇavo daharo vuttasiro soḷasavassuddesiko jātiyā, tiṇṇaṃ vedānaṃ pāragū sanighaṇḍukeṭubhānaṃ sākkharappabhedānaṃ itihāsapañcamānaṃ, padako, veyyākaraṇo, lokāyatamahāpurisalakkhaṇesu anavayo tassaṃ parisāyaṃ nisinno hoti. So vuddhānaṃ vuddhānaṃ brāhmaṇānaṃ bhagavatā saddhiṃ mantayamānānaṃ antarantarā kathaṃ opāteti. Atha kho bhagavā kāpaṭikaṃ māṇavaṃ apasādeti – “māyasmā bhāradvājo vuddhānaṃ vuddhānaṃ brāhmaṇānaṃ mantayamānānaṃ antarantarā kathaṃ opātetu. Kathāpariyosānaṃ āyasmā bhāradvājo āgametū”ti. Evaṃ vutte, caṅkī brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “mā bhavaṃ gotamo kāpaṭikaṃ māṇavaṃ apasādesi. Kulaputto ca kāpaṭiko māṇavo, bahussuto ca kāpaṭiko māṇavo, paṇḍito ca kāpaṭiko māṇavo, kalyāṇavākkaraṇo ca kāpaṭiko māṇavo, pahoti ca kāpaṭiko māṇavo bhotā gotamena saddhiṃ asmiṃ vacane paṭimantetu”nti. Atha kho bhagavato [M 2.0381] etadahosi – “addhā kho [P 2.0169] kāpaṭikassa etadahosi “kāpaṭikassa (ka.) māṇavassa tevijjake pāvacane kathā kathaṃ (sī. ka.), kathaṃ (syā. kaṃ. pī.) bhavissati. Tathā hi naṃ brāhmaṇā saṃpurekkharontī”ti. Atha kho kāpaṭikassa māṇavassa etadahosi [T 2.0599] – “yadā me samaṇo gotamo cakkhuṃ upasaṃharissati, athāhaṃ samaṇaṃ gotamaṃ pañhaṃ pucchissāmī”ti. Atha kho bhagavā kāpaṭikassa māṇavassa cetasā cetoparivitakkamaññāya yena kāpaṭiko māṇavo tena cakkhūni upasaṃhāsi.

426. Then the brahmin Caṅkī, together with a large company of brahmins, approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he exchanged greetings with the Blessed One. After exchanging pleasant and memorable conversation, he sat down to one side. At that time, the Blessed One was seated, having exchanged some memorable conversation with the elder brahmins. At that time, a young student named Kāpaṭika, sixteen years of age by birth, with a shaven head, was seated in that assembly. He was a master of the three Vedas with their glossaries, ritual treatises, phonology, and etymology, and the histories as a fifth. He was a master of the verses and a grammarian, and fully versed in natural philosophy and the marks of a great man. As the elder brahmins were conversing with the Blessed One, he kept interrupting their discussion. Then the Blessed One dismissed the student Kāpaṭika: “Venerable Bhāradvāja, do not interrupt the discussion of the elder brahmins. Let Venerable Bhāradvāja wait until the discussion has come to an end.” When this was said, the brahmin Caṅkī said to the Blessed One: “Let not the Venerable Gotama dismiss the student Kāpaṭika. The student Kāpaṭika is of good family, learned, wise, an eloquent speaker, and capable of engaging in discussion with the Venerable Gotama on this matter.” Then this thought occurred to the Blessed One: “Surely, the student Kāpaṭika’s discussion will concern the teaching of the three Vedas, for the brahmins hold him in such high esteem.” Then this thought occurred to the student Kāpaṭika: “When the ascetic Gotama directs his eyes toward me, then I will ask him a question.” Then the Blessed One, knowing with his mind the thought in the student Kāpaṭika’s mind, directed his eyes toward him.

427. Atha kho kāpaṭikassa māṇavassa etadahosi – “samannāharati kho maṃ samaṇo gotamo. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ samaṇaṃ gotamaṃ pañhaṃ puccheyya”nti. Atha kho kāpaṭiko māṇavo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “yadidaṃ, bho gotama, brāhmaṇānaṃ porāṇaṃ mantapadaṃ itihitihaparamparāya piṭakasampadāya, tattha ca brāhmaṇā ekaṃsena niṭṭhaṃ gacchanti – ‘idameva saccaṃ, moghamañña’nti. Idha bhavaṃ gotamo kimāhā”ti? “Kiṃ pana, bhāradvāja, atthi koci brāhmaṇānaṃ ekabrāhmaṇopi yo evamāha – ‘ahametaṃ jānāmi, ahametaṃ passāmi. Idameva saccaṃ, moghamañña’”nti? “No hidaṃ, bho gotama”. “Kiṃ pana, bhāradvāja, atthi koci brāhmaṇānaṃ ekācariyopi[V 2.0388], ekācariyapācariyopi, yāva sattamā ācariyamahayugāpi, yo evamāha – ‘ahametaṃ jānāmi, ahametaṃ passāmi. Idameva saccaṃ, moghamañña’”nti? “No hidaṃ, bho gotama”. “Kiṃ pana, bhāradvāja, yepi te brāhmaṇānaṃ pubbakā isayo mantānaṃ kattāro mantānaṃ pavattāro yesamidaṃ etarahi brāhmaṇā porāṇaṃ mantapadaṃ gītaṃ pavuttaṃ samihitaṃ tadanugāyanti tadanubhāsanti bhāsitamanubhāsanti vācitamanuvācenti seyyathidaṃ – aṭṭhako [T 2.0600] vāmako vāmadevo vessāmitto yamataggi aṅgīraso bhāradvājo vāseṭṭho kassapo bhagu, tepi evamāhaṃsu – ‘mayametaṃ jānāma, mayametaṃ passāma. Idameva saccaṃ, moghamañña’”nti? “No [P 2.0170] hidaṃ, bho gotama”.

427. Then the student Kāpaṭika thought: “The ascetic Gotama is paying attention to me. Surely I should ask the ascetic Gotama a question.” Then the student Kāpaṭika said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable Gotama, with regard to the brahmins’ ancient sacred verses, handed down through a continuous tradition and textual transmission, the brahmins arrive at the absolute conclusion: ‘This alone is true, anything else is worthless’—what does the Venerable Gotama say about this?” “What do you think, Bhāradvāja? Is there even a single brahmin who says: ‘I know this, I see this. This alone is true, anything else is worthless’?” “No, Venerable Gotama.” “What do you think, Bhāradvāja? Is there even a single teacher among the brahmins, or a teacher of teachers, up to the seventh generation of teachers, who says: ‘I know this, I see this. This alone is true, anything else is worthless’?” “No, Venerable Gotama.” “What do you think, Bhāradvāja? Those former seers of the brahmins, the composers of the sacred verses, the expounders of the sacred verses, whose ancient sacred verses the brahmins today sing, utter, and reiterate, repeating what was spoken, reciting what was recited—such as Aṭṭhaka, Vāmaka, Vāmadeva, Vessāmitta, Yamataggi, Aṅgīrasa, Bhāradvāja, Vāseṭṭha, Kassapa, and Bhagu—did even they say: ‘We know this, we see this. This alone is true, anything else is worthless’?” “No, Venerable Gotama.”

“Iti kira, bhāradvāja, natthi koci brāhmaṇānaṃ ekabrāhmaṇopi yo evamāha – ‘ahametaṃ jānāmi, ahametaṃ passāmi. Idameva saccaṃ, moghamañña’nti; natthi koci brāhmaṇānaṃ ekācariyopi ekācariyapācariyopi, yāva sattamā ācariyamahayugāpi, yo evamāha – ‘ahametaṃ [M 2.0382] jānāmi, ahametaṃ passāmi. Idameva saccaṃ, moghamañña’nti; yepi te brāhmaṇānaṃ pubbakā isayo mantānaṃ kattāro mantānaṃ pavattāro yesamidaṃ etarahi brāhmaṇā porāṇaṃ mantapadaṃ gītaṃ pavuttaṃ samihitaṃ tadanugāyanti tadanubhāsanti bhāsitamanubhāsanti vācitamanuvācenti seyyathidaṃ – aṭṭhako vāmako vāmadevo vessāmitto yamataggi aṅgīraso bhāradvājo vāseṭṭho kassapo bhagu, tepi na evamāhaṃsu – ‘mayametaṃ jānāma, mayametaṃ passāma. Idameva saccaṃ, moghamañña’nti.

“So it seems, Bhāradvāja, that there is not a single brahmin among the brahmins who says: ‘I know this, I see this. This alone is true, anything else is worthless.’ Nor is there a single teacher among the brahmins, nor a teacher of teachers, up to the seventh generation of teachers, who says: ‘I know this, I see this. This alone is true, anything else is worthless.’ And those former seers of the brahmins, the composers of the sacred verses, the expounders of the sacred verses, whose ancient sacred verses—sung, uttered, and compiled—the brahmins nowadays chant in turn, speak in turn, repeat what was spoken, and recite what was recited—namely, Aṭṭhaka, Vāmaka, Vāmadeva, Vessāmitta, Yamataggi, Aṅgīrasa, Bhāradvāja, Vāseṭṭha, Kassapa, and Bhagu—even they did not say: ‘We know this, we see this. This alone is true, anything else is worthless.’”

428. “Seyyathāpi, bhāradvāja, andhaveṇi paramparāsaṃsattā purimopi na passati majjhimopi na passati pacchimopi na passati; evameva kho, bhāradvāja, andhaveṇūpamaṃ maññe brāhmaṇānaṃ bhāsitaṃ sampajjati – purimopi na passati majjhimopi na passati pacchimopi na passati. Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, bhāradvāja[T 2.0601], nanu evaṃ sante brāhmaṇānaṃ amūlikā saddhā sampajjatī”ti? “Na khvettha, bho gotama, brāhmaṇā saddhāyeva payirupāsanti, anussavāpettha brāhmaṇā payirupāsantī”ti. “Pubbeva kho tvaṃ, bhāradvāja, saddhaṃ agamāsi, anussavaṃ idāni vadesi. Pañca kho ime, bhāradvāja, dhammā diṭṭheva dhamme dvedhā vipākā. Katame pañca? Saddhā, ruci, anussavo, ākāraparivitakko, diṭṭhinijjhānakkhanti – ime kho, bhāradvāja[V 2.0389], pañca dhammā diṭṭheva dhamme dvedhā vipākā. Api ca, bhāradvāja, susaddahitaṃyeva hoti, tañca hoti rittaṃ tucchaṃ musā; no cepi susaddahitaṃ hoti, tañca hoti bhūtaṃ tacchaṃ anaññathā. Api ca, bhāradvāja[P 2.0171], surucitaṃyeva hoti…pe… svānussutaṃyeva hoti…pe… suparivitakkitaṃyeva hoti…pe… sunijjhāyitaṃyeva hoti, tañca hoti rittaṃ tucchaṃ musā; no cepi sunijjhāyitaṃ hoti, tañca hoti bhūtaṃ tacchaṃ anaññathā. Saccamanurakkhatā, bhāradvāja, viññunā purisena nālamettha ekaṃsena niṭṭhaṃ gantuṃ – ‘idameva saccaṃ, moghamañña’”nti.

428. “Just as, Bhāradvāja, in a line of blind men linked one to another, the first one does not see, the middle one does not see, and the last one does not see; even so, Bhāradvāja, the statement of the brahmins seems to me to be like a line of blind men: the first one does not see, the middle one does not see, and the last one does not see. What do you think, Bhāradvāja? This being so, does not the faith of the brahmins prove to be baseless?” “Venerable Gotama, it is not only on faith that the brahmins rely in this matter; the brahmins also rely on oral tradition.” “First, Bhāradvāja, you resorted to faith, and now you speak of oral tradition. Bhāradvāja, there are these five things that have a twofold outcome in this very life. What five? Faith, inclination, oral tradition, reasoned consideration, and acceptance of a view upon reflection. These, Bhāradvāja, are the five things that have a twofold outcome in this very life. Furthermore, Bhāradvāja, something may be well-believed, yet it may be empty, hollow, and false; and something may not be well-believed, yet it may be real, true, and not otherwise. Furthermore, Bhāradvāja, something may be well-liked… it may be well-heard… it may be well-considered… it may be well-reflected upon, yet it may be empty, hollow, and false; and something may not be well-reflected upon, yet it may be real, true, and not otherwise. Bhāradvāja, a wise person who safeguards the truth is not able to come to the definite conclusion: ‘This alone is true, anything else is false.’”

429. “Kittāvatā pana, bho gotama, saccānurakkhaṇā hoti, kittāvatā saccamanurakkhati? Saccānurakkhaṇaṃ mayaṃ bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ pucchāmā”ti. “Saddhā cepi, bhāradvāja, purisassa hoti; ‘evaṃ me saddhā’ti – iti vadaṃ saccamanurakkhati evameva sijjhatīti iti vā, taṃ saccamanurakkhati (ka.), natveva tāva ekaṃsena niṭṭhaṃ gacchati [T 2.0602] – ‘idameva saccaṃ, moghamañña’nti [M 2.0383] ( ) (ettāvatā kho bhāradvāja saccānurakkhaṇā hoti, ettāvatā saccamanurakkhati, ettāvatā ca mayaṃ saccānurakkhaṇaṃ paññāpema, na tveva tāva saccānubodho hoti) (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.). Ruci cepi, bhāradvāja, purisassa hoti…pe… anussavo cepi, bhāradvāja, purisassa hoti…pe… ākāraparivitakko cepi, bhāradvāja, purisassa hoti…pe… diṭṭhinijjhānakkhanti cepi, bhāradvāja, purisassa hoti; ‘evaṃ me diṭṭhinijjhānakkhantī’ti – iti vadaṃ saccamanurakkhati, natveva tāva ekaṃsena niṭṭhaṃ gacchati – ‘idameva saccaṃ, moghamañña’nti. Ettāvatā kho, bhāradvāja, saccānurakkhaṇā hoti, ettāvatā saccamanurakkhati, ettāvatā ca mayaṃ saccānurakkhaṇaṃ paññapema; na tveva tāva saccānubodho hotī”ti.

429. “But to what extent, Venerable Gotama, is there safeguarding of truth? To what extent does one safeguard the truth? We ask the Venerable Gotama about the safeguarding of truth.” “If, Bhāradvāja, a person has faith, by saying, ‘Such is my faith,’ he safeguards the truth, but he does not yet arrive at the definite conclusion: ‘This alone is true, anything else is false.’ If, Bhāradvāja, a person has an inclination… if a person has an oral tradition… if a person has reasoned consideration… if, Bhāradvāja, a person has an acceptance of a view upon reflection, by saying, ‘Such is my acceptance of a view upon reflection,’ he safeguards the truth, but he does not yet arrive at the definite conclusion: ‘This alone is true, anything else is false.’ To this extent, Bhāradvāja, there is safeguarding of truth; to this extent one safeguards the truth; and to this extent we describe the safeguarding of truth. However, there is not yet the awakening to the truth.”

430. “Ettāvatā, bho gotama, saccānurakkhaṇā hoti, ettāvatā saccamanurakkhati, ettāvatā ca mayaṃ saccānurakkhaṇaṃ pekkhāma. Kittāvatā pana, bho gotama, saccānubodho hoti, kittāvatā saccamanubujjhati? Saccānubodhaṃ mayaṃ bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ pucchāmā”ti. “Idha idha kira (syā. kaṃ. ka.), bhāradvāja, bhikkhu aññataraṃ gāmaṃ vā nigamaṃ vā upanissāya viharati. Tamenaṃ gahapati vā gahapatiputto vā upasaṅkamitvā tīsu dhammesu samannesati – lobhanīyesu [P 2.0172] dhammesu, dosanīyesu dhammesu, mohanīyesu dhammesu. Atthi nu kho imassāyasmato tathārūpā lobhanīyā dhammā yathārūpehi lobhanīyehi dhammehi pariyādinnacitto [T 2.0603] ajānaṃ vā vadeyya – jānāmīti, apassaṃ vā vadeyya – passāmīti, paraṃ vā tadatthāya samādapeyya yaṃ paresaṃ assa dīgharattaṃ ahitāya [V 2.0390] dukkhāyāti? Tamenaṃ samannesamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘natthi kho imassāyasmato tathārūpā lobhanīyā dhammā yathārūpehi lobhanīyehi dhammehi pariyādinnacitto ajānaṃ vā vadeyya – jānāmīti, apassaṃ vā vadeyya – passāmīti, paraṃ vā tadatthāya samādapeyya yaṃ paresaṃ assa dīgharattaṃ ahitāya dukkhāya dukkhāyāti (sabbattha). Tathārūpo tathā (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) kho panimassāyasmato kāyasamācāro tathārūpo tathā (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) vacīsamācāro yathā taṃ aluddhassa. Yaṃ kho pana ayamāyasmā dhammaṃ deseti, gambhīro so dhammo duddaso duranubodho [M 2.0384] santo paṇīto atakkāvacaro nipuṇo paṇḍitavedanīyo; na so dhammo sudesiyo luddhenā’”ti.

430. “To this extent, Venerable Gotama, there is safeguarding of truth; to this extent one safeguards the truth; and to this extent we regard the safeguarding of truth. But to what extent, Venerable Gotama, is there an awakening to the truth? To what extent does one awaken to the truth? We ask the Venerable Gotama about the awakening to the truth.” “Here, Bhāradvāja, a bhikkhu dwells depending on a certain village or town. A householder or a householder’s son approaches him and investigates him in regard to three kinds of states: states connected with greed, states connected with hatred, and states connected with delusion. ‘Are there in this venerable one any such states connected with greed that, with his mind overcome by them, he might say, “I know,” when not knowing, or say, “I see,” when not seeing, or might he cause others to undertake that which would lead to their long-term harm and suffering?’ While investigating him, he comes to know: ‘There are in this venerable one no such states connected with greed that, with his mind overcome by them, he might say, “I know,” when not knowing, or say, “I see,” when not seeing, or might he cause others to undertake that which would lead to their long-term harm and suffering. Indeed, this venerable one’s bodily conduct and verbal conduct are like that of one who is without greed. And the Dhamma that this venerable one teaches is profound, difficult to see, difficult to understand, peaceful, sublime, beyond the scope of reasoning, subtle, and to be experienced by the wise; that Dhamma cannot be well taught by one who is greedy.’”

431. “Yato naṃ samannesamāno visuddhaṃ lobhanīyehi dhammehi samanupassati tato naṃ uttari samannesati dosanīyesu dhammesu. Atthi nu kho imassāyasmato tathārūpā dosanīyā dhammā yathārūpehi dosanīyehi dhammehi pariyādinnacitto ajānaṃ vā vadeyya – jānāmīti, apassaṃ vā vadeyya – passāmīti, paraṃ vā tadatthāya samādapeyya yaṃ paresaṃ assa dīgharattaṃ ahitāya dukkhāyāti? Tamenaṃ samannesamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘natthi kho imassāyasmato tathārūpā dosanīyā dhammā yathārūpehi dosanīyehi dhammehi pariyādinnacitto ajānaṃ vā vadeyya – jānāmīti, apassaṃ vā vadeyya – passāmīti, paraṃ vā tadatthāya samādapeyya [T 2.0604] yaṃ paresaṃ assa dīgharattaṃ ahitāya dukkhāya. Tathārūpo kho panimassāyasmato kāyasamācāro tathārūpo vacīsamācāro yathā taṃ aduṭṭhassa. Yaṃ kho pana ayamāyasmā dhammaṃ deseti, gambhīro so dhammo duddaso duranubodho santo paṇīto atakkāvacaro nipuṇo paṇḍitavedanīyo; na so dhammo sudesiyo duṭṭhenā’”ti.

431. “When, upon investigating him, one sees that he is purified of states of greed, then one further investigates him regarding states of aversion. ‘Are there in this venerable one such states of aversion that, with his mind overcome by them, he might say, “I know,” when he does not know, or say, “I see,” when he does not see, or might cause another to undertake that which would lead to their long-term harm and suffering?’ Investigating him thus, one comes to know: ‘There are no such states of aversion in this venerable one that, with his mind overcome by them, he would say, “I know,” when he does not know, or say, “I see,” when he does not see, or might cause another to undertake that which would lead to their long-term harm and suffering. Moreover, this venerable one’s bodily conduct and verbal conduct are such as that of one without aversion. And the Dhamma that this venerable one teaches is profound, difficult to see, difficult to understand, peaceful, sublime, beyond the scope of conjecture, subtle, to be experienced by the wise; that Dhamma is not easily taught by one with aversion.’”

432. “Yato naṃ samannesamāno visuddhaṃ dosanīyehi dhammehi samanupassati[P 2.0173], tato naṃ uttari samannesati mohanīyesu dhammesu. Atthi nu kho imassāyasmato tathārūpā mohanīyā dhammā yathārūpehi mohanīyehi dhammehi pariyādinnacitto ajānaṃ vā vadeyya – jānāmīti, apassaṃ vā vadeyya – passāmīti, paraṃ vā tadatthāya samādapeyya yaṃ paresaṃ assa dīgharattaṃ ahitāya dukkhāyāti? Tamenaṃ samannesamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘natthi kho imassāyasmato tathārūpā mohanīyā dhammā yathārūpehi mohanīyehi dhammehi pariyādinnacitto ajānaṃ vā vadeyya – jānāmīti, apassaṃ vā vadeyya – passāmīti, paraṃ vā tadatthāya samādapeyya yaṃ paresaṃ [V 2.0391] assa dīgharattaṃ ahitāya dukkhāya. Tathārūpo kho panimassāyasmato kāyasamācāro tathārūpo vacīsamācāro yathā taṃ amūḷhassa. Yaṃ kho pana ayamāyasmā dhammaṃ deseti, gambhīro so dhammo duddaso duranubodho santo paṇīto [M 2.0385] atakkāvacaro nipuṇo paṇḍitavedanīyo; na so dhammo sudesiyo mūḷhenā’”ti.

432. “When, upon investigating him, one sees that he is purified of states of aversion, then one further investigates him regarding states of delusion. ‘Are there in this venerable one such states of delusion that, with his mind overcome by them, he might say, “I know,” when he does not know, or say, “I see,” when he does not see, or might cause another to undertake that which would lead to their long-term harm and suffering?’ Investigating him thus, one comes to know: ‘There are no such states of delusion in this venerable one that, with his mind overcome by them, he would say, “I know,” when he does not know, or say, “I see,” when he does not see, or might cause another to undertake that which would lead to their long-term harm and suffering. Moreover, this venerable one’s bodily conduct and verbal conduct are such as that of one without delusion. And the Dhamma that this venerable one teaches is profound, difficult to see, difficult to understand, peaceful, sublime, beyond the scope of conjecture, subtle, to be experienced by the wise; that Dhamma is not easily taught by one with delusion.’”

“Yato naṃ samannesamāno visuddhaṃ mohanīyehi dhammehi samanupassati[T 2.0605]; atha tamhi saddhaṃ niveseti, saddhājāto upasaṅkamati, upasaṅkamanto payirupāsati, payirupāsanto sotaṃ odahati, ohitasoto dhammaṃ suṇāti, sutvā dhammaṃ dhāreti, dhatānaṃ dhāritānaṃ (ka.) dhammānaṃ atthaṃ upaparikkhati, atthaṃ upaparikkhato dhammā nijjhānaṃ khamanti, dhammanijjhānakkhantiyā sati chando jāyati, chandajāto ussahati, ussahitvā tuleti, tulayitvā padahati, pahitatto samāno kāyena ceva paramasaccaṃ sacchikaroti paññāya ca naṃ ativijjha passati. Ettāvatā kho, bhāradvāja, saccānubodho hoti, ettāvatā saccamanubujjhati, ettāvatā ca mayaṃ saccānubodhaṃ paññapema; na tveva tāva saccānuppatti hotī”ti.

“When, upon investigating him, one sees that he is purified of states of delusion, then one establishes faith in him. With faith born, one approaches him. Approaching, one attends upon him. Attending upon him, one lends ear. Lending ear, one hears the Dhamma. Having heard the Dhamma, one retains it. One examines the meaning of the teachings that have been retained. When one examines the meaning, the teachings are approved for contemplation. When the teachings are approved for contemplation, zeal is born. With zeal born, one strives. Having striven, one weighs. Having weighed, one exerts oneself. Being resolute, one realizes the supreme truth with the mental body and sees it, having penetrated it with wisdom. To this extent, Bhāradvāja, there is the awakening to the truth. To this extent, one awakens to the truth. And to this extent, we declare the awakening to the truth; but there is not yet the attainment of the truth.”

433. “Ettāvattā, bho gotama, saccānubodho hoti, ettāvatā saccamanubujjhati, ettāvatā ca mayaṃ saccānubodhaṃ pekkhāma. Kittāvatā pana, bho gotama, saccānuppatti hoti, kittāvatā saccamanupāpuṇāti? Saccānuppattiṃ mayaṃ bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ pucchāmā”ti. “Tesaṃye[P 2.0174], bhāradvāja, dhammānaṃ āsevanā bhāvanā bahulīkammaṃ saccānuppatti hoti. Ettāvatā kho, bhāradvāja, saccānuppatti hoti, ettāvatā saccamanupāpuṇāti, ettāvatā ca mayaṃ saccānuppattiṃ paññapemā”ti.

433. “To this extent, Master Gotama, there is the awakening to the truth; to this extent, one awakens to the truth; and to this extent, we too regard it as the awakening to the truth. But to what extent, Master Gotama, is there the attainment of the truth? To what extent does one attain the truth? We ask the venerable Gotama about the attainment of the truth.” “Bhāradvāja, it is through the cultivation, development, and frequent practice of these very same dhammas that there is the attainment of the truth. To this extent, Bhāradvāja, there is the attainment of the truth; to this extent, one attains the truth; and to this extent, we declare the attainment of the truth.”

434. “Ettāvatā, bho gotama, saccānuppatti hoti, ettāvatā saccamanupāpuṇāti, ettāvatā ca mayaṃ saccānuppattiṃ pekkhāma. Saccānuppattiyā pana, bho gotama, katamo dhammo bahukāro? Saccānuppattiyā bahukāraṃ dhammaṃ mayaṃ bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ pucchāmā”ti. “Saccānuppattiyā [T 2.0606] kho, bhāradvāja, padhānaṃ bahukāraṃ. No cetaṃ padaheyya, nayidaṃ saccamanupāpuṇeyya. Yasmā ca kho padahati tasmā saccamanupāpuṇāti. Tasmā saccānuppattiyā padhānaṃ bahukāra”nti.

434. “To this extent, Master Gotama, there is the attainment of the truth; to this extent, one attains the truth; and to this extent, we too regard it as the attainment of the truth. But, Master Gotama, which dhamma is of great help for the attainment of the truth? We ask the venerable Gotama about the dhamma that is of great help for the attainment of the truth.” “For the attainment of the truth, Bhāradvāja, exertion is of great help. If one did not exert oneself, one would not attain this truth. And because one does exert oneself, one therefore attains the truth. Therefore, for the attainment of the truth, exertion is of great help.”

“Padhānassa pana, bho gotama, katamo dhammo bahukāro? Padhānassa bahukāraṃ dhammaṃ mayaṃ bhavantaṃ [V 2.0392] gotamaṃ pucchāmā”ti. “Padhānassa kho, bhāradvāja, tulanā [M 2.0386] bahukārā. No cetaṃ tuleyya, nayidaṃ padaheyya. Yasmā ca kho tuleti tasmā padahati. Tasmā padhānassa tulanā bahukārā”ti.

“But, Master Gotama, which dhamma is of great help for exertion? We ask the venerable Gotama about the dhamma that is of great help for exertion.” “For exertion, Bhāradvāja, weighing is of great help. If one did not weigh, one would not exert oneself. And because one does weigh, one therefore exerts oneself. Therefore, for exertion, weighing is of great help.”

“Tulanāya pana, bho gotama, katamo dhammo bahukāro? Tulanāya bahukāraṃ dhammaṃ mayaṃ bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ pucchāmā”ti. “Tulanāya kho, bhāradvāja, ussāho bahukāro. No cetaṃ ussaheyya, nayidaṃ tuleyya. Yasmā ca kho ussahati tasmā tuleti. Tasmā tulanāya ussāho bahukāro”ti.

“But, Master Gotama, which dhamma is of great help for weighing? We ask the venerable Gotama about the dhamma that is of great help for weighing.” “For weighing, Bhāradvāja, striving is of great help. If one did not strive, one would not weigh. And because one does strive, one therefore weighs. Therefore, for weighing, striving is of great help.”

“Ussāhassa pana, bho gotama, katamo dhammo bahukāro? Ussāhassa bahukāraṃ dhammaṃ mayaṃ bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ pucchāmā”ti. “Ussāhassa kho, bhāradvāja, chando bahukāro. No cetaṃ chando jāyetha, nayidaṃ ussaheyya. Yasmā ca kho chando jāyati tasmā ussahati. Tasmā ussāhassa chando bahukāro”ti.

“Furthermore, Venerable Gotama, what dhamma is of great help for effort? We ask the Venerable Gotama about the dhamma that is of great help for effort.” “For effort, Bhāradvāja, wholesome desire is of great help. If this wholesome desire were not to arise, one would not make this effort. And because wholesome desire arises, therefore one makes effort. Therefore, for effort, wholesome desire is of great help.”

“Chandassa pana, bho gotama, katamo dhammo bahukāro[P 2.0175]? Chandassa bahukāraṃ dhammaṃ mayaṃ bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ pucchāmā”ti. “Chandassa kho, bhāradvāja, dhammanijjhānakkhanti bahukārā. No cete dhammā nijjhānaṃ khameyyuṃ, nayidaṃ chando jāyetha. Yasmā ca kho dhammā [T 2.0607] nijjhānaṃ khamanti tasmā chando jāyati. Tasmā chandassa dhammanijjhānakkhanti bahukārā”ti.

“Furthermore, Venerable Gotama, what dhamma is of great help for wholesome desire? We ask the Venerable Gotama about the dhamma that is of great help for wholesome desire.” “For wholesome desire, Bhāradvāja, the approval of contemplating the dhammas is of great help. If these dhammas were not approved for contemplation, this wholesome desire would not arise. And because the dhammas are approved for contemplation, therefore wholesome desire arises. Therefore, for wholesome desire, the approval of contemplating the dhammas is of great help.”

“Dhammanijjhānakkhantiyā pana, bho gotama, katamo dhammo bahukāro? Dhammanijjhānakkhantiyā bahukāraṃ dhammaṃ mayaṃ bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ pucchāmā”ti. “Dhammanijjhānakkhantiyā kho, bhāradvāja, atthūpaparikkhā bahukārā. No cetaṃ atthaṃ upaparikkheyya, nayidaṃ dhammā nijjhānaṃ khameyyuṃ. Yasmā ca kho atthaṃ upaparikkhati tasmā dhammā nijjhānaṃ khamanti. Tasmā dhammanijjhānakkhantiyā atthūpaparikkhā bahukārā”ti.

“Furthermore, Venerable Gotama, what dhamma is of great help for the approval of contemplating the dhammas? We ask the Venerable Gotama about the dhamma that is of great help for the approval of contemplating the dhammas.” “For the approval of contemplating the dhammas, Bhāradvāja, the examination of the meaning is of great help. If one were not to examine this meaning, these dhammas would not be approved for contemplation. And because one examines the meaning, therefore the dhammas are approved for contemplation. Therefore, for the approval of contemplating the dhammas, the examination of the meaning is of great help.”

“Atthūpaparikkhāya pana, bho gotama, katamo dhammo bahukāro? Atthūpaparikkhāya bahukāraṃ dhammaṃ mayaṃ bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ pucchāmā”ti. “Atthūpaparikkhāya kho, bhāradvāja, dhammadhāraṇā [V 2.0393] bahukārā. No cetaṃ dhammaṃ dhāreyya, nayidaṃ atthaṃ upaparikkheyya. Yasmā ca kho dhammaṃ dhāreti tasmā atthaṃ upaparikkhati. Tasmā atthūpaparikkhāya dhammadhāraṇā bahukārā”ti.

“Furthermore, Venerable Gotama, what dhamma is of great help for the examination of the meaning? We ask the Venerable Gotama about the dhamma that is of great help for the examination of the meaning.” “For the examination of the meaning, Bhāradvāja, retaining the Dhamma is of great help. If one were not to retain this Dhamma, one would not examine this meaning. And because one retains the Dhamma, therefore one examines the meaning. Therefore, for the examination of the meaning, retaining the Dhamma is of great help.”

“Dhammadhāraṇāya pana, bho gotama, katamo dhammo bahukāro? Dhammadhāraṇāya bahukāraṃ dhammaṃ mayaṃ bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ pucchāmā”ti. “Dhammadhāraṇāya [M 2.0387] kho, bhāradvāja, dhammassavanaṃ bahukāraṃ. No cetaṃ dhammaṃ suṇeyya, nayidaṃ dhammaṃ dhāreyya. Yasmā ca kho dhammaṃ suṇāti tasmā dhammaṃ dhāreti. Tasmā dhammadhāraṇāya dhammassavanaṃ bahukāra”nti.

“Furthermore, Venerable Gotama, what dhamma is of great help for retaining the Dhamma? We ask the Venerable Gotama about the dhamma that is of great help for retaining the Dhamma.” “For retaining the Dhamma, Bhāradvāja, listening to the Dhamma is of great help. If one were not to hear this Dhamma, one would not retain this Dhamma. And because one hears the Dhamma, therefore one retains the Dhamma. Therefore, for retaining the Dhamma, listening to the Dhamma is of great help.”

“Dhammassavanassa pana, bho gotama, katamo dhammo bahukāro? Dhammassavanassa bahukāraṃ dhammaṃ mayaṃ bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ pucchāmā”ti[T 2.0608]. “Dhammassavanassa kho, bhāradvāja, sotāvadhānaṃ bahukāraṃ[P 2.0176]. No cetaṃ sotaṃ odaheyya, nayidaṃ dhammaṃ suṇeyya. Yasmā ca kho sotaṃ odahati tasmā dhammaṃ suṇāti. Tasmā dhammassavanassa sotāvadhānaṃ bahukāra”nti.

“Furthermore, Venerable Gotama, what dhamma is of great help for listening to the Dhamma? We ask the Venerable Gotama about the dhamma that is of great help for listening to the Dhamma.” “For listening to the Dhamma, Bhāradvāja, lending the ear is of great help. If one were not to lend the ear, one would not hear this Dhamma. And because one lends the ear, therefore one hears the Dhamma. Therefore, for listening to the Dhamma, lending the ear is of great help.”

“Sotāvadhānassa pana, bho gotama, katamo dhammo bahukāro? Sotāvadhānassa bahukāraṃ dhammaṃ mayaṃ bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ pucchāmā”ti. “Sotāvadhānassa kho, bhāradvāja, payirupāsanā bahukārā. No cetaṃ payirupāseyya, nayidaṃ sotaṃ odaheyya. Yasmā ca kho payirupāsati tasmā sotaṃ odahati. Tasmā sotāvadhānassa payirupāsanā bahukārā”ti.

“Furthermore, Venerable Gotama, what dhamma is of great help for lending the ear? We ask the Venerable Gotama about the dhamma that is of great help for lending the ear.” “For lending the ear, Bhāradvāja, attending upon is of great help. If one were not to attend upon, one would not lend this ear. And because one attends upon, therefore one lends the ear. Therefore, for lending the ear, attending upon is of great help.”

“Payirupāsanāya pana, bho gotama, katamo dhammo bahukāro? Payirupāsanāya bahukāraṃ dhammaṃ mayaṃ bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ pucchāmā”ti. “Payirupāsanāya kho, bhāradvāja, upasaṅkamanaṃ bahukāraṃ. No cetaṃ upasaṅkameyya, nayidaṃ payirupāseyya. Yasmā ca kho upasaṅkamati tasmā payirupāsati. Tasmā payirupāsanāya upasaṅkamanaṃ bahukāra”nti.

“Furthermore, Venerable Gotama, what dhamma is of great help for attending upon? We ask the Venerable Gotama about the dhamma that is of great help for attending upon.” “For attending upon, Bhāradvāja, approaching is of great help. If one were not to approach, one would not attend upon. And because one approaches, therefore one attends upon. Therefore, for attending upon, approaching is of great help.”

“Upasaṅkamanassa pana, bho gotama, katamo dhammo bahukāro? Upasaṅkamanassa bahukāraṃ dhammaṃ mayaṃ bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ pucchāmā”ti. “Upasaṅkamanassa kho, bhāradvāja, saddhā bahukārā. No cetaṃ saddhā jāyetha, nayidaṃ upasaṅkameyya. Yasmā ca kho saddhā jāyati tasmā upasaṅkamati. Tasmā upasaṅkamanassa saddhā bahukārā”ti.

“Furthermore, Venerable Gotama, what dhamma is of great help for approaching? We ask the Venerable Gotama about the dhamma that is of great help for approaching.” “For approaching, Bhāradvāja, faith is of great help. If this faith were not to arise, one would not approach. And because faith arises, therefore one approaches. Therefore, for approaching, faith is of great help.”

435. “Saccānurakkhaṇaṃ [V 2.0394] mayaṃ bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ apucchimha, saccānurakkhaṇaṃ [T 2.0609] bhavaṃ gotamo byākāsi; tañca panamhākaṃ ruccati ceva khamati ca tena camha attamanā. Saccānubodhaṃ mayaṃ bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ apucchimha, saccānubodhaṃ bhavaṃ gotamo byākāsi; tañca panamhākaṃ ruccati ceva khamati ca tena camha attamanā. Saccānuppattiṃ mayaṃ bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ apucchimha, saccānuppattiṃ bhavaṃ gotamo byākāsi; tañca panamhākaṃ ruccati ceva khamati ca tena camha attamanā[M 2.0388]. Saccānuppattiyā bahukāraṃ dhammaṃ mayaṃ bhavantaṃ [P 2.0177] gotamaṃ apucchimha, saccānuppattiyā bahukāraṃ dhammaṃ bhavaṃ gotamo byākāsi; tañca panamhākaṃ ruccati ceva khamati ca tena camha attamanā. Yaṃyadeva ca mayaṃ bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ apucchimha taṃtadeva bhavaṃ gotamo byākāsi; tañca panamhākaṃ ruccati ceva khamati ca tena camha attamanā. Mayañhi, bho gotama, pubbe evaṃ jānāma – ‘ke ca muṇḍakā samaṇakā ibbhā kaṇhā bandhupādāpaccā, ke ca dhammassa aññātāro’ti? Ajanesi vata me bhavaṃ gotamo samaṇesu samaṇapemaṃ, samaṇesu samaṇapasādaṃ, samaṇesu samaṇagāravaṃ. Abhikkantaṃ, bho gotama…pe… upāsakaṃ maṃ bhavaṃ gotamo dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṃ saraṇaṃ gata”nti.

435. “We asked the Venerable Gotama about guarding the truth, and the Venerable Gotama explained guarding the truth; this pleases and is acceptable to us, and we are delighted by it. We asked the Venerable Gotama about the understanding of truth, and the Venerable Gotama explained the understanding of truth; this pleases and is acceptable to us, and we are delighted by it. We asked the Venerable Gotama about the attainment of truth, and the Venerable Gotama explained the attainment of truth; this pleases and is acceptable to us, and we are delighted by it. We asked the Venerable Gotama about the Dhamma that is very helpful for the attainment of truth, and the Venerable Gotama explained the Dhamma that is very helpful for the attainment of truth; this pleases and is acceptable to us, and we are delighted by it. Whatever we asked the Venerable Gotama, the Venerable Gotama explained just that; this pleases and is acceptable to us, and we are delighted by it. For previously, Master Gotama, we thought thus: ‘Who are these shaven-headed ascetics, these commoners, dark fellows, offspring from the kinsman's feet? And what could they know of the Dhamma?’ But the Venerable Gotama has generated in me affection for ascetics, confidence in ascetics, and reverence for ascetics. Excellent, Master Gotama… May the Venerable Gotama regard me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge from this day forward, for as long as life lasts.”

Caṅkīsuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ pañcamaṃ.

The Caṅkī Sutta, the fifth, is concluded.

6. Esukārīsuttaṃ

6. The Esukārī Sutta

436. Evaṃ [T 2.0610][V 2.0395] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Atha kho esukārī brāhmaṇo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho esukārī brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “brāhmaṇā, bho gotama, catasso pāricariyā paññapenti – brāhmaṇassa pāricariyaṃ paññapenti, khattiyassa pāricariyaṃ paññapenti, vessassa pāricariyaṃ paññapenti, suddassa pāricariyaṃ paññapenti. Tatridaṃ, bho gotama, brāhmaṇā brāhmaṇassa pāricariyaṃ paññapenti – ‘brāhmaṇo vā brāhmaṇaṃ paricareyya, khattiyo vā brāhmaṇaṃ paricareyya, vesso vā brāhmaṇaṃ paricareyya, suddo vā brāhmaṇaṃ paricareyyā’ti. Idaṃ kho, bho gotama, brāhmaṇā brāhmaṇassa pāricariyaṃ [P 2.0178] paññapenti. Tatridaṃ, bho gotama, brāhmaṇā khattiyassa pāricariyaṃ paññapenti – ‘khattiyo vā khattiyaṃ paricareyya, vesso vā khattiyaṃ paricareyya, suddo vā khattiyaṃ paricareyyā’ti. Idaṃ kho, bho gotama, brāhmaṇā khattiyassa pāricariyaṃ paññapenti. Tatridaṃ, bho gotama, brāhmaṇā vessassa pāricariyaṃ paññapenti – ‘vesso vā vessaṃ paricareyya, suddo vā vessaṃ [T 2.0611] paricareyyā’ti. Idaṃ kho, bho gotama, brāhmaṇā vessassa pāricariyaṃ paññapenti[M 2.0389]. Tatridaṃ, bho gotama, brāhmaṇā suddassa pāricariyaṃ paññapenti – ‘suddova suddaṃ paricareyya. Ko panañño suddaṃ paricarissatī’ti? Idaṃ kho, bho gotama, brāhmaṇā suddassa pāricariyaṃ paññapenti. Brāhmaṇā, bho gotama, imā catasso pāricariyā paññapenti. Idha bhavaṃ gotamo kimāhā”ti?

436. Thus have I heard: At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī, in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery. Then the brahmin Esukārī approached the Blessed One; having approached, he exchanged greetings with the Blessed One. After exchanging pleasant and courteous conversation, he sat down to one side. Sitting to one side, the brahmin Esukārī said this to the Blessed One: “Master Gotama, the brahmins prescribe four kinds of service: they prescribe service for a brahmin, service for a noble, service for a merchant, and service for a worker. Therein, Master Gotama, the brahmins prescribe service for a brahmin thus: ‘A brahmin should serve a brahmin, a noble should serve a brahmin, a merchant should serve a brahmin, or a worker should serve a brahmin.’ This, Master Gotama, is how the brahmins prescribe service for a brahmin. Therein, Master Gotama, the brahmins prescribe service for a noble thus: ‘A noble should serve a noble, a merchant should serve a noble, or a worker should serve a noble.’ This, Master Gotama, is how the brahmins prescribe service for a noble. Therein, Master Gotama, the brahmins prescribe service for a merchant thus: ‘A merchant should serve a merchant, or a worker should serve a merchant.’ This, Master Gotama, is how the brahmins prescribe service for a merchant. Therein, Master Gotama, the brahmins prescribe service for a worker thus: ‘A worker should serve a worker. Who else would serve a worker?’ This, Master Gotama, is how the brahmins prescribe service for a worker. Master Gotama, the brahmins prescribe these four kinds of service. What does the Venerable Gotama say about this?”

437. “Kiṃ pana, brāhmaṇa, sabbo loko brāhmaṇānaṃ etadabbhanujānāti – ‘imā catasso pāricariyā paññapentū’”ti paññapentīti (sī. ka.)? “No hidaṃ, bho gotama”. “Seyyathāpi, brāhmaṇa, puriso daliddo daḷiddo (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) assako anāḷhiyo. Tassa akāmassa bilaṃ olaggeyyuṃ – ‘idaṃ te, ambho purisa, maṃsaṃ khāditabbaṃ, mūlañca anuppadātabba’nti. Evameva kho, brāhmaṇa, brāhmaṇā appaṭiññāya tesaṃ samaṇabrāhmaṇānaṃ, atha ca panimā catasso pāricariyā paññapenti. Nāhaṃ, brāhmaṇa, ‘sabbaṃ paricaritabba’nti [V 2.0396] vadāmi; nāhaṃ, brāhmaṇa, ‘sabbaṃ na paricaritabba’nti vadāmi. Yaṃ hissa, brāhmaṇa, paricarato pāricariyāhetu pāpiyo assa na seyyo, nāhaṃ taṃ ‘paricaritabba’nti vadāmi; yañca khvāssa, brāhmaṇa, paricarato pāricariyāhetu seyyo assa na pāpiyo tamahaṃ ‘paricaritabba’nti vadāmi. Khattiyaṃ cepi, brāhmaṇa, evaṃ puccheyyuṃ – ‘yaṃ vā te paricarato pāricariyāhetu pāpiyo assa na seyyo, yaṃ vā te paricarato pāricariyāhetu seyyo assa [T 2.0612] na pāpiyo; kamettha paricareyyāsī’ti, khattiyopi hi, brāhmaṇa[P 2.0179], sammā byākaramāno evaṃ byākareyya – ‘yañhi me paricarato pāricariyāhetu pāpiyo assa na seyyo, nāhaṃ taṃ paricareyyaṃ; yañca kho me paricarato pāricariyāhetu seyyo assa na pāpiyo tamahaṃ paricareyya’nti. Brāhmaṇaṃ cepi, brāhmaṇa…pe… vessaṃ cepi, brāhmaṇa…pe… suddaṃ cepi, brāhmaṇa, evaṃ puccheyyuṃ – ‘yaṃ vā te paricarato pāricariyāhetu pāpiyo assa na seyyo, yaṃ vā te paricarato pāricariyāhetu seyyo assa na pāpiyo; kamettha paricareyyāsī’ti, suddopi hi, brāhmaṇa, sammā byākaramāno evaṃ byākareyya – ‘yañhi me paricarato pāricariyāhetu pāpiyo assa na seyyo, nāhaṃ taṃ paricareyyaṃ; yañca kho me paricarato pāricariyāhetu seyyo assa na pāpiyo tamahaṃ paricareyya’nti. Nāhaṃ, brāhmaṇa, ‘uccākulīnatā seyyaṃso’ti vadāmi, na panāhaṃ, brāhmaṇa, ‘uccākulīnatā pāpiyaṃso’ti [M 2.0390] vadāmi; nāhaṃ, brāhmaṇa, ‘uḷāravaṇṇatā seyyaṃso’ti vadāmi, na panāhaṃ, brāhmaṇa, ‘uḷāravaṇṇatā pāpiyaṃso’ti vadāmi; nāhaṃ, brāhmaṇa, ‘uḷārabhogatā seyyaṃso’ti vadāmi, na panāhaṃ, brāhmaṇa, ‘uḷārabhogatā pāpiyaṃso’ti vadāmi.

437. “But, brahmin, does the whole world approve this of the brahmins: ‘Let them prescribe these four kinds of service’?” “No, indeed, venerable Gotama.” “Suppose, brahmin, a man is poor, destitute, and penniless. They would hang up a portion of meat for him against his will, saying: ‘Here, good man, this meat must be eaten by you, and the price must also be paid!’ In the same way, brahmin, the brahmins prescribe these four kinds of service without the consent of those ascetics and brahmins. I do not say, brahmin, that everyone should be served; nor do I say, brahmin, that no one should be served. Brahmin, if by serving a person, on account of that service, one would become worse and not better, I do not say that person should be served. And brahmin, if by serving a person, on account of that service, one would become better and not worse, I say that person should be served. If, brahmin, a khattiya were asked: ‘Between a person whom, by serving, you would become worse and not better on account of that service, and a person whom, by serving, you would become better and not worse on account of that service, whom among these would you serve?’—a khattiya, answering rightly, would say: ‘The person whom, by serving, I would become worse and not better on account of that service, I would not serve. And the person whom, by serving, I would become better and not worse on account of that service, that one I would serve.’ If a brahmin were asked… if a vessa were asked… if a sudda were asked: ‘Between a person whom, by serving, you would become worse and not better on account of that service, and a person whom, by serving, you would become better and not worse on account of that service, whom among these would you serve?’—a sudda, answering rightly, would say: ‘The person whom, by serving, I would become worse and not better on account of that service, I would not serve. And the person whom, by serving, I would become better and not worse on account of that service, that one I would serve.’ I do not say, brahmin, that being of high birth makes one better, nor, brahmin, do I say that being of high birth makes one worse. I do not say, brahmin, that having a fine appearance makes one better, nor, brahmin, do I say that having a fine appearance makes one worse. I do not say, brahmin, that having great wealth makes one better, nor, brahmin, do I say that having great wealth makes one worse.”

438. “Uccākulīnopi hi, brāhmaṇa, idhekacco pāṇātipātī hoti, adinnādāyī hoti, kāmesumicchācārī hoti, musāvādī hoti, pisuṇāvāco hoti, pharusāvāco hoti, samphappalāpī hoti, abhijjhālu hoti[T 2.0613], byāpannacitto hoti, micchādiṭṭhi hoti. Tasmā ‘na uccākulīnatā seyyaṃso’ti vadāmi. Uccākulīnopi hi, brāhmaṇa, idhekacco pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti, adinnādānā paṭivirato hoti, kāmesumicchācārā paṭivirato hoti, musāvādā paṭivirato hoti, pisuṇāya vācāya paṭivirato hoti, pharusāya vācāya paṭivirato hoti, samphappalāpā paṭivirato hoti, anabhijjhālu hoti, abyāpannacitto hoti, sammādiṭṭhi hoti. Tasmā ‘na uccākulīnatā pāpiyaṃso’ti vadāmi.

438. “For, brahmin, here a certain person of high birth is one who destroys living beings, takes what is not given, engages in sexual misconduct, speaks falsely, speaks divisively, speaks harshly, engages in idle chatter, is covetous, has a mind of ill will, and holds wrong view. Therefore, I do not say that being of high birth makes one better. And, brahmin, here a certain person of high birth is one who abstains from destroying living beings, abstains from taking what is not given, abstains from sexual misconduct, abstains from false speech, abstains from divisive speech, abstains from harsh speech, abstains from idle chatter, is not covetous, has a mind without ill will, and holds right view. Therefore, I do not say that being of high birth makes one worse.”

439. “Uḷāravaṇṇopi [V 2.0397] hi, brāhmaṇa…pe… uḷārabhogopi hi, brāhmaṇa, idhekacco pāṇātipātī hoti…pe… micchādiṭṭhi hoti. Tasmā [T 2.0614] ‘na uḷārabhogatā seyyaṃso’ti vadāmi. Uḷārabhogopi hi, brāhmaṇa, idhekacco pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti…pe… sammādiṭṭhi hoti. Tasmā ‘na uḷārabhogatā [P 2.0180] pāpiyaṃso’ti vadāmi. Nāhaṃ, brāhmaṇa, ‘sabbaṃ paricaritabba’nti vadāmi, na panāhaṃ, brāhmaṇa, ‘sabbaṃ na paricaritabba’nti vadāmi. Yaṃ hissa, brāhmaṇa, paricarato pāricariyāhetu saddhā vaḍḍhati, sīlaṃ vaḍḍhati, sutaṃ vaḍḍhati, cāgo vaḍḍhati, paññā vaḍḍhati, tamahaṃ ‘paricaritabba’nti (vadāmi. Yaṃ hissa, brāhmaṇa, paricarato pāricariyāhetu na saddhā vaḍḍhati, na sīlaṃ vaḍḍhati, na sutaṃ vaḍḍhati, na cāgo vaḍḍhati, na paññā vaḍḍhati, nāhaṃ taṃ ‘paricaritabba’nti) ( ) etthantare pāṭho sī. syā. kaṃ. pī. potthakesu natthi vadāmī”ti.

439. “For, brahmin, a certain person with a fine appearance… and a certain person with great wealth here is one who destroys living beings… and holds wrong view. Therefore, I do not say that having great wealth makes one better. And, brahmin, a certain person with great wealth here is one who abstains from destroying living beings… and holds right view. Therefore, I do not say that having great wealth makes one worse. I do not say, brahmin, that everyone should be served; nor, brahmin, do I say that no one should be served. Brahmin, if by serving a person, one's faith, virtue, learning, generosity, and wisdom increase on account of that service, I say that person should be served. Brahmin, if by serving a person, one's faith, virtue, learning, generosity, and wisdom do not increase on account of that service, I say that person should not be served.”

440. Evaṃ vutte, esukārī brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “brāhmaṇā, bho gotama, cattāri dhanāni paññapenti – brāhmaṇassa sandhanaṃ paññapenti, khattiyassa sandhanaṃ paññapenti, vessassa sandhanaṃ paññapenti, suddassa [M 2.0391] sandhanaṃ paññapenti. Tatridaṃ, bho gotama, brāhmaṇā brāhmaṇassa sandhanaṃ paññapenti bhikkhācariyaṃ; bhikkhācariyañca pana brāhmaṇo sandhanaṃ atimaññamāno akiccakārī hoti gopova adinnaṃ ādiyamānoti. Idaṃ kho, bho gotama, brāhmaṇā brāhmaṇassa sandhanaṃ paññapenti. Tatridaṃ, bho gotama, brāhmaṇā khattiyassa sandhanaṃ paññapenti dhanukalāpaṃ; dhanukalāpañca [T 2.0615] pana khattiyo sandhanaṃ atimaññamāno akiccakārī hoti gopova adinnaṃ ādiyamānoti. Idaṃ kho, bho gotama, brāhmaṇā khattiyassa sandhanaṃ paññapenti. Tatridaṃ, bho gotama, brāhmaṇā vessassa sandhanaṃ paññapenti kasigorakkhaṃ; kasigorakkhañca pana vesso sandhanaṃ atimaññamāno akiccakārī hoti gopova adinnaṃ ādiyamānoti. Idaṃ kho, bho gotama, brāhmaṇā vessassa sandhanaṃ paññapenti. Tatridaṃ, bho gotama, brāhmaṇā suddassa sandhanaṃ paññapenti asitabyābhaṅgiṃ; asitabyābhaṅgiñca pana suddo sandhanaṃ atimaññamāno akiccakārī hoti gopova adinnaṃ ādiyamānoti. Idaṃ kho, bho gotama, brāhmaṇā suddassa sandhanaṃ paññapenti. Brāhmaṇā, bho gotama, imāni cattāri dhanāni paññapenti. Idha bhavaṃ gotamo kimāhā”ti?

440. When this was said, the brahmin Esukārī said this to the Blessed One: 'Master Gotama, brahmins declare four kinds of wealth. They declare the personal wealth of a brahmin, they declare the personal wealth of a khattiya, they declare the personal wealth of a vessa, and they declare the personal wealth of a sudda. Therein, Master Gotama, brahmins declare the practice of alms-gathering as the personal wealth of a brahmin. But a brahmin who despises the practice of alms-gathering, his personal wealth, is a doer of what ought not to be done, like a guardian who appropriates what is not given. This, Master Gotama, is the personal wealth that brahmins declare for a brahmin. Therein, Master Gotama, brahmins declare the bow and quiver as the personal wealth of a khattiya. But a khattiya who despises the bow and quiver, his personal wealth, is a doer of what ought not to be done, like a guardian who appropriates what is not given. This, Master Gotama, is the personal wealth that brahmins declare for a khattiya. Therein, Master Gotama, brahmins declare agriculture and cattle-herding as the personal wealth of a vessa. But a vessa who despises agriculture and cattle-herding, his personal wealth, is a doer of what ought not to be done, like a guardian who appropriates what is not given. This, Master Gotama, is the personal wealth that brahmins declare for a vessa. Therein, Master Gotama, brahmins declare the sickle and carrying-pole as the personal wealth of a sudda. But a sudda who despises the sickle and carrying-pole, his personal wealth, is a doer of what ought not to be done, like a guardian who appropriates what is not given. This, Master Gotama, is the personal wealth that brahmins declare for a sudda. Master Gotama, brahmins declare these four kinds of wealth. Regarding this, what does the venerable Gotama say?'

441. “Kiṃ pana, brāhmaṇa, sabbo loko brāhmaṇānaṃ etadabbhanujānāti – ‘imāni cattāri dhanāni paññapentū’”ti? “No [P 2.0181] hidaṃ, bho gotama”. “Seyyathāpi, brāhmaṇa, puriso daliddo [V 2.0398] assako anāḷhiyo. Tassa akāmassa bilaṃ olaggeyyuṃ – ‘idaṃ te, ambho purisa, maṃsaṃ khāditabbaṃ, mūlañca anuppadātabba’nti. Evameva kho, brāhmaṇa, brāhmaṇā appaṭiññāya tesaṃ samaṇabrāhmaṇānaṃ, atha ca panimāni cattāri dhanāni paññapenti. Ariyaṃ kho ahaṃ, brāhmaṇa, lokuttaraṃ dhammaṃ purisassa sandhanaṃ paññapemi. Porāṇaṃ kho panassa mātāpettikaṃ kulavaṃsaṃ anussarato yattha yattheva [T 2.0616] attabhāvassa abhinibbatti hoti tena teneva saṅkhyaṃ gacchati. Khattiyakule ce attabhāvassa abhinibbatti hoti ‘khattiyo’tveva saṅkhyaṃ gacchati; brāhmaṇakule ce attabhāvassa abhinibbatti hoti ‘brāhmaṇo’tveva saṅkhyaṃ gacchati; vessakule ce attabhāvassa abhinibbatti hoti ‘vesso’tveva saṅkhyaṃ gacchati; suddakule ce attabhāvassa abhinibbatti hoti ‘suddo’tveva [M 2.0392] saṅkhyaṃ gacchati. Seyyathāpi, brāhmaṇa, yaṃyadeva paccayaṃ paṭicca aggi jalati tena teneva saṅkhyaṃ gacchati. Kaṭṭhañce paṭicca aggi jalati ‘kaṭṭhaggi’tveva saṅkhyaṃ gacchati; sakalikañce paṭicca aggi jalati ‘sakalikaggi’tveva saṅkhyaṃ gacchati; tiṇañce paṭicca aggi jalati ‘tiṇaggi’tveva saṅkhyaṃ gacchati; gomayañce paṭicca aggi jalati ‘gomayaggi’tveva saṅkhyaṃ gacchati. Evameva kho ahaṃ, brāhmaṇa, ariyaṃ lokuttaraṃ dhammaṃ purisassa sandhanaṃ paññapemi. Porāṇaṃ kho panassa mātāpettikaṃ kulavaṃsaṃ anussarato yattha yattheva attabhāvassa abhinibbatti hoti tena teneva saṅkhyaṃ gacchati.

441. 'But, brahmin, does the entire world consent to this declaration of the brahmins: ‘Let them declare these four kinds of wealth’?' 'Indeed not, Master Gotama.' 'Suppose, brahmin, there is a man who is poor, without property, and destitute. Against his will, they might hang a portion of meat for him, saying: "Here, good man, this meat is to be eaten by you, and the price for it must be paid." In the very same way, brahmin, the brahmins make this declaration for those ascetics and brahmins without their consent. I, brahmin, declare the noble, supramundane Dhamma as a person's personal wealth. However, for one who recollects his ancient maternal and paternal lineage, in whatever family his rebirth occurs, by that very family is he designated. If his rebirth occurs in a khattiya family, he is designated as a 'khattiya.' If his rebirth occurs in a brahmin family, he is designated as a 'brahmin.' If his rebirth occurs in a vessa family, he is designated as a 'vessa.' If his rebirth occurs in a sudda family, he is designated as a 'sudda.' Just as, brahmin, a fire is designated according to the very fuel on which it depends when it burns. If a fire burns depending on wood, it is designated as a 'wood-fire.' If a fire burns depending on wood-chips, it is designated as a 'wood-chip-fire.' If a fire burns depending on grass, it is designated as a 'grass-fire.' If a fire burns depending on cow-dung, it is designated as a 'cow-dung-fire.' In the very same way, brahmin, I declare the noble, supramundane Dhamma as a person's personal wealth. However, for one who recollects his ancient maternal and paternal lineage, in whatever family his rebirth occurs, by that very family is he designated.'

“Khattiyakule ce attabhāvassa abhinibbatti hoti ‘khattiyo’tveva saṅkhyaṃ gacchati; brāhmaṇakule ce attabhāvassa abhinibbatti hoti ‘brāhmaṇo’tveva saṅkhyaṃ gacchati; vessakule ce attabhāvassa abhinibbatti hoti ‘vesso’tveva saṅkhyaṃ gacchati; suddakule ce attabhāvassa abhinibbatti hoti ‘suddo’tveva saṅkhyaṃ gacchati.

“If the birth of a person occurs in a khattiya family, he is designated as a ‘khattiya’; if the birth of a person occurs in a brahmin family, he is designated as a ‘brahmin’; if the birth of a person occurs in a vessa family, he is designated as a ‘vessa’; if the birth of a person occurs in a sudda family, he is designated as a ‘sudda’.”

“Khattiyakulā [T 2.0617] cepi, brāhmaṇa, agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajito hoti, so ca tathāgatappaveditaṃ dhammavinayaṃ āgamma pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti, adinnādānā paṭivirato hoti, abrahmacariyā paṭivirato hoti, musāvādā paṭivirato hoti, pisuṇāya vācāya paṭivirato hoti, pharusāya vācāya paṭivirato hoti, samphappalāpā paṭivirato hoti, anabhijjhālu hoti, abyāpannacitto hoti, sammādiṭṭhi hoti, ārādhako hoti ñāyaṃ dhammaṃ kusalaṃ.

And if, brahmin, one from a khattiya family goes forth from the household life into homelessness, and that person, relying on the Dhamma-Vinaya proclaimed by the Tathāgata, abstains from the destruction of life, abstains from taking what is not given, abstains from unchastity, abstains from false speech, abstains from divisive speech, abstains from harsh speech, abstains from idle chatter, is not covetous, is of a mind without ill will, and possesses right view, he is one who accomplishes the right and wholesome Dhamma.

“Brāhmaṇakulā [V 2.0399][P 2.0182] cepi, brāhmaṇa, agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajito hoti, so ca tathāgatappaveditaṃ dhammavinayaṃ āgamma pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti…pe… sammādiṭṭhi hoti, ārādhako hoti ñāyaṃ dhammaṃ kusalaṃ.

And if, brahmin, one from a brahmin family goes forth from the household life into homelessness, and that person, relying on the Dhamma-Vinaya proclaimed by the Tathāgata, abstains from the destruction of life... and possesses right view, he is one who accomplishes the right and wholesome Dhamma.

“Vessakulā cepi, brāhmaṇa, agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajito hoti, so ca tathāgatappaveditaṃ dhammavinayaṃ āgamma pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti…pe… sammādiṭṭhi hoti, ārādhako hoti ñāyaṃ dhammaṃ kusalaṃ.

And if, brahmin, one from a vessa family goes forth from the household life into homelessness, and that person, relying on the Dhamma-Vinaya proclaimed by the Tathāgata, abstains from the destruction of life... and possesses right view, he is one who accomplishes the right and wholesome Dhamma.

“Suddakulā cepi, brāhmaṇa, agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajito hoti, so ca tathāgatappaveditaṃ dhammavinayaṃ āgamma pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti…pe… [T 2.0618] sammādiṭṭhi hoti, ārādhako hoti ñāyaṃ dhammaṃ kusalaṃ.

Brahmin, if one from a Suddā family has gone forth from the household life into homelessness, and, relying on the Dhamma and Vinaya proclaimed by the Tathāgata, he abstains from the destruction of life... he has right view, he succeeds in the right, wholesome Dhamma.

442. “Taṃ [M 2.0393] kiṃ maññasi, brāhmaṇa, brāhmaṇova nu kho pahoti asmiṃ padese averaṃ abyābajjhaṃ mettacittaṃ bhāvetuṃ, no khattiyo no vesso no suddo”ti? “No hidaṃ, bho gotama. Khattiyopi hi, bho gotama, pahoti asmiṃ padese averaṃ abyābajjhaṃ mettacittaṃ bhāvetuṃ; brāhmaṇopi hi, bho gotama… vessopi hi, bho gotama… suddopi hi, bho gotama… sabbepi hi, bho gotama, cattāro vaṇṇā pahonti asmiṃ padese averaṃ abyābajjhaṃ mettacittaṃ bhāvetu”nti. “Evameva kho, brāhmaṇa, khattiyakulā cepi agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajito hoti, so ca tathāgatappaveditaṃ dhammavinayaṃ āgamma pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti…pe… sammādiṭṭhi hoti, ārādhako hoti ñāyaṃ dhammaṃ kusalaṃ.

442. “What do you think, Brahmin? Is it only a Brahmin who is able, in this region, to develop a mind of loving-kindness that is without enmity and without ill will, and not a Khattiya, not a Vessa, not a Suddā?” “No, indeed, Master Gotama. A Khattiya, Master Gotama, is also able, in this region, to develop a mind of loving-kindness that is without enmity and without ill will. A Brahmin, Master Gotama… a Vessa, Master Gotama… a Suddā, Master Gotama… indeed, Master Gotama, all four castes are able, in this region, to develop a mind of loving-kindness that is without enmity and without ill will.” “Just so, Brahmin.
