If one from a Khattiya family has gone forth from the household life into homelessness, and, relying on the Dhamma and Vinaya proclaimed by the Tathāgata, he abstains from the destruction of life... he has right view, he succeeds in the right, wholesome Dhamma.

“Brāhmaṇakulā cepi, brāhmaṇa… vessakulā cepi, brāhmaṇa… suddakulā cepi, brāhmaṇa, agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajito hoti, so ca tathāgatappaveditaṃ dhammavinayaṃ āgamma pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti…pe… [T 2.0619] sammādiṭṭhi hoti, ārādhako hoti ñāyaṃ dhammaṃ kusalaṃ.

Brahmin, if one from a Brahmin family… Brahmin, if one from a Vessa family… Brahmin, if one from a Suddā family has gone forth from the household life into homelessness, and, relying on the Dhamma and Vinaya proclaimed by the Tathāgata, he abstains from the destruction of life... he has right view, he succeeds in the right, wholesome Dhamma.

443. “Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, brāhmaṇa, brāhmaṇova nu kho pahoti sottisināniṃ ādāya nadiṃ gantvā rajojallaṃ pavāhetuṃ, no khattiyo no vesso no suddo”ti? “No hidaṃ, bho gotama[V 2.0400]. Khattiyopi hi, bho gotama, pahoti sottisināniṃ ādāya nadiṃ gantvā rajojallaṃ pavāhetuṃ; brāhmaṇopi hi, bho gotama… vessopi hi, bho gotama [P 2.0183]… suddopi hi, bho gotama… sabbepi hi, bho gotama, cattāro vaṇṇā pahonti sottisināniṃ ādāya nadiṃ gantvā rajojallaṃ pavāhetu”nti. “Evameva kho, brāhmaṇa, khattiyakulā cepi agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajito hoti, so ca tathāgatappaveditaṃ dhammavinayaṃ āgamma pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti…pe… sammādiṭṭhi hoti, ārādhako hoti ñāyaṃ dhammaṃ kusalaṃ.

443. “What do you think, Brahmin? Is it only a Brahmin who is able, having taken bath powder, to go to the river and wash away dust and dirt, and not a Khattiya, not a Vessa, not a Suddā?” “No, indeed, Master Gotama. A Khattiya, Master Gotama, is also able, having taken bath powder, to go to the river and wash away dust and dirt; a Brahmin, Master Gotama… a Vessa, Master Gotama… a Suddā, Master Gotama… indeed, Master Gotama, all four castes are able, having taken bath powder, to go to the river and wash away dust and dirt.” “Just so, Brahmin. If one from a Khattiya family has gone forth from the household life into homelessness, and, relying on the Dhamma and Vinaya proclaimed by the Tathāgata, he abstains from the destruction of life... he has right view, he succeeds in the right, wholesome Dhamma.

“Brāhmaṇakulā cepi, brāhmaṇa… vessakulā cepi, brāhmaṇa… suddakulā cepi[T 2.0620], brāhmaṇa, agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajito hoti, so ca tathāgatappaveditaṃ dhammavinayaṃ āgamma pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti…pe… sammādiṭṭhi hoti, ārādhako hoti ñāyaṃ dhammaṃ kusalaṃ.

Brahmin, if one from a Brahmin family… Brahmin, if one from a Vessa family… Brahmin, if one from a Suddā family has gone forth from the household life into homelessness, and, relying on the Dhamma and Vinaya proclaimed by the Tathāgata, he abstains from the destruction of life... he has right view, he succeeds in the right, wholesome Dhamma.

444. “Taṃ [M 2.0394] kiṃ maññasi, brāhmaṇa, idha rājā khattiyo muddhāvasitto nānājaccānaṃ purisānaṃ purisasataṃ sannipāteyya – ‘āyantu bhonto ye tattha khattiyakulā brāhmaṇakulā rājaññakulā uppannā sākassa vā sālassa vā salaḷassa vā candanassa vā padumakassa vā uttarāraṇiṃ ādāya aggiṃ abhinibbattentu, tejo pātukarontu; āyantu pana bhonto ye tattha caṇḍālakulā nesādakulā venakulā rathakārakulā pukkusakulā uppannā sāpānadoṇiyā vā sūkaradoṇiyā vā rajakadoṇiyā vā eraṇḍakaṭṭhassa vā uttarāraṇiṃ ādāya aggiṃ abhinibbattentu, tejo pātukarontū’”ti?

444. “What do you think, Brahmin? Suppose a consecrated Khattiya king were to assemble a hundred men of various origins and say: ‘Come, sirs, those of you who are born from Khattiya families, Brahmin families, or royal families—taking the upper fire-stick made of teak, sāla, salaḷa, sandalwood, or padumaka wood, produce fire, make heat appear. And come, sirs, those of you who are born from Caṇḍāla families, Nesāda families, Vena families, Rathakāra families, or Pukkusa families—taking the upper fire-stick made of a dog’s trough, a pig’s trough, a washerman’s trough, or castor wood, produce fire, make heat appear.’”

“Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, brāhmaṇa, yo evaṃ nu kho so khattiyakulā brāhmaṇakulā rājaññakulā uppannehi sākassa vā sālassa vā salaḷassa vā candanassa vā padumakassa vā uttarāraṇiṃ ādāya aggi abhinibbatto tejo pātukato so eva nu khvāssa aggi accimā ceva vaṇṇavā ca pabhassaro ca tena ca sakkā agginā aggikaraṇīyaṃ [T 2.0621] kātuṃ; yo pana so caṇḍālakulā nesādakulā venakulā rathakārakulā pukkusakulā uppannehi sāpānadoṇiyā vā sūkaradoṇiyā vā rajakadoṇiyā vā eraṇḍakaṭṭhassa vā uttarāraṇiṃ ādāya aggi abhinibbatto tejo pātukato svāssa aggi na ceva accimā na ca vaṇṇavā na ca [V 2.0401] pabhassaro na ca tena sakkā agginā aggikaraṇīyaṃ kātu”nti? “No hidaṃ, bho gotama. Yopi hi so, bho gotama, khattiyakulā brāhmaṇakulā rājaññakulā uppannehi sākassa vā sālassa [P 2.0184] vā salaḷassa vā candanassa vā padumakassa vā uttarāraṇiṃ ādāya aggi abhinibbatto tejo pātukato svāssa aggi accimā ceva vaṇṇavā ca pabhassaro ca tena ca sakkā agginā aggikaraṇīyaṃ kātuṃ; yopi so caṇḍālakulā nesādakulā venakulā rathakārakulā pukkusakulā uppannehi sāpānadoṇiyā vā sūkaradoṇiyā vā rajakadoṇiyā vā eraṇḍakaṭṭhassa vā uttarāraṇiṃ ādāya aggi abhinibbatto tejo pātukato svāssa aggi accimā ceva vaṇṇavā ca pabhassaro ca tena ca sakkā agginā aggikaraṇīyaṃ kātuṃ. Sabbopi hi, bho gotama, aggi accimā ceva vaṇṇavā ca pabhassaro ca sabbenapi sakkā agginā aggikaraṇīyaṃ kātu”nti.

“What do you think, Brahmin? If a fire were produced and heat made to appear by those born from Khattiya families, Brahmin families, or royal families, taking an upper fire-stick of teak, sāla, salaḷa, sandalwood, or padumaka wood—would that very fire have a flame, have color, and be radiant, and would it be possible with that fire to do any work that requires fire? But if a fire were produced and heat made to appear by those born from Caṇḍāla families, Nesāda families, Vena families, Rathakāra families, or Pukkusa families, taking an upper fire-stick from a dog’s trough, a pig’s trough, a washerman’s trough, or castor wood—would that fire not have a flame, not have color, not be radiant, and would it not be possible with that fire to do any work that requires fire?” “No, indeed, Master Gotama. The fire produced by those born from Khattiya families, Brahmin families, or royal families, taking an upper fire-stick of teak, sāla, salaḷa, sandalwood, or padumaka wood, would have a flame, have color, and be radiant, and it would be possible with that fire to do any work that requires fire. The fire produced by those born from Caṇḍāla families, Nesāda families, Vena families, Rathakāra families, or Pukkusa families, taking an upper fire-stick from a dog’s trough, a pig’s trough, a washerman’s trough, or castor wood, that fire too would have a flame, have color, and be radiant, and it would be possible with that fire to do any work that requires fire. For, Master Gotama, all fire has a flame, has color, and is radiant, and with any fire it is possible to do any work that requires fire.”

“Evameva [M 2.0395] kho, brāhmaṇa, khattiyakulā cepi agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajito hoti, so ca tathāgatappaveditaṃ dhammavinayaṃ āgamma [T 2.0622] pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti…pe… sammādiṭṭhi hoti, ārādhako hoti ñāyaṃ dhammaṃ kusalaṃ. Brāhmaṇakulā cepi, brāhmaṇa… vessakulā cepi, brāhmaṇa… suddakulā cepi, brāhmaṇa, agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajito hoti, so ca tathāgatappaveditaṃ dhammavinayaṃ āgamma pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti, adinnādānā paṭivirato hoti, abrahmacariyā paṭivirato hoti, musāvādā paṭivirato hoti, pisuṇāya vācāya paṭivirato hoti, pharusāya vācāya paṭivirato hoti, samphappalāpā paṭivirato hoti, anabhijjhālu hoti, abyāpannacitto hoti, sammādiṭṭhi hoti, ārādhako hoti ñāyaṃ dhammaṃ kusala”nti.

“Just so, Brahmin, even if one from a khattiya family has gone forth from the household life into homelessness, and relying on the Dhamma and Vinaya proclaimed by the Tathāgata, he abstains from the destruction of life… and so on… has right view, he is an accomplisher of the right, wholesome Dhamma. Brahmin, even if one from a brahmin family… Brahmin, even if one from a vessa family… Brahmin, even if one from a sudda family has gone forth from the household life into homelessness, and relying on the Dhamma and Vinaya proclaimed by the Tathāgata, he abstains from the destruction of life, abstains from taking what is not given, abstains from unchaste conduct, abstains from false speech, abstains from slanderous speech, abstains from harsh speech, abstains from idle chatter, is not covetous, has a mind free from ill will, has right view, and is an accomplisher of the right, wholesome Dhamma.”

Evaṃ vutte, esukārī brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “abhikkantaṃ, bho gotama, abhikkantaṃ, bho gotama…pe… upāsakaṃ maṃ bhavaṃ gotamo dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṃ saraṇaṃ gata”nti.

When this was said, the Brahmin Esukārī said to the Blessed One: “Excellent, Master Gotama! Excellent, Master Gotama!… May Master Gotama remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life, from this day forth.”

Esukārīsuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ chaṭṭhaṃ.

The Esukārī Sutta, the Sixth, is concluded.

7. Dhanañjānisuttaṃ

7. The Dhanañjāni Sutta

445. Evaṃ [T 2.0623][V 2.0402] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe. Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā sāriputto dakkhiṇāgirismiṃ cārikaṃ carati mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ. Atha kho aññataro bhikkhu [P 2.0185] rājagahe vassaṃvuṭṭho vassaṃvuttho (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) yena dakkhiṇāgiri yenāyasmā sāriputto tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmatā sāriputtena saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho taṃ bhikkhuṃ āyasmā sāriputto etadavoca – “kaccāvuso, bhagavā arogo ca balavā cā”ti? “Arogo cāvuso, bhagavā balavā cā”ti. “Kacci panāvuso, bhikkhusaṅgho arogo ca balavā cā”ti? “Bhikkhusaṅghopi kho, āvuso, arogo ca balavā cā”ti. “Ettha, āvuso, taṇḍulapālidvārāya dhanañjāni dhānañjāni (sī. pī.) nāma brāhmaṇo atthi. Kaccāvuso[M 2.0396], dhanañjāni brāhmaṇo arogo ca balavā cā”ti? “Dhanañjānipi kho, āvuso, brāhmaṇo arogo ca balavā cā”ti. “Kacci panāvuso, dhanañjāni brāhmaṇo appamatto”ti? “Kuto panāvuso, dhanañjānissa brāhmaṇassa appamādo? Dhanañjāni, āvuso, brāhmaṇo rājānaṃ nissāya brāhmaṇagahapatike vilumpati, brāhmaṇagahapatike nissāya rājānaṃ vilumpati[T 2.0624]. Yāpissa bhariyā saddhā saddhakulā ānītā sāpi kālaṅkatā; aññāssa bhariyā assaddhā assaddhakulā ānītā”. “Dussutaṃ vatāvuso, assumha, dussutaṃ vatāvuso, assumha; ye mayaṃ dhanañjāniṃ brāhmaṇaṃ pamattaṃ assumha. Appeva ca nāma mayaṃ kadāci karahaci dhanañjāninā brāhmaṇena saddhiṃ samāgaccheyyāma, appeva nāma siyā kocideva kathāsallāpo”ti?

445. Thus have I heard: At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrel Sanctuary. Now at that time, the Venerable Sāriputta was wandering in the Southern Hills with a large Saṅgha of monks. Then a certain monk who had spent the rains in Rājagaha approached the Southern Hills, where the Venerable Sāriputta was. Having approached, he exchanged greetings with the Venerable Sāriputta. When the courteous and amiable talk was finished, he sat down to one side. Sitting to one side, the Venerable Sāriputta said to that monk: "I hope, friend, the Blessed One is free from illness and strong?" "The Blessed One is free from illness and strong, friend." "I hope the Saṅgha of monks is also free from illness and strong?" "The Saṅgha of monks is also free from illness and strong, friend." "Here, friend, near the Taṇḍulapāli gate there is a brahmin named Dhanañjāni. I hope, friend, the brahmin Dhanañjāni is free from illness and strong?" "The brahmin Dhanañjāni is also free from illness and strong, friend." "But I hope, friend, the brahmin Dhanañjāni is heedful?" "How could the brahmin Dhanañjāni be heedful, friend? The brahmin Dhanañjāni, relying on the king, robs the brahmin householders; relying on the brahmin householders, he robs the king. His wife, who was faithful and came from a faithful family, has passed away; another wife, who is faithless and comes from a faithless family, has been brought in." "Truly, friend, what we have heard is ill-heard! Truly, friend, what we have heard is ill-heard, in that we have heard that the brahmin Dhanañjāni is heedless. Perhaps someday we might meet with the brahmin Dhanañjāni; perhaps there might be some conversation."

446. Atha kho āyasmā sāriputto dakkhiṇāgirismiṃ yathābhirantaṃ viharitvā yena rājagahaṃ tena cārikaṃ pakkāmi. Anupubbena cārikaṃ caramāno yena rājagahaṃ tadavasari. Tatra sudaṃ āyasmā sāriputto rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe. Atha kho āyasmā sāriputto pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya rājagahaṃ piṇḍāya pāvisi[P 2.0186]. Tena kho pana samayena dhanañjāni brāhmaṇo bahinagare gāvo goṭṭhe duhāpeti. Atha kho āyasmā sāriputto [V 2.0403] rājagahe piṇḍāya caritvā pacchābhattaṃ piṇḍapātapaṭikkanto yena dhanañjāni brāhmaṇo tenupasaṅkami. Addasā kho dhanañjāni brāhmaṇo āyasmantaṃ sāriputtaṃ dūratova āgacchantaṃ. Disvāna yenāyasmā sāriputto tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ sāriputtaṃ etadavoca – “ito, bho sāriputta, payo, pīyataṃ tāva bhattassa kālo bhavissatī”ti. “Alaṃ, brāhmaṇa. Kataṃ me ajja bhattakiccaṃ. Amukasmiṃ me rukkhamūle divāvihāro bhavissati. Tattha āgaccheyyāsī”ti. “Evaṃ, bho”ti kho dhanañjāni [T 2.0625] brāhmaṇo āyasmato sāriputtassa paccassosi. Atha kho dhanañjāni brāhmaṇo pacchābhattaṃ bhuttapātarāso yenāyasmā sāriputto tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmatā sāriputtena saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho dhanañjāniṃ brāhmaṇaṃ āyasmā sāriputto etadavoca – “kaccāsi, dhanañjāni, appamatto”ti? “Kuto, bho sāriputta, amhākaṃ appamādo yesaṃ no mātāpitaro [M 2.0397] posetabbā, puttadāro posetabbo, dāsakammakarā posetabbā, mittāmaccānaṃ mittāmaccakaraṇīyaṃ kātabbaṃ, ñātisālohitānaṃ ñātisālohitakaraṇīyaṃ kātabbaṃ, atithīnaṃ atithikaraṇīyaṃ kātabbaṃ, pubbapetānaṃ pubbapetakaraṇīyaṃ kātabbaṃ, devatānaṃ devatākaraṇīyaṃ kātabbaṃ, rañño rājakaraṇīyaṃ kātabbaṃ, ayampi kāyo pīṇetabbo brūhetabbo”ti?

446. Then the Venerable Sāriputta, having stayed in the Southern Hills as long as he pleased, set out on a journey to Rājagaha. Traveling stage by stage, he arrived at Rājagaha. There the Venerable Sāriputta stayed in Rājagaha, at the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrels' Sanctuary. Then the Venerable Sāriputta, having dressed in the morning, took his bowl and robe and entered Rājagaha for alms. Now at that time the brahmin Dhanañjāni was having cows milked in a cow pen outside the city. Then the Venerable Sāriputta, having walked for alms in Rājagaha, after the meal, on his return from the alms round, approached the brahmin Dhanañjāni. The brahmin Dhanañjāni saw the Venerable Sāriputta coming from afar. Seeing him, he approached the Venerable Sāriputta and said: "Here, Master Sāriputta, drink some milk. It will soon be time for the meal." "Enough, brahmin. My meal for today is done. I will spend the day at the foot of a certain tree. You may come there." "Very well, Master." Thus the brahmin Dhanañjāni assented to the Venerable Sāriputta. Then the brahmin Dhanañjāni, after his breakfast, approached the Venerable Sāriputta. Having approached, he exchanged greetings with the Venerable Sāriputta. When the courteous and amiable talk was over, he sat down to one side. Sitting to one side, the Venerable Sāriputta said to the brahmin Dhanañjāni: "I hope, Dhanañjāni, you are heedful?" "How, Master Sāriputta, can we be heedful? We must support our parents, support our wives and children, support our servants and workers, do our duties to friends and companions, do our duties to relatives, do our duties to guests, do our duties to the departed, do our duties to the deities, do our duties to the king, and this body must be nourished and strengthened."

447. “Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, dhanañjāni, idhekacco mātāpitūnaṃ hetu adhammacārī visamacārī assa, tamenaṃ adhammacariyāvisamacariyāhetu nirayaṃ nirayapālā upakaḍḍheyyuṃ. Labheyya nu kho so ‘ahaṃ kho mātāpitūnaṃ hetu adhammacārī visamacārī ahosiṃ, mā maṃ nirayaṃ nirayapālā’ti[P 2.0187], mātāpitaro vā panassa labheyyuṃ ‘eso kho amhākaṃ hetu adhammacārī visamacārī ahosi, mā naṃ nirayaṃ nirayapālā’”ti? “No hidaṃ, bho sāriputta. Atha kho naṃ vikkandantaṃyeva niraye [T 2.0626] nirayapālā pakkhipeyyuṃ”.

447. “What do you think of this, Dhanañjāni? Suppose a certain person here, for the sake of his parents, were to be one of unrighteous conduct and wrong conduct. On account of that unrighteous and wrong conduct, the hell-wardens might drag him to hell. Would he indeed obtain his wish by saying: ‘Indeed, for the sake of my parents, I was of unrighteous conduct and wrong conduct. May the hell-wardens not drag me to hell!’? Or, on the other hand, would his parents obtain their wish by saying: ‘Indeed, for our sake, this one was of unrighteous conduct and wrong conduct. May the hell-wardens not drag him to hell!’?” “No, indeed, venerable Sāriputta. But rather, the hell-wardens would throw him, even while he is wailing, into hell.”

“Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, dhanañjāni, idhekacco puttadārassa hetu adhammacārī visamacārī assa, tamenaṃ adhammacariyāvisamacariyāhetu nirayaṃ nirayapālā upakaḍḍheyyuṃ. Labheyya nu kho so ‘ahaṃ kho puttadārassa hetu adhammacārī visamacārī ahosiṃ, mā maṃ nirayaṃ nirayapālā’ti, puttadāro vā panassa labheyya ‘eso kho amhākaṃ hetu adhammacārī visamacārī [V 2.0404] ahosi mā naṃ nirayaṃ nirayapālā’”ti? “No hidaṃ, bho sāriputta. Atha kho naṃ vikkandantaṃyeva niraye nirayapālā pakkhipeyyuṃ”.

“What do you think of this, Dhanañjāni? Suppose a certain person here, for the sake of his wife and children, were to be one of unrighteous conduct and wrong conduct. On account of that unrighteous and wrong conduct, the hell-wardens might drag him to hell. Would he indeed obtain his wish by saying: ‘Indeed, for the sake of my wife and children, I was of unrighteous conduct and wrong conduct. May the hell-wardens not drag me to hell!’? Or, on the other hand, would his wife and children obtain their wish by saying: ‘Indeed, for our sake, this one was of unrighteous conduct and wrong conduct. May the hell-wardens not drag him to hell!’?” “No, indeed, venerable Sāriputta. But rather, the hell-wardens would throw him, even while he is wailing, into hell.”

“Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, dhanañjāni, idhekacco dāsakammakaraporisassa hetu adhammacārī visamacārī assa, tamenaṃ adhammacariyāvisamacariyāhetu nirayaṃ nirayapālā upakaḍḍheyyuṃ. Labheyya nu kho so ‘ahaṃ kho dāsakammakaraporisassa hetu adhammacārī visamacārī ahosiṃ, mā maṃ nirayaṃ nirayapālā’ti, dāsakammakaraporisā vā panassa labheyyuṃ ‘eso kho amhākaṃ hetu adhammacārī visamacārī ahosi, mā naṃ nirayaṃ nirayapālā’”ti? “No hidaṃ, bho sāriputta. Atha kho naṃ vikkandantaṃyeva niraye nirayapālā pakkhipeyyuṃ”.

“What do you think of this, Dhanañjāni? Suppose a certain person here, for the sake of his slaves, workers, and servants, were to be one of unrighteous conduct and wrong conduct. On account of that unrighteous and wrong conduct, the hell-wardens might drag him to hell. Would he indeed obtain his wish by saying: ‘Indeed, for the sake of my slaves, workers, and servants, I was of unrighteous conduct and wrong conduct. May the hell-wardens not drag me to hell!’? Or, on the other hand, would his slaves, workers, and servants obtain their wish by saying: ‘Indeed, for our sake, this one was of unrighteous conduct and wrong conduct. May the hell-wardens not drag him to hell!’?” “No, indeed, venerable Sāriputta. But rather, the hell-wardens would throw him, even while he is wailing, into hell.”

“Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, dhanañjāni, idhekacco mittāmaccānaṃ hetu adhammacārī visamacārī assa, tamenaṃ adhammacariyāvisamacariyāhetu nirayaṃ [M 2.0398] nirayapālā upakaḍḍheyyuṃ. Labheyya nu kho so ‘ahaṃ kho mittāmaccānaṃ [T 2.0627] hetu adhammacārī visamacārī ahosiṃ, mā maṃ nirayaṃ nirayapālā’ti, mittāmaccā vā panassa labheyyuṃ ‘eso kho amhākaṃ hetu adhammacārī visamacārī ahosi, mā naṃ nirayaṃ nirayapālā’”ti? “No hidaṃ, bho sāriputta. Atha kho naṃ vikkandantaṃyeva niraye nirayapālā pakkhipeyyuṃ”.

“What do you think of this, Dhanañjāni? Suppose a certain person here, for the sake of his friends and associates, were to be one of unrighteous conduct and wrong conduct. On account of that unrighteous and wrong conduct, the hell-wardens might drag him to hell. Would he indeed obtain his wish by saying: ‘Indeed, for the sake of my friends and associates, I was of unrighteous conduct and wrong conduct. May the hell-wardens not drag me to hell!’? Or, on the other hand, would his friends and associates obtain their wish by saying: ‘Indeed, for our sake, this one was of unrighteous conduct and wrong conduct. May the hell-wardens not drag him to hell!’?” “No, indeed, venerable Sāriputta. But rather, the hell-wardens would throw him, even while he is wailing, into hell.”

“Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, dhanañjāni, idhekacco ñātisālohitānaṃ hetu adhammacārī visamacārī assa, tamenaṃ adhammacariyāvisamacariyāhetu nirayaṃ nirayapālā upakaḍḍheyyuṃ. Labheyya nu kho so ‘ahaṃ kho ñātisālohitānaṃ hetu adhammacārī visamacārī ahosiṃ, mā maṃ nirayaṃ nirayapālā’ti, ñātisālohitā vā panassa labheyyuṃ ‘eso kho amhākaṃ hetu adhammacārī visamacārī ahosi, mā naṃ nirayaṃ nirayapālā’”ti? “No hidaṃ, bho sāriputta. Atha kho naṃ vikkandantaṃyeva niraye nirayapālā pakkhipeyyuṃ”.

“What do you think of this, Dhanañjāni? Suppose a certain person here, for the sake of his relatives and kinsmen, were to be one of unrighteous conduct and wrong conduct. On account of that unrighteous and wrong conduct, the hell-wardens might drag him to hell. Would he indeed obtain his wish by saying: ‘Indeed, for the sake of my relatives and kinsmen, I was of unrighteous conduct and wrong conduct. May the hell-wardens not drag me to hell!’? Or, on the other hand, would his relatives and kinsmen obtain their wish by saying: ‘Indeed, for our sake, this one was of unrighteous conduct and wrong conduct. May the hell-wardens not drag him to hell!’?” “No, indeed, venerable Sāriputta. But rather, the hell-wardens would throw him, even while he is wailing, into hell.”

“Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, dhanañjāni, idhekacco atithīnaṃ hetu adhammacārī visamacārī assa, tamenaṃ adhammacariyāvisamacariyāhetu nirayaṃ nirayapālā upakaḍḍheyyuṃ. Labheyya nu kho so ‘ahaṃ kho atithīnaṃ hetu adhammacārī visamacārī ahosiṃ, mā maṃ nirayaṃ nirayapālā’ti, atithī vā panassa labheyyuṃ ‘eso kho amhākaṃ hetu adhammacārī visamacārī ahosi, mā naṃ nirayaṃ nirayapālā’”ti? “No hidaṃ, bho sāriputta. Atha kho naṃ vikkandantaṃyeva niraye nirayapālā pakkhipeyyuṃ”.

“What do you think of this, Dhanañjāni? Suppose a certain person here, for the sake of his guests, were to be one of unrighteous conduct and wrong conduct. On account of that unrighteous and wrong conduct, the hell-wardens might drag him to hell. Would he indeed obtain his wish by saying: ‘Indeed, for the sake of my guests, I was of unrighteous conduct and wrong conduct. May the hell-wardens not drag me to hell!’? Or, on the other hand, would his guests obtain their wish by saying: ‘Indeed, for our sake, this one was of unrighteous conduct and wrong conduct. May the hell-wardens not drag him to hell!’?” “No, indeed, venerable Sāriputta. But rather, the hell-wardens would throw him, even while he is wailing, into hell.”

“Taṃ [T 2.0628][V 2.0405][P 2.0188] kiṃ maññasi, dhanañjāni, idhekacco pubbapetānaṃ hetu adhammacārī visamacārī assa, tamenaṃ adhammacariyāvisamacariyāhetu nirayaṃ nirayapālā upakaḍḍheyyuṃ. Labheyya nu kho so ‘ahaṃ kho pubbapetānaṃ hetu adhammacārī visamacārī ahosiṃ, mā maṃ nirayaṃ nirayapālā’ti, pubbapetā vā panassa labheyyuṃ ‘eso kho amhākaṃ hetu adhammacārī visamacārī ahosi, mā naṃ nirayaṃ nirayapālā’”ti? “No hidaṃ, bho sāriputta. Atha kho naṃ vikkandantaṃyeva niraye nirayapālā pakkhipeyyuṃ”.

“What do you think of this, Dhanañjāni? Suppose a certain person here, for the sake of his departed ancestors, were to be one of unrighteous conduct and wrong conduct. On account of that unrighteous and wrong conduct, the hell-wardens might drag him to hell. Would he indeed obtain his wish by saying: ‘Indeed, for the sake of my departed ancestors, I was of unrighteous conduct and wrong conduct. May the hell-wardens not drag me to hell!’? Or, on the other hand, would his departed ancestors obtain their wish by saying: ‘Indeed, for our sake, this one was of unrighteous conduct and wrong conduct. May the hell-wardens not drag him to hell!’?” “No, indeed, venerable Sāriputta. But rather, the hell-wardens would throw him, even while he is wailing, into hell.”

“Taṃ [M 2.0399] kiṃ maññasi, dhanañjāni, idhekacco devatānaṃ hetu adhammacārī visamacārī assa, tamenaṃ adhammacariyāvisamacariyāhetu nirayaṃ nirayapālā upakaḍḍheyyuṃ. Labheyya nu kho so ‘ahaṃ kho devatānaṃ hetu adhammacārī visamacārī ahosiṃ, mā maṃ nirayaṃ nirayapālā’ti, devatā vā panassa labheyyuṃ ‘eso kho amhākaṃ hetu adhammacārī visamacārī ahosi, mā naṃ nirayaṃ nirayapālā’”ti? “No hidaṃ, bho sāriputta. Atha kho naṃ vikkandantaṃyeva niraye nirayapālā pakkhipeyyuṃ”.

“What do you think of this, Dhanañjāni? Suppose a certain person here, for the sake of the devas, were to be one of unrighteous conduct and wrong conduct. On account of that unrighteous and wrong conduct, the hell-wardens might drag him to hell. Would he indeed obtain his wish by saying: ‘Indeed, for the sake of the devas, I was of unrighteous conduct and wrong conduct. May the hell-wardens not drag me to hell!’? Or, on the other hand, would the devas obtain their wish by saying: ‘Indeed, for our sake, this one was of unrighteous conduct and wrong conduct. May the hell-wardens not drag him to hell!’?” “No, indeed, venerable Sāriputta. But rather, the hell-wardens would throw him, even while he is wailing, into hell.”

“Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, dhanañjāni, idhekacco rañño hetu adhammacārī visamacārī assa, tamenaṃ adhammacariyāvisamacariyāhetu nirayaṃ nirayapālā upakaḍḍheyyuṃ. Labheyya nu kho so ‘ahaṃ kho rañño hetu adhammacārī visamacārī ahosiṃ, mā maṃ nirayaṃ nirayapālā’ti, rājā [T 2.0629] vā panassa labheyya ‘eso kho amhākaṃ hetu adhammacārī visamacārī ahosi, mā naṃ nirayaṃ nirayapālā’”ti? “No hidaṃ, bho sāriputta. Atha kho naṃ vikkandantaṃyeva niraye nirayapālā pakkhipeyyuṃ”.

“What do you think of this, Dhanañjāni? Here, a certain person might, for the sake of a king, be one who practices unrighteously, who practices wrongly. On account of that unrighteous and wrong practice, the hell-wardens might drag him to hell. Would that person indeed obtain his wish by saying: ‘I was one who practiced unrighteously, who practiced wrongly for the sake of a king. May the hell-wardens not drag me to hell’? Or, on the other hand, would the king obtain this for him by saying: ‘This person was one who practiced unrighteously, who practiced wrongly for our sake. May the hell-wardens not drag him to hell’?” “This is not so, Venerable Sāriputta. But rather, the hell-wardens would cast him, while he is wailing, into hell.”

“Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, dhanañjāni, idhekacco kāyassa pīṇanāhetu brūhanāhetu adhammacārī visamacārī assa, tamenaṃ adhammacariyāvisamacariyāhetu nirayaṃ nirayapālā upakaḍḍheyyuṃ. Labheyya nu kho so ‘ahaṃ kho kāyassa pīṇanāhetu brūhanāhetu adhammacārī visamacārī ahosiṃ, mā maṃ nirayaṃ nirayapālā’ti, pare vā panassa labheyyuṃ ‘eso kho kāyassa pīṇanāhetu brūhanāhetu adhammacārī visamacārī ahosi, mā naṃ nirayaṃ nirayapālā’”ti? “No hidaṃ, bho sāriputta. Atha kho naṃ vikkandantaṃyeva niraye nirayapālā pakkhipeyyuṃ”.

“What do you think of this, Dhanañjāni? Here, a certain person might, for the sake of nourishing and developing the body, be one who practices unrighteously, who practices wrongly. On account of that unrighteous and wrong practice, the hell-wardens might drag him to hell. Would that person indeed obtain his wish by saying: ‘I was one who practiced unrighteously, who practiced wrongly for the sake of nourishing and developing the body. May the hell-wardens not drag me to hell’? Or, on the other hand, would others obtain this for him by saying: ‘This person was one who practiced unrighteously, who practiced wrongly for the sake of nourishing and developing the body. May the hell-wardens not drag him to hell’?” “This is not so, Venerable Sāriputta. But rather, the hell-wardens would cast him, while he is wailing, into hell.”

448. “Taṃ [V 2.0406] kiṃ maññasi, dhanañjāni, yo vā mātāpitūnaṃ hetu adhammacārī visamacārī assa, yo vā mātāpitūnaṃ hetu dhammacārī samacārī assa; katamaṃ seyyo”ti? “Yo hi, bho sāriputta, mātāpitūnaṃ hetu adhammacārī visamacārī assa, na taṃ seyyo; yo ca kho, bho sāriputta, mātāpitūnaṃ hetu dhammacārī samacārī assa, tadevettha seyyo. Adhammacariyāvisamacariyāhi, bho sāriputta, dhammacariyāsamacariyā seyyo”ti. “Atthi kho, dhanañjāni, aññesaṃ hetukā dhammikā [M 2.0400] kammantā, yehi sakkā mātāpitaro ceva posetuṃ, na ca pāpakammaṃ kātuṃ, puññañca paṭipadaṃ paṭipajjituṃ.

448. “What do you think of this, Dhanañjāni? Between one who, for the sake of his parents, might be a person who practices unrighteously and wrongly, and one who, for the sake of his parents, might be a person who practices righteously and evenly—which is better?” “Indeed, Venerable Sāriputta, the one who for the sake of his parents practices unrighteously and wrongly is not the better one; but, Venerable Sāriputta, the one who for the sake of his parents practices righteously and evenly—that very one is better. Righteous practice and even practice, Venerable Sāriputta, are better than unrighteous practice and wrong practice.” “There are indeed, Dhanañjāni, other righteous and well-founded occupations, by which it is possible to support one’s parents, and not to do an evil deed, and to undertake a meritorious course of practice.”

“Taṃ [T 2.0630] kiṃ maññasi, dhanañjāni, yo vā puttadārassa hetu adhammacārī visamacārī assa, yo vā puttadārassa hetu dhammacārī samacārī assa; katamaṃ seyyo”ti? “Yo [P 2.0189] hi, bho sāriputta, puttadārassa hetu adhammacārī visamacārī assa, na taṃ seyyo; yo ca kho, bho sāriputta, puttadārassa hetu dhammacārī samacārī assa, tadevettha seyyo. Adhammacariyāvisamacariyāhi, bho sāriputta, dhammacariyāsamacariyā seyyo”ti. “Atthi kho, dhanañjāni, aññesaṃ hetukā dhammikā kammantā yehi sakkā puttadārañceva posetuṃ, na ca pāpakammaṃ kātuṃ, puññañca paṭipadaṃ paṭipajjituṃ.

“What do you think of this, Dhanañjāni? Between one who, for the sake of his wife and children, might be a person who practices unrighteously and wrongly, and one who, for the sake of his wife and children, might be a person who practices righteously and evenly—which is better?” “Indeed, Venerable Sāriputta, the one who for the sake of his wife and children practices unrighteously and wrongly is not the better one; but, Venerable Sāriputta, the one who for the sake of his wife and children practices righteously and evenly—that very one is better. Righteous practice and even practice, Venerable Sāriputta, are better than unrighteous practice and wrong practice.” “There are indeed, Dhanañjāni, other righteous and well-founded occupations, by which it is possible to support one’s wife and children, and not to do an evil deed, and to undertake a meritorious course of practice.”

“Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, dhanañjāni, yo vā dāsakammakaraporisassa hetu adhammacārī visamacārī assa, yo vā dāsakammakaraporisassa hetu dhammacārī samacārī assa; katamaṃ seyyo”ti? “Yo hi, bho sāriputta, dāsakammakaraporisassa hetu adhammacārī visamacārī assa, na taṃ seyyo; yo ca kho, bho sāriputta, dāsakammakaraporisassa hetu dhammacārī samacārī assa, tadevettha seyyo. Adhammacariyāvisamacariyāhi, bho sāriputta, dhammacariyāsamacariyā seyyo”ti. “Atthi kho, dhanañjāni, aññesaṃ hetukā dhammikā kammantā, yehi sakkā dāsakammakaraporise ceva posetuṃ, na ca pāpakammaṃ kātuṃ, puññañca paṭipadaṃ paṭipajjituṃ.

“What do you think of this, Dhanañjāni? Between one who, for the sake of his slaves, workers, and servants, might be a person who practices unrighteously and wrongly, and one who, for the sake of his slaves, workers, and servants, might be a person who practices righteously and evenly—which is better?” “Indeed, Venerable Sāriputta, the one who for the sake of his slaves, workers, and servants practices unrighteously and wrongly is not the better one; but, Venerable Sāriputta, the one who for the sake of his slaves, workers, and servants practices righteously and evenly—that very one is better. Righteous practice and even practice, Venerable Sāriputta, are better than unrighteous practice and wrong practice.” “There are indeed, Dhanañjāni, other righteous and well-founded occupations, by which it is possible to support one’s slaves, workers, and servants, and not to do an evil deed, and to undertake a meritorious course of practice.”

“Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, dhanañjāni, yo vā mittāmaccānaṃ hetu [T 2.0631] adhammacārī visamacārī assa, yo vā mittāmaccānaṃ hetu dhammacārī samacārī assa; katamaṃ seyyo”ti? “Yo hi[V 2.0407], bho sāriputta, mittāmaccānaṃ hetu adhammacārī visamacārī assa, na taṃ seyyo; yo ca kho, bho sāriputta, mittāmaccānaṃ hetu dhammacārī samacārī assa, tadevettha seyyo. Adhammacariyāvisamacariyāhi, bho sāriputta, dhammacariyāsamacariyā seyyo”ti. “Atthi kho, dhanañjāni, aññesaṃ hetukā dhammikā kammantā, yehi sakkā mittāmaccānañceva mittāmaccakaraṇīyaṃ kātuṃ, na ca pāpakammaṃ kātuṃ, puññañca paṭipadaṃ paṭipajjituṃ.

“What do you think of this, Dhanañjāni? Between one who, for the sake of his friends and companions, might be a person who practices unrighteously and wrongly, and one who, for the sake of his friends and companions, might be a person who practices righteously and evenly—which is better?” “Indeed, Venerable Sāriputta, the one who for the sake of his friends and companions practices unrighteously and wrongly is not the better one; but, Venerable Sāriputta, the one who for the sake of his friends and companions practices righteously and evenly—that very one is better. Righteous practice and even practice, Venerable Sāriputta, are better than unrighteous practice and wrong practice.” “There are indeed, Dhanañjāni, other righteous and well-founded occupations, by which it is possible to fulfill one’s duties to friends and companions, and not to do an evil deed, and to undertake a meritorious course of practice.”

“Taṃ [M 2.0401] kiṃ maññasi, dhanañjāni, yo vā ñātisālohitānaṃ hetu adhammacārī visamacārī assa, yo vā ñātisālohitānaṃ hetu dhammacārī samacārī assa; katamaṃ seyyo”ti? “Yo [P 2.0190] hi, bho sāriputta, ñātisālohitānaṃ hetu adhammacārī visamacārī assa, na taṃ seyyo; yo ca kho, bho sāriputta, ñātisālohitānaṃ hetu dhammacārī samacārī assa, tadevettha seyyo. Adhammacariyāvisamacariyāhi, bho sāriputta, dhammacariyāsamacariyā seyyo”ti. “Atthi kho, dhanañjāni, aññesaṃ hetukā dhammikā kammantā, yehi sakkā ñātisālohitānañceva ñātisālohitakaraṇīyaṃ kātuṃ, na ca pāpakammaṃ kātuṃ, puññañca paṭipadaṃ paṭipajjituṃ.

“What do you think of this, Dhanañjāni? Between one who, for the sake of his kinsmen and blood relatives, might be a person who practices unrighteously and wrongly, and one who, for the sake of his kinsmen and blood relatives, might be a person who practices righteously and evenly—which is better?” “Indeed, Venerable Sāriputta, the one who for the sake of his kinsmen and blood relatives practices unrighteously and wrongly is not the better one; but, Venerable Sāriputta, the one who for the sake of his kinsmen and blood relatives practices righteously and evenly—that very one is better. Righteous practice and even practice, Venerable Sāriputta, are better than unrighteous practice and wrong practice.” “There are indeed, Dhanañjāni, other righteous and well-founded occupations, by which it is possible to fulfill one’s duties to kinsmen and blood relatives, and not to do an evil deed, and to undertake a meritorious course of practice.”

“Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, dhanañjāni, yo vā atithīnaṃ hetu adhammacārī [T 2.0632] visamacārī assa, yo vā atithīnaṃ hetu dhammacārī samacārī assa; katamaṃ seyyo”ti? “Yo hi, bho sāriputta, atithīnaṃ hetu adhammacārī visamacārī assa, na taṃ seyyo; yo ca kho, bho sāriputta, atithīnaṃ hetu dhammacārī samacārī assa, tadevettha seyyo. Adhammacariyāvisamacariyāhi, bho sāriputta, dhammacariyāsamacariyā seyyo”ti. “Atthi kho, dhanañjāni, aññesaṃ hetukā dhammikā kammantā, yehi sakkā atithīnañceva atithikaraṇīyaṃ kātuṃ, na ca pāpakammaṃ kātuṃ, puññañca paṭipadaṃ paṭipajjituṃ.

“What do you think of this, Dhanañjāni? Suppose a person, for the sake of guests, were to be of unrighteous conduct and wrong conduct; or suppose a person, for the sake of guests, were to be of righteous conduct and right conduct. Which is superior?” “Venerable Sāriputta, if a person, for the sake of guests, were to be of unrighteous conduct and wrong conduct, that is not superior. But indeed, Venerable Sāriputta, if a person, for the sake of guests, were to be of righteous conduct and right conduct, that one is superior in this case. Venerable Sāriputta, righteous conduct and right conduct are superior to unrighteous conduct and wrong conduct.” “Indeed, Dhanañjāni, there are other righteous, well-founded undertakings by which it is possible to perform one's duties to guests, and not to do evil deeds, and to undertake a meritorious practice.”

“Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, dhanañjāni, yo vā pubbapetānaṃ hetu adhammacārī visamacārī assa, yo vā pubbapetānaṃ hetu dhammacārī samacārī assa; katamaṃ seyyo”ti? “Yo hi, bho sāriputta, pubbapetānaṃ hetu adhammacārī visamacārī assa, na taṃ seyyo; yo ca kho, bho sāriputta, pubbapetānaṃ hetu dhammacārī samacārī assa, tadevettha seyyo. Adhammacariyāvisamacariyāhi[V 2.0408], bho sāriputta, dhammacariyāsamacariyā seyyo”ti. “Atthi kho, dhanañjāni, aññesaṃ hetukā dhammikā kammantā, yehi sakkā pubbapetānañceva pubbapetakaraṇīyaṃ kātuṃ, na ca pāpakammaṃ kātuṃ, puññañca paṭipadaṃ paṭipajjituṃ.

“What do you think of this, Dhanañjāni? Suppose a person, for the sake of departed ancestors, were to be of unrighteous conduct and wrong conduct; or suppose a person, for the sake of departed ancestors, were to be of righteous conduct and right conduct. Which is superior?” “Venerable Sāriputta, if a person, for the sake of departed ancestors, were to be of unrighteous conduct and wrong conduct, that is not superior. But indeed, Venerable Sāriputta, if a person, for the sake of departed ancestors, were to be of righteous conduct and right conduct, that one is superior in this case. Venerable Sāriputta, righteous conduct and right conduct are superior to unrighteous conduct and wrong conduct.” “Indeed, Dhanañjāni, there are other righteous, well-founded undertakings by which it is possible to perform one's duties to departed ancestors, and not to do evil deeds, and to undertake a meritorious practice.”

“Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, dhanañjāni, yo vā devatānaṃ hetu adhammacārī visamacārī assa, yo vā devatānaṃ hetu dhammacārī samacārī [T 2.0633] assa; katamaṃ [M 2.0402] seyyo”ti? “Yo hi, bho sāriputta, devatānaṃ hetu adhammacārī visamacārī assa, na taṃ seyyo; yo ca kho, bho sāriputta, devatānaṃ hetu dhammacārī samacārī assa, tadevettha seyyo[P 2.0191]. Adhammacariyāvisamacariyāhi, bho sāriputta, dhammacariyāsamacariyā seyyo”ti. “Atthi kho, dhanañjāni, aññesaṃ hetukā dhammikā kammantā, yehi sakkā devatānañceva devatākaraṇīyaṃ kātuṃ, na ca pāpakammaṃ kātuṃ, puññañca paṭipadaṃ paṭipajjituṃ.

“What do you think of this, Dhanañjāni? Suppose a person, for the sake of deities, were to be of unrighteous conduct and wrong conduct; or suppose a person, for the sake of deities, were to be of righteous conduct and right conduct. Which is superior?” “Venerable Sāriputta, if a person, for the sake of deities, were to be of unrighteous conduct and wrong conduct, that is not superior. But indeed, Venerable Sāriputta, if a person, for the sake of deities, were to be of righteous conduct and right conduct, that one is superior in this case. Venerable Sāriputta, righteous conduct and right conduct are superior to unrighteous conduct and wrong conduct.” “Indeed, Dhanañjāni, there are other righteous, well-founded undertakings by which it is possible to perform one's duties to the deities, and not to do evil deeds, and to undertake a meritorious practice.”

“Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, dhanañjāni, yo vā rañño hetu adhammacārī visamacārī assa, yo vā rañño hetu dhammacārī samacārī assa; katamaṃ seyyo”ti? “Yo hi, bho sāriputta, rañño hetu adhammacārī visamacārī assa, na taṃ seyyo; yo ca kho, bho sāriputta, rañño hetu dhammacārī samacārī assa, tadevettha seyyo. Adhammacariyāvisamacariyāhi, bho sāriputta, dhammacariyāsamacariyā seyyo”ti. “Atthi kho, dhanañjāni, aññesaṃ hetukā dhammikā kammantā, yehi sakkā rañño ceva rājakaraṇīyaṃ kātuṃ, na ca pāpakammaṃ kātuṃ, puññañca paṭipadaṃ paṭipajjituṃ.

“What do you think of this, Dhanañjāni? Suppose a person, for the sake of the king, were to be of unrighteous conduct and wrong conduct; or suppose a person, for the sake of the king, were to be of righteous conduct and right conduct. Which is superior?” “Venerable Sāriputta, if a person, for the sake of the king, were to be of unrighteous conduct and wrong conduct, that is not superior. But indeed, Venerable Sāriputta, if a person, for the sake of the king, were to be of righteous conduct and right conduct, that one is superior in this case. Venerable Sāriputta, righteous conduct and right conduct are superior to unrighteous conduct and wrong conduct.” “Indeed, Dhanañjāni, there are other righteous, well-founded undertakings by which it is possible to perform one's duties to the king, and not to do evil deeds, and to undertake a meritorious practice.”

“Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, dhanañjāni, yo vā kāyassa pīṇanāhetu brūhanāhetu adhammacārī visamacārī assa, yo vā kāyassa pīṇanāhetu brūhanāhetu dhammacārī samacārī assa; katamaṃ seyyo”ti? “Yo hi, bho sāriputta, kāyassa pīṇanāhetu brūhanāhetu adhammacārī visamacārī [T 2.0634] assa, na taṃ seyyo; yo ca kho, bho sāriputta, kāyassa pīṇanāhetu brūhanāhetu dhammacārī samacārī assa, tadevettha seyyo. Adhammacariyāvisamacariyāhi, bho sāriputta, dhammacariyāsamacariyā seyyo”ti. “Atthi kho, dhanañjāni, aññesaṃ hetukā dhammikā kammantā[V 2.0409], yehi sakkā kāyañceva pīṇetuṃ brūhetuṃ, na ca pāpakammaṃ kātuṃ, puññañca paṭipadaṃ paṭipajjitu”nti.

“What do you think of this, Dhanañjāni? Suppose a person, for the sake of pleasing and developing the body, were to be of unrighteous conduct and wrong conduct; or suppose a person, for the sake of pleasing and developing the body, were to be of righteous conduct and right conduct. Which is superior?” “Venerable Sāriputta, if a person, for the sake of pleasing and developing the body, were to be of unrighteous conduct and wrong conduct, that is not superior. But indeed, Venerable Sāriputta, if a person, for the sake of pleasing and developing the body, were to be of righteous conduct and right conduct, that one is superior in this case. Venerable Sāriputta, righteous conduct and right conduct are superior to unrighteous conduct and wrong conduct.” “Indeed, Dhanañjāni, there are other righteous, well-founded undertakings by which it is possible to please and develop the body, and not to do evil deeds, and to undertake a meritorious practice.”

449. Atha kho dhanañjāni brāhmaṇo āyasmato sāriputtassa bhāsitaṃ abhinanditvā anumoditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkāmi. Atha kho dhanañjāni brāhmaṇo aparena samayena ābādhiko ahosi dukkhito bāḷhagilāno. Atha kho dhanañjāni brāhmaṇo aññataraṃ purisaṃ āmantesi [M 2.0403] – “ehi tvaṃ, ambho purisa[P 2.0192], yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkama; upasaṅkamitvā mama vacanena bhagavato pāde sirasā vandāhi – ‘dhanañjāni, bhante, brāhmaṇo ābādhiko dukkhito bāḷhagilāno. So bhagavato pāde sirasā vandatī’ti. Yena cāyasmā sāriputto tenupasaṅkama; upasaṅkamitvā mama vacanena āyasmato sāriputtassa pāde sirasā vandāhi – ‘dhanañjāni, bhante, brāhmaṇo ābādhiko dukkhito bāḷhagilāno. So āyasmato sāriputtassa pāde sirasā vandatī’ti. Evañca vadehi – ‘sādhu kira, bhante, āyasmā sāriputto yena dhanañjānissa brāhmaṇassa nivesanaṃ tenupasaṅkamatu anukampaṃ upādāyā’”ti. “Evaṃ[T 2.0635], bhante”ti kho so puriso dhanañjānissa brāhmaṇassa paṭissutvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho so puriso bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “dhanañjāni, bhante, brāhmaṇo ābādhiko dukkhito bāḷhagilāno. So bhagavato pāde sirasā vandatī”ti. Yena cāyasmā sāriputto tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ sāriputtaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho so puriso āyasmantaṃ sāriputtaṃ etadavoca – “dhanañjāni, bhante, brāhmaṇo ābādhiko dukkhito bāḷhagilāno. So āyasmato sāriputtassa pāde sirasā vandati, evañca vadeti – ‘sādhu kira, bhante, āyasmā sāriputto yena dhanañjānissa brāhmaṇassa nivesanaṃ tenupasaṅkamatu anukampaṃ upādāyā’”ti. Adhivāsesi kho āyasmā sāriputto tuṇhībhāvena.

449. Then the brahmin Dhanañjāni, having delighted in and rejoiced at the Venerable Sāriputta's words, rose from his seat and departed. Then, at another time, the brahmin Dhanañjānī became sick, afflicted with suffering, and gravely ill. Then the brahmin Dhanañjānī addressed a certain man: “Come, good man, go to where the Blessed One is. Having approached, pay homage with your head to the Blessed One’s feet with my words, saying: ‘Venerable Sir, the brahmin Dhanañjānī is sick, afflicted with suffering, and gravely ill. He pays homage with his head to the Blessed One’s feet.’ And go to where the Venerable Sāriputta is. Having approached, pay homage with your head to the Venerable Sāriputta’s feet with my words, saying: ‘Venerable Sir, the brahmin Dhanañjānī is sick, afflicted with suffering, and gravely ill. He pays homage with his head to the Venerable Sāriputta’s feet.’ And also say this: ‘It would be good, Venerable Sir, if the Venerable Sāriputta would approach the residence of the brahmin Dhanañjānī out of compassion.’” “So be it, sir,” that man replied to the brahmin Dhanañjānī, and he went to where the Blessed One was. Having approached and paid homage to the Blessed One, he sat down to one side. Seated to one side, that man said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable Sir, the brahmin Dhanañjāni is sick, afflicted with suffering, and gravely ill. He pays homage with his head to the Blessed One’s feet.” Then he went to where the Venerable Sāriputta was. Having approached and paid homage to the Venerable Sāriputta, he sat down to one side. Seated to one side, that man said this to the Venerable Sāriputta: “Venerable Sir, the brahmin Dhanañjānī is sick, afflicted with suffering, and gravely ill. He pays homage with his head to the Venerable Sāriputta’s feet, and he also says this: ‘It would be good, Venerable Sir, if the Venerable Sāriputta would approach the residence of the brahmin Dhanañjānī out of compassion.’” The Venerable Sāriputta consented by his silence.

450. Atha kho āyasmā sāriputto nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya yena dhanañjānissa brāhmaṇassa nivesanaṃ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi. Nisajja kho āyasmā sāriputto dhanañjāniṃ brāhmaṇaṃ etadavoca – “kacci te, dhanañjāni, khamanīyaṃ, kacci yāpanīyaṃ? Kacci dukkhā vedanā paṭikkamanti, no abhikkamanti? Paṭikkamosānaṃ paññāyati[V 2.0410], no abhikkamo”ti? “Na me, bho sāriputta, khamanīyaṃ na yāpanīyaṃ. Bāḷhā me dukkhā vedanā abhikkamanti, no paṭikkamanti. Abhikkamosānaṃ paññāyati, no paṭikkamo. Seyyathāpi, bho sāriputta[P 2.0193], balavā puriso tiṇhena sikharena muddhani muddhānaṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) abhimattheyya; evameva kho[M 2.0404], bho sāriputta, adhimattā vātā muddhani ca ūhananti. Na me, bho sāriputta, khamanīyaṃ, na yāpanīyaṃ. Bāḷhā me [T 2.0636] dukkhā vedanā abhikkamanti, no paṭikkamanti. Abhikkamosānaṃ paññāyati, no paṭikkamo. Seyyathāpi, bho sāriputta, balavā puriso daḷhena varattakkhaṇḍena varattabandhanena (sī. pī.) sīse sīsaveṭhaṃ dadeyya; evameva kho, bho sāriputta, adhimattā sīse sīsavedanā. Na me, bho sāriputta, khamanīyaṃ na yāpanīyaṃ. Bāḷhā me dukkhā vedanā abhikkamanti, no paṭikkamanti. Abhikkamosānaṃ paññāyati, no paṭikkamo. Seyyathāpi, bho sāriputta, dakkho goghātako vā goghātakantevāsī vā tiṇhena govikantanena kucchiṃ parikanteyya; evameva kho, bho sāriputta, adhimattā vātā kucchiṃ parikantanti. Na me, bho sāriputta, khamanīyaṃ, na yāpanīyaṃ. Bāḷhā me dukkhā vedanā abhikkamanti, no paṭikkamanti. Abhikkamosānaṃ paññāyati, no paṭikkamo. Seyyathāpi, bho sāriputta, dve balavanto purisā dubbalataraṃ purisaṃ nānābāhāsu gahetvā aṅgārakāsuyā santāpeyyuṃ samparitāpeyyuṃ; evameva kho, bho sāriputta, adhimatto kāyasmiṃ ḍāho. Na me, bho sāriputta, khamanīyaṃ na yāpanīyaṃ. Bāḷhā me dukkhā vedanā abhikkamanti, no paṭikkamanti. Abhikkamosānaṃ paññāyati[T 2.0637], no paṭikkamo”ti.

450. Then the Venerable Sāriputta, having adjusted his lower robe and taken his bowl and outer robe, went to the residence of the brahmin Dhanañjānī. Having gone there, he sat down on the prepared seat. Seated, the Venerable Sāriputta said this to the brahmin Dhanañjānī: “Are you bearing up, Dhanañjāni, are you managing? Are your painful feelings receding and not advancing? Is their receding apparent, and not their advancing?” “I am not bearing up, Venerable Sāriputta, I am not managing. My severe painful feelings are advancing, not receding. Their advancing is apparent, not their receding. Just as, Venerable Sāriputta, a strong man might crush one’s head with a sharp blade, so too, violent winds are pounding my head. I am not bearing up, Venerable Sāriputta, I am not managing. My severe painful feelings are advancing, not receding. Their advancing is apparent, not their receding. Just as, Venerable Sāriputta, a strong man might tie a tight leather strap around one’s head as a headband, so too, there are extreme headaches in my head. I am not bearing up, Venerable Sāriputta, I am not managing. My severe painful feelings are advancing, not receding. Their advancing is apparent, not their receding. Just as, Venerable Sāriputta, a skilled butcher or a butcher’s apprentice might slice up one’s belly with a sharp butcher’s knife, so too, violent winds are slicing up my belly. I am not bearing up, Venerable Sāriputta, I am not managing. My severe painful feelings are advancing, not receding. Their advancing is apparent, not their receding. Just as, Venerable Sāriputta, two strong men might seize a weaker man by his arms and heat and scorch him over a pit of coals, so too, there is an extreme burning in my body. I am not bearing up, Venerable Sāriputta, I am not managing. My severe painful feelings are advancing, not receding. Their advancing is apparent, not their receding.”

451. “Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, dhanañjāni, katamaṃ seyyo – nirayo vā tiracchānayoni vā”ti? “Nirayā, bho sāriputta, tiracchānayoni seyyo”ti. “Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, dhanañjāni, katamaṃ seyyo – tiracchānayoni vā pettivisayo vā”ti? “Tiracchānayoniyā, bho sāriputta, pettivisayo seyyo”ti. “Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, dhanañjāni, katamaṃ seyyo – pettivisayo vā manussā vā”ti? “Pettivisayā, bho sāriputta, manussā seyyo”ti. “Taṃ [P 2.0194] kiṃ maññasi, dhanañjāni[V 2.0411], katamaṃ seyyo – manussā vā cātumahārājikā cātummahārājikā (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) vā devā”ti? “Manussehi[M 2.0405], bho sāriputta, cātumahārājikā devā seyyo”ti. “Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, dhanañjāni, katamaṃ seyyo – cātumahārājikā vā devā tāvatiṃsā vā devā”ti? “Cātumahārājikehi, bho sāriputta, devehi tāvatiṃsā devā seyyo”ti. “Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, dhanañjāni, katamaṃ seyyo – tāvatiṃsā vā devā yāmā vā devā”ti? “Tāvatiṃsehi, bho sāriputta, devehi yāmā devā seyyo”ti. “Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, dhanañjāni, katamaṃ seyyo – yāmā vā devā tusitā vā devā”ti? “Yāmehi, bho sāriputta, devehi tusitā devā seyyo”ti. “Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, dhanañjāni, katamaṃ seyyo – tusitā vā devā nimmānaratī vā devā”ti? “Tusitehi, bho sāriputta, devehi nimmānaratī devā seyyo”ti. “Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, dhanañjāni, katamaṃ seyyo – nimmānaratī vā devā paranimmitavasavattī vā devā”ti? “Nimmānaratīhi[T 2.0638], bho sāriputta, devehi paranimmitavasavattī devā seyyo”ti. “Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, dhanañjāni, katamaṃ seyyo paranimmitavasavattī vā devā brahmaloko vā”ti? “‘Brahmaloko’ti bhavaṃ sāriputto āhāti, katamaṃ sāriputto āha brahmalokoti. (ka.) – bhavaṃ sāriputto āha; ‘brahmaloko’ti – bhavaṃ sāriputto āhā”ti bhavaṃ sāriputto āhāti, katamaṃ sāriputto āha brahmalokoti. (ka.).

451. “What do you think, Dhanañjāni, which is better—hell or the animal realm?” “Venerable Sāriputta, the animal realm is better than hell.” “What do you think, Dhanañjāni, which is better—the animal realm or the realm of ghosts?” “Venerable Sāriputta, the realm of ghosts is better than the animal realm.” “What do you think, Dhanañjāni, which is better—the realm of ghosts or humans?” “Venerable Sāriputta, humans are better than the realm of ghosts.” “What do you think, Dhanañjāni, which is better—humans or the gods of the Four Great Kings?” “Venerable Sāriputta, the gods of the Four Great Kings are better than humans.” “What do you think, Dhanañjāni, which is better—the gods of the Four Great Kings or the Tāvatiṃsa gods?” “Venerable Sāriputta, the Tāvatiṃsa gods are better than the gods of the Four Great Kings.” “What do you think, Dhanañjāni, which is better—the Tāvatiṃsa gods or the Yāma gods?” “Venerable Sāriputta, the Yāma gods are better than the Tāvatiṃsa gods.” “What do you think, Dhanañjāni, which is better—the Yāma gods or the Tusita gods?” “Venerable Sāriputta, the Tusita gods are better than the Yāma gods.” “What do you think, Dhanañjāni, which is better—the Tusita gods or the Nimmānaratī gods?” “Venerable Sāriputta, the Nimmānaratī gods are better than the Tusita gods.” “What do you think, Dhanañjāni, which is better—the Nimmānaratī gods or the Paranimmitavasavattī gods?” “Venerable Sāriputta, the Paranimmitavasavattī gods are better than the Nimmānaratī gods.” “What do you think, Dhanañjāni, which is better—the Paranimmitavasavattī gods or the Brahmā world?” “The Venerable Sāriputta says, ‘the Brahmā world’; the Venerable Sāriputta says, ‘the Brahmā world.’”

Atha kho āyasmato sāriputtassa etadahosi – “ime kho brāhmaṇā brahmalokādhimuttā. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ dhanañjānissa brāhmaṇassa brahmānaṃ sahabyatāya maggaṃ deseyya”nti. “Brahmānaṃ te, dhanañjāni, sahabyatāya maggaṃ desessāmi; taṃ suṇāhi, sādhukaṃ manasi karohi, bhāsissāmī”ti. “Evaṃ, bho”ti kho dhanañjāni brāhmaṇo āyasmato sāriputtassa paccassosi. Āyasmā [P 2.0195] sāriputto etadavoca – “katamo ca, dhanañjāni, brahmānaṃ sahabyatāya maggo? Idha, dhanañjāni, bhikkhu mettāsahagatena cetasā ekaṃ disaṃ pharitvā viharati, tathā dutiyaṃ, tathā tatiyaṃ, tathā catutthaṃ; iti uddhamadho tiriyaṃ sabbadhi sabbattatāya sabbāvantaṃ lokaṃ mettāsahagatena cetasā vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyābajjhena pharitvā viharati. Ayaṃ kho, dhanañjāni, brahmānaṃ sahabyatāya maggo”.

Then this thought occurred to the Venerable Sāriputta: “Indeed, these brahmins are inclined towards the Brahmā world. It would be good if I were to teach the brahmin Dhanañjāni the path to companionship with the Brahmās.” “Dhanañjāni, I will teach you the path to companionship with the Brahmās. Listen to it, pay proper attention, I shall speak.” “Yes, venerable sir,” the brahmin Dhanañjāni replied to the Venerable Sāriputta. The Venerable Sāriputta said this: “And what, Dhanañjāni, is the path to companionship with the Brahmās? Here, Dhanañjāni, a bhikkhu dwells pervading one direction with a mind accompanied by loving-kindness, likewise the second, likewise the third, likewise the fourth. Thus above, below, and across, everywhere, for all, he dwells pervading the entire world with a mind accompanied by loving-kindness that is expansive, exalted, immeasurable, without enmity, and without affliction. This, indeed, Dhanañjāni, is the path to companionship with the Brahmās.”

452. “Puna caparaṃ, dhanañjāni, bhikkhu karuṇāsahagatena cetasā…pe… muditāsahagatena cetasā… upekkhāsahagatena cetasā ekaṃ disaṃ pharitvā viharati, tathā dutiyaṃ, tathā tatiyaṃ, tathā catutthaṃ; iti uddhamadho tiriyaṃ sabbadhi sabbattatāya sabbāvantaṃ lokaṃ [T 2.0639] upekkhāsahagatena cetasā vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyābajjhena pharitvā viharati. Ayaṃ kho, dhanañjāni, brahmānaṃ sahabyatāya maggo”ti. Tena hi, bho sāriputta, mama vacanena bhagavato pāde sirasā vandāhi – ‘dhanañjāni[M 2.0406], bhante, brāhmaṇo ābādhiko [V 2.0412] dukkhito bāḷhagilāno. So bhagavato pāde sirasā vandatī’ti. Atha kho āyasmā sāriputto dhanañjāniṃ brāhmaṇaṃ sati uttarikaraṇīye hīne brahmaloke patiṭṭhāpetvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkāmi. Atha kho dhanañjāni brāhmaṇo acirapakkante āyasmante sāriputte kālamakāsi, brahmalokañca upapajji.

452. “Furthermore, Dhanañjāni, a bhikkhu dwells pervading one direction with a mind accompanied by compassion… with a mind accompanied by sympathetic joy… with a mind accompanied by equanimity, likewise the second, likewise the third, likewise the fourth. Thus above, below, and across, everywhere, for all, he dwells pervading the entire world with a mind accompanied by equanimity that is expansive, exalted, immeasurable, without enmity, and without affliction. This, indeed, Dhanañjāni, is the path to companionship with the Brahmās.” “In that case, Venerable Sāriputta, with my words, pay homage with your head to the feet of the Blessed One, saying: ‘Venerable sir, the brahmin Dhanañjāni is sick, afflicted with suffering, and gravely ill. He pays homage with his head to the feet of the Blessed One.’” Then the Venerable Sāriputta, having established the brahmin Dhanañjāni in the inferior Brahmā world while a further task remained to be done, rose from his seat and departed. Then, not long after the Venerable Sāriputta had departed, the brahmin Dhanañjāni died and was reborn in the Brahmā world.

453. Atha kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – “eso, bhikkhave, sāriputto dhanañjāniṃ brāhmaṇaṃ sati uttarikaraṇīye hīne brahmaloke patiṭṭhāpetvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkanto”ti. Atha kho āyasmā sāriputto yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi, ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā sāriputto bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “dhanañjāni, bhante, brāhmaṇo ābādhiko dukkhito bāḷhagilāno, so bhagavato pāde sirasā vandatī”ti. “Kiṃ pana tvaṃ sāriputta dhanañjāniṃ brāhmaṇaṃ sati [P 2.0196] uttarikaraṇīye hīne brahmaloke patiṭṭhāpetvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkanto”ti? “Mayhaṃ kho, bhante, evaṃ ahosi – ‘ime kho brāhmaṇā brahmalokādhimuttā, yaṃnūnāhaṃ dhanañjānissa brāhmaṇassa [T 2.0640] brahmānaṃ sahabyatāya maggaṃ deseyya’nti. “Kālaṅkatoca kālaṅkatova (syā. kaṃ. ka.), sāriputta, dhanañjāni brāhmaṇo, brahmalokañca upapanno”ti.

453. Then the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus, this Sāriputta, having established the brahmin Dhanañjāni in the inferior Brahmā world while a further task remained to be done, has risen from his seat and departed.” Then the Venerable Sāriputta approached the Blessed One, and having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the Venerable Sāriputta said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, the brahmin Dhanañjāni was sick, afflicted with suffering, and gravely ill. He pays homage with his head to the feet of the Blessed One.” “But why, Sāriputta, did you, having established the brahmin Dhanañjāni in the inferior Brahmā world while a further task remained to be done, rise from your seat and depart?” “Venerable sir, this thought occurred to me: ‘Indeed, these brahmins are inclined towards the Brahmā world. It would be good if I were to teach the brahmin Dhanañjāni the path to companionship with the Brahmās.’” “The brahmin Dhanañjāni has died, Sāriputta, and has been reborn in the Brahmā world.”

Dhanañjānisuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ sattamaṃ.

The seventh, the Dhanañjāni Sutta, is concluded.

8. Vāseṭṭhasuttaṃ

8. The Vāseṭṭha Sutta.

454. Evaṃ [T 2.0641][V 2.0413] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā icchānaṅgale icchānaṅkale (sī. pī.) viharati icchānaṅgalavanasaṇḍe. Tena kho pana samayena sambahulā abhiññātā abhiññātā brāhmaṇamahāsālā icchānaṅgale paṭivasanti, seyyathidaṃ – caṅkī brāhmaṇo, tārukkho brāhmaṇo, pokkharasāti brāhmaṇo, jāṇussoṇi jāṇussoṇī (pī.), jāṇusoṇī (ka.) brāhmaṇo, todeyyo brāhmaṇo, aññe ca abhiññātā abhiññātā brāhmaṇamahāsālā. Atha kho vāseṭṭhabhāradvājānaṃ māṇavānaṃ jaṅghāvihāraṃ anucaṅkamantānaṃ anuvicarantānaṃ anucaṅkamamānānaṃ anuvicaramānānaṃ (sī. pī.) ayamantarākathā [M 2.0407] udapādi – “kathaṃ, bho, brāhmaṇo hotī”ti? Bhāradvājo māṇavo evamāha – “yato kho, bho, ubhato sujāto mātito ca pitito ca saṃsuddhagahaṇiko yāva sattamā pitāmahayugā akkhitto anupakkuṭṭho jātivādena – ettāvatā kho, bho, brāhmaṇo hotī”ti. Vāseṭṭho māṇavo evamāha – “yato kho, bho, sīlavā ca hoti vattasampanno vatasampanno (pī.) ca – ettāvatā kho, bho, brāhmaṇo hotī”ti. Neva kho asakkhi bhāradvājo māṇavo vāseṭṭhaṃ māṇavaṃ saññāpetuṃ, na pana asakkhi vāseṭṭho māṇavo bhāradvājaṃ māṇavaṃ saññāpetuṃ. Atha kho vāseṭṭho māṇavo bhāradvājaṃ māṇavaṃ āmantesi – “ayaṃ kho, bho bhāradvāja, samaṇo gotamo sakyaputto sakyakulā [T 2.0642] pabbajito icchānaṅgale viharati icchānaṅgalavanasaṇḍe. Taṃ kho pana bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ evaṃ kalyāṇo kittisaddo abbhuggato – ‘itipi so bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho vijjācaraṇasampanno sugato lokavidū anuttaro purisadammasārathi satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavā’ti. Āyāma, bho bhāradvāja, yena samaṇo gotamo tenupasaṅkamissāma; upasaṅkamitvā samaṇaṃ gotamaṃ etamatthaṃ pucchissāma. Yathā no samaṇo gotamo byākarissati tathā naṃ dhāressāmā”ti. “Evaṃ, bho”ti kho bhāradvājo māṇavo vāseṭṭhassa māṇavassa paccassosi.

454. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Icchānaṅgala in the Icchānaṅgala forest grove. At that time, many well-known and distinguished brahmin householders were residing in Icchānaṅgala, namely, the brahmin Caṅkī, the brahmin Tārukkha, the brahmin Pokkharasāti, the brahmin Jāṇussoṇi, the brahmin Todeyya, and other well-known and distinguished brahmin householders. Then, while the young men Vāseṭṭha and Bhāradvāja were walking for exercise, strolling back and forth, this discussion arose between them: “How, friend, does one become a brahmin?” The young man Bhāradvāja said: “When, friend, one is well-born on both sides, from mother and father, of pure maternal descent, whose lineage is unblemished and irreproachable back to the seventh generation of ancestors—to this extent, friend, one is a brahmin.” The young man Vāseṭṭha said: “When, friend, one is virtuous and accomplished in conduct—to this extent, friend, one is a brahmin.” Bhāradvāja was not able to convince Vāseṭṭha, nor was Vāseṭṭha able to convince Bhāradvāja. Then the young man Vāseṭṭha addressed the young man Bhāradvāja: “This, friend Bhāradvāja, is the ascetic Gotama, a Sakyan son who has gone forth from the Sakyan clan, dwelling at Icchānaṅgala in the Icchānaṅgala forest grove. A good report about that venerable Gotama has spread thus: ‘The Blessed One is an Arahant, a Perfectly Enlightened One, perfect in knowledge and conduct, the Sublime One, knower of the world, unsurpassed trainer of persons to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, the Buddha, the Blessed One.’ Come, friend Bhāradvāja, let us go to the ascetic Gotama. Having approached, we shall ask the ascetic Gotama about this matter. As the ascetic Gotama explains it to us, so shall we remember it.” “Very well, friend,” the young man Bhāradvāja replied to the young man Vāseṭṭha.

455. Atha kho vāseṭṭhabhāradvājā māṇavā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṃ sammodiṃsu. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho vāseṭṭho māṇavo bhagavantaṃ gāthāhi ajjhabhāsi –

455. Then the young men Vāseṭṭha and Bhāradvāja approached the Blessed One. Having approached, they exchanged greetings with the Blessed One. When they had concluded their courteous and memorable talk, they sat down to one side. Sitting to one side, the young man Vāseṭṭha addressed the Blessed One in verse:

“Anuññātapaṭiññātā, tevijjā mayamasmubho;

Ahaṃ pokkharasātissa, tārukkhassāyaṃ māṇavo.

“We are both authorized and acknowledged, masters of the three Vedas. I am the pupil of Pokkharasāti, and this young man is the pupil of Tārukkha.”

“Tevijjānaṃ [V 2.0414] yadakkhātaṃ, tatra kevalinosmase;

Padakasmā veyyākaraṇā no byākaraṇā (syā. kaṃ. ka.), jappe ācariyasādisā;

Tesaṃ no jātivādasmiṃ, vivādo atthi gotama.

“In what is proclaimed by the masters of the three Vedas, we are fully accomplished. We are philologists and grammarians, like our teachers in recitation. For us, O Gotama, there is a dispute regarding the matter of birth.”

“Jātiyā [M 2.0408] brāhmaṇo hoti, bhāradvājo iti bhāsati;

Ahañca kammunā kammanā (sī. pī.) brūmi, evaṃ jānāhi cakkhuma.

“‘By birth one is a brahmin,’ so says Bhāradvāja; but I say it is by action. Know this, O One with Vision.”

“Te [T 2.0643] na sakkoma ñāpetuṃ saññattuṃ (pī.), saññāpetuṃ (ka.), aññamaññaṃ mayaṃ ubho;

Bhavantaṃ puṭṭhumāgamā, sambuddhaṃ iti vissutaṃ.

“We two are unable to convince one another. We have come to ask you, who are renowned as the Perfectly Enlightened One.”

“Candaṃ yathā khayātītaṃ, pecca pañjalikā janā;

Vandamānā namassanti, lokasmiṃ gotamaṃ.

“Just as people, with hands joined in reverence, approach and pay homage to the full moon, so in the world they pay homage to Gotama.”

“Cakkhuṃ loke samuppannaṃ, mayaṃ pucchāma gotamaṃ;

Jātiyā brāhmaṇo hoti, udāhu bhavati kammunā kammanā (sī. pī.);

Ajānataṃ no pabrūhi, yathā jānemu brāhmaṇa”nti.

“We ask Gotama, the Eye that has arisen in the world: Is one a brahmin by birth, or does one become so by action? Explain this to us who do not know, so that we may know what a brahmin is.”

456.

456.

“Tesaṃ vo ahaṃ byakkhissaṃ, (vāseṭṭhāti bhagavā)

Anupubbaṃ yathātathaṃ;

Jātivibhaṅgaṃ pāṇānaṃ, aññamaññāhi jātiyo.

“I will explain to you,” said the Blessed One, “O Vāseṭṭha, in due order and according to the truth, the classification of species among living beings, for their species are distinct from one another.”

“Tiṇarukkhepi jānātha, na cāpi paṭijānare;

Liṅgaṃ jātimayaṃ tesaṃ, aññamaññā hi jātiyo.

“Consider the grasses and trees: though they do not declare themselves, their characteristic is determined by their species, for their species are distinct from one another.”

“Tato kīṭe paṭaṅge ca, yāva kunthakipillike;

Liṅgaṃ jātimayaṃ tesaṃ, aññamaññā hi jātiyo.

“Then consider moths and grasshoppers, down to worms and ants. Their characteristic is determined by their species, for their species are distinct from one another.”

“Catuppadepi jānātha, khuddake ca mahallake;

Liṅgaṃ jātimayaṃ tesaṃ, aññamaññā hi jātiyo.

“Consider also the quadrupeds, both small and large. Their characteristic is determined by their species, for their species are distinct from one another.”

“Pādudarepi [V 2.0415] jānātha, urage dīghapiṭṭhike;

Liṅgaṃ jātimayaṃ tesaṃ, aññamaññā hi jātiyo.

“Consider also the long-backed serpents that move on their bellies. Their characteristic is determined by their species, for their species are distinct from one another.”

“Tato macchepi jānātha, udake vārigocare;

Liṅgaṃ jātimayaṃ tesaṃ, aññamaññā hi jātiyo.

“Then consider the fish that live and move in the water. Their characteristic is determined by their species, for their species are distinct from one another.”

“Tato pakkhīpi jānātha, pattayāne vihaṅgame;

Liṅgaṃ [T 2.0644] jātimayaṃ tesaṃ, aññamaññā hi jātiyo.

“Then consider the birds that travel through the sky on their wings. Their characteristic is determined by their species, for their species are distinct from one another.”

“Yathā etāsu jātīsu, liṅgaṃ jātimayaṃ puthu;

Evaṃ natthi manussesu, liṅgaṃ jātimayaṃ puthu.

“Just as among these species there is a distinct characteristic determined by species, so among humans there is no distinct characteristic determined by species.”

“Na [M 2.0409] kesehi na sīsehi, na kaṇṇehi na akkhīhi;

Na mukhena na nāsāya, na oṭṭhehi bhamūhi vā.

“Not by hair, not by head, not by ears, not by eyes, not by mouth, not by nose, not by lips, nor by brows.”

“Na gīvāya na aṃsehi, na udarena na piṭṭhiyā;

Na soṇiyā na urasā, na sambādhe na methune na sambādhā na methunā (ka.).

“Not by neck, not by shoulders, not by belly, not by back, not by hips, not by chest, not in the private parts, nor in sexual union.”

“Na hatthehi na pādehi, naṅgulīhi nakhehi vā;

Na jaṅghāhi na ūrūhi, na vaṇṇena sarena vā;

Liṅgaṃ jātimayaṃ neva, yathā aññāsu jātisu.

“Not by hands, not by feet, not by fingers, nor by nails; not by shanks, not by thighs, not by color, nor by voice. There is no characteristic determined by species, as there is in other species.”

457.

457.

“Paccattañca sarīresu paccattaṃ sasarīresu (sī. pī.), manussesvetaṃ na vijjati;

Vokārañca manussesu, samaññāya pavuccati.

“This individual distinction is not found in the bodies of humans. Any distinction among humans is spoken of merely by designation.”

“Yo hi koci manussesu, gorakkhaṃ upajīvati;

Evaṃ vāseṭṭha jānāhi, kassako so na brāhmaṇo.

“Whoever among humans makes a living by tending cattle, know this, Vāseṭṭha: he is a farmer, not a brahmin.”

“Yo hi koci manussesu, puthusippena jīvati;

Evaṃ vāseṭṭha jānāhi, sippiko so na brāhmaṇo.

“Whoever among humans makes a living by various crafts, know this, Vāseṭṭha: he is a craftsman, not a brahmin.”

“Yo [V 2.0416] hi koci manussesu, vohāraṃ upajīvati;

Evaṃ vāseṭṭha jānāhi, vāṇijo so na brāhmaṇo.

“Whoever among humans makes a living by trade, know this, Vāseṭṭha: he is a merchant, not a brahmin.”

“Yo hi koci manussesu, parapessena jīvati;

Evaṃ vāseṭṭha jānāhi, pessako pessiko (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) so na brāhmaṇo.

“Whoever among humans makes a living by serving others, know this, Vāseṭṭha: he is a servant, not a brahmin.”

“Yo [T 2.0645] hi koci manussesu, adinnaṃ upajīvati;

Evaṃ vāseṭṭha jānāhi, coro eso na brāhmaṇo.

Whoever among humans lives by what is not given, know this, Vāseṭṭha: he is a thief, not a brahmin.

“Yo hi koci manussesu, issatthaṃ upajīvati;

Evaṃ vāseṭṭha jānāhi, yodhājīvo na brāhmaṇo.

Whoever among humans lives by the bow, know this, Vāseṭṭha: he is a warrior, not a brahmin.

“Yo hi koci manussesu, porohiccena jīvati;

Evaṃ vāseṭṭha jānāhi, yājako so na brāhmaṇo.

Whoever among humans lives by the work of a priest, know this, Vāseṭṭha: he is a sacrificer, not a brahmin.

“Yo hi koci manussesu, gāmaṃ raṭṭhañca bhuñjati;

Evaṃ vāseṭṭha jānāhi, rājā eso na brāhmaṇo.

Whoever among humans rules over a village and a kingdom, know this, Vāseṭṭha: he is a king, not a brahmin.

“Na [M 2.0410] cāhaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ brūmi, yonijaṃ mattisambhavaṃ;

Bhovādi bhovādī (syā. kaṃ.) nāma so hoti, sace hoti sakiñcano;

Akiñcanaṃ anādānaṃ, tamahaṃ brūmi brāhmaṇaṃ.

I do not call one a brahmin for being born from a brahmin womb, from a brahmin mother. If he has impediments, he is merely one who addresses others as ‘bho.’ But the one who is without impediments and without clinging—him I call a brahmin.

458.

458.

“Sabbasaṃyojanaṃ chetvā, yo ve na paritassati;

Saṅgātigaṃ visaṃyuttaṃ visaññuttaṃ (ka.), tamahaṃ brūmi brāhmaṇaṃ.

He who, having cut off all fetters, truly does not tremble; who has gone beyond attachment and is disjoined—him I call a brahmin.

“Chetvā naddhiṃ naddhiṃ (sī. pī.) varattañca, sandānaṃ sahanukkamaṃ;

Ukkhittapalighaṃ buddhaṃ, tamahaṃ brūmi brāhmaṇaṃ.

He who has cut the strap, the thong, and the chain along with its latent tendencies; who has removed the crossbar and is awakened—him I call a brahmin.

“Akkosaṃ vadhabandhañca, aduṭṭho yo titikkhati;

Khantībalaṃ balānīkaṃ, tamahaṃ brūmi brāhmaṇaṃ.

He who, without anger, endures abuse, assault, and imprisonment; whose strength is patience, whose army is patience—him I call a brahmin.

“Akkodhanaṃ [V 2.0417] vatavantaṃ, sīlavantaṃ anussadaṃ;

Dantaṃ antimasārīraṃ, tamahaṃ brūmi brāhmaṇaṃ.

He who is free from anger, observant of vows, virtuous, without craving's swell, tamed, and bearing his final body—him I call a brahmin.

“Vāripokkharapatteva, āraggeriva sāsapo;

Yo [T 2.0646] na limpati kāmesu, tamahaṃ brūmi brāhmaṇaṃ.

Like a drop of water on a lotus leaf, like a mustard seed on the point of an awl, he who is not stained by sensual pleasures—him I call a brahmin.

“Yo dukkhassa pajānāti, idheva khayamattano;

Pannabhāraṃ visaṃyuttaṃ, tamahaṃ brūmi brāhmaṇaṃ.

He who knows distinctly, right here in this life, the destruction of his own suffering; who has laid down the burden and is disjoined—him I call a brahmin.

“Gambhīrapaññaṃ medhāviṃ, maggāmaggassa kovidaṃ;

Uttamatthamanuppattaṃ, tamahaṃ brūmi brāhmaṇaṃ.

He who is of profound wisdom, intelligent, skilled in what is the path and what is not the path, and who has attained the supreme goal—him I call a brahmin.

“Asaṃsaṭṭhaṃ gahaṭṭhehi, anāgārehi cūbhayaṃ;

Anokasārimappicchaṃ, tamahaṃ brūmi brāhmaṇaṃ.

He who is unentangled with both householders and the homeless, who wanders without an abode and has few wishes—him I call a brahmin.

“Nidhāya daṇḍaṃ bhūtesu, tasesu thāvaresu ca;

Yo na hanti na ghāteti, tamahaṃ brūmi brāhmaṇaṃ.

He who has laid down the rod toward beings, whether they be trembling or firm, who neither kills nor causes others to kill—him I call a brahmin.

“Aviruddhaṃ viruddhesu, attadaṇḍesu nibbutaṃ;

Sādānesu anādānaṃ, tamahaṃ brūmi brāhmaṇaṃ.

He who is unopposed among the opposed, at peace among those who have taken up the rod, and without clinging among those who cling—him I call a brahmin.

“Yassa rāgo ca doso ca, māno makkho ca ohito;

Sāsaporiva āraggā, tamahaṃ brūmi brāhmaṇaṃ.

He from whom passion, aversion, conceit, and contempt have fallen away, like a mustard seed from the point of an awl—him I call a brahmin.

459.

459.

“Akakkasaṃ [M 2.0411] viññāpaniṃ, giraṃ saccaṃ udīraye;

Yāya nābhisajje kiñci, tamahaṃ brūmi brāhmaṇaṃ.

He who utters speech that is not harsh, that makes the meaning known, and is true, by which he offends no one—him I call a brahmin.

“Yo ca dīghaṃ va rassaṃ vā, aṇuṃ thūlaṃ subhāsubhaṃ;

Loke adinnaṃ nādeti nādiyati (sī. pī.), tamahaṃ brūmi brāhmaṇaṃ.

He who in this world does not take what is not given, whether it be long or short, small or large, beautiful or ugly—him I call a brahmin.

“Āsā [V 2.0418] yassa na vijjanti, asmiṃ loke paramhi ca;

Nirāsāsaṃ nirāsayaṃ (sī. pī.) visaṃyuttaṃ, tamahaṃ brūmi brāhmaṇaṃ.

He for whom cravings do not exist, neither for this world nor for the next; who is free from longing and disjoined—him I call a brahmin.

“Yassālayā na vijjanti, aññāya akathaṃkathiṃ;

Amatogadhaṃ [T 2.0647] anuppattaṃ, tamahaṃ brūmi brāhmaṇaṃ.

He for whom attachments do not exist; who, through knowledge, is free from doubt and has reached the depths of the Deathless—him I call a brahmin.

“Yodhapuññañca pāpañca, ubho saṅgaṃ upaccagā;

Asokaṃ virajaṃ suddhaṃ, tamahaṃ brūmi brāhmaṇaṃ.

He who here has overcome attachment to both merit and demerit; who is sorrowless, stainless, and pure—him I call a brahmin.

“Candaṃ va vimalaṃ suddhaṃ, vippasannaṃ anāvilaṃ;

Nandībhavaparikkhīṇaṃ, tamahaṃ brūmi brāhmaṇaṃ.

He who is stainless and pure like the moon, exceedingly serene and untroubled, in whom delight in existence is exhausted—him I call a brahmin.

“Yo imaṃ palipathaṃ duggaṃ, saṃsāraṃ mohamaccagā;

Tiṇṇo pāraṅgato jhāyī, anejo akathaṃkathī;

Anupādāya nibbuto, tamahaṃ brūmi brāhmaṇaṃ.

He who has overcome this mire, this difficult path, this saṃsāra, this delusion; who has crossed over and gone to the other shore; who is meditative, free from craving, and without doubt; who, through non-clinging, is extinguished—him I call a brahmin.

“Yodhakāme pahantvāna pahatvāna (sī.), anāgāro paribbaje;

Kāmabhavaparikkhīṇaṃ, tamahaṃ brūmi brāhmaṇaṃ.

He who here, having abandoned sensual pleasures, goes forth as a homeless one, in whom sensual existence is exhausted—him I call a brahmin.

“Yodhataṇhaṃ pahantvāna, anāgāro paribbaje;

Taṇhābhavaparikkhīṇaṃ, tamahaṃ brūmi brāhmaṇaṃ.

He who here, having abandoned craving, goes forth as a homeless one, in whom craving for existence is exhausted—him I call a brahmin.

“Hitvā mānusakaṃ yogaṃ, dibbaṃ yogaṃ upaccagā;

Sabbayogavisaṃyuttaṃ, tamahaṃ brūmi brāhmaṇaṃ.

He who, having abandoned the human yoke and overcome the divine yoke, is disjoined from all yokes—him I call a brahmin.

“Hitvā ratiñca aratiṃ, sītībhūtaṃ nirūpadhiṃ;

Sabbalokābhibhuṃ vīraṃ, tamahaṃ brūmi brāhmaṇaṃ.

He who, having abandoned delight and discontent, has become cool and is without substrata; the hero who has conquered all worlds—him I call a brahmin.

“Cutiṃ yo vedi sattānaṃ, upapattiñca sabbaso;

Asattaṃ sugataṃ buddhaṃ, tamahaṃ brūmi brāhmaṇaṃ.

He who knows in every way the passing away and rebirth of beings; who is unattached, well-gone, and awakened—him I call a brahmin.

“Yassa [V 2.0419] gatiṃ na jānanti, devā gandhabbamānusā;

Khīṇāsavaṃ arahantaṃ, tamahaṃ brūmi brāhmaṇaṃ.

He whose destination is not known by gods, gandhabbas, or humans; the Arahant in whom the taints are destroyed—him I call a brahmin.

“Yassa [T 2.0648][M 2.0412] pure ca pacchā ca, majjhe ca natthi kiñcanaṃ;

Akiñcanaṃ anādānaṃ, tamahaṃ brūmi brāhmaṇaṃ.

He for whom there is no impediment in the past, the future, or the present; who is without impediment and without clinging—him I call a brahmin.

“Usabhaṃ pavaraṃ vīraṃ, mahesiṃ vijitāvinaṃ;

Anejaṃ nhātakaṃ nahātakaṃ (sī. pī.) buddhaṃ, tamahaṃ brūmi brāhmaṇaṃ.

The noble bull, the excellent, the hero, the great seer, the victor; the one free from craving, the one who has bathed, the Awakened One—him I call a brahmin.

“Pubbenivāsaṃ yo vedi, saggāpāyañca passati;

Atho jātikkhayaṃ patto, tamahaṃ brūmi brāhmaṇaṃ.

He who knows past abodes, who sees heaven and the states of woe, and who has attained the destruction of birth—him I call a brahmin.

460.

460.

“Samaññā hesā lokasmiṃ, nāmagottaṃ pakappitaṃ;

Sammuccā samudāgataṃ, tattha tattha pakappitaṃ.

For this is a mere designation in the world, this name and lineage that is devised. It has arisen by convention and is devised in various places.

“Dīgharattānusayitaṃ, diṭṭhigatamajānataṃ;

Ajānantā no ajānantā noti ajānantā eva (ṭīkā) pabrunti pabruvanti (sī. pī.), jātiyā hoti brāhmaṇo.

This wrong view has long lain latent in those who do not know. Not knowing, they declare: ‘By birth one is a brahmin.’

“Na jaccā brāhmaṇo vasalo (syā. kaṃ. ka.) hoti, na jaccā hoti abrāhmaṇo brāhmaṇo (syā. kaṃ. ka.);

Kammunā brāhmaṇo vasalo (syā. kaṃ. ka.) hoti, kammunā hoti abrāhmaṇo brāhmaṇo (syā. kaṃ. ka.).

Not by birth is one a brahmin, not by birth is one not a brahmin. By action one is a brahmin, by action one is not a brahmin.

“Kassako kammunā hoti, sippiko hoti kammunā;

Vāṇijo kammunā hoti, pessako hoti kammunā.

By action one is a farmer, by action one is a craftsman; by action one is a merchant, by action one is a servant.

“Coropi kammunā hoti, yodhājīvopi kammunā;

Yājako kammunā hoti, rājāpi hoti kammunā.

By action one is a thief, by action one is a soldier; by action one is a sacrificer, and by action one is a king.

“Evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ, kammaṃ passanti paṇḍitā;

Paṭiccasamuppādadassā, kammavipākakovidā.

Thus the wise, who see dependent origination and are skilled in kamma and its result, see this action as it really is.

“Kammunā [V 2.0420] vattati loko, kammunā vattati pajā;

Kammanibandhanā sattā, rathassāṇīva yāyato.

By kamma the world revolves, by kamma people revolve; beings are bound by kamma, like the linchpin of a moving chariot.

“Tapena [T 2.0649] brahmacariyena, saṃyamena damena ca;

Etena brāhmaṇo hoti, etaṃ brāhmaṇamuttamaṃ.

By ascetic practice, by the holy life, by restraint, and by taming—by this one is a brahmin. This is supreme brahmin-hood.

“Tīhi vijjāhi sampanno, santo khīṇapunabbhavo;

Evaṃ vāseṭṭha jānāhi, brahmā sakko vijānata”nti.

“One endowed with the three knowledges, peaceful, with future existence destroyed—know this, Vāseṭṭha: for those who understand, he is a Brahmā and a Sakka.”

461. Evaṃ [T 2.0650][M 2.0413] vutte, vāseṭṭhabhāradvājā māṇavā bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ – “abhikkantaṃ, bho gotama, abhikkantaṃ, bho gotama!
